items.statement: Retail loan book growth guidance of 17% for FY25
items.quote: We are looking at book growth of 17% in retail segment FY’25 onwards with higher focus on Affordable and Emerging segment.

items.statement: Margin guidance of around 3.5% for FY25
items.quote: In terms of guidance, the margin would be around 3.5%, ROA will be more than 2.1%, credit cost for FY’25 is expected to be around 30 bps.

items.statement: OPEX to ATA guidance of 95-100 bps for FY25
items.quote: So, there will be some lag effect, but I think we should be able to catch up and OPEX would be 95 to 100 bps.

items.statement: Retail loan book grew 14.1% YoY to Rs.1,790 crore in Affordable segment
items.quote: Affordable book on a QoQ basis, we have grown by 56%, on a YoY, it's over 11 times. We are looking at book growth of 17% in retail segment FY’25 onwards with higher focus on Affordable and Emerging segment.

items.statement: Corporate loan book reduced 46% YoY to Rs.2,052 crore as planned
items.quote: Corporate: The book last year was Rs.3,802 crores and this year it is Rs.2,052 crores. The book has degrown by 46% as per plan and run-off last year that is FY’23, it was 18.7%, we have a good story here; run-off has come down to 16.7%.

items.statement: Retail disbursements grew 35% YoY in Q4 and 19% for full year FY24 to Rs.17,483 crore
items.quote: Talking about disbursements, retail disbursements grew by 35% in Q4 and 19% in FY ’24. We disbursed loans worth Rs.5,541 crores, which is again all-time high in the last over five years. And if you have to look at the whole year, the disbursement was Rs.17,483 crores.

items.statement: Affordable and Emerging segments to contribute 40-42% of incremental disbursements in FY25
items.quote: So, our plan is to try and build the book from both Affordable and Emerging, which would contribute to almost about 40 % to 42% of incremental business. So, whatever business we're going to do this year, incrementally, Affordable and Emerging would contribute to 42% of the overall disbursement, and the rest 58% would come from Prime.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 300 branches: 160 Affordable, 50 Emerging, 90 Prime
items.quote: As we speak, we have totally 300 branches, out of 300, 160 would be Affordable, 50 branches would be in Emerging segment and the balance 90 will cater to Prime.

items.statement: Opened 90 branches in Q4 FY24: 60 Affordable, 22 Emerging, balance Prime
items.quote: We have further invested in around 90 additional branches for Roshni and Emerging verticals in Q4 FY’24. This will help us in scaling up Roshni and Emerging verticals faster.

items.statement: NIM was 3.65% in Q4 FY24, expected to stabilize around 3.5% in FY25
items.quote: NIM during Q4 was at 3.65%, which is in line with the last quarter X 1-off NIM. The reported NIM last quarter was 3.49 %, against that in Q4, it is 3.65 %. Next year we expect this to be somewhere around 3.5%.

items.statement: Yield on Affordable segment expected to increase 100 bps to 12.5-12.6% in FY25
items.quote: On Affordable, last year, the yield was about 11.6%. In FY’25, there will be 100 bps lift in terms of yield and Affordable. So, we are looking at 12.5% to 12.6%.

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowing at 7.93% in Q4 FY24, expected to decrease due to rating upgrade
items.quote: The incremental cost of borrowing for the quarter is 7.93 %. Deposits grew by 3% during the year with 88% as public dep osits. We are well capitalized with CRAR of 29.3% and out of that tier-I is 27.9%.

items.statement: NHB refinance increased to 9.2% of borrowing mix from 5.7%, at ~50 bps lower cost
items.quote: In FY’24, we received Rs.3,000 crores from NHB which started in FY’24 and it was not there in prior two to three years' time because of high GNPA and high net NPA. We started off in FY’24 and we have availed Rs.3,000 crores from NHB which will come at a n approximately about 50 bps lower than the others average source of borrowing.

items.statement: GNPA reduced 57% YoY to Rs.984 crore (1.50% from 3.83%), NNPA at 0.95%
items.quote: Our GNPA reduced by 57% YoY to INR 984 crore, FY’23 the GNPA was 3.83% and FY’24 that is as of March it is 1.5%. Net NPA declined to less than 1%. So, it is at 0.95% as on 31st March '24.

items.statement: Corporate GNPA improved from 22.5% to 3.31%, Retail GNPA from 2.57% to 1.45%
items.quote: Corporate GNPA in March '23 was 22.5%, March '24 is 3.31%, Retail GNPA as of March '23 was 2.57% and March '24 is 1.45%.

items.statement: Sold 268 properties via auction in FY24 with no principal loss, recovered Rs.100 crore from write-off pool
items.quote: We sold 268 properties in FY’24 through auction as compared to 95 properties in F Y’23. And in F Y’24 on those 2 68 properties which went through auction, there was no principal loss at an enterprise level.

items.statement: Raised Rs.3,000 crore from NHB, Rs.1,500 crore via NCDs, Rs.10,000 crore via CPs in FY24
items.quote: We restarted raising funds from wholesale debt market. We raised about Rs.1,500 crores through NCD and Rs.10,000 crores via CPs in FY’24.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded from AA to AA+ by India Ratings, ICRA and CARE
items.quote: As you are aware , we got rating upgrade from AA to AA + from three rating agencies , that is India Ratings, ICRA and CARE.

items.statement: ROA improved to 2.2% in FY24 from 1.61% in FY23, ROE at 10.9%
items.quote: Our return on asset improved to 2.2% in F Y’24 from 1.61% in FY’23. Return on equity was at 10.9%.

items.statement: PAT grew 44% YoY to Rs.1,508 crore in FY24 (79% ex-one-off)
items.quote: In terms of profitability , in FY’24 PA T stood at Rs.1,508 crores, registering a growth of 44% YoY; X 1-off. PA T registered a growth of 79% Y oY.

items.statement: Overall book depletion rate at 16.7% in FY24, BT-out rate at ~7%
items.quote: Our overall closures have been 16.7% in the year. BT out used to be higher; if you compare FY’23, it used to be higher, in FY’24, it has come down, so now it will be in the range of about 7%-odd, on a YoY basis BT out has come down by 10%.

items.statement: Regulatory audit by NHB completed with initial observations discussed, nothing serious, awaiting final confirmation
items.quote: There was an audit by the regulator, and we have discussed the initial observations . So, there's nothing serious in nature and we are still awaiting final confirmation from the regulator.

items.statement: Dedicated vertical teams for Affordable, Emerging and Prime with separate sales, credit, ops and collections
items.quote: In order to bring undivided focus on retail segment, we ensured that we set up different verticals, for example, Affordable, Emerging and Prime. These three are different verticals within retail, which means there is a dedicated team starting from sales , credit, operations and collections.

items.statement: Corporate lending to restart in H2 FY25, to remain under 10% of portfolio long-term
items.quote: So, corporate, we have planned to start this year, maybe we might start in second half, so that would also assist in better yields.

items.statement: Emerging segment yield 50-75 bps higher than Prime, Affordable yield 12.5-12.6%
items.quote: Within our segment composition, this would be about 50 to 75 bps higher than the Prime yield.

items.statement: Cement demand expected to grow 8.5% to 9% in FY25; Dalmia targets 1.5x sector volume growth excluding Jaypee assets, plus 4-5% incremental from Jaypee
items.quote: I believe that the cement demand should grow between 8.5% to 9%. Dalmia Bharat Limited. April 25, 2024 I believe that we can deliver a volume growth of 1.5x of the sector, excluding sales from the Jaypee assets. The additional volumes from Jaypee should give us an incremental 4% to 5% growth on an overall basis

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of INR3,500-4,000 crores for organic projects plus INR3,500 crores for Jaypee acquisition; peak gross debt ~INR9,000 crores, net debt INR5,000-5,250 crores by year-end
items.quote: We expect capex spending of about INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores of capex in FY '25, which will largely include spends towards Northeast expansion projects, Rohtas Cement plant in Bihar and als o certain ROE and maintenance capex. This will be besides the outflow for Jaypee assets, which is expected to be around INR3,500 crores for 5.2 million tons, cement capacity of Rewa, Churk, Chunar, and

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA/t fell to INR743 (down from INR917 FY24 avg) due to 7.5% QoQ price drop, higher logistics (+4.7% YoY), marketing (+INR30cr QoQ), inventory depletion (INR137cr); expect partial reversal in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: During the quarter, the prices in our key markets declined. And due to lower realizations and higher cost, our EBITDA per ton declined to INR743 per ton. The price drop in Q4 is far more than what we have seen in similar periods in any previous year. Prices on an average declined by 7.5% Q-o-Q, while exit prices in March were lower by 9% to 10% compared to Q3 average.

items.statement: Power & fuel cost down 21% YoY to INR1,018/t (blended fuel INR1.45/Mn Kcal); green power 28% (up from 21%); petcoke 56% of fuel mix; expect 1-2% further fuel cost reduction in Q1
items.quote: Power and fuel costs declined 21% Y-o-Y to INR1,018 per ton of cement, mainly due to $48 decline in the fuel consumption cost on a Y-o-Y basis. With this, our blended fuel cost during the quarter stands at INR1.45 per Mn Kcal rate. Besides the correction in fuel prices, our efficiency parameters like usage of renewal power improved to 27% from 21% in FY '23.

items.statement: Final dividend INR5/share proposed (plus INR4 interim) = INR9/share total for FY24
items.quote: Lastly, in line with the capital allocation framework, the Board has proposed a final dividend of INR5 per share, which is subject to the approval of the shareholders in the ensuing AGM. This is in addition to the interim dividend of INR4 per share. A total dividend declared for the year, including interim, is INR9 per share.

items.statement: Marketing spend INR70cr in Q4 (+INR30cr QoQ) for new 'RCF Strong toh Ghar Strong' campaign; aim to reduce dealer discounts via brand pull
items.quote: During the year, we launched a new brand campaign, "RCF Strong toh Ghar Strong", and repositioned Dalmia as Roof, Column, Foundation Expert. That is our RCF Expert. We have invested about INR70 crores during the quarter in marketing, which is an increase o f about INR30 crores on a Q-o-Q basis

items.statement: Industry consolidation accelerating: UltraTech-Kesoram, Ambuja-Sanghi, Dalmia-Jaypee, plus grinding unit deals; structural view: incumbents investing signals long-term confidence
items.quote: We are already seeing 3 transactions, which are in the works. UltraTech is buying Kesoram. Ambuja is buying Sanghi, and our transaction with Jaypee is under process. These 3 are large transactions. There are some small transactions, which were announced recently in terms of grinding units, which were bought by UltraTech and Ambuja.

items.statement: Jaypee acquisition delayed: NARCL bid for Jaypee debt under lender evaluation; procedural delays may push closure to Q2 FY25; SAIL JV partner evaluating right of first refusal
items.quote: The Jaypee transaction has taken longer than we anticipated, bu t it is progressing in the right direction. As you all must have read in the papers, NARCL has put in a bid to buy the entire debt of Jaypee and it is under evaluation by the current lenders. We understand that the lenders are keen to create lending capaci ty on their balance sheet by transferring this debt to NARCL, but there are pro

items.statement: Unprecedented Q4 price drop (7.5% QoQ) across all regions, not led by Dalmia; excess industry capacity persists; margin recovery depends on price rebound and cost normalization
items.quote: I think the price decline is not just for Dalmia, it is for the whole industry. And as regards whether price increases can happen in the election quarter, the answer is that, yes, it can happen. However, I think given the momentum that we are seeing in April, we feel that the price increases are unlikely to come through this quarter. That's what we feel. But again, who knows, hard to forecast how

items.statement: Mr. Singhi moved from employee role to strategic advisor; his cost shifted from employee expense to other expenses
items.quote: See, Mr. Singhi earlier was on the roles of the company, and he moved as a strategic adviser. So his cost has, under the new agreement, has moved to other expenses from the employee cost. So that is one significant change.

items.statement: Depreciation policy changed: Northeast units from WDV to SLM from Jan 1, 2024; salvage value raised from 1% to 5%; Q4 depreciation lower by INR60cr, FY24 higher by INR193cr (INR108cr from debottlenecking)
items.quote: revaluated the economic benefits derived from property, plant and equipment of our Northeast units and decided to change the method of providing depreciation on PPE from written down value method to straight line method with effect from January 1, 2024. Now we are providing depreciation on SLM method across the company. Further, we have also Dalmia Bharat Limited. April 25, 2024 reassessed the sal

items.statement: Expect sugar production of 2.75 lakh quintals in Q1 FY25
items.quote: 2.75 lakh quintals is what we expect to produce this quarter.

items.statement: Expect May-June sugar quotas 4-5% higher than last year
items.quote: I would not be surprised if they are 4% to 5% higher than last year.

items.statement: Target dual-feed distillery conversion ready within calendar year 2024
items.quote: We are targeting to have it ready in this calendar year for sure.

items.statement: Project FY25 capex of INR35 crore +/- INR5 crore for maintenance and bottlenecking
items.quote: We do believe our capexes should be in the region of INR35 crores plus minus 5 crores is what we are projecting for the current off-season.

items.statement: Dual-feed distillery conversion capex expected below INR60 crore with interest subvention eligibility
items.quote: Our capex is going to be considerably, it's only a marginal capex. We do hope it will be a little lower than INR60 crores. And we are eligible for the interest subvention scheme of the government of India for this set capex.

items.statement: Asmoli refining capacity 1,800 TPD (600 TPD pharma-grade, 1,200 TPD conventional)
items.quote: We have about 1,800 tons of per day refining capacity in Asmoli. Out of which 600 odd tons is able to produce pharma grade sugar and 1,200 will produce normal refined sugar.

items.statement: No capacity augmentation needed; cane crush seen flat next season
items.quote: We don't need capacity augmentation. We already crushed 4.27 crore quintals of cane, 42.7 lakh tons of cane last year. And looking at the cane numbers, we don't see a big jump in the coming year.

items.statement: Branded sugar sales 31,000 tons (INR120 crore) in FY24
items.quote: We sold 31,000 tons of branded sugar this year, which accounts for around INR120 crores of turnover in our total sugar turnover.

items.statement: Country liquor sales grew 115% to 2.50 million cases in FY24
items.quote: Our country liquor sale volume in our spirits segment had an impressive growth of about 115%. Our sale volume stood at 2.50 million cases as compared to 1.16 million cases last year.

items.statement: FY24 sugar segment EBIT margin improved to 4.99% from 4.52%
items.quote: EBIT margins for the financial year for this segment were at 4.99% as against 4.52% in FY '23.

items.statement: FY24 biofuels segment EBIT margin fell to 10.83% from 19.32%
items.quote: EBIT margin was at 10.83% in FY '24 as against 19.32% in FY '23.

items.statement: FY24 country liquor EBIT margin (net of excise) rose to 14.72% from 4.56%
items.quote: EBIT margin based on revenue net of excise for the full year is 14.72% as against 4.56% in FY '23.

items.statement: Average sugar realization FY24 INR38,350/ton vs INR36,684/ton FY23
items.quote: Average sugar realization stood at INR38,350 per ton as against INR36,684 per ton in FY '23.

items.statement: Ethanol realization FY24 INR58.81/BL vs INR60.83/BL FY23 due to mix shift
items.quote: Ethanol sales were at 82.68 million BL of ethanol at an average realisation of INR58.81 per BL in FY '24 as against 88.52 million BL of ethanol sales at an average realisation ofINR60.83 per BL in FY '23

items.statement: Current sugar prices INR39-39.5/kg in April 2024
items.value: INR39 per kg and INR39.5 per kg
items.quote: In April, the prices are in the region of INR39.5 per kg. Between INR39 per kg and INR39.5 per kg.

items.statement: Domestic pharma-grade sugar demand growing; exports banned
items.quote: We are also seeing a steady increase in demand in the domestic sector.

items.statement: Branded sugar volume growth expected low double-digits organically
items.quote: If you look at historical trends about 10% to 15% growth will probably be the right number for our own brand.

items.statement: Ethanol production mix shifted: 84.39M BL B-heavy, 3.5M BL syrup, rest C-heavy in FY24
items.value: 84.39 million BL B-heavy, 3.5 million BL syrup
items.quote: We produced 93.14 million BL of ethanol in this year out of which 84.39 million BL was derived from B-Heavy, 3.5 million BL was from syrup while the remaining was from the C-Heavy.

items.statement: Pharma-grade sugar sales ~25,000-30,000 tons expected in FY25 vs ~10,000 tons FY24
items.quote: We will have a couple of maybe about 25,000, 30,000 tons of sugar will go towards this segment in different players.

items.statement: Institutional/pharma sugar customers have lengthy qualification processes
items.quote: They have lengthy processes, but this is again a growing market.

items.statement: Net fund-based working capital utilisation rose to INR804 crore (Mar'24) from INR460 crore (Mar'23) due to higher inventory
items.quote: Net fund based working capital utilisation as on 31st March '24 stood at INR804 crores as against INR460 crores as on 31st March '23.

items.statement: Long-term debt stable at INR241.44 crore (Mar'24) vs INR246.32 crore (Mar'23); repaid INR78.28 crore, fresh loans INR72.33 crore
items.quote: Long term loan as on 31st March '24 stood at INR241.44 crores as against INR246.32 crores as on 31st March '23. We paid long term loans ofINR78.28 crores in this year and availed fresh term loans ofINR72.33 crores for the capexes

items.statement: Expect ethanol policy to turn favourable with comfortable sugar stocks (8.5-9M MT closing)
items.quote: We do believe the ethanol policy should be more favourable towards diversion.

items.statement: Red rot disease not fully contained in West UP; eradication and variety replacement ongoing
items.quote: I don't think West UP is completely out of the woods. We are making all out intensive effort towards containment of red rot not to allow it to spread. Eradication of infected bushes and replacement of varieties into COl lA 15023.

items.statement: Distillery idle time expected 4-5 months until grain conversion completes in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our grain-based capacity is still not on stream. It will only come on to stream somewhere during Q3. So we do estimate that we will have some idle time in our distillery during the next four to five months.

items.statement: Gross sugar recovery improved to 11.37% in FY24 from 11.01% in FY23
items.quote: Our gross recovery stood at 11.37% this year as compared to 11.01 % last year.

items.statement: Net sugar recovery improved to 10.3% in FY24 from 9.4% in FY23
items.quote: Our cane recovery efforts have paid off as net recovery for the quarter came to 10.3% as against 9.4% in FY '23.

items.statement: No immediate buyback plans; will evaluate after cash flows materialize
items.quote: We do not have any plans for the immediate future to do a share buyback. Let the top line and the money come into the balance sheet and then we will, only after the money is realized and the money is realized in our balance sheet, then we will look at the best way to utilize this money.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of Rs 50 crore for FY25 and Rs 110 crore for FY26
items.quote: Our revenue projections for the next two years will be 50 and 110 for crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 45% for next two years with potential to grow further
items.quote: 45% for the next two years. But as Raja said, that with revenue growing and you're pretty much sorted on your cost, there shouldn't. Your EBITDA margins should only grow from here.

items.statement: Aim to maintain annual EBITDA margin around 43-46%
items.quote: We should be able to maintain whatever the annual EBITDA margin that we have, 43%. We should aim at being around between 43 to 45, 46%.

items.statement: Strong pipeline sufficient for next two years with large deals expected
items.quote: Our current pipeline is good enough for us for the next two years. There will be large deals which will keep coming up and which will keep getting added.

items.statement: Expect similar annual growth rates over next three to five years driven by strong pipeline
items.quote: Whatever we are seeing right now on supply chain and the numbers and the growth rates that you are seeing you will continue with very similar annual growth rates over the next three to five years.

items.statement: Won 17 new deals in FY24, went live with 9 clients, 12-15 clients on verge of going live
items.quote: If you see the deals that we have won in the last financial year, there were 17 deals that we have won and we have gone live with nine clients.

items.statement: Global bank conversations doubled from 64 to 135 banks in last year
items.quote: And in April 24, that 64 moved to 135. So we doubled the number of banks already conversations.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 43% in FY24 from prior year, driven by fixed cost base
items.quote: And you will see this kind of trend in the future. Also, because our cost base, which is there a cost base is very nearly fixed.

items.statement: Pricing model charges few basis points to 30-40 bps on assets under management based on spreads, portfolio migration, and volume potential
items.value: single digit basis points to as much as 30 40 basis points
items.quote: It could vary from a few basis points, single digit basis points, to as much as 30 40 basis points.

items.statement: Expanding from financial institutions to large corporates directly; signed large corporates already
items.quote: Now, going forward, what you will also see is we will start interacting and working directly with large corporates. We have already started signing on large corporates.

items.statement: Capitalized Rs 52.8 crore in FY24; expect 15-20% growth in capitalization for FY25
items.quote: 52.8 crores is the total capitalization that we've done during the year. And, and like Raja said, you can. Expect 15%, 20% growth on it for the next year.

items.statement: Amortization expected to increase significantly in FY25 due to projected revenue growth
items.quote: Ideally a much bigger amount we expect. Because it's based on projected revenues being a SAAS based model, our revenues are going to have a cumulative effect.

items.statement: Country directors now in 27 countries, doubled from previous year
items.quote: Our number of country directors that we have at a global level, that number has doubled. Now we have country directors in 27 different countries.

items.statement: PSB Alliance platform 95% ready, targeting go-live by July 2024
items.quote: for that is nearly ready when I say nearly, I would say it's 95% ready. We are right now at some nuts and bolts space. We think we should be going live on this by sometime in the month of July

items.statement: Platform processes $25 billion annual disbursements across 50+ banks and NBFCs
items.quote: As of last numbers, $25 billion is the number that we are seeing annual disbursements on our platform across all our banking clients.

items.statement: Net DSO at 144 days as of March 2024; collections exceeded revenue in FY24
items.quote: Our net DSO is at 144. As of March 24. And our collections, if you see our collections have outstripped our revenue.

items.statement: Near-zero attrition over last 24 months; certified Great Place to Work for two consecutive years
items.quote: In last 24 months, w e have not lost anybody on the team that we would not have wanted to lose. So our attrition is close to 0% over the last 24 months and for the last two consecutive years we have been certified as a great place to work

items.statement: Differentiated by end-to-end product, low attrition, faster implementation, pay-as-you-use model; do not lose deals on pricing
items.quote: We do not lose deals today on pricing.

items.statement: PSB Alliance opportunity estimated at 20 lakh crore (10x current 2 lakh crore market); execution depends on bank underwriting capacity
items.quote: If as on date, you were to ask us what is the opportunity size? It is more like two lakh. It's more ten times that. That means 20 lakh crores.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guided at 15-16%
items.quote: From a FY '25 perspective, what we believe is, given the performance which we had in FY '24, we are fairly confident that we should be in the range of 15% to 16% for FY '25.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin at 16.5%, full year at 17.8%
items.quote: We exited Q4 FY '24 at EBITDA of 16.5%. Full-year EBITDA stood at 17.8%, which is an increase of 640 basis points year -on-year basically.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 gross margin 30.6%, down 50 bps QoQ due to leave utilization reversal and delivery cost increase
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter stood at 30.6%, drop of 50 basis points quarter -on-quarter. Decline was primarily due to: Reversal of 120 basis point benefit received in the last quarter on account of higher leave utilization and Increase in cost of delivery and other operational cost increase in travel, recruitment, et cetera, impacting the margin by 130 basis points.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 order book $181.5M, up 8.4% QoQ; full year $698M, up 22% YoY
items.quote: Order book for the quarter stood at $181.5 million, increase 8.4% from last quarter. Order book for the full year was $698 million, which is an increase of 22.0% year-on-year.

items.statement: Sequential growth across all verticals in Q4 FY24; BFSI +2.0%, MCS +2.3%, Hitech +0.7%, Healthcare +3.5% in constant currency
items.quote: In constant currency terms on a Q -o-Q basis, our services revenues in Banking and Financial Services grew by 2 .0%, Manufacturing and Consumer Services grew by 2.3% and even Hitech grew by 0.7% and our newest baby, Healthcare, by 3.5%.

items.statement: Client satisfaction score reached 70, up 17 points over 2 years
items.quote: I'm also very proud of the fact that we have achieved the highest client satisfaction score in our history of 70. Just for context, just 2 years back, this score was 53. So, that is a Seventeen-percentage point increase over the last 2 years.

items.statement: Normalized depreciation expected at $3.2-3.5M per quarter going forward after lease resizing
items.quote: But at the same time, we expect that the normalized depreciation going forward could continue to be in the range of $3.2 million to $3.5 million per quarter.

items.statement: DSO improved to 73 days, down 2 days QoQ; cash and equivalents $261.7M, up $13.3M QoQ
items.quote: DSO for the quarter stood at 73 days improved by 2 days from the last quarter. For the quarter, cash and cash equivalents, including investments, stood at $261.7 million, $13.3 million increase from last quarter.

items.statement: Final dividend of Rs. 7 per share recommended; total FY24 payout 450% of face value
items.quote: The Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of Rs. 7 per share for the financial year FY '24, subject to approval of shareholders. With this, total dividend payout, including interim dividend for the financial year FY '24, will be 450% of the face value.

items.statement: Service lines revenue share increased to 52.7% in FY24; Experience Services +9.1%, SaaS +6.9% QoQ
items.quote: The share of revenues of our service lines, that is advanced engineering services, data engineering and analytics, experience services and foundation services, increased to 52.7% in FY '24. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, in reported terms, Experience services revenue grew by 9.1%, Application Services and Enterprise Applications (SaaS) grew by 6.9%.

items.statement: Utilization improved 300 bps QoQ and 230 bps YoY; pyramid optimization and subcontractor management continuing
items.quote: Our utilization improved by 300 basis points se quentially and 230 basis points year -on-year. Rigor associated with accelerated fulfillment and capability engagement continued in Q4.

items.statement: Healthcare strategy includes acquisition targets in defined sub-industries and value chain
items.quote: We have defined clearly the sub -industries where we want to play. We have cle arly identified parts of the value chain where we have to play. And we are looking at acquisition targets also based on that.

items.statement: Other income benefited from ~8% yield on investable surplus and lease termination gains
items.quote: So, the other income, we had almost close to 8 .0% yield on our investable surplus that is what is getting reflected over there. Additionally, we have also resized and terminated a few of our leased facilities in U.S. and India. That has also resulted in some portion of it in other income.

items.statement: Effective tax rate 24.1% vs 26.2% last year; no debt or borrowing details discussed
items.quote: The effective tax rate for the year stood at 24.1% against 26.2% last year.

items.statement: 98% of Pune campus energy from green sources effective January 2024; infrastructure retrofit saved 1 lakh kWh
items.quote: Effective January 2024, 98% of our total energy consumption in Pune campus is from green energy. The infrastructure retrofit project contributed the reduction of 1 lakh kilowatt energy units, resulting in carbon emission reduction thereof.

items.statement: Leadership team stabilizing; no wholesale changes expected; focus on performance and culture alignment
items.quote: I have been very satisfied with my team. And hence, I don't think that you should expect any wholesale changes. I'm not one of those IT services CEOs who will come and say that I'll bring my entire new team.

items.statement: FY24 PAT 13.6%, EPS Rs. 29.1 more than doubled YoY
items.quote: Our full year PAT stood at 13.6%. EPS for the year stood at Rs. 29.1, which has more than doubled from last year.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth expected above industry average with visible gains from tech-led strategy and client mining
items.quote: We expect that in FY '25, we will be at above industry growth with visible gains from tech-led and account focused strategy, including share gains, consolidation and continued active mining of clients, especially in the 11 to 30 and the NCA categories.

items.statement: FY25 EBIT margin guided at 14.6% to 16% with focus on operational rigor and productivity levers
items.quote: Our operating margins will remain in the stated band of 14.6% to 16% in the upcoming year with a continued focus on operational rigor, giving u s increased confidence on the trajectory of our performance

items.statement: FY24 new TCV wins at $1.38 billion, Q4 FY24 TCV at $177 million with 77% powered by next-gen technology adoption
items.quote: We closed the year with new TCV wins at $1.38 billion in FY24 and closed deals worth $177 million in Q4 '24. Notably, significant TCV wins continue to be from our beyond top 10 accounts and are well distributed between our various service lines. 77% of our deal wins in this quarter were powered by next-gen technology adoption.

items.statement: Pipeline grew 5% sequentially in Q4, BFS pipeline up 19% YoY, 76% of deals from proactive pursuits
items.quote: We are pleased with the pipeline growth outside of the top 10 accounts, which has grown by 10% year-over-year as well as 19% growth in our BFS pipeline. Our proactive deal pipeline is strong with about 76% of our deals from proactive pursuits.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue $410.7M, up 2.1% QoQ CC; FY24 revenue $1.61B, down 6.5% YoY CC; Direct revenue 95% of total
items.quote: Our Q4 FY24 revenue came in at USD410.7 million, a growth of 2.1% over previous quarter in constant currency terms. For the full year, we closed FY24 at revenues of $1.61 billion, a decline of 6.5% over previous year in constant currency terms. Direct business accounted for about 95% of our overall revenue in Q4 '24 and for the full year.

items.statement: Top 10 accounts declined 10.8% YoY LTM; Top 11-20 grew 10.5% YoY; Top 21-30 grew 17.3% YoY; New client acquisition revenue up 27%
items.quote: Our top 10 accounts declined 10.8% Y-o-Y on an LTM basis, mainly impacted by macro conditions, seasonality and the regional banking issues in the early part of the year. Our top 11 to 20 clients increased by 10.5% Y-o-Y, and 21 to 30 client segment grew by 17.3% Y-o-Y on an LTM basis. Our new client acquisition revenue continues to grow well, sustaining its strong growth trajectory at 27%.

items.statement: Emerging verticals (insurance, TMT, logistics, transportation) share increased from 49% to 52% of revenue; Canada revenue up 42% YoY in FY24
items.quote: The share of our emerging verticals such as insurance, TMT, logistics and transportation and others has increased from 49% to 52% of revenue. In Canada, we started with a set of financial services focused customers, and we now have a well-diversified clientele across verticals, and we recorded a 42% year-over-year increase in revenues in FY 24.

items.statement: Q4 growth led by BFS (+2.6% QoQ), TMT (+4.5% QoQ), Logistics (+2.2% QoQ); Others vertical up 21.6% YoY
items.quote: As guided in Q3 earnings call, growth was led by BFS and TMT. BFS was up 2.6% sequentially in Q4, and TMT and logistics were up by 4.5% and 2.2%, respectively, driven by client and deal wins in recent quarters. Similarly, our others vertical in direct is growing quite well as reflected in the 21.6% year-over-year growth in Q4 FY24.

items.statement: FY25 near-term growth expected from BFS and TMT; Logistics worst behind; Insurance and Travel showing decent traction
items.quote: On outlook by vertical, I think we mentioned in the last quarter call that at least for the short term, we expect growth to be driven by BFS and TMT. And I think that is still the case, at least in the very short run. We do think that the worst is behind us in the logistics business. Travel business already actually been growing well for us between airlines and railroads. And I think even insuranc

items.statement: Nearshore headcount increased 27% in Taiwan, Mexico, Poland, Costa Rica, Canada; Investing in AI, Salesforce capabilities and upskilling
items.quote: nearshore model and increased head count by 27% in regions such as Taiwan, Mexico, Poland, Costa Rica, Canada, etc. On technology, we made strategic choices to invest in capabilities and skills. In 2024, we were able to quickly acquire and rapidly integrate our AI, sales force and other capabilities with our tribes and archetypes and deliver a more well -rounded suite of services to our customers

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 55 per share for shareholder approval
items.quote: The Board of Mphasis also recommended a final dividend of INR55 per share to be placed before shareholders for approval.

items.statement: Acquired Silverline to expand Salesforce capabilities; Strategic partnerships with AWS, Google, Microsoft, Kore.ai, WorkFusion
items.quote: We also expanded our Salesforce capabilities with the acquisition of Silverline. We continue to diversify our revenue and pipeline beyond BFS and our top 10 clients. We've revitalized our leadership in core geos, verticals and technologies and have expanded our addressable market with new and enhanced capabilities.

items.statement: Launched Mphasis.ai business unit with Modernization and Developer Experience platforms; AI adoption framework to move beyond POCs; Gen AI foundry with AWS
items.quote: We have introduced two new platforms, as part of our Mphasis.ai business unit, Modernization and Developer Experience Acceleration. Recently, we have introduced an AI adoption framework, which enables our customers to move beyond POCs and adopt AI within the business.

items.statement: Mortgage segment stable but no volume pickup; Consumer lending stressed; Interest rate uncertainty persists; Capital markets recovery early stages
items.quote: The consumer lending segment is still a little bit stressed. The direct linkage of that to mortgage and auto loans. Both of those are either -- there's not enough volume or the delinquencies are higher. So those are actually a little bit of hot spots that we haven't yet found a full answer to.

items.statement: Indian IT growing faster than global SIs; Value migration to India-centric delivery continuing; AI adoption leveling playing field in production support and IT ops
items.quote: At this point, I do believe though that Indian IT is actually going to grow faster than global SIs. You can see that with some of the larger global SIs numbers and their forecast or consensus or guidance for '24, you'll still see that, that number is actually lower than the average of the Indian SI growth number.

items.statement: High single-digit DET revenue growth YoY in constant currency for FY25; EBIT margin expected at 16%
items.quote: We understand the challenges that are seen from the industry, and we are confident that we should be in a high single-digit DET revenue growth year-on-year in constant currency terms, and we expect the margins to be in the range of 16% for the financial year 25.

items.statement: Q4 order intake $227.8M, up 7.1% YoY; like-to-like down 6.2%; 9 large deals worth $197.6M
items.quote: We also have secured orders worth of $227.8 million in Q4, which is reported numbers at 7.1% year-on-year growth. Like -to-like, this is about minus 6.2%. And we also won about 9 large deals worth about $197.6 million in Q4.

items.statement: Full year order intake $902.2M, up 25.2% YoY; like-to-like up 15%; 28 large deals with $435.4M total contract potential
items.quote: For the full year order intake, we ended up at $902.2 billion, which has shown 25.2% year -on- year growth and a like-to-like basis, this is about 15% growth. And for the full year of fiscal 24, we have closed to 28 large deals with the total contract potent ial of about $43 5.4 million

items.statement: DET Q4 EBIT margin 16%, up 90 bps YoY; fourth consecutive quarter at 16%
items.quote: The Q4 FY24 DET EBIT margin stood at 16%, up by 90 bps year -on-year. And as you will notice, there is no normalization done in this quarter, in line with the commentary provided in the previous quarter.

items.statement: DET FY24 EBIT margin 16.1%, up 246 bps YoY; intend to maintain as platform for FY25 with focus on investing for growth
items.quote: The DET FY24 EBIT margin stood at 16.1%, up by 246 bps year-on-year. And as we discussed in detail in the previous earnings call and our Investor Day, the significant expansion was made possible due to the number of focused initiatives we executed through FY23 and FY24.

items.statement: 60% of key decision makers from top 40 customers see Cyient as strategic/advisory partner for 5-10 year transformation journey
items.quote: And we have also engaged some of our key decision makers and happy to share that 60% of our key decision makers, which is from top 40 customers who see Cyient as their strategic and advisory partner in their transformation journey that they are likely to take for the next 5 to 10 years.

items.statement: Sustainability grew 19.3% YoY, Transport 2.1% YoY; Connectivity and New Growth Areas declined YoY in Q4
items.quote: And if we translate into year-on-year, this translates into 1.8% growth, a strong growth delivered from sustainability vertical at 19.3% and transport grew by 2.1%, while connectivity and new growth areas have declined year-on-year.

items.statement: DET debt reduced from $94M to $54M; DE ratio improved from 0.24% to 0.12%; retired ~$40M debt in FY24; will continue debt retirement in FY25
items.quote: The DET DE ratio, which was 0.24% at the end of FY23 has now improved to 0.12% at the end of FY24. The DET debt position, which was $94 million at end of FY23, now stands at $54 million at the end FY24. This was made possible since we retired about $40 million of d ebt in FY24, and we have leveraged our focus on cash generation, which we talked about earlier to retire debt proactively.

items.statement: Final dividend INR18/share approved; full year dividend INR30/share, highest ever
items.quote: I'm also happy to announce a final dividend of INR18 per share which the Board has approved and will recommend to the shareholders for their approval. It's INR18 which brings the total to INR30 per share, which is the highest dividend that we have ever paid.

items.statement: Will sharpen focus on organic investments in technology to accelerate revenue growth and margin trajectory in FY25
items.quote: We're talking basically or ganic investment in technology that will accelerate our revenue growth and the margin trajectory. And this is what we've showcased also during the Investor Day as a part of the experience center visit that we have demonstrated.

items.statement: Headcount reduced in Q4 due to agile ramp-up alignment, unfilled attrition, performance management actions; expect growth trajectory in FY25
items.quote: Yes. So, I think we also looked at based on where the demand is, and we are trying to bring i n as close to th e agile ramp up as possible. Also, some of the attrition that we did not replace in Q4 and is the reason why you see headcount reduction and also, we have completed our performance management process as of Jan. And we also have taken some action on poor performers.

items.statement: Guidance assumes cautious pragmatism due to macro uncertainty; key variables: Aerospace supply catch-up and Connectivity Q1 revenue conversion; will update trajectory at end of Q2
items.quote: And therefore, thirdly, we've taken a cautious and pragmatic approach for the outlook, and we will go through this for Q1 and will come back at the end of Q2 and make an update to the trajectory as we see things progress.

items.statement: DET FCF INR232 crores in Q4, up 25.6% YoY, best ever quarter; FY24 FCF INR754 crores, up 71% YoY, best ever
items.quote: The DET FY24 free cash flow stood at INR754 crores, our best ever, a significant improvement of 71% year-on-year.

items.statement: Ranked leader in ER&D for North America and Europe by Zinnov Zones; debuted in data analytics and AI with leadership ranking
items.quote: We have also been ranked as a leader and a noteworthy player for the overall ER&D in North America and Europe by Zinnov Zones for ER&D services. We were recognized for our innovation and solution development in a range of industries, spanning aerospace, automotive, semiconductor and telehealth, among others. In a significant achievement, we also debuted in the data analytics and AI with a leadersh

items.statement: Medium to long-term growth prospects intact; ER&D spend, addressable market, partnership propensity, technology evolution drivers remain strong; expanding in Europe, Japan, Middle East
items.quote: No, we do feel that I think based on what we heard from our top 40 customers, and they are going through their own challenges, and they do see this is going to be a potential growth segment as we've envisaged earlier. I do feel that our medium - to long-term growth prospects are absolutely intact.

items.statement: Q1 softness expected; growth back-ended in FY25; will update trajectory at end of Q2
items.quote: We do expect some softness in the early part of the year, and it depends on how things pan out, and we should probably do well for the rest of the year. And that's the current view that we are carrying.

items.statement: Board approved new capital allocation policy to distribute at least 85% of free cash flow over five years via dividends or buybacks
items.quote: In the go forward policy, we have an endeavour to distribute at least 85% of our free cash flow generated over a period of five years to shareholders in the form of dividends or buyback.

items.statement: Targeting 15% EBIT margin by FY27
items.quote: From margin perspective, we have given a very clear ambition of reaching 15% EBIT by FY27.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration to be top three in peer group for EBIT profitability beyond FY27
items.quote: Our longer-term ambitions and our longer-term aspirations are more aggressive than what we have shared from an FY27 perspective. But we have to make a start. We have to make a start. And so therefore, this is what we feel the roadmap and the trajectory will be for the next three years.

items.statement: Focus on organic growth; not pursuing transformational M&A
items.quote: In a sense, yes. In a sense, the focus will very much be on organic growth. Never say no to really compelling opportunities. But we are not in the market for a transformational M&A at this time.

items.statement: Above-normal investment of ~1.5% of margin in next 12 months for long-term capability building, reducing to half thereafter
items.quote: It will be probably 1 .5% of our margin, given we are not doing any M&A. We are very clear that we want to make sure we take everything organically. So that's going to be the quantum, and then as we move forward and we start seeing the benefit, it will probably reduce to half of that and then get embedded over a period of time on FY27.

items.statement: Targeting $250 million average annual savings over three years, excluding incremental investments
items.quote: So this is average for the three years. It could be up, down each year, but that's outside of the investment. So, this is the saving that we'll drive and then fund some of the investments we'll deliver to be able to get the margins walk that period.

items.statement: FY25 margins expected to improve net of savings and 1.5% investment
items.quote: That's right. Yes, it is.

items.statement: FY25 is turnaround year; Q4 marks low point in YoY growth; expect YoY growth from Q1 FY25 and annual YoY growth by year-end
items.quote: We believe that Q4 marks the low point in our year-on-year growth journey, and that we will start turning around from Q1 onwards, and we expect to hit annual year-on-year growth by the end of the year.

items.statement: FY26: new service line structure and vertical focus to deliver growth results; early results from investments. FY27: full realization of investments and new structure
items.quote: By FY26, we expect that the new service line structure, the new vertical focus areas will start delivering results from a growth perspective, and that we will also start to see some early results from the investments that Rohit spoke about, and that the promise of these investments and the promise of the new structure will be fully realized in FY27.

items.statement: Consistent fresher hiring to rebuild pyramid; utilization dip in current quarter partly due to fresher additions
items.quote: In this quarter, in fact, you see a reduction in utilization. Some of that is attributable to, in fact, adding freshers. And as we go forward, we're going to be consistently applying that, because I think just focusing short term will not give us the right outcomes that we need, and this is an investment that's already baked in our plan.

items.statement: Pyramid correction and internal fulfillment to drive long-term margin improvement; benefit visible in 12-18 months
items.quote: I think that's going to be the maximum impact. And from a timeline perspective, that's going to take time, right? That's why I'm saying we invest in it right now, we start seeing the benefit probably I would say anywhere between 12 to 18 months onwards.

items.statement: Short-term margin levers: portfolio company integration, fixed-price program automation, pricing improvements
items.quote: We have significant opportunities as we look in our portfolio companies, as Mohit mentioned, we are going to integrate them. They're offering their frontend and backend more strongly with us. So that's a short term one for this year.

items.statement: Systematic program to grow top accounts; have billion-dollar-plus businesses in financial services, manufacturing, healthcare/life sciences; permission to hunt in top-tier clients
items.quote: We have a billion-dollar-plus business in financial services, we have a billion-dollar-plus business in manufacturing, we've got a sizable business in healthcare and life sciences across life sciences, payers, and providers, we've got an emerging business in retail, transportation, and hospitality.

items.statement: New deals signed are margin accretive on aggregate; initial 6-12 month dilution then expansion
items.quote: Yes. Rohit Anand: Yeah, from an aggregate perspective, that's true, Yogesh. And then as you look at any deal structure, the way the transition happens initially, the first 6 -8 months, 12 months, initially there's always a dilution and then the expansion happens after that

items.statement: Targeting improved cash conversion cycles; PAT to FCF alignment expected to be similar or higher over long term
items.quote: And in fact, the way we're going to target our improvement in the cash cycles, we feel that we can get some benefit out of that as well. They're quite aligned, actually.

items.statement: Billing rates comparable to peers; outsized fixed-price portfolio with some problem projects; pyramid restructuring may marginally lower billing rates but significantly lower cost
items.quote: I do feel that the billing rates by and large are comparable. But we do have an outsized fixed price portfolio within TechM. And obviously, within that, as is known, there are a couple of problem projects that we have.

items.statement: Plan built on market not falling off a cliff but not on incredible growth; expect to hit plan numbers even if current environment continues
items.quote: We obviously want to use this period of time, this slowness, to strengthen our capabilities and to build our institutional knowledge. So, I would say, the plan is built on the world not falling off a cliff, but it is not built on incredible growth, right? If the current market situation continues, I would still very much expect us to hit our plan numbers.

items.statement: New leadership hires: CHRO, Chief Marketing Officer, COO, Chief Learning Officer to build institutional capabilities
items.quote: Whether it's changing the capability from an HR perspective with our new CHRO, changing the capabilities from a marketing , advisor and analyst relationship perspective with Peeyush, changing the broader delivery capabilities through Atul, our new Chief Operating Officer, changing the capabilities from a learning perspective with the new Chief Learning Officer.

items.statement: Consolidated delivery under COO; 6 ADMS verticalized structure and 6 competency layers plus BPS for scale and execution
items.quote: And now when you look at the delivery, it's a consolidated organization. And we've kind of defined that under 6 ADMS verticalized structure and the 6 competency layers, and then the BPS additional to that.

items.statement: GenAI offering infusion percentage across clients tracked as key internal metric
items.quote: Mohit mentioned, we will share the percentage of clients where we are infusing GenAI offering; that's a very important lever that we're tracking internally.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration to reach 18-19%+ EBIT margin (top three peer group) beyond FY27
items.quote: Yes, that is absolutely the long-term aspiration, Ravi. There is no reason why this platform, with the strengths of the group, with a deep engineering heritage, with the sort of client base that we have, should not be delivering in the top three of the peer groups.

items.statement: No active divestment plan for acquired portfolio companies; focusing on deeper integration and synergies
items.quote: We have obviously worked to closely integrate all of the portfolio companies much more closely into our service line structure. And because we have said that we are not going to be hugely acquisitive anymore, it gives us the ability to drive synergies, including front -end integration and including back -end integration, a lot more effectively over time. But there is no active disposition plan at

items.statement: CME vertical contribution to decline as non-communications sectors grow faster; rebalancing ongoing for past five years
items.quote: But as we revert to, sort of, a mean of our peer group, that will mean faster growth in other sectors. And so, therefore, rebalancing of the portfolio with a lower overall weight for telecoms, it is something that has been happening in any case over the past five years. And I do expect the process to continue.

items.statement: Goodwill impairment review comprehensive; current performance reflects right representation; future projections expected to improve with integration
items.quote: No, I think, Sandeep, we've done a quite comprehensive review of the portfolio. So we feel that this is the current performance, this is the right representation of where we are.

items.statement: Peer group defined as top six or seven industry players for growth and margin benchmarking
items.quote: It is the top six or seven players in the industry. From margin perspective, we have given a very clear ambition of reaching 15% EBIT by FY27.

items.statement: Global leadership meet with 300 leaders held; organization has incredible energy and clarity on execution
items.quote: Like I'd shared at the start itself, we did a global leadership meet with close to 300 people just earlier this week in Bangalore. And all of you speak to people within the organization, right? There is incredible energy and there is incredible clarity in the organization about what needs to be done by each and every single person within the company.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at 25-30%, EBITDA margin 17-18%, net debt INR225-250 cr, capex INR250-300 cr, DI pipe production >4 lakh tons
items.value: 25-30% revenue growth, 17-18% EBITDA margin, net debt INR225-250 cr, capex INR250-300 cr, DI production >4 lakh tons
items.quote: For FY '25, we anticipate revenue growth in the region of 25% to 30%, EBITDA margins of around 17% to 18% and the net debt to be reduced to a range of around INR225 to INR250 crores. The capital expenditure is also expected to be in the range of INR300 to INR250 crores and we expect the ductile iron pipe production to exceed INR4 lakh tons.

items.statement: FY26 DI pipe production target 6 lakh tons, ferroalloy production 1.8-1.9 lakh tons
items.value: DI pipe 6 lakh tons, ferroalloy 1.8-1.9 lakh tons
items.quote: And in FY '26, we are looking to produce around 6 lakh tons. And as far as Ferroalloys are concerned, we are looking to produce around 1.5 lakh tons in the forthcoming year. With the capacity going up to 1.9 lakh tons, we expect to produce 1.9, 1.8 lakh tons in the FY '26.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin target 18-20% over next 4-5 years, sustainable even if steel prices fall 50%
items.quote: We've been repeating this continuously, is that we're looking at expanding our margins to 18% to 20% by the time the entire capex plan is completed over the next 15 to 18 months. So this is the guidance for the future. So this is the first part of your question. Coming to the second part of your question where you're asking, what will happen to the margins if the steel prices are to come down? See

items.statement: INR1000 cr capex plan, INR497 cr incurred, balance INR503 cr over next 15 months funded by internal accruals
items.value: INR497 cr incurred, INR503 cr balance
items.quote: you all on Page 2 o f 19 the capacity expansion and the capex plan of the company, we had earlier announced a capex plan of around INR1,000 crores and out of this, around INR497 crores has already been incurred and the balance INR503 crores is expected to be incurred in the next 15 months. All this capex is being done through internal accruals only

items.statement: DI pipe capacity expanded to 3 lakh tons from 2.4 lakh tons; 1.4 lakh tons (Phase 1 balance) and 2.2 lakh tons (Phase 2) to commission in FY25 and FY26; target 6.6 lakh tons
items.value: 3 lakh tons current, +1.4 lakh FY25, +2.2 lakh FY26, target 6.6 lakh tons
items.quote: Capacity of DI pipes has been expanded 3 lakh tons compared to 2.4 lakh tons last year. Furthermore, 1.4 lakh metric tons that is the balance of Phase 1 and 2.2 lakh metric tons that is Phase 2 is expected to be commissioned in FY '25 and FY '26 respectively. The capacity of ductile pipes will finally reach 6.6 lakh tons in the immediate future.

items.statement: Ferroalloy capacity increasing from 1.3 lakh to 1.66 lakh tons, balance 0.24 lakh tons by FY25; blast furnace capacity expanded to 6.3 lakh from 5 lakh tons, second blast furnace by next financial year; sinter capacity raised to 9 lakh tons
items.value: Ferroalloy 1.66 lakh tons, blast furnace 6.3 lakh tons, sinter 9 lakh tons
items.quote: The ferroalloy capacity is also being increased from 1.3 lakh tons to 1.66 lakh tons. The balance capacity of 0.24 lakh tons is expected to be commissioned by FY '25. In the blast furnaces, one of the blast furnaces has already been repaired and hence the capacity has expanded to 6.3 lakh tons up from 5 lakh tons of last year. The completion of the second blast furnace is anticipated by the next f

items.statement: DI pipe industry expected 13-15% CAGR driven by Jal Jeevan Mission and AMRUT; current 9-10% market share targeting 18-20% post expansion
items.quote: We expect that the DI pipe industry to go at 13% to 15% CAGR in the near future. The Jal Jeevan Mission and Mission Amrut Sarovar Infrastructure Development Plan which has been promoted by the government has led to an increased demand of these pipes and Jai Balaji is also contributing to the same. Currently we have around 9% to 10% of the DI pipe market share of India and our aim is to reach 18% t

items.statement: DI pipe margin 20-25%, specialised ferroalloy margin 25%; Q4 DI margin 22-25% vs Q3 20-21%; group EBITDA margin target 18-20%
items.quote: In terms of margin you asked, in percentages, in ductile pipes we have a margin of around 20% to 25% and in Ferroalloys, specialized Ferroalloys, we have a margin of around 25%. And this margin is expected to sustain? Yes, this margin is absolutely expected to sustain because as we, as I also mentioned, is that other than expanding the capacities, what we are also doing is that we are also underta

items.statement: Cost saving INR3000-4000 per ton on hot metal from blast furnace expansion, sinter plants, green power from waste gas
items.quote: In incremental what we are talking about is that on the metals produced entirely, we are looking at a cost saving of approximately INR3000 to INR4000 per ton on the hot material.

items.statement: Specialised ferroalloy buyers include JSW Steel, ArcelorMittal in India; automobile, aerospace, defense, oil drilling manufacturers in Japan, Europe, America; global buyer base in developed countries
items.quote: There are two parts to this question. Buyers are very varied in the world. There are some big buyers too. Like in India, there is JSW Steel, ArcelorMittal. These are big buyers. If we go to the world, then in Japan, there are automobile manufacturers. The founders of aerospace industry same for Europe and America. So the large steel players are also there. And other than that, there are very small

items.statement: Trade payables INR858 cr and other current liabilities INR264 cr high due to growth supported by creditors and buyers; expected to come down Q-on-Q; no bank credit facilities
items.quote: I would like to clarify that the trade payable number will also be coming down since the company does not have any bank credit facilities. The company is growing with the support of its creditors as well as the support of its buyers. So these numbers will be high right now. But on Q-on-Q basis, it will be coming down in the next quarter itself.

items.statement: Net debt reduced 54% to INR398 cr from INR871 cr in FY24; net debt/EBITDA 0.4x vs guidance 0.6x; targeting net debt free in 15 months; debt with Tata Capital only
items.value: INR398 cr net debt, 0.4x net debt/EBITDA
items.quote: In FY '24, the net debt decreased to INR398 crores from INR871 crores, marking a reduction of 54%. It's worth noting that our current net debt to EBITDA ratio stands only at 0.4 as of March 31, 2024, thus performing better than our guidance of maintaining 0.6 net debt EBITDA. This debt is associated with Tata Capital Limited and we are optimistic that within the next 15 months, we will achieve our

items.statement: FY24 revenue INR6414 cr (+5% YoY), EBITDA INR375 cr (+71% YoY), EBITDA margin 15% vs 9%, PAT INR880 cr (+1422% YoY), PAT margin 14% vs 1%
items.value: Revenue INR6414 cr, EBITDA INR375 cr, EBITDA margin 15%, PAT INR880 cr, PAT margin 14%
items.quote: Revenue for this year increased by 5% year over year to INR6414 crores and INR375 crores up 71% year over year. EBITDA margin also increased to 15% compared to 9% last year. PAT also showed a very significant increase of 1422% to INR880 crores compared to only INR58 crores earned last year. Similarly, PAT margin showed a jump from 1% in FY '23 '24 to 14% in FY '24.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue INR1846 cr (+7% YoY), adjusted EBITDA INR257 cr (-3% YoY due to provisions), PAT INR273 cr from loss, PAT margin 15% vs -1%
items.value: Revenue INR1846 cr, EBITDA INR257 cr, PAT INR273 cr, PAT margin 15%
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter increased to INR1846 crores up 7% year-over-year. The adjusted EBITDA showed a slight drop of 3% to INR257 crores year-over-year because of certain provisions taken in the books in this quarter only. The PAT increased significantly to INR273 crores up from losses reported in Q4 '23. The PAT margin also grew to 15% from minus 1% in Q4 '23.

items.statement: FY24 production: TMT 2.5 lakh tons (+18%), ferroalloy 1.2 lakh tons (+12%), DI pipe 2.4 lakh tons (+14%); sales: TMT 2.5 lakh tons (+22%), DI pipe 2.4 lakh tons (+14%)
items.value: TMT 2.5L tons, ferroalloy 1.2L tons, DI pipe 2.4L tons
items.quote: For FY '24 the production of TMT bars, ferroalloys and DI pipes showed an increase of 18%, 12% and 14% to 2.5 lakhs tons, 1.2 lakhs tons and 2.4 lakh tons respectively. items.statement: Management guides sustainable credit cost of 80 basis points
items.quote: The impairment cost, we believe, on a sustainable basis will be something like 80 basis points. So, that's what we are comfortable guiding ahead.

items.statement: Management guides AUM growth of 25% plus for FY25
items.quote: We believe that from where we are, we should be able to comfortably grow at a rate of 25% plus. And we will take advantage of any tailwinds that the environment affords us from time to time.

items.statement: Management guides cost-to-AUM improvement of 30-40 bps in FY25
items.quote: For the year gone by, we had a cost-to-AUM of 5.2%. We believe that in the coming year it should be better by between 30 basis points and 40 basis points.

items.statement: AUM grew 14% QoQ to Rs 12,191 crore in Q4 FY24
items.quote: We saw a strong AUM growth in the quarter, 14% increase over the quarter gone by. Our AUM closed at Rs. 12,191 crores. This is up from Rs. 10,748 crores at the end of Q3.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 17% QoQ to Rs 3,969 crore with 9.5 tons of gold
items.quote: The AUM there registered a 17% quarter-on-quarter increase. So, we closed our gold AUM at Rs. 3,969 crores, so that's 17% quarter-on-quarter and 33% year-on-year. The tonnage of our gold or the weight of gold that we have in our vaults is about 9.5 tons at this point in time.

items.statement: Off-book AUM increased to 18.7% from 17.4% driven by gold loan co-lending
items.quote: Our off-book AUM went up from 17.4% the previous quarter to 18.7%. Now, the kind of off-book that we did change in the quarter, this quarter's off-book was largely gold loan co-lending, and that went up from Rs. 176 crores at the end of Q3 to Rs. 522 crores at the end of Q4.

items.statement: Yields per product holding; NIM expected stable with potential upside from co-lending
items.quote: Our customer yields should stay at the current levels. Okay? The wisdom that we have received on the trajectory of interest rates is that the rate cuts will be more back-ended than front-ended during the course of the year, which is why we believe that our cost of borrowing will also stay sticky during the course of the year, which is why we believe that our spread will stay constant.

items.statement: Blended cost of funds increased 10-12 bps in Q3 due to RBI risk weight hike; incremental borrowing costs lower post rating upgrade
items.quote: In quarter three RBI had increased risk weights on bank lending to NBFCs. As a result of that, there has been a small increase in our cost of about 10 bps, 12 bps in terms of the blended cost of funds. But that being said, post our credit rating upgrade, we have been able to tie up incremental commitments at rates reasonably lower than the blended cost of funds.

items.statement: Plan to open 50 gold loan branches and 30 small mortgage locations in FY25
items.quote: In the coming years we want to open about 50 gold loan branches and 30 small mortgage locations. So, that is the plan for the year, and we will execute it, try and front-end that during the course of the year.

items.statement: Added 12 branches in Q4 FY24 taking total to 621
items.quote: We expanded our distribution further by adding 12 branches in the quarter, taking our total branch count to 621.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 1.66% from 2.2% QoQ; Rs 29.3 crore reduction including Rs 23.9 crore ARC sale
items.quote: We ended Q3 at about 2.2% GNPA and Q4 we closed at 1.66% GNPA. So, that's a reduction of 53 basis points over the quarter, or in absolute terms we reduced by about Rs. 29.3 crores. Now, this reduction of Rs. 29.3 crores was largely owing to the fact that we sold a large NPA account to an ARC that was worth Rs. 23.9 crores.

items.statement: Full year credit cost Rs 65.9 crore (ECL Rs 6.5 cr, write-offs Rs 73.6 cr, recoveries Rs 14.2 cr)
items.quote: For the entire year we have had an ECL impact of Rs. 6.5 crores, okay, write-offs of Rs. 73.6 crores, and a recovery of bad debts of Rs. 14.2 crores. So, the net of all these numbers is Rs. 65.9 crores, which is the total credit cost that we had over the course of the year.

items.statement: Q4 credit cost Rs 17.73 crore (write-offs Rs 28.86 cr, recoveries Rs 3.3 cr, ECL Rs 7.83 cr)
items.quote: The corresponding numbers for Q4 are write-offs of Rs. 28.86 crores, recoveries of Rs. 3.3 crores, and an ECL of Rs. 7.83 crores, giving us a net of Rs. 17.73 crores.

items.statement: Gold loan practices robust; regulatory issues raised in Feb-Mar already addressed pre-COVID
items.quote: All of what the regulator has said and which has been in the public domain in the months of Feb and March is really quite old hat for us, okay? And we are reasonably robust from that standpoint.

items.statement: Received rating upgrade to AA+ from CARE and India Ratings; CRISIL AA with positive outlook
items.quote: We have received a rating upgrade. We are rated AA+ by CARE and India Ratings, and CRISIL has assigned us a long-term credit rating of AA with a positive outlook.

items.statement: Zero commercial paper and zero short-term borrowing as of March end

items.quote: Finally, the ROA for FY'24 is 2.4%, ROE is 13.5%. The corresponding numbers for Q4 are 2.5% and 12.2%, respectively.

items.statement: Global uncertainties to continue causing crude/product price volatility; focus on efficient, safe, reliable, environmentally responsible operations

items.statement: Domestic volumes grew 15.5% YoY in Q4 and 7.5% for full FY24

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA per tonne considered sustainable at current levels

items.statement: Mass ABS margins expected better than polystyrene if demand is good

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with investable surplus of Rs 1080 crores at March 2024

items.statement: Employee cost up 16-17% due to manpower increase for new verticals and wage revisions
items.quote: No, see we are expanding, we have to also now increase our manpower for the new verticals, for the expanded capacities. So, the number of manpower have gone up and of course, there is a general increase in the wages.

items.statement: ABS market growing at 8-10% historically; may improve with EV and appliance growth
items.quote: Typically the market has been growing around same 8% to 10% and going forward with the growth in the EVs and the appliances it may improve.

items.statement: Chinese ABS overcapacity may shift supply chains; old plants may close but timing uncertain
items.quote: On the ABS side, yes supply chain would change in the sense that the countries who are supplying to China, they would have to look at other markets, they may look at the Western market, some of the old plants may get mothballed.

items.statement: Mass ABS Phase 1 expected 50% utilisation in first year (FY26)

items.statement: EPS Phase 2 and Masterbatch compounds expansion completing in FY25; benefits from FY26
items.quote: EPS phase two is getting fully implemented this year and the compounds part of that is getting implemented this year. And the benefit of that would occur to us only in the next financial year.

items.quote: So, the order book looks promising at this point of time. We plan to maintain the average through the year.

items.quote: Our short-term debt of course which has gone up by a lot, we expected to be moderated by at least to come down to from INR450 crores to INR100 crores in next three to four months.
