items.quote: We've gone and said it again as well, even after becoming SFB for the first couple of years, our payments revenues will grow as we've seen the current kind of growth which is coming across. So we are looking at a 75-25 split, where assets will become only one of the products in addition to everything else which we have still 75% of our income, we are expecting to come from the growth of payment bu

items.statement: FinoPay app launched on iOS; web and internet banking going live this quarter; women digital account recently launched
items.quote: I'm further delighted to share that our FinoPay app is now available on Apple store for our iOS users, which also enhances our target customer segment and lays foundation for digital cross-sell opportunities.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guided at ~30%, PAT margin at 18-20%
items.quote: Full year, we feel taking 30% will be safer, not 33% because somewhere some risk could come. We feel 30% EBITDA margin would be safer. But another thing is on the PAT margin generally we were saying 20%. But now even in the Middle East, Dubai also taxation has come, other countries also taxation is coming. We feel that on the whole the PAT margin can be 18% to 20% instead of taking 20%.

items.statement: Expect 25-30% revenue growth in coming years based on order book and historical performance
items.quote: So, that's why we think that ma ybe we may be able to do almost a 25% to 30% growth in revenue in the coming years based on this for our historical performance

items.statement: Opening order book for FY25 at Rs 148.6 crore for enterprise solutions, split 74% cybersecurity, 26% paperless
items.quote: Order book, based on product that's what we fell that the solution order book is the Rs. 148.6 crores. On that number of larger orders are now towards the cyber security and we have also given split somewhere that the cyber security is 74% and the paperless transformation is 26%.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 35.2% driven by Trust Services pricing uptick and lower hardware mix
items.quote: The margin I will explain then I will request Arvind to explain about the international positioning and marketing. On the margin, if you see this quarter alone, the margin increased because of the good jump in the Trust Services business and also lower hardware composition in the overall sales.

items.statement: Trust Services channel pricing increased 2.5x in Sep 2023; retail pricing unchanged; new CCA guidelines from Jul 2024 mandate direct-to-retail sales
items.quote: Pleasant surprise is because around September end, we increased the price by 2.5X. So, until March to September the price was very low. Then we increased the price. Then the others also because there could not be any alignment. So, we increased unilaterally.

items.statement: CCA new guidelines from July 1, 2024: no stock sale to partners, only direct retail sales with partner commission
items.quote: The thing what is happening is now the CCA has issued new guidelines that starting from July 1st of this year, we cannot sell any stock to any of the partners. Every sale has to be made individually to the retail people, but the partners can introduce and get the commission.

items.statement: Strong demand in India (government projects), Middle East, Africa (Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Uganda, Ethiopia); US traction via POCs; Europe and Philippines slower
items.quote: Now key geographies, the demand is very good from India because there are several large government projects going on. So, the trade demand is good. In the Middle East also demand is good. In Africa we expect a lot of order coming in the coming year because as I said a lot of discussions are going on in Tanzania, Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda and also in Ethiopia.

items.statement: QIP proceeds: Rs 80 crore reserved for acquisitions, Rs 43 crore for three new products (homomorphic encryption, mobile PKI, post-quantum crypto), Rs 10-12 crore spent so far
items.quote: On the QIP still lot of money is yet to be spent. Almost Rs. 80 crores is reserved for the acquisition. So, we are evaluating it is yet to be spent. Similarly on the prod uct Rs. 43 crores of three new products are there which is at homomorphic encryption, mobile PKI and post quantum cryptography. On that we have hardly spent some Rs. 10-12

items.statement: DSO ~94 days in Q4 FY24; target 85-90 days in FY25 via hardware unbundling in government contracts
items.quote: Our sundry debtors and receivable days almost remained same. So, even last quarter in September also same almost 94-95 days and similarly now also around 94 days, so, it has not increased. In the coming year we feel it should little bit come down because of unbundling all the hardware in all the government business.

items.statement: Enterprise solutions revenue Rs 2,687 crore (64% YoY); Trust Services Rs 1,444 crore (23% YoY); Solutions ~Rs 200 crore, Services ~Rs 68 crore (incl. Ikon)
items.quote: There was a rise in the enterprise solutions segment which generated a revenue of Rs. 2,687 million reflecting a year-on-year growth of 64.1%. While the Trust Services revenue grew by 22.8% YoY to Rs. 1,444 million.

items.statement: Key wins: national PKI for African country, managed PKI for large IT outsourcer, emSigner for US mid-size tech firm, private PKI for US mid-size IT firm, BFSI clients in India, MCA platform for Defence wing, PKI for Indonesian corporate, MC
items.quote: during the year key project wins partnered with a large IT outsourcing for the use of our managed PKI platform with SSL TLS certificate. This will en able securing website devices and enterprise IT infrastructure, rollout of national PKI infrastruc ture for a country in A frica to build digital signature infrastructure

items.statement: Ikon acquisition successful, enabling cross-sell/upsell; services business from Ikon ~Rs 68 crore in FY24
items.quote: The acquisition of Ikon has been successful, enabling us to leverage cross selling and upselling opportunities across both Ikon and eMudhra's offering to our client base.

items.statement: Hiring senior sales leaders in Europe, Philippines to build momentum; digital marketing automation and brand partnerships (e.g., Thales in Middle East)
items.quote: So, that's where we are trying to see how we can put a senior person who can get into the European market and improve. So, as of now if you see Europe is still not caught up to the level of Middle East and the US. Similarly, Indonesia also a lot of new things are emerging. But Philippines another area where we have put the senior person and then see how we can go to Philippines.

items.statement: Services business gross margin ~40% vs software ~80-85%; services contracts typically 1-3 years; services revenue expected to grow ~20-25%
items.quote: Gross margin because the product business, the gross margin is almost if you don't do hardware, it will be even 80%-85%. But in the services business the gross margin could be around 40% or something like that.

items.statement: New CCA direct-to-retail model from Jul 2024 may affect volumes and partner ecosystem; Europe and Philippines markets not yet scaled
items.quote: But on the whole the net realization what we receive as of now, I don't think it will come now. Only thing is because we have to directly reach the retail instead of through the partner, what will be the role of the partner, how many partners will be in business, how many men are in business, because of that would there be any effect on the volume of signature to be sold?

items.statement: International expansion focus: North America (advanced digital adoption), Middle East & Africa (e-governance, zero trust); Europe and Philippines early stage
items.quote: Our focus has been on establishing a strong market presence directly in regions like North America which have advanced digital technology adoption and the Middle East and Africa where there is a strong e-governance agenda centered on digital transformation and cybersecurity with zero trust transition.

items.statement: R&D underway in post-quantum cryptography, fully homomorphic encryption, mobile PKI; emSigner listed on AWS and Azure Marketplace; certified for SAP SuccessFactors
items.quote: Our R&D efforts are focused on reimagining security in the context of quantum computers, edge computing and data privacy. In line with this we have already embarked on R&D in post quantum cryptography, fully homomorphic encryption and mobile PKI.

items.statement: Cash balance ~Rs 250 crore post-QIP; comfortable with cash position given accruals and planned spend
items.quote: Yes, Rs. 250 crores is there. On that if you see some of these are based on the QIP thing. On the QIP still lot of money is yet to be spent. Almost Rs. 80 crores is reserved for the acquisition. So, we are evaluating it is yet to be spent.

items.statement: Reiterated 5-7% QoQ AUM growth, 50 bps cost-to-AUM reduction over two years, credit cost 80-100 bps, target 15% ROE by FY26
items.quote: We reiterate our guidance for 5% to 7% quarter-on-quarter growth, reduction of cost by 50 bps and credit costs in the range of 80 to 100 bps.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 yield 17.62%, spread 8.31%; full year yield 17.08%, spread 7.7%; QoQ borrowing cost down 8 bps, YoY up 37 bps
items.quote: Our yields on the loans are at 17.08% for the full year and 17.62% for the Q4 FY24. The spread for the full year FY24 is 7.7% and for the quarter is 8.31%.

items.statement: AUM grew 38% YoY, 9% QoQ to Rs 6,822 cr; MSME AUM grew 46% YoY, 9% QoQ to Rs 5,704 cr; co-origination 18.5% of borrowings
items.quote: Our AUM grew by 38% of Y-o-Y basis and 9% on Q-o-Q basis. Our AUM stands at Rs. 6,822 crores as of 31st March 24. Our MSME AUM grew 46% on a Y-o-Y basis and 9% on Q-o-Q basis to Rs. 5,704 crores.

items.statement: Added 31 branches in FY24 vs 17 in FY23; 6 branches added in Q4; branch expansion driving employee additions
items.quote: We added 31 branches against 17 last year and our business grew by 38% year-on-year.

items.statement: GNPA stable at 2.43%; PCR improved to 44.74% from 39%; credit cost steady at 80 bps; Stage-2 MSME stable ~3.2%, gold Stage-2 up slightly
items.quote: Our GNPA is stable, and range bound. It is at 2.43% as of 31st March 24. Our credit cost is steady at 0.8% for the year. Our PCR is increased further to 44.74%.

items.statement: MSME yield 16.75-17%, gold yield ~18%; co-origination reclassification added 45 bps to yield; sustainable yield ~17.2%
items.quote: In terms of the yields, we are now closer to 18% odd and in terms of the MSME, we are in the range of 16.75% to 17% odd.

items.statement: 85% of secured MSME customers are first-time property borrowers; top-up loans ~15% of portfolio; gold loan repeat rate 30-35%
items.quote: almost 85% of our customers who we disburse are of that category. So, we don’t take over those set of customers. We would tend to take over some of the customers, which would be in the ra nge of between 10 % and 15% odd

items.statement: RBI guiding lower system growth, NIM pressure from deposit competition, repo rate likely steady; MFI rate cap not expected to impact SBFC
items.quote: The regulator has been guiding a lower growth and eventually the industry always moves to what is regulatory guidance. So, we will see a slowdown of loan across the system next year in my opinion.

items.statement: Key risks: regulatory-driven growth slowdown, NIM compression from liability competition, credit cost normalization; internal risks from credit judgment and growth pace
items.quote: 3 clear headwinds for the industry and for us as well protecting NIMs, ensuring growth and ensuring the credit cost is under control.

items.statement: Added ~220 employees in Q4, mostly branch and collections staff; 14-15 people per branch; hired 400 fresh graduates from disadvantaged backgrounds
items.quote: We have continuously been investing in infrastructure, so what you are saying is right, the number of branch has been continuously going up at a slow and steady pace.

items.statement: ROA 4.14% FY24, 4.56% Q4; ROE 11.28% FY24, 11.9% Q4; capital adequacy 40.5%; debt-to-equity 1.6x; OPEX 5.34% FY24, 5.01% Q4
items.quote: Our return on average AUM for the full year is 4.14% and for the quarter is 4.56%. Our return on average tangible equity for the full year is 11.28% and for the quarter is 11.9%.

items.statement: Rating upgraded to AA- by India Ratings; raised NCDs from mutual funds; added foreign banks; planning to add DIIs to lender base
items.quote: Post our rating upgrade by India rating to AA-. We have diversified further and have raised money under NCDs from mutual funds and have added the couple of foreign banks as well.

items.statement: ALM: weighted average asset tenure ~4.5 years; no short-term borrowing; no ALM mismatch in any bucket; liquidity buffer maintained
items.quote: In a way the weighted average on the asset side comes to roughly about 4.5 years, but on the liability side, you are right, liability in the market is not available for so long.

items.statement: Small ticket MSME customers not price-sensitive; first-time borrowers; pricing based on business IRR; some pricing power but cautious
items.quote: These set of customers are not so price sensitive, and you are able to price what is reasonable and we also want to ensure that the IRR of the business should be sufficient to price it.

items.statement: Cost of funds contained via diversification: NCDs, co-origination, FCNR, foreign banks; bank MCLR leakage expected to continue
items.quote: Bank MCLRs will continue to leak into our cost of funds and NIMs will be a challenge that all of us will have to address.

items.statement: Target 20% market share by FY28 from current 14%+
items.quote: Adani Cement's current market share is about 14% plus with an internal target to hit 20% by FY28.

items.statement: Grinding capacity to double to 140 mt by FY28 via 35 new units; 4 mt clinker at Bhatapara and 4 mt at Maratha by Q4 FY25 and Q2 FY26 respectively
items.quote: For doubling the capacity of grinding facilities to 140 million tons by FY28, we are targeting 35 new grinding units.

items.statement: Growth capex of INR 5,000-6,000 crore for FY25; total capex including efficiency and green energy around INR 7,500 crore funded from internal accruals
items.quote: I would say our total capex would be for growth alone, if you're asking, would be in the range of about INR5,000 crores to INR6,000 crores. Purely growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 3.5% YoY to 19.1% in Q4 FY24; FY24 margin up 7.4% to 19.3%
items.quote: With the improvements mentioned on the revenue and cost front, the EBITDA grew by 37% at INR1,699 crores. EBITDA per ton grew by 17% at INR1,026 and the margin expanded by 3.5% to 19.1%.

items.statement: Target INR 530/ton cost reduction by FY28 from FY24 base of INR 4,170/ton; 40% from logistics, 55-60% from manufacturing
items.quote: We have already targeted to achieve almost INR530 a ton further reduction for which we are investing and target to achieve by FY'28.

items.statement: Won 3 coal mines (Gare Palma, Dahegaon Gowari, Lama Tola) covering 50% of current requirement; target 80-90% captive coal in 12 months
items.quote: Besides this, within the group, we are also working on other options and I believe with that, in the next 12 months’ time, we should be able to secure 80% to 90% of our coal through our own Ambuja captive sources

items.statement: Expect cement demand to grow 8-9% annually, outpacing capacity additions; GDP at 7% and cement multiplier 1.2-1.3x
items.quote: We expect higher utilisation over the next five years since demand is expected to grow at a rate of 8% to 9% faster than the capacity expansion rate.

items.statement: Blended cement at 86% of sales; premium products at 24% of trade sales, targeting higher share
items.quote: Blended cement as a mix of total sales maintained at 86%, premium products as a percentage of trade sales increased to 24%.

items.statement: Direct dispatch to customers maintained at 54%; secondary lead distance reduced 4 km to 48 km
items.quote: The transportation cost declined by 8% at INR1,280 per ton on account of footprint optimization, secondary lead distance reduced by 4 km to 48, the direct dispatch to customers has been maintained at 54%.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; promoters infused INR 8,339 crore via warrants in April 2024, total INR 20,000 crore; cash at INR 24,338 crore
items.quote: We will continue to r emain debt free. 4 million tons of clinkering and 4.8 million tons of cement capacity is expected to commence by Q4 FY25. The promoters have fully subscribed to the warrants program in the company by further infusing INR8,339 crores in April 24, thereby i nfusing a total amount of INR20,000 crores

items.statement: EBITDA per ton at INR 1,026 in Q4 FY24, up 17% YoY; FY24 EBITDA per ton INR 1,081, up 60%
items.quote: EBITDA per ton grew by 17% at INR1,026 and the margin expanded by 3.5% to 19.1%.

items.statement: Master Supply Agreement volume at 3.4 mt vs 2.4 mt YoY, up 42%; Sanghi to Ambuja 4.2 lakh tons, Sanghi to ACC 2.5 lakh tons in Q4
items.quote: The Master Supply Agreement volume stood at 3.4 million tons against 2.4 million tons, an increase of 42%.

items.quote: Three locations, one in West, one in North and one in South, 4 million, 3 kilns we are ready to place orders as soon as we have the EC. And this is not so far in distant future. I'm talking of only a quarter or two at the most.

items.statement: Sea freight share targeted at ~10% in 24 months via Sanghi jetty draft improvement to 4.5m and larger vessels
items.quote: We have a ballpark. I think sea freight we can expect around say 10% by next after 24 months.

items.quote: Sanghi already has been rated now AA. The rating has been upgraded from D to AA. And the journey is to become AAA for Sanghi as well like Ambuja and ACC.

items.statement: Increasing technical and field force; over 1 lakh channel partners; renewed brand focus
items.quote: We are investing more in the brands, and you would see that the renewed focus and thrust. We are increasing our technical and field force.

items.statement: Pricing may face pressure if sentiment weakens pre-elections; but expect stable to improving prices post-elections with 8-9% demand growth
items.quote: But yes as more capacity comes in and if the sentiment is a little down it can have an impact on pricing. I believe this is going to get improved because I think post elections we'll see a much more robust program.

items.statement: WHRS capacity target 186 MW by March 2025 (currently 134 MW); 1,000 MW RE by FY26 to meet 60% power needs; power cost to drop from INR 6.75 to INR 4.50/unit
items.quote: Our waste heat recovery capacity at the time of takeover was 40 MW in September '22, which we are now targeting to increase to 186 MW by March '25. Currently, the WHRS capacity is at 134 MW.

items.statement: Acquired 1.5 mt Tuticorin grinding unit in April 2024; Sanghi integration via MSA; 142 mt limestone reserves secured in Q4 FY24
items.quote: In April 24, Ambuja Cement successfully completed the acquisition of state-of-the-art 1.5 million ton grinding unit at Tuticorin in Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: Promoters increased stake by 3.6% to 70.3% via warrant subscription of INR 8,339 crore in April 2024
items.quote: Promoters have further increased their stake in the company by 3.6% to 70.3%.

items.statement: Focus on lowest cost producer status via Adani DNA; premium brand positioning (A/A+ pricing) insulates from commodity wars
items.quote: That's also the Adani DNA. You look at any of our Adani companies in each of the sector we are the lowest cost and highest productivity. And thereby it also renders us highest EBITDA.

items.quote: Our target is to reach almost 76 million tons of clinker by end of FY28 sorry 82 million tons of clinker when I look at 140 million tons.

items.quote: Kill-in-fuel cost by 17% to INR1.84 from INR2.21 per 1000 kcal.

items.quote: In April 24, Ambuja Cement successfully completed the acquisition of state-of-the-art 1.5 million ton grinding unit at Tuticorin in Tamil Nadu.

items.quote: What I have refrained from saying is till I have the EC in my hand, I generally don't speak about kiln lines.

items.quote: I think as a management team, we are one team which is running the show. So therefore, in terms of sharpness, focus, timelines from the time we make a decision to execution, I think there is no bureaucracy.

items.statement: Sanghi EBITDA margin ~9% under MSA; Q4 20.5% due to one-offs (discount write-back INR 33 cr, lower fuel/fixed cost)
items.quote: It is approximate 9% EBITDA margin for Sanghi.

items.quote: We have a ballpark. I think sea freight we can expect around say 10% by next after 24 months.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated revenue INR 33,160 cr (+7%), EBITDA INR 6,400 cr (+73%), PAT INR 4,738 cr (highest ever); net worth ~INR 51,000 cr
items.quote: In FY24, Ambuja and ACC both achieved all time highest annualized PAT.

items.statement: Cost reduction roadmap: from INR 5,300/ton (Sep'22) to INR 4,170/ton (Q4 FY24) to INR 3,640/ton (FY28 target); 20% achieved, 12.5% more targeted
items.quote: And this journey from INR 4170 to 3,640, INR 530 is a 12.5%. Whatever the idea which Ajayji has given 12.5% is strongly believed we will be able to reach another reduction.

items.statement: Sanghi clinker target 5 mt FY25 (0.7 mt Q4); kilns at 17,500 TPD H2; Tuticorin grinding 1.5 mt; Dahej grinding; South expansion via multiple grinding stations
items.quote: So, Navin, let me first handle the game plan for Sanghi. Sanghi has a great location. That's the reason we invested in that asset.

items.statement: ESG: Net zero 2050 (SBTi validated); 11x water positive Ambuja; 8x plastic negative; 21 mt waste derived resources FY24; 8.3 mn trees by 2030; 4.6 mn societal beneficiaries

items.statement: ROA expansion guided at 4-5 bps per year; FY25 ROA expected to continue expanding from FY24's 1.32%

We are now correcting for the one -off. It would have been a strong quarter, but full year was 1.32 in ROA, previous year at about 1.28. I see that expansion continuing into FY '25 and beyond.

items.statement: Fee income growth guided at 20-25% YoY for FY25
items.quote: On fee income, I think, it's -- no, I don't believe you can sort of sequentially plot it and say this will grow at. But a Y -on-Y basis, anything between 20%, 25% is very much on the cards, and we believe FY '25 will also see that kind of momentum.

items.statement: Credit cost guided around 30 bps for FY25 vs 23 bps in FY24
items.quote: I've said that, that is low, but I'm happy that low may not dramatically alter and shift up. But yes you could argue that somewhere around 30 basis points is what we would push and try to deliver in FY '25, but that's the run rate.

items.statement: NII growth expected in similar zone as FY24's 15% with slight improvement
items.quote: This year, we grew 15, our credit grew 20 . We would like to be better on both counts, but we just have to work through this cost of funds challenge. But yes, in that zone.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected back to ~50% in FY25 and improving thereafter
items.quote: We were looking to be -- last year was 49 and change. We were looking to be in that 49 or better, but some of these costs have come and impacted us. So I think FY'25 should be back to about 50-odd percent and then improving from there.

items.statement: NIM expected to expand 2-3 bps in FY25
items.quote: I thought I mentioned at the earlier part of the call, we think that 320 should inject about 2 -3 basis points in this financial year

Not driven by the aircraft at this point in time, but driven by increasing our CapExs into lease CapExs, and also driven by any of the

items.statement: Target PBT margin improvement of 2-5 percentage points from current 7.5-8% range over next nine months with better capacity utilization
items.quote: We would like to continue with our current range and to improve plus another 2% to 5% on that part, assuming that we would have a better utilization of our facility.

items.statement: Surface business is priority for future CapEx investment to improve ground infrastructure competitiveness
items.quote: Surface would be the priority. To be competitive on the ground as well, our outlook is to invest more into the surface business and get our infrastructure ready there.

items.statement: Management optimistic on domestic demand outlook citing GST collections and GDP growth predictions
items.quote: See. we expect, as we mentioned that we expect to improve our EBIT margins further from what we have currently. That in itself indicates that, yes, we show optimism in terms of the external demand, domestic demand that would be there in the country. And you have seen how the GST collections have improved, how the outlook about India overall, India's GDP growth is being predicted and there is a lot

items.statement: Price increase applied across all products including documents; document business grew better than budgeted expectations
items.quote: had aimed for a price increase across all our products which is documents and even in outliers and all of our product, Anshul, there. And in this segment also there has been a price increase accordingly. And though I would say that the large was into our B28 business rather than into the document business. however, we did have the decent higher price rises even into this document business. And wha

items.statement: Surface business growth outlook similar to current trends, no significant change expected
items.quote: Yes, I think similar levels. We do not see any significant change in the trend as such.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue growth guidance of 17%-20% with FY24 as new base
items.quote: Looking ahead, I would also like to reaffirm our revenue growth guidance. As previously stated, we expect to achieve a growth rate of 17%-20% in the medium term. However, we now use FY24 as our new base here for these projections.

items.statement: Pentonic portfolio contribution expected to cross 50% of revenue in 2-3 years
items.quote: So, currently, as I mentioned that Pentonic, portfolio contributes about 34% to our overall revenue and going forward definitely in another 2-3 years' time it will easily cross 50% contribution.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to reach 35%-36% in next 2-3 years, up ~5% from current 31%
items.quote: Gross margin will not have that substantial impact because of Pentonic. The reason is that we have got Deli range also where it's a purely trading product and margins are not that significant and we have got aggressive targets for Deli. So, we expect the margin to go up by say around 5%. So, maybe around 35%-36% over the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 11.1% in FY24, down 150 bps from FY23 due to 13% overhead increase vs 4% revenue growth
items.quote: FY24 EBITDA margin at 11.1% underwent a reduction of 1 50 BPS from FY23 levels. This contraction stemmed from an increase of over 13% in overhead expenses as compared with 4% growth in revenue.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 gross margin 32.5%, up 103 bps QoQ but down 178 bps YoY due to Gujarat minimum wage hike
items.quote: Q4 FY24 Gross Profit stood at 46 crores and the margin stood at 32.5%. The margin increased by 103 BPS over the previous quarter but fell by 178 BPS as compared to Q4 FY23. This fall was on account of rise in minimum wages in Gujarat leading to higher labor costs.

items.statement: Industry volume growth estimated at 4-6%, value growth higher due to premiumization
items.quote: I think that in terms of volume, the growth rate is going to be around 5% or anything between 4-6%. But definitely, with the premiumization, it is possible to achieve a higher growth in terms of value.

items.statement: Pentonic grew 21% in value in FY24, contributing 34% of revenue; Q4 saw 32% QoQ and 30% YoY growth
items.quote: Over the course of the year, the Pentonic range grew by over 21% in value and contributed approximately 34% to our total revenue. The final quarter saw even more impressive growth with a 32% increase quarter-on-quarter and a 30% rise year-on-year.

items.statement: Legacy product volumes declined due to strategic shift to premium; management now committed to protecting legacy volumes
items.quote: While our Pentonic portfolio has seen remarkable growth, we reckonize that some of our legacy products experienced a decline in volume. This was partly due to a strategic shift towards higher margin products. However, it is crucial to maintain a balanced approach to our product offerings to sustain our overall Market Share.

items.statement: Kolkata facility expansion: ₹35 crore for infrastructure in FY25, plus ₹10 crore routine capex, funded from internal accruals
items.quote: So, next year we will invest in plant and machinery to increase our capacities. - But for the time being the growth plans which we have for this year, we already have capacities lined up, both inhouse capacity as well as from outsourcing. So, yeah, right now for this year the CapEx is going to be 35 crores for the infrastructure of Kolkata facility and one other 10 crores for our regular… - Mr. N.

items.statement: Gujarat land expansion deferred by 1-2 years to prioritize Kolkata modernization
items.quote: In line w ith our strategic priorities , we have decided to defer the land expansion at our Gujarat facility by approximately 1-2 years. This decision allow us to focus on modernizing and enhancing our facilities in Kolkata first.

items.statement: Mold capacity: ~60 million/month each for Pentonic and Linc (highly underutilized); molding capacity fungible at ~100 million/year split 50-50 in-house/outsourced
items.quote: Today... I am talking of purely mold capacity because the molding capacity is quite fungible and flexible. So, in terms of mold c apacity for Pentonic portfolio, we can produce about 60 million per month, which is highly underutilized, let me clarify that. And insofar as Linc is concerned, we have a capacity of almost 50 to 60 million again.

items.statement: Kenya subsidiary current annual revenue ~₹14-15 crore; targeting multiplier growth via COMESA treaty access to 350M population in East Africa
items.quote: And just to give you a number, our existing revenue from Kenya subsidiary is on an annualized basis. It is about 14 to 15 crores in terms of Indian rupees. So that's the current annual revenue.

items.statement: North America distributor appointed; expecting multiplier growth over 3-5 years for Pentonic brand across US, Canada, Mexico
items.quote: So, for North America like we appointed a national distributor just last year. So, we are expecting, I would say, a multiplier growth over a period of next 3-5 years from where we are today. And this is purely our own brand, Pentonic brand, business that we're talking about and not any private label for any chain stores in U.S.

items.statement: Net debt negative ₹8 crore as of March 31, 2024 (net cash position)
items.quote: The company consistently utilized its free cashflow pr udently resulting in substantial redu ction of its Net Debt over the past five years. Net Debt stood at -8 crores as on 31st March, 2024.

items.statement: Dividend of ₹5 per share announced (~22% payout), pending AGM approval
items.quote: Finally, I'm pleased to inf orm that our Board of Directors have announced a dividend of ₹5 per share maintaining our commitment to rewarding our shareholders. This represents a payout of about 22% pending approval at our upcoming AGM.

items.statement: Corporate sales erratic, jumped to 18% in Q4 FY24 from ~5% normally; long-term range 5-10%
items.quote: So, Jainam, the corporate sales, let me clarify, is quite erratic. Because, in some, let's say, a corporate decides to have some cross-promotion program for their products, and we grab the order. So, a single corporate order Q4 FY24 & FY 24 Earnings Webinar 16 can be in the range of a few crores of rupees. But it is not cert ain that we can get such orders every year. We've been fortunate this yea

items.statement: Market share stable across industry; low entry barriers but differentiated Pentonic portfolio provides competitive moat
items.quote: Well, as per the feedback which we have in the last year, more or less, all the companies are maintai ning their market share. So, there has not been a real shift as such.

items.statement: Gujarat minimum wage hike ~30% (deferred 3 years) hit FY24 margins; no similar increase expected going forward
items.quote: As we mentioned in our opening remarks, this year the margin was affected by a wage hike in Gujarat, a minimum wage hike in Gujarat. This wage hike was deferred for about 3 years for the COVID-19 period. So suddenly, there was a sudden increase of around 30% in the minimum wages. So going forward, we don't expect this kind of increase in the minimum wages.

items.statement: Average realization per pen: FY24 ₹5.67 overall, Pentonic ₹5.83; management expects similar momentum, could reach Pentonic level in 2-3 years
items.quote: Yeah. I think definitely.

items.statement: Management not happy with FY24 numbers but optimistic on FY25 due to new product lineup
items.quote: Let me be very frank, that we are not really very hap py with the numbers of FY24. Although we are disappointed by the numbers, but definitely we are quite excited and optimistic because we know the lineup of new products which we have. And so, yes, we are looking for a good FY25.

items.statement: New launches: Pentonic GRT at ₹40 launched Q4; Pentonic CLR Ball Pen at ₹20 and Pentonic Evo Gel Pen at ₹30 upcoming; 3+ products in H1 FY25
items.quote: This year we've also been excited to introduce several new products including the Pentonic GRT at ₹40 which was launched in Q 4 finally and the rollout of some new variants in the Pentonic brand portfolio. Although the response to some of these variants was mixed, we are optimistic about the upcoming launch of the Pentonic CLR Ball Pen at ₹20 and the Pentonic Evo Gel Pen at ₹30. Our commitment to

items.statement: Entering adjacent categories: children's markers, permanent markers, highlighters, crayons, modeling dough; initially outsourced
items.quote: The second driver is going to be the adjacent categories, as I mentioned, that right now we Q4 FY24 & FY 24 Earnings Webinar 10 are largely in the popular category like ball pen and gel pens but we are absent in categories like children's markers, permanent markers, highlighters, and some such adjacent categories. So , which we are going to launch in the first half itself, which I did not mention

items.statement: Other income in FY24 largely one-off (VAT interest refund, provision write-back); not expected to recur
items.quote: So, other income is definitely one -off. Large part of the other income is one -off. We got a refund... not refund exactly, we got some interest on the State VAT, which we had paid in excess to the department. And we had some write back of some excess provision of the previous year. We don't expect these to continue for the future.

items.statement: Mitsubishi Pencil partnership: targeting ₹100 crore Uni-Ball brand revenue in 2 years; discussing deeper collaboration
items.quote: So we are doing good with the Mitsubishi Pencil Company and we are trying to grow the brand to a hundred crore level in next two years. So that's about the Uni -Ball brand. And of course, we'd like to work closer with them, going forward. So, we are at discussion level with them on that front that, you know, what more we can do together.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 first month showed double-digit growth despite high base; confident on full quarter with new products and export growth
items.quote: So, Q1 so far has been... I mean, it's just been one month, which is typically a low month for us. So we have a double-digit growth in the first month. We have a good task for Q1 because last year it had a high base. But yes, we are confident that with the help of the new products and increase in our exports, we'll definitely be able to deliver a good Q1.

items.statement: Target asset growth of 12-13% for FY25, similar deposit growth, medium-term NIM target of 3.5%, ROA to stay near 1% in near term
items.quote: Ma'am, we would -- we want to grow at the rate at which we grew this year, which is about 12% on assets -- 12%, 13%, so either 12% or early teens on the asset side, and deposit side of a similar number

items.statement: Q4 FY24 NIM at 3.38%, full year 3.31% highest in 18 years; aim to reach 3.5% medium term by restructuring balance sheet toward higher-yield assets
items.quote: Net interest margin for the quarter came in at 3.38% in Q4 2024, and for the full year, stood at 3.31%. It's the highest such number in 18 years.

items.statement: Gross NPA down 64 bps to 4.50%, net NPA down 40 bps to 1.46%; PCR (RBI) improved to 79.10%, expect 300-400 bps further improvement over next year
items.quote: Overall gross NPA reduced by 64 basis points to 4.50%. Net NPA reduced by 40 basis points to 1.46%. Recovery and upgradation in NPA accounts for the quarter stood at INR424 crores against a slippage of INR284 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: Gold loan book INR15,513 crores, average LTV 74.92% including buyouts, 70.73% own portfolio; LTV trend expected to decline further
items.quote: We continue to grow our gold loan business, which now stands at INR15,513 crores with an average LTV of 74.92%, including loans that have been bought out and an average ticket size of approximately INR1.56 lakhs.

items.statement: Corporate book ~INR32,000 crores, grew ~INR8,000 crores YoY; retail disbursements growing (home loans +26% QoQ, auto +23% QoQ) but on low base
items.quote: Our corporate business continued to grow robustly, coming in at about INR32,000 crores at the end of this quarter. The total growth on the corporate side is approximately -- on a year-on-year basis, is approximately INR8,000 crores

items.statement: Launched affordable housing, commercial vehicle & equipment, relaunched LAP; target INR1,000-1,100 crores CV/CE book by year-end, INR2,000 crores affordable housing, couple thousand crores LAP
items.quote: On the CV CE side, I think the thought process is that if we are able to get to about INR1,000 crores to INR1,100 crores of business by the end of the year, then I think we will be happy.

items.statement: First fully automated MSME lending solution live; plan to install 6-7 similar products by year-end to transform sales engine and processes
items.quote: Our first fully automated product has gone live, and we are hoping that it will perform well. We have an agenda of installing 6 or 7 similar products before the year is out

items.statement: Sales value addition metric targets branches to generate 50% of cost via new sales; Q4 saw ~202 branches meet target vs expected 100; current account originations up 4x, average balances +70%
items.quote: When we built this metric, our expectation was roughly about 100 branches will meet it because that was the historical trend line. But last quarter, approxim ately 202 did meet it

items.statement: Corporate yields improved via aggressive pricing, renegotiation of NBFC exposures post risk-weight change, and mix shift to supply chain/dealer finance
items.quote: We did go back and try and renegotiate wherever it is possible so that we got an incremental yield to cover for the incremental risk weights that RBI had prescribed for us.

items.statement: Credit card issuance halted per RBI direction; working on required changes, in dialogue with RBI; aim to restart next quarter subject to approval
items.quote: Our current wishlist, and I'm not saying that it will happen in that form, but our current wishlist is that we should be in a position to have crossed all the T's and dotted all the I's and restart next quarter subject to RBI approval.

items.statement: Rights issue completed in Q4 FY24; CAR 19.91%, Tier-1 17.65%; dividend paid INR78 crores (30% payout), up INR18 crores YoY
items.quote: The bank successfully completed its rights issue during Q4 FY'24, taking the capital adequacy ratio of the bank to 19.91% and Tier 1 capital to 17.65%.

items.statement: ROA 91 bps (highest ever), ROE 12.13% (10-year high); cost-to-income ratio elevated, target to reduce by ~1,000 bps over multiple years
items.quote: The bank declared its highest return on assets at 91 basis points and the highest return on equity in the last 10 years at 12.13%.

items.statement: Recovery-driven PCR improvement has 6-9 months runway; treasury gains limited near term as rates at ~7.20%; expense base 2/3 fixed, only 1/3 controllable
items.quote: We think that we still have another 6 to 9 months of runway where recoveries will remain reasonably buoyant. And consequently, we have that time horizon to actually change the asset mix.

items.statement: Tie-ups with Ashok Leyland, JCB for dealer floor finance to drive retail CV/CE; corporate RM team of ~60 with curated product approach winning business in Mumbai, Delhi
items.quote: We have multiple relationships with Ashok Leyland, so we do substantial quantums of business with Ashok Leyland. An area that we are looking with the act is the financing of their dealers.

items.statement: New branch incentive structure based on sales value addition live since Jan 1; merging with existing HR measurement over time
items.quote: We've been live now for -- we started on 1st of January, so we've completed 1 quarter. We are using this as a mechanism of incentivizing branch behaviour.

items.statement: Rights issue 1:4 completed in Q4 FY24; decision driven by trading below book value to avoid dilution via QIP
items.quote: The rights issue versus QIP, the decision was on the basis of the fact that at the point in time we made this decision, we were trading significantly below book.

items.statement: Co-lending discussions active with multiple counterparties and enablers; taking longer than expected but progressing
items.quote: We are in discussions with multiple counterparties as well as entities that can enable us to connect with multiple participants. So this is something that we are actively exploring.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM reached Rs 12,200 crore and PMS AUM reached Rs 914 crore at end of March 2024
items.quote: Mutual fund AUM of Rs. 12,200 crores end of March 24 and PMS AUM of Rs. 914 crores.

items.statement: Brokerage income share reduced to 45% of total revenue from 58% in FY20
items.quote: As envisaged some years before, we have reduced the dependence on the Brokerage business. The brokerage income is 45% of the total revenue compared to 58% in FY20.

items.statement: Distribution income crossed Rs 150 crore, stands at Rs 152 crore for FY24
items.quote: Another highlight was the distribution income crosse d Rs. 150 crores, stands at Rs. 152 crores now.

items.statement: Board approved investment of up to USD 1 million to form an entity in Dubai DIFC for wealth management
items.quote: the Board has approved an investment of up to USD1 million to form an entity in Dubai.

items.statement: DIFC entity will offer global products like structured notes, bonds, leverage products to ultra HNIs and HNIs
items.quote: This will be global products structured notes, bonds, leverage products, all that we are unable to do today in the local domestic market in Dubai , those products will be made available to large number of our own customers as well as new customers whom we could acquire there.

items.statement: Aggressive focus on private wealth and PMS businesses with CEO appointments for both
items.quote: So, these are the two business lines we would like to aggressively pursue going forward.

items.statement: Insurance premium collected Rs 100 crore in FY24 vs Rs 76 crore in FY23, expecting good growth in FY25
items.quote: For '23- 24, we have totally collected Rs. 100 crores of premium, which is compared to Rs. 76 crores for the previous financial year which includes, of course , Rs. 4 crores of general and health insurance.

items.statement: PMS AUM grew from Rs 450 crore to Rs 914 crore in FY24 with aggressive push continuing in FY25
items.quote: We have grown from Rs. 450 crores in FY23 to Rs. 914 crores and we have invested hugely in that business in terms of manpower cost.

items.statement: Mutual fund equity AUM grew 46% in FY24, at par with industry growth of 48%
items.quote: The industry equity AUM grew 48% FY24 over FY23, we have grown 46%.

items.statement: Mutual fund distribution income is 100% trail-based, grew 17% while AUM grew 46%
items.quote: Now mutual fund basis only on trail income.

items.statement: Mutual fund yield 0.8%, PMS yield estimated 2.2-2.4% including performance fees
items.quote: Yield on m utual fund is 0.8 and on PMS, it varies around we estimated around 2.2 – 2.4 percentage.

items.statement: Group cash Rs 750 crore, majority used for MTF lending and working capital requirements
items.quote: On the group basis, the cash available is Rs. 750 crores. But as MD said, the majority of that is used for MTF books, lending, MT F and another major portion is used for the working capital requirements on a regular basis.

items.statement: Will explore inorganic acquisitions aligning with culture and compliance, have options to manage funding
items.quote: inorganic acquisition is an opportunity we will explore as and when we see opportunities that are aligning with our culture as well as the, you know, particularly on the compliance culture, etc.

items.statement: Exploring geographies with significant NRI population where regulations permit operations
items.quote: we are a Company looking for opportunities wherever we could identify significant NRI population. If the local, you know regulations permit , we are on the lookout for geographies where regulations are permitting us to operate without much complexities.

items.statement: Software business not aggressive currently, will consider growth over next 1-1.5 years, largely services in-house operations
items.quote: At the moment we do not have an aggressive business plan on the software business, but over a period of next 1 year to 18 months, we will think about growing that business. It is largely servicing in-house operations.

items.statement: Interest income increased to around Rs 110 crore in FY24
items.quote: our interest income has gone up to around Rs. 110 crore last year.

items.statement: Other operational income breakdown: FD interest Rs 54 crore, PMS income Rs 18.57 crore (including Rs 5.22 crore performance fee), loan interest Rs 1.46 crore
items.quote: Other operational income for the year 23-24 interest on loans is Rs. 1.46 crores. Rs. 54 crore FD interest, and PMS Rs. 18.57 crores and other operating income of Rs. 1.65 crores.

items.statement: Declared interim dividend of INR6 per share in FY24 vs INR0.50 in FY23; announced buyback with promoter family abstaining, distributing INR37.19 crore to minority shareholders
items.quote: During FY24, we distributed a total interim dividend of INR6 per share as compared to INR0.50 per share in FY23. The Board of Directors have announced a buyback of shares the promoter family has decided to abstain from participating in the buyback. Therefore, the amount, the entire amount of INR37.19 crores excluding taxes will be distributed amongst minority shareholders.

items.statement: Targets 30% top-line growth in FY25 including Warner deal benefits
items.quote: As committed earlier, this year for FY25 I feel 30% growth on top line is possible -- as you see in FY24 bottom line as compared to last year was up by 66%. But still we feel on 66% we will do another 30% this year i.e. in FY 25 as well.

items.statement: Expects content investment in FY25 to be higher than FY24, budgeted at INR75-80 crore
items.quote: For FY25, we expect investment in content to be higher than last year, but it also depends upon availability of quality music, price that is being demanded, release calendar of films and other factors.

items.statement: Added 179 new songs in Q4 FY24, total FY24 releases ~733 vs 896 in FY23; focus on quality over quantity
items.quote: We have added 179 new songs in Q4 of FY24, bringing the total songs released in FY24 to approximately 733 as compared to 896 last year. This time the focus has been much more on quality songs.

items.statement: Plans to release ~150 songs in FY25 (8-10 films, ~5 songs per film) plus independent music signings
items.quote: I feel it's the right number. I'm not focusing on really a hardcore number, maybe it will be for 140 or 170, that depends upon how, whatever we are acquiring. We are acquiring some films and some film has 4 songs, some film has 8 songs. So we can't say the exact number, but approximately I told you that.

items.statement: FY24 revenue INR241.6 crore (+29% YoY), PAT INR127.2 crore (+66% YoY); dividend payout ratio ~60.6%
items.value: Revenue INR241.6 cr; PAT INR127.2 cr
items.quote: Revenue for FY24 reached INR241.6 crores up from INR186.8 crores in FY23 demonstrating a growth of 29%. PAT for FY24 stood at INR127.2 crores compared to INR76.52 crores previously marking a growth of 66%. During FY24, the company has declared a cumulative interim dividend of INR6 per share which brings the pay off ratio for FY24 to be around 60.6%.

items.statement: Catalogue strength driving growth: Dil Laga Liya crossed 1 billion YouTube views; Crew film songs trending; regional music (Telugu, Bhojpuri, Rajasthani) performing well
items.quote: Our catalog song Dil Laga Liya from the film Dil Hai Tumara crossed 1 billion views on YouTube. This marks a very significant milestone for us. On a regional music front, Telugu music from the film Hanuman continues to trend and stream across all audio platforms. Similarly, we had a good run with new Bhojpuri and Rajasthani releases.

items.statement: Paid streaming adoption growing but will take 2-3 more years for meaningful revenue; Spotify targeting 60-70% paid conversion in India over 5 years
items.quote: Yes, paid streaming is increasing, day by day it's showing a progress and all the focus of all these platform companies like Spotify or Wynk or Gaana all their focus is on the paid to increase paid by. So I think that's a good thing for the industry, but as mentioned earlier it will still take 2 years, 3 years more to have very good numbers to see.

items.statement: Open to acquiring small Hindi or regional music labels for inorganic growth
items.quote: We are always open to that. Whenever opportunity comes, we will definitely look at that.

items.statement: Hired new team for brands/sync business; CEO Hari Nair joined 6 months ago and brought in good people; employee cost run-rate to increase nominally
items.quote: Recently, we have Mr. Hari has joined us last six months. And he has also brought in many good people. And we are also concentrating on other businesses rather than regular businesses. We are talking to brands. We are talking to sync. There are lot many other options as well.

items.statement: Global music industry growing ~10% (IFPI, EY); Tips outperformed domestic and global averages
items.quote: So, as you see the global IFPI report, the average growth rate of the music industry is about 10%. Similarly, there was a report from EY Media and Entertainment, I think that also projected the same numbers. We have done better than the global and domestic average.

items.statement: Content cost timing volatile quarter-to-quarter depending on film release schedules; Q4 FY24 content cost INR23.95 crore (~45% of annual) due to Crew release
items.quote: It can happen in future also. Please understand, content is not in my hand. When producer decides, I want this crew on 29th March, so I have to release that in February. If they say, I am going to release in June, so it could have gone in the next quarter.

items.statement: Non-current liability increased ~INR70 crore+ due to Warner MG advance; current liability INR64 crore also includes advance portion
items.quote: Firstly, you have to look at both numbers, non-current and current. Let's say there is INR71 crores in the non-current. That is also pertaining to an advance. And let's say there is INR64 crores lying in, other current liabilities. So you have to look from an advance perspective, you have to look at both the numbers.

items.statement: Retains 65% of business directly (YouTube majority + 25% other revenues); gave Warner 5 small regional YouTube channels for testing
items.quote: Even today, I can assure you that the 40% 50% of our YouTube business the 1%, 2% that we have given to YouTube the majority is with us. Other all revenues the 25% that we have got that is with us. I still feel that we are holding 65% of our business ourselves.

items.statement: Tips Films (group company) signed Varun Dhawan-David Dhawan film; music rights acquisition from Tips Films at government-approved valuer formula, target 30-35% of content cost from group
items.quote: I think maximum it can be 30%-35% from our own company. We acquire content. I think it will be that much. And that is the target we have kept for this year. And so, let's see.

items.statement: Warner deal creates client concentration risk but management comfortable given content ownership and upfront MG; platforms approached Tips directly when prior deal ended
items.quote: Ultimately, if you look at our music business deeply, it is a content game. Main is a content game. Distribution is a secondary thing. So, the one who has the content he is the king. So, distribution is fine. We need them too. It's not that we don't need them. But as I was telling you when our deal was coming to an end, Spotify and all those players with whom we did not have a direct deal, they al

items.statement: Content acquisition prices were extremely high last year; focusing on quality at right price; FY24 investment fell short by INR15-16 crore due to lack of quality music
items.quote: We were not getting good quality music last year and even if we got it, the prices were extremely high. We will pick quality music at the right price, hence our investment in the content fell short by approximately INR15- 16 crores.

items.statement: Content monetization timeline: management expects to recover investment in 4-5 years; writes off entire content cost in quarter of release
items.quote: whatever we invest, we will recover our money in four to five years' time. But still, we write off our entire content cost acquisition in the same quarter. You know that, I feel. Abhishek N.: Yes. Kumar Taurani: We don't carry forward anything. We just write off everything in the quarter we release our content

items.statement: Management will evaluate tax-efficient shareholder return structures (bonds/recapitalization) suggested by analyst; currently continuing dividends and buybacks
items.quote: We will look into it. But currently, we will continue with dividends and buybacks. But since you brought to our notice on this, we will check with the consultants and circle back.

items.statement: Management aims for industry-leading revenue growth in FY25 but refuses to give numeric guidance due to volatility
items.quote: our endeavor, Ravi, will be to continue to focus on execution. We've delivered a strong year and we want to continue to focus and try and deliver above the industry average growth

items.statement: Management expects to remain in investment mode for 24-36 months, keeping EBITDA margin in a narrow band while investing 1-1.5% of revenue
items.quote: For the next 24 to 36 months we will be in an investment mode and we would love to keep the margin in a ramp narrow band. And if you realize that when we invest we will invest upwards of 1% or 1.5% of revenue in our business.

items.statement: Demand environment remains challenging with slower client decision-making and discretionary spend push-outs, unchanged from past 4-5 quarters
items.quote: We continue to see clients' decision-making becoming slower, and uncertainty continues. While our clients continue to realign budgets, taking the money away from discretionary spends and pushing decisions out.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin at 16.3%, up 31 bps QoQ and 265 bps YoY, exceeding the 16% exit target set at start of FY24
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for quarter 4 stands at 16.3%, which is a 31 basis points growth quarter-over-quarter. You may recall at the start of the financial year, we have indicated that we would like to exit the year with 1 6% EBITDA margin, and I'm happy to note that we've been able to deliver above that number

items.statement: Pipeline stands at $1.8 billion with target to improve to $2.4-2.5 billion over next 6-8 months

items.statement: Macro risks: access to funding at competitive rates, tight liquidity, higher-for-longer global rates, elevated competitive pressure
items.quote: a few challenges still persist in the NBFC sector in FY25, namely - access to funding at competitive rates, tight liquidity conditions and the 'higher -for-longer' global policy rate regime and elevated competitive pressure especially from other competitors in the market.

items.statement: ESG rating improved from BBB to A (MSCI) and from B to A- leadership category (CDP) in FY24

items.statement: Next-gen digital credit engine beta version expected to deploy in production by latter part of Q1FY25; BRAKE collections app went live; Planet App crossed 9M downloads

items.statement: Management guides NIM plus fee income between 11% and 11.25% for FY25.

items.statement: Management targets managing opex plus credit cost within 7% of cost to book over the next 15-18 months.
items.quote: So, I think the best barometer is to manage the overall opex plus credit cost within the range of 7% when it comes to cost to book.

items.statement: Management expects cost of funds to increase by 35-40 bps during FY25.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds expected around 8.15%-8.2% for the full year based on current situation.
items.quote: Yes, yes. So that is based on the current situation. Naturally, if something dramatic happens, we will have to factor in. But as we speak, this is what our expectation is.

items.statement: Cost-income ratio currently in 40%-41% range; expected to improve as balance sheet grows and wholesale book reduction completes.

items.statement: Wholesale book reduction largely completed at Rs 4,400 Cr; no significant reduction expected going forward.

items.statement: Retail AUM growing at ~30%; Lakshya 2026 target is 25% CAGR.

items.statement: Investments focused on technology, people, and marketing; new underwriting engine beta expected in latter part of Q1FY25.
items.quote: So, we are hopeful that the beta version will come into production in sometime around the latter part of Q1FY25.

items.statement: New Home Loan digital journey to go live in next couple of weeks; Personal Loan journey already live.

items.quote: Our commercial paper exposures are today just 5%. We can, as per the ALM go up to 15%. We have started seeing balance sheet growth from last quarter and we will have the opportunity of increasing the commercial paper exposure slowly and steadily.

We'll be growing it on cross-sell, and we'll be growing it to absolutely safe segments.

items.quote: We generated free cash flow of Rs. 3.3 billion in Q4 and our total free cash flow stood at Rs. 1.8 billion for the year. On account of accelerated rollouts by our major customer , our capex remained elevated in Q4 as well .

items.statement: EBITDA per ton grew 15-20% YoY on 12-month basis
items.quote: When you see 12 months to 12 months, EBITDA per ton has grown somewhere around 15% to 20%.

items.quote: Our glass container capacity utilization consistently exceeds 95%, showcasing a dedication to operational excellence and efficient production optimization.

items.quote: So, coal we are buying for our DRI plant either through auction route from WCL or importing it. And later on we start our blast furnaces, the coking coal will be imported.

items.quote: Out of 450 Megawatt, around 300 Megawatt we envisage to be waste heat recovery or waste coal recovery, waste products recovery basically, and around 150 Megawatt would be direct coal-based thermal power.

items.quote: We have declared a dividend this year of 100%. That is Rs. 1 per share.

items.quote: Regarding EBITDA, steel is a cyclical business. Between March and April, the price has gone up by Rs. 2,500 to Rs. 3,000. Why? Difficult to answer. So, it's a cyclical business. I cannot answer about what will be the EBITDA numbers per se.

items.statement: MoEF clearance for Chittapur and Devapur expansions expected around June 2024 after new government formation

items.quote: We are l ooking at a range of 45% to 50% of revenue growth in this year and subsequent years going forward

items.statement: Rental cluster targets 50%+ CAGR over three-year roadmap

items.statement: 5,000 student and shared living beds signed up for delivery over next few quarters
items.quote: We have close to 5,000 beds of student and shared living whose supply has already been signed up and which will be delivered to us over the next few quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 1,150 bps YoY in FY24
items.quote: this year, Y -o-Y, we have increased or w e have bettered our EBITDA by 1,150 basis points

items.statement: SaaS gross margins at 90-95%

items.statement: Co-living business registered 87% YoY growth

items.quote: We acquired and fractionalized a single asset worth INR70 crores in Pune, paving the way to apply for becoming one of the first MSME REITs in India.

items.quote: This year, our revenue per employee stands at 29 lakhs per employee. Whereas, the earlier year, we were at 25 lakhs per year.

items.statement: NestAway tech reorganization delivered INR 14 lakhs monthly savings
items.quote: NestAway itself, through its tech reorganization, has been able to deliver a savings of INR 14 lakhs per month, right?

items.quote: If the demand today is roughly INR 2 crores houses in terms of rental s, the formalized or the organized capacity is somewhere around 2 lakh units only

items.statement: FY24 volumes grew 7% YoY; revenue grew 5.6% YoY driven by debottlenecking and new product development
items.quote: We recorded a 7% YoY increase in volumes and 5.6% in revenue owing to debottlenecking of capacity and new product development.

items.statement: Majority of increased freight costs from Red Sea disruption passed on to customers; customers accepting higher freight
items.quote: Practically majority of freight cost is passed on to the customers. Customers are now gradually accepting the situation and they are ready to pay the freight cost, whatever increases.

items.statement: FY24 capacity utilization ~60%; peak utilization estimated 75-80%; monthly peak capacity ~5,000 tons

items.statement: Order book secure at 3-4 months of operations; typically maintain ~3 months order book

items.statement: 200+ customers; top 5 contribute <20% revenue; wallet share increasing with existing customers; 80% products exported to 55 countries
items.quote: We have more than 200 customers. So, the customer concentration like top five will be contributing to less than 20% of the revenue.

items.statement: Compete mainly with Korean and Turkish manufacturers; Indian cost advantage enables market share gains; global market $6-8 bn
items.quote: Yes, I am talking about non-value-added products because we are competing with mostly with Koreans and their cost of production and their sales price is higher than us.

items.statement: Export share 77%, domestic 23%; domestic share up from 10% to 22%; products sold in 55 countries
items.quote: Currently our market share is around 23% is domestic market and around 77% is export market.

items.statement: Debt ratio <0.25; interest cost ~3% of turnover; promoters offered to buy back CCPS from lenders, under bank consideration, may materialize in couple of months
items.quote: And our debt ratio is less than 0.2. So, I don't think financial risk we have.

items.quote: Last year that EBITDA is almost INR 41,000 per metric ton. And as we expected, we are going for the value-added products. So, this percent, this absolute number EBITDA per ton contribution is going to increase in the current year also.

items.statement: No major risk foreseen; financial risk negligible (debt ratio <0.25); Red Sea disruption stabilizing; geographically diversified across 52+ countries
items.quote: See, the major risk to business is always financial risk. And our debt ratio is less than 0.2. So, I don't think financial risk we have. Marketing risk? Yes, there is, because of Red Sea issue, but that is settled on now.

items.statement: Promoters offered to buy back CCPS from lenders; under bank consideration; may materialize in couple of months
items.quote: Yes. The promoters have already, in fact, offered to banks for buyback, and that is under consideration by banks.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on high value product development and new geographical penetration
items.quote: This growth c an be attributed to our strategic efforts in reducing raw material cost, power and fuel, debt reduction, and new product development along with the new geographical penetration

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 4.8% in Q4 FY24 from 4.5% a year earlier
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA margins have now improved from 4.5% same quarter of last year to 4.8% this quarter.

items.quote: Leading this improvement in margins was our India security business, where margins have improved substantially from 5% in the same quarter last year to 5.5% in this quarter, a change of over 50 basis points.

items.statement: Cash business EBITDA margin expanded to 18.2% in Q4 FY24, up 200 basis points year-on-year
items.quote: Cash business surges ahead with superior profitability metric s with an EBITDA margin of 18.2%, a growth of 200 basis points year-on-year, and a PAT margin of 7.7% this quarter.

So, our reality lies between 1x to 2x and we keep fluctuating between these two thresholds.

items.statement: India security business can maintain high-teens growth going forward
items.quote: I believe at a segmental level, security can maintain high-teens growth.

items.quote: In terms of growth, if you remove the 5% growth that came from our international operations, the Indian operations, security and FM grew at 11%. Certainly not our best year, but this is still 1.5x GDP growth.

items.statement: Wage inflation of 5-6% annually provides industry floor growth; living wage implementation could drive price-led growth
items.quote: Wage inflation in the same period, year -on-year, has been between 5% to 6%. So, everybody in this industry would have had at least 5% to 6% growth because of wage inflation.

items.quote: We have made a minority investment in Agarsha Senior Care, otherwise known as Emoha, an elder care platform, by acquiring 4% through a combination of primary and secondary investments.

items.statement: Demerger and listing of cash operations on track; scheme nearly ready, SEBI/NCLT filing in 4-6 weeks

items.statement: India security collections improved significantly in Q4 vs Q3, DSO number much better
items.quote: This is despite the fact that security has significantly improved its collection in Q4 versus Q3. But despite a much better DSO number, based on auditor advice, we have taken additional provisioning.

items.statement: India security growth of 11-12% in FY24 was largely volume-driven; no significant minimum wage price increase

items.quote: This year, for example, we have invoiced more than Rs. 100 crores out of our alarm business, which has zero manpower. We have billed Rs. 100 crores, generated 20% EBITDA from our VProtect business.

items.quote: As you can see, in this quarter, we have also recognized an impairment of Rs. 65.6 crores.

items.quote: That stands at a CAGR of 15.8%. So, I think the re is enough evidence that SIS is a high -teens growth business.

items.quote: For FY '25, we aspire to add between 120 to 150 stores on a net basis.

items.quote: But for Q1, our target would be to do an SSG of 2% to 3%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 31.8% FY24; pre-Ind AS EBITDA 17.7%

items.quote: During the year, we added a net total of 84 stores, bringing us to overall to count to 714 stores.

items.statement: Store closure rate to normalize to low single digits in FY25
items.quote: Going forward, we expect to return to a normalized store closure rate of single digit for the next year.

items.quote: Out of the entire of INR39 crores only INR1 lakh is relating to the interest kind of interest working something like that. INR39 crores is because of Ind AS.

items.quote: See I don't see that as a risk because Co -Ord sets and kurti sets are usually occasion -based buying. For every day wear the lady prefers to buy the bottom and top the separately.

items.quote: I'm happy to share that as on FY '24, we have witnessed a multi-fold jump in our Pre-Ind AS operating cash flow, which stood at INR111 crores, which was INR20 crores in FY '23.

items.statement: Guided AUM growth above 30% YoY for FY25
items.quote: As we have moved from COVID, we have been giving a 30% above growth year-on-year. That will continue for this year too.

items.statement: Guided disbursement growth of 25-27% for FY25
items.quote: So, roughly the dis bursal growth we are talking about will be more like 25 % kind of a growth that we are looking at for 25 % to 27% growth

items.quote: Our guidance for the next 3 years ROA will be around 6.5% to 7% and if you multiply that with the leverage of 3.5%, our guidance for next 3 years on so ROE will be around 20% plus.

items.statement: Guided cost-to-income ratio to remain stable at 35-37% in steady state

items.statement: Guided liquidity buffer of 15-18% of AUM in steady state

items.statement: Guided non-cash collections to reach 65-70% by FY25 end

items.statement: Guided 30+ dpd to remain in 7.5-8% range for FY25

items.statement: Guided provision coverage on overall AUM to settle at 1.5-1.65% for next 1-2 years

items.statement: Yields stable at 24-24.25%; incremental cost of funds 9.58%, book cost 9.71%; spread 14.55% in Q4; NIM 17.19% in Q4, 17.4% for FY24

items.statement: Strong mid-to-late stage sales funnel; deal sizes and decision cycles improving; green shoots in H2 CY24

items.statement: Management expects to deliver EBITDA and net margins in FY25 similar to FY22 and FY23 levels, in line with volume growth.
items.quote: I would not quote a number per se, but I can certainly confirm that we are on track to deliver the kind of EBITDA and the kind of net margins which we had shown in FY‘22 and FY‘23, which should happen in FY‘25, in line with the volume

items.statement: Branded edible oil volume growth targeted at 9-10% in FY25.

items.statement: Demand remained strong in Q4 FY24 and is expected to remain strong entering the new financial year.
items.quote: Demand remained strong during the quarter, which we saw, and we are hopeful that this demand should remain strong as we enter into a new financial year.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA run rate of ~INR 900 crore per half achieved in H2 FY24, close to H2 FY23 levels.
items.quote: EBITDA in H2 24 is close to INR 863 crores, so that run rate of INR 900 crores EBITDA in half is somewhere we are close to that, as compared to INR 962 crores of EBITDA in H2 of last year.

items.statement: Standard run rate for edible oil gross profit is INR 11,500-12,000 per ton and EBITDA ~INR 3,500 per ton.
items.quote: See, on edible oil, so for us the standard run rate for gross profit is anywhere between 11,500 to 12,000 per ton and the EBITDA margins of close to 3,500 metric tons per ton.

items.statement: HoReCa channel now contributes INR 400 crore revenue, 3x growth since launch a year ago.
items.quote: Similarly, on HoReCa, which is a new channel which we have created close to a year back, now it is 3x contributing a good 400 crore of business.

items.statement: Alternate channel revenue reached INR 2,700 crore+, growing 29% overall with e-commerce up 42%.
items.quote: In our case, this channel has contributed now for revenue close to 2,700 crore plus of revenue. In this whole alternate channel piece, e-commerce is growing faster than the modern trade. The overall growth of alternate channel is 29%, whereas the e-commerce has grown by 42%.

items.statement: Edible oil capacity utilization at 60%, providing headroom for growth.
items.quote: On capacity utilization, we are quite well placed, 60% capacity utilization. So, we still have good amount of headroom available for any kind of growth that we may see in coming years.

items.statement: Mustard crushing capacity expanded: 600 TPD commissioned, another 600 TPD at Gohana ready in ~1 month, adding ~35% Kachi Ghani volume.
items.quote: This year amongst the IPO project, one 600 ton crushing per day has been commissioned. So, that is now ready for operation in this season. In Gohana, we are coming up with another 600 ton plant, which will be ready by, say, another one month or so, and at least we can do crushing there. So, 1,200 ton of crushing should give you an additional around 35% of Kachi Ghani.

items.statement: Gohana rice milling unit (from IPO investment) expected ready by November for Basmati season.
items.quote: Second is that our Gohana unit, which is from the IPO investment we did, will be ready. Hopefully, the rice part should be ready by November as the season starts.

items.statement: Stable edible oil prices benefit branded margins; volatility reduction allows better MRP stability and higher margins.
items.quote: The markets remain stable and when it remains stable, the brands get a lot of strength because volatility in prices brings a lot of fluctuation in MRP. So, for us, the lower prices give us higher margins and we would always like higher production because that is better for the country as well as for the brand.

items.statement: Branded edible oil grew 15% YoY in FY24 vs industry <7%; branded share driving market share gains.
items.quote: Edible oil branded sales grew at a faster clip at a 15% year-on-year in FY‘24. This is something very exciting to us because the edible oil branded segment in an industry growing at single digit, and we have been also clocking single digit growth for the last couple of years. This time it is 15% for us

items.statement: Food and FMCG is >80% branded/packed; domestic food volumes grew 39% YoY in Q4 FY24.
items.quote: In food and FMCG, more than 80% is branded. It is packed. Now, when I say packed, it can be 25 kilo bags also, Fortune bags which goes to our hotels, which also goes to our out-of-home consumption plus in-home consumption. So, these are all packed and branded. So, more than 80%.

items.statement: Direct retail reach expanded to 7.2 lakh outlets (2.4x March 2020); overall reach 2.1 million outlets.
items.quote: Now we have close to 2.1 million outlet reach in whic h 7,20,000 is a direct reach. This direct reach is actually 2.4x when we compare it with the March '20

items.statement: Rural town coverage at 30,000+ towns, targeting 50,000 towns by end of next year; rural saliency improved to 31%.
items.quote: Right now, we are covering close to 30,000 towns, but we do have plans to take this to 50,000 towns. The rural saliency remains at 30%, 31% for us. It is improving. In fact, till last year, it was 30%. This year, it is actually 31% in terms of our overall scheme of things.

items.statement: Alternate channel market shares significantly higher than general trade: soybean oil 40-80%, mustard 30-70%, atta 10-20%, besan 20%.
items.quote: But when we look at a soybean and mustard, particularly, in sunflower, on alternate channel, our share is anywhere between 15% to 80%. So, there are, for example, in soybean oil, depending upon market-to-market, share might be in the range of anywhere between 40 to 80, for mustard 30 to 70, for atta 10 to 20, this is building up very fast and for the Besan it is 20%.

items.statement: White/broken rice export ban impacted FY24 volumes; G2G channel (NCEL/Kribhco) started for domestic procurement and export.
items.quote: White rice, we are not going to do because you are not supposed to do. The G2G business has now started. So, possibly some business is happening where we are supposed to buy and sell to the cooperatives, NCEL or Kribhco and they are exporting.

items.statement: Branded exports to 30+ countries grew 72% in FY24 to ~INR 200 crore; Basmati rice exports expected to grow with 15,000-20,000 tons branded target.
items.quote: On a branded export, which is again a focus area, we have more than doubled the sales which are growing by 72% and now close to 200 crore of turnover contributed by this channel, 30 plus countries, where we are exporting all the products on the brand name Fortune, whether it is an edible oil or whether it is a food product.

items.statement: Bangladesh JV issues (FX availability, price controls) largely resolved post-elections; no profitability drag expected in FY25.
items.quote: So, both this problem as we stand today, as we speak today are more or less got resolved. Bangladesh went into elections in January with a now fresh government coming in place. Most of the macros have been improving in Bangladesh. Availability of Fx is now there. Prices have cooled down. Government has also allowed us some free hand on the pricing and the business is now giving a good numbers in B

items.statement: Inventory management tightened post-H1 FY24 issues; risk management policy tweaked for just-in-time operations.
items.quote: We have changed our, tweaked our risk management policy to ensure that we remain tight on inventory and we have ensured that we are just in time managing, and hence we will not be saddled with any great inventory.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; depreciation declined due to useful life revision on newer plants, not a one-off.
items.quote: Basically, management keep doing the exercise of revisiting the useful life of the asset and what has happened is given the technological advances and the better technology coming in the play as far as the edible oil and the food business is concerned, a lot of plants which we have commissioned in last five years, we realize that they have got a better life than what we have estimated at the time

items.statement: Food segment EBITDA reached INR 170 crore on ~INR 5,000 crore turnover (~3.5% margin) in FY24.
items.quote: For the Financial Year 24, food contributed an EBITDA of 170 crore on a turnover of 5,000 crores close to 3.5% of EBITDA, which is quite encouraging for us.

items.quote: other income largely consists of ECAS charges of INR9.37 crores, e-voting charges of INR4.42 crores and miscellaneous income in terms of user facility charges, account maintenance charges and similar income heads.

items.statement: Jewellery EBIT margin guidance maintained at 12-13% for FY25
items.quote: I think both Ashok and I and all of us have been saying that 12% to 13% is a reasonable expectation to have for the EBIT margin.

items.quote: So the -- you are aware that last year, anyway, we had some onetime gains on account of inventory gains on diamonds and there was custom duty benefits. So there is that piece. items.quote: some of the major players and in fact, a lot of unbranded players, have actually -- are facing a lot of extra stock, which had been kind of built into their inventory plans. items.statement: Working capital loans INR 2,600 crore offset by INR 3,000 crore cash, comfortable with current leverage
