items.quote: We definitely see that next year '24-25 the demand growth will better as compared to '23-24.

items.quote: I am pleased to inform that we have declared a dividend of INR 0.50 paisa per equity share of INR 2 each, representing 25% of the paid-up capital for the financial year FY24.

items.statement: Expects incentives from Tamil Nadu government under INR 1,045 crore MoU; quantum under discussion
items.quote: We had some discussion with them. We are looking for more and they are giving us little less. So that number at this point of time, I don't have a number to share with you, but number will be a good number.

items.statement: Commissioned 15 MW renewable energy (total 62 MW); targeting 75 MW for cost savings and sustainability
items.quote: Further, we have also commissioned 15 megawatt of renewable energy, taking our total renewable energy towards 62 megawatt. We aim to expand our green energy portfolio to 75 megawatt and this expansion will provide cost benefit and further reinforces our commitment to environmental substantiality.

items.statement: Near-term margin visibility low due to volatile spreads; cannot predict Q1 FY25 margins
items.quote: Based on that, can I predict what will happen in Q1? No, I will not be able to predict. Okay, because the markets are fluctuating.

items.statement: Tracks value addition per ring frame and EBITDA margin as key internal KPIs
items.quote: We look at, frankly speaking, value addition per ring frame. Because ring frame is the same, that is a limiting capacity for me, right? I look at what is the value which this machine is giving to me either I'm producing a fine count or I'm producing a coarser count. How much value this machine is giving.

items.statement: Labour cost among lowest in industry at 3-4% of revenue
items.quote: Our cost of many fixed costs, like your labour cost, we are the lowest, almost around 3% to 4% labour cost.

items.statement: Evaluated acquiring distressed spinning units in Tamil Nadu; decided against small units due to culture/worker challenges; open to large unit acquisitions
items.quote: Yes, in the past we have looked at these possibilities and the couple of challenges which you face here. First, can I go for a smaller unit? No, we cannot, we should not. Why? Because the time and energy which you require to set a bad performing unit to a good because you don't need only the capital, you need the culture, you need the worker, you need many things in that, okay? And that is very ha

items.statement: 25,000 spindle expansion delayed to May-June 2025 (early FY26) due to machinery supply delays
items.quote: Basically, this project, some portion will start in the last year of, means last quarter of this year, but full completion will happen in the May and June next year only because of some delay in the machinery from the supplier likely to happen.

items.statement: Pre-sales target of INR850 crores for FY25
items.quote: With regards to the pre-sales, we are targeting a pre-sales of INR850 crores for the financial year 2024-25.

items.statement: Revenue recognition guidance of INR500-525 crores for FY25
items.quote: On the sales part, we are expecting to close sales in the range of INR500 crores to INR525 crores for FY'25.

items.statement: Pre-sales mix: INR650 crores residential and INR200 crores commercial for FY25
items.quote: So, we are targeting pre-sales of INR850 crores in FY'25 of which we are expecting INR200 crores from commercial segment and balance INR650 would come from the residential segment.

items.statement: Plan to launch 7 new projects with GDV of INR1,150 crores in FY25
items.quote: We expect to launch 7 new projects. As discussed on the call, we have a total GDV of INR1,150 crores which would be coming out of these new launches.

items.statement: Capital requirement of INR150 crores to launch 7 projects in FY25
items.quote: So, that would be in a range of INR150 odd crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at current levels for FY25 as land cost already funded
items.quote: Since the land's cost is already funded for, so we propose to maintain the margins.

items.statement: FY24 operating margin expanded 710 bps to 56.9% driven by product mix shift to luxury and commercial deals
items.quote: Product mix has changed. Value luxury and , luxury segment has been sold very well. There the realizations are a bit better than the value luxury segment.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR315 crores as of March 2024 from INR565 crores a year ago
items.quote: Our net debt as on March 24 stands at INR315 crores versus INR565 crores in the previous financial year March 23.

items.statement: High-cost debt of INR80-90 crores outstanding, expected to reduce as projects progress
items.quote: So, presently around INR80 crores-INR90 crores is high-cost debt.

items.statement: Blended interest cost expected at 14% for FY25, targeting 12-13% by FY26
items.quote: So, FY '25 we expect to maintain the same debt levels considering the seven project launches are there. We would require some capital for that. So, there will be repayments, there will be disbursements which will be taken. So, we will try to maintain the debt level in for FY '25. And the blended average cost can be considering the range of 14% odd for FY '25.

items.statement: Ongoing portfolio: 4.89 lakh sq ft sold, INR1,171 crores collected, INR719 crores receivable, unsold inventory GDV INR631 crores
items.quote: Out of the 6 lakh square feet, we have already sold 4.89 lakh square feet and have collected INR1,171 crores, with a balanced receivable of INR719 crores to be collected. The unsold inventory of 1.21 lakh square feet from the ongoing projects have an estimated GDV of approximately INR631 crores.

items.statement: Balance construction cost to complete ongoing projects estimated at INR600 crores
items.quote: Overall project cost can be in a range of INR600 crores, in the entire ongoing portfolio. This is balanced to be completed.

items.statement: Value luxury pricing INR38,000-44,000 per sq ft; luxury pricing INR60,000-90,000 per sq ft in South Central Mumbai
items.quote: If it's a value luxury segment anywhere between, it ranges from 38,000 all the way to 43,000 to 44,000. And if it's a luxury segment, it can go from 60,000 all the way to around 85,000-90,000 as well.

items.statement: Upcoming portfolio mix: 67% value-luxury, 21% value-luxury and luxury, 12% commercial
items.quote: 67% of this comprises of value-luxury projects, 21% belongs to the value-luxury and luxury projects and the balanced 12% is the commercial segment for sale.

items.statement: Bandra project received concession approvals for first phase; launch planned late FY25 or early FY26
items.quote: So with regards to Bandra we have already received our concession approvals from the Municipal Commissioner for the first phase. However, since we are planning to amalgamate a few more plots we plan to launch this later in the year FY24-25. It will be towards the end of the year or early next year.

items.statement: OLV/OLPS litigation settled: INR47 crores payment + 35,500 sq ft flats to society; unlocks GDV INR350 crores
items.quote: This settlement leaves us with a built-up area of more than 10,800 meters, including fungible FSI for sale, equating to a GDV of INR350 crores.

items.statement: Acquired freehold land 1,073 sq m at LJ Road, Mahim; 7 tenants vacated; estimated 30,000 sq ft carpet, GDV INR120 crores
items.quote: After accounting for the FSI required for rehabilitating these tenants/occupants and the surplus area to be handed over to MADA, the estimated balanced carpet area is approximately 30,000 square feet with a GDV of INR120 crores.

items.statement: FY24 pre-sales 1,07,136 sq ft (INR483 crores), up 10.5% YoY; realization INR45,074 per sq ft vs INR42,420 in FY23
items.quote: In FY24 in the residential segment, we have achieved pre-sales of 1,07,136 square feet versus 1,03,044 square feet in FY23 translating to a sales value of approximately INR483 crores versus INR437 crores in FY23 indicating year-on-year growth of 10.5% in the residential segment.

items.statement: INR500 crore equity raise approved as enabling provision; no immediate plans to utilize
items.quote: That is just an enabling provision. We have not planned anything as of now, but that's just an enabling provision from the Board and which we are taking and which we will take yearly.

items.statement: MMR absorption grew 14% CAGR 2018-23; inventory dropped to 13 months from 30 months; pricing up 5.2% CAGR
items.quote: From 2018 to 2023, absorption in the MMR surge at the rate of 14% annually, propelled by several factors, such as rise in disposable incomes and household savings, a growing preference for higher quality residences and larger living spaces, a reverse migration trend triggered by the lifting of COVID-related restrictions and the return to office mandate, along with the urbanization.

items.statement: Focus on amalgamating societies near existing projects in Mahim/Dadar; not bidding in Khar/Santa Cruz; Bandra land parcel size comparable to large developers
items.quote: We are looking at just acquisition of societies very close to what we already have so that we get a larger footprint. So that would be our prime objective right now.

items.statement: Sales receivables INR718 crores cover balance construction cost INR600 crores; unsold inventory GDV INR631 crores covers ongoing debt
items.quote: Yes, it is enough because the sales receivables are INR718 crores against which we have a balance cost to complete of around INR600 odd crores. But there is an unsold inventory which is about INR631 crores, which will take care of the ongoing debt which we have.

items.statement: Repaid INR285 crores high-cost debt from IPO proceeds in Dec 2023; additional INR23.5 crores unsecured loan repaid from collections
items.quote: During the year we have repaid high-cost debt to the tune of INR285 crores from the IPO proceeds in the month of December 2023. Further additional INR23.5 crores of unsecured loan was repaid from the gross collection proceeds.

items.statement: Suraj Lumina project (22,376 sq ft carpet, 35 units, GDV ~INR100 crores) launched in FY24; completion expected Dec 2028
items.quote: The project is expected to be completed by December 28.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin target 27-28%, EBITDA margin target 12-13%
items.quote: Hence, our estimate is that gross profit margin will be maintaining at a range of 27% to 28% going forward. From an EBITDA perspective, our target to maintain EBITDA is in the range of 12% to 13%.

items.statement: FY25 marketing spend target ~2% of revenue vs <1% in FY24
items.quote: We have planned to increase approximately 2% of revenue, which is currently less than 1%.

items.statement: Wafer revenue mix to rise from 8% to 12-13% in 2-3 years
items.quote: While other products like Gathiya Namkeen will be in the range of 10% to 12% growth. So, you can understand this 8% of overall revenue, the mix will change to 12%, 13%.

items.statement: Subsidy income run-rate INR10-12 cr/year for next 4-5 years from Nagpur and Modasa facilities
items.quote: Similar benefit and even for the Modasa facility the subsidy benefit will start coming in FY '25. This will be in the range of INR10 crores to INR12 crores year-on-year going forward.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 gross margin stable at ~28% (INR101 cr); EBITDA margin 11% vs 13% YoY due to employee and marketing cost inflation
items.quote: In terms of profitability, gross margin remained stable at almost 28% at an absolute amount of INR101 crores. EBITDA margin stood at 11% in Q4 versus 13% last year.

items.statement: FY24 gross margin 28.5%, EBITDA margin 12% vs 14% YoY; EBITDA dropped ~INR32 cr from salary and marketing cost
items.quote: Our revenue remained flat at INR1,400 crores and gross margin remained stable at 28.5% and EBITDA margin was at 12% compared to 14% of the previous year while gross profit margin remained stable at 28% but EBITDA dropped by 2%.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 palm oil prices -16% YoY, chana prices +20% YoY; net raw material benefit ~INR5 cr passed via grammage increase (20g to 25g on INR5 SKUs) and retailer margin hike (50p to 75p)
items.quote: During Q4 of FY '24, we have seen almost a reduction of 16% in our palm oil prices compared to last year Q4 of FY '23 and 20% increase in Ch ana prices versus Q4 of FY '23. So, the benefit of net reduction in the raw material prices which approximately amounts to INR 5 crores, we have passed this benefit to customers in terms of gra mmage increase on couple of our INR 5 SKU from 20 grammage to 25

items.statement: Raw material inflation outlook 3-5% for FY25; will use grammage changes if significant cost increase hits gross margin
items.quote: So, I said that the outlook what is coming out is that the future inflation is going to be in the range of 3% to 5%. And we would to , commodity prices going up in case there is a significant increase in the price of raw material. And if it is hitting us in terms of gross profit, margin, etcetera we will definitely look at a grammage change and will align to the industry practices also.

items.statement: Urban (Tier-1) 20-25% of sales; Rural (Tier-2/3) 75% of sales
items.quote: Rural is currently 75% of our. So, it is based on the population, Tier-1, Tier-2 and Tier 3. Tier-1 is 20%-25% of our sale. 75% comes from Tier-2 and Tier-3 market currently.

items.statement: Focus states competitors: Rajasthan (Bikaji, Balaji), MP (Yellow Diamond, Akash, Balaji, Haldiram), Maharashtra (Haldiram, Balaji), East (Prabhuji)
items.quote: For an example, in Rajasthan, there are Bikaji, Balaji. In MP, there are Yellow Diamond, Akash and Balaji, somewhat Haldiram. And in Maharashtra, it's Haldiram and Balaji. Where we move towards east, there are Prabhuji and other brands.

items.statement: INR200 cr cumulative capex across 3 facilities for 4 lakh+ MT/yr capacity; utilization 35-36%; no major capex until 75-80% utilization (~2 years)
items.quote: investment in plant and machinery etc etera we have INR 200 crores of capex spent in all our three facility put together where we have capacity of 4 lakh plus metric ton in a year. And this investment is made in couple of years in last 10 years or so. And this capacity utilization currently if you see it is 35 % to 36%. And we don't see in future the capex coming in, coming in till the time the ca

items.statement: Small packing unit capex possible; major capex ordering starts in year 2 when utilization reaches 80-85%
items.quote: So, while there will be some small capex putting some packing unit or some prior, but it will be very negligible. Once, after two years, when we'll reach to a capacity of 80 %-85%, while our ordering will start on capex in the second year going forward, but our peak is 75 %-80%, and then we will - you will see capex investment in the business.

items.statement: Revenue can double (2x) without major capex at current 35% utilization
items.quote: We have a potential to leverage this capacity. Our revenue can climb to 2x without any major capex. So, that's the healthy balance sheet we are talking about.

items.statement: Working capital increase due to lower EBITDA cash generation; inventory procurement seasonal (chana, potato in Q4); dealer sales on advance, vendor payments immediate
items.quote: capital has increased because you can see there has been a decrease in EBITDA to the close of INR20 crores-INR25 crores, and the cash generation from operation has come down to that extent. Otherwise, the investment in inventory is only, which is a temporary one. Otherwise, the working capital remains intact. In our business, we do selling to our dealer on advance basis and our payment to vendors,

items.statement: Employee cost INR102 cr FY24; headcount additions done, FY25 increase only from annual increments; may optimize excess manpower
items.quote: So, in terms of head count, it is already done. We may optimize in some area where there are excess manpower. But this INR102 crores definitely will have incremental impact, increment, the annual increment, which we give to our employee in FY '25, not in terms of head count, but the inflationary impact, which is normally there for each and every, for every organization.

items.statement: Promoter holding 81.48%; 3 years (per SEBI) to reduce to 75%; will dilute at right time
items.quote: As per the SEBI requirement, we have 3 years to bring down this promoter holding to 75%. We got listed only in the month of March. Our focus is to grow in terms of our revenue, profitability, etcetera. Definitely, at the right time, we will plan to dilute our holding.

items.statement: StAR MF 2.0 platform to launch in Q2 FY2025
items.quote: Given the growth, we are going to continue investing in StAR MF and improve it in terms of scalability, functionality and order processing and introduce a new platform called StAR MF 2.0 next quarter, that is Q2 FY 2025.

items.statement: Phase 1 data centre expansion completed; 100 new racks added including 15kVA racks
items.quote: I'm happy to update that we have completed Phase 1 of our expansion allowing us to accommodate more clients and ensure unmatched serving continuity.

items.statement: Plans to add 150 more colocation racks if market demand exists
items.quote: We already have plans of bringing in 150 more racks, if there is a market demand for which we have identified place.

items.statement: All 100 initial colocation racks consumed; Phase 1 expansion of 100 new racks completed and being allocated
items.quote: We started with around 100 racks when we just started the derivative segment. All those 100 racks are consumed. The Phase 1 of our expansion we had undertaken, and I'm happy to say that it is complete, and we are in the process of allocating those racks.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin expanded to 29% from 24% in FY24
items.quote: The operating EBITDA for FY '24 stands at INR 399.9 crores from I NR 197.4 crores last year with operating EBITDA margin expanding to 29% from 24% earlier

items.statement: Net profit margin excluding CDSL stake sale at 25% vs 22% prior year
items.quote: The net profit margin, excluding CDSL sales stands at 25% as against 22% last year.

items.statement: Transaction charges increased effective May 13, 2024 to match market rates and cover rising clearing/settlement costs and SEBI turnover fee
items.quote: We have brought the prices of the transaction charges of BSE on par with what is the market's existing charges now.

items.statement: Colocation rack rent brought on par with market rates to cover capex and opex for new racks
items.quote: In order to ensure that we were not out of pocket in respect of both the capex and opex, what now we have done is we have brought the colo rack rent on par with what is there in the market.

items.statement: Clearing and settlement charges incurred INR 206.5 crores standalone vs INR 61.7 crores prior year
items.quote: BSE has incurred a cost of INR 206.5 crores on a stand-alone basis compared to INR 61.7 crores in the previous year.

items.statement: Core SGF contribution increased 67% to INR 91.7 crores for equity and currency derivatives
items.quote: BSE's clearing arm ICCL has to contribute an amount of INR 91.7 crores for FY '24 towards its equity and currency derivatives segment, which is 67% higher compared to previous financial year.

items.statement: Received SEBI letter dated April 26, 2024 on differential regulatory fee for past 18 years; provided INR 170 crores as prudence
items.quote: BSE has received a letter from our market regulator, SEBI, dated 26th April 2024 with respect to differential regulatory fee for the past periods along with applicable interest. We are currently looking into the matter and pend ing finalization of the outcome based on the prudence the company has provided in the current period, an amount of INR 170 crores towards differential regulatory fees

items.statement: Will appeal to SEBI to reconsider differential fee decision based on premium vs notional turnover calculation
items.quote: Now that the letter has come, we will be requesting and representing and submitting and appealing to the regulators to reconsider this decision. And we are very hopeful that we will be heard by the regulator.

items.statement: Index derivatives relaunch drove INR 176 crores revenue; SENSEX derivatives hit record 52 crore contracts traded on May 3, 2024
items.quote: earned INR 176 crores from this segment despite having promotional offerings of lower transaction charges of INR 500 per crores of premium for Bankex and far-week contracts

items.statement: BSE Star MF revenue up 63% YoY to INR 128 crores; transactions up 55% to 41.1 crore in FY24
items.quote: BSE Star MF delivered yet another year of record revenues and performance, up 63% year -on-year to reach INR 128 crores. The total number of transactions processed at BSE StAR MF grew by 55% to reach 41.1 crores transactions in FY '24 from 26.5 crores in the previous year.

items.statement: Registered investors grew 41% from 12.1 crore to 17.1 crore unique client codes
items.quote: When I joined BSE, registered investors based on unique client code stood at 12.1 crores, which has since increased to 17.1 crores as on date, a growth of 41%.

items.statement: Derivatives segment has 400 members, 36 lakh active clients, and 100 FPIs; targets 500-600 members and 200-250 FPIs
items.quote: Today, we have around 400 members. We always like to grow to 500, 600 members. Today, we have around 3 million UCCs are trading with us. We always aspire for a bigger number there. Today, we have around 100 FPIs. We want to scale it to at least 200 to 250 FPIs.

items.statement: BSE StAR MF maintains 85-90% market share in mutual fund distribution
items.quote: We continue to have the same type of a market share of around 85% to 90%.

items.statement: Launched single stock derivatives effective July 1, 2024 with monthly expiry on second Thursday
items.quote: BSE has recently announced its foray into single stock derivatives space, effective 1st July 2024, all stock derivatives contract at BSE will expire on the second Thursday of the month.

items.statement: Developing new index products; will launch after current products stabilize
items.quote: we have qu ite a few product ideas. We are developing on every one of those ideas. I'm sure we will be coming with one behind the other as and when we feel the products that we have introduced are going on stabilizing

items.statement: NSE launched NIFTY Next 50 on Fridays without charge; BSE views market evolving toward buffet of products with high correlation enabling strategies
items.quote: over a period of time, I think more and more products will come in. So more and more products on a single day will continue to be there. And people will be choosing whatever for that day, they need to hedge whatever positions they have, so that every pr oduct will start functioning effectively and doing a very good economic role for the market

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 15 per share (face value INR 2); payout ratio 71.3% of standalone profit; total payout INR 206 crores
items.quote: The Board of Directors of BSE Limited has recommended a final dividend of INR 15 per equity share having a face value of INR 2 for the financial year 2023 -24, subject to the approval of shareholders in the ensuing Annual General Meeting. The total payout with a dividend payout ratio of 71.3% of the current year profits would be INR 206 crores on a stand-alone basis.

items.statement: Dividend payout reduced from ~100% to 71.3% due to INR 170 crore provision for SEBI differential fee and infrastructure investment needs
items.quote: This year, as you know, the last few weeks, we were to take the stand of providing for a significant amount of our profits towards the differential SEBI regulatory fee and we will be, of course, representing and requesting and appealing to the regulators. Notwithstanding that, as a matter of prudence, we have provided for that has significantly diverted the profits from what could be available for

items.statement: System stability issues on Feb 2 and Apr 12, 2024 due to sudden volatility and shallow order book; introduced Limit Price Protection surveillance measure
items.quote: On the two days that you mentioned, it is not the system's stability because of which any of those things happened. And the market movement suddenly happens in respect of exchange, where the order book is not very deep, when the stop-loss orders get triggered because of the change in volatility profile, trades happen at whatever prices that are available in the order book.

items.statement: Core SGF contribution for currency derivatives remains high despite volume decline; reduction requires regulatory approval and time due to peak-based calculation
items.quote: While technically over a period of time, this will be not required in currency because the volumes are coming down, it is suitable and necessary regulatory approvals it can be reused towards other things, other segments, I will not presume that because the volumes have fallen down in the last few weeks or few months immediately the Core SGF requirement will come down, because it is based on peak o

items.statement: Primary market capital raising via BSE platforms reached INR 21.3 lakh crores in FY24
items.quote: BSE platforms continue to remain the preferred choice by Indian companies to raise capital by enabling issuers to raise INR 21.3 lakh crores by means of equity, debt, bonds, commercial papers, etc.

items.statement: Combined market cap of BSE-listed stocks hit INR 400 lakh crores milestone for first time
items.quote: The combined market capitalization for all listed stocks on BSE hit the INR 400 lakh crores milestone for the first time ever, owing to the buoyancy in the Indian economy and participation across the spectrum.

items.statement: S&P Dow Jones Indices in discussions to divest stake in Asia Index Private Limited (50-50 JV with BSE)
items.quote: S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC is in discussion with BSE for divestment of its equity stake in Asia Index Private Limited, a 50 -50 joint venture with BSE.

items.statement: India INX volumes dwindling after NSE's GIFT NIFTY launch; BSE committed to developing GIFT City exchange
items.quote: Yes, we are also taking note of the fact that the volumes are dwindling. We are going to develop our efforts to do whatever best we can in the interest of the nation, whereby GIFT City continues to flourish and grow and most volumes come into the exchanges and give a breather for life.

items.statement: Revenue growth is a derivative of the overall economy and client earnings; management does not commit to a specific growth rate for the next 2-3 years.
items.quote: On on this front how the economy is likely to behave, your guess is as good as mine, but we are definitely a a derivative of the overall economy and earnings.

items.statement: H2 FY24 EBITDA margin dip to ~18% vs ~21% in H1 attributed to unbilled calls at quarter-end; gross margins remain stable.
items.quote: Okay, I think that has more to do with with the unbilled calls towards the end of the quarter should be broadly similar gross margin is what I would understand.

items.statement: Tech backend completely revamped and launched in first week of April 2024 to meet global standards for international expansion.
items.quote: Third and the most important up, more up, most important regular business update was we re -designed and re -developed the entire tech back -end. So that was , easily the most important update from us I list last year. So , we we just launched it in the first week of April, and, like this is the first week of this financial year.

items.statement: Headcount expanded by ~50 people in Q1 FY24; team now stabilized after recruitment and training phase.
items.quote: So, we did that in June, the first quarter was practically spent on recruitments, trainings, recruitments, trainings, and that is it. So , we expanded the company by almost 50 in in terms of number of people that was absolutely wonderful for us.

items.statement: US expert base expanding with 25-30 people working US hours; meaningful revenue from US clients expected in 1-2 years.
items.quote: On the US front, it is almost an independent team. Now , we have almost 25 -30 people, almost 3 teams working US hours. The business generation is still from India , but our Expert base in US has been expanding considerably, hopefully it should pay, pay us back in a few years.

items.statement: Launched visual mapping tools (Value Chains) out of beta; building expert-led courses (Pex-Panel) with a 3-4 member team under Research Head.
items.quote: Finally, somewhere at the end of last calendar year, we were able to launch it for our clients, and we've got some very good response that , that is fast turning our turning itself into a USB of sorts. We have been making a a lot of hundreds of Value Chains now, and updating them regularly.

items.statement: Top 10 clients contribute ~80-85% of revenue; concentration broadly unchanged since IPO, though trending slightly lower.
items.quote: Concentration, while within those 10 things have started stabilizing, but at at a top 10 level there is no significant change. It is, it might be on a lower trend. But it's broadly the same concentration even now.

items.statement: Top 4 industry verticals are IT Services, Healthcare Life Sciences, CPG Retail, and BFSI, representing ~60% of business.
items.quote: Industry basis, the top 4 would be top 4 would be as as it was reflected in the Indian economy, the IT services is top, Healthcare Life Sciences is is also amongst the top, CPG retail is, of course, there, and fourth is BFSI. These 4 together represent about 60% of our business.

items.statement: 70-80% of revenue comes from consulting firms (MBBs, tier-2, in-house strategy) vs financial markets.
items.quote: Most of our business actually comes from the consulting industry than the financial industry. We are more represented in the consulting industry which is the Big 3s, the way, the the MBBs, the Big 3s and tier-2 consulting firms, and maybe in-house strategy teams. Almost 70-80% would be from those set of clients.

items.statement: Business model is predominantly post-paid; financial services clients are more prepaid but smaller teams.
items.quote: Mostly, or mostly on on post, all on post -paid. The financial world is more prepaid where the teams are smaller.

items.statement: Holding ~Rs 30 Cr cash; ~Rs 10-12 Cr is residual IPO proceeds, rest earmarked for international expansion and potential inorganic opportunities.
items.value: Rs 30 Cr cash, Rs 10-12 Cr IPO proceeds
items.quote: Cash. Yes, so so out of that, out of that 30 Crores of sorts, I think somewhere around 10 to 12 Crores is the IPO cash or maybe a little less somewhere around 10, Abhishek would be able to give you the precise number, but the rest of it, we intend to use it for expansion outside the country.

items.statement: No specific acquisition targets identified; open to inorganic opportunities if they arise.
items.quote: Well, never say, never. But have we identified something, no.

items.statement: Abhay Sangal (VP-Operations) to take larger role in US Operations; operations to transition to autopilot mode.
items.quote: Abhay, who has been our offset , as of now in, you know, will likely to take up larger role in the US Operations and slowly we'll transition Ops more into autopilot mode.

items.statement: Repeat business high: 80%+ of calls by empanelled experts; 90%+ revenue from clients engaged 2-3+ years, many 5+ years.
items.quote: Two, repeat business, about 80% plus of our calls are done by Experts who are already empanelled with us in India and almost 90% of our business is by is our clients, which are probably 2, 3 years and more with us. In fact, a very significant percentage would be more than 5 years+.

items.statement: Ticket size in India broadly stable; focus on increasing calls per person via tech rather than raising prices; inflationary increases occur.

items.quote: I'm happy to share that we have recommended a total dividend of INR 5 per share, that is 100% of the face value of INR 5 each for the year ended March 2024.

items.statement: US 54% of revenue, UK/Europe 13%, Rest of World including India 33%
items.quote: In terms of geographical footprint, US remains our largest geo, with 54% of our business coming from US market, followed by U.K. and Europe at 13% and the rest of the world, including India at 33%.

items.statement: Digital Operations revenue INR 694.4 crores (10.1% YoY), EBIT margin 19.9% for FY24
items.quote: Our Digital Operations revenue was INR694.4 crores, which is 10.1% up from previous year. Digital Operations EBIT margin remains healthy at 19.9%.

items.statement: Digital Experience revenue INR 244 crores (11.2% YoY), EBIT margin 17.1% for FY24
items.quote: Our Digital Experience revenue was to INR 244 crores, which is 11.2% growth over previous year. And Digital Experience EBIT margin remains at 17.1% on a full year basis.

items.statement: Digital Technologies revenue INR 611.5 crores (0.4% YoY), EBIT margin 4.6% for FY24
items.quote: Our Digital Technologies revenue was at INR 611.5 crores, which is slight up 0.4%. EBIT margin for Technology business was at 4.6%.

items.statement: Macro uncertainty causing slowdown in Western tech/outsourcing spend; pipeline softness in Digital Technologies
items.quote: We see the Western world slowing down on their technology and outsourcing spends due to the uncertain macroeconomic environment. However, we expect a growth of 7% to 8%, while maintaining the current margins for the next financial year.

items.statement: AFC business targeting US metro/road deals ($10-40M range); bidding for Pune Metro, evaluating Mumbai Metro lines 4,5,6,9
items.quote: We're targeting the metro and the roads. And road means buses and things like that. And in the metros, there are multiple segments. The top ones like you have Chicago or New York City, these are very large, they are $500 million-plus deals. We will not qualify for those deals. Then the multitude of these that are between $10 million to $40 million. Datamatics qualifies for those deals very well.

items.statement: FY25 EXM payroll growth guided at 20-25% YoY; CXM full-year growth expected in high teens or early 20% range
items.value: 20-25% EXM, high teens to early 20% CXM
items.quote: Coming to EXM, as I have said in the previous calls also, we continue to believe that we can definitely grow in excess of 20% year-on-year. So, I would say that I would put a range of between 20% and 25% in terms of where we would grow the standalone payroll business.

items.statement: FY25 overall revenue growth guided at 18-22% for EXM and similar for CXM; EBITDA margin to see small uptick after investments and inflation
items.quote: So, yes, I think growth and margins have already covered both in the opening remarks and in the answer to the earlier question that we believe that we should be able to grow the respective businesses anywhere between 18% and 22-25% depending, of course, largely in terms of how the new sales span out.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps to 24.6%; Q4 CXM segment margin up 77.2% YoY, EXM segment margin up 47.7% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the Financial Year is INR 116 crores, a growth of 30.7% from last year. The EBITDA margin increased by 200 bps on a Y-o-Y and FY '24 EBITDA margin stands at 24.6%.

items.statement: EXM Q4 segment margin of 38% includes 3.5% one-time tax vouching benefit; steady-state target ~35%
items.quote: As far as EBITDA margins are concerned, I would just like to point out that the 38% margins have about 3.5% for the one time activities which we do in Q4 on the tax vouching. So, if we adjust this 3.5%, the quarter-on-quarter is about a percent more. The long-term target is around 35%-mark steady state.

items.statement: FY24 EXM new sales ACV INR 27 cr, up 35% YoY; Q4 EXM new sales ACV INR 7 cr vs INR 4 cr in Q3
items.quote: We have signed EXM sales with ACV of 7 crores in Q4, up from INR 4 crores in Q3. For FY '24. We have achieved new sales of ACV INR 27 crores, 35% higher than the previous year.

items.statement: CXM added two new logos aggregating just under INR 100 cr ACV for the year; healthcare account LOBs expanded
items.quote: In CXM we have added new LOBs in the healthcare account which we had won in the end of the previous financial year and also added two new logos aggregating to just under 100 crores ACV for the year.

items.statement: Demand environment stable; corporates open to outsourcing payroll/HR value chain; RFPs continue from in-house payroll
items.quote: We don't see either improvement or a diminution in the demand environment. What we continue to see is that corporates are pretty open to doing payroll or other parts of the HR value chain outsourcing.

items.statement: Manila CXM capacity near full; evaluating cost-effective expansion options; domestic CXM capacity adequate
items.quote: We are pretty much now with near full capacity in Manila. So, for our growth, we will have to keep our options open in terms of whether there are more cost effective options in Manila or we continue to grow in Central Manila where we are currently located.

items.statement: International revenue share rising: CXM international up 39% YoY and 13.3% QoQ; FY24 international contribution increased 12% YoY for EXM
items.quote: FY '24, our overall split between domestic and international was in the region of about 57-43 so 57% from international customers and 43% from domestic customers

items.statement: CXM vertical mix: BFSI ~60-65%, healthcare growing; EXM top sectors IT/ITES and manufacturing; no significant logo losses
items.quote: As far as the new business acquisition in CXM, I think it's a mix of both. So, as I mentioned, BFSI and Healthcare are two of our key verticals in CXM of which BFSI is almost about 60%-65% as of now, but with the growth in healthcare which has happened this year, that number will come down.

items.statement: Q4 collections INR 131.4 cr, up INR 7.1 cr QoQ; cash position robust
items.quote: Our collections for Quarter 4 increased to 131.4 crores up by 7.1 crores quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR 22.9 cr (INR 15/share); FY24 total dividend INR 68.6 cr (INR 45/share), 2.25x prior year
items.quote: Further, the Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of Rs. 22.9 crores at the rate of Rs. 15 per share, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM, which brings the total dividend payout for the full year at Rs. 68.6 crores, which would be Rs. 45 a share, 2.25 X (times) of the previous year.

items.statement: Platform upgrade costs (Smart Pay SP4, HRMS v2) already capitalized; no significant incremental capex expected in FY25
items.quote: On your question on platforms, as mentioned in one of our earlier calls, the cost relating to those are already in the balance sheet and those will be amortized over an appropriate period of time, again, as per the market practice and accounting standards. So, there are no incremental costs expected on those platforms, at least for this year other than small add-on investments if needed, but I don

items.statement: Average headcount grew ~12% YoY FY23-FY24; March-end headcount just under 6,000; headcount growth to remain in similar ballpark FY25
items.quote: So, the average headcount between FY '23 and FY '24 has grown by about 12%.

items.statement: EXM processes 1.32 million employee records (market leader, 20-30% above competitors); payslips per FTE improved 10% YoY
items.quote: We have added new employee records in excess of 4 lakhs in H2 and now process 1.32 million employee records at the end of March, remaining the clear market leader in the managed services space, being 20% to 30% higher than competitors' volume.

items.statement: CXM FTE grew 9.5% YoY, 1.7% QoQ; attrition maintained at 7.2% per month (near best-in-class)
items.quote: Our staff attrition was maintained at 7.2% per month for Q4, which continues to be near best-in-class in the domestic outsourcing industry.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by higher international mix, productivity (payslips/FTE), new logos, cost savings; absorbed salary and non-wage inflation
items.quote: A higher share of international and cost savings from operational efficiencies have enabled us to improve EBITDA margins by 200 basis points over FY '23 even after absorbing salary and other inflation.

items.statement: Evaluating niche capability acquisitions in healthcare/RCM; some targets acquired by others at higher valuations; organic build also an option but slower
items.quote: we continue to look at it, I mean, we will continue to balance the niche capability acquisition, the referenceability, the mar ket endorsement which an acquisition can get vis-a-vis what we have to pay for that acquisition. So, we were looking at some assets which have got concluded with other players at a much higher number, then what we were talking about

items.statement: CXM new US sales (hired sales leader March 1, account-based marketing for SME BFSI/Healthcare) expected to contribute only from Q2 FY25; quarterly mining visibility limited
items.quote: We believe that some of the revenues for the new business should only start getting in from Q2 and not prior to that as per our Annual plan.

items.statement: Local Level Compliance (LLC) business sold to Aparajitha Corporate Services; financial closure 30 April 2024; assets classified as held for sale
items.quote: And as far as the held for proceed (held for sale) number is concerned, that relates to our LLC transaction, which was the sale of our local level compliance business to Aparajitha C orporate Services. The formal financial closure of the transaction happened only on 30th April

items.statement: Management expects ~10% volume growth in coming years and targets value-added product mix >50% of revenue within 1-1.5 years
items.quote: So considering everything put together, we should be in a range of volumes. We should consider 10% around volumes for the coming up, coming years.

items.statement: Debt repayment of INR145 cr in FY25 and INR174 cr in FY26; no new loans planned for FY25
items.quote: Secondly, as far as going forward we are definitely tearing down some of our debt which is a normal repayment of debt of about INR150 crores in the next year. So that will definitely come down.

items.statement: Routine capex INR15-20 cr/year; major expansion capex not yet decided; INR840 cr invested over last 1.5 years (30% to fabric/knitting, rest to spinning)
items.value: INR15-20 cr routine; major capex TBD
items.quote: Normal capex, which is of the routine nature, is about INR15 crores to INR20 crores t hat is happening. That happens every year due to various requirements for debottlenecking and other things. Apart from that, major capex plan has not yet been decided

items.statement: Yarn capacity ~91k tons vs rated 110k tons (max 105k tons); fabric/weaving can improve 7-8%; knitting utilization lower with scope to improve; overall ~10% volume headroom
items.quote: Our rated capacity is around 1,10,000 tons per annum. And we can produce, after giving all efficiencies and others, about 1,05,000 tons. So, we are looking for that kind of capacity utilization which is about 10% more from the present last year's capacity.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 14.52%; management indicates maintaining ~14.5% would be substantial improvement over FY24 average 13%; long-term target 16-20% if export demand and FTAs materialize
items.quote: Basically, we do not give any projections for the margins. But just an indication is that our last quarter margin was 14.5. So, if you are able to maintain that also it should be substantial improvement from the existing levels, yearly levels.

items.statement: Cotton prices stable at INR57-58k/candy (±INR3k) for 6-8 months; expected to remain stable this calendar year; yarn realization FY24 INR274/kg vs FY23 INR338/kg (-19%); fabric realization FY24 INR160/m vs FY23 INR182/m
items.quote: Cotton prices have remained in the range of INR 57,000, INR58,000 plus minus INR3,000 a candy for good last 6 months, 7 months, 8 months which is going to continue going forward as well as we look forward.

items.statement: Export demand improving at normal pace; China re-importing cotton yarn (+35-40% YoY in March); Indian exports improved last 6-8 months, expected stable next 6 months; full demand recovery may take 5-6 more months
items.quote: Demand is definitely improving and it is not a very fast pace. It is a normal pace. If you see the data of imports by various of these countries we are seeing that China has started to re-import large quantities.

items.statement: Export mix targeted at 55-60% of revenue (down from 73% in FY22); domestic and export realizations similar; exports include both yarn and fabric
items.quote: As a strateg y, we would rather keep ourselves limited up to 50 -- in the band of 55 % to 60% on the export side. And that's what we're doing

items.statement: Total debt INR1,339 cr (INR811 cr long-term, INR383 cr WC, INR145 cr current maturities); term debt 5.5% net of subsidies (new loans at full rate pending sanction); WC ~7.5%; debt/equity 1.15-1.16; target interest cost 2.5-3% of revenue
items.quote: As of March 24, the company's debt profile stood at INR1,339 crores comprising INR811 crores in long-term debt, INR383 crores working capital and INR145 crores as current maturities of term loan.

items.statement: Solar capacity increased from 12-13 MW to 23 MW (+10 MW); adding 7-8 MW more in current year; solar generation ~2.7 cr units/yr at lower cost vs grid INR7-7.5/unit; renewables 7-8% of power mix; INR95-100 cr invested in solar over 3 years
items.quote: We have added substantial solar capacity -- solar power capacity. Now our capacity is about 23 megawatts. If you see at the end of the last year this capacity was about 12, 13 megawatts. So we have added more than 10 megawatts of capacity.

items.statement: Value-added products ~38-40% of revenue (fabric 25-26% + value-added yarn 14-15%); target >50% in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: So that all put together, it is about 38 % to 40%, where we do a reasonable value addition in comparison to normal commodity yarns. So this proportion slowly is going up. We expect that total, we should be doing it more than 50%.

items.statement: Government schemes (textile parks, PLI, export incentives) delayed due to elections; expected implementation post-elections to aid long-term growth; FTA with EU could benefit >20% of sales (UK only 3-4%)
items.quote: The measures were in active consideration, however held up due to elections. I hope implementation of these schemes post -elections will h elp long-term growth of Indian textile industry

items.statement: Board recommended dividend 25% (INR2.5/share), same as last year
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of 25% i.e. INR2.5 per share, i.e. same as last year.

items.statement: Captive consumption 20% of yarn production; depreciation run-rate INR36 cr/quarter (INR145 cr/yr) on current asset base
items.quote: Yeah, this INR36 crores every quarter will be charged. So the average -- the depreciation next year is expected to be on the current set of fixed assets is about INR145 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (Russia-Ukraine, Red Sea crisis) increasing freight costs and transit times; margin recovery dependent on export demand pickup and FTA implementation
items.quote: Despite ongoing geopolitical challenges such as Russia-Ukraine conflict, Red Sea crisis, which has resulted in a higher freight cost and extended transit times, our country's cotton textile exports have demonstrated a healthy rebound.

items.statement: Target to double AUM to $125 billion by 2030; could reach by 2029 if 15-20% growth sustained
items.quote: REC management and board have decided to have a clear-cut roadmap and we are targeting to double our asset under management to about $125 billion by the year 2030.

items.statement: Target renewable energy portfolio to grow 10x to $40 billion by 2030 from current $4 billion
items.quote: We are trying to increase our renewable energy portfolio by 10x to about $40 billion by the end 2030.

items.statement: Target non-power infrastructure logistics AUM to grow fourfold to $25 billion by 2030
items.quote: We are anticipating that our total asset under management from non-power infrastructure logistics will see fourfold growth to say about $25 billion by the end of 2030.

items.statement: Expect 30% AUM from renewables, 15-20% from non-power infra, 50-55% from conventional by 2030
items.quote: By the year 2030, we would like to double our asset under management to about $125 billion, 30% of it will come from renewable energy segment, 15% to 20% will come from non-power infrastructure logistics, and 50% to 55% of asset under management will come from conventional coal-based generation capacity, distribution and transmission sector.

items.statement: Sanctioned projects worth $43 billion in FY24, up 34% from $32.2 billion in FY23
items.quote: We sanctioned projects worth $43 billion in the last financial year, as compared to $32.2 billion which we had sanctioned in FY23.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 67% to $19.3 billion in FY24 from $11.6 billion in FY23
items.quote: The disbursements have also grown by 67% or total disbursement stood around $19.3 billion last financial year, as compared to $11.6 billion in FY23.

items.statement: Renewable energy sanctions pipeline of over INR175,000 crores for current financial year
items.quote: In the current financial year, we have a huge pipeline of projects amounted to more than INR175,000 crores.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced 15 bps to 7.13% in FY24; spread improved 41 bps to 2.86%; NIM up 19 bps to 3.57%
items.quote: We were able to bring down our cost of funds by 15 bps from 7.28% in the last financial year to 7.13% in FY '24. The spread has already improved by 41 basis points from 2.45% to 2.86%. The net interest margin has seen an increase of 19 bps from 3.38% to 3.57%.

items.statement: Profit after tax grew 29% to $2.12 billion (PBT); net profit up 27% to $1.68 billion in FY24
items.quote: Our total profit after tax at the end of the financial year was about $2.12 billion -- profit before tax, sorry, profit before tax. And our net profit has seen an increase of 27%. It was about $1.68 billion.

items.statement: Return on net worth at 22.17% in FY24
items.quote: Our return on net worth was about 22.17%.

items.statement: Power demand increased 8% in FY24 and 11% in April 2024
items.quote: Last year, power demand increased by 8%. And in the current financial in the last month in April, power demand has increased by 11%.

items.statement: RBI draft circular proposes phased additional provisioning for under-construction projects: 2% by Mar-25, 3.5% by Mar-26, 5% by Mar-27
items.quote: But it's to be effected in phased manner by 31st March, 2025, only 2% provision has to be done. By 31st March 2026, 3.5% provisioning has to be done. And by 31st March, 2027, 5% crossing has to be done.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines not applicable to loans backed by state government guarantees (~40% of loan book)
items.quote: This RBI guideline would not be applicable to these loans which have been supported by the state government guarantee. About 40% of our loan is supported by the state government guarantee.

items.statement: Distribution CapEx loans backed by state guarantees (65% of distribution portfolio) exempt from RBI provisioning
items.quote: the total book size under the distribution segment is close to 25.75 billion, out of which the CapEx which is supposed to attract provisioning requirement is only 9 billion, which is just 35% of total dis tribution portfolio

items.statement: Expect write-backs of INR1,500-2,000 crores in FY25; target net zero NPA by end FY25
items.quote: We are expecting a write-back to the tune of INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores in the financial year FY '25. And we hope that all this asset would get resolved in the current financial year itself and will become net zero NPA company by the end of FY '25.

items.statement: Gross NPA INR13,800 crores; INR2,222 crores (7 projects) fully provided heading to liquidation
items.quote: Our gross NPA is about INR13,800 crores. And out of that, about 7 projects are heading towards liquidation that is amounting to INR2,222 crores. For this, we already made 100% provisioning.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio 25.82% vs 15% minimum; Tier 1 capital 23.32% vs 10% minimum
items.quote: Our minimum capital ratio required is 15%, and we are having about 25.82%. For Tier 1 capital, the RBI statutory minimum requirement is 10%, and we are having to the tune of 23.32%.

items.statement: May pass on some RBI provisioning impact to borrowers via higher lending rates, but lower borrowing costs may offset
items.quote: We'll have to pass on some impact of this -- we'll be able to pass on to the borrower. But another -- the silver line of fact is that, our cost of borrowing is going to come down in after Q2, Q3. Once this cost of borrowing comes down, we'll pass on or perhaps balance out actually.

items.statement: Green bond funding provides 10-15 bps cost advantage for renewable projects, offsetting provisioning impact
items.quote: There are a number of lenders who are willing to lend at slightly lower rates as compared to the normal raising, which we are doing, both in domestic market as well as the international market. So there are enough funds which are available, and the differential is about 10 to 15 basis points as compared to the normal borrowing which we are doing for general purposes, for conventional generation al

items.statement: Additional 94 GW coal capacity identified by 2032; REC targets 30-40% share of capex financing
items.quote: About 94 gigawatt capacity has been identified to be brought in by year 2032, in the next 8 years, all the approvals for this additional coal-based capacity will happen next 2 to 3 years. There also, we see a huge potential or REC, we'll be able to share at 30% to 40% of the coal base capacity, addition capital would be coming in the next 8 years.

items.statement: Distribution infrastructure upgrade opportunity over next 10-12 years as assets are 40-50 years old
items.quote: After RDSS period is over and the modernization is over, in the next 4 to 5 years, country will still require a lot of CapEx for upgrading the infrastructure, because distribution infrastructure all the poles, wires, the distribution transformer is quite old, 40 to 50 years old.

items.statement: Renewable sanctions in FY24: large hydro INR32,450 Cr, pump storage INR28,304 Cr, solar INR21,000 Cr, module manufacturing INR21,565 Cr, green hydrogen INR8,000 Cr, e-mobility INR8,000 Cr
items.quote: Last year, we sanctioned project of INR136,515 crores. Out of this, large hydro projects constitute about INR32,450 crores, pump storage hydro project was about INR28,304 crores; followed by solar, about INR21,000 crores. Then model manufacturing was INR21,565 crores; followed by green hydrogen project, about INR8,000 crores we have sanctioned; electric mobility, about INR8,000 crores.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines may reduce Tier 1 capital by INR2,000-3,000 crores over 3 years but won't impact approval process
items.quote: Even if this Tier 1 capital gets reduced by say 2,000 to 3,000, it will not impact our approval process.

items.statement: Only ~20% of AUM (INR1 lakh crore) impacted by RBI draft guidelines; 80% of renewable book already commissioned
items.quote: Out of 5 lakh crores this asset under management, most of them are already commissioned. Only 1 lakh crore of projects are under construction, which will get impacted.

items.statement: Ramped up manpower and hired sector experts for infrastructure logistics appraisal since Oct 2022 diversification
items.quote: We have ramped up our manpower strength. We have got in experts from different fields, putting to infrastructure logistics.

items.statement: Government committed to 50 GW annual renewable capacity addition from FY25 vs 12-14 GW previously
items.quote: From this year onwards, they stepped up their ambitions and per annum, they are targeting installation of 50 gigawatt capacities.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines on project finance exposure norms will impact Tier 1 capital; state government guaranteed loans are kept out of exposure norms per common understanding with RBI.
items.quote: As for exposure is concerned, we are very clear that state government guaranteed loan are not counted. Yes, out of the purview.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines apply to all under-construction capex projects regardless of DCCO extension; company will request RBI to limit applicability to DCCO-funded projects only.
items.quote: It will be on all under-construction project -- all CapEx projects. So we have made it clear, it will be affecting all the under construction projects despite whether it is DCCO shift or not.

items.statement: Loan book grew 17% in current year; if sustained, INR 10 lakh crore target could be reached by FY29 instead of FY30.
items.quote: If we are able -- like this year, our asset grew by about 17%. If this 17% growth is continued, then we'll be able to reach this INR10 lakh crores by the year 2029 itself, in next 5 years, not 6 years.

items.statement: Targeting minimum INR 175,000 crore disbursements this year, up from INR 151,000 crore last year, with significant increase in capex disbursements.
items.quote: But this year, o ur CapEx disbursement are going to jump quite substantially. And we are targeting minimum INR175,000 crores

items.statement: Renewable energy share of total assets to grow from 7% to 30% in 5-6 years; conventional generation 29% growing 2-3% annually; distribution & transmission 40% stable; logistics 15-20% by 2030.
items.quote: Right now, share of renewable energy is only 7% of our total assets. It will gradually increase to 30% in the next 5 to 6 years. So every year, we see that incremental growth of 5% to 7% growth will be there as far as renewable energy is concerned.

items.statement: Spread expected to improve from 2.8% to 3% driven by higher-margin coal-based generation (94 GW pipeline, 40% share target), large hydro, pump storage, and non-power infra.
items.quote: So we do hope that our spread is going to improve further, not going to come down. It may go up to 3% actually, from 2.8% it may increase to 3% actually.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced 15 bps from 7.28% to 7.13%; ECB share increased from 24% to 29%; all-in ECB cost 6.6-6.7% via innovative hedging; 54EC bonds target >INR 50,000 crore.
items.quote: You might have seen that our cost of funds has come down by 15 basis points from 7.28% to 7.13%. And the share of our external commercial borrowing has increased from 24% to 29%.

items.statement: 7 projects worth INR 2,222 crore heading for liquidation, fully provisioned; no new NPA added in last 9 quarters; targeting net NPA zero by FY25.
items.quote: Not 9, 7 projects are getting towards liquidation, total value of INR2,222 crores, for which we already made 100% provisioning.

items.statement: No impairment reserve currently as Ind AS provisioning already exceeds IRAC norms; standard asset provisioning ~0.5% overall, up to 1% on individual projects.
items.quote: Our provisioning is already higher than the IRAC norms, there is no impairment reserves at present.

items.statement: Power demand grew 8% last year and 11% in April; DISCOM AT&C losses fell from 22% to 15.5% over 2 years under RDSS; state gencos/transcos health improving.
items.quote: The AT&C loss, which was 22% 2 years back, came down to roughly 16.5% and then it has now further come down to 15.5%.

items.statement: 94 GW coal-based capacity pipeline; targeting minimum 40% business share; lending rates 10-11% for coal projects with ability to pass on incremental provisioning costs.
items.quote: You might have observed that our lending rate is the highest in respect of coal based capacity only. It varies from 10% to 11% actually. This 94 gigawatt capacity, some additional impact was because additional provisioning some impact would be there, that we'll be able to pass on actually.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines may impair bank lending capacity for private capex, creating opportunity for REC to capture high-quality assets with less competition.
items.quote: But then that gives us greater opportunity. In any case, we are a very active lender in the power sector space, and we started lending operations in the interest space as well.

items.statement: Tier 1 capital impact from RBI guidelines to be calculated after final norms; comments due by June; impact may reflect in Q1 or Q2 results depending on final guideline timing.
items.quote: So whatever impact will be there in any case, the comments are to be sent by June. So in case they come out with the final guidelines before the first quarterly results, then in any case, we'll be having the impact there in the first quarterly result itself.

items.statement: Collections increasing; 54EC capital gains tax saving bonds at INR 40,000 crore targeting >INR 50,000 crore; foreign currency borrowing with innovative hedging at 6.6-6.7% all-in cost.
items.quote: One is 54 EC bonds that is capital gains tax saving ins trument, that is about 40,000. That also will increase to more than INR50,000 crores. That's what we are targeting.Collections are going to increase

items.statement: Bridge financing and RBPF not covered under RBI project finance definition as DCCO required; only projects meeting specific definition fall under new norms.
items.quote: There is a definition of project which is given under these guidelines. So we have to go by that definition. So these type of bridge financing which they are doing or even if we are doing RBPF for this type of funding, so that won't be covered in -- because in any case, DCCO has to be there for these type of project.

items.statement: Banks largely absent from infra financing; private sector banks (ICICI, HDFC) not in infra; state banks lend to REC which on-lends to projects leveraging REC's evaluation capability.
items.quote: Actually, banks in any case are not lending for the infra. In case you see the private sector banks, ICICI, HDFC nowhere they are in case of the infra financing. It's only the state sector banks which are there.

items.statement: 70% of profits retained to grow net worth (ROE >20%), 30% paid as dividend; write-backs from stressed asset resolutions (KSK etc.) expected next year.
items.quote: So there'll be 70% in any case will be going towards the net worth itself, 30% we have to declare by way of dividend. Remaining will be incrementally going towards the net worth itself.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires mentioned in transcript.
items.quote: On behalf of REC, I would like to thank all the participants for asking inquisitive questions and hope that we have been able to answer your queries and on the various issues to your satisfaction.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected around INR 5,500-5,600 crore based on order book execution
items.quote: So, INR 1,700 crores of CV, about INR 3,600 crores of wagon. So that means INR 5,300 crores and maybe some amount of the current year order book executed. So, about INR 5,500 crores, INR 5,600 crores turnover is a reasonable possibility, right? For the current year?

items.statement: Order backlog at INR 7,10,166 lakh, highest ever, with 75% wagons executable over 18 months and balance CV business in FY25
items.quote: In terms of outlook, we are pleased to report an order backlog of INR 7,10,166 lakh our highest ever.

items.statement: Capex of INR 1,000-1,500 crore planned for Bonatrans wheel set backward integration over 18-24 months

items.quote: In security services, our sales pipeline remains robust with 26 new contracts with an ACV of INR 23 crores between Q4 and Q1.

items.statement: Invested in technology and process automation with BCG; reduced FTE headcount from 5,500 to 5,300
items.quote: Our investment in technology and process automation have complemented the productivity improvement projects that we ran in association with BCG. We added 149 new contracts, with an ACV of INR 232 crores, during the quarter, bringing the total number of new contracts signed during FY 2024 to 737.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced INR 162 cr in FY24 to INR 369 cr, lowest in 5 years; cumulative INR 700+ cr repaid over 5 years
items.quote: Our gross debt is at its lowest level in last five years, ending the year at INR 369 crores of gross debt, a reduction of INR 162 crores during this fiscal.

items.statement: DSO reduced 4 days to 53 days; OCF/EBITDA at 67%; driven by disciplined WC management, business mix, Qdigi divestment
items.quote: Our cash conversion continues to be strong with operating cash -to-EBITDA at a healthy 67%, aided by reduct ion of four days in DSO which now stands at 53 days.

items.statement: Further DSO improvement possible with continued disciplined WC management across group
items.quote: We do believe, if we'll continue with disciplined working capital management across the group we'll be able to even further improve from the present DSO range.

items.statement: Final dividend INR 6/share declared, full year INR 10/share; INR 488 cr cumulative dividends over 4 years
items.quote: We declared a final dividend of INR 6 per share, aggregating to INR 10 per share for full year. Our prudent capital allocation policy has resulted in a cumulative debt repayment of INR 700+ crores and dividend payout of INR 488 crores in last 5 years.

items.statement: Capital allocation priority: optimize OCF, retire debt, return balance to shareholders per dividend policy
items.quote: So we'll continue to do three things; optimize our operating cash flows, retire as much debt as possible and return the balance money to the shareholders in line with our stated dividend policy.

items.statement: Divested break-fix business Qdigi effective 31 Mar 2024 at 15% IRR; FY24 revenue INR 370 cr
items.quote: As part of our strategy to fo cus and nurture our core businesses, we completed our divestment of our break-fix business Qdigi, effective 31st March 2024, with an IRR of 15%.

items.statement: IT staffing softness reflected in top 5 IT cos headcount decline; GCCs now employ 1.6M; focus on capturing GCC market share
items.quote: Coming to IT staffing, the softness in overall IT indu stry is reflected in the fact that aggregate head count of top 5 IT companies declined by 11,200 in Q4 and 69,000 in FY 2024. Addition to the IT workforce in India has been mostly through GCCs, who now employ about 1.6 million. We expect this trend to continue along with stabilization in hiring in IT services companies.

items.statement: Foundit operational breakeven achieved in Q4; FY24 loss reduced to INR 55 cr from INR 95 cr; target zero loss FY25
items.quote: foundit has achieved its operational breakeven during the year in Q4 with a reduction in bur n. The sales grew by 9% year -on-year and 13% quarter -on-quarter driven by enterprise sales and B2C sales.

items.statement: Foundit targets zero EBITDA loss in FY25 driven by growth; cost structure stabilized post product development phase
items.quote: And the objective clearly is to ensure that this number goes down to INR 0 in FY 2025 and which is going to primarily come from growth. And most of the costs have stabilized in the system.

items.statement: GTS internal target ~20% growth; 3-4 year CAGR ~18%; no formal 2-year revenue guidance given
items.quote: If you just go by what happened in the past and go to the last Quess Corp Limited. May 10, 2024 three to four years, consistently, we have tried to, internally, we have tried to grow at 20% plus growth. Some years, we have been successful. Some years, we have just fallen short, but you'll find, I think, CAGR would be around 18% over the last three, four

items.statement: OAM FY24 grew 7%; order book strong for FY25; targeting growth beyond current numbers
items.quote: In the current financial year, in FY 2024, we grew at 7%. This is on back of certain operational levers we worked on, on profitability, as we discussed in the past quarters. I think we look for growth beyond these numbers.

items.statement: General staffing headcount crossed 400k milestone; added 60k associates in FY24 (excl F&F); 274 new logos, 30% first-time outsourcers
items.quote: During the year, we have crossed 400,000 headcount milestone. We are now among the top 5 global staffing companies by head count and aspire to become the largest staffing company globally. Business added 78 new logos in Q4, taking the financial year total to over 274. Among the clients added during the year, 30% have used outsourcing staffing for the first time.

items.statement: Associate pulse survey: 88% very satisfied/satisfied (up from 85%), 78% definitely/very likely to recommend Quess
items.quote: I am happy to announce that in a recent conducted survey between Q3 and Q4, our pulse survey covering 156,000 associates, 88% have rated themselves as 'very satisfied' or 'satisfied', up by 85% compared to the previous year. 78% of our associates are 'definitely likely' or 'very likely' to recommend Quess to their peers.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to moderate to 45-46% range over next couple of quarters due to salary hikes
items.quote: However, 46.1% is probably the higher end of what we will expect going forward. There could be some moderation in the next quarter or 2 because of the sal ary impact. However, we will work to kind of keep it within range bound around 45% to 46

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin at 46.1%, up 220 bps YoY and over 100 bps QoQ
items.quote: Operating EBITDA of 46.1% is the highest we have seen in the last 2 years. It's up 220 basis points year-on-year. So not only have we seen the margin grow in terms of absolute numbers, the mark-in has also expanded in terms of the percentage.

items.statement: Non-MF EBITDA margin crept up from 15% to over 20%, steady state seen at 35-40%
items.quote: We have seen a creep up in the margins of non-MF given that the platform businesses are predominantly are all platform businesses. We've seen what used to be a 15% kind of overall EBITDA level across all businesses, that's now crept up to more than 20%.

items.statement: Live SIP book grew 37% YoY vs industry 32%, unique investor base up 25% to 30 million vs industry 18%
items.quote: Our live SIP book grew 37% ahead of an overall industry number of 32%. So that was very satisfying. And then our unique investor base crossed INR3 crores or INR30 million. And this again is a foundational metric, if you get more investors, they come into more SIPs.

items.statement: Payments added over 80 new client wins in FY24

Revenue grew a stratospheric 90%.

items.statement: Significant investment in data centers, capacity, availability, storage, processing, perimeter security, monitoring
items.quote: it also means a significant investment in data centers, capacity, availability, storage, processing, perimeter security, monitoring. Just think of every aspect of it. items.statement: GIFT City larger office leased, opening in July, larger team hired

items.statement: Yields broadly in line with expectations, minor depletion from telescopic pricing but no big disruption seen over next few quarters
items.quote: We do not see a big d isruption happening or depletion happening in the yields going forward. items.statement: Pay, KRA, AIF to remain top 3 non-MF growth engines in FY25, account aggregator to start contributing
items.quote: What added to the momentum of non-MF growth is KRA as the biggest engine, pay as the second and AIF as the third. And I think in this year, I'm expecting the same to happen, which means these 3 will remain the engines, which will drive the growth.

items.quote: So if you -- and even after that, we will have excess of INR525 crores, INR530 crores of cash on the books. That is the minimum net worth requirements for specific businesses. items.quote: We believe that a good target could come out of payments and insurance. And more than that, I don't have much to share because we haven't really thought sharper than that. We continue to scan the market all the time.

items.quote: Going forward, we see that there will be some -- there could be some moderation because of the annual appraisal cycle coming in, in April. However, now we will look to mitigate it to the maximum possible extent.

items.quote: For the current financial year as well, keeping in mind the similar set of objectives, we have set certain targets. We have drawn upon our plans to add 130 showrooms in India, 80 Kalyan and 50 Candere. And we will also open 6 showrooms overseas during the current financial year.

So there, it will be only INR 150 crores.

items.statement: Opened 58 new Kalyan franchise showrooms in India and 1 in Middle East in FY24
items.quote: In line with our already announced showroom network expansion plan, we launched 58 new Kalyan showrooms through the capital efficient FOCO model in India during the last financial year. items.statement: Franchise revenue share was ~25% in Q4 FY24 and ~20% for full year FY24

items.quote: While we reduced our non-GML loans in India by INR 435 crores, we have been successful in securing additional GML limits of INR 170 crores. Overall, working capital loans in India came down by INR 270 crores.

items.quote: In line with our announced dividend policy, Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of approximately INR120 crores, payout in excess of 20% of the net profit generated during FY 2024. This represents more than doubling of the dividend paid for FY 2023.

items.statement: Dividend policy payout range 15-30% of net profit
items.quote: Yes. I mentioned it's between 15% to 30%. And this year, there's 20% of net profit approximately, which we have already announced.

items.statement: No pricing pressure from competition for past 4-5 quarters; margins stable year-on-year
items.quote: We have not seen a major difference in price competitiveness over the past 4 or 5 quarters. And you see our margins have also been stable over the last 4 quarters year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin decline solely due to franchise mix shift, not making charges or gold pricing

items.statement: First US store (owned) expected before end of H1 FY25

items.statement: Lesser provision for bad debts this year versus last year
items.quote: We also have lesser provision of bad debts this year versus what it was last year.

items.quote: We are looking at a strong double-digit growth in Elite and Premium. We also mentioned that we're looking at single-digit growth in economy and popular. So, when you take those two together, you're not looking at 15% volume growth.

items.statement: Wine tourism revenue expected to grow at very strong double-digit in FY25 and decade beyond
items.quote: We continue to be extremely bullish about the growth prospects ahead and we see very strong double-digit growth ahead in FY'25 and in the decade beyond.

items.statement: Long-term elite and premium volume growth guidance of 15% remains intact

items.quote: In FY25 we are expecting a 3% decline in packaging material cost per case which goes well for margins going forward. In FY24 with some of the geopolitical issues we have seen a 4% to 5% increase in packaging material costs and that is now moderating coming down by about 3%.

items.statement: Non-traditional markets (Telangana, Rajasthan) driving growth; CSD business grew >50% and is biggest growth segment; Mumbai and Goa challenging in FY24, expect softness to continue in FY25; Karnataka growing well

items.quote: We see some softness in Q1. However, we have some very strong hopes for the entire FY. In Q1, with the elections happening, the kind of restrictions that have been placed on AlcoBev, are much harder than anything that we've seen in the past.

items.quote: The headcount of our sales team will be growing in the region of 8%-10% and I am happy to report that almost 80% of this increase is going to be coming from Tier 2 and smaller cities as we look to build a broad base for wine consumption.

items.statement: FY24 standalone: Revenue INR103.19 crores (+46.34%), EBITDA INR51.68 crores (+40.69%), PBT INR50.18 crores (+41.64%), PAT INR26.44 crores, EPS INR17.69

items.quote: We will be, again, in a kind of an imported situation by FY28-29, at least 3.5 million tons to 4 million tons or 5 million tons.

items.statement: Raw material hedging via monthly pricing with primary mills (JSW, Tata, SAIL) and daily pricing in secondary; pass-through clauses in government contracts

So whatever the increase or decrease in the market there is, it's on a daily basis, not even on an hourly basi

items.statement: Industry growing at 13-14% CAGR; no structural slowdown; H2 FY25 demand pickup expected post-elections
items.quote: The market has been growing at a rate of 12%—13%. And this is what we're expecting, or maybe higher than this is going to happen post-elections. So the industry, for primary and secondary, both, is growing at a good 13%, 14%.

items.statement: Export demand strong in Q1 FY25; export share hard to quantify as domestic also strong
items.quote: As of today, we have also been seeing very good demand from the export market. We are very confident that we should achieve a new all-time high this quarter.

items.statement: DFT technology limited to 2-3 players in India; JTL to be 2nd/3rd entrant creating differentiated demand

items.statement: Asset turnover declining from 18-19x to 12-13x as gross block rises from INR90 cr to INR150 cr+ with capex

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; promoter funding supports expansion without leverage

items.statement: Promoter shareholding temporarily diluted by warrant conversions; to return to 60%+ after promoter warrant exercise
items.quote: The promoter shareholding has gone down because we converted some warrants. There is no sale of stake from the promoter or any of the promoter entities. items.statement: Nabha Steels utilisation expected at 65-70% (not 100%)

items.quote: I think we are saying pre-COVID level margins, which is around 26% EBITDA margin, where we are confident that we can maintain.

items.quote: My personal view is our industry would see better growth in FY25 than what we have seen in FY23 or even FY24.

items.statement: Gross margin at ~80% with limited room for further improvement; sustainable range 78-80%
items.quote: I think it's pretty high. I mean 80% roughly is gross margin. I think what we can do is, in my view, we can sustain here. But beyond this, I don't think there is a room to improve further.

items.statement: Suburban Diagnostics FY24 EBITDA margin 13% for full year, 17% in Q4

items.statement: Monitoring evolving regulatory frameworks and adapting approach for compliance

items.quote: Cash and cash equivalent as on March'24 is Rs. 960 Crore. Net of borrowing, it is Rs. 877 crore.

items.quote: As you know, we will be having Shankha Banerjee, leading the business as CEO, going forward, and he is here today. I welcome him into this role.

items.statement: Patient volume growth 3.2% in FY24; targeting 6%+ quarterly growth in FY25
