items.statement: Management cautious about assuming volume growth sustainability; wants to wait another quarter before confirming trend
items.quote: I think from here on, we'll have to probably wait it out for another quarter before we start making any sort of view on this.

items.statement: Tier-3/4 cities now 34% of revenue; franchise model enables expansion with minimal capex
items.quote: The second question which is on the model. So the collection network primarily which is linked to all the lab infrastructure is franchisee-driven.

items.statement: Actively exploring inorganic opportunities, especially in South India where presence is weak (6% revenue); open to tuck-in acquisitions
items.quote: So it is natural for us to look at in those places where our business is weak, which, to my mind right now it looks like South is the place.

items.statement: International and CTL combined contribute ~3% of revenue
items.quote: Others will constitute international and CTL.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected to be similar to FY24 levels even with zero new orders
items.quote: Even if we had zero inflow coming in this financial year, the new financial year. Even if there is zero inflow of orders we would still be doing a revenue of almost what we have done in this year the same range we should be getting in FY '25 as well of the same '24 revenues.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow target of Rs 10,000-12,000 crores across all sectors
items.quote: Shravanji this year, the total order inflow that we're looking at is to INR 10,000 crores to 12,000 crores at least that is the kind of range that we're looking for.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin target of 12-14%
items.quote: So for EBITDA, like we have given you a target for last time . We are looking at that same 12% to 14% kind of EBITDA targets, that I mentioned earlier as well.

items.statement: FY25 capex target of Rs 50-70 crores
items.quote: In terms of capex, the same INR50 crores to INR70-odd crores of capex is what we will be looking at.

items.statement: FY25 net debt reduction target of at least Rs 500 crores
items.quote: I'm happy to report that in this financial year in FY '25, we are targeting to further reduce the net debt by at least INR 500 crores plus.

items.statement: FY25 finance cost target of Rs 350 crores vs Rs 500+ crores in FY24
items.quote: In terms of finance cost, the finance cost this year reduced marginally because the debt reduction significantly happened in Q4. But for FY '24 -25 the targeted finance cost is INR 350 crores against the INR 500-plus crores finance costs.

items.statement: Target to become net debt-free on standalone basis within next two years (FY25-FY26)
items.quote: Our aim is to become a net debt -free company on a stand alone basis within the next two years. So FY25-FY '26, we will be net debt free company.

items.statement: InvIT expected to generate Rs 400-500 crores annual free cash flow in two years
items.quote: In two years, as our whole InvIT gets completed, we are expecting INR 400 crores to INR 500 crores of free cash flow coming from the InvIT as dividends and principal repayment back.

items.statement: FY24 order wins of Rs 3,602 crores: 42% irrigation, 35% water supply, 15% roads, 8% urban development
items.quote: In FY 23-24, the company won orders worth Rs.3,602 crores, which obviously was lower than expected for the reasons that I mentioned. Of this total orders, 42% of the projects are in irrigation, 35% in water supply, 15% in roads and 8% in urban development.

items.statement: Road sector exposure reduced from 65% in FY20 to 37% currently
items.quote: In the pre -COVID year of FY '20, it was 65% and in the current year, it's at 37%.

items.statement: FY24 standalone net debt reduced by Rs 861 crores; net debt-to-equity 0.29x, net debt/EBITDA 1.15x
items.quote: I'm very happy to say that we have reduced our debt this year by INR 861 crores through our various initiatives. This I'm talking about the standalone level. What this translates into is now the net debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.29x.

items.statement: Equipment debt of ~Rs 170 crores, 80% to be repaid in FY25
items.quote: currently, our equipment debt stands at about INR170-odd crores, like I said, somewhere in that range is where we are standing, almost 80% of which we will be paying down in this financial year anyways.

items.statement: DBL Infra debt of Rs 675 crores, Rs 30 crore prepayment started
items.quote: So INR 675 crores as on today is, yes, we have already started prepayment of around INR30 crores. So by next month this will be reduced by INR30 crores.

items.statement: Alpha Alternatives warrant issue: Rs 533 crores total, Rs 133 crores received, balance Rs 400 crores by June 2025
items.quote: In this year, the company issued warrants worth INR 533 crores to Alpha Alternatives, out of which Alpha has taken 25% as the rules for the warrant and the company has received INR 133 crores. The rest of the money as per the guideline, and rules provided by SEBI, that will come into the company by June 2025.

items.statement: Divestment of 26% in 3 HAM assets to Alpha for Rs 130 crores completed; balance 5 HAM assets to yield Rs 508 crores in H1 FY25
items.quote: In this financial year, we will be divesting 2 6% in the balance five HAM assets through which we are expecting INR 508 crores as money to come. This money is expected in the first half of the financial year.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin up 256 bps YoY to ~12.3% on better execution and lower material costs
items.quote: The EBITDA margin witnessed a significant increase by 256 basis points. The EBITDA margin increased on account of better execution of the projects and reduction in cost of construction material.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin up 250 bps YoY on higher revenue and lower construction material costs
items.quote: The EBITDA margin witnessed a significant increase by 250 basis points. The EBITDA margin increased on account of higher revenue and reduction in construction material costs.

items.statement: Siarmal coal mine FY24 production 7M tons vs 5M target (40% overachievement); FY25 target 15M tons vs 10M scheduled
items.quote: In Siarmal coal mine, in the financial year, the company has overachieved its target by more than 40% by extracting over 7 million tons compared to our target of 5 million tons. For the next year, we are planning to achieve production of 15 million tons compared to the scheduled target of 10 million tons.

items.statement: Pachhwara coal mine FY24 delivery 4.6M tons; full year target 7M tons on track
items.quote: On the other Coal MDO in the Pachhwara mine, we have delivered 4.6 million tons in this financial year as per the agreed terms as based on when we started this mine. The net sales target for full year is of 7 million tons, we are on target to deliver that too.

items.statement: Siarmal coal mine extraction price ~Rs 550/ton with inflation component
items.quote: Currently, if you want to understand Siarmal we are getting about INR 550 or somewhere in that range of price. It's INR 500 something range. And obviously this keeps on moving based on certain parameters of the government that's set for the contract.

items.statement: HAM project financing at 9-9.5% during construction, ~9.1% post-construction (MCLR-linked)
items.quote: Now the HAM projects financing because the MCLR of all the banks are close to 9%. So the various banks basically financing new project between 9% to 9.5% in the construction phase. And post-construction, it is on MCLR around 9.1% types.

items.statement: FY24 working capital days improved 5 days to 65 days; debtors down to Rs 1,392 crores from Rs 1,606 crores
items.quote: Working capital days also improved by five days from 70 days to 65 days from FY '23 to FY '24. And now we can open the floor for the questions and answers. Thank you, all.

items.statement: Inventory levels flat; working capital improvement expected quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Yes, on the inventory side more or less it is looking like the same. So the inventory levels are the same, but the overall basis 5 days increment. But individual items wise we're working , there will be improvement quarter -on-quarter every time.

items.statement: NHAI/MORTH have floated Rs 1,20,000 crores orders stalled by election code of conduct
items.quote: Even at the NHAI level there is more than INR 1,00,000 crores of orders that have already been floated. So, INR 1,20,000 crores of orders purely on NHAI and MORTH levels that have been floated.

items.statement: Election year historically slow for ordering; expect significant pickup post-election with 100-day government plan
items.quote: I can also tell you right now that all the different ministries are working on a very aggressive 100-day plan. So the Government is also very focused on wanting to start immediately off the blocks. So once the election gets over and results are out and the new Government comes into place, we should see a flurry of orders happening.

items.statement: Shrem InvIT distribution: Rs 94 crores total (Rs 65-70 crores dividend/interest, 30% principal) on console basis
items.quote: In terms of the other income total from the existing set of Shrem InvIT units we have already detailed out in the investor presentation, we will be receiving around INR 94 crores total distribution. And generally, the distribution is a principal is around 30% of the total distribution. So yes, you can say around INR 65-70 crores from the dividend and interest and balance 30% from the principal ret

items.statement: Core ROE (ex-asset investments) jumped from 6.9% to 13.8% in FY24
items.quote: I'm very happy to report that if we look at our return on equity, on a core basis, where we minus our investments into our assets, it has jumped from 6.9% of last year's ROE to 13.8% ROE this year.

items.statement: Siarmal coal mine: 80M tons cumulative extraction over next 4 years; 50M tons/year from year 6
items.quote: In this mine, in the next four years, the total extraction will be about 80 million tons cumulatively and from the sixth year onwards of this mine, we will be expecting 50 million metric ton of coal per year.

items.statement: Alpha deal: 26% stake in 18 HAM assets to be divested; 3 done, 5 in H1 FY25, balance 10 post-PCOD
items.quote: Out of the total 19 projects, 3 projects, 26% were already given to Alpha after completion. So as of 31st March, 16 projects were under construction. Out of 16 projects also 5 projects out of the first bucket 8 assets buckets are remaining. So out of 5 HAM projects, 2 projects the COD is received, 2 projects COD will be received in June, one in May and one in June. So out of 16 also , 11 projects

items.statement: Expect revenue growth slightly better than FY24's 12% and EBITDA margin expansion of ~100 bps per year for next couple of years
items.quote: More generally, my expectation is that we should be able to grow at a level slightly better than what we grew this year from the previous year . Margin expansion in terms of EBITDA should reflect our endeavor which I have outlined a couple of years ago, to have our EBITDA margin increase by 100 basis points every year for the next couple of years and I think that should hold .

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA grew 18% vs 12% revenue growth; margin expansion driven by mix shift and international
items.quote: Our EBITDA has grown by 18% during the same period. So basically due to the margin expansion the EBITDA increase in absolute terms is outpacing the revenue growth and we expect this trend to continue in the years to come.

items.statement: MarTech EBITDA margin target 10.5-11% for coming year
items.quote: Broadly there were some one -time adjustments of older projects etc . older costs which we closed which flowed in from Q3 and into Q4 and hence there was slight mutation of profitability in Q4 but overall I think we are on track to maintain a 10½ - 11%, a bit on that business going forward at least in the coming year.

items.statement: Test-prep enrollments up 10%, billing up 10%; MBA billing +11%, UG billing +9%, IPM/BBA strong, Law declined due to exam calendar shift
items.quote: FY24 we saw our volume expansion by about 10 % in terms of enrollment and the billing also has increased by 10% that would basically mean m ore or less consistent or constant average realization per student .

items.statement: Paper prices cooled ~25% in last 6-9 months, stable last quarter; expect price hikes in select titles to improve publishing margins
items.quote: As I shared about 12 months ago paper prices had hit the r oof but they have now cooled down by about 25% in the last 6 - 9 months, have been pretty stable in the last quarter and we expect that the price stability will hold and the enhanced margin should only get better in the new season because of price hike s which we will go through with in certain select title segments .

items.statement: ARPU flat in FY24 due to price rationalization in some segments; expect 3-5% ARPU expansion in FY25
items.quote: going forward we are reasonably confident of a 3-5% ARPU expansion in the current fiscal year

items.statement: MarTech margin expansion driven by pivot to higher-margin revenue mix and international growth (35% intl growth, higher margins)
items.quote: MarTech showed a highly divergent trend, with revenue expanding by about 6% but margin expanding by a healthy 29 % which was predominantly driven by two parameters - one being the pivoting of the revenue mix to higher margin business thereby effectively increaseing our gross margin and hence the follow -through into the business EBITDA. Second a rapid expansion in our international business portfo

items.statement: International revenue grew 32% YoY; MarTech intl +34%, EdTech intl +28%; Indonesia & US 50% of MarTech intl growth
items.quote: if you look at our international revenues, they have grown by about 32% in the year gone by , the MarTech revenue increase internationally has been 34 % and in the EdTech segment that revenue expansion has been about 28 %. Indonesia and US have contributed to 50 % of the growth internationally in the MarTech business

items.statement: Middle East EdTech: 6 locations, 20% volume growth, 16% billing growth; plan to double locations in 12 months
items.quote: business in the Middle East has been growing steadily with a 20 % volume expansion and a 16 % billing expansion. We currently have 6 locations operational there and we are looking to double that number in the next 12 months .

items.statement: Running pilot with 7 top US universities for direct partnerships; expect more partnerships in next 2 years
items.quote: we have started direct university partnership tie-ups. W e are currently in the process of running a pilot program with seven top US universities and we expect more and more direct partnerships to come our way in the next two years .

items.statement: Added 25 new test-prep centers in FY24; expect 30-40 new centers in FY25
items.quote: Just to add the new centers which were added was the number was 25 and we expect somewhere between 30 to 40 new centers to go live in the current fi scal year.

items.statement: Core test-prep uses negative capex franchise model; intangible investments (product, tech, content, metaverse) ~Rs13 cr in FY24, amortized over 5-10 yrs; expect 15-20% lower investment rate going forward
items.quote: They would be in the Rs.13 crore odd range for this year and we see that those kinds of investments are typically amortized anywhere between 5 to 10 years, on an average of 7 years and we will continue to make such investments over the years ahead but probably at a reducing rate of about 15 to 20 % compared to what we did this year.

items.statement: Borrowings increased due to year-end project execution vendor payments and 361DM consolidation (Rs2.2 cr)
items.quote: Our borrowings also increased due to the consolidation of 361D egree Minds Consulting Pvt. Ltd.(“361 DM) in which we increased our share from 11 %-39% in February 2024 and now post the second phase of the transaction we are now close to 54 %. A s a result of effective management control and board control the consolidation of financials resulted in overall borrowing increase of Rs.2.2 crores.

items.statement: Completed Rs10 crore buyback in FY24; gross cash up Rs6 cr to Rs115 cr, net cash down to Rs95 cr post buyback
items.quote: cash position currently seems to be pretty healthy despite a Rs.10crore buyback which we affected during the year . O ur gross cash has increased by about Rs.6 crores from Rs.109 to Rs.115 crores and our net cash , though, has decreased post buyback from Rs.99 Rs.95 crores

items.statement: Increased stake in 361DM from 11% to 54% (Feb 2024 + second phase); consolidated financials
items.quote: Our borrowings also increased due to the consolidation of 361D egree Minds Consulting Pvt. Ltd.(“361 DM) in which we increased our share from 11 %-39% in February 2024 and now post the second phase of the transaction we are now close to 54 %.

items.statement: Actively evaluating inorganic opportunities in EdTech, MarTech; initial discussions ongoing; hopeful of decision in 2-4 quarters
items.quote: Yes, we are always on the outlook of inorganic opportunities, both, in the EdTech, MarTech, and associated areas . R ight now there are initial discussions which are evaluations of opportunities happening if and when we take a final decision , a nd we get the board approval to proceed forward we will come back and share .

items.statement: No specific corporate action decided currently; board reviews shareholder wealth maximization regularly
items.quote: We are always at the lookout for maximization of shareholder wealth . A s and when any corporate action is deemed appropriate from a shareholder per spective we discuss during our Board Meeting every time and as and when the bo ard takes a final decision , the decision will be communicated and shared. At this point of time, no specific action has been decided

items.statement: Significant leadership hiring in EdTech, MarTech and international; CEO relocated to US for international push
items.quote: This year also has been a year of significant investments in terms of hiring and expanding our business leadership not only in our EdTech business but also in our MarTech business as well as expanding internationally into newer geographies especially Indonesi a and the US, where we restarted our operations last year with me relocating to the US to give a greater push to our international operation

items.statement: MarTech virtual revenue 6-7% of total; expect 1-2pp increase per year, targeting 20% in 3-5 years
items.quote: the total virtual revenue to both the virtual events platform and some bits of meta commerce of transformations into 3d environment would be in the currently the range of 6 to 7% of the total revenue, going forward we see this percentage increasing marginally every year by 1-2% points of the total revenue and we are hoping to hit that in 3 to 5 years. 20% of over total revenue comes from the techn

items.statement: CUET & International EdTech revenue in Rs18-25 cr range for FY24
items.quote: There are questions about our CUET and our international business revenues , this year those will be in the Rs.18 to 25 crore range .

items.statement: Test-prep centers on 3-year contracts; FY24 saw ~40-50 renewals/additions and 10-15 closures
items.quote: typically our centers are on a 3-year contract with us and every three years they go through a renewal process. So we've had a bunch of renewals , a few exits, and you know and about 25 new additions. So just to give you an estimate , that number would have been about between renewals and additions that number would have been in the 40 to 5 0 range and another you know 10 -15 would have shut over

items.statement: Africa subsidiary transferred from Kestone Singapore to CL Singapore subsidiary for focused EdTech/MarTech separation; not a demerger precursor
items.quote: the Africa busines s was transferred from the Kestone Singapore subsidiary to the CL Singapore subsidiary and we will continue to manage our test prep and our EdTech growth ambitions through the Singapore subsidiary for our international market growth.

items.statement: No plans to enter JEE/NEET nationally; focus on aptitude-based tests (MBA, Law, IPM, BBA, CUET, study abroad)
items.quote: For now we do not have any plans to get into JEE and NEET on a pan -India national level. So we'll continue to focus on our products where we are market leaders like MBA, Law, IPM, BBA and CUET and the markets for some of them are large and big enough for us to expand our market share and keep growing for the next couple of years .

items.statement: Animal feed FY25 EBIT per ton expected to exceed FY24 average of Rs 1,531/ton
items.quote: Our average last year was about Rs. 1,531 and I can definitely F.Y. 2024 was Rs. 1,531. The only thing I can say is that F.Y. 2025 will better than that.

items.statement: CDMO revenue to maintain ~67% growth run-rate in FY25 with base now over Rs 250 Cr
items.quote: This year we have grown by almost 67% from last year and we have a very good confidence that we'll continue to maintain that run rate as we get into F.Y. 2025. Now our base for the CDMO new products have also crossed 250 Crore.

items.statement: Dairy VAP salience targeted to grow another 4-5% in FY25 from 36%
items.quote: we hope that this year we will grow the salience by another 4%-5%.

items.statement: Cattle and Fish feed volumes expected to sustain double-digit growth for foreseeable future
items.quote: Cattle Feed and Fish Feed the game is wide open. There is no integration likely to happen because Cattle Feed market is huge. Category conversion is at 20% level, and we believe Cattle Feed and Fish Feed can both grow in double digits for the next at least foreseeable future.

items.statement: Branded poultry share to reach 80%+ earlier than FY28 target
items.quote: No, I think this will happen much earlier because we are getting very good traction in our processed chicken business and good thing, we did is that about 2 years ago we enhanced capacity marginally.

items.statement: Consolidated capex run-rate of Rs 250-300 Cr to be maintained in FY25; oil palm refinery expansion decision by end of Q2
items.quote: On an average we keep on investing about Rs. 250 to 300 Crore. I think, we will maintain that run rate but the investment will come. We just have added some capacities in our dairy business. We have to invest in distribution in our chicken and dairy business. I will tell you how we invest in distribution because wherever we go , we require freezers and chillers which we invest in and a big chunk o

items.statement: Astec herbicide plant commissioned in Q1; further capex tied to CDMO pickup in Q3-Q4
items.quote: Astec, we have commissioned one herbicide plant and capitalized it in Q 1, so we are in a situation where we have capacity to fill. But I am very sure that Astec CAPEX cycle will come under discussion in Q3 and Q4 because in case contract manufacturing or CDMO business picks up , we will require specialized capacity for specialized product for specialized customers.

items.statement: Dairy plant utilisation to rise from 60% to 75-80% over next 2 years via geography saturation
items.quote: We plan to at least saturate these geographies in the next 2 years and grow to a level where our plant utilization from currently 60% come to about 75% to 80% which is the ideal.

items.statement: Oil palm refinery and solvent extraction capacities to match in-house production within 2 years
items.quote: I am very sure that we will have to do it for a year or two, but my sense is that all our capacities will match with our produc tion in 2 years’ time

items.statement: Animal feed Q4 EBIT/ton reached Rs 1,874; upward trend expected to continue near Q4 levels
items.quote: Q4 we have gone to Rs. 1,874. So, my sense is that the upward trend will continue and I am very sure whatever on the year-on-year basis I am saying, and we will be able to maintain close to Q4 numbers in this quarter also.

items.statement: Standalone Crop Protection segment margin 31% in FY24, 3.4x FY23
items.quote: The segment margin of 31% in Fiscal Year '24 was 3.4 times that of Fiscal Year '23.

items.statement: Branded poultry contribution margins: Yummy's ~35%, Real Good Chicken ~15% vs live bird -25% to +25%
items.quote: Yummy's our contribution margin which is margin after variable is about +35% and Real Good Chicken is close to 15%. I must tell you that a large portion of Real Good Chicken is B2B to QSRs and E-com and direct to home Company.

items.statement: Oil palm value addition limited PBT decline to ~20% despite 20% CPO price drop
items.quote: we had a target of Rs. 184 Crore PBT and there was a significant drop in CPO prices. There was almost a 12% - 13% drop in crude palm oil price, 20% drop. So, if we were only in crude palm oil and palm kernel oil , our profits should have fallen by 40%. But because of these profits came down only by about 20%.

items.statement: Astec enterprise business seeing no green shoots; CDMO and new products to drive FY25 performance
items.quote: On the enterprise side , we haven't seen any green shoots in the market. But internally I would hate to give any forecast on when the market should revive back. In turn what we are focusing on are the things which are in our hand which are the CDMO, and the new product development and our entire goal and ambition is that as we get into F.Y. 2025, we completely de-lever ourselves from enterprise pr

items.statement: Fish meal prices softening; company well positioned with low inventory in India and Bangladesh
items.quote: You are absolutely right that the fish meal prices were very high. But what we are seeing now is some kind of softening has started happening and good thing is that we don't have too much of stock either in Bangladesh or India. So , my sense is that we are reasonably well placed in case the price falls.

items.statement: Dairy VAP salience rose to 36% from 32% in FY24; target another 4-5% increase
items.quote: Salience of value-added products has improved to 36% of total sales from 32% a year ago.

items.statement: Branded poultry volumes grew ~15% in FY24 (Yummy's 13%, Real Good Chicken 15.6%); live bird de-growing
items.quote: Yummy's grew about 13% and Real Good Chicken grew about 15.6% and if we take the blended number, then the branded volumes grew by about 15% in F.Y. 2024 over F.Y. 2023 and that is the focus for this year also.

items.statement: Oil palm moving down value chain: now selling PFAD, Stearin, palm kernel extraction instead of only CPO/PKO
items.quote: setting up a solvent extraction plant, other wealth from waste project plus refinery now we are less impacted by volatility of CPO and CPKO because we are selling only Palm Fatty Acid Distillates (PFAD), Stearin, palm kernel extraction which is one level of value addition

items.statement: DDGS availability from ethanol program offset corn price rise in animal feed
items.quote: The good thing which happened is that we have substantial DDGS availability. So, if the energy prices because of corn have gone up , the protein prices because of DDGS have come down which has helped utilize the cost increase in our feed segment.

items.statement: Palm oil prices stabilizing; import duty may rise post-elections due to bumper mustard crop
items.quote: Palm oil prices have dropped somewhat but they seem to be stabilizing now and of course they could rise a little bit. We don't expect that palm oil prices will go very high but Indian prices also depend on the import duty and since we have bumper red seed crops and farmers have to be kept satisfied it is likely that after the elections import duties on imported oil could be raised.

items.statement: Astec CDMO new products commercializing from July-August FY25; revenue contribution to start then
items.quote: as we move forward in F.Y. 2025 from July-August onward we will start seeing the financial performance kicked in from some of these new products which we have been working on.

items.statement: Unallocable expenses of Rs 50 Cr in Q4 sustainable; prior year lower due to land sale netting
items.quote: Yes, that is a sustainable number. Last year was because of the netting-off of the income.

items.statement: Astec debt-equity ~1.3x; no equity raise planned as internal support sufficient
items.quote: we strongly believe that we have industry has bottomed out and now the journey will be upwards and in this business, I am saying that debt equity is still about 1.3 or something. So, it's not a very big concern. We can tide over whatever is the short-term requirement by supporting internally.

items.statement: Import duty on edible oils may increase post-elections to support mustard farmers
items.quote: since we have bumper red seed crops and farmers have to be kept satisfied it is likely that after the elections import duties on imported oil could be raised.

items.statement: Liquid milk competitive intensity remains high; focus shifting to branded VAP for better margins
items.quote: I must tell you very honestly, that the competitive intensity in liquid milk is very high in all parts of the country where cooperatives are also big. In the South there are a lot of private players. So that will always be highly competitive and that will also be price sensitive also.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs 9,561 Cr in FY24 vs Rs 9,374 Cr FY23; PBT up 55% to Rs 434 Cr
items.quote: Godrej Agrovet recorded consolidated revenue from operations of Rs. 9,561 Crore in Fiscal Year '24 as against Rs. 9,374 Crore in Fiscal Year '23 . While the revenues were flat , Fiscal Year '24 augured well in terms of a strong resurgence in profitability. Profit before tax improved by 55% to 434 Crore as compared to 280 Crore in Fiscal Year '23.

items.statement: Animal feed volumes: Cattle +11%, Fish +19%, Poultry feed lower; overall +3% in FY24
items.quote: For Fiscal Year '24 sustained volume growth in Cattle Feed and Fish Feed of 11% and 19% respectively over Fiscal Year '23 was partly offset by lower Poultry feed sales resulting in volume growth of 3%.

items.statement: Fresh fruit bunch volume +6% in FY24; CPO price -20%, PKO -28% vs FY23
items.quote: For Fiscal Year '24 fresh fruit bunch volume growth of 6% was more than offset by lower crude palm oil and palm kernel oil prices which came off the highs of Fiscal Year '23 and normalized in Fiscal Year '24. The CPO and PKO prices were lower by 20% and 28% respectively compared to Fiscal Year '23.

items.statement: ACI Godrej Bangladesh revenue +8% YoY; profit +117% on lower input costs
items.quote: GAVL's joint venture in Bangladesh ACI Godrej recorded revenue growth of 8% year-on-year in Fiscal Year '24. Profitability improved remarkably and was higher by 117% over Fiscal Year '23 on account of lower input costs.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: AUM growth target of 30% for FY25
items.quote: AUM growth overall, we are targeting a 30% AUM growth.

items.statement: Ex-co-lending spread guidance of 5.0-5.25% for medium term
items.quote: Our ex-CL Spread guidance of 5.0-5.25% stands for the medium term.

items.statement: Opex to assets guidance of around 3.0% going forward
items.quote: We continue to maintain the guidance of around 3.0% going ahead; as we focus on expansion and get deeper into new markets.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 30-40 bps
items.quote: We continue to maintain our credit cost guidance of 30 to 40bps.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing expected to rise 10-20 bps and flatline at 8.5% in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: From a projection perspective, the 8.3% would look more like 8.5% in 2 quarters to 3 quarters and hopefully flatline there.

items.statement: ROA expected around 3.5% (3.4-3.6%) with ROE 16%+
items.quote: So that range can be 3.4% to 3.6%. But let's say you anchor around 3.5% plus/minus which essentially leaves you with a 16% plus ROE.

items.statement: Branch expansion target of 20-25 branches and 60-70 touchpoints per year
items.quote: Branch expansion, we are targeting 20 to 25 branches every year. And along with that, say, about 60 to 70 touchpoints per year.

items.statement: LAP portfolio target of 20% of AUM by March 2027
items.quote: Our 3-year plan is to take it to 20%. So, it will be gradual, it will not be very sharp but March'27 is 20%.

items.statement: Co-lending to contribute ~10% of disbursements in near future
items.quote: Co-lending business is growing and expect this to contribute around 10% of disbursements in the near future.

items.statement: Insurance income expected to add INR 5-6 cr quarterly from Q3 FY25
items.quote: Once we sign with at least 2 to 3 companies and cover the entire book that we onboard today, my expectation is that should add close to INR5 crores to INR6 crores of additional income into the P&L, on a quarterly basis. So, let's say Q3 onwards is when you should be able to see the full income.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity target of 5x (asset-to-equity 6x) with 2-2.5 years runway
items.quote: At our planned expansion, debt-to-equity of 5x or asset-to-equity of 6x is what we have in mind. We also look at capital adequacy ratios and what is the comfort level with banks and rating agencies. So, all of that, we've taken into consideration and asset to equity of 6x, which gives us another 2- 2.5 years of runway is what is on our mind.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target of ~30% in 3-5 years
items.quote: Our aim in the medium term is to get that down to around close to 30% levels. In maybe 3- to 5-year timeframe, we should be able to get it down to 30% levels.

items.statement: Added 22 branches in FY24, total 133 physical branches and 321 touchpoints
items.quote: Overall, we have added 22 branches in FY24 and now have 133 physical branches. Including potential & digital branches, we now do busine ss across 321 touchpoints across Tier 1 to Tier 5 markets in 13 states / UT of India

items.statement: Disbursements Rs 3,963 Cr in FY24, up 31.5%; AUM grew 34.7%
items.quote: Disbursements at Rs 3,963 Crs, grew by 31.5% and AUM grew by 34.7%.

items.statement: Co-lending volume Rs 68 Cr in Q4, Rs 214 Cr in FY24
items.quote: Our total Co-lending volume in Q4 was Rs 68 Crs & Rs 214 Crs in FY24.

items.statement: Q4 spread 5.2%, ex-CL spread 5.4%, NIM 5.3%; compression from cost of borrowing, leverage, cash
items.quote: Our overall Spread is at 5.2% and our spread ex CL is 5.4%. Our overall Q4 Net Interest Margin stands at 5.3%. The NIM compression is an outcome of continued growth and increase in financial leverage, increased cost of borrowing and higher cash and cash equivalent holding in Q4.

items.statement: NIM expected to stabilize at 5.3-5.5% going forward
items.quote: Our NIM should be in a similar range where we are today like 5.3% - 5.5% is what we have thought.

items.statement: Marginal cost of borrowing 8.25%, up 3 bps q-o-q; NHB refinance 50 bps cheaper
items.quote: Our cost of borrowing is competitive at 8.25%, an increase of only 3 bps on q-o-q basis.

items.statement: NHB borrowing rate range 5.5-8.5% depending on scheme
items.quote: NHB, again, has multiple schemes. It varies from scheme to scheme. The range that we get from NHB is anywhere from 5.5% to 8.5%.

items.statement: Origination yield target 13.5% ex-co-lending; co-lending yield ~10%
items.quote: Our target is 13.5% kind of an origination yield, but there will be some quarter-to-quarter fluctuations on that.

items.statement: 1+ DPD 4.2% (-30 bps q-o-q), 30+ DPD 2.8% (-20 bps), GNPA 1.7% flat, credit cost 10 bps (-20 bps)
items.quote: DPD is at 4.2%, decline of 30 bps on q-o-q. 30+ DPD at 2.8%, decline of 20 bps on q-o-q. Gross Stage 3 (GNPA) is at 1.7%, flat q-o-q. Prior to RBI classification circular of Nov’21, it stands at 1.1%. Our credit cost at 10bps , decline of 20 bps on q -o-q

items.statement: Provision coverage 50.9% (75.7% pre-RBI circular); ECL provision ~0.8-0.9% of principal outstanding
items.quote: Total Provision coverage ratio stands at 50.9%. Prior to NPA reclassification as per RBI circular, PCR stands at 75.7%.

items.statement: Written-off pool ~INR 20 Cr; expect INR 50-70 lakh quarterly recoveries
items.quote: The potential target pool, the number would be close to INR20 crores, but we do not expect the INR20 crores to come and hit us as write-backs anytime in the future. What we see is usually a reversal of around INR50 lakhs - INR70 lakhs every quarter.

items.statement: Borrowing mix: 60% banks (31% private, 29% public), 18% NHB, 14% DA, 3% co-lending, 3% IFC NCD; zero CP
items.quote: Our Borrowings mix is: 60% of our borrowings from Banks (Private sector 31% and public sector 29%). NHB refinance share at 18%, we have drawn Rs 250 Crs in Apr'24 from NHB. 14% from Direct Assignment and 3% from Co-lending. 3% is from IFC NCD. We continue to have zero borrowings through Commercial paper.

items.statement: CRAR 39.5%, Tier-1 39.1%, D/E 3.4x, Networth Rs 2,122 Cr, BVPS Rs 239.7
items.quote: Our total CRAR is at 39.5% and Tier 1 CRAR is at 39.1%. Our Debt to Equity is now at 3.4 times. Our Mar'24 Networth stands at Rs 2,122 Crs. Our Book Value per share (BVPS) stands at Rs. 239.7.

items.statement: Drew Rs 250 Cr from NHB in Apr'24; expect significant NHB line in FY25
items.quote: NHB refinance share at 18%, we have drawn Rs 250 Crs in Apr'24 from NHB.

items.statement: Cash salaried ~20-25% of total book, ~30%+ of salaried book
items.quote: Cash salaried will be around, so out of the total, it will be around 20%, 25%. So, within the salaried, it will be maybe 30% plus.

items.statement: BT-out driven by rate hikes (PLR raised thrice in 2 years); migration to larger banks
items.quote: BT Out rates are higher largely because of rates being higher because we have repriced the large part of our book and that is creating some tension with customers. That's primarily the reason. We have analysed our BT Out also. In the last 2 years, we have increased the PLR thrice. The customers who received the three hikes are more prone to BT Out.

items.statement: Total runoff (18-20%) in line with peers despite higher pricing
items.quote: If you compare runoff, it's identical. Pricing in the market is higher so that makes us more prone to BT Out by design.

items.statement: Chairman Deepak Satwalekar tenure extended for second 5-year term subject to AGM approval
items.quote: Another important point to communicate is that our Chairman Mr. Deepak Satwalekar tenure has been extended for a second term of 5 years subject to shareholders approval at the upcoming AGM.

items.statement: Active connectors ~3,000; RMs ~700 as of Mar'24
items.quote: Active connectors, we had about 3,000 connectors for the quarter. And RMs was in the range of about 700.

items.statement: Digital adoption: 95% customers on app, 53% unique logins, 89% service requests on app, 47% sanctions via Account Aggregator
items.quote: 95% of our customers are registered on our app as on Mar'24. Unique User Logins was 53% in Service requests raised on app was stable at 89%. In Q4FY24, we have processed 47% of loan sanctions with data coming from Account Aggregator.

items.statement: Promoters (True North, Aether) to exit ~10% per year via block deals with 6-month lock-in
items.quote: The aim is to probably exit by about 10% every year. So, once a year, there will be a 10% sale in the market through a block and exit through that process. We have tried to give it a bit of predictability in structure. And since the last transaction they have given a 6-month lock-in after previous transaction, which happened in November.

items.statement: Gross advances grew 41.5% YoY to Rs 8,650 crore in FY24
items.quote: On gross advances front, the Bank's gross advances stood at 8,650 crores in FY24 as compared to Rs. 6,114 crores in FY23, an increase of 41.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Full-year disbursements rose 36.1% to Rs 6,919 crore in FY24
items.quote: Our Bank disbursement for the full year rose by 36.1% to Rs. 6 ,919 crores as compared to corresponding previous period last year.

items.statement: Vikas Loan AUM surpassed Rs 2,600 crore, contributing over 53% of inclusive finance portfolio
items.quote: We're happy to share that Vikas Loans, the individual loan portfolio offered to Bank's graduating JLG customers has surpassed Rs. 2,600 crores of AUM and now contributes over 53% of the inclusive finance portfolio.

items.statement: Deposits grew 50.5% to Rs 7,777 crore in FY24
items.quote: On the deposits and borrowing front , our deposits witnessed a growth of 50.5% to Rs. 7,777 crores in FY24 against Rs. 5,167 crores in FY23.

items.statement: CASA ratio improved to 20.1% in FY24 from 17.1% in FY23
items.quote: The CASA ratio has increased from 17.1% in FY23 to 20.1% in FY24.

items.statement: Retail deposits now 78.8% of total deposits in FY24 vs 73.1% in FY23
items.quote: The retail deposits as a percentage of overall deposits, currently stand at 78.8% in FY24 versus 73.1% during FY23.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 2.8% in FY24 from 3.1% in FY23; NNPA improved to 0.8% from 1.5%
items.quote: Our Bank's gross nonperforming assets have reduced to 2.8% in FY24 from 3.1% in FY23 and the net non-performing assets has decreased to 0.8% in FY24 compared to 1.5% in FY23.

items.statement: NIM increased to 9.8% in FY24 from 9.5% in FY23; yield improved to 20.2% from 19.3%
items.quote: Our yield has improved to 20.2% in FY24 from 19.3% for FY23. NIM has increased from 9.5% in FY23 to 9.8% in FY24.

items.statement: Cost of funds increased to 7.3% in FY24 from 6.7% in FY23
items.quote: Our cost of funds has increased from 6.7% in FY23 to 7.3% in FY24.

items.statement: Cost-to-income excluding CGFMU improved to 57.1% in FY24 from 60% in FY23
items.quote: Our cost to income excluding CGFMU investment stood at 57.1% as compared to 60% in FY23.

items.statement: Loan book growth guidance of 30%-35% for FY25; deposit growth guidance of 40%-45% for FY25
items.quote: So, in terms of loan book, we are talking about a 30%-35% of growth and in terms of deposits we intend to have somewhere around a 40 %-45% kind of a growth.

items.statement: Secured book mix target of ~45% by end of FY25 from 41% currently
items.quote: So today my secured book is about 41% and by the end of next year we would want to be around 45%.

items.statement: ROA guidance range of 2.3%-2.5% for medium term; ROE target of 14%-16% steady state
items.quote: No, given the way we would want to increase the mix of our secured book, we would want to be range bound to 2.3 to 2.5. So that's the kind of a horizon that we have in mind.

items.statement: CGFMU expense expected at Rs 70-80 crore for FY25
items.quote: So, I think with the way that we see the book growing , our expense on CGFMU will be somewhere in the range of 70 to 80 crores.

items.statement: CGFMU gross claims target of Rs 45-50 crore for FY25 with ~70% recovery rate
items.quote: So, for this financial year we would look to make claims, gross claims somewhere in the region of 45 to 50 crores. As per the program parameters about 70% of the claim that is made by us gets paid back to us.

items.statement: Cost-to-income including CGFMU target of ~57% for FY25 vs 61.6% in FY24
items.quote: Our ambition is that for the next year , our cost to income including CGFMU will be in the region of 57%.

items.statement: Credit cost outlook of 1.5%-1.8% for FY25
items.quote: Well very difficult to predict. But I mean if you ask me my opinion would be that I would want to be at the same stage where we are today for this financial year which has been somewhere in the range of 1.5% to 1.8%.

items.statement: PCR target to stay close to 70% and try to improve further
items.quote: Yes, it will be our endeavor to stay very close to that number. As you are aware when we started the year, we were a little under 50% and took us a year to reach to this number as we had guided right throughout the year. So going forward we would stay very much close to that 70% number and as a matter of fact even try to improve it.

items.statement: Added 70 branches in FY24; plan to continue similar branch expansion pace
items.quote: Shailesh, we added around closer to 70 branches in a year. The intent is to really kind of increase at least the new customer acquisition to 40 ,000 to 50,000 which you are seeing a traction.

items.statement: Branch expansion to continue at similar pace for next 2 years
items.quote: Branch expansion we will keep doing. This year also we have added 70branches in micro -banking. This will be our endeavor to keep expanding like this.

items.statement: SLTRO borrowing of Rs 750 crore maturing by December 2024; plan to substitute with CASA growth
items.quote: For example, for the last two quarters we have been actively looking at the IBPC market which does provide us with a 2% interest that we charge. But at the same time, we are conscious of the fact that a component of our financing is SLTRO financing which came to us at 4% and that financing will retire and mature by December of this year.

items.statement: Borrowings form ~20% of total liabilities, mainly from SIDBI and NABARD refinancing
items.quote: Our borrowings at the end of March '24 formed approximately 20% of the total liabilities , the majority of which is from refinancing institutions SIDBI and NABARD.

items.statement: Eligible to apply for universal bank license in about a year after meeting GNPA <3% for two consecutive years and NNPA <1%
items.quote: So, I think we will take about a year to be eligible to fulfill all the criteria for being eligible to apply for being a universal Bank.

items.statement: GNPA below 3% and NNPA below 1% achieved in FY24; need one more year of compliance for universal license
items.quote: Last year our GNPA was above 3%, there are four-five conditions, one was GNPA should be below 3% for the two consecutive financial years, net NPA should be 1%. So, we had 1% more last year. We have 0.84% for this year.

items.statement: No slowdown or stress observed due to elections; ongoing practice of tightening policies in bottom 25 branches
items.quote: We haven't. We haven't to an extent not heard anything from the market or from our peers. So , one I think it's a phased-out election and we haven't really seen or heard anything.

items.statement: CGFMU maximum portfolio cover claim limited to 15% of disbursed amount at 72.75% recovery rate
items.quote: Maximum on a portfolio cover basis the claim will be 15% of the amount which is dis bursed. So obviously basis the rundown, it may become a little higher percentage in terms of what can be claimed but obviously we don't believe we would want to reach to that levels.

items.statement: Rebuilding collection organization for Vikas Loan portfolio which has grown 2x to Rs 2,600 crore
items.quote: So , we are already in the process of recreating our collection organization where , given that these are individual borrowers , we will have a collection mechanism commensurate to the portfolio size. So , we are rebuilding our entire collection organization which caters specifically to the increasing number of VL customers.

items.statement: Plan to reduce Vikas Loan pricing from 28% to ~24% over next year for second-cycle customers
items.quote: So initially the cost of operations for Vikas Loan was higher as KC mentioned as we have more and more seasoned customers who are paying on their own as a Bank our intent was really going on the pricing path in terms of reducing it from current 28% to around closer to around 24% over the next 1 year.

items.statement: Focus on growing micro-LAP, micro-mortgage, merchant funding and bancassurance to improve fee income
items.quote: So like Baskar indicated, micro-LAP and micro mortgage is something that we would need to grow in a big way. Some of the other products like providing funding to merchants is something that we would need to start building up in a big way. And importantly bancassurance business is something that we are really looking forward to build so that we can see significant growth in our fee business.

items.statement: CRAR at 28.4% in FY24, well above regulatory requirement; comfortable at ~20% as secured mix increases
items.quote: We continue to remain well capitalized with our C RAR at 28.4% which is well above the regulatory requirement.

items.statement: Risk-weighted assets at ~77% currently; CGFMU cover could provide up to 15% risk weight benefit but not exercised yet
items.quote: So today if you look at the composition of our book , our risk weighted assets are around 77% which very closely approximates to the 75% risk weight that we carry for MFI business which is about 60% of what we have today.

items.statement: Management expects demand recovery from Q2 FY25 and significant improvement in H2 FY25 across both segments
items.quote: We are optimistic that once the situation starts stabilizing, we are well positioned to leverage our state-of-the-art infrastructure along with the backward integration.

items.statement: Management expects overall FY25 to be significantly better than FY24 but not as good as pre-downturn levels
items.quote: It won't be as good as before two years position. It will be significantly better than the last financial year.

items.statement: Major capex completed before downturn; no significant capex planned for next 1-2 years
items.quote: We already completed all our major capex. So I would say in next one or two years, there is not going to be major capex.

items.statement: INR 140 crore debt repayment planned in FY25 with further reduction in FY26
items.quote: This financial year, we'll be repaying about INR140 crores repayment is going to be there. Again, subsequently in the next financial year, there will be further debt reduction.

items.statement: Crop protection capacity utilization at 67% in FY24 (36,780 MT production)
items.quote: In the crop protection segment, production stood at about 36,780 metric tons with a capacity utilization of about 67%

items.statement: Pigment capacity utilization at 41% in FY24 (13,721 MT production)
items.quote: For pigment segment, production stood at 13,721 metric tons with a capacity utilization of about 41%.

items.statement: Titanium dioxide plant utilization expected to reach 60%+ from Q1 FY25
items.quote: So, as of now, the utilization level is low. But we see from the first quarter, in this quarter onwards, only the utilization level will reach to 60% plus.

items.statement: Nano urea capacity at 5 crore bottles/year (25,000 tons); meaningful utilization expected from year 2-3
items.quote: Regarding capacity utilization, our capacity is about 5 crores bottles a year, which is a very high capacity. So it would be very difficult to achieve a significant capacity level in the first year. But from second and third year onwards, there will be reasonably capacity utilization.

items.statement: Nano urea margins expected at 15-17%
items.quote: Yes. So, the margin level would be in the range of about 15%-17%.

items.statement: Pigment and agrochemical prices have bottomed out; raw material to sales ratio normalized
items.quote: Yes, definitely we can say that not only in the pigment segment but even in the agro segment. Prices have bottomed out completely and with the improvement in demand, we see the prices will also go up

items.statement: Agrochemical product prices at lowest levels, even below 2019 prices
items.quote: So I would say all the products prices have gone to the almost at the lowest level. So, even before 2019 prices even below those level prices have gone.

items.statement: Customers placing smaller, more frequent orders indicating demand recovery
items.quote: Customers have also started showing positivity and regarding placing the order. The only thing is people have got, you know, burned their fingers significantly because of high inventory. So, people are going cautious rather than putting big orders. They are putting small, small orders in more number of orders they are putting with the small, small quantities.

items.statement: Provisional anti-dumping duty on Chinese titanium dioxide imports expected in 4-6 months
items.quote: So, we see some preliminary anti-dumping duty coming on titanium dioxide on Chinese goods somewhere in next four to six months' time.

items.statement: Chinese export incentives of 13-15% enabling dumping across multiple markets
items.quote: Chinese government is giving huge incentive on the export. So not only on titanium dioxide but I would say on majority of the products. So because of that, they get export incentive to the tune of about 13%-15%

items.statement: Plan to launch 4-5 new products in fertilizer, biofertilizer, biostimulant categories
items.quote: Further, we also plan to introduce about four to five new products in the segments of fertilizer, biofertilizer, and biostimulant category to add more products in our basket

items.statement: Export to 70+ countries in agrochemicals; strong global customer relationships providing market visibility
items.quote: As an agrochemical segment point of view, we are exporting to more than 70 countries. So, we have got pretty strong presence, and we are in touch with all of our customers globally.

items.statement: Debtor and inventory days increased in FY24 but expected to significantly improve in FY25
items.quote: That's correct. So, right now it has gone up, you rightly mentioned. And in this financial year, it will significantly improve again.

items.statement: Both debtor and creditor days expected to come down in FY25 improving working capital cycle
items.quote: So, both will come down, yes. So, there will be improvement in the working capital.

items.statement: European pigment producer bankruptcies creating opportunity for Indian manufacturers
items.quote: Recently you rightly mentioned some of the multinational companies based out in Europe facing problems. And I would say it is a good thing because the high-cost companies which are present in developed markets like U.S. and Europe, they will shut down their manufacturing base in those countries and the market will move to India as well as China.

items.statement: India has competitive advantage over China in copper phthalocyanine pigments and pyrethroids
items.quote: In the pigment segment and where we are, which is a copper phthalocyanine-based pigment, India has got upper edge over China. So definitely the advantage will come to India

items.statement: Indian titanium dioxide market at 400,000 tons with domestic capacity of only 80,000 tons; >70% imported
items.quote: Indian market size is close to 400,000 tons and the major application of titanium dioxide is in the paint segment. More than 70% of the titanium dioxide is being consumed in the paint segment.

items.statement: Government targeting replacement of 9 million tons imported urea with nano urea by 2025-26
items.quote: Government has already declared that 9 million tons of urea which is being imported right now, by '25, '26 government is going to completely restrict these 9 million tons first.

items.statement: Chinese dumping risk in titanium dioxide mitigated by pending anti-dumping duty
items.quote: China is dumping the material. And because of that, only the anti-dumping initiation has started place on titanium dioxide.

items.statement: Co-gen power plant commissioned in Q4 FY24 to reduce energy cost in titanium dioxide manufacturing
items.quote: Moving to titanium dioxide, we have commissioned the Co-gen Power Plant, which will help us to reduce the energy cost, which is a major cost component in titanium dioxide manufacturing process.

items.statement: Paisabazaar growth expected at 0-10% for next quarter due to process-based slowdown
items.quote: I expect this to last at least one more quarter. And the expectation, I think, is going to be below that. So I think we would be good at maybe 0 to 10% growth for Paisa.

items.statement: Full year PAT breakeven achieved in Q3, ended year with PAT of ₹64Cr
items.quote: We had the aimed for a full year PAT break even and we are very happy to announce that we achieved that ahead of the target in Q3 itself. And have now ended the year with a PAT of ₹64Cr from a loss of ₹488Cr last year.

items.statement: Health and life insurance new premiums grew 53% YoY in Q4
items.quote: health and life insurance combined, which is the core of our business and a bulk of our long term value; had a combined growth of 53% YoY in new premiums for the quarter.

items.statement: Total insurance premium for quarter was ₹5,123Cr, ARR reached ₹20,000Cr milestone
items.quote: Our total insurance premium for the quarter was ₹5,123Cr, and that gives us an ARR of ₹20,000Cr, which was also a long -awaited milestone.

items.statement: Core online marketplaces revenue grew 39% to ₹2,375Cr, adjusted EBITDA margin improved from 6% to 14%
items.quote: Revenue for our online marketplaces Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, which we referred to as t he core businesses, grew 39% to ₹2,375Cr, while improving their adjusted EBITDA margin from 6% to 14

items.statement: New initiatives broke even at contribution basis in FY24
items.quote: If you notice this year, the new initiatives broke even at a contribution basis.

items.statement: Persistency at highest ever, 1-2 percentage points higher than before, porting at ~20% vs market at ~40%
items.quote: our persistency on renewals in both number of transactions and pr emium, it is the highest ever. It is a percentage or a percentage to 2 percentage more than it has been in the past ever

items.statement: Credit Score consumer base increased to 43Mn, 75% cards processed digitally, 75% disbursals from existing customers
items.quote: The Credit Score consumer bas e has now increased to 43Mn. 75% of the cards were processed end to end digitally, and 75% of disbursals are from existing customers

items.statement: CSAT reached 89%, highest ever reported
items.quote: We continue to improve on CSAT. This is another number, which was at a particular number, pretty high, but it was stuck there. We have now got a CSAT of 89%, which is actually the highest we have ever reported.

items.statement: Secured disbursals at 13-15% quarterly, targeting to increase secured loan contribution
items.quote: Currently a secure d disbursal percentage would be about 13% to 15% on a quarterly basis. And one of our key priorities for this year is to try and increase the secure d growth and hence the secured contribution.

items.statement: Offline channel (feet-on-street) contribution inching up from ~20% to ~22%, same product mix and quality as online
items.quote: the number you correctly said used to be around 20%. It's inching upwards every quarter, every month. You know, th e rest of the business is also growing quite rapidly, so it's hard for the proportion to change dramatically

items.statement: PB Partners POSP business at ₹1,200Cr premium in Q4, corporate at ₹200Cr, motor:non-motor back to 80:20
items.quote: POSP is ₹1,200. You know, our corporate is about ₹200.

items.statement: Branding cost growing at roughly half the rate of premium growth, as percentage of revenue keeps coming down
items.quote: Like Sarbvir said, the brand cost increases roughly, half of the premium increase and as a percentage of revenue, it keeps coming down.

items.statement: Adding people and centres for offline channel, deploying more feet-on-street for health and life
items.quote: We are deploying lot more people in the field. And we are very encouraged by the response to the model. So I think in both the life side and the health side, we are adding people, and we are adding centres also.

items.statement: Carried forward tax losses of ₹2,100Cr available for future years
items.quote: Yeah, we have about ₹2,100Cr of carried forward losses. So, of course, as the future years play by, we should get the benefit of those.

items.statement: Health insurance affordability focus: preferred provider networks, deductibles, monthly/quarterly payment modes
items.quote: We are focused on deductibles, offering small deductibles. We are offering monthly and quarterly modes of payment on our platform right now.

items.statement: Claims process innovation: green channel concept with pre-populated documentation to reduce hospital wait times
items.quote: we are working with our insurance partners to try and see that at least for Policybazaar with our customers, are there ways that we can provide , like a green channel kind of concept where you know the documentati on, a lot of the stuff that is required, is pre-populated

items.statement: Reinsurance broking license obtained few months ago, early stage, focusing on protection category
items.quote: We just got our license a few months ago. We are working on it. As you correctly said, protection is one category that we definitely see it impacting and we'll see how that goes as the year progresses.

items.statement: Renewal premium grew to ₹5,845Cr from ₹4,400Cr, renewal rate stable at 69%
items.quote: It is exactly 69%. It was 70% earlier and 69% right now. So, it's been the same. If I look at the last 4-5 quarters, it's all 68% to 70

items.statement: Trail revenue ₹577Cr up from ₹388Cr at 85% margin, core insurance renewal take rate ~7%
items.quote: Our trail revenue, which was ₹577Cr up from ₹388Cr last year. So if you notice, that's almost ₹190Cr growth, and this comes at 85% margin and is a significant source of profit.

items.statement: Bima Sugam seen as market enabler, not threat; digital backend rails benefit digital players like Policybazaar
items.quote: I think it's a fantastic thing that would happen. It would expand the market dramatically, I think with it coming in, the market might be 20x of where it is, and you know, if it is 20x, I'm sure we'll also have some share out there.

items.statement: Volume growth target of more than 30% for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: The target is around more than 30%.

items.statement: Export revenue target of at least 20% of total revenue for FY25
items.quote: we believe the export should b e at least 20% of our total revenue for the coming year and definitely the endeavor will be to increase it further

items.statement: Export revenue target of 30-35% by FY26
items.quote: In FY26 we are targeting between 30% and 35%.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA per kg target to maintain or increase from current Rs 65-66 level
items.quote: Absolutely. It should also increase revenue.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 175 crore over two phases: Phase 1 Rs 115 crore by March 2025, Phase 2 balance by December 2025
items.quote: Phase one, including setting up for capacity to manufacture value fitting solutions and , titanium welded tubes, which is to be completed by March 2025. Phase two includes the capacity expansion for setting up a fitting solution and welded or seamless pipe or tubes by December 2025.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of Rs 15-20 crore annually
items.quote: Apart from that, there can be few more CAPEX, those will be not significant in size. So, would be maintenance sort of CAPEX which can be in the range of Rs. 15 to Rs. 20 crores.

items.statement: Welded pipe capacity utilization target of 80%, seamless at 85-95%
items.quote: In case of seamless, we have been achieving around 85 to 95 that can be maintained and in case of welded the target is around 80% sort of number.

items.statement: Titanium welded tube capacity of 300 metric tons per month in Phase 1
items.quote: On the side of welded, wherein we are putting higher grade of titanium and few categories where which can be used for food processing and pharmaceutical, so those capacity would be roughly in the range of 300 metric tons on the per month basis in the first phase.

items.statement: Current order book of Rs 240 crore with execution cycle of roughly 100 days
