There are some sure questions, I already see what is likely to be JLR's investment and what is ours - about GBP 3.5 billion in JLR and broadly similar lines for Tata Motors

items.statement: CV business achieved double-digit EBITDA for FY24, Q4 EBITDA ~12%, PBT ~Rs 6,000 Cr, $1bn EBITDA new high
items.quote: Overall numbers, it's been again a very strong year, there's a highest ever revenues, highest ever proﬁts as far as this business is concerned as well. And we ended at Rs. 78,800 Cr revenue with a double -digit EBITDA that we had co mmitted. And for the quarter the EBITDA came in stronger at about 12

items.statement: PV industry growth expected <5% in FY25 due to high base, channel inventory, elections, heatwave; secular growth 6-8%
items.quote: after triangulating the projections from multiple places, we clearly see that the industry will moderate and grow less than 5%, given that the pent -up demand has got exhausted, the channel inventory is high a nd in the ﬁrst quarter, we will face certain factors like that of elections, heat wave which might dampen the demand temporarily for quarter one

items.statement: JLR order book 133k units (excl. 33k Range Rover BEV waitlist), above normalized 110k; Europe/UK soft, NA/Overseas/China strong
items.quote: We did end the year with an order book of 133,000 units, that includes orders for SV vehicles that does not include the 33,000 people I mentioned to have signed up to the waiting list on Range Rover BEV. Pre-COVID, our order bank sort of averaged a normalized level, of around 110,000 units.

items.statement: JLR Range Rover/RR Sport production capacity ramped up; Solihull plant at record 201k Range Rover sales, Defender 115k record
items.quote: Range Rover is up 27%, that's driven by progressive improvements in both our production system and those of our suppliers, allowing us to move up capacity levels in our Solihull plant. That level of 201,000 units is a record sales for the Range Rover brand.

items.statement: PV Sanand EV facility ramp: Jan <1k, last month 6,500, targeting 10k soon, then 15-16k/month
items.quote: Sanand facility, we started in Jan, we did about less than 1,000 production in Jan, but we have progressively ramped up. And last month we crossed 6,000, to be speciﬁc, 6,500. And soon the production ramp-up is going to attain a level of 10,000. And going forward then, you know, further improvement up to 15,000 to 16,000 numbers

items.statement: JLR VME increased from 0.5% to 3% YoY, offset by material cost improvements (GBP 267m, half raw materials, half non-repeat of semi/supplier costs)
items.quote: price is now a negative in this walk, whereas historically for the last few quarters, it's been positive. That is due to slow increases in our VME rates from 0.5% a year ago to 3%, that 3% is still very light in comparison to many others in the market. Those increases in VME have however been more than oﬀset by material cost improvements versus a year ago

items.statement: CV commodities: ferrous metals softened, aluminum up, other non-ferrous stable; Q1 seeing increases in castings, forgings, aluminum, tires, forex; will pass through price increases
items.quote: In Q1 itself, we are seeing some increase in casting , forgings, aluminum, tires. Fore x will also have some impact. So, yes, Balaji, I think we will have some impact due to commodities, which we will pass through appropriate price increases at the right time

items.statement: PV battery costs still declining, secured best costs from supplier; further reduction expected but nearing floor; better realizations from this quarter
items.quote: So far, you know, we have been seeing the battery prices still coming down. We have secured the best possible battery costs from our supplier. Going forward, I think this is going to still go down to some extent, but I think this would be more or less reaching the level of what we can think as the best possible reduction of sale prices.

items.statement: PV multi-powertrain mix: petrol 58%, diesel 13%, EV 13%, CNG 16%; CAFE headroom substantial, prepared for CAFE III/IV
items.quote: With petrol at 58%, diesel at 13%, 13% EVs, and 16% CNGs, so we are playing all the powertrains and it's coming through very nicely. And that has ensured those green emissions friendly vehicles also mean that our CAFE headroom that we have is substantial at this point in time.

items.statement: Tata Motors Finance GNPA 5.6%, NNPA 3.2%, collection efficiency improving, early delinquency healthy, capital adequacy and liquidity adequate
items.quote: Collection eﬃciency continues to improve and that's why GNPA has now reduced to 5.6% and NNPA is 3.2%. So from that perspective, the portfolio is back under control

items.statement: Consolidated automotive debt Rs 16,000 Cr (Rs 7,300 Cr external, Rs 8,700 Cr finance leases); India business Rs 1,000 Cr net cash; JLR net debt GBP 732m (from GBP 3bn), repaid >GBP 1.8bn from operating cash flow
items.quote: automotive debt is now Rs. 16,000 Cr, of it Rs. 7,300 Cr is the external debt a nd Rs. 8,700 Cr is ﬁnancial leases. And split diﬀerently, the India business is now Rs. 1,000 Cr positive cash. JLR and Singapore are the two places where we have the debt to be knocked out, and the plan is to ensure this year we take that out completely

items.statement: JLR no immediate plans to access bond markets; will fund in due course
items.quote: At the moment there are no plans to access the bond markets, but in due course, we will of course do funding again, but no direct, no immediate plans.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend: Rs 3 ordinary + Rs 3 special = Rs 6/share; DVR Rs 3.1 + Rs 3.1 = Rs 6.2/share; total payout ~Rs 2,300 Cr (highest ever)
items.quote: the Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 3 for the ordinary shareholders, Rs. 3.1 for the DVR shareholders, which is the normal dividend and there is also a special dividend in lieu of the successful TTL IPO of Rs. 3 per share for Ordinary and Rs. 3.1 for the DVR holders . So together is about Rs. 6 and Rs. 6.2 resulting in a cash ﬂow of almost Rs. 2,300 Cr, the highest ever dividend that Tata

items.statement: PV PLI: certificate for Tiago EV received, SOP for disbursement being finalized, expect disbursement H2 FY25; applying for 2 more products in Q1, 1 in Q2
items.quote: PLI, so far we have got the cer tiﬁcate for Tiago EV. And right now the SOP for disbursement is being ﬁnalized. And we are hoping that in the second half of this ﬁnancial year, we may start getting the disbursement. We are also going to apply for additi onal two products in Q1 and for the additional one product in Q2 also

items.statement: Management expects FY25 volume growth of around 10% and EBITDA margin of 20-22%
items.quote: we have always been optimistic, and we always feel that 10% to 15% growth rate has been our norm. There have been a few years like last year where we have dropped below that. But otherwise, 10% is, I think, what we expect.

items.statement: FY24 capex was INR120 crores; FY25 capex planned at INR60-80 crores plus potential INR75-200 crores for new products over 2 years
items.quote: this year, our total capital expenditure is about INR120 crores. In that INR120 crores is also some expenditure for routine maintenance capex and the solar plant to supply electricity to our Dahej facility.

items.statement: Ethylamine plant (100 TPD, INR375 cr capitalized) commissioned and running well; utilization ~60% in H2 FY24
items.quote: the ethylamines plant, which we had been constructing over the last 2, 2.5 years has been commissioned and has been running very well much better than our expectations. And it is now probably the largest ethylamine plant in the world.

items.statement: Acetonitrile plant utilization ~55-60% in H2 FY24 due to Chinese competition
items.quote: The second half was not as good as the first half because the Chinese pressure continued in terms of price and aggressive selling in the Indian market. So -- we were at about half our capacity 55%, a little better than half.

items.statement: Pharma demand stable and growing; agrochemical destocking ending but Chinese competition increasing
items.quote: the market demand for pharma is quite stable now and growing. And we have managed to increase our sales in terms of tonnage.

items.statement: Ethylamine margins improved in last 3-4 months due to lower ethanol prices and stable selling prices; methylamine margins stable; MIPA margins pressured after anti-dumping duty expiry
items.quote: But as far as pricing is concerned, yes, it has improved on both the selling side as well as the raw material side, the ethyl alcohol has softened. compared to what it was, say, 6 months, | year ago.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 20-22%; FY24 average selling price dropped ~20%, top line down ~14%
items.quote: I would say that 20% EBITDA margin is what we hope to achieve between 20% and 22%.

items.statement: FY24 volume growth under 10% (just short of 1 lakh tons); H2 weaker due to acetonitrile and MIPA pressure
items.quote: Yes, total volume growth for the whole year is under 10%. Second half was much -- I mean, it was disappointing largely under pressure from Acetonitrile, as I said earlier, to Nilesh.

items.statement: Acetonitrile prices stabilized around INR145-160/kg; ethylamine prices INR150-160/kg; raw materials: ammonia INR50-52/kg, acetic acid <INR40/kg, methanol <INR30/kg
items.quote: About INR150 or so. For the larger people INR145, for the smaller people INR160 that kind.

items.statement: Chinese competition across products (acetonitrile, MIPA, methylamine); Balaji adding 40k ton methylamine plant; Chinese methylamine capacity announcement noted
items.quote: it's not just acetonitrile, it's across the board, they have too much capacity in most of their chemical industry. And in fact, we recently saw an announcement by one of their companies for a huge methylamines plant.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty investigation on acetonitrile initiated March 2024; interim relief possible Q4 FY25; injury estimated 15-20%
items.quote: we have filed antidumping in December and in March '24, the investigation has been initiated, hearings are going on right now and we are planning for filing interim relief also in that. But it will take time. Maybe in Q4 of '24-'25, we expect that to come, if it is favorable on our side. Injury is in the range of 15% to 20%.

items.statement: FY24 sales mix: ~40-50% amines, ~25% derivatives, ~20-25% specialty (mainly acetonitrile)
items.quote: It's still, I think, in the region of 40% to 50% is the main Amines about 25% is derivatives and about 20% to 25% is specialty, which is the main one being Acetonitrile.

items.statement: Other expenses up INR15 crores QoQ due to CSR provision, Patalganga asset impairment, higher power/fuel from increased production
items.quote: So mainly CSR expenses, which we could not spend, we had to make provision for that, and there was one asset at Patalganga, which was not being used, so we had to impair that. and since there is increase in production, the power and fuel expenses have increased.

items.statement: Solar capacity 8.5 MW total (3.5 MW added in Jan FY24); saves INR3-4 crores/year vs grid; power cost lower in FY24 due to lower coal prices
items.quote: Yes, about -- my estimate would be these 8 megawatts would be giving you about INR3 crores to INR4 crores of savings in view of if you were buying from the grid, right?

items.statement: Old ethylamine plant at Patalganga (15k tons) to be converted to methylamine over ~2 years; Dahej methylamine plant at 80-85% utilization (45k tons/yr)
items.quote: No, we are having plans to convert it into methylamines. The engineering has just started. It would take a little time to convert it but_we are preparing for 2 years down the line when the demand has grown to a level where we will need it.

items.statement: Acetonitrile market size 30-35k tons; 50-55% imported in FY24
items.quote: Market size would be in the range of 30,000 to 35,000 tons. And I would say about 50% of that estimated is imported last year. 50% to 55% was imported.

items.statement: FY25 pre-sales guidance of Rs.1,350-1,400 crores, implying 33-35% growth over FY24
items.quote: In all of these projects, launches and the expansions, we are looking at a guidance of about 33% to 35% growth in our pre-sales figure from what we did this year, where we are aiming between Rs.1,350 plus crores in this FY25.

items.statement: Target to reduce debt-to-equity ratio to 0.8x by end of FY25
items.quote: And our target is to bring this to 0.8x by the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain stable at 30% or above in FY25
items.quote: But however, the EBITDA margin should be in the range of 30% or 30% plus kind of a thing, as we are maintaining the stable margin out of the portfolio.

items.statement: Revenue visibility of Rs.6,400 crores from OC received, ongoing projects and launch pipeline over ~4 years
items.quote: With our OC received and ongoing project portfolio, we have a revenue visibility of Rs.1,860 crores from our ongoing projects. And we are expecting Rs.4,570 crores of the launch pipeline. And that is going to deepen further the revenue visibility to totaling to Rs.6,400 crores.

items.statement: Estimated net cash flow of Rs.750 crores from OC received and ongoing portfolio
items.quote: The 5 estimated net cash flow from OC received and ongoing portfolio is estimated to be Rs.750 crores

items.statement: FY24 pre-sales of Rs.1,017 crores and 4.73 lakh sq ft; Q4 FY24 sales of Rs.287 crores and 1.13 lakh sq ft
items.quote: Our sales value and revenue crossed the mark of, in the history, and hence we have achieved the back of pre-sales of Rs.1,017 crores and the pre-sale area of 4,73,000 square feet.

items.statement: Manhattan project 76% sold, Eden project >50% sold in first year, Prive project 38% sold, Bangalore projects 85% sold
items.quote: Our flagship, Ajmera Manhattan Project which is in Wadala has seen about 76% sales already happening in that project. Whereas I am very proud to say we are currently just above the podium parking levels on the E-deck level, and we still have about 35 to 36 floors to complete.

items.statement: Greenfinity next phase launched in Q4 FY24, 19% sold
items.quote: We also launched Greenfinity the next phase during this quarter and have sold about 19% of its inventory, and the project is currently at the exploration stage.

items.statement: Plan to launch 8 projects in FY25 with total GDV of Rs.4,500+ crores and 1.9 million sq ft development
items.quote: We are about to launch about 8 projects with a total GDV of about Rs.4,500 plus crores with a total development of about 1.9 million square feet.

items.statement: New Wadala phase with GDV of Rs.1,500 crores to be launched in FY25
items.quote: I am very happy to say that on the back of a profound sales of Ajmera Manhattan, we are also adding in our existing new launches, a new phase of Wadala, which will have a GDV of about Rs.1,500 crores.

items.statement: Business development pipeline targeting Rs.3,000-3,500 crores of new projects in FY25
items.quote: We also have further guided that we are also looking at our portfolio expansions wherein we are under advanced talks to a lot of projects, and hopefully that should materialize during this financial year, the coming financial year. And we are looking to add about Rs.3,000 crores to Rs.3,500 crores of project in our pipeline from what we are existing already having.

items.statement: Manhattan new phase targeting launch in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our estimate is that towards the last quarter of FY25 we should be able to launch this.

items.statement: Kanjurmarg project phase launch planned in FY25, Bhandup project official launch by June 2024
items.quote: And definitely we are going to launch one of the phases this financial year. And we are working on the same. And hopefully we should be giving a good announcement soon.

items.statement: Existing land bank of ~12 million sq ft carpet area (Wadala, Kanjurmarg, others) to be launched over next 2-4 years
items.quote: With our existing portfolio and existing land banks, that is Wadala, Kanjurmarg and other places, we have about 12-odd million square feet of carpet area to be launched.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 30%, PAT margin 15%; Q4 FY24 EBITDA Rs.69 crores, PAT Rs.29 crores
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs.209 crores which is 56% Y-o-Y increase, which is having the EBITDA margin of 30%. And PAT stood at Rs.103 crores, witnessing 44% Y-o-Y growth, resulting in a PAT margin of 15%.

items.statement: Manhattan realization increased from Rs.28,500/sq ft (FY23) to Rs.31,100/sq ft (FY24)
items.quote: To give you a very significant sales contribution from the Manhattan, last year FY23, on an average basis Manhattan had a 28,500 plus on a carpet basis, which has moved up to 31,100 on FY24 basis.

items.statement: Redevelopment project margins: slum 18-22%, society 25-35%, MHADA 30-35%, own land 40-50%
items.quote: Whenever it is a slum, it is usually around 18% to 22%. If it is society, it is about 25% to 35%. MHADA redevelopment is about 30%, 35%. So, that's where we range. And if it is our own land, then it is about 40%, 50%.

items.statement: Debt stable at Rs.780 crores, debt-to-equity 0.9x, weighted average cost of debt below 12%
items.quote: I am pleased to inform that despite aggressive business development activities, our debt remained stable at Rs.780 crores, improving the debt equity ratio below 1x benchmark and precisely at 0.9x to equity. The weighted average cost of the debt remains stable and below 12%.

items.statement: FY24 collections Rs.570 crores; Q4 FY24 collections Rs.197 crores (91% YoY growth)
items.quote: The collections stood at Rs.570 crores.

items.statement: Strong demand across segments: high-end (Juhu 38% sold pre-completion), mid-affordable (Bangalore), mass (Manhattan 76% sold at podium stage)
items.quote: So, if you really look at the way sales are happening, just to give you an example of Juhu, as I said, usually in the earlier days and when we actually took up the project, in a micro market like Juhu where the project is a little high end, usually these sales are happening towards the completion of the project or once the project is completed. But if you really look at it, we have already sold ab

items.statement: New players entering MMR but established brand and 55-year track record (45,000+ apartments) provide competitive advantage in redevelopment deals
items.quote: People are entering, market is good, so obviously many new players are coming in, and which is good for the market. But most importantly, for us, we are not too worried is primarily because we see that today in spite of there being competition, there has been enough and good demand for established players.

items.statement: Portfolio average realization ~Rs.19,000/sq ft (Rs.1,000+ crores sales / 4+ lakh sq ft); Bangalore Rs.6,000-9,000/sq ft, Mumbai varies by micro-market
items.quote: So, typically like Rs.1,000 crores of sales and having 4 lakhs plus square feet kind of a thing. So, on an average we have about Rs.19,000 as per square feet realization on a portfolio level basis.

items.statement: Diverse portfolio: Wadala (Manhattan, Greenfinity), Ghatkopar (Eden), Juhu (Prive), Bangalore (Lugaano, Florenza), upcoming Kanjurmarg, Bhandup
items.quote: In Mumbai market, we are spending on a very different micro market right from our own land at Wadala to Juhu or to the Pantnagar Eden Project, Greenfinity which is another affordable product at Wadala kind of a thing.

items.statement: Cluster redevelopment requires minimum 4,000 sq meters land; MHADA/cluster redevelopment has 30-year building age criteria
items.quote: It's about 4,000 square meters of land.

items.statement: Pre-sales guidance conservative due to launch timing (majority in Jan-Mar FY25) and phased launch strategy (60% of project value launched, targeting 30-35% sell-through)
items.quote: Now the timing of these projects is going to be anywhere between November to March. So, some will be earlier, some will be towards August, some will be November, and majority of the larger ones are going to be between Jan to March. So, to capture that entire figure in a larger way is going to be difficult, and hence looking all the permutation and combination we have given a guidance of Rs.1,350 c

items.statement: Residential market at 10-year high in CY2023; Mumbai highest sales volume and YoY growth; demand fueled by need for larger spaces and upgraded lifestyle
items.quote: Sales volume in primary markets have grown at an extremely healthy rate since 2020 and it has culminated into a 10 year high in the calendar year 2023. The last quarter, Mumbai has witnessed the highest sales volume and year on year growth all across the Indian metros.

items.statement: Redevelopment deals preferred by societies/slum dwellers due to brand trust, quality, and timeline confidence
items.quote: Now society, slum dwellers, even the cluster people, all of them prefer to have larger branded developers coming and doing their development because, A, they are convinced with the kind of project quality; B, they are convinced with the kind of timeline.

items.statement: Targets FY26 revenue of about 4,000 crores with steady EBITDA margin around 12.5%
items.quote: we aim to achieve a top line of about 4,000 crores while maintaining a steady EBITDA margins at around Sangam (India) Limited 13 th May 2024 12.5% for FY26

items.statement: Denim and Phase 1 synthetic fabric capex completed, yielding benefits from Q1 FY25; Phase 2 synthetic fabric underway; Phase 3 yarn on track for Q1 FY26 completion
items.quote: Denim and Phase 1 of synthetic fabric CAPEX has been successfully completed within the expected timeline and will be yielding benefits from Q1 Financial year 25 and this quarter onwards. Phase 2 of synthetic fabric is currently under way and is progressing as per schedule. Phase 3 of yarn segment is also scheduled and it is on track for completion by Q1 FY26

items.statement: Capacity utilization improved across all segments in Q4 FY24; running at broadly full utilization currently
items.quote: During this quarter, there has been an improvement in capacity utilization under all the segments of the company

items.statement: Exported approximately 160 lakh meters of denim fabric in FY20-23; won Texprocil award for highest denim exports
items.quote: During the year, we exported approximately 160 lakhs meter denim fabric across the world

items.quote: EBITDA margin is at 10%, which is expanded about 1.7% quarter on quarter again

items.statement: Value-added (fabric & garment) share at 53% of revenue in FY24; targets ~60% in 2 years, yarn share to fall from 47% to ~40%
items.quote: Currently, 53% of our product mix comprises of value-added products, and going forward, we are committed to increase this further

items.statement: Slight uptake in demand as sector headwinds reduce; improved price relations across all product segments
items.quote: As the sector headwinds have reduced a little, we are witnessing a slight uptake in demand, reflected in improved price relations across all our product segments

items.statement: Exports 33-40% of revenue across 60+ countries; key markets: Bangladesh, South America, Europe, Turkey, Africa, Egypt, Middle East; expects export share to remain in similar range
items.quote: currently about one third of the business in the company comes from the export market and two third comes from the domestic market

items.statement: Cotton prices at Rs 57-58k per candy, 2% cheaper than international; grid power blended cost Rs 7.25/unit; 10% energy from renewables
items.quote: And it is around 57 to 58,000 rupees is the prices per candy. So it is in the reasonable market

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity comfortable; at 85-90% of peak debt levels; undrawn long-term debt Rs 150-200 cr; peak interest cost in Q4 FY24, expected to decline
items.quote: We can safely say that we are at least about 85-90% at the peak debt levels

items.statement: Working capital borrowing cost blended at around 8%
items.quote: Working capital is between around 8%. Blended

items.statement: Last fundraise Rs 100 cr (60% promoter, 40% non-promoter); no further equity infusion foreseen; well capitalized
items.quote: Last fundraising was about 100 crores where 60% was funded by the promoter and 40% was from a non-promoter entity

items.statement: Maintained 20% dividend for continuity; will work on codified dividend policy
items.quote: So we just tried to maintain continuity. Last year, it could have been a higher number, but since we could see that, you know, margins are going to be under pressure in the future. So we tried to be conservative last year and this year we try to maintain some continuity there

items.statement: FTA talks with UK and Australia advanced; expected to progress after new government forms in a couple of months
items.quote: the very advanced talk with the UK and Australia, but it will take some time with the new government will come into power, right? Probably it will happen in a couple of months time

items.statement: Dyes and chemicals cost (classified in other expenses) rises with fabric turnover increase
items.quote: For example dyes and chemicals used in processing. When our fabric turnover increases the raw material on the processing division is dyes and chemicals but that is classified in other expenses

items.statement: Garment segment ~3% of total revenue; substantial growth expected in FY25 as garment capex completed
items.quote: Currently, Garment consists of about 3% of the total business

items.statement: Interest rates at global peak; any further rate hikes could increase finance cost beyond current peak
items.quote: we are at the peak of the interest rates across the globe. So now that is beyond our control. So whatever easing will happen there, that can contribute

items.statement: 30-40 major clients across segments; details in investor presentation
items.quote: there are about 30-40 big clients that we put on the presentation

items.statement: Competitive advantage from diversified portfolio across cotton/synthetic yarn, denim, synthetic fabric, garment; ability to supply multiple products to brands
items.quote: we are better placed in terms of the varied product ranges and when we are entering some markets where you know we're dealing with brands so we are able to supply various products versus just doing one product there

items.statement: ESOP/Sweat equity issued 2 years ago amortized over 5 years; exceptional item relates to this non-cash cost
items.quote: this is with regards to the the ESOPs and SWEAT equities that that were issued to various company, company officials, I think 2 years back. So that is that that is going to be amortised over 5 years

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth target upwards of 20%
items.quote: We continue to be bullish in terms of our outlook for '25 and expect revenue growth to be upwards of 20%.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin target high-teens
items.quote: In terms of margins, we are looking at high-teen margins on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: INR75 crore committed for Surat greenfield Phase 1
items.quote: We have also broken ground in our Surat greenfield project and have committed INR75 crores for Phase 1 expansion.

items.statement: Total CAPEX ~INR100 crore over next 1.5 years across Surat, Nadiad, Nashik
items.quote: So overall, between Surat, Nadiad, Nashik, we are looking at about INR100 crores CAPEX.

items.statement: Surat greenfield expected ready in 15 months; existing plants at 70-85% utilisation
items.quote: We have just broken ground. So we expect that factory to be ready within the next 15 months.

items.statement: Soul brand FY24 revenue ~INR3 crore, run-rate INR6 crore, FY25 target INR30 crore
items.quote: Our internal target for this year on Soul is around INR30 crores.

items.statement: Truly Indian brand 3-4% of standalone revenue, targeting Ashoka size in 3-5 years
items.quote: We are looking at anywhere between 3 to 5 years for the Truly Indian brand to get to that.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin 20.2%, up 230 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 20.2%, expanding by 230 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin 22.3%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin stood at 22.3%.

items.statement: Standalone FY24 EBITDA margin 24.6%, up 290 bps YoY
items.quote: We managed to expand EBITDA margin by 290 basis points, reaching 24.6%.

items.quote: Freight cost was around 7% in the previous quarter for us of the top line, went up to 9% in Q4.

items.statement: Strong demand across all brands; volume and revenue growth near equal in FY24
items.quote: We continue to witness strong demand across all our brands.

items.statement: Processed food share increase drove gross margin improvement in Q4
items.quote: If you also see the processed food as a share of total revenue is also higher compared to the previous quarter. And hence, the gross margins are better in this quarter.

items.quote: We've got listed in 2 more chains in the U.S., which will give us -- for the Truly Indian brand, we will have some 300 stores from these 2 chain stores.

items.quote: We expect that business to grow in this year and probably we might see another 5% growth. So it might go up to close to 30% in terms of on a standalone basis.

items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to remain debt-free as on date.

items.quote: This is largely into the CAPEX, which we have done over the last 3 years.

items.quote: There, I think our number of stores should be in excess of 1,000 or 1,500 stores where we are there in the major chains out there. U.K., we would be in about, I would say, close to 500 to 600 stores across 4 major supermarket chains there.

items.statement: Soul brand launching 20+ new products in FY25 including frozen foods, sauces, dips
items.quote: In this year, you will see we would have another 20-odd products lined up for India under the Soul brand in this financial year.

items.statement: FY24 CAPEX INR8 crore debottlenecking + INR4 crore cold storage
items.quote: Our CAPEX for FY '24 was INR8 crores in debottlenecking and another INR4 crores in cold storage project.

items.statement: Record quarterly revenue of INR898 crores in Q4 FY24, up double digits YoY driven by rail and domestic sectors; exports down and expected to remain soft short to medium term

items.statement: Export markets not buoyant in short to medium term; heavy truck market soft globally, rail markets in South America robust, North America okay, Australia flattish, ASEAN flat to low, China wind down

items.statement: Rail order book robust for next 15 months; visibility for full FY25 and into mid-FY26

items.statement: Rail demand sustainable for many years driven by wagon manufacturing, Vande Bharat, metro, locomotive, electrification, dedicated freight corridor, track doubling

items.statement: New Bharuch plant on track; main shop floor completed, pre-engineering building up, roofing and substation work in progress, ERP live, machines arriving, PPAP by end of calendar year, commercial production thereafter

items.quote: As I said that it is a volume and mix driven. So, some quarters go up, some quarters come down. So that up and down remains for every company.

items.statement: Heavy truck (Class 8) market soft globally including US and India; rail exports to South America robust, North America okay; off-highway US also weak

items.quote: Yes. 25%-30%, that is the correct range. But the long answer, definitely, Indian market is growing. And then there is definitely China-PLUS-One, which is going to and is benefitting India.

items.quote: Inorganic is always a question mark. So I think what I can only say is that if we find suitable opportunities, we will look at them. And the balance sheet supports us, I think. As you know and as you mentioned, the capex that Raju just mentioned is probably taken care of even by internal accruals. So inorganic growth is always depending on whether we find the right fit, right asset, right valuatio

items.statement: No significant price hikes; only 1-2% price impact on revenue growth; founder vision to keep prices affordable, pass on only if significant input cost increase.
items.quote: We normally -- like we said, the founder's vision was trying to keep prices affordable and get growth through volume and new customers. Until and unless, we see a significant increase in price and input costs, we do not pass it on to the customers. items.quote: The revenue per test was INR462. And the revenue per footfall was INR1,589 during this current quarter. And we reached a key milestone of 1 million patient footfall in this current quarter.

items.statement: Talent and skilled manpower (70% of ops) is key constraint for faster hub rollout; building team through skill development programs; pace limited by ability to maintain quality and customer experience.

That's also the reason why we do a lot of skill development programs and all that. But building that is not as easy as probably we speak. So that's something that we're building. items.quote: So Rishi, based on our internal assessment, I don't think there will be a chance for any impairment on the goodwill because even if you make projections on just 3 hubs and 3 spokes at the current revenue run rate of INR45 crore, you see in the financial year, it's INR45 crore. In this current quarter, we reported INR12 crore. So the annual run rate is between INR45 crores to INR48 crores run rate,

So the movement in the goodwill number that you see is INR114 crore is on account of this acquisition of PH, that is one. And there are 2 more intangibles that are recognized during this purchase price allocation, that was the

items.statement: Cash conversion strong: 28-29% cash back on revenue, generating INR170-190 crores free cash flow annually; surplus cash INR184 crores.
items.quote: currently, the cash back is going to be at a 28% - 29% level. So you will be generating almost close to INR170 crores to INR190 crores of free cash flows every year.

items.statement: Point-of-care testing not a threat; PCR is confirmatory gold standard, POC is screening only; Vijaya focused on high accuracy/sensitivity technologies.
items.quote: So basically, point-of-care is not new. It has been around for a long time. And you have to differentiate between POC and PCR. Where PCR is considered as confirmatory gold standard kind of a test, whereas point-of-care is usually done more from a screening point of view. So whether it is in COVID or in other indication, the market is very different for both. Somebody who gets a point-of-care will

items.statement: Aspiration to grow revenue 25% YoY, EBITDA 30% YoY and double store count over 3-4 years from Dec 2021
items.value: revenue 25% YoY, EBITDA 30% YoY, double store count
items.quote: In December '21, after we listed, we have guided that, our aspiration is to grow revenues by 25% year -on-year, grow EBITDA by 30% year-on-year and double the store count over a 3 to 4-year period.

items.statement: KFC long-term restaurant EBITDA margin target around 20%
items.quote: the overall long -term guidance on KFC margins we have called out that we would like to be in that 20% zone.

items.statement: Pizza Hut India expansion will be extremely cautious; markers for acceleration are SSSG recovery, ADS towards INR 50,000-55,000, restaurant EBITDA 8-10%
items.quote: The markers, I would say, 3 markers which we'll track internally. One is certainly looking at can the SSSG come back on the brand. That's the first. Reasonable ADS at a store. So moving towards INR50,000 ADS level marks again gives us some comfort, which helps us to manage costs more efficiently and deliver some sensible level of profitability. And the third would be the profit itself. I think mov

items.statement: Sri Lanka expansion to remain very cautious (single-digit store additions) until restaurant EBITDA reaches mid-teens (~15%)
items.quote: For Sri Lanka, actually it's getting it back into those -- hitting those mid-teens level, I think, will be key. So being at 15%, I think -- in and around that 15% would be good place to again look at expanding aggressively.

items.statement: Demand across consumer categories remains constrained; private final consumption expenditure worst in 2 decades over last 6 quarters
items.quote: And really, the story as we indicated even in February was that demand across all consumer product categories remains constrained. And now we've got the private final consumption expenditure metrics released by the government over the last 6 quarters. It's been the worst it has been over the last 2 decades.

items.statement: KFC Q1 FY25 trends: April impacted by Chhota Navratri; May significantly better than Jan-Mar but in line with YoY improvement; no further improvement seen
items.quote: May has -- May is significantly better than either Jan, Feb, March quarter. But I mean, it is more or less in line with the improvement that we see on a year -on-year basis. Sequentially, this quarter -- so sequentially, this quarter is a better quarter if I remove Navratri, and we are seeing trends along those lines. We are not seeing even further -- or we are not seeing further improvement in --

items.statement: Pizza Hut seeing improvement vs last year but brand still fragile; need more quarters to confirm turnaround
items.quote: On Pizza Hut, we are seeing improvement compared to what we saw last year. But because the brand is -- has undergone a fragile few quarters, I'm still wanting to see how it pans out. And perhaps before the next -- or during the next quarterly results, we s hould give you concrete evidence that indeed we are starting to turn the corner on the brand

items.statement: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA margin 13.6% in Q4 FY24, down 260 bps YoY; adjusted EBITDA margin 8.6%, down 3% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA declined 5% year -on-year and margin was 13.6%, down 260 basis points. Consolidated EBITDA at INR 110 crores, 17.5%, grew Y -on-Y by 7%. Adjusted EBITDA, that is pre-Ind AS 116, at INR54 crores in the quarter, 8.6%, declined by 3% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Pizza Hut Q4 FY24 restaurant EBITDA -2.7%; excluding additional marketing spend, brand broke even at restaurant EBITDA level
items.quote: And while gross margins improved year -on-year by 120 bps, the impact of negative SSSG and higher marketing spends meant that the restaurant EBITDA came at negative 2.7%. If we exclude the additional marketing spend done during the year -- during the quarter, the brand broke even at the restaurant EBITDA level.

items.statement: Sri Lanka Q4 FY24 restaurant EBITDA 12.3%, impacted by store operating cost inflation despite gross margin improvement of 90 bps QoQ
items.quote: And while gross margin saw also an improvement even in Lanka business by -- up by 90 basis points quarter-on-quarter, restaurant EBITDA came at 12.3%, impacted by, as Sanjay mentioned, the cost inflation which we experienced on the operating expense side of the store.

items.statement: Pizza Hut added 33 stores in FY24; Q4 FY24 net-zero additions; expansion to remain extremely cautious
items.quote: Last -- with the year gone by, we added 33 restaurants for Pizza Hut. Yes, for the quarter, 0 additions. And for the previous quarter, it was 8. As we called out, the expansion will be c autious. We are not saying we are going to be 0 or pausing completely. It will be extremely cautious, suffice to say

items.statement: Sri Lanka store additions to remain single-digit in FY25 until margins recover to mid-teens
items.quote: You could see it as single digit in terms of a store count addition for the financial year.

items.statement: FY24 capex ~INR 385 crores; KFC capex ~INR 2 cr/store (1,500-1,600 sq ft); Pizza Hut capex ~INR 1.42-1.45 cr/store
items.quote: As I called out previously, if you look at the CapEx per store per format, so KFC CapEx is generally in the ra nge of INR 2 crores per store for around 1,500 to 1,600 square feet. Pizza Hut, we are seeing it in the range of INR 1.42 crores to 1.45 crores per store on Pizza Hut.

items.statement: Gross margins improved 150 bps YoY for KFC and 120 bps for Pizza Hut in Q4 FY24; expect gross margins to range +/- 2 bps sequentially going forward; no material price increases expected
items.quote: So whatever benefit had to come in into the P&L in terms of gross margin improvement, I think that's locked largely starting Q3 of last year. And if you see sequential gross margin, we had called out that it will be ranged from plus/minus 2 basis points. I think going forward, we expect that the gross margins would be ranged about plus/minus 2 basis points. And we don't see any price increase -- m

items.statement: KFC launched 5 new burgers (American, Caribbean, Mexican, Indian veg/non-veg) and relaunched Chizza LTO and paneer Zinger in Q4 FY24
items.quote: And this quarter, we've taken our burger game to the next level by launching 5 new burgers: American, Caribbean, Mexican, Indian and Indian veg and Indian nonveg. We've re launched also, which you will discover only at the store, the Indian veg option, a paneer Zinger.

items.statement: New fried chicken entrants (Popeyes, Wow Chicken) create positive category noise; KFC's scale and sourcing economies protect margins; unlikely competitors can sustain price leadership
items.quote: So in that sense, competition is only good. Now the second part to that question is that however, at the scale that KFC operates, we undoubtedly have economies of scale also. So it is difficult for any competitor to come in and be a cost leader and, therefore, impair margins. So I don't think that should happen, point number two.

items.statement: KFC SSSG -3% in Q4 FY24; ADS INR 114,000 (impacted by ~25% new store additions which operate at 70-80% of brand average in year 1)
items.quote: SSSG came at minus 3%. Our ADS is at INR114,000. Just to clarify, the ADS is also impacted by new store additions, which we're, over the year almost at 25% restaurant additions. And as we called out, generally, the new stores take time to scale up. And their ADS are generally lower initially the first year compared to the brand average.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; consolidated PBT INR 80 lakhs (0.1%), adjusted PBT INR 8.3 cr (1.3%) in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Consolidated PBT of INR8 million or INR80 lakhs, or 0.1%. Adjusted PBT was INR8.3 crores or 1.3%.

items.statement: Demand environment soft; seasonal calendar shifts (Navratri, Adhik Maas, Shravan) make quarterly trends noisy; annual view preferred for KFC
items.quote: unfortunately, over the last 3 to 4 years post COVID, every year and every quarter that there has been some of the other exceptions. As a result the trends, which are sequential trends or year -on-year trends, some quarters where it gives out a good picture, some quarters, they are not strictly comparable.

items.statement: Ranked top 3 franchisee by Yum! on customer metrics and operating standards for both KFC and Pizza Hut; #1 QSR in India on ESG (Dow Jones Sustainability Index), 95th percentile globally; best-ever employee engagement score at 88th percentil
items.quote: We are ranked among the top 3 franchisees by Yum! on -- in both KFC as well as Pizza Hut on our customer metrics and our operating standards. We're also quite proud that we were ranked the number 1 QSR in India on our ESG score rated by Dow Jones Sustainability Index, and we are 95th percentile among all QSRs globally. We also achieved -- this is an internal metric, but I'd like to share with you.

items.statement: Appointed new CFO Munish Gupta (CA, IIM Ahmedabad, 20 years experience) and new COO Mukul Khanna (25 years in consumer durables, telecom, e-commerce)
items.quote: I am accompanied by our new CFO, Mr. Munish Gupta. He is a CA and an Executive MBA from IIM Ahmedabad with 20 years of expertise in construction, hotels, IT travel, start-ups, and FMCG.

items.statement: Appointed new COO Mukul Khanna with 25 years experience in consumer durables, telecom, and e-commerce
items.quote: In addition, we have appointed a new Chief Operating Officer, Mr. Mukul Khanna, a 25-year business leader in consumer durables, telecom, and e-commerce.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue grew 21.7% YoY to INR252.5 crores; FY24 revenue grew 26.7% to INR999 crores
items.quote: Revenue from operations is up by 26.7% to INR 999 crores from INR 788 crores in FY '23.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA grew 36% to INR175.3 crores with 17.1% margin; PAT grew 38.1% to INR83.3 crores at 8.1% margin
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 36% to INR175.3 crores. EBITDA margin stood at 17.1%. PAT grew by 38.1% to INR83.3 crores. PAT margin for FY '24 stood at 8.1%.

items.statement: Inventory days stood at 161 days as of March 31, 2024; cash and bank balance at INR345.5 crores
items.quote: Inventory days as of March 31 stood at 161 days. Cash and bank balance stood at INR345.5 crores as on March 31, 2024.

items.statement: EFTA agreement will phase out Swiss watch customs duty from 20% to 0% over 7 years, starting H2 FY25 with ~3% annual reduction
items.quote: Custom Duty on Swiss watches is currently at 20% and 2% CESS on that. Under the EFTA agreement, duty on Swiss watches will be reduced to 0 in a 7-year period. This change is likely to start in the second half of this financial year with a 3% decrease in duty every year.

items.statement: EFTA duty reduction expected to improve gross margins and attract more luxury brands to India
items.quote: This will improve Ethos' gross margins. More importantly, it will open doors for many more luxury brands to come in, for whom these rates were a deterrent to profitability and therefore, an Indian presence.

items.statement: Store count increased from 54 stores in 20 cities to 63 stores in 24 cities in FY24; added Surat, Bhubaneshwar, Raipur, Mohali and Breitling boutiques in Pune
items.quote: We started FY '24 with 54 stores in 20 cities, and we currently have 63 stores in 24 cities. We added new cities such as Surat, Bhubaneshwar, Raipur, M ohali and Breitling boutiques at Pune

items.statement: Spent INR38.3 crores on new store fit-outs and restoration in FY24
items.quote: In FY '24, we spent INR38.3 crores on the fit-out of new stores and restoration of existing ones.

items.statement: Exclusive brands accounted for nearly 29% of total sales from portfolio of 51 brands; target 50% revenue from exclusive brands long-term
items.quote: In FY '24, exclusive brands accounted for nearly 29% of our total sales from our portfolio of 51 brands.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth (SSG) was 10% for Q4 FY24
items.quote: SSG is 10% for the quarter.

items.statement: Volume growth of 19% for watches above INR1 lakh (18,471 in FY23 to 22,000 in FY24); exiting sub-INR1 lakh fashion category
items.quote: FY '23, we sold 18,471 watches above INR1 lakh. In FY '24, we sold 22,000 watches, an increase of 19%.

items.statement: Average price increase of 7-8% in Q1 FY25; most brands priced around INR92-93 CHF/INR, exclusive brands at ~INR100
items.quote: The average price increase in the first quarter was roughly about 7% to 8%. Most brands are priced around the INR92 mark.

items.statement: Target 18-20% return on capital in first year for new stores; most boutiques profitable from year one
items.quote: We try to touch 18% to 20% return on capital in the first year itself. That's how we target it.

items.statement: Lifestyle division: RIMOWA Mumbai store profitable from month 1; signing 2 more RIMOWA boutiques (Delhi Emporio, Bangalore Mall of Asia) for H2 FY25 or early FY26
items.quote: Our first store in Mumbai is doing quite well. As we said recently in all -- in our most recent results call, it has been profitable on a PAT basis since month 1.

items.statement: Opening first QlockTwo luxury clocks boutique at UB City Bangalore; actively seeking flagship Messika boutique; discussing brands with $700-800M global turnover
items.quote: We will open our first boutique this year for luxury clocks at UB City in Bangalore, with a brand known as QlockTwo. We are now actively -- also now actively looking for our first flagship boutique for Messika in the country.

items.statement: Second service centre in Bengaluru to be operational in Q2 FY25; Delhi service centre performing well
items.quote: We now plan to open a second service centre in Bengaluru, which will be operational in the second quarter of this year, allowing us to expand our geographic footprint for service.

items.statement: Pre-owned CPO billing was INR66 crores in FY24; committed to growing this business with manpower and training investments
items.quote: Billing from pre-owned CPO was INR66 crores in FY '24.

items.statement: Election Model Code of Conduct subdues April-May sales due to cash movement restrictions and event limitations; June expected strong; April went well, May doing well
items.quote: Every time there are elections, the 2 months leading up to the election are a little bit subdued, and we see great numbers in the months after it. This is because of typically a couple of things. Number one is the Model Code of Conduct, which comes into play and restricts cash movement.

items.statement: Kochi store (5,000 sq ft) opening ~July 1; 6 boutiques at Mall of Asia Bangalore delayed pending luxury floor handover; Dehradun in 45 days; Bangalore airport duty-free in 60 days; Mangalore before H2; flagship City of Time around Diwali
items.quote: Kochi, which is our -- it's a 5,000 square feet boutique will open around the 1st of July. We already have another store in Pune that is already opened. We have 6 boutiques which are lined up for opening in Mall of Asia, Bangalore. That's the landmark boutique mall coming up from

items.statement: Transferred Favre Leuba stake to KDDL to focus on retail; KDDL to handle manufacturing; Ethos retains ~30% stake to influence brand strategy for India; target 50% revenue from exclusive brands
items.quote: Ethos will focus upon India. Ethos' core competency is retail in India, right? Our long-term goal is to reach 50% of our brands coming where we have exclusivity and through strategic tie-up, right?

items.statement: Investing in HR professionalization, training school for shop floor talent, design and tech teams to support 10-year 10x revenue goal
items.quote: The need for the hour to achieve the 10-year goal of 10x revenue is to get great talent at every level. We will make investments into our training school for talent on the shop floor as well as investments into engagement of the HR to lower attrition.

items.statement: No short-term guidance going forward; focusing on long-term strategies and 10-year vision after 2 years of quarterly guidance
items.quote: These earnings call now represent 2 years of earnings calls since we listed. We have given short-term guidance till now to guide investors and increase stability. We will now focus on long-term strategies and long-term visions instead of just focusing on giving short-term guidance.

items.statement: CHF/INR forex: started FY24 at INR92, peaked at INR99 in Dec'23, back to INR92; Q4 forex gain INR1.3 crores; full year forex loss INR1 crore
items.quote: The CHF to INR at the start of the year was INR92. At in December '23, it was INR99, which was not seen historically. And again, now it's INR92. In terms of overall forex gain in Q4, we are positive by INR1.3 crores. And for the full year, the overall forex's, there is a loss of INR1 crore.

items.statement: Launching app and overhauling website for better UI/UX, personalization, concierge service; deploying AI with 4 use cases including proprietary LLMs for visual search and customer presentations
items.quote: With the launch of the app and an upcoming overhaul of the website, we will focus on better user interaction, UI/UX, digital journey personalization and better service provided by our concierge with the help of technology.

items.statement: Target loan book growth of 22-24% for FY25 and 22-25% CAGR over next 3-5 years
items.quote: we are looking for a growth for FY '25, a growth of 22% to 24% on the advanced book si de. And going forward also, we want to look to increase our loan growth on a CAGR of 22% to 25% over the next three to five years

items.statement: Target ROTA expansion to 1.4% for FY25 with continuous improvement thereafter
items.quote: We target ROTA expansion to 1.4% for FY'25 and continuous ROTA expansion going forward.

items.statement: Opex ratio expected to remain around current FY24 level of 2.95% in FY25
items.quote: We believe our opex ratio going forward will remain around the same level as in the current fiscal year.

items.statement: Plan to add 25+ branches in FY25 to cross 200 total branches
items.quote: Post the growth capital pouring in, we are intending to scale up our branch expansion by adding 25 plus branches and we want to cross our branch count by end of this year to 200 plus.

items.statement: Target medium-term CD ratio in mid to high 80s from current 79%
items.quote: So we typically look for the medium term range to take it mid to the high 80s.

items.statement: NIM for FY24 was 3.9%; expect expansion via CD ratio improvement and loan repricing
items.quote: The NIM for the year is 3.9% and our non-interest income is 0.8% against 0.6% a year before.

items.statement: 35-40% of floating rate book to reprice in Q1 FY25 after 35 bps MCLR hike in FY24
items.quote: Now we believe around our 35% to 40% of the book will be starting repricing in quarter one only of FY '25 so which will be giving us a benefit as we move forward.

items.statement: Cost of deposits stabilized at 7.55-7.65% retail rate; expect stable cost of funds
items.quote: our offered rate on retail deposit is now constant over the last, for a while, say six months to nin e months. That is the almost similar rates. We believe the rate of deposit, cost of deposit is getting optimized

items.statement: Gross advances at INR 6,160 crore as of March 31, 2024 with 19% 5-year CAGR
items.quote: Our gross advances stood at INR 6160 crores as on March 31, registering 5-year CAGR of 19%, Q-o-Q growth of 8% and Y-o-Y growth of 12% respectively.

items.statement: FY24 disbursements INR 2,068 crore; Q4 FY24 disbursements INR 675 crore (76% QoQ growth)
items.quote: Our disbursements for FY24 were INR 2,068 crores consisting of around 27% to agriculture, 24%-25% to mortgage, 22%-23% to MSME and trading segment.

items.statement: GNPA 2.8%, NNPA 1.4% in FY24; slippage ratio 2.4%, upgrade/recovery 2.1%
items.quote: We have industry leading asset quality with GNPA and NNPA off 2.8% and 1.4% respectively. Our NNPA is stable around the same level over the last 3 years.

items.statement: PCR maintained at 50%+; near-zero write-offs and nil NPA sell-off since inception
items.quote: Our provision coverage ratio for the current period is around 50% and we are maintaining almost similar type of PCR over the period.

items.statement: SMA 1+2 at 4.5% of portfolio; 90%+ recovery via standing instruction route
items.quote: If we look into SMA 1 and 2, which put together is 4.5%. SMA 0 being 0 to 30 days is one segment given we being using our own accounts for recovery and our 90% plus recovery through SI route.

items.statement: Branch expansion to 200+ branches in FY25; majority outside Punjab
items.quote: We are presently having 177 branches spread over 5 states and 1 union territory of Chandigarh. Post the growth capital pouring in, we are intending to scale up our branch expansion by adding 25 plus branches and we want to cross our branch count by end of this year to 200 plus.

items.statement: Regional/cluster and head office infrastructure ready to support 225-250 branches from current 177
items.quote: We have the regional cluster and head office level readiness t o support up to 225 to 250 branches from 177

items.statement: Deposit rates stable at 7.55-7.65% for retail; MCLR increased 35 bps in FY24 (20 bps in Q4)
items.quote: During FY '24 our deposit rate remain almost at the same level throughout beginning of the year and at the end of the year with our highest rate of deposit for retail was around 7.55% to 7.65%. At the end of the year also it is 7.55 % to 7.65% and if we look into the MCLR we have increased the MCLR by 35 basi s points during FY '24 out of which 20 basi s point increase in the Q4 FY '24

items.statement: Quarterly pattern: Q1/Q3 deposit-heavy, Q2/Q4 advance-heavy due to SURU branch mix (74%)
items.quote: If you look into our historical trends, you will find our Q1 will be heavy on deposit growth, Q2 being heavy on our advanced growth, Q3 being heavy on our deposit growth, Q4 being our heavy on the advanced growth.

items.statement: On track for universal bank license; meet all criteria except net NPA <1% (currently 1.4%); target 12-18 months
items.quote: If we look into that particular guidelines, we have complied with all the requirements except net NPA, which is prescribed to be 1%. We believe that given our plan going ahead, keeping in view the macroeconomic factors which are prevailing as on date, we intend to achieve that over the next 12 to 18-month period.

items.statement: No significant impact from farmer protests on recoveries or asset quality; minimal historical impact
items.quote: Whether we took into from the perspective of the growth rate or from the asset qualityyou can see there is no impact of the same. Yes, we believe strongly as a corporate , this thing should settle quickly. But presently we are not seeing any significant impact on it on our balance sheet and the book

items.statement: ECL framework adoption expected to have positive impact (reduced provision requirement)
items.quote: As far as the last calculation which we have done on the ECL, we are finding a positive impact on the reduced ECL provision requirement as per the performance.

items.statement: Dividend payout 4% of profit; board decision balancing growth capital retention and investor cash flow
items.quote: So, this is a decision of my board. So, being a growth-oriented organization / we being in a growth engine-based organization, which will necessitating to sow a seed for our future growth. So, this is as part of that strategy that we continue to sow a seed for our future growth and keep on keeping/retaining the profit/money with us.

items.statement: CASA ratio 38%+ (retail CASA 41%+); retail deposits 92.9% of total deposits
items.quote: If we look into our CASA number if you slice it further and divide it with our deposit which is retail deposit you will find still our retail CASA deposit is 41% plus which is almost a similar level which was a year back.

items.statement: Staff cost 55-60% of opex; no significant middle management hiring needed for 225-250 branch capacity
items.quote: Our overall opex ratio, given staff cost and other staff cost, that is the split which we are talking about is typically, we are typically maintaining 55% to 60% in one of the segment, being 40% to 45% being other segment.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs.675 crores (~30% growth)
items.quote: I am pleased to inform you that we are expecting close to 30% growth this year and achieve a combined revenue of Rs.675 crores.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target of over Rs.1000 crores
items.quote: we aim to now double our Jash Engineering Limited revenue to over Rs.1000 crores FY28 that is in four years time

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 23-24% over time
items.quote: As I have been informing all the investors over the last few years, we are quite hopeful of increasing our EBITDA margin up to 23-24% in time to come to come.

items.statement: PAT margin target range of 12-14%
items.quote: As already informed by me before that we expect PAT margins to grow between 12-14% in time to come.

items.statement: Combined order book of Rs.816 crores (excl. Waterfront) as of FY24 end
items.quote: Our combined orderbook is Rs.816 crore of which business outside India is Rs.551 crores and within India is Rs.265 crores.

items.statement: Waterfront UK order book ~Rs.30 crores; 80% consolidation adds Rs.225-235 crores
items.quote: This Rs.816 crores does not include the current order booking of Waterfront UK. This current order booking is close to Rs.30 crores and we hope that when 80% of this order book of Waterfront is added to the combine orderbook we are looking at something like Rs.225-235 crores as our combined order book including Waterfront.

items.statement: Negotiated orders Rs.31 crores and under negotiation Rs.33 crores as of 1st May (excl. large tickets)
items.quote: As on 1st May our orders which we have already negotiated and which we expect to receive are of Rs.31 crores and orders under negotiations are also around Rs.33 crores and t his does not include marqu ee big orders which are under negotiation

items.statement: Annual capex of Rs.20-25 crores for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Every year somewhere between Rs.20-25 crores. So, every year we will be investing Rs.20-25 crores to add some facility and this will keep on happening for next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Current manufacturing potential ~Rs.800 crores; targeting Rs.1000 crores with new plants
items.quote: with all these facilities whi ch we own now, our turnover potential has come to around Rs.800 crores. So, we are committed to build facility as we grow, with Rs.800 crores facility we would be able to sustain till next year.
