items.statement: Fierce competition and pricing actions by some competitors in some markets
items.quote: But what we are seeing definitely in the market i s fierce competition and even pricing actions being taken by some competition in some markets

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on PVC paste resin reimposed; minimal impact as EPVC volume only 6,000-7,000 tons
items.quote: So there is an anti -dumping duty which has been notified recently. It used to be there earlier, Ritesh. And some years ago, it was taken away and now it has been reimposed. So on us, it does not have a material impact because our volume of EPVC is very, very low.

items.statement: Net cash surplus ~INR1,820 crores as of March 31, 2024; land sale in April 2024 added INR417 cr gain (not in FY24 profits)
items.quote: The company continues to have a strong balance sheet with a net cash surplus of roughly INR1,820 crores as on 31st of March '24.

items.statement: Power costs reduced due to stabilized coal rates; EDC inventory shored up for monsoon
items.quote: See, one thing is power was down because coal rates have kind of stabilized. So power has reduced. So that is one of the reasons.

items.statement: Agri demand expected high single digits in Q1 FY25; Building & Construction (non-agri) expected high teens growth
items.quote: Yes, you're right with stable PVC prices, our expectation is that the agri demand will be in the high single digits. And you also look at it from the Building & Construction segment, you are seeing a robust growth in that segment as well, and we expect that to be in the high teens.

items.statement: No major election impact on volumes except on active polling days; demand pull strong in both agri and non-agri
items.quote: Not really. See, except in those weeks or in those days when there are active elections, we have not seen as such a major impact of elections on our volumes, markets have been strong.

items.statement: Fittings plant commissioned March FY23 running at near-full capacity (900-1,000 MT/month); fittings contribution to revenue expected to grow
items.quote: the plant is close to near -end capacity utilization. Capacity was set up for almost 1,000 -- 900 to 1 ,000 metric tons per month. And we are hitting close to that.

items.statement: PVC price outlook uncertain due to Middle East volatility and anti-dumping duty talks; watching closely
items.quote: We have to wait and watch. It's not just anti-dumping duty. It's also going to be dependent upon the Middle East situation, which has been quite volatile. So we are constantly watching -- very closely watching this situation.

items.statement: No inorganic growth planned; capacity expansion will be organic only
items.quote: It will be organic growth.

items.statement: Management team complete; plumber loyalty program launched with strong traction, targeting pan-India rollout in a year
items.quote: our "Plumber loyalty program", which went l ive. This is something that was a gap, probably I can say, for quite a while. And it is having good traction. We are receiving very strong feedback on the cities and the market where we've launched it.

items.statement: PVC resin external sales FY24 ~14,000-15,000 tons (vs 27,000 tons FY23); Q4 external sales ~6,000 tons; balance consumed in-house
items.quote: So this year, we have sold roughly 14,000, 15,000 tons of PVC externally, balance all we have consumed in-house. So last year, if you remember, we had sold roughly 27,000 tons outside.

items.statement: No material inventory gain/loss in Q4; FY24 not material vs prior year where Q2 losses offset Q1 profits
items.quote: No, there has not been any material gain or loss this quarter at least. In September, in the third quarter, there was some inventory loss because if you remember, prices went down by INR11 right after the end of September.

items.statement: No diversification into OPVC, PERT, or HDPE; focusing on PVC segment only
items.quote: At the moment, we are just observing and evaluating these new pro ducts. The PVC demand is robust enough to us -- for us to focus at the PVC segment at the moment for us for Finolex

items.statement: Management targets INR 300 crore+ per quarter revenue in FY25 and aims for double-digit EBITDA margin.
items.quote: But more or less, our strive is that to get into the INR 300 crores and INR 300 crores plus for the quarter in the coming year.

items.statement: Management expects to achieve INR 2,000 crore turnover without significant capex.
items.quote: And we expect that with increased market access, achieving a turnover up to INR 2,000 crores, as I have said in many of my investment calls is possible without significant capex or modernization.

items.statement: Simone Frederico & Figli brand expected to generate minimum INR 25 crore turnover in FY25, doubling annually.
items.quote: Simone itself, we expect about INR25 crores minimum turnover to happen in FY '25. And then we hope that this will continue to double every year.

items.statement: Gradual industry recovery expected in FY25 driven by domestic demand revival, export recovery, and lower raw material prices.
items.quote: A gradual recovery at an industry level is expected in the next financial year '25, and on the back of improvements in sales realizations and stabilized raw material costs.

items.statement: USA market showing strong interest and new customers joining; expects to recover close to prior year levels.
items.quote: U.S.A. is showing a lot of interest now. We lost 56% compared to last year in the U.S.A. market. And we expect now to recover and get pretty close to where we were last year in the U.S.A. market again.

items.statement: EBITDA margin lower in FY24 due to subdued demand and inventory correction after COVID over-ordering; aims for double-digit margin in FY25.
items.quote: The reason is that everybody in the financial year '24 had the subdued demand and the latent demand after COVID and had ordered more than they thought.

items.statement: Endeavors to reach double-digit EBITDA margin in FY25, subject to market dynamics.
items.quote: Aditya, yes, endeavors are there to really get into the double digit for surely. Also, it has external effect and the constraints from the market also.

items.statement: Order cycles: Fabric ~60 days, Garment ~90 days, Yarn ~30 days; uniform orders have longer projections.
items.quote: Otherwise, generally, the order cycling for fabric is around 60 days. 60 days before they need it, they tell you that this is a fabric order. For Garment, it's is usually 90 days and for Yarn, it's usually 30 days.

items.statement: No significant capex needed to reach INR 2,000 crore turnover; considering third automotive textile unit in Madhya Pradesh.
items.quote: We have one in Banswara, and we are considering a third in Madhya Pradesh.

items.statement: Raw material costs stabilized; cotton prices falling but pricing under pressure; linen and wool prices rising.
items.quote: With the cotton prices falling, I think that will continue to remain good. The only problem is the pricing is now under pressure in the cotton and the natural fibers.

items.statement: Focus on high-value yarn products, synthetic/wool blends, technical synthetics, flame retardant curtains, tent fabric, automotive textiles, sportswear.
items.quote: We will continue to focus on high-value yarn products that will lead to enhancing value growth along with the overall top line.

items.statement: Bangladesh and Vietnam compete only in garments; FTAs needed to compete; Banswara's strength in yarn/fabric and sustainability compliance gives edge.
items.quote: So when you speak of Bangladesh and Vietnam, they're only doing garments, right? our bigger business is yarn and fabric. The garment part, you are correct that because unless we get FTAs, there's no way to compete.

items.statement: Hopeful for UK FTA to significantly enhance garment business outlook.
items.quote: On the regulatory front, we are hopeful that the U.K. free trade agreement happens, and that would significantly enhance the company's business outlook on Garment.

items.statement: Exports declined to 42% of revenue in FY24 from 48% in FY23; sequential recovery of 31% in Q4 FY24 driven by UAE and European uniform orders.
items.quote: The exports have declined to42% of the overall revenues in FY '24 as compared with the 48% in last year for the same period, mainly due to decline in export of more than 50% in key markets of Europe, Turkey, U.S. and the U.K.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced from 185 to ~175 days; debtor days cyclical; working capital borrowings lowered.
items.quote: Working capital cycle on the inventory side, if you look at, there is a reduction of a number of days coming from the previous year to this year. So now the inventory cycle goes like, okay, it's 175 days kind of average, which we were at 185.

items.statement: Working capital borrowings reduced due to improved working capital cycle.
items.quote: And that's the reason like our borrowings have also, on the working capital side, was lowered.

items.statement: Tesca JV (automotive textiles) turned profitable, paid tax first time; sales INR 80-100 crore range, 20% drop in FY24 but strong profitability.
items.quote: Tesca actually has the sales in the ranging from INR80 crores to INR100 crores. Like in FY '23, they did touch near to INR100 crores, like INR99.8 crores, so they were near to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Synthetic fiber consumption growing faster than cotton globally; technical synthetics (moisture management, performance fabrics) driving future demand.
items.quote: Synthetics is growing now faster than cotton. And the wool part is more ceremonial and for weddings and is more aimed at the upper end of the market.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, inflation impacting discretionary spending, inventory overhang, and lack of FTAs for garment exports remain key risks.
items.quote: The global economic climate remains challenging with geopolitical uncertainties dampening consumer confidence and impacting global trade.

items.statement: Enhanced travel budgets, larger marketing team, digital marketing tools adopted to explore new geographies.
items.quote: Travel budgets have been enhanced. We have a larger team available, and we are using all sorts of tools of digital marketing in terms of digitizing the product.

items.statement: Middleweight segment expected to grow in double digits; premiumisation theme continuing in India; motorcycle industry slowly returning to pre-COVID levels month-on-month
items.quote: What we can say is the two-wheeler market is poised for a growth, and especially the middleweight. We anticipate the middleweight growth will be in double-digit.

items.statement: Himalayan 450 currently clocking 200-plus motorcycles a day; preparing for higher numbers given global potential; supply ramp-up ongoing for domestic and international markets
items.quote: As far as the Himalayan is concerned, we launched and it has been a super hit for us and happy to share with you, it's beyond the expectation of the numbers, which we are talking about.

items.statement: New products lined up on 450cc Sherpa Platform and 650cc platform; platforms grouped to address different consumer segments with differentiated experiences
items.quote: We have currently three platforms. We have our super refined J-platform. Then we have our 450cc platform, which is the Sherpa Platform and the 650cc platform.

items.statement: Focus on absolute EBITDA increase rather than percentages; international market share recovery and non-motorcycle business growth accretive; monitoring commodity prices but no significant pressure currently
items.quote: First of all, revenue growth itself is something that we are actually focused on. We're looking at absolute increase as far as EBITDA is concerned. We're not necessarily so focused on percentages, as you know.

items.statement: No recent price hike for Royal Enfield; VECV focusing on discount reduction rather than MRP increases to improve transaction prices
items.quote: Royal Enfield side, we haven't taken the price hike very recently. VECV, Vinod? Vinod Aggarwal: In VECV, we are focusing more and more on the discount reduction

items.statement: Commodity prices stable currently; not a headwind or tailwind; tracking PGMs and working on value engineering to offset costs; pricing decisions based on price-value proposition for consumer
items.quote: Commodities, it is not a headwind as of now. Is it a tailwind? May not be. So to that extent, there is some amount of stability, which is there.

items.statement: Export retail sales strong across all markets globally; wholesale picking up slowly; long-term strategy focused on brand building, community, own subsidiaries and CKD plants in key markets
items.quote: international market, Jinesh? Jinesh Gandhi: Yes. B. Govindarajan: No. In the last quarter also I was just telling, we don't track the wholesale. Wholesale is only a transaction number for us. We always look at retail

items.statement: Export strategy divided into richer Western markets (strong profitability, salience) and high-potential LatAm/Southeast Asia markets aiming to create 'mini Indias' with deep penetration over 5-15 years
items.quote: We divided in our export markets into two. One is the richer countries, such as U.S., Europe, Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Korea, where the markets are there, they're not growing, maybe even declining, but affordability is very strong.

items.statement: CV industry has good growth potential driven by 7%+ GDP growth, strong infrastructure programme, and pent-up replacement demand for new technology trucks enhancing productivity
items.quote: As far as the demand for commercial vehicle market is concerned, I think it has got a very good potential for growth. Fundamentally, because our economy is continuing to do well, and of course, we are expecting on the back of around 6% to 8% of last year, we are expecting that this year also the economy should grow by 7% plus.

items.statement: E-bus products ready (9m, 12m, 13.5m intercity); electric truck traction good with 75 sold last year; small commercial EV on pilot with 10 customers, commercial launch from January next year followed by diesel/CNG variants
items.quote: As far as the trucks are concerned, we were the first one to introduce electric truck in 5.5 tonne category. And last year, we have sold 75 electric trucks. And this year, of course, the traction is good.

items.statement: VECV Q4 margin decline YoY due to one-off fiscal incentives accrued last year in Madhya Pradesh; no other reasons for margin decline QoQ despite volume growth
items.quote: Basically, last year in Q4, there were some fiscal incentives, which we had accrued based on the very old, which were pending in Madhya Pradesh. So due to that, there was one-off in last year Q4.

items.statement: Royal Enfield finance penetration at 61% and steadily growing; digital finance marketplace integrated; REOWN upgrade programme piloted in few cities, slowly gaining traction with dealership ecosystem
items.quote: Our finance penetration, as of now is about 61%. It's steadily growing over the period of time. I mean because when the demography is coming down, it also is quite natural that the finance penetration will be there.

items.statement: Replacement cycle for Royal Enfield yet to kick in but preparing with REOWN platform for 6 million vehicle park; focus on frictionless upgrade experience rather than pushing new motorcycles
items.quote: You touched upon the topic of the replacement cycle. In the last call, also I mentioned, it is yet to kick in. But we have to be prepared. So what we have done is to give a very frictionless experience for those consumers almost about 6 million motorcycles, which are there in the market as a vehicle park.

items.statement: Royal Enfield sold 912,000 motorcycles in FY24 (highest ever), up from 834,700 in FY23; 30% market share in 125cc+ category; 7.2% overall motorcycle market share
items.quote: For the financial year, as Siddhartha mentioned, we sold about 912,000 motorcycles, which is compared to last year, which was only about 8,34,700 motorcycles. This is our highest ever volumes in the country, India.

items.statement: VECV sold 85,560 units in FY24 (7.5% growth vs industry 4%); heavy-duty truck market share 9.2% (up from 4% industry growth); light/medium-duty market share 34.7% (market dropped 5.9%)
items.quote: For the full-year, we had 85,560 units as against last full-year of 79,623 units. So with a growth of 7.5% for the full-year. If you look at the industry, industry had grown by 4%.

items.statement: Oragadam plant awarded future-ready factory by Frost & Sullivan; plants creating benchmarks in efficiency, automation and manufacturing excellence; produced 9.2 lakh motorcycles (highest ever)
items.quote: On manufacturing, just to add, we have produced 9.2 lakh motorcycle this year, which is, once again, highest ever production with high quality fit and finish motorcycles for the globe.

items.statement: All VECV vehicles comply with BS-VI OBD2 standards; working on H2ICE technology, hydrogen fuel cells, CNG and LNG trucks; aiming to reduce water usage per vehicle by 5%
items.quote: And all our existing digital vehicles, they comply with all the strict current BS-VI, OBD2 standards. And then, of course, we are committed to increase the use of renewable energy and energy efficiency at our plants and operations.

items.statement: Achieved zero liquid discharge in all operations; all plants and warehouses net water positive (Oragadam index 3.23, Vallam 2.02); 35% renewable energy consumption; on track for 20% carbon emission reduction vs last year; motorcycle reusabi
items.quote: We have achieved zero liquid discharge in all our operations and all our plants and our warehouses are all net water positive, with an index of almost 3.23 in Oragadam and 2.02 in Vallam. We have been constantly working on improving the renewable energy usage. And during this year, further, we enhanced that, and we have 35% of total consumption onto the renewable energy.

items.statement: International market macro situation varies by market; not all markets recovering simultaneously; cautious approach to e-bus tenders under PM-eBus Sewa due to difficult payment model (per km for 12 years)
items.quote: But of course, we will be very careful, not putting in the bids to pursue the volumes at any cost. So therefore, we will see that what makes sense for us. But of course, as far as the products are concerned, we are all ready with the 9-meter bus product, 12-meter bus product, and we are also going to introduce 13.5-meter intercity bus product.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 18-20% for next 3-4 years reiterated, but near-term visibility reduced to 4-5 months due to high coffee prices
items.quote: we have been expecting more of an 18%, 20% going forward

items.statement: Domestic branded business revenue growth target of 30-40% year-on-year
items.quote: we are looking to drive that aggressively in the range of anything around 30% to 40%

items.statement: Volume growth of 14% achieved in FY24 vs 18-20% guidance due to NCL unit breakdown in Q2 and high coffee prices limiting customer acquisition
items.quote: our volume growth was approximately 14% for the full year

items.statement: Coffee consumption remains intact globally, no reduction in in-home consumption despite high prices
items.quote: there has been no reduction in the consumption for coffee

items.statement: EBITDA per kg maintained despite high coffee prices; gross margin percentage decline attributed to higher coffee prices not per kg margin drop
items.quote: our per kg EBITDA hasn't come down much there, maybe INR2, INR3 or INR5 here or there

items.statement: Cost-plus pricing model maintains per kg margins regardless of green coffee price direction
items.quote: we work on a pass-on model, which is a cost-plus model that whatever the price is, we keep a certain amount of per kilo margin

items.statement: Vietnam freeze-dried capacity to start commercial operations by September-October 2024, completing expansion to ~77,000 MT capacity
items.quote: the Vietnam freeze dried capacity will be up and running by the month of September and October, and that will complete our current expansion process

items.statement: India capacity utilization near 100% (excluding new SMB plant started mid-March); Vietnam utilization at 65-70% including new capacity
items.quote: Vietnam the total, meaning, the new capacity included, we are almost at around 65% to 70%

items.statement: Order visibility shortened from 9-12 months to 4-5 months due to high coffee prices making clients reluctant for long-term contracts
items.quote: the visibilities have shortened to maybe 4 to 5 months

items.statement: Green coffee prices at unprecedented highs ($4+), but Brazilian pre-harvest prices softened $600-800/MT indicating post-harvest correction
items.quote: Brazilian coffee prices have already softened by almost $600 to $800 per metric ton

items.statement: Working capital debt likely to increase further due to volume growth and coffee prices; INR200 cr more term loans to be drawn for F&B and FD projects
items.quote: another INR200 crores on account of term loan is likely to increase somewhere

items.statement: 70-75% of sales are FOB, limiting freight cost exposure; shifting from CNF to FOB to reduce logistics cost impact
items.quote: approximately 70% to 75% of our sales are FOB sales

items.statement: Total debt ~INR1,600 cr (INR600 cr long-term, INR1,000 cr working capital); optimizing interest costs by leveraging lower-cost borrowing in Vietnam and Swiss entities
items.quote: Out of the INR1,600 crores debt approximately INR600 crores is long-term debt and INR1,000 crores is working capital

items.statement: Not concerned about debt levels as working capital debt is backed by confirmed orders
items.quote: our working capital debt is against confirmed orders

items.statement: Higher coffee prices driving down-trading: spray-dried demand up, freeze-dried demand down; small pack volumes increasing in both domestic and exports
items.quote: the demand for spray dried started to increase because there was a certain bit of down-trading that happens at the consumer level

items.statement: Domestic branded sales INR210 cr out of INR320 cr total domestic sales; market share ~4-4.5% in South India, firmly #3 player nationally
items.quote: out of INR320 crores India sales, the brand sales is now at INR210 crores

items.statement: Modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce contribute 35% of domestic branded business, growing high double-digits
items.quote: modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce, all of them would contribute to 35% of our business

items.statement: US business growing at decent pace through associates; China/Taiwan market entry in progress with active client discussions
items.quote: We are acquiring new clients through our associates there. So that is there

items.statement: Performance significantly better than most peers in high coffee price environment due to economies of scale and global network
items.quote: our performance has been significantly, significantly better than most of them

items.statement: Receiving acquisition proposals regularly due to industry stress on smaller players; evaluating on merit but capacity expanded for FY27-28
items.quote: every other day we get a proposal from somewhere across the globe

items.statement: Insurance claim process ongoing, no money received yet
items.quote: process is still going on. So we haven't got the money

items.statement: EBITDA per kg: domestic ~INR85, Vietnam ~INR110-115; freeze-dried typically INR120-130, spray-dried INR90-100 at lower coffee prices
items.quote: Vietnam, it was a little lower at INR110 or INR115

items.statement: Percol acquisition (UK) completed July 2023; retailer contracts renegotiated, relaunch with new packaging/formulation this month, production moved in-house
items.quote: The acquisition of Percol finished in the month of July '23. Thereafter contracts with all the retailers were negotiated and renegotiated

items.statement: Domestic distribution at 110,000 general trade outlets (85,000 in South) plus 700-800 modern retail stores; online presence on all platforms
items.quote: only in general trade, which is the kirana stores, we are now at CCL Products ( 1,10,000 outlets total

items.statement: Vending machine business part of branded sales (~INR20-25 cr); focusing on profitable growth with stronger contract model
items.quote: out of INR210 crores, probably INR20 crores, INR25 crores will be vending business

items.statement: FY25 expected to be a year of normalized revenue and margin as the company is in an investing phase; momentum expected to return in subsequent years based on project visibility
items.quote: We expect that FY25 will be a year of normalized revenue and margin as we will be in the investing phase. We are cautiously optimistic that our businesses will once again be in momentum in the subsequent years based on the current visibility of our project and portfolio products.

items.statement: Medium-term growth CAGR target of 20% over a 4-5 year period; growth not expected to be linear year-on-year
items.quote: I think what we have always indicated is that over a 4 -5-year period, we will be able to target a 20% kind of growth. And I think that's something that we are comfortable. And our plans are all kind of built around that.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin at 30%, up from 23% in FY23 and 15% in FY22; FY25 margins expected to normalize from FY24 peak due to investments and input cost increases
items.quote: During the same two years, our EBITDA margins have also grown. They were actually 15% in FY22they grew to 23% in FY23 and then further this year they've grown to 30%.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 gross margin at 58.8% vs 54.1% in Q4 FY23 and 59.8% in Q3 FY24
items.quote: Our gross margin was 58.8% of Q4FY24 as compared to 54.1% in Q4 FY23 and 59.8% in Q3 FY24.

items.statement: Short-term margin normalization expected in FY25 due to investments and input cost increases; business mix expected to remain steady and gradually improve
items.quote: In the short run, however, we expect moderation in revenue growth as well as normalization to some extent on margins due to the investments that we're making in the business and also input cost increases. We expect the business mix to remain steady and gradually improve.

items.statement: CMS business contributed close to 50% of revenues in FY24, growing 30% on top of 30% growth in FY23; robust growth driven by projects near launch and scaling commercial products
items.quote: Number one, we have seen the CMS business this year contribute close to 50% of our revenues, which already had grown 30% last year. Our CMS business saw this robust growth in FY24 as some projects, as we mentioned before, are near launch while key commercial products continue to scale.

items.statement: Added projects across preclinical, Phase I and Phase II; seeing steady inflow of new opportunities and RFPs in improving biotech environment; expect increase in total projects over next 12 months
items.quote: Number two, we have added a number of projects across preclinical phase one and phase two. In light of the improving biotech environment in the US, we see the new business environment continuing to look favorable.

items.statement: FY24 capex of Rs. 143.7 crores; FY25 baseline capex guidance of INR 100+ crores with opportunistic additional spending for growth projects; internal benchmark of not allocating more than 60% of operating cash to capex
items.quote: So our capex guidance continues to be the same as we have guided earlier. The baseline would be always INR100-plus crores but we will be opportunistic. I f we find something, which meets our growth plans. We would appropriately come back to

items.statement: Land purchased adjacent to Unit 1 for future expansion; 5-year plan in place for capacity addition and integration
items.quote: So Ankeet the land was primarily procured to make way for the future expansion for the product that's been made in those facilities. So we have a 5-year plan in place and looking at the needs of the plan, we are adding to the capacity and integrating it in line with the protections and that's pretty much the objective.

items.statement: New plants being built are multi-product facilities identified with specific products but not dedicated; designed for flexibility across molecules
items.quote: I think the plants that are being designed or bui lt are always identified with one, two, or three products. But by design, they're always made to be multi-product facilities.

items.statement: Steady increase in flow of new opportunities and RFPs; biotech funding environment improving; new project inflows expected to add significantly to business 2-3 years down the line
items.quote: At the moment, as it stands, we're seeing a steady increase in flow of new opportunities, new RFPs are coming our way. So , in the next 12 months, there should be an increase in the total number of projects.

items.statement: Specialty GDS contribution steadily increasing vs Prime GDS; Prime products like mirtazapine grew significantly in FY24; mix expected to remain steady and gradually improve
items.quote: Yes, I think there has been a steady increase in the contribution of specialty vis-a-vis Prime. And I think that's something that we expect to happen.

items.statement: Input costs have stabilized lately; no significant pricing pressure in Prime GDS; short-to-medium term corrections due to nitrosamine regulations and customer handling choices
items.quote: We have lately witnessed stability in terms of input costs. We also continue to be mindful of managing our operational costs, resulting in financial revenue.

items.statement: Net debt position negative Rs. 32.6 crores (net cash); reduced debt by Rs. 39.4 crores in FY24 using cash surplus; peak cash flow generation of Rs. 116.4 crores in FY24
items.quote: Consequently, our net debt position stands at negative Rs. 32.6 crores. We also reduced our working capital cycle to 122 days at the end of March'24 as compared to 141 days at the end o f March’23

items.statement: FDA inspections completed at Unit 3 and Unit 1 in past year; regulatory track record reiterated
items.quote: The past year has seen a reiteration of our regulatory track record as both unit three and unit one was inspected by the FDA.

items.statement: Biosecure Act not yet passed; operationalization and impact uncertain; seeing increased RFI/RFP activity from innovators seeking alternative supply chains but no surge in actual business yet
items.quote: One, there is this overall bill about the Biosecure Act, which hasn't been passed yet. The second thing is about how that will actually get operationalized and the impact of that we will see for India and other countries.

items.statement: GDS pipeline: Difelikefalin DMF filing expected later in CY24; GLP-1 asset DMF filing expected in CY26; generic GLP-1 opportunity seen as huge with global demand potential
items.quote: The first one which we expect to file DMF later this year is Difelikefalin which is something that is still on track and that is something that we are excited about. There's another one which is a GLP1 which we are working on for which the DMF will be filed perhaps maybe in 2026.

items.statement: European CDMOs and API makers are credible competitors with active capacity creation; China less of a competitive threat; some innovators prefer Europe for geodiversity despite cost advantage of India
items.quote: We actually see less competition for us in China. And in that sense, the European CDMOs, European API makers are always a credible threat. And there is also capacity creation in these regions.

items.statement: CMS commercialized projects at 18 (8+10); key revenue-contributing molecules around 4-5; no biologics - all small molecules, peptides or peptide fragments; customer switching difficult post-commercialization
items.quote: None of them. We are essentially a synthetic organic chemistry company, so we do not make any biologics. They're all small molecules or peptides or peptides related fragments.

items.statement: Individual product performance, forex fluctuations, raw material cost volatility and other business variables can affect outlook; IP landscape unpredictability for GLP-1 generics; innovators constantly protecting their interests
items.quote: As always, we maintain that variables such as individual product performance, forex fluctuations, raw material cost volatility and other business variables can have a bearing on our outlook.

items.statement: Operating expenses up ~18% in FY24 due to manpower costs, professional fees and manufacturing expenses; increase was as per plan
items.quote: Our operating expenses has gone up by around 18% because the rest of it is variable. And that is predominantly because of manpower costs and other expenses, which is on account of professional fees and some amount because of manufacturing expenses.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; using internal cash generation for capex and debt reduction; net cash position achieved
items.quote: We generated a peak cash flow for FY24 of Rs. 116.4 crores. We utilized part of this cash surplus to reduce our debt by Rs. 39.4 crores.

items.statement: Dividend policy benchmarked against similar growth companies; board reviews annually based on profitability and guidelines; practice to continue
items.quote: Today, we use those guidelines and we debate in the board meeting every year based on the profitability and in line with that dividend policy to declare that dividend for a specific year. And this practice will continue.

items.statement: Malabar Retreat pre-sales at Rs 67 crore from 27-30 apartments booked so far
items.quote: And thus we saw very good interest with bookings as of now of up to about 27 to 30 apartments totaling to around Rs. 67 crores and more in revenues and pre-sales.

items.statement: Malabar Exotica 60% revenue recognized, balance 40% to be booked in Q1 FY25
items.quote: 60% is already booked and about 40% is what is yet to be booked, which will be booked, mostly this entire 40% will be booked in current financial quarter of FY ‘25.

items.statement: One Thaltej commercial project 1.8 msf, Rs 2,100 crore revenue, start H2 FY25, finish H2 FY28
items.quote: Additionally, a new project, One Thaltej, which is a commercial project is being added to the repertoire in the current year. It is an additional 1.8 million square feet with about Rs. 2,100 crores in revenue. It is expected to start in H2 FY ’25, the second-half of this year, and finished by the second-half of FY ’28, that's just about three years.

items.statement: Million Minds two residential phases 1.8 msf total, launches Q3 and Q4 FY25
items.quote: But in this year FY ‘25, we shall be launching both the phases of residential in Million Minds , one phase being launched in third quarter of this FY ’25, and the s econd phase in the fourth quarter. Together, the development of this is about 1.8 million square feet.

items.statement: Smile City township deferred to H1 FY26 for better planning amid vicinity developments
items.quote: Hence we are now thinking that the project will start in H1 of FY ‘26. With all these ongoing and the upcoming projects, the company is set to develop over 5.5 million square feet of area which are under various stages of development, making this the highest development at any point in time in the company's history.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 70%, Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 55%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the full year was about 70% and for the quarter was about 55%.

items.statement: Net debt zero with Rs 230 crore cash surplus as of March 31, 2024
items.quote: Our cash flows have been very strong and even after spending for CapEx on the SE Z, as you know we have not raised any money, we are net debt zero. And given various advances for land purchases from our own sources, we still have a cash surplus of Rs. 230 crores as at March 31, 2024, far more than what we need for our CapEx expenditure this year.

items.statement: Board recommends dividend of Rs 11 per share (110%), 20% payout, Rs 92 crore outflow
items.quote: Looking to the robust performance and the healthy cash flows, the Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of Rs. 11 per share, that is 110%, the previous best ever was 22%, and now it is 110%. This is a 20% payout in line with our dividend policy, having about Rs. 92 crores outflow.

items.statement: Ahmedabad residential demand rose 21.5% in Q1 calendar 2024 with 1.5% price increase
items.quote: houses demand rose by about 21.5% in the first quarter of this calendar, accompanied by about 1.5% increase in the average property rates

items.statement: Total 5.5 msf under development across projects, highest in company history
items.quote: With all these ongoing and the upcoming projects, the company is set to develop over 5.5 million square feet of area which are under various stages of development, making this the highest development at any point in time in the company's history.

items.statement: Targets Rs 10,000 crore expected FCF capitalized value including One Thaltej outright sale value
items.quote: Yes, sir. See, except for the SEZ commercial which is there, Million Minds, that's the only place where we are looking at a release model. Rest of the place is all on a sale, the outright sale basis. So only that has been capitalized to come to this value, but rest of them are all on actual sales revenue really. And actually more importantly, is the cash flows realized.

items.statement: Current inventory Rs 421 crore to be sold over 2-3 years
items.quote: See, our current inventory somewhere around Rs. 421 crores, which would be sold over two, three years.

items.statement: Smile City township to be self-funded from internal accruals and booking cash flows
items.quote: That will be self funded, and also from internal accruals. It is something like what we have the residential projects wherein the bookings happen and the cash keeps coming in from the booking site itself, and partly coming from the internal accruals. So it will be actually be resulting into a cash surplus rather than requiring any cash upfront in that.

items.statement: SEZ commercial project Million Minds engaging Tishman for tenant acquisition, targeting Q2-Q3 FY25 for leasing discussions
items.quote: And Tishman, as I said, have been also given the responsibility of trying to find the right tenants . And we are confident . And as we speak , actually we a lot of developments have happened in terms of speaking to the right likely tenants by Tishman itself. And I think in this yea r, as we go closer towards completion of that, maybe in the second or third quarter, as I said, it is going to be com

items.statement: Demand growth 21.5% absorbs new supply from prominent developers in Ahmedabad
items.quote: First quarter of this calendar year itself, the demand has increased by 21.5%. And therefore all the development which is happening, whether by us or with the other prominent developers, or are addressing the demand increase in this segment.

items.statement: No exchange notification policy for project launches; considers it day-to-day business
items.quote: We believe that launching a new project or selling some units in project or booking certain units is day-to-day business for us. And hence such activity does not require any notification to be sent to investors or shareholders at large.

items.statement: FY25 capex planned at INR60 crores for existing fastener and MCU businesses, excluding magnetics JV
items.quote: So overall, we'll be investing around to the tune of about INR60 crores next year. And that's without the -- any investment in the magnetics business. This is only for existing businesses. That's fasteners and motor control units.

items.statement: MCU capacity at 600,000 units annually with 2,000+ units daily production; finishing touches on expansion remain
items.quote: So as of today, we are consistently producing more than 2,000 units a day. This is not -- but that takes us to about 600,000-unit capacity for the full year. And we actually hope to be able to debottleneck and improve process flows further to be able to optimize output.

items.statement: SGEM targets 10-12% steady-state EBITDA margin; current adjusted EBITDA margin 12.4% consolidated, 14.8% standalone
items.quote: We will definitely see an improvement in margins in the coming year, and we continue to make progress towards our stated goal of 10% to 12% EBITDA margins in this business in a steady state.

items.statement: EV business now 35% of consolidated revenue vs 23% in FY23; SGEM revenue grew 86% to INR323 crores
items.quote: SGEM now accounts for 35% of our consolidated revenue up from 23% in FY '23. Furthermore, we are excited to announce that Sterling Tools has entered into an MOU with South Korea's Yongin Electronics to establish and EV components facility in India.

items.statement: Magnetics JV differentiates via Yongin's 35-year pedigree, design expertise, process control; global competitors are Japanese/German Tier 1s not localized in India
items.quote: The competitors for them are from Japanese Tier 1 who are fairly large, but who don't really manufacture in India, they only manufacturer in Japan or in the United States. So globally, competitors for them are Japanese Tier 1 companies or electronic companies or German Swiss electronics and electrical companies.

items.statement: Fastener margins pressured by steel price pass-through without conversion price increases; raw material costs stabilized in FY24
items.quote: The margins have substantially shown a decrease mathematically on account of steel price increase, which we have got from our customers, but we have not been able to get any price increase on account of value addition or conversions we do on top of the raw materials.

items.statement: Magnetics raw materials like core components not available in India; will depend on overseas suppliers for foreseeable future
items.quote: There are certain components in these magnetics which are not available in India, for which we will have to depend from overseas suppliers to get to the certain products.

items.statement: ESOP expense INR2 crores in FY24 (2 months); FY25 impact INR10-11 crores; total 4-year cost INR22-23 crores front-loaded 60-65% in first 2 years
items.quote: So the INR2 crores is the impact of FY '24 is only for the last 2 months because we only -- this is 2 months impact, and the next impact will be the biggest one in the entire platform. So -- and just around -- it should be around INR10 crores to INR11 crores.

items.statement: Chairman and MD roles segregated; next generation elevated to expanded roles for EV and green energy focus
items.quote: We have announced segregation of Chairman and Managing Director roles in order to provide greater focus for two electric vehicles and other green city verticals. In line with our succession strategy, we have also initiated role transitions elevating members of the next generation to assume expanded roles and responsibilities within the company.

items.statement: LCV EV market ramp delayed despite nominations from all major players; regulatory challenges affecting EV industry growth
items.quote: The LCV segment where we have been nominated by nearly all of the major players is one that we keep waiting for the take off and for various reasons, it hasn't happened. The reasons aren't necessarily in the control -- in our control or that our customers.

items.statement: EV industry facing regulatory policy changes creating challenges; April industry numbers muted but expecting 30% industry growth in FY25
items.quote: Despite the challenges that we have and the changes in government policy and regulations have thrown up a lot of challenges for this industry. But regardless of that, we still hope to see about 30% market, 30% growth in this industry in the coming year.

items.statement: Board approved investments to make Sterling E-Mobility and Sterling Tech Mobility wholly owned subsidiaries
items.quote: Against this backdrop the Board has approved investments in two companies namely Sterling E-Mobility Private Limited and Sterling Tech Mobility Limited transforming them into wholly owned subsidiaries of Sterling Tools Limited.

items.statement: Gradual uptick in demand with rural demand converging with urban; most portfolio seeing positive volume momentum
items.quote: During the quarter gone by for the FMCG sector, we witnessed a gradual uptick in demand and growth in rural demand which started converging with that of urban demand.

items.statement: Expect demand to pick up on good monsoon and improving macro-economic factors
items.quote: The company further expects demand to pick up in the hope of good monsoon and improvement in macro-economic factors.

items.statement: Consolidated net sales grew 9.6% YoY with 5.5% volume growth
items.quote: As a result, the company registered consolidated net sales growth of 9.6% on year-on-year basis of which 5.5% is due to volume.

items.statement: Personal care segment registered strong double-digit growth for the quarter
items.quote: The personal care segment continues to register strong double-digit growth for the quarter with both Everyuth and Nycil portfolio witnessing a good demand traction.

items.statement: Food and nutrition segment reported mid-single-digit value growth YoY
items.quote: The food and nutrition segment also turned positive and reported a mid-single-digit value growth for the quarter on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Cross-margin expansion of 377 bps YoY in Q4 from calibrated price increases and efficient hedging
items.quote: We continue to witness cross-margin expansion with the improvement of 377 basis points on a year-on-year basis for the quarter 4 of the financial year contributed by calibrated price increase taken earlier and efficient hedging strategy for key commodities.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 12.2% YoY to Rs 1,622 million in Q4
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 12.2% year-on-year to Rs. 1,622 million.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA down 8.6% YoY to Rs 3,082 million; EBITDA margin 13.2%
items.quote: Our EBITDA was down by 8.6% year-on-year to Rs. 3,082 million. EBITDA margin as percentage of total income from operations stood at 13.2%.

items.statement: Target 17-18% EBITDA margin in next 2 years
items.quote: Within that, I think we hold our wish list to be a much higher 17%, 18% EBITDA in the next 2 years.

items.statement: Expect double-digit revenue growth in FY25
items.quote: Yes, I agree. We should see a double digit.

items.statement: Committed to consistent double-digit growth over next few years
items.quote: We do believe that we have the right capability inputs as a company to build on a double-digit growth path. We have part of the macro environment we operate and that's why there was some challenges in the past but we think with a stable environment we are on the path to deliver a consistent double-digit growth over the next few years.

items.statement: Consolidated capex for FY24 was Rs 489 million
items.quote: Our consolidated capex for the year was Rs. 489 million.

items.statement: Net debt stood at Rs 77 million; company is practically debt-free with net cash of Rs 8 lakhs
items.quote: Net debt stood at Rs. 77 million.

items.statement: No cash tax outflow in FY25; partial tax outflow in FY26 due to Sikkim facility benefit; tax outflow in FY27
items.quote: So for this financial year ending 2025, we won't be paying any tax. And of course, there will be a deferred tax liability would be there, but there won't be any cash outflow on the tax front. In the year 2026-27, there would be partial tax outflow because we will have benefit of Sikkim facility as well, ATI. So for financial year 2027, we will have some tax outflow.

items.statement: Launched Glucon-D Activors, Electrolyte Energy Drink, I'mlite sweetener, and sugar-free delight range for international business
items.quote: The company's research and development capabilities continue to be on the forefront helping the company to launch new products and extensions namely Glucon-D Activors, Electrolyte Energy Drink, a ready-to-drink format for on-the-go consumption in a couple of states. The company also extended its Sweetener portfolio with the launch of I'mlite, a unique formulation of sugar blended with stevia to of

items.statement: Organized trade share ~20%, expected to reach 21-22% in 1-2 years; direct coverage 6.5 lakh outlets, target to expand portfolio within these outlets
items.quote: So maybe whether it's quick commerce or whatever be the kind of initiatives they may be doing and expansion of stores by some of the offline organized retail, the share of organized trade will continue to go up. It's about a 20%. We expect it to continue to 21%-22% over next one year or two years.

items.statement: Products available at ~3 million outlets; target to reach 3.5 million outlets in 2 years
items.quote: From a traditional trade point of view, our products are available close to about 3 million outlets. Our journey or our plan would be to how do I build it to be available at 3.5 million outlets.

items.statement: Sugar-free green growing at high double-digits; I'mlite launched to drive sweetener portfolio growth; no significant competition impact
items.quote: Sugar-free green continues to grow at high double digit led by volume offtake growth.

items.statement: Market share gains in personal care not fully reflected in Nielsen data due to lag; local competition increasing
items.quote: So I think there is some bit of catch up for Nielsen specifically in the personal care space where we've seen they've been at a category level showing only a 2% to 3% growth for last year as well as continuing. So I think there is a lag and I hope Nielsen shares will catch up with our internal growth because that's been sustained.

items.statement: Everyuth scrub market share 45.6% (+369 bps YoY); peel-off share 80.2% (+174 bps); facial cleansing share 6.5%
items.quote: Everyuth scrub has maintained its leadership position with market share of 45.6% in the facial scrub category which is an increase of 369 basis points over the same period last year.

items.statement: Nycil prickly heat powder market share 35%; highest household penetration 8.5% at MAT Feb 24
items.quote: Nycil has maintained its number one position with a market share of 35% in the prickly heat powder category. Nycil has recorded its highest household penetration at 8.5% at MAT February '24 level with its volume growth ahead of the category.

items.statement: Glucon-D glucose powder market share 59.5% at MAT; brand penetration up 62 bps YoY
items.quote: Glucon-D continues to maintain its leadership position in its glucose powder category with a value market share of 59.5% at MAT level.

items.statement: Complan market share 4.3% at MAT; category grew 6.4%; brand penetration up 26 bps YoY to 2.9%
items.quote: Complan market share stood at 4.3% at MAT level.

items.statement: Sugar substitutes category grew 5.5% at MAT; Sugar-free market share 95.9%
items.quote: Sugar substitutes category has grown by 5.5% at MAT March level. The sugar-free brand continues to dominate sugar-free substitutes with a market share of 95.9%.

items.statement: International business 3.5-4% of revenue; targeting 7-8% share; double-digit growth in GCC and Indian subcontinent; Nigeria under macro pressure
items.quote: So at international business level for the full year, we are about 3.5%-4% range. This been range bound because if I were to break it down into three geographies or three focus markets, namely we've talked about it, Africa led by Nigeria, India sub-continent which is Bangladesh, Nepal, and there is GCC in the Middle East. We've seen good double-digit growth in both GCC as well as India subcontinen

items.statement: Expect normal inflation of 3-5% going forward vs extreme inflation of past 2 years
items.quote: So going forward we expect the inflation to be normal which is a manageable 4%, 5% or 3%, whatever that we've seen over the last 8 to 10 years rather than the extreme inflation that we saw over the last 2 years.

items.statement: Temporary working capital borrowing of Rs 50 crore in March quarter repaid
items.quote: That was temporary working capital inflow that has been repaid now.

items.statement: Guidance for FY25: low double-digit revenue growth driven by volume from new Max plant and existing capacity; EBITDA margin improvement of 1-1.5% subject to stable gas prices; brand spend to increase to ~3% of revenue
items.quote: The guidance for next year is that we are looking at a low double-digit growth largely fueled by volume on the back of the new Max plant, which has started, and all the other plants also which are running at capacity.

items.statement: GVT share guidance: expects GVT mix to reach ~38% in FY25 and 40% going forward from 34% in FY24
items.quote: We do believe that next year this will be notching up closer to 38% and going forward to 40 %.

items.statement: Domestic tile industry expected to grow 5-6% in FY25; company aims to grow at double that rate; exports recovering from 1,200-1,300 cr/month to ~1,700 cr/month
items.quote: I think the industry domestically is slated to grow at about 4% to 5%, maybe 6% , and to that extent, we would grow almost at double that rate.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 9.8% from 7.7%; Q4 FY24 at 10.9%; targets further 1-1.5% improvement in FY25 subject to stable gas prices
items.quote: EBITDA on a consol level is up from 9% to 10.9% and the entire year from 7.7% to 9.8%.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin trajectory around 11% (+/-1-2%); Q4 FY24 margin not sustainable in Q1-Q2 due to election impact
items.quote: we have been maintaining our guidance that our normalized EBITDA margin is something which should be around 11% or so plus/minus 1%, 2% and we are reaching towards that normalized trajectory of EBITDA.

items.statement: FY25 capex planned at Rs 50-60 crore, routine only; no major expansion capex
items.quote: So, we are not planning much any major CAPEX in the next financial year. It will all be routine CAPEX, routine in nature, so maybe around 50 to 60 crores are what we are targeting for next year.

items.statement: Total installed capacity ~78-79 mn sq mtrs; FY24 sales ~68 mn sq mtrs; capacity utilization 86% for FY24 (down 1.5% YoY), Q4 at 89%; Max plant currently at 40-50% utilization, targeting >80% by March 2025
items.quote: We have a total capacity of approximately 78 to 79 mn.sq.mtrs. of installed capacity. This year we sold approximately 68 mn.sq.mtrs.

items.statement: GVT capacity 25 mn sq mtrs (21 own + 4 outsourced) out of total 78 mn; adequate for next 18 months
items.quote: Out of the 78 million, we have a capacity of 25 million GVT, 21 of that is our own capacity, four is outsourced.

items.statement: FY24 product mix: Ceramic 37%, PVT 29%, GVT 34%; Q4 FY24: Ceramic 35%, PVT 29%, GVT 36%; GVT share up 2% YoY in FY24, 4% in Q4
items.quote: If you look at Q4 FY'24, ceramic was 35%, PVT was 29% and GVT was 36%.

items.statement: Average gas price fell from Rs 59/scm in FY23 to Rs 45/scm in FY24; current prices: North Rs 45, Morbi Rs 47, South Rs 50/scm; gas ~30% of total production cost
items.value: FY24 avg Rs 45/scm vs FY23 Rs 59/scm
items.quote: Just to point out in FY'23, the average gas price across per year was Rs.59 standard cubic meter and in FY'24 it came down to Rs.45 standard cubic meter.

items.statement: ASP declined slightly due to sales incentives and discounting to promote sales; GVT pricing under pressure as everyone adds GVT capacity
items.quote: The other highlight is not a positive side is the ASP. Our ASP has gone down a little bit due to the added pressure and the sales incentive schemes which we've given to promote sales.

items.statement: Nepal project delayed to H2 FY25; Nepal market slowed from 25 to 13-14 mn sq mtrs; current inventory sufficient for Nepal demand
items.quote: Nepal Project is again due to issues over there or rain , this, that and the other, that is delayed a little bit, it will probably only be in place next year . And even from that point of view , Nepal market which is estimated to be a 25 mn.sq.mtrs market, last year, it slow ed down to approximately 13 to 14 mn.sq.mtrs.

items.statement: Dealer network: net addition of 110 dealers in FY24; targeting 100-150 net additions in FY25 with focus on reducing non-performing dealers
items.quote: So, a net addition of 110 dealers during this fiscal year. Abhishek Somany: And I think we would add anywhere between 100 to 150 dealers next year, but also we are going to try and see as to how the net addition goes up a little more where we have lesser number of non-performing dealers coming out

items.statement: Sales mix: 80% retail (dealer network), 20% institutional (government, private builders, corporates); expects institutional share to rise to 25% over next few years
items.quote: Our retail a lmost is 80% of our sales mix and 20% is coming through institutional, which comprises various segments including the government contracts, the private builders, the corporates, all these institutions put together is around 20% and 80% is coming through our retail network which we call dealer network

items.statement: Morbi export-oriented capacity dumped in domestic market after exports fell from ~1,800-1,900 to 1,200-1,300 cr/month in Q3; Morbi utilization at 65-70%; 6-7 new export-oriented plants expected in 3-4 months but offset by closures of non-vi
items.quote: lot of the plants which came up in Morbi were primarily for export market and export kind of crumbled in Q3, from an average of about 1 ,800 crores to 1,900 crores a month, it crumbled to about 1 ,300 crores, even in one month it was 1,200 crores.

items.statement: Working capital improvement normalized; payable days up, inventory down; debtor days may reduce slightly but current levels sustainable
items.quote: I think this is a normalized scenario. The only thing which may happen henceforth, there is a small reduction in debtor days, but otherwise it's a normal scenario.

items.statement: Standalone net debt positive for 2 years; consolidated long-term borrowing ~Rs 185 crore in SPVs amortizing ~Rs 40 crore/year over 3-4 years; no plan to become debt-free at consolidated level
items.quote: If SPV debt is outstanding in various multiple small SPV , SPV is for project financing. And we have been amortizing schedule for almost 40 and odd crore s every year and as of now our long-term borrowing is around Rs.185 crores.

items.statement: Capital allocation: favorable dividend payouts likely if cash flows permit and no expansion needed; share buyback uncertain
items.quote: And as far as capital allocation is concerned, we will see how and when the cash flows are , whether we need it for expansion, if not then we will obviously have a more favorable dividend payout or I am not too sure about the share buyback , if that happens or not at that level but definitely would be more favorable dividend payouts.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 expected to be very weak due to elections (April-May); labor unavailable, builders cautious; no significant growth expected in Q1-Q2; robust growth from H2 onwards
items.quote: Q1 is extremely sluggish specifically because of the election. You must appreciate that all the labor goes back for voting , plus, our business has certain other elements which restrict the purchase if what I am saying in these two months, the builders are extremely cautious.

items.statement: Sanitaryware capacity utilization ~70%; faucets at 100% utilization; bathware revenue grew 9% YoY in FY24 (Q4: Rs 80 cr vs Rs 74 cr); targeting double-digit growth in FY25
items.quote: Capacity utilization in the sanitary ware segment is at about 70% and the faucet segment is run at 100% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Exports recovered to ~Rs 1,700 cr/month from lows of Rs 1,200-1,300 cr/month in Q3; FY24 exports ~Rs 19,000 cr industry; expects export growth of Rs 2,000-3,000 cr on current base
items.quote: No, I don't have exact scenario but what I do here is it is up from the 1 ,300 crore s to approximately 1,700 crores right now.

items.statement: Morbi pricing has bottomed out; further price cuts would mean product quality compromise visible to dealers and consumers
items.quote: the pricing in Morbi has more than bottomed out. Anything going forward now is getting compromised on the product and the dealer and the consumer is clearly being able to visualize the compromised product which they're getting at a cheaper price.

items.statement: Targets INR300bn AUM by FY27
items.quote: We are well placed to drive growth and achieve the targeted INR300 billion AUM by FY27, as we stated earlier.

items.statement: AUM crossed INR150bn to INR156.5bn in FY24, second consecutive year of 50% growth
items.quote: During FY24, we crossed various business milestones with AUM crossing INR150 billion to touch INR156.5 billion. This was a second consecutive year of 50% AUM growth.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 3.1x YoY to INR34.9bn including co-lending, 750 exclusive branches
items.quote: As guided, our gold loan AUM increased to 3.1x YoY to cross INR30 billion AUM target. The gold loan AUM including co-lending AUM stood at INR34.9 billion in March '24.

items.statement: MSME AUM grew 15% YoY to INR50.2bn
items.quote: Talking about one of our key growth drivers, MSME, our AUM has grown to INR50.2bn, which is growth of about 15%YoY.

items.statement: Housing finance book grew 52.8% YoY to INR40.7bn, expects 30%+ growth for next 4-5 years
items.quote: If we talk about housing finance, our book has grown 52.8% YoY, from INR26.7bn to INR40.7bn. Home loans will continue to grow in coming years in the range of about 30%+ growth rate.

items.statement: Spreads stable at 6.4% for second consecutive quarter; expects spread to improve to 6.8-6.9% as gold loan share rises
items.quote: Our spreads were stable at 6.4% for a second consecutive quarter. The inc rease in marginal cost of funds was more than offset by an improvement in yield

items.statement: Expects spread improvement to 6.8-6.9% range as gold loan proportion increases
items.quote: As I said, since our go ld loan proportion is increasing in the overall AUM, our spread will improve from 6.4% to -- it should improve to -- in the range of about 6.8%, 6.9

items.statement: Cost of funds up ~50bps QoQ in FY24; partly passed on via floating rate loans and higher gold loan pricing
items.quote: If you talk about the cost of funds, cost of funds have gone up about 50 bps between Q1 and Q4. Out of that, we were able to pass on partly because some of the loans are semi-fixed in nature and some of the loans are on a floating rate.

items.statement: Expects cost of funds to stabilize; potential reduction if rating upgrades occur in 6 months
items.quote: I think cost of fund should stabilize at this level. I don't see any further hike going forward. However, we expect if there is a strong performance, in six months or so, we should see some ratin g upgrades

items.statement: Spent INR112cr on technology and data science in FY24; expects cost-income ratio improvement in H2 FY25 as initiatives complete
items.quote: If you talk about the last year, we have spent about INR112 crores on technology and data science. And this is a significant investment and that is one of the reasons that our cost income ratio is quite elevated.

items.statement: Gold loan branches at 750; targets AUM per branch of INR85mn next year vs INR50mn currently
items.quote: I believe that this year, we have closed AUM of INR50mn per branch. And next year, we are targeting to close the AUM at about INR85mn per branch.

items.statement: Plans to add 20-30 housing finance branches annually; new branches in UP and Uttarakhand under discussion
items.quote: On an average, we will keep adding 20 to 30 branches every year.

items.statement: Gold loan share 37% of AUM and ~50% of disbursals in Q4 FY24; co-lending AUM rose to 11.7% of total AUM
items.quote: The share of gold loan AUM was 37% and the share in disbursal was approximately 50% in Q4 as well as FY24, respectively.

items.statement: Co-lending AUM increased to 11.7% of AUM from 8.9% in Q3 FY24 and 5.3% in Q4 FY23
items.quote: Our co-lending AUM continued to rise during Q4 FY24 increasing to 11.7% of AUM compared to 8.9% in Q3 FY24 and 5.3% in Q4 FY23.

items.statement: GNPA declined 18bps QoQ to 1.92%; PCR 43.2%; Net NPA down 28bps QoQ to 1.1%
items.quote: Our GNPA ratio declined 18 bps QoQ to 1.92%. The PCR on GNPA stood at 43.2%, and the net NPA ratio declined by 28bps QoQ to 1.1%.

items.statement: RBI circular on cash disbursement >INR20k clarified; stopped cash disbursements, volumes unaffected; <INR20k loans <10% of gold ATS
items.quote: I think this circular on cash disbursement in excess of Rs20,000 has been clarified by RBI that NBFCs should not have done it. So, I think all NBFC s will not be doing it

items.statement: Gold loan valuation controls: dual valuer approval, 100% internal audit coverage, 1,600 staff certified, 35 AI/ML triggers, cross-audit rotation
items.quote: Each gold (jewellery) is valued by 2 of the valuers. So there's a maker-checker control in the system built-in. And both of them have to put their approval authority into the system through their user ID.

items.statement: Board approved 15% dividend per share on INR1 face value for FY24; equity base increased 4x post split and 1:1 bonus
items.quote: The Board of Directors approved dividend at the rate of 15% per share on the face value of INR1 for FY24.

items.statement: Appointed L.V. Prabhakar (former Canara Bank MD & CEO) as Independent Chairman effective 29 April 2024
items.quote: CGCL's Board in the meeting dated 29th April 2024, has appointed Shri L. V. Prabhakar, Independent Director as Chairman of the Board of Directors.

items.statement: Pre-provisioning operating profit declined 16% QoQ to INR1,096mn but up 22% YoY; full year up 37% YoY
items.quote: A result of higher quarterly opex, the pre-provisioning operating profit declined 16%QoQ to INR1,096mn, but was up 22% YoY.

items.statement: Net profit INR826mn, up 27% YoY and 26% QoQ; ROA 2.3%, ROE 8.7% in Q4 FY24
