items.quote: I think it is very unpredictable to comment on the prices. Right now, we already see that most of the generic products have bottomed out and few products, the increase is already seen due to unavailability of raw materials or increase in the prices of raw materials.

items.statement: Passing on raw material price changes to customers monthly; branded product prices increased where technical prices rose
items.quote: Wherever the technical prices have increased, we have also increased the prices of our branded products. We are passing on the increase as well as the decrease of raw material prices to the ultimate customers on a monthly basis.

items.statement: Dahej chemical synthesis plant commenced operations in FY24; new herbicide plant planned in H2 FY25
items.quote: Also in FY '24, Dhanuka has commenced operations at our Dahej chemical synthesis plant, and we are working to create breakthroughs in chemical synthesis with our new R&D laboratory with 30 chemists for research and chemical processes.

items.statement: New chemical R&D lab with 30 chemists established at Sanand to support Dahej manufacturing and contract manufacturing
items.quote: I'm also happy to share that we have established a new chemical R&D lab with 30 chemists to build speed in our product and process development capabilities at Sanand. This will help us in developing new products for manufacturing in Dahej and capture contract manufacturing opportunities.

items.statement: Generic:specialty revenue mix expected at 1/3:2/3 in FY25 vs 60:40 in FY24
items.quote: This year, generic and specialties, we are expecting around 1/3, 2/3.

items.statement: Launched 2 new 9(3) products in first 45 days of FY25; expecting 1 more in Q1; total 8 planned over 2 years, all in-licensed
items.quote: So the 9(3) products are the registration by Dhanuka. And we have already launched 2 products in the first 45 days and expecting to launch 1 more 9(3) plus in this quarter itself.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing discussions ongoing with Japanese and other international companies; positive interest but nothing matured yet
items.quote: Yes. There are -- discussions are going on. We will come back to you when something matures.

items.statement: Channel inventories at higher levels in March; slow uptake in current quarter; expecting faster movement from June with monsoon onset
items.quote: The channel inventory for the industry in the month of March has again gone up to some extent. However, in the current quarter, we see a little slow uptake. And I think once the rains arrive from the month of June onwards, we should see faster movement.

items.statement: Dahej plant revenue INR7.5 crores in FY24; full-year operations in FY25
items.quote: It's around INR7.5 crores.

items.statement: Interim dividend 400% (INR8/share) paid in FY24; final dividend 300% (INR6/share) recommended for AGM on 21 Aug 2024
items.quote: The company has already rewarded its members by paying an interim dividend at a rate of 400%. That is INR8 per equity share, having face value of INR? per share, which has absorbed INR36.47 crores. The Board of Directors has further recommended 300% final dividend that is INR6 per equity share.

items.statement: Marketing spend at 6-7% of revenue; increasing ~1% in FY25; employee cost ~20% of revenue with ~15% increase expected
items.quote: You see our marketing spend is in the range of around 6% to 7%. And this year, it will be around 1% higher than the previous year.

items.statement: Industry volume growth low single digits in FY24; Dhanuka volume growth 9.07%
items.quote: For Dhanuka, volume growth was 9.07%. For the industry, it was low single digits.

items.statement: Global agrochemical demand muted; US/Brazil destocking continuing; China supply ample; current Indian price increases may be temporary
items.quote: Yes, Rohanji, you're absolutely correct. And the general understanding in the industry is globally, the demand remains muted. And in my interactions with the companies in China also there is no dearth of supply right now. I think the current trend that we are seeing in the price increase is due to the momentary factor as Dhanukaji said around low inventory of technical and intermediates with India

items.statement: Kimitec collaboration at LOI stage only; no significant developments or launches expected in FY25
items.quote: So that is Mr. Shivam not a joint venture. It actually is right now only a letter of intent. And the idea is for research, development, marketing and manufacturing of the product. And right now, it is under work and it will take some time for it to commercialize.

items.statement: Guided FY25 EBITDA margin pre-ESOP in low-to-mid teens range and aim for high teens over 3 years
items.quote: we do expect next year our EBITDA margins to be the low to mid-teen range in terms of what we will exit. And we hope that we're able to do better. But that's, of course, what is the band in which we would like to give the guidance right now.

items.statement: Target double-digit top-line growth over next 3 years on organic basis
items.quote: we would like to grow our top line in double digits for the next -- on a 3-year basis. That's what as far as our top line and our margin line is concerned.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin pre-ESOP at 11.4%, up 220 bps QoQ and 790 bps YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, our EBITDA margin pre-ESOP cost have expanded by 220 bps quarter-on-quarter to 11.4% and 790 bps year-on-year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 660 bps YoY to 46.1% in Q4 FY24 driven by mix, cost optimization and price increases
items.quote: I'm happy to share that our gross margin ha s improved by 660 basis points t hat is from 39.5% in quarter 4 financial year '23 to 46.1% in quarter 4 financial year '24

items.statement: Expect Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin level to be sustainable in FY25 with quarterly fluctuations
items.quote: We believe, based on the projects that we are undertaking and the structural changes we had done, the margin of Q4 should be sustainable next year as well.

items.statement: API order book strong with regulated market orders allowing selectivity in price-sensitive markets
items.quote: I'm optimistic, looking at our current order book and our stable regulated market orders coming in through also allow us to be selective while participating in growth opportunities in some of the more price-sensitive markets.

items.statement: API capacity utilization at 70-75%; capacity sufficient for at least another year with plans to reshape mix
items.quote: We are today at about 70% to 75% is what we use. And that -- we have capacity with us, as for our current portfolio, is something that we largely have at least for another year.

items.statement: Turkey pricing actions fully compensating 60% inflation; price increases executed in June and January
items.quote: we are able to take our pricing increases to completely compensate for any inflation. And therefore, that helps us keep the margin in place as well as the top line.

items.statement: Portfolio reshaping toward higher-margin regulated markets and companion animal APIs; discontinued less attractive segments
items.quote: We have driven business growth with -- on portfolio, which are high growth, higher margins, and at the same time, we have also discontinued less attractive segments that we participate in.

items.statement: Expanding API customer base with new customers and commercialization of older contracts; 70% API revenue from regulated markets
items.quote: we are a very strong regulated markets player nearly 70% of our business comes from markets which have -- which are from Europe or the US a nd in these kinds of customers tend to give a lot of premium and reference for suppliers who are quality suppliers

items.statement: Leveraging regulated market strength to compete in emerging markets on margin-accretive basis
items.quote: when you have a leverage because of your regulated market supplies, you can be competitive in the emerging markets as well. So it's not a market that we're going to ignore. It's just that we will not be selling at any kind of price and compete just for that.

items.statement: Successfully completed WHO and global customer audits enhancing credibility as preferred supplier
items.quote: We have, also, successfully completed audits from WHO and many other global customers. This will enhance our credibility as a preferred supplier.

items.statement: Turkey hyperinflation accounting continues under IndAS 29; early signs of currency stabilization
items.quote: Net monetary loss on hyperinflation economy which is Turkey is shown under IndAS 29 adjustment which continues because the situation in Turkey. Turkey is amongst one of the 3 or 4 countries in hyperinflation as of now, so that still continues.

items.statement: Working capital improved to INR4,201 million from INR4,354 million YoY
items.quote: Our working capital stands at INR4,201 million as on March '24 as compared to INR4,354 million as of March '23.

items.statement: Net debt INR3,789 million; net debt/EBITDA improved to 3.55x from 4.70x; debt level expected stable but ratio to decline with EBITDA growth
items.quote: Net debt as on date, as on March 31, '24, is INR3,789 million against INR3,654 million in March '23. Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio has seen an improvement and which stands at 3.55 as on March '24 versus 4.70 in March '23.

items.statement: Actively evaluating M&A targets in formulations and API for R&D and manufacturing synergies; supported by promoter
items.quote: M&A is part of our growth plan. We are constantly evaluating targets, including some in India. And as far as the nature of targets are concerned, we are open both to targets and formulations as well as any opportunity on the API side

items.statement: API quarterly run rate targeting INR100 crore consistently in next 12-24 months; FY24 API revenue INR325 crore
items.quote: a three-digit number per quarter is what we certainly aspire to have consistently in the next 12 to 24 months. But beyond that, it would, of course, depend on how fast we are able to commercialize some of the new products

items.statement: Emerging markets mixed: Turkey stabilizing but Brazil tender volatility and MENA currency/repatriation challenges persist
items.quote: emerging markets will be a mix for a while. And the fact that the larger market sector, Turkey etcetera, for us are growing, we'll make sure that at an aggregate level, we will do well.

items.statement: U.S. formulation entry on hold; focusing on organic growth; M&A would be incremental if accretive
items.quote: I think the U.S. formulation piece, as we have said before, is on hold for us. We will look at our strategic priorities. As I said earlier, we are looking at M&A. We are looking at business development.

items.statement: ESOP cost declining trend expected to continue; may increase if leadership hires made
items.quote: ESOP generally, the impact is very high in initial few years, which we have seen in the last couple of years. And since last two quarters, the trend has already, if you see, has started going down. We believe that based on our current calculation, yes, the trend continues and our ESOP cost keeps on coming down.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA guidance maintained at Rs 1,450-1,700 crore
items.quote: With commissioning of several ongoing projects and anticipated volume ramp-ups in existing products, we continue to maintain our expected EBITDA guidance of Rs. 1,450-1,700 crore for FY25.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth guidance raised to 20-30% from 20-25%
items.quote: Yes. Actually, our earlier guidance was 20% to 25% in the last con-call, so that we have increased to 20% to 30% as a range.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA split expected 40-45% in H1 and 55-60% in H2
items.quote: Yes, I think it will be more 40%-45% and 55%-60%.

items.statement: FY24 capex over Rs 1,280 crore; FY25 capex planned at Rs 1,500-1,800 crore
items.quote: We entailed a CAPEX of over Rs 1,280 crore in FY24 on project expansions, and plan to spend another Rs 1,500-1,800 crore in FY25.

items.statement: FY26 capex upward of Rs 1,000 crore, not yet finalized
items.quote: FY'26, no, we have not yet fully finalized the numbers. I think that will be maybe in the next couple of quarters, where we'll be able to give a clearer guidance on the capex for FY'26.

items.statement: Nitro Toluene and ethylation blocks commissioning in Q2 FY25
items.quote: That will be looking at Q2 of FY'25, the commissioning for both Nitro Toluene and the downstream.

items.statement: Chloro Toluene project initial phase projected to commence by FY26
items.quote: Our Chloro Toluene project is also advancing well, with the initial phase projected to commence by FY26.

items.statement: Agrochemical segment under pressure; discretionary segments (dyes, pigments, specialty polymers, additives) seeing recovery
items.quote: This agrochemical segment is under pressure. So volumes in that segment are getting impacted. Whereas on the discretionary side, dyes, pigments, and other segments, there we are seeing good traction as far as demand is concerned.

items.statement: Agrochemical recovery expected in H2 FY25; calendar year 2025 near normal
items.quote: Yes. Agrochemical first half will be challenging. But I think in the second half, I think we should see a good recovery in agrochemical.

items.statement: Value-added downstream products expected to deliver 25-30% EBITDA margin on average
items.quote: No, we have a basket of products. So some of the products, there may be pressure. So on an average, this value-added product will give you a 25%, 30% range as EBITDA margin in that.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin to structurally improve from FY26-27 with Chloro Toluene range
items.quote: As we had mentioned earlier that Chloro Toluene range these are more value-added products, so structurally, there the EBITDA margin is higher. So with those products coming in line on a weighted average basis, combined EBITDA also as a percentage will increase from FY '26-'27 onwards.

items.statement: First long-term contract (agro intermediate) contributed below Rs 100 crore in FY24; expected ~Rs 250 crore in FY25
items.quote: FY'24, I think it was below INR100 crore as some agrochemical impact had taken place. But this year, we expect more around INR250 crore or so.

items.statement: MMA contract revenue expected to grow 50-60% YoY in FY25
items.quote: Y-o-Y, this is 50% to 60% at least.

items.statement: FY24 revenue split: agro/pharma ~35%, discretionary ~65%
items.quote: This agro and pharma were around 35% and discretionary around 65%, and 35%, 65% kind of a number was there between discretionary and non-discretionary.

items.statement: Long-term contracts on raw-material-plus pricing; short-term contracts quarterly with price movement
items.quote: Certainly, in all the long-term contract we have structured pricing in place, whereas contracts which are more of a quarterly; orders which are more on a quarterly basis, there the prices may have some inherent movement also, up and downside.

items.statement: Absolute debt not expected to reduce due to ongoing capex; working capital optimization efforts continue
items.quote: So on an absolute basis, I'm not expecting debt numbers to reduce, but there will be efforts in terms of optimizing the working capital days, which could pot entially provide some optimization of debt, but the debt will be a bit higher than what it is currently right

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of Rs 1 per share (20%) for FY24
items.quote: The Board has recommended a dividend of Rs 1/- share (i.e 20%) for FY24.

items.statement: R&D centre at Navi Mumbai driving in-house development for Chloro Toluene range and sunrise sectors
items.quote: Yes, this entire Chloro Toluene range that is all in-house because we'll be adding a lot of new chemistry in that photochemistry, ni trilation, hydrolysis and grignard chemistry. So a lot of different chemistries, the products will be coming up in this entire Chloro Toluene range and also in a multipurpose plant

items.statement: Peak EBITDA from existing assets (excl. Chloro Toluene/MPP) estimated ~Rs 2,000 crore (10-15% above FY25 guidance high end)
items.quote: Yes. I think another additional 10% to 15% should be possible. So more towards INR 2,000 crores kind of a number should be possible from ongoing existing location expansion.

items.statement: Agrochemical demand recovery product-specific; some products may normalize only by calendar 2025
items.quote: Basically, it will be generally, this will be always product specifics. So somewhere the demand will pick up in this quarter, next quarter, and all. And some of them which are annual bases, where the demand pickup will be more happening in calendar year '25.

items.statement: Export geography mix: ~11% North America, 6% Europe, 4% China, 3% Japan, 28% rest of world
items.quote: But overall, on an an nualized basis, we had about 11% North America, 6% Europe and 4% in China, 3% Japan and rest of the world, 28

items.statement: Tax rate for FY25-26 expected around 12-16%
items.quote: Our tax rate for FY'25, FY'26, I believe it should be around 15%, maybe around 12% to 15% or 12% to 16%.

items.statement: Cable division guided at 25% year-on-year growth for FY25
items.quote: our guidance has been that we are expecting 25% year-on-year growth. Last year, the growth was lower than 25% because we had a big drop in Cable exports to the U.S. market.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR 350-400 crores per year remains on track, focused on conductor rod making, alloying, CTC, bus bars, rods
items.quote: We were talking about doing INR350 crores to INR400 crores capex year-on-year. So that program still remains pretty much on track.

items.statement: Conductor order book INR 6,885 crores (premium 44.8%, export 37%); Q4 order inflow INR 3,018 crores (premium mix 57.5%); Cable order book INR 1,436 crores (export ~20%)
items.quote: Overall, our order book stands at about INR 6,885 crores, with the premium basket contributing to 44.8% and the export mix contributing to 37%. New order inflow for the quarter came in at INR 3,018 crores, of which the premium product mix is 57.5%.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong across conductors, cables, transformer oil; Export demand weak from US (deinventorising, high rates, elections); Global sales ex-US grew 29.8% (Q4) and 51.8% (Cables Q4)
items.quote: Domestic demand continues to be strong, offsetting the weaker export demand that has been coming, especially from the U.S. market, where customers had been deinventorizing. Global sales growth, ex the U.S., actually grew at 29.8% in Q4.

items.statement: US market share fell from 26% (FY23 peak) to 12-13% (FY24); Australia third largest export market, growing; Indian Railways, solar, wind, renewables driving domestic cable growth
items.quote: Anand, it was at 26%. And today, at its peak, I mean in FY '23, it was at 26% of the revenues of that year. Today, it's about half of that, about 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Chinese competition intensifying in conductors and cables, especially building wires and solar cables in US, Asia, Africa, Latin America; US authorities cracking down on illegal routing; Sterlite Power main premium conductor competitor; GSK
items.quote: we see increased competition coming from Chinese exporters in most of the markets. Even in the U.S. market, they have been trying to skirt around the tariffs by illegally routing products through alternate geographies.

items.statement: CEA mandate: copper transposed conductors required for transformers >400 amps, driving CTC growth; RDSS scheme EPC portion ~35-40%, metering large allocation; MVCC projects under RDSS for safety
items.quote: There is a new requirement that has come in from Central Electricity Authority, which requires you to use copper transposed conductors for all transformers that exceed 400 amps.

items.statement: Full back-to-back hedging on copper/aluminum; margins per unit unchanged by raw material price moves; higher commodity prices may delay customer projects
items.quote: our margin will not change depending on the prices of copper or aluminum going up and down because we run a full hedge book. There is complete back-to-back hedging that happens on all the orders.

items.statement: QIP funds deployed in working capital reducing interest-bearing LC; No new debt details discussed
items.quote: because of the QIP funds coming in and getting deployed in working capital, our interest-bearing LC has come down.

items.statement: India transmission line addition: 14,203 ckm (FY24) vs 16,602 ckm target; FY25-27 target 17,500 ckm/yr and 80,000 MVA/yr transformation capacity; Renewable capacity addition 18.48 GW (FY24) vs 15.27 GW (FY23); Solar 81% of RE addition
items.quote: On a 12-month basis, 14,203 circuit kilometers of transmission lines were added, which has fallen short of the planned addition of 16,602. However, looking ahead in the next 3 years, it is targeted to add about 17,500 circuit kilometers of transmission lines per year and about 80,000 MVA of transformation capacity per annum.

items.statement: US market softness to continue near term (high rates, elections); Chinese export aggression; Short-term tender slowdown due to Indian elections; Red Sea freight costs hurting Europe exports
items.quote: We are also seeing a short-term slowdown in demand from tenders and some of the new conducting work, at least for this period given the fact that decision-making is reasonably paralyzed due to the ongoing elections

items.statement: Management targets double-digit revenue growth for FY25 and calls it a breakout year with internal stiff targets set.
items.quote: I am saying that it's going to be double-digit. It's not going to be and much more than this is what, internally, that's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Telcos are embracing AI and GenAI with real use cases; Subex has paid POCs with at least two telcos for GenAI fraud solutions.
items.quote: We have almost believed that we are witnessing history in making with what was once just a mere concept is now finding acceptance in real use cases for telcos.

items.statement: Portfolio transformed to telco AI-first; new products include AI agents for fraud investigation, interconnect wholesale billing, and enterprise billing solutions.
items.quote: We have something called AI agents right now. So, AI agents are people. It's almost like it's a product that sits on alongside our fraud management solution where it can go and investigate a fraud entirely for someone.

items.statement: EBITDA positive in Q3 and Q4 FY24; Q4 EBITDA INR 31 million vs INR 6 million in Q3; full-year EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 157 million from INR 307 million.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at 31 million as against 6 million for the previous quarter. This is EBITDA growth of about 3% quarter on quarter.

items.statement: Strategic Tier 1 wins in Q4 with significant AI component; win rate higher than announced deals; SaaS model delays revenue recognition until implementation completes.
items.quote: We have had some strategic Tier 1 wins in Q4, which also includes significant AI component.

items.statement: Budgeting for FY25 completed in December; investments planned in product roadmaps, engineering, and AI technologies while preserving bottom line.
items.quote: We have actually done the budgeting for this year already, and we have taken the investment calls on which products need to briefed up and all that.

items.statement: Routine annual goodwill impairment of INR 148 crore taken in consolidated books; goodwill reduced from INR 344 crore to INR 196 crore; non-cash charge taken from reserves.
items.quote: This year there's a charge of close to INR 148 crore has happened which is in the consol books. The value of the goodwill is reduced from INR 344 crore now to INR 196 crore.

items.statement: Cash balances above INR 100 crore; financial health described as good to fund core portfolio investments.
items.quote: I want to emphasize that the financial health of the company is good with respect to cash balances being above INR 100 crores right now.

items.statement: Attrition arrested to industry target levels; annual increment cycle in June-July; headcount considered well-staffed with no major gaps.
items.quote: We also arrested attrition successfully last year. So, we are at what is the target of industry right now.

items.statement: Account Aggregator in-principle approval received; full license requires infrastructure investment and viable India-market business case; not a fintech entry strategy.
items.quote: We have an in-principle approval. We don't have the license yet. So, what that requires is for us to identify a business case and make investments in the infrastructure this year.

items.statement: IDC customer base around 125; Sectrio contracts in Middle East and CALA region; win rate higher than announced material deals.
items.quote: IDC, I think we have around maybe 125 or so. I can come back to you with the right number, but I think it's around 125.

items.statement: AI spend by telcos projected at $15 billion by 2027 with rapid CAGR; Subex aims to be global leader in AI-driven fraud management for telcos and fintechs.
items.quote: The market size in 2027 of the pure AI spend for telco is $15 billion. It's no joke action. It's growing. The CAGR is growing so rapidly.

items.statement: No further impairment expected next quarter; annual impairment exercise completed; management focuses on prudent capital allocation with IRR above cost of capital.
items.quote: I don't think that you will see another impairment in the next quarter or something like that. You wouldn't see that, actually.

items.statement: FY24 revenue grew 11.1% YoY to INR 3,097 million, highest in a decade; Q4 revenue INR 833 million, up 2% QoQ.
items.quote: The revenue for the YoY ended at INR 3,097 million, that's INR 309 crores as against INR 2,787 million for the year that ended on March 31, 2023. This is the growth that I was speaking about. This is 11.1%.

items.statement: Analyst roadshows and investor meets planned within a quarter now that growth numbers are visible.
items.quote: Very much on the cards this year, which I want to pick up, in a quarter from now we want to pick up that activity.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 2,900 crore by March 2027, implying 16.02% CAGR from FY24 exit
items.quote: Originally, aiming for INR 2,900 crore in sales by September 2025, the target date has been recalibrated to March 2027 , that is a stretch of 1.5 years. This adjustment reflects a compounded annual growth rate of 16.02%

items.statement: Sluggy demand to persist in Q1FY25 due to elections and heatwave; improvement expected post Q1FY25
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate the trend of sluggish demand conditions to continue in Q1FY25 with a further exacerbated by the ongoing general elections in April and May. Additionally, seasonal factors like prevailing extreme heatwave conditions in many parts of the country, shortage of labor, especially in the real estate sector are expected to pose further challenges. However, we remain optimistic

items.statement: Routine capex budget for FY25 is INR 25.4 crore; greenfield sanitaryware plant estimated at INR 125-130 crore
items.quote: Our routine capex budget for FY 2024-2025 is INR 25.4 crore. This includes essential upgrades in our sanitaryware and faucetware plants, focusing on machinery replacement, enhancing customer touch points and IT -related developments, ensuring operational efficiency, business continuity and improved logistics.

items.statement: Faucetware capacity expanded to 4 lakh pieces/month with 90% utilization in Q4FY24; sanitaryware greenfield plant land acquisition mostly done, operational in 18 months from zero date
items.quote: I am pleased to share that following the completion of the ramp-up phase, our plant is now fully capable of delivering 4 lakh pieces per month. During Q4FY24, our faucetware capacity utilization reached an impressive 90% , leveraging the augmented capacity from the brownfield expansion. Furthermore, the majority portion of the land for our greenfield sanitaryware project was acquired by March 2024

items.statement: New product development accounts for 30-35% of total sales
items.quote: The sharp increase in new design and product launches over the past 3 years has involved substantial efforts and is paying rich dividends with new product development accounting for 30% to 35% of the total sales.

items.statement: 2% price hike in sanitaryware in Feb 2024 to offset input costs; no price hikes in prior 20 months; future hikes depend on market conditions
items.quote: price rise, which was taken in February 2024 was 2% in sanitaryware segment to offset the impact Transcript of CERA Sanitaryware Ltd. Q4 FY24 Earnings Call of the increased input costs. So ideally speaking, the price rise has been taken, but it is just to offset this impact

items.statement: Dealer network grew from 5,400 to 6,200; retailer base enrolled in loyalty program grew from 14,500 to 19,300
items.quote: So, regarding the distribution networking, if we see, we are having a base of around 6,200 dealers. And this networks, if you see in terms of the growth versus the previous year, so previous year, we were having around 5,400 dealers were there. So, there is a growth of around 800 dealers. And of these if you see the base of the retailers also because our distribution network is largely through dea

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced from 69 to 59 days; inventory days 77 to 70, receivables 32 to 34, payables 40 to 45
items.quote: The changes in the working capital position in the current quarter as compared to the corresponding quarter for the previous year were as follows: Inventory days reduced from 77 to 70 days, receivables days slightly increased from 32 days to 34 days and payable days increased from 40 to 45 days. Therefore, the net working capital days were reduced from 69 days to 59 days in Q4FY24.

items.statement: No plans for debt raising or equity dilution; capacity expansions funded from internal accruals and cash of INR 828 crore
items.quote: During the recent past, internal accruals were utilized to fund the two capital expenditure programs. Looking ahead, we aim to maintain the flexibility to use a portion of our cash and cash equivalents as needed without any plans for debt raising or equity dilution to support the capacity expansions.

items.statement: Dividend of INR 60 per share (1,200% of face value) approved, representing 32.6% of PAT
items.quote: Additionally, the Board of Directors announced a dividend of INR 60 per share, representing 1,200% of the face value per share.

items.statement: ESOP scheme introduced in Q4FY24 to motivate and retain key talent
items.quote: In line with the above, Cera has introduced an ESOP scheme this quarter. This will help to motivate and reward key human resources within the organization on a medium to long-term basis, ensuring stability and longevity in their tenure, enabling them to contribute to the Company's growth plan and retaining knowledge and experience within the organization.

items.statement: New entrants from pipes segment not seen as major threat due to lack of manufacturing, limited SKUs and dealer network
items.quote: We are of the sense that they have been having a very difficult time because what they are doing is, they're mostly trying to, they have not yet set up a factory. Most of them do not have a manufacturing facility. They are trying to source from the outsourcing partners, and they don't have the kind of depth and the range of SKUs that we have been able to offer and also the kind of dealer network t

items.statement: China imports only INR 10 crore (1.8% of sales) in Q4FY24; strategic focus on minimizing China reliance
items.quote: In Q4FY24, our China imports totalled INR 10 crore, representing 1.8% of the sales. Cera has consistently maintained a strategic approach to minimize reliance on products made in China, leveraging our in-house capabilities.

items.statement: 16% CAGR driven by 10-13% volume, 4-6% mix, 2-3% price over next 3 years
items.quote: So ideally, the factors which are going to contribute to this growth of 16% will be led by volume, which may be around 10% to 13%. And there will be some benefit from mix also, which is going to be around 4% to 6%, and the price will play between 2% to 3%.

items.statement: Expects to open 120 new screens and close 70 screens in FY25, net addition of 50 screens
items.quote: For FY'25, the company expects to open 120 new screens and exit 70 screens resulting in a net addition of 50 screens.

items.statement: Projects FY25 capex to be 25% lower than FY24's INR630 crores, including Devyani JV investment
items.quote: Actually, if you look at ou r total capex outlay this year was about INR630 -odd crores. So we expect that to go down by at least 25% this year

items.statement: Aims to reduce capex intensity by 30-50% over time via capital-light and FOCO models
items.quote: Our focus going forward I think is incrementally the new screen additions that we make. eventually want to evolve to a capex -light model which means that over a period of time, reduce our capex intensity by 30% to 50%.

items.statement: Gross margin target of 22% in FY25
items.quote: Dhavan Shah: Okay. In FY '25, so you are saying that we can reach to 22%. Sudipta Mukherjee: Yes.

items.statement: Railway floated 15,000+ wagon tenders; another 20,000-25,000 expected this financial year; private tenders 17,000+ wagons
items.quote: And further in this financial year, we feel that there will be another 20,000, 25,000 tender is expected to come. Other than that, there is a significant growth in the private wagon requirement.

items.statement: Consistent annual wagon procurement of 14,000-15,000 minimum expected
items.quote: So we believe that consistency of 14,000, 15,000 minimum per annum would be there.

items.statement: Order book of 14,000+ wagons as of date; total order book value ~INR8,000 cr (Freight Car INR5,500 cr, Rail Infra INR750 cr, Infra Electrical INR1,150 cr, JV/subs INR500 cr)
items.quote: So Vishal, yes, we have an order of close to INR8,000 crores. If you see the breakup freight car division would be INR5,500 crores; Rail Infra and Green Energy would be INR750 crores; Infra Electrical which is Bright Power is INR1,150 crores. Our various joint venture and subsidiary is close to INR500.

items.statement: Private orders ~15% of order book (~1,000 wagons, INR800 cr value)
items.quote: And actually -- it was my mistake. You are correct, it is INR800 crores, not INR500 crores.

items.statement: Current infrastructure can grow 20-30% more; achieved 850 wagons in March 2024; FY24 production 7,028 wagons
items.quote: in the current infrastructure, we feel t hat we can still grow anywhere around 20% to 30

items.statement: Steel foundry production 35,100 MT in Q4 FY24, up 42-43% YoY from 25,700 MT
items.quote: So steel foundry, Prat eek, you see, we have done the highest ever production, that is close to 35,100 metric tons against last year of 25,700 metric tons

items.statement: Freight car division EBITDA ~12.5-13% after removing one-offs; consolidated Q4 EBITDA 9.5% including other income
items.quote: So if we remove these two numbers and we compare apple-to-apple with the freight car division to the freight car division of our competitors, I think we should be close to that number. Our EBITDA would be somewhere around 12.5% to 13%.

items.statement: Material cost 80.2% of revenue for FY24 (INR2,879 cr / INR3,587 cr); product mix drives variation
items.quote: If you look at the yearly results which is the material, I think the material cost is INR2,879 crores and the total income is INR3587 so it's walks out to be 80.2%.

items.statement: Wagon price increase due to specification differences, not demand-supply; railway pricing follows escalation/de-escalation matrix
items.quote: So the type of the wagon and the design and the specification was different. That is the main reason of increase of price. But I mean it is not related to any demand and supply issue.

items.statement: Foundry exports to US (AAR approved) and Europe; target to increase foundry exports >50% YoY in FY25
items.quote: For this financial year, at least we want to increase our export to more than 50%, whatever we have done in the last year.

items.statement: Export market strong in Europe and US due to geopolitical factors (China exports down, Ukraine production down)
items.quote: The market in Europe and the U S. because of various geopolitical reasons which is supporting India, not only in this respect, but for all engineering aspect, all engineering products, the export market in Europe and the US are very, very strong.

items.statement: Total debt INR630 cr (LT INR241 cr, ST INR388 cr); repaid INR175 cr in April 2024; debt now ~INR450 cr
items.quote: We have already repaid as we talked INR175 crores in the month of A pril. So the debt stands at INR450 crores as of now

items.statement: QIP2 funds (INR800+ cr) received end-March, deployed in April to reduce borrowings
items.quote: This balance what you are seeing INR800 crores, this includes the funds which we have received during QIP 2 towards end of March which was line in the bank escrow account, and we could utilize this only in first week of April.

items.statement: Demerger of Rail Infra & Green Energy applied to stock exchanges; SEBI approval pending; lender NOCs mostly received, few awaited (10-15 days)
items.quote: We have applied to stock exchanges. They have given certain queries to SEBI. SEBI is yet to approve that. So once SEBI approves, then it would be decided -- we get an approval for that.

items.statement: Dividend increased to 50% (INR0.5/share) due to tender requirements needing dividend-paying track record and to reward shareholders
items.quote: Since last year, we had made a profit of INR28 crores. This year, we made a profit of INR178 crores, PBT. The Board has taken a call that the dividend percent be increased to 50%.

items.statement: New risk management setup with Chief Risk Officer; ESG focus including green power at Urla foundry, water harvesting, renewable energy group
items.quote: We have a very Texmaco Rail & new setup for risk management with very strong actions being taken with the Chief Risk Officer who is working with us now and -- to ensure that most of the risks are understood well in advance and we mitigate them

items.statement: Market share in freight wagon business 25-30% over last couple of years
items.quote: So it is typically has been -- ranges between 25% to 30% that has been in last couple of years.

items.statement: Maintaining 70-30 railway-to-private wagon mix for higher returns; intend to continue similar mix
items.quote: And if you have seen our results as committed, we have maintained a ratio of 70-30 because we wanted to have a good mix for higher returns.

items.statement: EPC division: stopped taking long-term contracts; executing 3-4 old contracts (Bangladesh Railway, Bangalore Metro, WDFC, EDFC); no new orders until strategy reorganization
items.quote: There are no long-term contracts currently, which are inflowing to this division. There are a few old contracts three to four old contracts which are currently under execution.

items.statement: Bad debt write-off INR14 cr (freight car division) for receivables >4 years old
items.quote: So yes, this bad debt -- the bad debt what we have written-off -- the amount which we have written-off. All these amounts were more than 4 years' old in our book, and we had written off in this quarter.

items.statement: Passenger mobility segment: building 360-degree capability; too early to disclose specific components; working with partners
items.quote: We consider passenger mobility as a segment, not only the coaches making. So for making the coaches, you need certain kind of eligibility, but there are many other things also goes into it, which are very high value added.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment improving with better mobility, youth consumption rising, and rural demand expected to benefit from good rabi crop and monsoon.
items.quote: Things are looking a little brighter. A lot of mobility is being seen in the market. So, there is a lot of action in the market, a lot of movement of political parties, election hoardings, lot of gossip in the market, lot of media watch.

items.statement: Consumers shifting to lower price-point products; premium and exclusive brands muted while value fashion gains traction.
items.quote: People are spending, people are coming out to spend but they are still spending on little lower price point products compared to the higher price point products that they used to.

items.statement: Targeting 8-10% same-store sales growth for two consecutive years to reach pre-COVID EBITDA margin of 8%.
items.quote: See, definitely it is a tough ask. But yes, we need to grow at least 8% to 10% for two consecutive years to reach that level.

items.statement: Plan to open 40-50 new stores in FY25 with potential closure of 5-7 underperforming stores.
items.quote: So, I think we should be looking at between 40 to 50, we would definitely want to open more, but let's see how it goes.

items.statement: Limeroad losses targeted at less than half of FY24 levels (40-50% of prior year loss).
items.quote: See, we should model that we should not go beyond 40% to 50% of the loss that we have done for the year. So, we should not do that.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin at 31.7%, down 20 bps YoY due to higher old inventory liquidation and conservative provisioning; V-Mart gross margin down 0.5%.
items.quote: Coming to gross margins, the total gross margin at 31.7% was 20 bps lower than last year due to higher old inventory liquidation , and also marginally higher inventory provisioning as well as mentioned earlier due to more stringent and more con servative norms

items.statement: Not targeting higher gross margin percentage; focus on volume growth and rupee gross margin per store at effective prices.
items.quote: Definitely percentage of gross margin cannot go up, and we will not target that. We will definitely want to target higher volume and more rupee gross margin from the same store.

items.statement: V-Mart sales grew 13% with 6% L2L; Unlimited L2L grew 13%; Limeroad revenue grew 29%.
items.quote: So, for the quarter, sales grew by 13% with a L2L of 6%. This is probably the second or third consecutive quarter with a good L2L growth with both V-Mart stores and UL firing quite well.

items.statement: FY24 capex incurred Rs. 137 crores (net ~Rs. 120 crores); ~50% on new warehouse operational since June, Rs. 40 crores on 46 new stores, Rs. 26 crores on renovations.
items.quote: On the CapEx side, our CapEx incurred for the year was Rs. 137 crores, with net CapEx of roughly around Rs. 120 crores. Almost 50% of this was on the new warehouse which already got operational in June.

items.statement: Opened 46 stores, closed 25 in FY24; net store count reduced in Unlimited; new Unlimited stores in Tier-3/4 South India delivering 15-20% higher sales per sq ft than legacy stores.
items.quote: On the new stores, as I mentioned, we opened 46 stores and closed 25. And for the next year, we still would plan to open roughly around 40 to 50 stores, with possibly some 5 to 10 stores closure not identified but depending on their performance and improvement in the current year.

items.statement: V-Mart strategically reduced apparel ASPs by ~5% over last year to attract entry-point customers; Unlimited reduced ASPs by >20% over 1-1.5 years; price correction now complete.
items.quote: And with ASPs remaining flat, we have improved or rather strategically reduced our apparel ASPs in the last one year by almost 5% to make the pricing more attractive for the lower end entry point customer.

items.statement: Overall inventory reduced 6% YoY; per store inventory improved from Rs. 2.1 cr to Rs. 1.8 cr; inventory freshness and sell-throughs healthy.
items.quote: Overall inventory levels reduced by 6% year on year, and the per store inventory improved from Rs. 2.1 crores to Rs. 1.8 crores at the end of the year.

items.statement: Generated free cash flow of Rs. 44 crores in FY24 with good inventory management.
items.quote: We also generated free cash this year of Rs. 44 crores with very good inventory management.

items.statement: Competition intense with many new competitor stores; monitoring closely; some competitors using short-term tactics (lower prices, higher rentals) but V-Mart focused on sustainable levers.
items.quote: But yes, I think there are also enough competition which is now in the market, definitely lot of stores have opened up. So, that competition spree continues, we keep hearing about stores which have been opened by the competitors.

items.statement: Footfall growing (25% reported), driven by price correction, new merchandise, youth engagement, and standardized footfall counting; conversion rate at 49% due to group shopping and research-oriented behavior.
items.quote: The biggest factor of it is actually, I mean we have been doing it for multiple months, but still there were regions which were still not recording the right footfalls, and the way of recording the right footfall is manual.

items.statement: Experimenting with GenZ merchandise and unlabeled entry-price inventory in Unlimited; response very good, planning to expand; focus on quality and forward fashion.
items.quote: We also have experimented largely with the GenZ merchandise. We created a small team and we have started focusing on experimenting certain lines of product which we have experimented in few limited stores. The response of those particular lines has been very good.

items.statement: Added two new independent directors with expertise in marketing, HR, and technology to strengthen board governance.
items.quote: We also introduced two new members on the board, we want to broaden our board of independent directors. So, there have been very good two resources that we have found and very, good experts in marketing and in human resource subject and even technology.

items.statement: Integrating V-Mart, Unlimited, and Limeroad; omni-channel 'One Click' tool rolled out to 100% V-Mart stores generating 1,200-1,500 orders/day; Limeroad targeting breakeven.
items.quote: lot of omni-channel drive which has to go on. A lot of omni-channel drive has also resulted into better customer satisfaction at V-Mart and Unlimited stores, because the customers who would have gone on unsatisfied or unserved when they do not get sizes or they do not get certain product, have really got satisfied with more than 1,200, more than 1,500 orders are being generated every day from thos

items.statement: Unlimited legacy stores have high rentals (12-15% of revenue) vs new stores (5-6%); 58 legacy stores at marginal 4-5% EBITDA margin; closure benefits only from FY25.
items.quote: The big difference also is that the new stores that we have opened in South are largely in Tier-3 Tier-4 locations versus the legacy stores which were in Tier-1, Tier-2 locations. Tier-3 and Tier-4 format is something that we have always specialized in and is also giving us good results in South.

items.statement: Sales per sq ft grew 2-3% YoY; per store inventory down 10% despite festive build-up; V-Mart volume growth 12% with flat ASP.
items.quote: The sales per square feet also grew by 2%, in fact 3%, while per store inventory came down by minus 10% despite a festive build up for upcoming Eid at the end of March.

items.statement: Elections injecting money into economy; post-election markets showing growth after 7-10 days; good monsoon expected to support rural consumption.
items.quote: Even the elections are going to bring i n a lot of money. So, we have been watching all of those. Some of those we have seen that wherever the elections have got over and after seven days or after 10 days we start seeing good growth coming in from that market

items.statement: Closed 10 V-Mart and 9 Unlimited stores in Q4 (mostly March); annualized EBITDA savings estimated at Rs. 4-5 crores; focus on capital allocation to profitable stores.
items.quote: The closure of 10 stores in V-Mart and nine in Unlimited during the quarter will further improve the overall performance going forward. As most of these stores got closed in March only, and as such the benefit on account of the expense reduction shall start flowing in from April onwards.

items.statement: Limeroad expenses down 18% YoY with revenue up 29%; burn and EBITDA losses reducing double-digits for three consecutive quarters.
items.quote: For Limeroad, the revenues grew by 29% and the expenses reduced by 18% over last year. We have been strategically reducing the expenses at Limeroad without significantly impacting the top line by increasing the synergies and customer acquisition through the omni model being propagated throu gh V-Mart offline stores

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA grew 76% YoY; Limeroad EBITDA losses down 44%; 12 underperforming stores closed in South, 13 in rest of India.
items.quote: As a result of all these initiatives, the quarter four EBITDA grew by 76% year on year, while the LR EBITDA losses came down by 44%. We closed 12 underperforming stores in south, which will further help improve the EBITDA in the coming years.

items.statement: Order book of US$585 million, up 30% year-on-year
items.quote: And as I am talking to you today, we have a healthy order book of about US $585 million which is almost close to Rs. 5000 crores and it is a 30% increase over the same period last year.

items.statement: Targeting 10% topline growth and 15% PAT growth for FY25
items.quote: We have mentioned a 10% year-over-year kind of outlook that we are seeing ourselves. Currently, we are very positive with the order book in hand, 30% up, but I think we are a bit cautious given the overall environment, but at present in hand the order book is much better than the 10% that we are aspiring to grow the year with.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin expanded from 4.7% in FY23 to 5% in FY24; reported EBITDA margin 3.9%
items.quote: Similarly, our normalized EBITDA margin expanded from 4.7% last year to 5% this year.

items.statement: Capex of Rs.167 crores in FY24 including Rs.100 crores for UK property and sampling unit in Bangladesh
items.quote: We had Rs. 60 crores CAPEX in year FY23 and we have a CAPEX of about Rs. 167 crores. That is almost close to about Rs. 110 crores increase and he answered that about 10 million which is about Rs. 85 to Rs. 86 crores including some taxes went into the UK property.

items.statement: Net debt Rs.259 crores; net debt/EBITDA 0.61x, net debt/equity 0.22x
items.quote: Turning to our balance sheet, the net debt was Rs. 259 crores. However, in spite of the growth in Q4, we have managed to curtail our debt levels to the previous December quarter despite the industry dynamics, our balance sheet remains robust with strong leverage ratios of net debt to EBITDA at 0.61 and net debt to equity at 0.2 2.

items.statement: Net working capital days decreased to 7 days (1 day excluding Ted Baker)
items.quote: With regards to our working capital days, it decreased to seven days by the end of the year compared to 9 days in December. Excluding Ted Baker business, our net working capital days stand at one day.

items.statement: Proposed final dividend Rs.3.15/share; total FY24 dividend Rs.4.75/share (43% payout)
items.quote: We are also pleased to announce that we have proposed a dividend of Rs. 3.15 per share. We had declared an interim dividend of Rs.1.6 per share in the first half. This makes the total dividend to Rs.4.75 per share for the year, a payout of 43%.

items.statement: Q4 revenue grew 25% QoQ after flat Q3; FY24 revenue declined only 2% YoY despite industry headwinds
items.quote: And as I mentioned, it was a tough year, but somewhere in quarter three, we could as a first step neutralize the declining trend, we almost had a flat quarter, but in the quarter 4 we had a 25% growth over quarter 3.

items.statement: Sourcing as a service GMV grew 240% YoY to US$440 million; brand management revenue grew 96% YoY
items.quote: Our sourcing as a service segment experienced remarkabl e growth with a staggering 240% increase in GMV totaling to approximately US $440 million.

items.statement: Onboarded Target US, expanding with Walmart US; Walmart invited PDS to Bentonville for 5-year vision targeting US$400 million
items.quote: Walmart had a summit in India. They came to India and I think February, March this year and they met almost 65 vendors to talk about strategy and growth and only one vendor was invited back to Bentonville, which was PDS. So out of 65 evaluations of different companies, they did on the apparel side, PDS was the only company that was invited back to Bentonville where we went and met them last week a

items.statement: Invested Rs.100 crores through P&L in new verticals (North America, UK brand, home, CSS) in FY24
items.quote: Meaning of further growth, we made investment of approximately Rs. 100 crores through our P&L. In our company, which is an asset light company, any investment that we make into future revenues is primarily through P&L and that is where it aggregated to about Rs. 100 crores.

items.statement: Gross merchandise value (GMV) grew 25% YoY to Rs.15,048 crores in FY24
items.quote: Moving on, we achieved a gross merchandise value of about Rs. 15,000 crores during the year, marking a 25% increase over the same year last year.

items.statement: Sourcing as a service EBIT margin 38.5%; brand management EBIT margin 5%; manufacturing EBIT margin 4%
items.quote: Within sourcing, our design-led sourcing offering achieved a gross margin of 17% and an improvement of 179 basis points while sourcing as a service achieved a growth in top line of 125% with an EBIT margin of 38.5%. Brand management continued its growth trajectory registering a growth of 96% compared to last year with gross margin and EBIT margin of 33 % and 5% respectively. Our manufacturing oper

items.statement: Acquired Ted Baker wholesale business (Rs.150 crores initial, now ~Rs.110 crores net); 26% stake in Sri Lanka factory for Rs.8.5 crores
items.quote: It is circa Rs. 150 crore. That is the amount of cheque we wrote to begin with, and subsequently, we did re cover the part of the investment to working capital squeeze. So if I am giving an approximate number, I think the 150 is down to close to Rs. 110 crores, the 44 got squeezed.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA of FY24 (5% margin) targeted as reported EBITDA baseline for FY25; significant investment benefits expected from FY26
items.quote: Yes, I think firstly we would request, we are very happy to get all your questions and we would really request if you can have one to one meeting to get deeper so that we can take more questions. But taking this as your last question, yes, our endeavor is that whatever is the normalized EBITDA for FY24, we should target to achieve that as the EBITDA from normal operations, post the investments.

items.statement: Investor Day scheduled for June 11 at Jio Center BKC with top 5-6 business heads presenting
items.quote: We also sent a save the date for June 11th in Jio Center, BKC , we are hosting our Investor Day. We are inviting our top 5-6 business heads who are flying in from various locations to get an opportunity to meet you and vice versa as well.

items.statement: Conservative FY25 guidance due to uncertain H2 environment despite strong H1 order book
items.quote: I think you have to permit us to be a bit conservative, we want to make sure that we are in a position to try and beat these estimates that we have for the year. And our endeavor is to improve the margins going forward as well.

items.statement: Hired Mark Green (ex-PVH) for North America strategy; Damian Hopkins for UK brand business; Gaurav Pandey for Walmart business
items.quote: For instance, under the leadership of Mark Green, a very senior industry professional who has had a long inning with PVH, which is the house which holds Tommy Hilfiger, he has come on board and under his overall guidance, we have formed a robust team to drive our North America strategy.

items.statement: Interest expenses flat despite topline growth and base rate increase from 4.9% to 5.3%
items.quote: Our interest expenses were largely flat in spite of the increase in top line and increase in the base lending rate, which is so far from 4.9% to 5.3%.

items.statement: PDS Ventures investments driven by regulatory pressure on sustainability, circularity, traceability in Western markets
items.quote: There is a lot of discussion around sustainability, circularity, and new material science in our industry. So we were seeing that some of our strategic customers were like really getting impacted. The business models are getting impacted because of all the regulatory pressure coming in and all the activist pressure coming in the West that were questioning the retailers' practices on their environm

items.statement: North America revenue declined 15% YoY in FY24 despite investments; green shoots visible, real impact expected next financial year
items.quote: My first question is that despite the accelerated investments in the US market that we have made over the last two quarters, it seems like the revenue from North America business has declined 15% year-on-year in FY24, so what is the reason for such a degrowth despite these investment? And when would our efforts in US start to produce result?

items.statement: QIP enabling resolution obtained but no pressing need; cash Rs.680 crores used to reduce borrowings and as margin money for factoring
items.quote: Yes, I think the cash is about Rs. 680 crores on 31st March 24. And when we report net debt, we net it off. This is typically the cash that is spread across various legal entities of PDS and this is also the cash t hat is pending dividend distribution. What Rahul Ahuja, our CFO as a first step trying to do is that one hand if there is this ca sh, then there is borrowing on the other side. So can y

items.statement: PDS differentiated as only corporate treasury structurally investing in innovation; co-invests with Walmart, Target, IKEA, Patagonia
items.quote: So the impact on repetition, the impact on gaining new customers and solidifying our position with existing customers was a very strong outcome from our deci sion to get into this activity. Now coming to why so many investments, we've identified around 4 or 5 buckets, one is material science. We are seeing that a l ot of when garments go into store, they must come from a sustainable source for PDS

items.statement: PDS Ventures MTM gain Rs.36 crores included in capital employed of Rs.254 crores; venture tech investment Rs.29 crores in FY24 vs Rs.70 crores in FY23
items.quote: On the capital employed front in PD S Ventures and others , the capital employed stands at Rs. 254 crores. It is important to note that this includes Rs. 36 crores attributable to MTM gain. We are also pleased to announce that we have proposed a dividend of Rs. 3.15 per share.

items.statement: FY25 gross revenue guidance 3,900-4,200 crores, net revenue 450-500 crores, EBITDA 275-300 crores, PAT 175-200 crores
items.quote: We are setting our sights on achieving a gross revenue in the range of INR 3,900 crores to 4,200 crores. Net revenue between INR 450 crores to 500 crores, EBITDA within a range of 275 to 300 crores and profit after tax at 175 to 200 crores.

items.statement: FY24 guidance achieved at high end: gross revenue 3,171 crores vs 3,000-3,300 target, net revenue 429 crores vs 410-415 target, EBITDA 253 crores vs 235 target, PAT 148 crores vs 130-150 target
items.quote: We closed the year recording gross revenue of 3,171 crores and net revenue of 429 crores which is at the high end of the estimates. Both EBITDA and PAT also reached and exceeded the high end of our guidance.

items.statement: Take rate improved from 8.5 bps in Q1 FY24 to 9.2 bps in Q4 FY24; targeting double-digit take rate in India for FY25
items.quote: We increased our take rates from 8.5 basis points in the beginning of the year in Q1 FY24 to 9.2 basis points in Q4 FY24. This increase in take rate is a result of discipline, execution , optimization and reimag ining a lot of digital

items.statement: Merchant accounts exceed 10 million; processed 2.57 lakh crores in FY24 excluding RuPay and UPI; UAE processes 1 billion+ dirhams monthly across 6,000-7,000 clients
items.quote: As of March 2024, we had (+10) million merchant accounts with more than 200 payment options and in this FY24 we processed transactions in excess of 2.57 lakh crores.

items.statement: CAPEX rule of thumb $5-6 million per region for international expansion; AI hub investment in Gujarat completed
items.quote: I think the large investments in CAPEX, it's reasonable to assume that it's about $5 to $6 million per region as a rule of thumb.

items.statement: International revenue target 30% of total in coming years from <10% currently; doubled Middle East metrics YoY; Oman third major bank Sohar International went live
items.quote: In the next 2 years our focus will be intensified as we elevate our international business to new heights, aiming to contribute 30% to our total income. Presently our in ternational operations account for less than 10% of our total

items.statement: Invested USD 10 million for 20% stake in XDuce (US enterprise AI company) to enhance Phronetic.ai and CCAvenue in US market; strategic not financial investment
items.quote: This past quarter we anno unced to invest USD10 million for a 20% stake in XDuce, a leading US based enterprise application and AI development Company. This strategic move is aimed to enhance Infibeam Avenues Phronetic.ai solutions and CCAvenue payments business in the US market

items.statement: Launching merchant finance offering (business loans, insurance, wealth management) under new brand; TapPay expansion for card-present transactions; THEIA video AI platform in pilot phases with multiple customers
items.quote: We also plan to offer access to merchants with financial products through the business loan products, insurance product, as well as wealth management under a new brand name which will collectively refer to as a merchant finance offering.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents INR 837 crores vs 365 crores YoY (129% increase); operating cash flow 720 crores up 537% YoY; expect GeM receivables within 6 months estimated at few hundred crores
items.quote: The Company has built a very strong liquidity position holding cash and cash equivalent of INR 837 crores versus 365 crores that we reported in 2023. Our cash and cash liquidity position has increased by 129% year-over-year.

items.statement: Board proposed final dividend of 5% for FY24 subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: Finally, we are pleased that board has proposed a final dividend of 5% for FY24, subject to the approval of the shareholders.

items.statement: Promoter shareholding decreased after brother removed from promoter list; promoter intends to increase stake over time via creeping acquisition and other methods
items.quote: Promoter shareholding traditionally would have been increased through many methodologies including creeping acquisition and many others. So having said that and that would also require capital to be able to deploy.

items.statement: NUE license application with consortium (Reliance, Meta, Google) pending with RBI; no official update on timeline; GeM commercial terms unresolved with zero revenue booked in Q4
items.quote: The NUE network is a similar to a network license like a Mastercard or a Visa or a NPCI. So those were applied a year or two back and they're still sitting with the central bank. So, there have been different news coming in but no official uptake.

items.statement: ROE improved from 7% (FY23) to 9% (FY24); ROCE ex-goodwill 12% vs 10% YoY; targeting double-digit ROE in FY25
items.quote: Our return on equity for FY24 stood at 9% as compared to 7% in FY23 while our return on capital employed excluding goodwill which reached at 12% compared to 10% in FY23.

items.statement: UAE subsidiary pre-IPO round up to USD 25 million expected to close this month; funds for express settlement, geographic expansion, TapPay rollout; PayPal partnership in Middle East
items.quote: In FY25 we will focus on international growth and our international subsidiary has announced a pre-IPO round of up to USD25 million to accelerate our growth in the Middle East region.

items.statement: International business doubled YoY in Middle East; expect to double again in FY25; Saudi Arabia targeting 130 million tourists annually by 2030 Vision; India digital payments growth strong
items.quote: We have doubled in all our metrics over one year in that region and with express settlement to merchants, rollout of tap as well as international expansions in the neighboring countries there, we believe there is a tremendous potential to grow.

items.statement: Competitors faced regulatory restrictions on merchant onboarding for over a year; Infibeam maintained compliance gold standard per RBI; management estimates 10-15% market share based on profitable transactions
items.quote: We have always scored and always been on the right side. And that definitely if you see even on the online space, 2-3 of the biggest competitors or 4 of the biggest competitors could not onboard merchants for over a year and same happened in the offline speed.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 25-27% for FY25
items.quote: Our intention is to be around 25% - 27%. That is our target to reach immediately.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected to rise to ~12% in FY25
items.quote: We are now around 7% to 8%. It will go to around 12%-ish.

items.statement: iDATA revenue and EBITDA to scale 25-30% in FY25
items.quote: Again, we are looking at scaling those operations by at least 25% to 30%, both on the top line as well as on the bottom line.

items.statement: Visa volume growth of 5-10% expected in Q1 FY25
