items.statement: Additional Rs 10 crore capex for Gujarat wood coating facility, space identified
items.quote: we will be doing 100% of CAPEX on the wood coating facility in the Gujarat region, space already identified with the minimum CAPEX, which will stand under Rs. 10 crores.

items.statement: Sonipat facility at 7.5 lakh liters/month in March, targeting 90% utilization (16,000 tons) in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: in March we recorded a manufacturing volume quantity of about 7.5 lakh liters, which takes us to an annual count of about 8,400 tons and along with this, we expect that the kind of growth we are expecting this year, we should be able to reach to almost 90% of the capacity utilization, which is about 16,000 crore in next 1-1.5 year at max.

items.statement: Plan to double shift at Sonipat and add Gujarat facility to double volumes in 2-3 years
items.quote: But from the existing facility also with the 16,000 tons capacity yearly in single ships, we are already aligning ourselves and planning ourselves to take it to double shift.

items.statement: Q4 impacted by muted Jan-Feb demand and deep competitor discounts, March recovery seen
items.quote: Quarter 4, though, was not the easy quarter for the whole industry due to muted demand in January and February and deep discounts offered in the market due to inventory is talking from the competition. However, we saw a decent offtake in the month of March with continued momentum going forward.

items.statement: Delhi NCR pollution impact caused ~Rs 10 crore sales loss in Q3, plan to recover Rs 10-12 crore from East/South/Gujarat
items.quote: So, practically from Delhi NCR, in the month of November-December quarter 3, company almost loses a sale of Rs. 10 crores, so we have a very active plan that if it happens the same way this year, the company is going to recover Rs. 10 to Rs. 12 crores sale loss from the specified region with a very strong plan on the paper.

items.statement: Delhi NCR contributed 40% of FY24 sales, dealer network grew from 174 to 210
items.quote: So, if we talk about the whole Financial Year '24, again only from Delhi NCR, almost 40% of our sales of the total year were coming from only Delhi and NCR and we have registered almost 20% growth in the dealer network earlier from 174 dealers altogether in Delhi NCR, we are now almost working with 210 at same shops.

items.statement: Targeting 150 new exclusive retailers in FY25 across Gujarat, South, East (50 each)
items.quote: FY25 from the new regions, we are expecting almost 50 strong exclusive retailers to be added. The company will be working on the strategy of giving exclusivity in a radius of 3 Km for active interest of the retailer to start the business with. So, for example, if you talk about Surat, we have added almost 17 retailers in Ahmedabad, almost 30. Likewise in Bangalore and Hyderabad, we will add anothe

items.statement: OEM revenue Rs 60 crore from North, Rs 28 crore from South/West in FY24
items.quote: No, it was more. So, almost the OEM contribution only from North India was about Rs. 60 crores and other Rs. 28 crores was coming from the South and the West.

items.statement: Wood coating 85-86% of FY24 revenue (Rs 290 crore), decorative only Rs 24 crore
items.quote: Last year, out of the whole year, Rs. 312 crores, only Rs. 24 crores was contributed by the decorative paint segment and the rest Rs. 290 crores was contributed by the wood coating segment.

items.statement: Acrylic PU grew 2x to Rs 60 crore in FY24, expected 30% of wood coating revenue in FY25
items.quote: So, Acrylic PU, surprisingly for us this year in numbers has grown double, so almost Rs. 60 crores were coming only from the Acrylic PU and which is growing very fast. So, Acrylic PU has better gross margins and better as a product, low competition and is aggressively growing, especially when it comes to the application on the veneers and specially pre-tinted dyed veneers which is the core product

items.statement: Wall paint target Rs 60-65 crore in FY25 vs Rs 24 crore FY24, luxury OIKOS products Rs 12-15 crore
items.quote: With the addition of these five high end products, we are expecting to add additional revenue of about Rs. 12 to Rs. 15 crores of the high end value products and take 24 to almost Rs. 48 to Rs. 50 crores in this financial year of the economical wall paint products, which company is already selling and now in future will be sold under the supervision and under the name of OIKOS. So, this year, from

items.statement: First 3 export containers to Nepal, Sri Lanka, Dubai in Q1; targeting 6-7 containers by Q2
items.quote: Yes. So, I think already the three containers which are going to move will move in the quarter one itself. And again within the quarter one only, we are expecting some live action to happen in Dubai and by quarter two, we are expecting that the samples, which have been sent through Sirca Italy to some Eastern European countries and to other parts of Asia Pacific should come and we would have at le

items.statement: Target working capital days 60-65 vs current higher levels, import dependency down 55%
items.quote: So, considering the total credit days that we have from the vendors and Sirca Italy and considering the credit days we are offering in the market, considering the working capital now which we have to maintain of minimum 90 days from Sirca Italy, which will be the 40%-45% of our total sales and considering the 30 days working capital in terms of RM and FG from the plant side, we are expecting that

items.statement: Inventory days high due to import lead times (90-95 days), local production to cut to 30 days RM+FG
items.quote: Now, the dependency on the imports has reduced by almost 55% which will enable us to reduce our inventory days because the covenant is coming to the local production. All the goods are available with the target of 10 days, the raw materials. So, a total of 30 days, RMC and FG will allow us to reduce our inventory days in the coming quarters quite noticeably.

items.statement: South India acquisition under process at non-binding stage, timelines uncertain
items.quote: Yes, that acquisition is still under process at a non-binding level, but yes, it has its own internal queries which are still to be resolved. So, we cannot comment currently the timelines related to this, but yes it is under process.

items.statement: Acrylic PU has only 1-2 competitors, helps offset PU scheme pressure; luxury OIKOS products have no competition currently
items.quote: Otherwise if we talk about the competition at the polyurethane front, fortunately for us, with the polyurethane there is a strong contribution of sales, which has started to come from the Acrylic PU where mass competition doesn't lie there. There are only one and two immediate competitors in this segment.

items.statement: Volume growth 18% in wood coating segment for FY24
items.quote: So, the total volume growth in the wood coating segment was about 18%. The consolidated growth of volume this year was about 18%.

items.statement: 50+ new hires for wall decorative vertical, aggressive hiring in Q4 for Gujarat/South/East regions
items.quote: This year, the wall segment becoming a separate vertical for us with new, at least 50 new hirings in the wall decorative segment after the JV with OIKOS, all the wall paints will be sold under a new brand, co-brand called Sirca OIKOS in the coming months.

items.statement: BIS norms on furniture imports helping Indian furniture industry and OEM demand
items.quote: The Indian furniture industry is growing. There is a strong decline if we talk about the imports of the furniture from different countries like Italy and China, which is pushing the Indian furniture industry because of the implement of BIS and other norms on the parts of furniture to be imported, so this is helping the whole Indian furniture industry to grow

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance retained at 25-26%
items.quote: For FY '25, we are retaining our guidance of EBITDA margin for the full year to be in the range of 25% to 26%.

items.statement: Consumer Healthcare projected mid-teens growth for FY25
items.quote: We have observed some recovery in this quarter and are projecting mid-teens growth for financial year '25.

items.statement: Export business expected mid-teens growth going forward
items.quote: So we can expect about a growth of mid-teens to the export business.

items.statement: Modern trade growth normalized to 10-15% for FY25 aligned with IPM
items.quote: FY '25, it will be normalized and aligned with whatever is the growth of modern trade in IPM. It will be aligned with them around 10% to 15% that is the guidance we gave.

items.statement: New product launches expected to contribute 3.5-4% to growth
items.quote: We believe that 3.5% to 4% contribution in growth is going to come from new products.

items.statement: Price increase component expected 4-5% of overall growth this year
items.quote: This year we believe the price increase component in overall growth is going to be between 4% to 5%?

items.statement: Q4 FY24 gross margin 69.8%, up 2.6% YoY
items.quote: The gross margins of the company has increased by 2.6% year-on-year to 69.8% in Q4, FY '24, as compared to 67.2% in Q4 last year.

items.statement: FY24 gross margin 68.9%, up 2.2% YoY
items.quote: For the full year, the gross margin increased by 2.2% year-on-year basis to 68.9% as compared to 66.7% in FY'23.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 24.3%, up 3.9% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA margin increased by 3.9% to 24.3% versus 20.4% in Q4 FY '23.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 24.7%, up 2.8% YoY
items.quote: For FY '24, we have reported an EBITDA of INR2,550 crores, which is up by 33% year-on-year basis with an EBITDA margin of 24.7% as compared to 21.9% for FY'23.

items.statement: Consumer Healthcare EBITDA margins lower than corporate average but potential to match
items.quote: Yes. If you compare the EBITDA margins as compared to the company average, yes, they are lower than the company average. Having said that, there is some potential to match up to the company level in the near future for this business.

items.statement: Chronic share increased 160 bps YoY to 36% in FY24
items.quote: expansion in chronic share by 160 bps year-on-year to 36%.

items.statement: Chronic market share reached 37.4% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: This robust performance has led to an increase in our chronic market share to 37.4%.

items.statement: Added 3 new brand families to INR100 crore category, total 23
items.quote: This year, we added 3 new brand families to INR100 crore category, bringing the total to 23.

items.statement: Dydrogesterone plant capacity utilization ~60%, demand fully serviced
items.quote: And the demand is fully serviced from this plant, where we have reached capacity utilization of about 60% or so.

items.statement: FY24 total CapEx INR389 crores, less than 4% of revenue
items.quote: The total CapEx spending for FY'24 was at INR389 crores, which is less than 4% of the total revenue.

items.statement: No capital deployment planned for export business
items.quote: So there is no capital deployment, which is on the cards for export business.

items.statement: Udaipur plant operationalized in Q2 FY24
items.quote: higher capitalization of completed projects, which included Udaipur plant getting operati onalized in Q2 FY'24

items.statement: Dydrogesterone plant started Sep-Oct 2023, capacity for domestic and export
items.quote: So the plant was started last year in September, October timeframe. And the demand is fully serviced from this plant, where we have reached capacity utilization of about 60% or so.

items.statement: Price increase contributed 1.4% to Q4 gross margin; non-scheduled portfolio takes 10% hike annually
items.quote: Firstly, it's a full year price increase, has provided a benefit of 1.4%.

items.statement: Raw material prices not expected to jump significantly next couple quarters
items.quote: We don't see any significant jump in the RM prices over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: In-licensed Symbicort from AstraZeneca for asthma/COPD; one more in-license coming next quarter
items.quote: we have recently entered into an in-licensing agreement with Astra Zeneca for their world-class brand, Symbicort.

items.statement: Field force increased to 16,000 (12,500 MRs); plan to add 700-900 this year
items.quote: Current number is 16,000

items.statement: Net operating working capital reduced from 45 to 42 days Mar'23 to Mar'24
items.quote: reduction in our working capital from 45 days in March '23 to 42 days in March '24.

items.statement: Net cash position INR3,260 crores as of Mar 31, 2024
items.quote: As on March 31, 2024, the net cash position of the company stands at INR3,260 crores.

items.statement: Debt-to-EBITDA target not exceeding 2-2.5x for M&A financial discipline
items.quote: we are talking about debt-to-EBITDA, not exceeding around 2 - 2.5x. So that financial discipline will be maintained

items.statement: Enabling resolution for INR7,500 crores raised; war chest ready for strategic acquisitions in chronic/consumer with high entry barriers
items.quote: we have added an enabling resolution for INR7,500 crores. So we want to keep the war chest ready.

items.statement: Panacea Biotec brands growing 25%+; Glizid crossed INR100 crores; Sitcom patent product bet heavily
items.quote: whatever brands in the company we took from Panacea, everything has been fantastic, growth is in the vicinity of more than 25% plus.

items.statement: R&D expenses 2.2% of revenue in FY24, in line with 2-2.5% guidance
items.quote: The R&D expenses for the year are at INR223 crores, which is 2.2% of the revenue, is in line with our guidance of 2% to 2.5% of sales.

items.statement: MR productivity improved from 6.1 to 6.5
items.quote: MR productivity. So there also, it has improved from 6.1 last year to now 6.5.

items.statement: Export one-off product faces generic competition risk; base business growing to compensate
items.quote: It's a generic product. It's not a patented or para 4 kind of a product. So we can't say that there will be no competition, but it would be safe to assume that competition can come in any time, we can't predict when.

items.statement: Total premiums under management reached Rs. 19,050 crores as of March 31, 2024, up 30.7% YoY.
items.quote: The total premiums under management that we administered as a Company was at Rs. 19,050 crores as on 31st of March 2024, a growth of 30.7% over the corresponding period of the previous year.

items.statement: Group premiums grew 30.4% YoY to Rs. 16,709 crores; retail premiums grew 33.2% YoY to Rs. 2,341 crores.
items.quote: Further, if I break this down into its respective segments of group a nd retail , t he group segment fund was Rs. 16,709 crores, a growth of 30.4% on a year-on-year basis. The retail segment was Rs. 2,341 crores which is a growth of 33.2% on a year-on-year

items.statement: Market share of total health insurance premiums administered rose 186 bps YoY to 19.6%; group share up 229 bps to 30.4%, retail share up 50 bps to 5.5%.
items.quote: As a share of total industry health insurance premium that we administered, this takes into account both group and retail policyholders. Our share was at 19.6% delivering our share growth of the total health insurance industry premium up by 186 basis points over the correspo nding period of the previous year

items.statement: FY24 operating EBITDA margin was 21% vs 23-24% historically; Q4 FY24 margin improved to 22.2% as acquisition synergies kick in.
items.quote: EBITDA, excluding other income, operating EBITDA is Rs. 133.3 crores, a growth of. 11.7% over the previous year, a margin of 21% on the operating revenue.

items.statement: Management expects margins to return to 23-24% range as integrations of Mayfair, Medvantage, Raksha complete over next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: So, we expect to finish integrations as planned and get back on track at the earliest. So, that is where we are on the margins.

items.statement: FY24 total income grew 25.8% to Rs. 653.1 crores; operating revenue grew 25.7% to Rs. 634.7 crores.
items.quote: The total income is Rs. 653.1 crores, a growth of 25.8% over the previous year. Revenue from contracts with customers, excluding other income which is operating income is Rs. 634.7 crores, a growth of 25.7% over the previous year.

items.statement: Organic same-store revenue growth was ~14%; acquisitions contributed ~12% to the 26% total growth.
items.quote: If I look it from the full year perspective, Aditya about 14% would be the same store growth and 12% is from the acquisitions of the total 26%.

items.statement: DSO improved to 102 days in FY24 from 135 days at H1; target is ~90 days; no debtors >365 days unprovided.
items.quote: When we came to the six-month numbers we are up to 135 days is our DSO. In the nine months we were down to 105, currently we were down to 102. That is what we had so for the Company. And we should be around 90 days.

items.statement: Contract liabilities (deferred revenue) of Rs. 220 crores will flow into FY25 revenue; unbilled receivables Rs. 117 crores, 25% billed post year-end.
items.quote: So, if you take the next year what about the revenues, Rs. 220 crores of that is already earned that will go to into the next year. That will flow into the next year , automatically of income that is booked.

items.statement: Tech spend ~3-4% of revenue annually; platform investment Rs. 10 crores capitalized as of Mar'23, ~Rs. 8-9 crores for UK platform in FY24.
items.quote: We are spending on an average working about 3% to 4% of our revenues every year on the tech side, etc.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with net cash of Rs. 245 crores after Rs. 135 crores of acquisitions during FY24.
items.quote: The net cash balance on our books is about Rs. 245 crores. This is what we compared Rs. 255 crores in the previous year post all the acquisitions of Rs. 135 crores which we got through the year.

items.statement: Headcount 6,140 at FY24 end vs 5,470 prior year; Raksha added ~750-800 employees.
items.quote: The total employee base is about 6140. We have disclosed this in the investor presentations , 6140 last year was 5470. Raksha ballpark added about 750 to 800 employees that we can get back to you with the actual number.

items.statement: Acquired Mayfair We Care (UK), Medvantage and Raksha TPA in last 12-15 months for ~Rs. 135 crores; integrations take 3-4 quarters.
items.quote: As you are aware, we have acquired and integrated 3 companies in the last 12 to 1 5 months, including Mayfair We Care, which is a UK based Company and Medvantage for TPA in India an d Raksha TPA in the month of August last year.

items.statement: No active acquisition plans currently; will continue to evaluate opportunities.
items.quote: Aditya, I have no forward -looking statements to make. We will continue to evaluate, but have no plans at this point in time.

items.statement: Group take-rates 2.5-4.5%, retail 2.5-5.5%; base plan rates stable, add-on plans at lower rates.
items.quote: We have also historically mentioned that in the group products, our take rates vary anywhere from 2 .5% to 4.5% depending on the key product and the policy. And in retail and especially when the benefit policies, again, we see anywhere from our 2.5%-3% all the way up to 5.5%.

items.statement: Group retention improved to 94.7% in FY24, up ~50 bps YoY; cashless inpatient >60%, outpatient ~30%.
items.quote: Our proposition is very strong, and it has only gotten stronger with the addition of the group portfolio. We maintain about 94.7% retention higher than what we had presented earlier, in fact, almost by 50 bps.

items.statement: TPA industry share of health premium was 55% as of 2022 (latest data); FY23 data unavailable due to TPA license changes.
items.quote: We published data till 2022 where the share of the TPA industry out of the total health insurance premium was about 55% and there was a 3- or 4-year trend of increasing from lower number to 55%.

items.statement: Raksha TPA acquired at lower margin (~10-20%); integration to Medi Assist margin profile (21-22%) expected over next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: Raksha as a standalone entity continues to be profitable. What we are talking about is bringing the margin p rofile to our margin profile, we are talking about the 21% or the 22% companies and acquiring a 10% or 20% Company and then bringing it to our margin profile

items.statement: Subcontracting costs doubled to ~Rs. 60 crores due to government project staff and support services; advertising ~Rs. 19 crores for relationship engagement.
items.quote: So, subcontracting is a combination of s ome government teams who are not on full time basis with us. We do hire people who are not on full time and the second is support services. There are some support services which are on contracted

items.statement: Premium growth driven by new lives, price inflation, benefit expansion; product mix shifts affect take-rate conversion.
items.quote: So, the premium growth is a combination of new life, new members, the inflation which is the price increase by the insurer and the expansion of benefits. So, these are the three key factors that are contributing to the premium growth.

items.statement: Depreciation & amortization up Rs. 18 crores from acquisitions (Rs. 10 crores customer relationships, Rs. 8 crores assets); March quarter run-rate is new base.
items.quote: The impact for that division on depreciation and amortization is about Rs. 18 crores, Rs. 10 crores of that came on account of customer relationships that w e created as intangible , Rs. 10 crores is on account of that and Rs. 8 crores is on account of th e assets we acquired from the business so total is Rs. 18 crores.

items.statement: Staff cost stable at 40-41% of revenue despite volume doubling; technology automation drives productivity.
items.quote: I think we have been very consistently around the 40 %-41% mark as a percentage of revenue , despite almost 3 years now, despite our volumes and the business more than doubling.

items.statement: Effective tax rate ~16% in FY24 due to one-time benefits; normalized ETR 21-22% for forecasting.
items.quote: So, our ETR that we can say is about 16% and that is our normal tax rate should be for tax with range of 22%. This year we had a benefit of Rs. 4.8 crores which is from, there are two factors that contributed to it.

items.statement: ESOP cost stable at Rs. 3.5-4 crores annually; no significant change expected.
items.quote: The ESOP cost impact on the P&L is about Rs. 3.5 to Rs. 4 crores and that has been in the range. Here on we have seen that as a stable range. So, you can take that as a number.

items.statement: Management declined to give revenue guidance for FY25 due to volatile pricing but outlined volume growth drivers in Specialty segment
items.quote: It would be very difficult as of now to give a guidance on the revenue. However, having said that, whatever revenues we've done this year is on our depressed price as what we have seen and the prices have gradually fallen over the year.

items.statement: SIOP production capacity to increase from 18,000 to 27,000-28,000 tons per annum after debottlenecking; target sales of 25,000-26,000 tons in FY25
items.quote: As we complete the debottlenecking the capacity gets recasted to 27,000 to 28,000 tons, which we intend to fill up in the next one, one and half years.

items.statement: CPVC capacity doubled to 20,000 tons per annum; running at full production of ~1,800 tons per month
items.quote: the within capacity stands, which was standing at 10,000 tons that has become 20,000 tons now, full capacity of 1800 tons a month approximately.

items.statement: Synthetic Rutile capacity 40,000 tons per annum post debottlenecking; running at 90% utilization
items.quote: Post the debottlenecking of out capex, for Synthetic Rutile, our capacity is 40,000 tons, so we have been producing 90%.

items.statement: Soda Ash plant technical issues to be resolved by Q4 FY25; targeting 85% utilization this fiscal year
items.quote: We think that the support will be in place somewhere in Q4 of FY25, so we have to live for the next 3-4 quarters with us 90% kind of our capacity.

items.statement: SIOP margins steady around 35%, may improve slightly with economies of scale from additional production
items.quote: In SIOP, we have been seeing a very steady margin of around 35%. We hope that would continue or maybe slightly improve because of the economies of scale of additional production coming in.

items.statement: CPVC margins around 30% at current prices
items.quote: CPVC at current prices as well, we are seeing a 30% kind of a margin.

items.statement: Soda Ash margins 18-20% normally; expect north of 20% once plant operates at 100%
items.quote: Soda Ash is roughly the stable business, which gives us 18% to 20% kind of a margin for us, we have been bit challenged because of the technical issue to operate the plant at 80%. Once we go to our 100%, we think we should be north of 20% in terms of steady margin.

items.statement: Caustic Soda currently operated not-for-profit due to subdued chlorine prices; used to derive inputs for Synthetic Rutile and CPVC
items.quote: Caustic, obviously, as of now, the current prices have still been falling so QoQ there has been a reduction. We have now been operating Caustic not-for-profit because it's not yielding profits.

items.statement: PVC standard margin 3-5%; profit/loss driven by inventory carry effect on price movements
items.quote: PVC, we are a VC and PVC producer, the standard margin is 3% to 5%, but the profit string happens because of the inventory. So, when the PVC prices go up, we then report higher profits, if the PVC prices go down, we report a loss because of the effect of inventory carry.

items.statement: PVC demand strong, growing 8-10% per annum; piping sector set for 10-12% volume growth
items.quote: The PVC Pipe industry is set to score a hat-trick of double digit volume growth of 10% to 12% YoY in this financial, signaling a strong demand from the end user industries. Owing to this, PVC demand is expected to remain strong and is growing at around 8% to 10% per annum.

items.statement: Synthetic Rutile demand improving from Q2/Q3 FY25 into China and other markets; inventory movement seen in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Unlike Quarter 3 of last year, we have seen some movement of our built-up inventory in Quarter 4 and are seeing improvement in the demand situation from Quarter 2, Quarter 3 of this year into China as well as into other markets.

items.statement: Caustic Soda domestic market has surplus capacity putting pressure on utilization and margins; other products in reasonably good demand position
items.quote: All products, I think, except Caustic Soda, I think we are in a reasonably good place in terms of the demand. Only Caustic Soda, we are seeing a surplus capacity in the domestic industry, which will have some pressure on the production capacity, utilization and margin.

items.statement: Routine capex Rs 35-40 crore per annum; efficiency capex Rs 15-20 crore; growth capex to be announced and funded via bank borrowings
items.quote: Routine CAPEX roughly is around Rs. 35 to Rs. 40 crores per annum. Growth CAPEX is something we will just hold back, that is something of which we are deliberating, I think the announcement will come soon. And some efficiency CAPEX we will do, that's to the tune of around Rs. 15 to Rs. 20 crores.

items.statement: Major growth project payments of Rs 125 crore for CPVC and SIOP completed in FY24; Rs 20 crore invested in captive solar
items.quote: It's worth mentioning that the company has also completed the major payment, for its growth project of Rs. 125 crores in CPVC and SIOP, which was announced earlier. The company has also further invested Rs. 20 crores in group Captive Solar investment.

items.statement: Long-term debt reduced by Rs 100 crore to Rs 409 crore; cash Rs 170 crore; net debt ~Rs 280 crore; short-term funded borrowing Rs 330-340 crore; current maturities Rs 131 crore
items.quote: Net gross, the long-term borrowing has come down by Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 409 crores and the cash in the balance sheet is Rs. 170 crores. So, if you talk, we are talking of Rs. 280 crores of net debt.

items.statement: SIOP prices firm, not corrected with market; benchmarked to Chinese pricing
items.quote: Prices have been firm for SIOP and it's not corrected with the market correction or other commodities or even CPVC. We hope that the price is maintained at this level. Saket Kapoor: How should we benchmark it? What are the key indicators to track SIOP prices? Management: It's basically the international pricing. All said and done China is the biggest producer in the world, so we have to follow

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals EBITDA target >50% of total EBITDA in outer years; Specialty EBITDA Rs 135 crore in FY24 vs Rs 115 crore in FY23 despite 28% CPVC price erosion
items.quote: So, our target is basically to take our Speciality EBITDA to more than more than 50% in the outer year.

items.statement: New Black SIOP variant developed; samples sent to buyers and well accepted
items.quote: We make Red and Yellow but now very recently we have come up with the Black, whose samples have been sent to the buyer, and the initial reports which we have got is very well accepted by the buyers.

items.statement: Inventory buildup in Synthetic Rutile and SIOP in FY24; no inventory buildup in PVC and CPVC
items.quote: We have not built-up inventory in PVC and CPVC; we have built up inventory in SR and SIOP.

items.statement: Caustic Soda production in India regulated by chlorine and hydrochloric acid consumption; chlorine sometimes negative contribution
items.quote: frankly speaking sometimes it is like a negative contribution, and that is the reason at least DCW has not put an any new money investments in Caustic Soda business and, well the rest of the industry is also struggling. So, as and when international prices firm up a little, we export, otherwise, I think by force the production gets dropped because until the chlorine cannot be utilized, you cannot

items.statement: Soda Ash plant technical issues persist; German technical support expected by Q4 FY25; operating at ~90% capacity until then
items.quote: I think a support from the technical disruption has comes from Germany and that we have done whatever has to be done from our side. We think that the support will be in place somewhere in Q4 of FY25, so we have to live for the next 3-4 quarters with us 90% kind of our capacity.

items.statement: Forex business guided to grow 10%-12% annually with retail at high double-digits and corporate at 12%-15%
items.quote: Our focus has been building scale on the retail side, whether it's the student market, whether it's the remittance market, whether it's the corporates or whether it is the holiday product. So I think we are taking strides on those segments. And my expectation continues to be that the retail business will continue to grow at high double-digit numbers. Corporate portfolio will grow at about 12%- 15%

items.statement: Long-haul outbound recovery expected to reach 100% of pre-pandemic levels in FY25
items.quote: Our expectation, as we have guided before, is that FY '25 should see more like 100% recovery to the long haul.

items.statement: India inbound DMS expects 18% growth in coming year
items.quote: We expect a growth of 18% for the coming year and as now business has stabilized.

items.statement: Sterling targets EBITDA margin range of 34%-36% going forward
items.quote: Now even going forward, it will be in this range of 34% to 36%. I think that's the right range to actually be in.

items.statement: Group capex expected to decline from FY24 level of INR 104 crores as major tech spends are one-time
items.quote: We haven't done too much of branch set up this year. But our capex is not expected to be in this range. We expect it to go down, most of this technology development spends happen once in 3 or 4 years.

items.statement: Forex EBIT margin expanded to 41% for FY24 and 44% in Q4 FY24, within guided 40%-45% range
items.quote: I'm happy to report that for the full year, we actually ended the EBIT margin at about 41%. And if I just look at the quarter that went by, which is the fourth quarter for FY '24, EBIT margin actually expanded even faster. It was at 44%.

items.statement: Travel vertical EBIT margin improved to 3.42% in FY24 from 0.233%, targeting 5%
items.quote: EBIT margins on this business improved from just about 0.233% to 3.42%. And I will call out again, we guided the market to close to a 5% EBIT margin that we are targeting on this business.

items.statement: Sterling EBITDA margin expanded to 37.1% in FY24 from 31.7% in FY23
items.quote: The EBITDA increased by 46% to close at INR1,711 million, while the EBITDA margins have also grown from 31.7% of FY '23 to 37.1% in FY '24.

items.statement: DEI revenue grew 5% in Q4 FY24 despite low-margin pricing in USA and China
items.quote: Our revenue has grown at 5% range despite some of the low-margin price predominantly in U.S.A. and China.

items.statement: Forward holiday bookings show 18% growth over previous year at same time
items.quote: Our forward bookings for the current quarter on the holiday side looks promising. We have about 18% growth over the previous year at the same time, and we believe that we are in for a good season ahead.

items.statement: Summer season expected to extend into August 2024 due to post-election conversion pickup
items.quote: Our expectation is that this year, we are going to see probably a longer summer. It may not end in June or first week of July. We will probably see this all the way running into August of 2024.

items.statement: Corporate travel volumes grew 16% YoY, exceeding pre-pandemic levels with domestic at 90% mix
items.quote: On the corporate travel side, the volumes continue to grow higher than pre -pandemic level actually grew about 16% as compared to the previous year. The mix of business continues to be lopsided towards domestic, 90% towards domestic and 10% to international.

items.statement: International DMS grew 27% in FY24, now 41% of travel turnover vs 30% pre-COVID, all regions performing
items.quote: Overall, they grew by about 27%, and it's about 16% for the quarter. It is interesting to note that the international DMS segment now contributes to about 41% of the travel segment turnover. And this number used to be about 30% pre-COVID.

items.statement: Sterling Q4 FY24 revenue grew 39% driven by 7% ARR growth, 9% non-member occupancy increase, 12% room inventory rise
items.quote: Sterling has delivered a strong performance in Q4, Jan-Feb-March with a growth of 39% in revenues to INR 1,179 million, driven primarily by the growth in ARR by 7%, an increase in non -member occupancies by 9% from 62% to 71% and higher room inventories also by 12%.

items.statement: Sterling launched 3 new resorts in Q4 FY24 (Athirappilly, Pushkar, Sariska) adding 12% room inventory
items.quote: During this quarter, Sterling has also launched 3 new resorts Athirappilly in Kerala, Pushkar in Rajasthan and Sariska in Rajasthan, resulting in this increased room supply.

items.statement: Sterling has pipeline of over 20 resorts to be added in next 15 months on asset-right model
items.quote: Sterling shall continue to expand its portfolio, and we have a healthy pipeline of over 20 resorts in India to be added in the next 15 months.

items.statement: Input costs (air fares, hotel rates, transfers, guides) have risen post-COVID; group focuses on sustaining margins not discounting
items.quote: We've seen that our input costs across all our businesses have actually grown, whether you look at air fares, whether you look at hotel rates, whether you look at transfers, guides, everybody 's rates have gone up.

items.statement: Forex retail portfolio grew 19% in FY24: student 15%, holiday 57%, remittance 20%; digital penetration rose to 22%
items.quote: It's also noteworthy to mention here that the retail portfolio during the year grew 19%, aided by the student segment growing at about 15%, holiday business growing by about 57% and the remittance business growing by about 20%. Our digital penetration of transactions improved from 17% to 22% for FY '24 as compared to FY '23.

items.statement: Forex card portfolio grew 40% to $795M; float increased from INR 800Cr to INR 1,200Cr in FY24
items.quote: Our card portfolio improved by about 40%, roughly about $600 million to about $795 million, and that's a strong momentum that we have on the portfolio also. Consequently, the flo at that we generated on the business improved from roughly about INR 800 crores in FY '23 to about INR 1,200 crores in FY '24.

items.statement: Launched Enterprise green prepaid card with lounge access and Study Buddy student product; video KYC enables 2-hour forex delivery
items.quote: We have actually launched an Enterprise card, which is a green card. Again, it's a plastic that you contribute to the environment, and we believe that's the first of a kind that any travel company or any pre paid card company has launched in this market.

items.statement: Sterling became completely debt-free as of March 31, 2024
items.quote: With strong cash collections and higher margins, the company is also happy to report that we've become completely debt-free as on March 31, 2024.

items.statement: Declared dividend of INR 0.60 per share (INR 0.40 normal + INR 0.20 special) for FY24
items.quote: The last point I want to make is that you may have read about the announcement of our dividend of INR 0.60 per share. This has been driven and split into 2 parts, INR 0.40, which is the normal dividend and INR 0.20, which is the special dividend.

items.statement: Forex retail volume grew 18% in Q4 FY24 and 19% in FY24; corporate FX volumes recovered to 100% of 2019 levels
items.quote: We are seeing growth, and this is not a peak of any travel season in that sense. So the aided growth that comes in this business was not there. Despite that, our retail business actually grew by about 18%.

items.statement: Sterling non-member occupancy rose from 62% to 71% in Q4 FY24; room nights sold up 13%
items.quote: Driven primarily by the growth in ARR by 7%, an increase in non -member occupancies by 9% from 62% to 71% and higher room inventories also by 12%.

items.statement: DEI Saudi operations started at 5 sites with potential INR 21Cr annual revenue; Indonesia Taman Safari group adds INR 35-40Cr
items.quote: In Saudi Arabia we have started we've started operations in 5 sites, and that has the potential of doing about INR 21 crores in a complete year. The biggest spurt of growth in new business was in Indonesia, particularly with the Taman Safari Group, which is the large group that we acquired wi th revenues to the tune of roughly about INR 35 crores to INR 40 crores.

items.statement: Expect outbound travel revenue to recover to FY20 level of INR2,400 crores in FY25 from INR1,400 crores in FY24
items.quote: And our expectation is that we will see that number coming back in FY '25. That's the point we are making, yes. And that comprises of your short haul as well as long haul.

items.statement: Expect MICE business to grow at high double-digit 15-20% in FY25 and beyond
items.quote: So we expect this growth to be in the, as I said, high double digit, in the range of about 15% to 20%. That's the kind of expectation we have for FY '25 and beyond.

items.statement: Expect DMS business to repeat similar strong growth trend next year
items.quote: And our expectation next year is that we should be rather repeating a similar growth trend.

items.statement: Expect travel segment EBIT margin to improve from current 3.5% towards 5% range
items.quote: Our ambition is to move our EBIT margin to close to that 5% range. We are currently about 3.5%.

items.statement: Expect overall travel segment recovery to be almost closer to pre-pandemic level in 2025
items.quote: we expect the recovery in 2025 on the travel segment to be almost closer to the pre-pandemic level.

items.statement: Travel segment EBIT margin improvement driven by volume growth and cost transformation benefits
items.quote: So clearly, we expect a lot of flow-through of the increased revenue to come to the bottom line. And hence, it's reasonable to estimate that our EBIT margins will improve from where we are currently based on the higher volumes that will come through.

items.statement: DMS business is currently very profitable
items.quote: But I can assure you one thing. But then if you look at DMS as a whole, it is certainly very profitable right now.

items.statement: Strong demand for MICE from corporates expanding distribution networks in Tier 2-4 markets
items.quote: So clearly, each one trying to expand their volumes will either go and get new set of distributors or piggy bank on the existing network. And there is this race to be better than the other.

items.statement: Inbound travel expected to grow 18-20% in current year
items.quote: Dipak, during his conversation, spoke about inbound businesses and s aid how he expects the recovery to happen and expecting an 18%- 20% growth in the current year

items.statement: DMS now contributes 41% of travel segment turnover vs 30% pre-COVID, grew 27% during the year
items.quote: DMS now contributed 41% of the turnover for the travel segment, which used to be about 30% pre-COVID. The business has grown about 27% during the year.

items.statement: Deploying technology to reduce transaction time by 70% and enable instant mobile downloads for Digiphoto
items.quote: the entire mode of transaction is going to reduce some time by at least 70%. So if average transaction time if we assume is 3 minutes, it can be done and lessened in about 40-50 seconds.

items.statement: Full benefit of Digiphoto technology deployment expected next year
items.quote: we see a full blown benefit of this in the next year, precisely.

items.quote: Typically, in a model like this, floats account for about anywhere between 4% to 5% of your overall portfolio. And we expect that this addition year-on-year will be anywhere between $20 million to $30 million.

items.statement: Forex floats managed through swaps and forwards, not deployed into working capital
items.quote: We actually do swaps, yes, because what happens is you will appreciate that when I sell a prepaid card to a customer, I sell in foreign currency and he pays me in rupee and there is a delay from the time that I raised an invoice for the corporate to process the invoice and take the payment back to me.

items.statement: Finance charges INR26 crores in current quarter vs INR23 crores YoY; real interest INR5.5 crores vs INR8 crores YoY
items.quote: our total finance charges, as I would like to put it, is about INR26 crores as against INR23 crores last year, same quarter last year. Out of the INR26 crores, about INR5.5 crores is the real interest. About INR6.5 crores is the interest on lease rental, interest component of lease rental, which is more of accounting thing than anything else. And the balance, which is the bigger part, the INR14.5

items.quote: So at the overall level, yes, the overall finance cost will keep on going up, but it really ind icates the improvement in volumes rather than charges for working capital

items.statement: Prepaid forex card represents 26% market share, growing at 40% YoY and 15% 10-year CAGR
items.quote: our prepaid card today, we represent about 26% of the market, and it's been growing at about 40%. And if I look at the 10-year CAGR on this, we've been growing at about 15% on a 10-year period.

items.statement: No acquisition plans currently; focus on building cash on balance sheet after pandemic hit
items.quote: We don't have anything in the horizon, neither are we in any conversation with anyone at this point in time.

items.statement: No buyback plans; focus on showing gratitude to investors who stayed through pandemic period
items.quote: I think the word reward depends on how you perceive it. In our case, it's not a question of reward, but it is our way of showing gratitude to our investors who stayed with us through this period.

items.statement: Continuous innovation and adaptation across distribution channels and customer interactions over past couple of years
items.quote: That entire exercise has been going on for a couple of years. So it's not a question of whether our model works or not. It's our ability to adapt to the requirements of the market, and that's something that we have done.

items.statement: Sterling ROCE for FY24 close to 20%, ahead of peer comparison
items.quote: It's 20% and it's ahead of the peer comparison.

items.statement: Focus on getting business completely back to normal across all segments and geographies; reviewing AI implementation opportunities
items.quote: But right now, our focus is to get our business completely back to normal across all the segments that we operate in. And the reality is we operate in multiple geographies as well as multiple segments.

items.statement: Targets 18-20% EBITDA margin by FY26
items.quote: Our visibility and confidence in our performance in FY25, and our ability to achieve the long-term aspiration of 18-20% EBITDA by FY26, has further bolstered.

items.statement: Expects meaningful profitability improvement in FY25 from Q2

items.statement: FMCG ad spending recovery driving ad revenue growth
items.quote: The FMCG sector has been recovering with the rural sentiment witnessing an uptick, leading to a healthy increase in advertisement revenue for the Company, both, on a quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Industry ad and subscription revenue expected to grow high single digits in FY25
items.quote: I think the industry itself will see healthy growth in the high single digits for both subscription and advertising.

items.statement: Q4 operating costs steady YoY, up QoQ due to Zee5 and sports
items.quote: In Q4FY24 our YoY operating cost base has remain steady, while it has seen some uptick QoQ due to Zee5 and sports.

items.statement: Cost optimization initiated, one-time costs in Q1 FY25, margin improvement from Q2 FY25
items.quote: While these interventions will have some one-time costs coming in Q1 FY25, we are well setup for driving a healthy margin improvement beginning Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Zee5 EBITDA loss flat in FY24, costs at peak, will trend down after streamlining
items.quote: In FY24, Zee5 EBITDA loss remained flat. As part of our overall performance enhancement plan, we are revisiting and optimising the overall Zee5 cost structure in line with our strategic priorities.

items.statement: Ad revenue grew 8.1% QoQ and 10.4% YoY in Q4 FY24
items.quote: These factors enabled us to post healthy 8.1% QoQ growth on a festive quarter base, and 10.4% YoY growth.

items.quote: Similarly, Q4 FY24 Subscription revenues are up at a healthy rate of 12% YoY and 3.1% QoQ.

items.statement: Zee Music Company #2 music channel with 149M YouTube subscribers and 165B video views in FY24
items.quote: Zee Music Company (ZMC) continues to be the #2 music channel with over 149 Mn subscribers on YouTube and over 165 Bn total video views during FY24.

items.statement: Content inventory declined by Rs 5.4 Bn YoY to Rs 74.2 Bn in Mar'24
items.quote: Mar'24 Content inventory, advances, and deposits were at Rs 74.2 Bn, lower by Rs 5.4 Bn on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Generated strong FCF in Q4 driven by working capital optimization
items.quote: During the quarter, we generated strong FCF driven by optimization of working capital.

items.statement: Cash and treasury investments at Rs 11.9 Bn as of Mar'24 (Rs 5.7 Bn cash, Rs 6.2 Bn FDs)
items.quote: The cash & treasury investments increased duri ng the quarter and as of Mar’24 stood at Rs 11.9 Bn, which includes a Cash balance of Rs 5.7 Bn and FDs of Rs 6.2 Bn

items.statement: Withdrew merger implementation application from NCLT, continuing SIAC arbitration

items.statement: Expects NTO 3.0 and tariff forbearance to strengthen pay-TV ecosystem
items.quote: We remain hopeful that NTO 3.0 implementation and tariff forbearance will strengthen the pay-TV ecosystem and pave way for sustained growth in subscription revenues.

items.statement: Being cautious on content acquisition pricing, may slow down buying
items.quote: We have been aggressive already Pankaj in terms of buying movies, but there are times when in situations like today, where we have to become a bit frugal to make sure that we are buying the right content at the right pricing.

items.statement: Zee5 pricing competitive, room for pricing to go up across industry
items.quote: We are competing in the market on pricing with everybody, and we have pretty competitive or even equal to whatever the pricing may be, maybe a little bit lower than them, but that is for the reasons for the content that we do not offer, whether it be sports or the English language content.

items.statement: Zee5 pivoting to balanced cost structure, expects short-term financial aberration
items.quote: We have been over-indexing on the growth and investments in the past, but the need of the hour is to pivot the business to achieve a balanced cost structure, in order to sustain long-term growth.

items.statement: Focus on quality content over big-budget films for movie business
items.quote: If you look at most of our successes in the last 2 years, have not been high -cost content. T hey have been reasonable cost or even low cost that has worked for

items.statement: Merger arbitration sub-judice, will safeguard stakeholder interests
items.quote: Sameer, these things are very sub-judice, so I would not like to comment on those things, but we will do everything that's possible to safeguard the interest of our stakeholders and the company. That is our prime objective.

items.statement: Full repayment of USD 314.4 million debt at Maamba Collieries completed during FY24 ahead of schedule.
items.quote: Our commitment to financial prudence and operational excellence has resulted in significant milestones including the full debt repayment of USD314.4 million during the financial year at Maamba Collieries ahead of schedule.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue and profit reached highest ever levels in FY24.

items.statement: No interest cost in FY25 as zero debt at standalone and consolidated levels; only minimal working capital borrowings.
items.quote: There is no interest cost for FY '25 as of now because there is no debt either at a stand -alone level or at a consolidated level. It's only normal working capital, which is very minimal.

items.quote: And our EBITDA margin was at 8.2%, it was a bit lower than we expected because of several onetime expenses that we had in the quarter.

items.statement: Strong demand across all three verticals; pipeline better than ever; re-signed three lost customers; old customers returning
items.quote: So, V.P, our whole world has changed from April 1 because we all are fresh. There's nothing for us to move away from anymore. It's better and bigger than we've ever seen, I continue to maintain that.

items.statement: Active client roster reduced to 84 from 250; exited bottom 10-15 customers; target 75 clients for INR 800 cr revenue
items.quote: And while we added a lot of new customers, we also exited the bottom 10 - 15 customers. And now, our active client roster is down to a healthy 84.

items.statement: Just signed a Fortune 50 company as new healthcare customer; healthcare domestic and Europe revenue to go to zero, US/Canada to grow
items.quote: And as we speak, we have just signed a Fortune 50 company as a new customer. I'll get to that later.

items.statement: DSO improved from 86 days to 72 days; further improvement opportunity exists
items.quote: In terms of DSO, which I already touch base upon, we had a huge improvement from 86 days to 72 days, and we still see a lot of opportunity for us to improve.

items.statement: New office opening in Bangalore Whitefield in July; upgrading to A-grade tech parks for data security and amenities
items.quote: In addition to this, we strengthened our offshore infrastructure, whether it is Pune, Chennai and then very soon coming in July, we have a new office in Bangalore in Whitefield opening up

items.statement: Global headcount 2,529, down ~200 YoY due to exit of domestic volume business; target 2,700-2,800 with majority outside India
items.quote: I want to acknowledge my entire team, which is now at 2,529 employees globally. So, if you see this compared from a year ago, we've gone down by about 200-odd people.

items.statement: Key managers moved to USA and UK for global roles; hiring local talent and transferring employees from India; trend to continue 3 years
items.quote: Now, under each of these leaders, we are hiring local people and in parallel, we are transferring many more employees from our various India offices. I expect this trend to continue for next 3 years as we build our global presence and account management capabilities.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 5 per equity share, highest ever, 9th consecutive year, subject to AGM approval in July
items.quote: Based on the performance, our Board has recommended this morning a dividend of INR 5 per equity share, the highest ever in our history and marking the ninth consecutive year of dividend payout, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming 33rd Annual General Meeting in July.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Industrial Equipment 52%, Transportation & Mobility 37%, Healthcare 8%; 98% from three verticals, 2% ITS to go away
items.quote: Industrial Equipment & Heavy Machinery continues to be our largest vertical and growing very well, and we see amazing potential is at 52%; Transportation & Mobility, which is where automotive is predominantly the largest vertical and now rail is where we are investing, contributed 37% of our revenues; and Healthcare, which is our new vertical, contributed about 8% of our revenue.

items.statement: Pivoted from pure-play mechanical to software (embedded, digital, AI, ML, cybersecurity, data analytics); largest RFPs and deals in software
items.quote: The other side of the story, which is a real ga me changer for us for the last three years, has been when we pivoted from just a pure -play mechanical and engineering services company to software, both on the embedded side and digital side.

items.statement: Sales team fully relocated to US (Michigan) and Europe (London); no sales team in India from April 1; lead gen and presales remain offshore
items.quote: Our entire sales team led by Vignesh, who's Executive Vice President and part of my global management team, he has moved to Michigan. He's building a team around there. Pramod Patil, who's again Executive Vice President, part of the management team; has moved to London. He's building a whole team in Europe.

items.statement: US immigration opened up; Canada visa processing down to 3-4 months from 6-12; Germany 3-6 months, targeting 1 month
items.quote: US was shut for us till about last year. And now, US is open. So, we have people going to US. Canada, which was taking 6, 9 months, 12 months is now taking 3 to 4 months only. Germany is still 3 to 6 months, and we hope it goes down to 1 month.

items.statement: No active M&A discussions; open to acquisitions with cash and PE partner Convergent; priority is finding company supporting existing clients
items.quote: Shriram, on the M&A side, nothing concrete as of today. We haven't , there is nothing that we are actively discussing. But as I always said, we are very open. We have the cash. We have very strong PE partner in Convergent.

items.statement: Exited large Indian healthcare customer end of April (~130 engineers at USD 4.5-5/hr); domestic healthcare revenue to become zero
items.quote: So, for example, we exited a large Indian customer end of April where about 120 engineers moved away, and we transitioned them to some other pay roll the customer chose. So that significant number of headcounts will come down.

items.statement: Revenue grew from INR 440 cr to INR 470+ cr (7%+ YoY); PAT grew 194% (3x) from INR 11+ cr to INR 34+ cr; cash from INR 48 cr to INR 93 cr
items.quote: In terms of revenue, we have grown from INR 440 crores to INR 470 + crores, which is a 7%+ growth. I think we could have done much better if it wasn't for all the clients that we were exiting during our transition phase.

items.statement: Revenue grew from INR 307 cr to INR 472 cr over last 8 quarters; Q4 revenue INR 118 cr after Q3 dip from furloughs/holidays
items.quote: And the exact number from INR 307 crores in the last 8 quarters we have gone to INR 472 crores in quarters. So huge growth for a company of our size and I'm very excited and very happy where we are.

items.statement: Moving engineers from India billing (USD 5-10/hr) to onsite global billing (USD 18-75/hr) drives margin improvement; not headcount-driven growth
items.quote: Let us say we are invoicing at USD 5, USD 6, USD 7, USD 8, USD 10 an hour. And they are moving to my international business where we are invoicing from USD 18 an hour to USD 75 an hour if they are on site.

items.statement: Not competing with GCCs; focus on 80% of global companies in three verticals without India GCC; target customers wanting flexibility, agility, speed
items.quote: Less than 20% of the global companies in my 3 verticals that Onward is playing today, has a GCC in India. My focus is other 80%.

items.statement: Target 10 customers at USD 10 million/year each; currently have 3-5 customers at USD 3-4 million; sweet spot is scaling engagements
items.quote: We have 75 customers. We just need 10 customers to win, 10 customers which can get to USD10 million a year, right? So, for us, it's that.

items.statement: Expects AHP revenue to grow 20% in FY25 from Rs 310 crore base
items.quote: We are looking forward for the overall improvement in the volumes of animal health division from 310 crores to plus-20% for this financial year.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 estimated at Rs 40-50 crore with no major projects
items.quote: As such, there is no major capitalization during '24-25. Only the existing capital of all the units will be there, that's not much, maybe to the extent of 40 to 50 crores in all put together of all the existing unit of poultry, AHP, oil segment and all, but there's no any major project in hand.

items.statement: New AHP plant at 35-40% utilisation; old plant at 75-80%; full utilisation in 4-5 years
items.quote: New plant initially they will be utilizing around 35% to 40% of the capacity and the old plant is almost running at 75% to 80% of the capacity, yes, and in the subsequent year, it will definitely improve further.

items.statement: Summer mortality 10-11% vs 5-6% in winter; body weight drops to 2.1-2.2 kg from 2.4-2.5 kg
items.quote: So in terms of productivity or body weight, there is a decrease of 10% body weight and in terms of mortality, mortality goes to 4% to 5%. So put together close to 12% to 15% less yield is achieved during the period of summer.

items.statement: April broiler realization Rs 108-116/kg across India; expected to continue till monsoon
items.quote: Usually, if you see the year -on-year and month-on-month, this particular April month has gone and average realization has closed 108 to 116 all over India, same is the trend expected for the month of May also and it is likely to continue till the monsoon reaches until the heat is I mean the currently the temperature is on higher side.

items.statement: FY24 avg maize Rs 22.80/kg, soya Rs 47.60/kg vs FY23 Rs 23.90/kg and Rs 52.80/kg; April maize Rs 23.50, soya Rs 44.60

items.value: similar line what it was in FY'24
items.quote: However, monsoon can have a greater impact either on positive side or negative side. But considering overall situation, we expect that the maize price and soya price looks to be on a similar line what it was in FY'24 as of now.

items.statement: Poultry margin was ~3% in FY24; expects good margin if input prices stay stable
items.quote: Financial year '24 also has recorded close to 3% in terms of turnover overall profitability. items.quote: This number what you are saying 4% to 5%, it was also not there in the '22 -23 also, that was not there, it was 2.5 only and this year it is 1.23. Poultry being the temperature through and through is not in a favorable conditions, but then the subsequent quarter hopefully there will be improvement.

items.quote: 42% is the revenue from the group companies and 58% is the revenue from the outside business.

items.statement: Grown-up broiler segment revenue improved most among poultry sub-segments
items.quote: Yes, grown up broiler segment has improved the revenue. If we compare with broiler chicks and layer checks in general, even in the last quarter also as well as in the coming quarters also.

items.statement: Receivables expected to improve sharply in Q1 FY25 as poultry prices recover from April
items.quote: Because the indicators are shown in the month of April also, because of these, I mean, poultry as such is improving, industry as such is improving throughout the country, so hopefully in the first quarter ending as well as the subsequent quarter, this area of receivable will also be improved to the greater extent.

items.statement: Maize diversion to ethanol unlikely at current Rs 23-24/kg prices; feasible only below Rs 21/kg
items.quote: As of now, as per the policy, whatever has been directed, it shows that some of the maize is expected to divert towards ethanol. We are also clueless that at this price diverting this maize to ethanol and then having the ethanol production at that particular cost of pr

items.statement: No development on US broiler import WTO dispute; only turkey import duty reduced
items.quote: There is no development on that front. It is settled on the prices or the import duty on the Turkey, where the Turkey prices for import of Turkey from USA to India, the import duty was reduced. However, the import duty for chicken still continues and presently the preference of Indians towards the purchase of a chicken is on the smaller side of the birds.

items.statement: Venky's Xpress: 13 company-owned outlets, 52 franchise outlets; added 1 company and 14 franchise outlets since Q2
items.quote: So presently we have about a Company owned outlets are 13 and we have 52 outlets which are for chicken experience, that is the franchisee outlets.

items.statement: FY24 broiler chick realization Rs 30.38 vs Rs 27.57; layer chick Rs 38.51 vs Rs 36.38; broiler bird Rs 84.16 vs Rs 89.36

items.quote: For broiler chicks, the realization in '23 -24 was Rs.30.38 paisa against corresponding broiler chicks realization was Rs.27.57. In terms of layer commercial chicks, the realization in '23 -24 is Rs.38.51 paisa against corresponding '22 -23 is Rs.36.38 paisa. In terms of broiler bird, the realization has gone down in '23-24; it is Rs.84.16 paisa per Kg which was in '22-23 it was Rs.89.36 paisa.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 realization for broiler chicks, layer chicks and birds better than Q4 FY24
items.quote: The trend in broiler chicks, layer chicks and birds prices in the first quarter seems to be better than the last quarter of '23-24.

items.quote: Biological notional loss was there and it was not an actual loss, but it was a notional loss, because at the time of closing of the financial, you will have to have a cost basis or NRB basis, so it is a notional loss which is not there.

items.statement: Other financial assets jumped to Rs 110 crore from Rs 17 crore due to Rs 96.07 crore bank deposit
items.quote: It is a bank deposit to the extent of Rs.96.07 crores.

items.quote: It is the area book ed which has experienced a remarkable surge, rising from approximately 50,000 square feet in Q4 FY23 to an all-time high of 4.6 lakh square feet approximately in Q4 FY24.

items.quote: The booking value for the quarter was also at an all-time high at about INR250 crores, compared to INR25 crores in Q4 FY'23.

items.statement: FY24 area booked was ~7.8 lakh sq ft with value of INR388 crores, both highest in company history
items.quote: The area booked for the year was 7.8 lakh square feet approximately with a value of INR388 crores. Both the numbers are the highest in the company's history.

items.statement: Acquired ~61 acres across 3 sites in Lucknow in FY24; anticipate launching at least 2 projects in FY25
items.quote: We acquired approximately 61 acres of land across 3 different sites in Lucknow, where we continue to aggregate more land. We anticipate launching at least two of these projects in the fiscal year '24 -25.

items.statement: Aim to meet or surpass FY24's historic sales figures (INR388 crores booking value) in FY25; hope to launch at least 2 of 3 new acquisitions plus Trinity and Latitude 27
items.quote: For these upcoming projects, we aim to meet or surpass the historic sales figures set in FY'24.

items.statement: INR388 crores booking value is high watermark; do not want to go below that and should only increase from here
items.quote: So INR388 crores is the highest ever number. Earlier, our highest was INR250 crores. So I don't want to go below what we have already achieved. This is a high watermark and we should only increase from here.

items.statement: Luxury project Eldeco Trinity (5 lakh sq ft) to launch in Q1 FY25; also have Twin Tower (10-12 story), Latitude 27 (4.5 lakh sq ft), and GH-4 group housing in pipeline
items.quote: We are preparing for the debut of our luxury development, Eldeco Trinity, which will be launched in the first quarter of FY'25.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 per sq ft realization hit all-time high of INR5,500, up from historical INR3,200 and recent INR4,500 levels
items.quote: But this last quarter, it has been the highest in terms of per square foot realization. I think it was INR5,500 per square foot. So, that's another metric on which is the highest ever.

items.statement: INR5,500 per sq ft realization appears to be the new normal; weighted average may increase annually if market supports
items.quote: So, on a weighted average basis, I think this seems to be the new normal. And I think that if the market keeps supporting us, then it may increase on an annual basis also.

items.statement: Trinity is a much higher-priced luxury product with higher per sq ft realization than Imperia Phase 2
items.quote: Trinity is definitely a much higher-priced product. I would not say we'll probably get sold at the same pace at which the lower -priced products were sold. But it is definitely a product which gives us good margin.

items.statement: Historically margins ~40%; expect 30% as more sustainable level; do not see margins falling below 30%; range 30-40% depending on product mix
items.quote: Historically, our margins have been in the region of 40%. That does look like a very abnormally high margin to sustain. I always said that I do expect it to come down a little bit. I think 30% would be more like it. And of late, it has come down to 30%. But definitely, I don't see it falling below 30%.

items.statement: Should be able to hold or improve margins (30% EBITDA, 23% PAT) in coming years despite new launches
items.quote: Yes, these margins, definitely, you should be able to hold on to, if not improving them.

items.statement: Demand in Lucknow is strong and latent; whatever supply is brought to market gets lapped up quickly; not worried about demand-supply mismatch
items.quote: So at the moment, whatever you supply, because the supply is so constrained, whatever you supply is getting lapped up.

items.statement: Lucknow market sold ~3,000-4,000 units/year but can absorb much more; city poised for explosive growth over next 10-15 years like Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Hyderabad
items.quote: I would know that what the demand is once we supply the market with enough stuff. I don't think the market is getting supplied enough stuff. So it's not selling, I think in a year about 3,000 to 4,000 units were sold in Lucknow. But I think the market can take much more if there was enough supply for that.

items.statement: New land acquisitions add ~INR1,000 crores to gross developable value over next 3-4 years; more deals in pipeline
items.quote: With these acquisitions, I think it will approximately add about INR1,000 crores to our gross developable value in the next 3 -4 years. And we are looking for more, there are some m ore deals in the pipeline.

items.statement: Have 5-6 more land deals in pipeline for FY25; could surpass FY24 business development if they pass due diligence
items.quote: There are at least 5-6 more deals that are still in the pipeline. I don't know how many of those will actually get inked, and we will actually take them all because I will not like to do projects just for the sake of our market pressure to do projects.

items.statement: Expect national and regional players to enter Lucknow, intensifying competition for land; but market maturation favors larger branded players gaining market share
items.quote: I do. I do. If our location is going to do so well, why would the national players or even other regional players not look at that location with more keenness. They will. I have no doubt about it, and it's only going to become the competition for land.

items.statement: Key risk is unforeseen legal/statutory trouble on projects; mitigate via tight risk filters, compliance focus, careful title and approval due diligence
items.quote: There can always be an unforeseen legal or statutory trouble in one of the projects. So that's why we've been so conservative and careful in our project acquisition.

items.statement: Land supply remains difficult; entry barrier is availability of developable land at reasonable prices; but well-placed in Lucknow with 4-5 potential projects in pipeline
items.quote: It is going to be difficult. But as I said, we have been able to, with the hard work in the last 3, 4 years, we've been able to deve lop another potential supply of another 4 or 5 projects, out of which 1 or 2 will see the light of day because of the risk filters that we tend to put in.

items.statement: First time took loans in FY24 to fund new land acquisitions; deployed for the 61 acres acquired
items.quote: For the first time we have taken some loan last year, and we've deployed it for the new land acquisitions, which we have disclosed.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR8 per equity share for FY24, same as last year; no current plans for bonus issue
items.quote: Additionally, for the FY24, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR8 per equity share, which is the same as last year.

items.statement: No plans for bonus issue currently; free float unchanged regardless of share count; INR1,000 share price not prohibitive
items.quote: Right now, there's no plans about bonus.

items.statement: Ticket size INR1-1.5 crores is reasonable with strong demand; not making INR20 crore products in Lucknow
items.quote: Our ticket size is only INR1 crores, INR1.5 crores, which is quite reasonable, and it has a lot of demand there.

items.statement: Received preliminary approvals for one of three new Lucknow land parcels; applying for approval on another in couple of days; Trinity received RERA approval
items.quote: We have, in fact, received preliminary approvals in one of them already. And another one, we are applying for approval, I think, in a couple of days.

items.statement: Eldeco Housing (listed) operates only in Lucknow; sister company EIPL (unlisted) operates rest of India; no conflict of interest by agreement; will only expand outside Lucknow if necessitated and with arrangement with sister company
items.quote: Eldeco Group has 2 companies. One is the listed company, Eldeco Housing, which works in Lucknow. And the other is an unlisted company, EIPL, Eldeco Infrastructure, which works in the rest of the country is not the parent company of Eldeco Housing. They are entirely separate companies.

items.statement: Company listed in 1985 raising INR50 lakh; never skipped dividend in 40 years; market cap grown from INR1 crore to INR1,000 crores; no compelling reason to delist
items.quote: Well, I have a confession to make. There was hardly any strategic intent when it went public in 1985. So I don't think anybody saw 40 years into the future. And the company went public in 1985 and it raised a grand total of INR50 lakh.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue growth expected at high teens, all businesses double-digit, assuming Asacol competition
items.quote: At the aggregate level, we expect high teens growth. This is obviously after assuming competition in Asacol in FY25.

items.quote: On the EBITDA margins front, I think, assuming we have competition in Asacol, we expect to comfortably maintain FY24 margins of 27.5% in the coming year and we will make our best efforts to continue to improve those margins.

items.statement: FY25 R&D spend guided at 7-8% of revenue
items.quote: I think with revenue growth that we expect and also there w ill be growth on R&D, I think we are still giving guidance of around 7-8% for

items.quote: So, gross margin without special products is sustainable . A nd with continuous efforts in terms of cost rationalization, normal price increases that we can take in cons umer business, we are able to ta ke care of inflation in terms of input cost

items.quote: So far as other expenses are concerned, for the quarter, the increase is partly because of one-off expenses to the extent of about 50 cr ores and largely because of the seasonality of Consumer Wellness

items.quote: The base business achieved sequential growth every quarter through the year on the back of vol ume expansion and new product

items.quote: Revenues of the business crossed US$ 1 billion for the first time on the back of strong, double digit growth.

items.quote: We have launched Vascepa, I think recently, but w e don't have scale manufacturing capacity yet, which we do to third party.
