These are, of course, driven by volume demand for our products, and they are c oming along with some pressures on pricing, but we see sustained demand in volume for our products, I think, both in the private and the government sectors

items.statement: Biocon Generics formulation share of product sales increased to approximately 35% from 25% in FY23, expected to overtake APIs in coming years
items.quote: During the fiscal, formulation share of product sales increased to approximately 35% from 25% last year, and it is expected to increase and overtake APIs as a share of our business mix in the coming years.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics secured 4 new commercial formulary agreements in U.S. including United Healthcare Commercial Medical Benefit Drug Policy effective May 1, 2024 as preferred oncology product
items.quote: We have also secured 4 new commercial formulary agreements, including United Healthcare's Commercial Medical Benefit Drug Policy effective 1st of May this year as a United Healthcare preferred oncology product.

items.statement: U.S. FDA accepted Biologics License Application for Biosimilar Ustekinumab for review under 351(k) pathway; settlement and license agreement signed with Janssen Biotech Inc. and Johnson & Johnson for U.S. commercialization no later than Feb
items.quote: We are pleased to share that the U.S. FDA has accepted our Biologics License Application for Biosimilar Ustekinumab for review under the 351(k) pathway and we have signed a settlement and license agreement with Janssen Biotech Inc., and Johnson & Johnson that clears the way to commercialize the product in the U.S., subject to regulatory approval, no later than February 22, 2025.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics signed settlement agreement with Bayer and Regeneron for YESAFILI (biosimilar Aflibercept) introduction in Canadian market no later than July 2025; product already approved by Health Canada
items.quote: Biocon Biologics has also signed a settlement agreement with Bayer and Regeneron that paves the way for the introduction of YESAFILI, our biosimilar Aflibercept into the Canadian market no later than July'25. The product has already been approved by Health Canada.

items.statement: FDA unable to inspect Bengaluru Bevacizumab facility within goal date timeline, issued supplementary CRL with no outstanding scientific issues; documentation submitted
items.quote: the FDA was unable to undertake an inspection of our Bengaluru facility that manufactures our Biosimilar Bevacizumab within the initially proposed goal date timeline and therefore, issued a supplementary CRL. The CRL did not identify any outstanding scientific i ssues and we have submitted all required documentation to the agency

items.statement: Malaysia site completed all corrective and preventative actions (CAPA) per committed timelines; provided comprehensive update to U.S. FDA; anticipating agency inspection of both Bengaluru and Malaysia sites
items.quote: Here, we have completed the implementation of all the corrective and preventative actions (CAPA), as per the committed timelines and have provided the U.S. FDA with a comprehensive update. As a next step, we are now anticipating the agency to visit and to inspect both the Bengaluru and Malaysia sites, which subject to outcome, would pave the way for approval of our biosimilar A spart from the Mala

items.statement: Biocon Generics appointed Vishal Nayyar as Head of Supply Chain Management and Amit Kaptain as Head of Commercial for global API business and Generic Formulations in select emerging markets
items.quote: I am very pleased to announce the appointment of Vishal Nayyar as Head of Supply Chain Management and Amit Kaptain as Head of Commercial for our global API business as well as for Generic Formulations in select emer ging markets

items.statement: Biocon Biologics appointed Dwight Hanshew as new Chief Quality Officer with over 30 years global leadership experience across Operations, Quality and R&D; most recently Head of Quality for Cipla in United States
items.quote: delighted to announce the appointment of Dwight Hanshew as its new Chief Quality Officer this quarter. Dwight brings with him over 30 years of global leadership, experience and expertise across Operations, Quality and R&D. And most recently, he was the Head of Quality for Cipla in the United States.

items.statement: Targets 30-40% revenue growth over FY24 and mid-teens EBITDA margin in FY25
items.quote: So we are looking at something like 30 % to 40% increase on the FY23 -24 sales numbers, but there's going to be a substantial increase on the profitability primarily because we've improved on a lot of parameters which includes manpower utilization, which includes revision of our contractual rates with our customers, which includes a little reduction in the overall raw material prices, giving us th

items.statement: Firm order book of INR110 crore for FY25, execution starting Q1
items.quote: So, we have an order book of about INR110 crores for the current financial year.

items.statement: Current utilization 30-35%, targeting 70-80% in next 2 years with minimal capex except moulds
items.quote: All in all, we are working to improving our capacity utilization, which is at about 30 %-35% overall. And some new clients are being added, as I mentioned, and our target is to have maximum capacity utilization, at least 70% to 80% of it in the next 2 years. And this would not involve much of a capex, except certain moulds that we might have to make specific to the requirement of our customers.

items.statement: New product categories beyond oral care will require capex for packaging lines; toothbrush capacity expansion needs only 5-8% mould cost
items.quote: Yes, that will require some capex. In terms of packaging lines, because it's going to be unique to each one of the products that we get. Some of the brands sell in pouches, some brands sell in bottles, some sell in pumps. So, each one of them have different packaging styles. So, that's probably we'll need to invest in.

items.statement: Expects healthy double-digit EBITDA margin in FY25 driven by price increases, cost reductions, operational efficiencies and volume leverage
items.quote: So considering all this added with the increased sales, I think we should be in a healthy double digit number on the EBITDA margins in the current financial year.

items.statement: Added Reliance (toothbrush, toothpaste, mouthwash), Unilever (Close-up toothpaste), Amway, Nycil (Zydus); CSD/CPC sales up 40%; no customer >25% of revenue
items.quote: We've got some new clients added. Reliance is one of the clients with whom we've started domestic sales to their retail stores and also the GT, the general trade division that they've opened is something that we'll be supplying to subsequen tly because the same products are being approved for the GT sales

items.statement: Exports recovering from 1-2% of sales; shifted payment terms from 180-day credit to documents through bank on fixed tenure; targeting global private label shows
items.quote: Apart from this, we've also renewed our focus back on exports, which during the COVID times had taken a major hit and from almost 25% of our sales to 1 or 2% of our sales, the export sales had dropped, which has started looking up again with a decent profit margin.

items.statement: Average credit period reduced from ~100 days to ~60 days; export credit cut from 180 to 45 days; some domestic from 90 to 60 days; supplier credit extended from 30 to 45 days
items.quote: So, earlier in exports, we were giving about 180 days credit, which is down to 45. There were a lot of our customers, which were at 90 days, we brought them down to 60 days. So, our average credit period is now down to, I would say, from a high of 100 days to about 60 days on an average.

items.statement: 50% contracts have price pass-through, 50% fixed annual; secured price increases by justifying input cost inflation (labour, electricity)
items.quote: 50% I would say are price pass-on contracts and 50% are full year fixed contracts.

items.statement: FY24 revenue mix: 60% toothbrush, 30% toothpaste, 10% talcum/mouthwash/tongue cleaners; toothbrush share up from 57% toothpaste previously
items.quote: So, in current financial year '24, 60% of our revenues are driven from the toothbrush segment, while 30% coming in from the toothpaste segment. Rest of the revenues are from the new segment, which is the talcum powder coupled with mouthwash and tongue cleaners.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisitions in broader personal care (creams, lotions, soaps, shampoos) using cash and stock; no more mergers
items.quote: We are now looking at acquisitions very actively and we are very confident that in the current financial year, we will be able to do a substantial acquisition with whatever cash that the company holds currently and maybe some stock.

items.statement: Added senior team members and new marketing team; hiring young talent for unconventional sales channels
items.quote: We've also added a few senior team members in our company, which has seen a change in the overall outlook in terms of the deliveries, in terms of capacity utilization, in terms of order book.

items.statement: Oral care market INR15,000 crore dominated by 5 players (85% share); JHS now supplies to 3 of top 5 (Colgate, P&G historically, now Unilever, Reliance)
items.quote: So as you would know that oral care as a category is about INR15,000 crores in India, and it is predominantly dominated by four big companies, which is Colgate number one, Oral-B number two, Dar bar number three, Unilever number four. So four of these companies and fifth Sensodyne, which is GSK now, Haleon, together five of these own about 85% of the market.

items.statement: CSD (canteen stores) sales up 40%; now among top 7 brands sold in CSD
items.quote: There also, the sales have improved. We've increased the sales and profitability specific to that section by about 40%.

items.statement: Past over-dependence on P&G (70% revenue) led to plant stranding; now consciously limiting each customer to <25% of sales
items.quote: We've consciously kept all our customers less than 25% of our sales. None of them wou ld be now more than 25%, like P& G at one point in 2012 -2013 and INR180 crores revenue was close to 70

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20-22% for next 3 years
items.quote: We expect to maintain the momentum of revenue growth of 20% – 22% going forward as well for the next 3 years.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target of 12-13%
items.quote: We are confident of maintaining long-term EBITDA margin at 12% to 13% from the operations, which we have guided historically.

items.statement: Interest cost expected to reduce by Rs 5-6 Crores
items.quote: We expect the interest cost to further go down as I said because the arbitration money was only used in the February and March months to repay the banks. So we expect the interest cost to be further reduced by Rs 5 Crores to Rs 6 Crores going forward as well.

items.statement: Interest cost guidance of Rs 25-26 Crores for FY25
items.quote: We expect the interest cost in this year to be almost Rs 25 Crores – Rs 26 Crores.

items.statement: Net unexecuted order book of Rs 3,099 Crores as of April 1, 2024
items.quote: As of April 1, 2024, we have a net unexecuted order book of almost Rs 3,099 Crores, with order inflow for the year being Rs 1,841 Crores amounting to almost 3.02x our FY'24 revenues, thus providing strong visibility to the management.

items.statement: L1 in Rs 700 Crores of new orders expected post elections
items.quote: we are L1 in almost Rs 700 Crores of new orders, which we expect to be finalized post the Code of Conduct of the general GPT Infraprojects Limited M ay 21, 2024 elections being over

items.statement: Long-term book-to-bill ratio target of 3x
items.quote: Going forward, we expect to maintain long-term book-to-bill ratio of almost 3x.

items.statement: Concrete sleeper order book of Rs 222 Crores executable over 1.5 years
items.quote: So the concrete sleeper segment has an outstanding order book of Rs 222 Crores that is to be executed over the next 1.5 years.

items.statement: Concrete sleeper segment peak revenue capacity of Rs 250 Crores
items.quote: At the peak this segment can generate revenues of close to Rs 250 Crores.

items.statement: Ghana factory technical approval received, revenue booking expected from Q2 FY25
items.quote: We expect the company, the subsidiary to start booking revenue in the second quarter of this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin threshold of 13% maintained for bidding discipline
items.quote: We have a very strict discipline in terms of maintaining our EBITDA margin. Our EBITDA margin is in the range of 12.5% - 13%, and we will be able to maintain that threshold.

items.statement: Both infrastructure and sleeper segments have comparable EBITDA margins of ~13%
items.quote: It's almost comparable at 13%.

items.statement: Debt reduced to Rs 186 Crores, further reduction expected from strong cash flows
items.quote: In terms of the debt position, you're right, it is at almost Rs 186 Crores. Like I said in my opening remarks, we expect to further reduce the debt from the strong cash flow that the management has.

items.statement: CRISIL credit rating upgraded from BBB+ to A- in February 2024
items.quote: As you are aware, we have already informed the stock exchanges earlier that the external rating agency, CRISIL, has upgraded the external rating -- or credit rating of the company in February 2024 from BBB+ to A-.

items.statement: Contract assets reduced by ~30% despite revenue growth
items.quote: The management has been able to reduce the contract assets by almost 30% despite the increase in volume of business, thus evidencing more optimized balance sheet, which is reflecting in the return ratios.

items.statement: Target working capital days in double digits
items.quote: We have been able to keep the working capital days also closer to double digits, which will be the long-term target as well.

items.statement: Trade payables decreased by Rs 10 Crores vs Rs 61 Crores increase last year
items.quote: If you see last year, as a number, trade payables on a stand-alone basis increased by Rs 61 Crores. This year, it has decreased by almost Rs 10 Crores. So that Rs 70 Crores delta is coming from the trade payable number only.

items.statement: Target payable days of ~2 months for better supplier pricing
items.quote: So the idea is to maintain a reasonable payable day of almost 2 months so that we get better pricing from the suppliers as well as better -- they also want to work with us.

items.statement: Bonus issue 1:1 and total dividend of Rs 3 per share (30%) for FY24
items.quote: The Board has recommended has already announced a bonus issue of equity shares in the proportion of 1:1 by capitalizing the reserves of the company. The company has also declared a third interim dividend of Re. 1 per share, that is 10%. The total dividend for the year will be Rs 3 per share, that is 30%.

items.statement: International revenue ~2% (Rs 20 Crores) in FY24, targeting 7-8% in FY25
items.quote: It's only 2%-odd percent currently, about Rs 20-odd Crores last year. We expect this year to be much stronger to be almost 7% – 8%.

items.statement: No EPC business outside India, only product exports
items.quote: Yes, we don't -- no, we don't do EPC outside the country.

items.statement: Competition not affecting order inflow; Rs 1,840 Crores new orders in FY24
items.quote: Given the increase in the volume of business and the opportunities available even if more people do enter the field, there is no challenge in terms of new contracts that can be procured. So, that is not affecting our inflow of orders. Like I said, we are at an all-time high in terms of new orders that we procured last year of Rs 1,840 Crores.

items.statement: Key risk is government infrastructure focus deviation
items.quote: Obviously, this is subject to government having a focus on the infrastructure sector which we don't think that the focus will be different. So that is one of the major risks that always will be there. If the government's focus on infrastructure deviates, then obviously the pipeline will shrink.

items.statement: Cash flow to EBITDA conversion at 103%
items.quote: Our cash flow from operations to EBITDA conversion continues to be strong and stands at an industry-leading 103% conversion.

items.statement: ROE and ROCE north of 20%
items.quote: This has led to both ROE and ROCE being north of 20% for the year, and we expect to maintain the same going forward as well.

items.statement: Currently bidding for projects up to Rs 900-1000 Crores, largest won Rs 740 Crores
items.quote: So we are already bidding for projects upto Rs 900 Crores – Rs 1000 Crores. And for the largest contract that we got last year was Rs 740 Crores from NHAI.

items.statement: Insurance surety bonds used as alternative to bank BGs for bidding
items.quote: In terms of bidding opportunities, we have the flexibility of also using these insurance surety bonds as well. The government has allowed most of the government departments nowadays except these surety bonds, like NHAI, MORTH, etc.

items.statement: Management expects 12-15% volume growth for FY25
items.quote: And at the end of the -- on a full year basis, yes, definitely, you can expect around 12% to 15% volume growth.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is around INR300 crores, predominantly for vehicles
items.quote: Yes, since to grow at around again, 12% to 15% growth in tonnage, definitely we n eed to have a capex in the range of around INR300 crores

items.statement: Branch addition target for FY25 is around 100-plus branches, with most in Q1
items.quote: Yes. More branches is in Q1 and in subsequent period, there will be lesser additions. And on a full year basis, definitely it will be in the range of around 100-plus branches.

items.statement: South zone tonnage grew only 2% in FY24 due to poor monsoon; north 15%, east 20%, northeast 25%
items.quote: On an origination basis, actually, south zone contributed around -- growth is around 2% and the north is around 15% and east is around 20%, nort heast is around 25% and the rest is around 10

items.statement: Textile segment grew 6% in FY24, expected 14-15% in FY25; agro grew 4-5%, expected double digits in FY25
items.quote: we are expecting that the textile which was impacted in the last year, again, the growth in textile we are expecting at least around 14% to 15% in the current year. That's one. And agro commodities, still the improvement is not there because the rainy season is yet to start now. So since most of the reports are giving positive outlook on the monsoon in the current year, we are expecting that defin

items.statement: EBITDA margin fell YoY due to higher employee cost (15.4% to 16.6% of revenue), rent, toll, repair costs; fuel cost fell 31% to 29% of revenue
items.quote: The key changes in the operational costs, which are reasons to decrease in EBITDA margins are: the major impact i s on account of increase in employee cost. The employee cost as a percentage to the total revenue increased by around from 15.4% to 16.6

items.statement: Sequential EBITDA margin improved from 13% to 14% in Q4 due to lower fuel cost (30% to 29% of revenue) and lower employee cost percentage
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has increased from 13% to 14% and the improvements in EBITDA margin is on account of the decrease in fuel costs, which is a major cost in our operations.

items.statement: Management targets return to 16-17% EBITDA margin (post Ind AS) if tonnage grows 12-15%
items.quote: Even if the tonnage growth, say, at least around 12%, 15%, then again, our EBITDA margin is around 16%, 17%.

items.statement: Freight rates linked to fuel rates; no rate hike taken as fuel rates stable; fuel cost benefit retained, not passed to customers
items.quote: No, basically, the thought process is very clear because the freight rates are directly linked with the fuel rates. So it all depends on the movement in the fuel rates. And if a substantial increase in the fuel rate, then definitely, we look forward to increase the freight rates along with to take care of increase in other expenses.

items.statement: Customer base grew from 8 lakh to 9 lakh in FY24 due to shift from unorganized to organized transport and GST compliance
items.quote: Further, our customer base has increased from 8 lakh customers at the beginning of the financial year to 9 lakh customers by end of the year due to shift from dependency on the unorga nized transport service providers to organized transport service providers on account of better service level and also increase in GST compliances

items.statement: Own vehicle capacity reached 86,405 tons as of March 31, 2024; added 83 branches in FY24, 184 in FY23
items.quote: With this, our own vehicle capacity has reached to around 86,405 tons capacity as at 31st March 2024.

items.statement: Trailers currently 25-30 ton capacity; target 10% of total carrying capacity via trailers; 15-20 of 50 hubs trailer-enabled
items.quote: So that's the reason, instead of calculating based on the number of trailers, I can say that at least around in the near future, we may reach around 10% of overall carrying capacity what we are having, it will be through trailers.

items.statement: Net debt rose from INR167 crores to INR262 crores YoY; fell sequentially from INR271 crores to INR262 crores; FY25 debt not expected to rise above current level due to strong cash flows (INR350-400 crores free cash flow)
items.quote: See, even with capital expenditure of INR300 crores, our debt level will not increase from the current level. The reason is we are having good cash flows. And on a periodical basis, there will be some movement. So if we decide to add more vehicle in this quarter, the debt will increase to some extent. And again, it will normalize in the subsequent quarter. Again, debt level will come down. Since w

items.statement: Employee count up 1,132 YoY due to branch expansion and more drivers for own vehicles; employee cost rose from INR108 crores to INR128 crores
items.quote: The number of employees also increased by around 1,132 numbers as compared to the last year and mainly in -- on account of expansion in branch network and also due to increase in number of drivers because the number of own vehicles are increased.

items.statement: Competition increasing from express players offering non-time-sensitive rates and local operators; VRL responding with aggressive branch expansion in untapped markets
items.quote: And aggressively in the current year, actually, most of the branches we are planning to open in quarter 1 only because we identified those places and those are very potential areas where actually we can enhance our business in those locations.

items.statement: Realization per ton up 1% YoY to INR6,724 due to route mix change; freight rates unchanged as fuel rates stable
items.quote: During the quarter, there was an increase in total realization per ton by around 1% from INR6,650 to INR6,724. The increase is mainly on account of change in route mix in our overall operations.

items.statement: Fuel procurement cost fell from INR89 to INR87 per liter YoY; bulk purchase share rose from 28% to 31%
items.quote: The reduction in fuel cost is mainly on account of decrease in average fuel procurement cost from INR89 it was there in Q4 FY '23 now it has been reduced to INR87 in Q4 of FY '24. And also the bulk purchase of the fuel from the refineries a t a discounted price is increased from 28% to 31% in the current quarter

items.statement: April-May operations impacted by driver and labor shortage due to general elections; issue resolving as elections complete
items.quote: However, in quarter 1 of the current year, in April and May period, we faced some performance impact because of some disturbances in our operations on account of short in attendance by the drivers and loading and unloading labors, especially in the metro cities like Chennai, Bangalore, Pune, Ahmedabad, et cetera.

items.statement: Operating under 5% GST reverse charge mechanism; evaluated 12% forward charge but found 5% reverse charge more beneficial after customer survey and government consultation
items.quote: We examined this option. In fact, we are closely working with the government ministry also. And the thing here that we analyze, we made a survey of our customers and everything. And based on that outcome, what rate we are already practicing, at 5% on a reverse charge, that is beneficial to us compared to the 12%.

items.statement: Focusing on trailer additions (25-30 ton capacity) to reduce hub waiting time, improve driver utilization and turnaround; planning larger trailers for long routes like Delhi-Bangalore
items.quote: As mentioned in the presentation, we are concentrating more on addition of trailers in our fleet that will result into increase in turnaround time of the vehicles and the increase in the utilization of drivers, etcetera.

items.statement: Free cash flow estimated at INR350-400 crores annually, supporting capex without increasing debt
items.quote: Since we are having the cash flows of almost close to around INR350 crores to INR400 crores as our free cash flows, so that will support to add this capex.

items.statement: Capex plan for next two years is roughly Rs 80-100 crore, focused on manufacturing capability improvement and product development/innovation.
items.quote: Roughly, we are looking about 80 to 100 crores. This will be largely towards manufacturing capability improvement, also behind product development and product innovation.

items.statement: ECD EBIT margin improved from 12.7% in Q1 FY24 to 17.2% in Q4 FY24 (excluding EPR impact of Rs 14.1 crore).
items.quote: ECD EBIT margins have consistently increased during the year from 12.7% in Q1 FY24 to 17.2% in Q4. Again, the Q4 number excludes the EPR impact because obviously that is the entire impact of EPR has been taken in one quarter.

items.statement: Lighting EBIT margin is at 11.1% excluding EPR impact.
items.quote: Lighting EBIT even as we are coming back to a stable lighting business in the face of declining prices in the market , has remained very strong. So, lighting EBIT margin is at 11.1% , again, excluding the EPR impact.

items.statement: Fans gross margins improved from about 23% in Q1 to about 25% in Q4 FY24.
items.quote: this is of course, also enabled us to improve our gross margins in fans and they have gone up order of magnitude from about 23% to about 25% this quarter - 23% in Q1 to about 25% in this quarter.

items.statement: Butterfly long-term target is double-digit EBIT margin; near-term focus is to restore growth and return to category EBIT margins of 1-2 years ago.
items.quote: In the long run we should look at a double digit margin for this business, Renu, but in the near term we want to get this back on growth, get into a category EBIT margin that the business used to operate say 1-2 years back and then expand from there.

items.statement: Demand outlook for summer is reasonably good and robust, despite some recent rains.
items.quote: Insofar as the outlook for the summer is concerned, actually the demand outlook has been reasonably good. There have been some rains the last few days, but other than that the demand outlook has be en quite

items.statement: Solar pumps secured fresh orders of Rs 87 crore in Q4, total empanelment for the year ~Rs 122 crore; pipeline of Rs 85+ crore orders to be executed plus Rs 35 crore already executed in Q4.
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured fresh orders of 87 crores making our total empanelment for the year of about 122 crores. Needless to say, we have therefore a strong pipeline going forward.

items.statement: Butterfly revenue was Rs 166 crore in Q4 with EBITDA loss of Rs 20 crore, impacted by transition and one-offs.
items.quote: This quarter the revenue of Butterfly came in at 166 crores. The EBITDA was -20 crores and you can tell that the transition is having an impact , and one off s are having an impact on the EBITDA there.

items.statement: Premium saliency improved YoY by 300 bps overall; ceiling fans +380 bps, lighting +410 bps in large domestic appliances; premium fans mix improved from 1 in 5 to >1 in 4.
items.quote: We witnessed an improvement in premium saliency YoY of 3 percentage points, that is 300 basis points . In ceiling fans, 380 basis points in lighting, and 410 basis points in large domestic appliances .To put our premiumization journey in fans in perspective, a year ago we were selling one out of five premium fans. Now, we are probably selling more than one out of every four fans.

items.statement: Fans volume grew strong double-digit in Q4 and full year FY24; premium fans growing at ~2x overall category growth; non-ceiling fans (TPW, exhaust, DOMEX) also strong double-digit growth.
items.quote: we do see from a category perspective, premium fans are growing at almost a 2x of the overall category growth for fans has been growing in. In terms of mass premium or the value segment is concerned, if I look at our overall fans performance on the market share also, it's reflecting that we are moving in the right direction. Equally important to look at non-ceiling as a category. So today we see t

items.statement: Took measured price increases in fans (Sept, Nov, Feb, and another upcoming), pumps, LDA and SDA; cost savings via Unnati program contributing to margin improvement.
items.quote: We are continuing to take both measured price increases sometimes or even frequently, not the approach that the rest of the industry is taking, but we are taking them and we are working on costs. So, yes, I remain quite positive about the way margins will evolve going forward.

items.statement: A&P spend increased 49% YoY to Rs 217 crore (3.14% of revenue vs 2.5% last year); R&D spend Rs 71 crore with 85 design registrations, 17 patent applications, 10 patents granted.
items.quote: During the year A &P spends were 217 crores, which was about 3.14% of our revenue versus about 2.5% of revenue last year. That's about 1.1% higher and that is a structural change that we have done and like I said before, our A &P spends are up about 49% over the last year.

items.statement: Alternate channels (e-commerce, MOR, rural) now ~20% of overall sales; e-commerce recorded >Rs 100 crore sales for second consecutive quarter; rural channel grew 23%; exports crossed Rs 100 crore for first time.
items.quote: reported last quarter that they account now for about 20% of overall sales. Make no mistake, it's very, very important for an organization like us to have a great mix of channels because that is the secret to profitability. So, while we are investing in alternate channels, which are areas like ecom merce, MOR, rural, we are very clear we also are continuing to invest a piece in our general trade c

items.statement: Cash flow from operations was 130% of PBT in FY24 vs 72% last year.
items.quote: During the year, cash flow from operation was 130% of PBT, which compares with about 72% cash conversion last year.

items.statement: Solar pumps cash flow cycle is very good; for bulk of orders executed last year, money is in the bank.
items.quote: The profit profile in solar pumps is very good and as is the cash flow cycle. So, for a large bulk of the orders that we executed last year, the money is in the bank.

items.statement: EPR liability of Rs 14.1 crore (standalone) and Rs 15.2 crore (consol) fully accrued in Q4 FY24.
items.quote: Standalone 14.1 crores and 15.2 crores consol. It is also there in the press release that we have made. Kaleeswaran A. And that is a fully a liability accrued in Q4

items.statement: Sweta Sagar joined as Chief Business Officer, Butterfly (~1 month ago); 20 years experience across Versuni, Hindustan Coca-Cola, Hutchison Essar.
items.quote: I'll quickly introduce Sweta Sagar who we have just announced as the Chief Business Officer, who has joined us in about a month ago now almost and she's just been announced as the Chief Business Officer for Butterfly a couple of days ago. She is no stranger to kitchen appliances, has about 20 years of experience much of it Versuni and also at Hindustan Coca-Cola, Hutchison Essar, and a few other n

items.statement: Butterfly merger plan did not work out; transition underway with management strengthening, policy alignment, channel de-risking (institution/corporate), manufacturing reorganization (surrendered one facility).
items.quote: As you recall to merge Butterfly that didn't work out. So, we are moving on. A transition is well underway in Butterfly and we are strengthening the management there. Sweta joining is one of the key elements of that. You will continue to see some of this going forward. We are also in the process of making various interventions, aligning of policies at Butterfly ensuring that the revenue recognitio

items.statement: Fans sales crossed 2 crore units per annum for the first time; strong double-digit growth for three consecutive quarters post-pandemic.
items.quote: We have also crossed the milestone by some margin of selling 2 crore fa ns per annum for the first time. We have had strong double-digit growth in fans in our portfolio for the first time since the pandemic. items.statement: Post-moratorium govt liabilities (from Sep-25): plan to convert eligible installments per reforms package; non-convertible portion to be met from operational cash generation
items.quote: In FY26 and FY27, we will probably be looking at the conversion of the installments which are convertible as per the reforms package. That is what we are currently looking at.

items.statement: Ranked 15th across industries and 1st in telecom in Business Today's 'Best Companies to Work For in India'
items.quote: I am proud to share that we have been recognized as one of the ‘Best Companies to Work For in India’ by the Business Today magazine in its recent publication. We have attained rank 15 across industries in India and rank 1 in the telec om industry

items.statement: Subscriber loss driven by 4G coverage gap; aim to stop loss and grow share in 12-15 months via coverage expansion; capacity decongestion in 2-3 months
items.quote: First thing we have to achieve is that we should stop the loss of subscribers and we should start growing.

items.statement: International roaming: unlimited packs across 29 countries (70% of IR traffic); added 27 new countries including Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Iraq
items.quote: Vi is the only operator in the country to offer unlimited packs across a vast expanse of 29 countries that contributes to 70% of the international roaming traffic.

items.statement: Revised full-year FY25 EBITDA margin guidance to 24%-28% due to investments in sales and delivery capabilities
items.quote: These investments will result in a n impact of about 400 bps to EBITDA. So , we are revising the range for full year EBITDA to 24% to 28%.

items.statement: Aspiration for double-digit revenue growth in FY25
items.quote: Absolutely, aspiration. Why wouldn't we aspire for double-digit. Our aspirations are higher, so.

items.statement: Expect Q1 FY25 to be the lowest margin quarter due to wage hikes and full impact of Q4 investments
items.quote: So, you would expect that Q1 will be the quarter of the lowest margin, predominantly because of wage hikes and the full impact of the investments that we have made in Q4 that will hit Q1, and any additional investment that we might do.

items.statement: Target to be in top quartile for both growth and EBITDA margins over 4-year strategy period
items.quote: Our 4-year aspirations are that we want to be in a top quadrant on growth and [with] industry-leading margins.

items.statement: Adding office space in Mumbai, Pune, and Chandigarh; new spaces go live in about 6 months
items.quote: We are also taking up additional space in 3 cities we operate. These investments will result in a n impact of about 400 bps to EBITDA.

items.statement: Opened new office in Switzerland to serve clients in that geography
items.quote: We opened a new office in Switzerland to be able to serve clients in that geography.

items.statement: Seat count reduced due to giving up Gurugram office; will add seats in Mumbai, Pune, Chandigarh over next few months
items.quote: The seat count has reduced because we gave up an office in Gurugram. But as Kapil mentioned, we will be adding seats in Mumbai, Pune, Chandigarh over the next few months and seat count will increase.

items.statement: New deal ACV for FY24 was USD 91 million, up 10% from USD 82 million in FY23
items.quote: New deal ACV for the year was USD 91 million, up 10% from FY '23, which was USD 82 million.

items.statement: Pipeline is healthy across all three businesses entering FY25
items.quote: Our pipeline is healthy across all 3 businesses as we get into FY '24/'25.

items.statement: Strong demand in Financial Markets and Customer Operations driven by compliance offerings, client lifecycle management, and transaction volumes
items.quote: We saw strong demand around our compliance offerings, client life cycle management f rom several clients. We also saw an increase in transaction volumes.

items.statement: Digital business soft in Q4 due to slow 2024 budget allocations; expect some momentum in Q1 but environment remains cautious
items.quote: It was a soft quarter for Digital with clients starting slowly with their 2024 budget allocations and renewals. We expect momentum to make up a little bit in Q1, but overall environment continues to be cautious for the digital business.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin was 28.1%; sequential decline in Q4 due to investments in sales and delivery capabilities
items.quote: There is a sequential decline in margin in this quarter, primarily going to our investments in strengthening our sales and delivery capabilities. For the full year, we delivered an EBITDA of 28.1 %.

items.statement: Subcontracting costs expected to remain in 2%-2.5% range depending on project ramp-up needs
items.quote: So sub-contracting cost should remain in the same range , between 2 -2.5 specifically in every quarter depends on what kind of search volume that we get, what kind of projects we get that we have to ramp up in a very short period of time.

items.statement: Willing to offer competitive pricing on strategic deals to gain market share; market will determine price
items.quote: Because my view always has been you lose a deal, you lose a deal forever. So, we need to be competitive and see how we deliver, and market will determine the price [at which] we should do business.

items.statement: BPaaS business grew 4% YoY to USD 86 million, primarily from Financial Markets; Analytics and Automation declined 8% YoY to USD 65 million due to client challenges and reduced discretionary spending
items.quote: Our BPaaS business has grown by 4% Y-o-Y to USD 86 million. This has primarily come from the Financial Markets business. Our Analytics and Automation business at USD 65 million has shown an 8% Y-o-Y decline because business challenges faced by some of our clients and reduction in discretionary spending.

items.statement: Top 10 client concentration increased due to Personiv client roll-off (outside top 10) and strong growth in existing Financial Markets and Customer Operations clients
items.quote: Top 10 client concentration has gone up, partly because of the roll off of the client in Personiv, which was outside the top 10, and partly because of the strong growth in existing clients in customer operations and finan cial markets.

items.statement: Exit headcount up ~270 QoQ; attrition increased from 16% to 22%, still below normal operating range
items.quote: Headcount, i.e. exit headcount, is up by about 270 people over the previous quarter, [and] while attrition is up from 16% to 22%, it is still some way away from the range that we usually operate in.

items.statement: DSO at ~84 days, higher than previous quarter but in line with Q4 last year
items.quote: DSO is about 84 days, higher than the previous quarter, but in line with Q4 of last year.

items.statement: Cash and investible surplus of ~INR 1,100 crores; announced buyback of INR 385 crores and dividend of INR 1 per share subject to approvals
items.quote: We have about INR 1100 crores of cash on our books and in line with the usual practice of returning excess cash to shareholders, we have announced a buyback of INR 385 crores and a dividend of INR 1, subject to shareholder approvals.

items.statement: M&A strategy continues, focusing on complementary capabilities and capability access; dedicated person handling outbound and inbound targets
items.quote: On the M&A, yes, that continues to be our strategy. We would be looking at areas where we bring in complementary and that also helps us on our capability access. So that's what we will continue, and we have a dedicated person who is looking at outbound as well as inbound M&A targets.

items.statement: Revenue growth in USD terms: 1.5% QoQ in Q4 to USD 91.9M; 6.4% YoY for FY24 to USD 353.9M, exceeding industry average
items.quote: For the full year, our revenue in USD terms grew by 6.4% Y-o-Y to USD 353.9 million, exceeding the industry average .

items.statement: Net profit for FY24 up 4.6% to INR 5,115 million
items.quote: Net profit for FY '24 was up 4.6% to INR 5,115 million.

items.statement: Revenue concentration in volatile industries (retail, financial markets) but balanced portfolio manages risk; pricing pressure expected when gaining market share
items.quote: As you know that there is a revenue concentration across volatile industry because the re tail, financial markets have higher volatility than some of the evergreen industries. But our portfolio and balanced portfolio allows us to manage their risk. And obviously, we want to gain market share. So, there will be some pricing pressure on the deals.

items.statement: Renewable electricity share in India offices increased from 32% to 68% over last year; awarded Ecovadis bronze medal (top 35% sustainability reporting)
items.quote: Across our India offices, the share of electricity from renewable sources has increased from 32% to 68% over the last year. And we have been awarded the bronze medal by Ecovadis, which places us in the top 35% of sustainability reporting across 1000+ companies.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 10% to 10.5% reiterated
items.quote: We are evaluating pricing actions in some products, which combined with some further initiatives should aid us in bringing EBITDA margins back to the range of 10% to 10.5% that we have indicated earlier.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 100 crores for FY25
items.quote: Capex, there's no change in the guidance, whatever we said last time. We probably see about INR100 crores of capex in the coming year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 310 bps YoY and 40 bps QoQ in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Gross margins continue to improve. In this quarter, we have reported an improvement of 310 basis points Y -o-Y and 40 basis points Q -on-Q.

items.statement: Consumer Durables EBITDA margin at 3% in Q4 FY24, target pre-COVID levels of 6-7%
items.quote: Sudarshan Kasturi: EBITDA was 3%. Mithun K Chittilappilly: So I think this was something like 7% or 6% pre -COVID. That's where the main drop has happened.

items.statement: Strong summer demand in South and East drove 18.6% YoY growth in South markets in Q4
items.quote: In terms of geographies, we witnessed a top line growth of 18.6% Y -o-Y in Q4 in the South market, while the non-South market grew by 15.8% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: April 2024 fan sales decent; air coolers and stabilizers grew stronger due to harsh summer
items.quote: However, I have to say that the growth in certain other categories like air coolers and voltage stabilizers has been stronger than fans because the summer has been very, very harsh at least in Southern and East part.

items.statement: Non-summer categories like wires seeing uptick due to copper price rise; other non-summer categories flat
items.quote: Yes. for non-summer products, I think, right now see, like I mentioned, only wires, we are seeing an uptick because of the increase in copper prices. So it may be too early to call it out; so far, we are not seeing much of a change in demand for non-summer categories.

items.statement: Pricing actions initiated in fans and pumps in April (~2% realized); further actions planned for May
items.quote: Maybe about 2% has flown through in maybe fan. And maybe in May, we expect in pump.

items.statement: Commodity costs bottomed out in Nov-Dec 2023; copper rise impacts fans and pumps; aluminium stable
items.quote: But definitely, I think, as of now, maybe a 1% or 2% impact is there. But having said that, we have already taken some pricing increases in categories like fan and pumps because of this.

items.statement: In-house manufacturing at 65%, targeting 75% in next 12-18 months as new factories scale
items.quote: On the current manufacturing status, in-house is about 65%. With all the new factories that are coming online, we probably expect it to go to about 75-odd-percent in the next 18 months or so.

items.statement: Battery and kitchen appliance factories commenced commercial production; benefits expected in FY25
items.quote: The battery and kitchen appliances factories, which recently commenced commercial production are expected to deliver benefits during the coming year.

items.statement: TPW fan factory in Hyderabad to be completed in 18-24 months for premium TPW manufacturing
items.quote: And we are also in the process of setting up our own factory for TPW for making the premium end of TPW fans in Hyderabad, which should get completed in the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Sunflame revenue grew 28.3% YoY in Q4 FY24; integration progressing with focus on e-commerce and South
items.quote: Sunflame also delivered robust growth in top line of 28.3% on a Y -o-Y basis in Q4 leveraging on our various strategic initiatives implemented over the last year.

items.statement: Electronics margin impacted by product mix shift to AC stabilizers and EPR charge on batteries in Q4
items.quote: For example, in Q3, we sell more of smaller, lower KVA that are refrigerator and television stabilizers. Whereas in fourth quarter, it will be largely air conditioner, stabilizers. So, there is a mix impact there. I think there's also an EPR impact coming in fourth quarter.

items.statement: Water heater premium model Pebble Neo launched end of FY24; next premium models in 18 months
items.quote: So I think in case of water heaters, we have launched a face lifted version of our premium range call Pebble. It's called Pebble Neo, it's a digital model. So that has just got launched at the fag -end of last financial year.

items.statement: Direct retail placement in modern trade without bulk deals to protect pricing; 22% direct channel share vs market 35%
items.quote: We are placing our product into stores and we are replenishing them based on uptick, because that's the only way that we can protect our price positioning.

items.statement: Total retail outlets touched nearly 100,000 as of March 2024 vs earlier estimate of 40,000-50,000
items.quote: So we have now in the last 1 year have completed scan of the number of outlets we are present in, and I think it's now touching almost 1 lakh as we speak.

items.statement: Direct partners count ~3,500 (10-15% distributors, 80-85% direct dealers/wholesalers)
items.quote: See, the total direct partners, what we have is about 3,500 -odd people. That includes 10% to 15% of that are distributors and about 80%, 85% are direct dealers.

items.statement: Fan pricing pressure from competitors not proactive on price hikes; demand environment may enable pass-through
items.quote: All that has grown, but we have found it extremely difficult to pass prices because some of the competitors are not very proactive about increasing prices. But I think with this kind of demand environment and this kind of a summer hopefully, this should be through.

items.statement: EPR charge on batteries ~INR 70 lakhs in Q4; calculated on weight and useful life
items.quote: Yes, Achal. It's not major. It's only about INR70 lakhs for battery. So that's not a big factor. The major factor is the product mix, which Mithun spoke about.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR 1.4 per equity share (face value INR 1) recommended for FY24
items.quote: The Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of INR1.4 per equity share of INR1 each for financial year '24.

items.statement: Sunflame integration includes investments in people, technology, and ATL marketing
items.quote: We might make investments in the business and our systems and ways of working will also involve focus on many areas, which may not have been focused on earlier. So there may be some investment in people and some investment in technology that we'll have to factor. And there will be some investment on ATL, right?

items.statement: Commodity price flare-up evolving; copper at $10,500/ton; pricing actions may not fully offset if shocks are steep
items.quote: But definitely, commodity price increase will have an impact on the margins. The only product where this is a positive is wires. So when copper prices go up, there is a tendency by retailers to upstock wires.

items.statement: Gegadyne Energy Labs investment for next-gen battery tech; meaningful revenue in 24-30 months
items.quote: I think maybe it's at least another 24 to 30 months away before we can be able to derive meaningful revenue out of the technology.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain in 13%-15% range
items.quote: the entire range from 13%-15% is the standard industry range where we continue to be a part of. And this will continue to be the same within this particular span of EBITDA margins that we are discussing

items.statement: CapEx planned for next financial year to build capacities for certain products
items.quote: In the second aspect we plan to do cert ain amount of CapEx, also for the subsequent financial year, that is the next financial year where we will start building up on certain capacities for certain products within this financial year

items.statement: Dividend of 25% announced in last board meeting
items.quote: definitely we have already announced a dividend of 25% in the last board meeting last week for the shareholders

items.statement: Net debt reduced by around INR 20 crore to INR 55 crore
items.quote: net debt is reduced by around INR 20 crore. Total borrowing is INR 115 crore vs INR 109 crore. And if you deduct cash and bank bal ance it is INR 60 crore. So, if you deduct cash and bank balance net debt has come to INR 55 crore

items.statement: Comfortable working capital level; no additional funds needed for working capital cycle
items.quote: we are already at a comfortable level in terms of the working capital that we are at. So, we will not be needing more additional funds to manage the working capital cycle

items.statement: Collective manufacturing capacity of more than 4,50,000 metric tons per annum across nine facilities
items.quote: With nine state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities and warehouses across India, including Gujarat, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, we have a collective manufacturing capacity of more than 4,50,000 metric tons per annum

items.statement: FY24 volume growth of 14% to 450,000 metric tons
items.quote: So, we had about 14% volume growth

items.statement: Value-added products contribute 20% of revenue; industrial minerals 80%
items.quote: So, about 20% comes from our value-added products and about 80% comes from our industrial minerals

items.statement: Calcium carbonate accounts for about 50% of revenue
items.quote: So about 50% of our revenue comes from calcium carbonate

items.statement: Kaolin contributes about 20% of revenue
items.quote: Yes, about 20% of revenue

items.statement: Currently using 50% in-house mining material and 50% procured externally for Kaolin
items.quote: we are currently using about 50% of our mining material in -house and 50% we are procuring from outside

items.statement: Export revenue INR 95 crore in FY24, 15% of total revenue
items.quote: We are at INR 95 crore

items.statement: Export value growth 5%-7% YoY; FOB/XWorks value growth 18%-20%
items.quote: value would seem quite less. It's about a 5 %-7% growth that you'll see on the overall value because some of the freights and some of the sectors which we were catering to, they have kind of changed. And because of that, our overall CIF value that we work on that has kind of gone down and because of that. But if you look at the FOB value, the XWorks value there, we have seen a significant growth o

items.statement: Supplying to JSW Paints regularly; started supplying to Grasim Paints with grades approved
items.quote: JSW has been our customer for quite a long time now since they've entered into the paint business, and we are supplying quite a few products to them on a regular basis. In terms of Grasim, who has recently entered into the paint business, we have already started supplying to them

items.statement: Formed joint venture with German company Sievert for construction chemicals
items.quote: we have r ecently joined hands with Sievert, which is a German -based company with expertise in construction chemicals and building -related materials

items.statement: Expect good growth from domestic sectors (paints, plastics, rubber, paper, ceramics) and international markets (Middle East, South Asia, Far East, Latin America)
items.quote: definitely see a good share of growth happening in these sectors. 20 Microns Limited - 8 - 21.05.2024 Q4 FY24 Earnings Conference Call Definitely we will be catering to that growth with the products that we already have and with the product we are planning to develop in the coming months

items.statement: Facing freight and container cost increases due to Red Sea issues and supply chain disruptions; export customers support temporary pricing, import costs harder to pass through
items.quote: Yes. To be very honest, we have been facing a lot, many issues since December, not only pertaining to the Red Sea. The Red Sea is just one of the factors which had kind to led the hike in the freights for our export markets

items.statement: Uncertainty in global economies and trade routes; Chinese products may get dumped in Asian markets due to anti-dumping duties in US/Europe
items.quote: we have to get ready for that in the coming future. So, that is the reason that we are gearing up to have better products than the Chinese products in most of the customers that we cater to

items.statement: R&D team of 45 to 30 people continuously focusing on innovation at Vadodara facility
items.quote: Our dedicated team of 45 to 30 people continuously focusing on innovation by developing a wide range of products in our in-house R&D facility in Vadodara

items.statement: Added 10-plus products in FY24; expanding into Eastern Europe, Russia, Italy, Middle East, Southeast Asia
items.quote: We added 10-plus products in our offerings during the financial year FY24. We are delighted to announce that we have begun supplying our products to many customers in Eastern Europe, Russia and Italy

items.statement: EV battery and semiconductor products under development; commercialization expected by end of FY25
items.quote: we are expecting it to happen sometime towards the end of this financial year

items.statement: Evaluating mining options in India and internationally for calcium carbonate, clays, talcs; groundwork ongoing
items.quote: we have identified few potential sources in India and internationally. And so, since a lot of groundwork is being done to evaluate the quality of the mines and the quality of the material which originates there

items.statement: No immediate plans for rights issue or private placement; may consider in future
items.quote: We have not thought of it as of now but maybe in the future, it might be a scenario. We are not sure

items.statement: No current government schemes for import substitution from China; potential anti-dumping duties could benefit company
items.quote: No, there is nothing being worked upon right now with these kind of schemes from the Government. But in case in the near future, if there is any kind of anti-dumping duty being levied upon for certain kind of products which we don't know if the Gov ernment is going to get into, but if that happens, then definitely it could maybe benefit 20 Microns to some extent

items.statement: FY25 footfall growth expected at max 5% for existing parks; ARPU growth 10-12%
items.quote: But having said that, I think at a company level we are not expecting more than 5% footfall growth for FY'25. But the footfall growth and ARPU growth will be about 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Odisha park targeting 4 lakh footfalls at ARPU Rs 800-1,000 in first year
items.quote: We are expecting about 4 lakh visitors at an ARPU of roughly Rs.800-1,000. So that's the way we are looking at it. This is our conservative estimate.

items.statement: Existing parks ARPU growth ~10% in FY25; marginal footfall growth
items.quote: We are expecting an ARPU growth in our existing parks of around double digits, 10% this year because we've had huge ARPU growth in the last two years.

items.statement: Odisha park EBITDA positive from year 1; PAT positive from year 2-3
items.quote: We are expecting it will be EBITDA positive from first year itself, and at the PAT level, it should be positive from year two or three.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin may shrink 3-4 percentage points due to Bhubaneswar park
items.quote: In the next FY , Bhubaneswar Park into our k itty, there could be some little shrinkage in the margin percentage of about some three to four percentage.

items.statement: Chennai park revised budget Rs 515 crore including land; Rs 194 crore committed/paid by Mar 2024
items.quote: In Chennai Park, we had a revised budget expense of somewhere close to 515 crore s and including the orders what we committed, we have about 194 crores has been committed or paid till 31st of March 2024.

items.statement: Odisha park budget ~Rs 190 crore; nearly complete
items.quote: And then in Odisha Park, we had a budget of about 189 crores and we are at the last leg of completing it. So probably , we'll be finishing it up for maybe around 190 crores.

items.statement: Maintenance capex ~10% of park top line annually for new rides
items.quote: We typically spend 10% of our top line from a particular park as we earmark with and keep it for adding new rides to the park.

items.statement: IT/digital transformation investment ~Rs 4-5 crore in next year
items.quote: In fact, we have a new IT head has joined and so in the next one year, we will be investing I think about 4-5 crores in new tech for our parks.

items.statement: Odisha park soft launch 24 May 2024; full opening next week
items.quote: We are actually soft launching from 24th onwards. I'm taking this call from Bhubaneswar. We just finished the press launch of the park. Tomorrow and day after we having a preview meet for some well-wishers and influencers and all that. And then the next week the park is opening.

items.statement: Chennai park commissioning likely Q3 FY26; targeting late Q2 if no rain delays
items.quote: We will be commissioning most likely in the third quarter. We are trying to finish in second quarter because we would like to be ready before the third quarter. There could be some delays because of unseasonal rains plays havoc in Chennai sometime.

items.statement: Plan to open ~1 new park per year; 5 more locations targeted by FY30
items.quote: We are looking at another five more locations in addition to what we already have. One or two of them will get closed and before the end of this financial year and the rest we will announce as and when they are ready.

items.statement: Bangalore & Kochi parks at capacity in peak season; headroom in Q2/Q4
items.quote: There is a limit, for example, on a summer season, our parks are already running pretty full. So it's hard for us to justify higher footfalls. But there are like for example Q2 and Q4, we do feel that there is some more headroom for us to grow.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 footfall hit by exam prepone & elections (Kochi group -37%); heat wave impacted Bangalore
items.quote: Normally, our Cochin park has a high contribution from group sales in January . That did not happen this year. Now the reason we are told is because of change in exam dates and also preponing of exams because of elections. So these are the two reasons that we were given. The other two parks I've not seen this issue. Only Cochin, I think the group footfalls degrew by 37%.

items.statement: Hyderabad park at 70% of Bangalore/Kochi footfalls; expanding marketing to Andhra Pradesh
items.quote: If you look at footfalls in Hyderabad compared to like for example, Kochi or Bangalore, it's only 70% of the other two parks, whereas we feel that it should be at par with the other parks. So we still feel there is a headroom for us to grow foot falls in Hyderabad.

items.statement: ARPU grew 15% in FY24 driven by non-ticket revenue (F&B, retail)
items.quote: ARPU for the quarter s tood at Rs.1,349, an increase of 14% , and for F Y'24 at Rs.1,430, registering a growth of 15%. Our increase in ARPU was driven by a healthy growth in non-ticket Wonderla Holidays Limited May 17, 2024 revenue along with encouraging response from walk-in groups and all aspects of our customer base

items.statement: Employee cost up 16% YoY in FY24 due to salary revision & headcount increase (+54 for year)
items.quote: There is actually 16% revision in the salary cost as compared to the previous year, and at the same time we had a headcount increase for this quarter as well as for the year, there was about some 16 number has added to the corporate team in the current year and even to the parks as well and then 38 numbers have been added during the full year.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 38.7% (-28pp YoY) due to lower footfall, higher payroll, lower other income
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter reached Rs.40.5 crores, degrew by 28 percentage on year-on-year basis. This was due to reduction in our footfall, increase in our payroll expenses and reduction in other income. EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 38.7%.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 49.4% (adj. 49.7%); PAT margin 31.2%
items.quote: EBITDA for the year stood at Rs.250.1 crores as againstRs.234.6 crores same period last year, showing a 6.6 % year-on-year increase. EBITDA margin for the year was 49.4% . Adjusted EBITDA for FY'24 was at Rs.251 crores as against Rs.235 crores for the same period last year with the margin of 49.7 percentage.

items.statement: Will raise funds (debt/equity combo) for new projects; Chennai capex large
items.quote: We will be looking at some fundraise. Some amount of debt depending on how many projects we sign in the next year or so, we'll take a call on that. We will be definitely doing some fundraise in the form of either debt or equity or most likely a combination of both.

items.statement: Reorganising sales, marketing, IT teams; new IT head hired; beefing up projects team for parallel execution
items.quote: We are reorganizing our sales team and our marketing team is going through a bit of a reorganization. Because of the way we are also going through a digital transformation , our IT team is also going through a substantial change. In fact, we have a new IT head has joined and so in the next one year, we will be investing I think about 4-5 crores in new tech for our parks. So thos e are some of the

items.statement: Government talks on hold due to election code of conduct; will resume after elections
items.quote: Nothing as of now, because this is election season. I think all of those conversations have been put on hold as of now because of code of conduct . We are waiting for normal government functioning to resume, then we will take up.

items.statement: Resort occupancy fell to 55% in FY24 due to loss of long-stay industrial guests
items.quote: In the current year, there were no major long stays. So that's the reason why the occupancy has reduced to 55% in the current FY.

items.statement: Footfall volatile due to exams, elections, heat waves; seasonality limits peak-season growth
items.quote: Every year the story tends to be little different. For us, the best way to mitigate this is to be in more locations and I have always some projects in the pipeline.

items.statement: Depreciation policy: rides & machinery over 10 years; consistent across parks
items.quote: Asset side for the plant and machinery like these rides and things like that we are depreciating over a period of 10 years.

items.statement: FY25 capex expected around Rs 4,000 million, similar to FY24
items.quote: Next year, the figure should be similar to about Rs. 4,000 million, unless there are other new opportunities.

items.statement: Europe FY25 capex budget approx €40 million to complete EV capacity installation
items.quote: Speaking about FY 25, the budget is to implement the total production capacity with an effort of approx. 40 million euro as gross amount.

items.statement: Target four-wheeler share of consolidated business 45% by FY30 from 25% now
items.quote: Increase our four-wheeler share of consolidated business from 25% now to 45% by FY 30.

items.statement: Target aftermarket sales 10% of India sales by FY28
items.quote: Our focus also is to reach 10% of India sales in our aftermarket business in India by FY28.

items.statement: Carbon neutral target >50% by FY30 from 35% in FY24
items.quote: the aspiration is to reach a carbon-neutral percentage of more than 50 % by FY30

items.statement: AURIC non-auto/4W plant capex Rs 4,009 million through March 2028, SOP Q1 FY26
items.quote: The total CAPEX is expected to be Rs. 4,009 million which should be spent in stages from now to March 2028, with the sales expectation of more than Rs. 5,000 million per annum.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated capex Rs 3,833 million, 81% for growth
items.quote: We have done Capex of about Rs. 3,833 million in FY24, which was 81% for growth, which included building, plant machinery and dies.

items.statement: Europe FY24 capex €62 million (VW €8m, Stellantis €33m, Mercedes €10m)
items.quote: In FY24, we booked capex of €62 million of investment in order to install this production capacity.

So now our net debt level stand at Rs. 163.5 million, reflecting our strong cash flow performance.

items.statement: Board recommended first-ever final dividend of 20% on face value since IPO
items.quote: I'm very happy to inform you all that as a reward to our long-term shareholders for the first time since our IPO, the Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of 20% on the face value.

items.statement: Adding ~6MW captive solar across facilities; Bangalore facility already 95% renewable; target 75% consolidated power from green energy soon
items.quote: We are in process of adding around 6 megawatts of captive solar power across our facilities. This strategic move is expected to yield cost efficiencies while significantly reducing our carbon footprint. It is noteworthy that our Bangalore facility already meets around 95% of its energy needs through renewable sources. We are now extending this sustainable energy initiative to our other facilities,

items.statement: Cover glass business: margins may be low initially due to validation/trials; phased margin improvement expected over 3 phases
items.quote: So Phase one could be lower margin, Phase two could be better margin, Phase three will be even better margins. So this is how it will pace out and as if any new technology product once you launch it, a lot of effort goes into proving validation, internal trials, which don't earn revenue to you. So it's just learning to walk before we run.

items.statement: Content per vehicle in PV segment increased 10x in 2-3 years (from ~Rs.80 to Rs.8,000-10,000)
items.quote: We've increased the content in the passenger vehicle from Rs.80 that we had about four years ago to almost Rs.8,000 - 10,000 now.

items.statement: Expects e-commerce industry growth of 15-20% and plans internal operations for that range
items.quote: See, I think industry growth, at least as far as we've been able to gather from our clients as well and their appetite, remains in that 15% to 20% range.

items.statement: Expects FY25 capex to decline to 6.6-6.9% of revenue from 7.4% in FY24
items.quote: We expect this to decline in fiscal '25 to somewhere between 6.6% and 6.9% of revenue overall.

items.statement: Sufficient capacity to grow through FY25; only major addition is Bangalore mega facility; Tauru gateway capacity expanded 10-15% via process improvements
items.quote: we have sufficient capacity available to grow through fiscal '25. We will need to build our Bangalore mega facility. And there may be some smaller hubs that are planned here and there, but there's nothing major outside of this

items.statement: Express Parcel service EBITDA at 18.4% for FY24, in line with long-term 18-20% target; PTL incremental margins 40-50%; SCS service EBITDA doubled to 6.8%
items.quote: Total service EBITDA from the Express Parcel business has grown from Rs. 636 crores in fiscal '23 to Rs. 934 crores in fiscal '24, which represents 18.4% of revenue and is in line with our long-term targets for this business.

items.statement: Express Parcel volumes grew 12% YoY to 740M in FY24; PTL freight grew 30% YoY to 1.4M metric tons; Truckload grew 40% YoY
items.quote: We delivered 740 million Express Parcels in our Express Parcel business in fiscal '24, which is a growth of nearly 12% year-on-year and 1.4 million metric tons of Part Truckload freight, which is a growth of nearly 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: No significant pricing movements needed or anticipated; will pass cost efficiencies to customers; yields up 6% YoY due to mix, weight increases, and some account repricing
items.quote: We haven't seen any significant sort of pricing movements being necessary in the market so far, and we don't anticipate that there will be significant pricing movements at this point going forward.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved from 38 to 31; receivable days down from 77 to 66; expects further improvement in FY25
items.quote: We are now closing fiscal '24 with a net working capital position of 31 days. Receivable days have declined consistently over the last 5 financial years and especially between '23 and '24 from 77 days to 66 days, and we expect to see further improvements to this financial year.

items.statement: Sandeep Barasia (ED & CBO) leaving after 9 years to pursue personal interests
items.quote: Mr. Sandeep Barasia has announced his decision to move on from Delhivery to pursue personal interests. On behalf of the employees, the Board of Directors and the shareholders of Delhivery, I'd like to place on record our gratitude to Mr. Barasia for his service as an Executive Director and Chief Business Officer of Delhivery for 9 years.

items.statement: Delhivery >100% of Express Parcel profit pool (ex-captives); PTL growth driven by service quality not discounting; pricing comparable to market
items.quote: We are fairly certain that if you take the third-party players put together and our Express business, we are materially over 100% of the profit pool of this industry.

items.statement: PTL truck utilization ~65% on trailer network, 55-60% on secondary line haul; room for improvement
items.quote: Broadly across the trailer network, if I break it in half, I think truck utilization on the trailer network would have been in the range of about 65% or thereabouts. Broadly speaking, on the secondary line haul, we would have been closer to about 55% to 60% utilized.

items.statement: Express Parcel 62% of revenue, PTL 19%, Supply Chain ~10%, Truckload & Cross Border ~9%; PTL share up from 16%
items.quote: Express Parcel continues to be the largest part of our business overall at 62% of revenue. The PTL business has grown significantly between fiscal' 23 and fiscal '24 from 16% of revenue to 19% of revenue.

items.statement: Active multi-service customers increased to 33,278; Meesho volume impact stabilized; new SCS customers ramped in Q3-Q4
items.quote: We have expanded the overall number of active customers who access multiple services of Delhivery with 33,278 customers as of the end of Q4.

items.statement: FY24 revenue Rs 8,142 crores (+12.7% YoY); EBITDA Rs 127 crores (1.6% margin) vs loss of Rs 452 crores; PAT loss narrowed 75% to ~Rs 250 crores
items.quote: We've delivered Rs. 8,142 crores of revenue in fiscal '24, which is a growth of 12.7% compared to fiscal '23 with an EBITDA profit of Rs. 127 crores and an adjusted EBITDA profit of Rs. 76 crores as opposed to an EBITDA loss of Rs. 452 crores.

items.statement: Good order inflow from existing molecules despite pricing pressure and fire accident
items.quote: Inspite of the pricing pressure and the fire accident at site two, we have been able to sustain the market of our products and we are seeing a good inflow of orders through our existing molecules.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 25% in FY24 vs 30% in FY23 due to fire accident one-time costs
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 25% in FY24 as against 30% in FY23.

items.statement: Robust growth expected in all three business segments in FY25
items.quote: Robust growth in all these three business segments is expected in the current financial year 2024-25.

items.statement: Site 2 expected to resume 75% capacity shortly, 100% soon; Site 4 commissioned for oil field services
items.quote: We are expecting to receive revocations of the closure order of site 2 to resume operations to the extent of 75% and 100% of the environmental clearance capacity shortly.

items.statement: Pricing pressure from China due to raw material cost reduction; expect pricing to improve from Q2 FY25
items.quote: Currently for Q1 and Q2, no, we are not expecting any price to be correcting, but we are seeing a good demand at least to start with, which is a very positive note and with the demand we hope that from Q2 onwards, the pricing will go towards the North.

items.statement: Converge polyol technology commercialized with H.B. Fuller; electrolyte additives partially commercialized, full commercialization in Site 3++
items.quote: We announced the first commercialization of the novel Converge polyol technology which we have developed in collaboration with Saudi Aramco and this first commercialization was led by one of the largest US based adhesives manufacturer H.B. Fuller.

items.statement: Lost some market share in certain products due to 50% plant downtime; confident of regaining in Q1-Q2 FY25
items.quote: However, we have only lost a certain market share in certain products because of our inability to produce because we have only 50% of our production plant which is online. So, that product is where we have lost some market share. But we are very, very confident that we will regain this market share in Q1 and Q2 respectively.

items.statement: Working capital days increased due to higher work-in-progress inventory from fire incident; expected to normalize by end of FY25
items.quote: main reason for the increase is attributable to the inventory days wherein the working progress inventory has gone up. So, this work-in progress inventory has been higher this side and this will moderate and we will again come back to th

items.statement: Non-current borrowings are working capital limits (CC, PCFC, LC) from banks
items.quote: Non-current borrowings are the working capital limits which we are enjoying with the banks. So, these are towards, CC, PCFC and LC limits, which we're using from the bank.

items.statement: Dr. James Ringer appointed CTO with attractive ESOPs; works full month every quarter across US and India time zones
items.quote: We have announced Dr. James Ringer as our CTO who has already been associated with us since the last 3 years as a Business Development Leader for the Americas. He is a very well recognized R&D professional with the career spanning more than 30 years at the Dow Chemical Company in the USA at an R&D Director level.

items.statement: Average selling price Rs 1,509 per kg for FY24
items.quote: Average selling price per Kg was Rs. 1,509.

items.statement: Management expects 30-35% year-on-year revenue growth and targets INR1,000 crore revenue in FY25
items.quote: Gradual growth for the industry. And for our company, it will be around 30% to 35% year-on-year.

items.quote: Volume side also, the demand has been increasing and it will increase substantially.

items.quote: The current bifurcation, I don't hold much. Actually, for the gold ornaments, we are having a sale of around INR650 crores and for bullions, around INR140 crores.

items.quote: Yes, possibility those products which are we supplying to our B2B clients, which are in very much huge volumes, we are planning to have manufacturing units in the near future.

items.quote: So Speedy JNPT, we have the license till 2025 December. We have had a good track record of performance. And as of now, the indication is as per the tender document, you get the renewal in the first quarter of the last year of operation.

items.quote: Our brand recall and service quality continues to outperform industry peers. This can be witnessed from the fact that we have been able to maintain our volumes during the quarter and have grown the same by 8% for the full year 2024 as compared to last year.

Next week, they'll send us more bids, award it.

items.statement: Outpatient pharmacy revenue grew 32% YoY from INR 850 million to INR 1,120 million in FY24

items.statement: Management plans 15-18% top-line and bottom-line growth in FY25
items.quote: this years. That is the current year FY’25, we plan to do between 15% to 18% both top line and bottom line growth. I'm talking of reported PAT.

items.statement: Net operating cash flow Rs. 878 crore in FY24 driven by improved working capital and operational gains
items.quote: Our cash flow generation remains sturdy with net operating cash flow of Rs. 878 crore recorded in FY24 driven by improved working capital and operational gains.

items.quote: So, the matter is sub-judice, it is already we have a favorable judgment at High Court level, but matter is under appeal. So, whatever time it takes, but in all forums, currently we have had judgments in our favor recognizing our ownership of the mark.

Again, we are not going to be at the levels that we see our peers at, the guidance or rather their levels are anywhere between 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Hope EPR regime stabilizes in FY25 to provide long-term positive cash flow for increased investment

items.quote: We will continue to remain focused on tightening working capital as we invest in synergistic businesses, and we are hoping this will bring our overall working capital even lower.
