items.quote: we expect the momentum to be there . We are looking and closely monitoring the situation because we see a number of transmission projects which are under finalization now where the reverse options and things are happening. So, we are looking at the sustained ‘24-25 as well.

items.statement: FY24 revenue was INR 31.7 billion, up 14% YoY
items.quote: On an FY basis, our FY23-24 revenue stood at 31.7 billion INR vs 27.7 billion INR in FY22-23, up by 14% YoY.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin was 12.8%, up 8.3 percentage points YoY
items.quote: we have about 12.8% EBITDA for the quarter, a significant 8.3 points improvement versus the corresponding quarter in the last year.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin was 10.8%, up 5.9 percentage points YoY
items.quote: On an overall basis the EBITDA for the financial year was 10.8%, which represents about 5.9 points increase versus the corresponding last financial year.

items.statement: FY24 gross margin was 34.5%, up 5.5 percentage points YoY
items.quote: On a full financial year basis, we achieved a gross margin of about 34.5% which was 5.5 percentage points higher than the last financial year.

items.statement: Company became debt-free with cash and equivalents of INR 2,765 million as of March 31, 2024
items.quote: The cash and cash equivalent balance was at 2,765 MINR as on March 31, 2024 vs 1,573 MINR as on Dec 31, 2023 and Net debt of 1,730 MINR as on March 31, 2023.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of Rs 2 per share after 5-year gap
items.quote: We are also pleased to inform all our shareholders that board has recommended a dividend of Rs 2/- per share after a gap of 5 years which is subject to shareholder's approval.

items.statement: Export orders were 32% of FY24 order bookings, domestic 68%
items.quote: overall for the financial year, the overall 57 billion orders that we booked, 68% of the orders were from domestic market and about 32% orders from the export market.

items.statement: Export revenue was 31% of FY24 revenue, domestic 69%
items.quote: On the revenue front, on the entire financial year, out of total 31.6 billion of revenue, 69% of the revenue is from the domestic market and about 31% o f revenues from the export

items.statement: Order backlog split: 63% private customers, 27% central utilities, 10% state utilities
items.quote: End of the financial year, we have about the backlog of 63 billion of which 63% coming from the private customers, state utilities have about 10% share and about central utilities have about 27% of the backlog.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 70% products/services, 30% projects in FY24
items.quote: project is we have about 30% of the total 31 billion revenue that we achieved in the last financial year and 70% is from the products, services and other business.

items.statement: Transformer nameplate capacity estimated at 18,000-20,000 MVA
items.quote: I would have assumed that it would be 18,000 to 20,000 MVA. Is that a ballpark range where we are on an installed capacity basis? Sandeep Zanzaria: Yes, I would say that's a fair guess.

items.statement: Expect 15-20 STATCOM projects in India over next 2-3 years, each INR 250-500 crore
items.quote: We are looking at about—close to in next 2 to 3 yea rs we are looking at about—15 to 20 STATCOMs to be put in India. And individually I think one project would be some, it depends upon rating because the ratings of STATCOMs are diff erent. So that's why the total configuration would be totally different. But each S TATCOM project can range somewhere between 250 crores to about 500

items.statement: STATCOM installation mandated by grid operators for renewable substations
items.quote: This is a mandate which is coming from the grid operators as well, that along with the substation you need to put the STATCOM.

items.statement: Committed to being important player in India HVDC market
items.quote: But yes, we are a global player of HVDC and definitely India remains a very important market for HVDC. So yes, we are committed to Indian HVDC market.

items.statement: No capex plans disclosed on call; will announce officially if any
items.quote: So, if that will be there then we will be anyhow de claring that officially to all our shareholders at the same time. We would not like to comment anything on an investor call on this subject

items.statement: Cash generated INR 1,192 million in Q4 FY24 and INR 4,495 million in FY24
items.quote: The cash generated was 1,192 MINR in Q4 and 4,495 MINR during the FY 23-24.

items.statement: Adequately staffed; recruitment plan under review based on order intake
items.quote: So, I would say that we are adequately staffed. But depending upon the orders what we are taking and things like that, there is a plan which is always under a review. And whenever we think that we are going to need people there is a plan toward that.

items.statement: Fixed-variable cost split approximately 50-50 for staff and other operating expenses
items.quote: we can on a very high level take about 50-50 ratio.

items.statement: HVDC project execution timelines: 48 months for first 3,000 MW, 54 months for next 3,000 MW
items.quote: It is 48 months for the first 3,000 MW and 54 months for the next 3,000 MW.

items.statement: Related party export orders subject to parent winning tenders and internal negotiation
items.quote: those contracts are still under discussion and negotiation and the related parties or the other group companies are participating in further tenders with the third parties. If they win and we are able to negotiate with the related parties, we expect to have a momentum in the first half of this financial year.

items.statement: One-time tax provision of INR 85 million for prior years in Q4 FY24
items.quote: we have already classified 85 million of tax related to the earlier year as a separate line item. So that's a one-off item.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target INR1,600-1,800 crore including benzene downstream contribution
items.quote: So nearly INR1,600 crores to INR1,800 crores can be a range where we will target to close our business.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA target INR160-200 crore including other income
items.quote: If I give broader range, then it can be in the range of INR160 crores to INR200 crores or something like that.

items.statement: FY25 revenue minimum INR1,700 crore and EBITDA margin 10-12%
items.quote: So we should do minimum of around INR1,700 crores because the new business will also add on. So around INR1,700 crores to INR1,800 crores of top line, we should be able to do. And I think EBITDA level, we can be around 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Benzene downstream greenfield project investment INR390 crore excluding land
items.quote: So the total investment other than the land and everything, it's less than INR400 crores, so it's around INR390 crores that has been the investment.

items.statement: No new capex planned for next 2 years except maintenance
items.quote: Yes. That is what we are planning at present.

items.statement: Benzene downstream utilization expected 60-70% after 1.5-2 months
items.quote: So, I think for another 1 to 2 months, we'll not be selling much in the market. So, I think after 1.5, 2 months, we will be coming to the market full-fledged with utilization of at least 60%, 70%.

items.statement: Chlor Alkali utilization at 82-83%, targeting 85-87% blended for FY25
items.quote: Yes, it is already at 82%, 83%. I think there is still room to go up to 92%, 93% utilization. And things are in place for that. So I think about 8 months of the year, we should do around 90% and the remaining about 80%. So yes, blended, I think we should be doing about 85%, 87%.

items.statement: Dye Intermediates and Dyestuffs near peak utilization at 80%, limited volume growth room
items.quote: So Dye Intermediates and Dyestuffs, they are a batch type manufacturing process. So there, reaching 90% plus is not possible. Usually, the work -- the peak utilization is about 80%. We are already close to that.

items.statement: Benzene downstream expected turnover INR400 crore at 85-90% utilization
items.quote: And the expected turnover at 85%, 90% utilization is around INR400 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA improvement of INR50-60 crore expected in FY25 from unit closures and Punjab incentives
items.quote: So, what we have ended at INR120 crores EBITDA level in last year, there should be at least improvement of INR50 crores, INR60 crores, considering all this level.

items.statement: Chlor Alkali steady margins 16-20%, peak revenue INR350-370 crore at full utilization
items.quote: Chlor Alkali margins vary from say, 16% to 20%. And before 2 years, there was very good time over at that time, even more than 25% margin was also there, but that was normal. We steady case, we can expect about 18% to 20%, 16% to 20% margin.

items.statement: Dyestuff and Dye Intermediates realization flat after slight increase 2-3 months ago
items.quote: Realization increased a little bit 3 months before, 2 to 3 months before. Since then, it has been flat.

items.statement: Net debt INR830 crore at March FY24, targeting INR100 crore annual reduction
items.quote: See, at March balance sheet, our net debt was about INR830 crores. This is something a peak debt of what we are estimating. And every year, about INR100 crores reduction should be there.

items.statement: Term debt INR538 crore, repaying INR100-120 crore annually to become debt-free in 5 years
items.quote: Company has a term based and the balance sheet debt is about INR538 crores. And we are going to pay every year INR100 crores to INR120 crores. So we should become debt-free within 5 years.

items.statement: Debtor days improved due to focused working capital management, expected to remain similar
items.quote: So it's based working capital management, we can say, that has helped the company to recover the debtors days.

items.statement: Inventory days to remain at current elevated levels due to integration and product variety
items.quote: So, this is the level that will remain more or less same. We are not expecting much improvement from this level.

items.statement: Diversifying from dyestuffs to benzene derivatives for pharma and agrochemical end-markets
items.quote: So what we have now done, added Chlor Alkali, now we have added benzene derivatives. So now our significant volumes will go into pharma, significant volumes will go into agrochemicals.

items.statement: Punjab government incentives ~INR20 crore per annum expected within 2-3 months
items.quote: There are certain government incentives that we are eligible in Punjab that should be available to the company that are in the range of about INR20 crores per annum. So, because of election process that has deferred, so we are expecting within 2, 3 months that will be approved by the state government.

items.statement: Demand stability since last 2-3 months, destocking ended, gradual recovery at low speed
items.quote: Since last couple of months, we have been experiencing stability in the demand for our industry products. It seems destocking position has come to an end and gradual recovery, but at low speed, is there.

items.statement: US and Europe markets still slow due to inflation and geopolitical headwinds
items.quote: The 2 major markets, the United States and Europe, have been still slow due to multiple headwinds from rising inflation to uncertain geopolitical scenarios.

items.statement: Domestic competitors include Colourtex and Jai Chemicals; Far East players compete in exports
items.quote: So, the competitors are domestically, there are companies like Colourtex. There are companies like Jai Chemicals, these are a couple of the largest players. There are a few players in Far East countries, Taiwan and South Korea. They are also good sizable players and they also compete with Indian players when it comes to exporting to Bangladesh or exporting to Turkey or Italy.

items.statement: Turkey subsidiary recovery delayed due to earthquake impact on textile industry
items.quote: Still the challenges are there. Volumes are gradually picking up, but it is taking time. As I mentioned earlier, earthquake has affected severely to the Dyestuff industry, consuming industry, that is the textiles industry.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 was difficult with sharp price drops in packaging board, maplitho and coated paper; wood cost up 30-35% hurt profitability despite pulp and coal correction.
items.quote: In fact, the Q4 has been a difficult quarter, I must say the year '23-24 first half was relatively better year from a pricing point of view and also the cost point of view, but thereafter we have seen a sharp drop in the prices of Packaging Board as well as the Maplitho Paper and the Coated Paper.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin at 26-27%, above paper industry long-term average and company's own long-term average.
items.quote: But somehow I would say that the major reason for the drop in profitability, which was expected I must say, is primarily because of the lower prices despite the higher input cost.

items.statement: FY25 likely tougher due to competition and dumping from ASEAN countries.
items.quote: The year gone by is over but the coming year is likely to be tougher I would say that the competition and also the dumping of paper from the ASEAN countries will pose a challenge in time to come.

items.statement: Sirpur Paper EBITDA ~30% for FY24 including state incentive on accrual basis; excluding incentive, EBITDA ~22-23%.
items.quote: I would say that the Sirpur EBITDA is in the range of somewhere around 30%, but when you talk about the Q3 and Q4, it sharply dropped because of the price drop, so year as a whole is around 30%, but that includes the state incentive accounted for on accrual basis, which we did not receive during this year.

items.statement: Corrugation business EBITDA normally 12-14%, but FY24 was around 10% due to bad year.
items.quote: In fact the corrugation industry has a very bad time the year '23-24 in the normal course, their EBITDA should be around 12% to 14%, but it was a bad year and it was around 10%.

items.statement: Wood cost increased sharply by 30-35%; pulp prices stable earlier but moved up sharply in last 2-3 months to $700-750/ton; long-term pulp price expected at $550 (+/-25).
items.quote: The wood cost which is a basic raw material for integrated pulp manufacturer remain very high in fact, it has gone up sharply by close to 30%-35%, so that has impacted the result.

items.statement: April NSR increase only in packaging board segment, not major; does not cover wood inflation.
items.quote: No, see the NSR increase in April this year increase is just in a packaging board one particular segment. There is nothing as a major increase.

items.statement: BCTMP mechanical pulp mill to be commissioned next fiscal year (FY25-26); will integrate ~70% of mechanical pulp requirement, reduce imports to 30-35% (softwood).
items.quote: Once the capacity is in place next year fiscal year it should be in place, so close to 70% of our mechanical pulp will be integrated and only 30%-35% we will import thereafter and that would also be the softwood.

items.statement: Mechanical pulp mill expected to save $100-150 per ton vs market purchase, depending on market price at that time.
items.quote: We always calculate that it should give us a saving of $100 to $150 per ton of pulp, but it all depends on the price scenario at that point of time.

items.statement: Packaging board machine (FY22) running at 100% installed capacity; debottlenecking to add 10-15% more production from same machine.
items.quote: Such a mega investment we want to utilize it fully say right now we have achieved 100% of the installed capacity, but we are doing debottlenecking of the same machine and hopefully we should be able to increase production by close to 10% to 15% from the same machine this is 1.

items.statement: Corrugation capacity utilization currently 55-60% annually; industry best practice is 70-75% due to peak season requirements.
items.quote: Right now, our capacity utilization is close to 55%-60% month different month different period, but on an annual basis, our utilization is close to 55%-60%.

items.statement: JK Paper targets double-digit plus growth, higher than paper industry's single-digit growth.
items.quote: See, we are very clear on this part that the industry, I said there is a single digit growth, but I didn't say about JK Paper growth and the JK Paper growth has to be a double digit and double digit also plus double digit.

items.statement: Acquired 85% of Horizon & Securipax for ~Rs 590 cr; later acquired balance 15% for Rs 104 cr; Manipal acquired later; total ~Rs 800 cr for 3 companies.
items.quote: When we acquired 85%, it was close to Rs. 590 crores, that was the consideration and the 15% when we acquired balance equity, it was rightly you yourself said Rs. 104 crores, so this is the consideration part when we acquired these 3 companies.

items.statement: Acquisition criteria: geography/demand center, customer profile/quality, competitive intensity, asset quality; target ROIC ~14-15% (4-5% over ~9-10% post-tax WACC).
items.quote: Whenever we do any project capital investment or acquisition, our basic criteria is the return on investment, something around 4% to 5% over the cost of capital that is our criteria and in long run, it should be better than that.

items.statement: Open to further corrugation acquisitions if right valuation, good customer base, asset quality, preferred geography; must be value-accretive.
items.quote: I would say that we will always be open and that will be always our aspiration to acquire some more and that is how we can expand faster, but again it has to be at a right valuation because at any valuation we are not interested in acquiring.

items.statement: FTA review with ASEAN due since 2019 but not done; government intent to protect domestic industry but process cumbersome; antidumping petition filed against Indonesia, China, Chile for packaging board.
items.quote: There are announcements or the communication from the government side, but nothing has happened. And I would say that the review was due because this was effective in 2014 and 2019 review was due, it was not reviewed because those countries were not interested in review because they are benefited.

items.statement: Imports from Indonesia (ASEAN FTA, forest concessions) and China (surplus capacity, US duties diverting volumes) are main concern; dumping defined as selling below home-market price.
items.quote: I would say that we are more worried on the import coming from the Indonesia because the Indonesia is a part of ASEAN bloc.

items.statement: Import intensity may reduce if pulp prices stay high ($750-800) and paper prices behave rationally ($950-1000), but surplus capacity in exporting countries leads to dumping regardless.
items.quote: If the pulp prices remains $750 or $800, paper prices should always be $950 or $1,000 and if the pulp prices remain at that level and the paper prices behave in a rational manner, then I find no set of import you have rightly said this, but there are countries they don't follow rational and the logical risk cost comparison and since they have the surplus capacities available, so they just dump it.

items.statement: Comfortable debt position; will maintain some borrowing on balance sheet; free cash flow ~Rs 500 cr after repayments, dividend, maintenance capex; not targeting zero debt.
items.quote: Our free cash flow at this performance level would be close to Rs. 500 crores because when you have this kind of a profitability Rs. 400 crores, Rs. 350 crores or Rs. 400 crores is the repayment part, then we have Rs. 135 crores to Rs. 140 crores of a dividend.

items.statement: Cannot comment on additional dividends or buybacks at this point; free cash flow retained as war chest for projects/acquisitions.
items.quote: That I can't comment at this point.

items.statement: 100% integrated for chemical pulp; mechanical pulp currently 100% imported; after new mill, ~70% mechanical pulp integrated (hardwood only; softwood still imported).
items.quote: The chemical pulp what we require for our paper and board manufacturing we are 100% integrated, we don't import. We only import the mechanical pulp which is required for packaging board.

items.statement: VFB (virgin fibre board) imports affect 15-20% of market sold off-the-shelf without approvals; JK Paper's open-market share broadly in line with industry.
items.quote: Of course, you are absolutely right that it takes time, but the only thing is that 15% to 20% of the packaging board of what you said is also sold in off the shelf and that is where it goes.

items.statement: Corrugated box conversion cost typically Rs 7-10/kg for normal boxes, up to Rs 20/kg for specialized boxes; pricing linked to kraft paper prices.
items.quote: In a normal box it may be Rs. 7 to Rs. 10 conversion cost.

items.statement: Maintenance capex Rs 100-150 cr/year; further packaging board expansion when demand-supply favorable; corrugation footprint expansion at appropriate time.
items.quote: At the same time when there is appropriate time, as I said that we will further expand our footprints in the packaging industry means the corrugation and at an appropriate time, if there is a I would say that good demand supply mismatch of packaging board we will further expand our capacity.

items.statement: Antidumping petition outcome timing uncertain; government says fast but practical experience shows much longer.
items.quote: It is a million dollar question and I must say that many a times the government and the Minister they say that we will be very fast, we can decide in a month time, but my practical experience that it takes much longer time.

items.statement: Raw material cost expected to stay at current levels (+/-5%); margin outlook depends on price scenario and dumping behavior.
items.quote: I personally see that the raw material cost should remain now at this point, I mean, whatever is the raw material cost today will remain more or less maybe 5% here or there. The only question mark is on the price scenario.

items.statement: Invested ~Rs 60 cr surplus funds from Sirpur Paper in mutual funds/treasury for ~7-8% return.
items.quote: No, it is just a treasury investment, so the surplus funds were deployed in the mutual fund and the treasury where you get a return of something around about 7%-8%, so we felt that it may give a better return, so we invested and it was from the open market.

items.statement: Management expects continued top-line growth in FY25 similar to FY24 but declines to provide specific revenue or margin percentage guidance.
items.quote: We are working towards it. We hope for the best. Definitely don't want to make any forward-looking statements, especially given the question that the previous gentleman asked, on this call. So, we'll work towards it for sure.

items.statement: Demand outlook is positive with a healthy government pipeline expected to convert in the next two quarters.
items.quote: It's looking positive for us, Pratik. The same investments that we made last year continue to pay off. We also have a very healthy pipe on the government front, which hopefully will bear fruit in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA margin percentage expected to remain around 20% in the near term due to continued investment in sales and AI/ML; absolute EBITDA will grow.
items.quote: We're in the transitioning as I mentioned, we are in the transitioning stage because we are investing in growth. We would want to maintain that margin and over a long-term period, improve the margins.

items.statement: Added ~3 banking logos (including Sri Lanka and Dubai) and ~10 government logos (ULBs in UP, Telangana, Andhra) in FY24.
items.quote: So, in terms of logo additions, we were we were able to add, I think, about three on the banking side. We added one in Sn Lanka, one in the Middle East from Dubai. And then on the government side, I think we added almost 10 logos last year.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted: existing platform business grew to INR92.98 Cr from INR79.08 Cr; new tech-enabled services grew 87% to INR21.5 Cr from INR11.5 Cr.
items.quote: Our existing business grew to INR92.98 crores from INR79.08 crores. Our additional tech-enabled services business grew to INR21.5 crores from INR11.5 crores, that's almost 87% growth.

items.statement: DSO reduced by 20% due to disciplined weekly collection reviews, contributing to cash balance increase to INR64.62 Cr.
items.quote: I'm very happy to inform you that our receivables position today, our DSO is down by 20%. It is because of a lot of discipline with which we are looking at and reviewing our collections on a weekly basis.

items.statement: Cash balance increased from INR37.99 Cr to INR64.62 Cr; debt reduced from INR53.66 Cr to INR44.99 Cr.
items.value: INR64.62 Cr cash, INR44.99 Cr debt
items.quote: And the good thing is that cash balance has been commendably, it increased from INR37.99 crores to INR64.62 crores. And even the data has come down from INR53.66 crores to INR44.99 crores.

items.statement: Headcount reduced from ~600 to 540; redeployed savings into sales and AI/ML hiring; COO Anil Vengayil left, strategic advisor Apparao Varre (ex-HCL) joined.
items.quote: Last year when we had this conversation, we have almost 600 people. This year, we have 540, that 60 people left. And we've invested all of this money into bringing in more sales personnel and investing in AI/ML.

items.statement: Plan to sell owned office property (estimated INR6-7 Cr) and use proceeds for share buybacks via ESOP trust.
items.quote: The idea is precisely what you've mentioned, Mr. Abhiram, the idea is to see how we can probably look at selling this property, and those proceeds, we will definitely see how we can invest in buying back as well.

items.statement: Revenue grew 27% YoY to INR116.51 Cr; EBITDA grew 22% to INR22.71 Cr; PAT grew 14%; EPS grew to INR6.66 from INR5.86.
items.quote: This year has been a transitioning year, I would say, for Intense Technologies, as there is a growth of 26% in the top line. We have done INR116.51 crores compared to INR91.83 crores last year. Similarly, the EBITDA has gone up from INR18.63 crores to INR22.71 crores and the PAT, there's been a marginal increase in PAT. That is about 14%.

items.statement: Government projects carry high risk; formed internal risk assessment team, turning down high-risk deals, partnering to mitigate risk after BSNL experience.
items.quote: We have a risk assessment team internally, which has been formed now, is once bitten, twice shy, there are many deals which we are even turning it down until unless things are there.

items.statement: International expansion focus on US/UK via partnership model with system integrators (Infosys, IBM, TCS) rather than direct sales.
items.quote: Our U’S. strategy is to partner with a lot of these companies and work through them because we don't have direct relationships with this and the sales cost and the nature of sales in the U.S. are different.

items.statement: Leveraging IP niche (3 platforms: communications, data, low-code) to partner with large SIs (Infosys, IBM, TCS) for US market access.
items.quote: Because of our IP capabilities in niche areas, what we are working on, a lot of the large payers look forward to partnering with us and taking our solutions ahead.

items.statement: Platform helps BFSI customers comply with regulatory data quality requirements (referencing Paytm, Kotak regulatory actions).
items.quote: And you've also seen what has happened recently in the regulatory landscape with the likes of the Paytms and Kotaks, etc. Our platform and services help our customers improve on their data quality so that they're able to leverage it better to cross-sell as well as they are regulatorily also complying.

items.statement: Project Butterfly strategy: 3 of 4 green shoots (data, transmission, talent, managed services) bearing fruit; farming revenue up 18% YoY.
items.quote: So, for example, in farming, we saw an increase of almost 18% from last year to this year, and that happened because of all these additional green shoots that we've added. And a few of these -- so out of the 4 green shoots that we added, I say 3 of them are starting to bear fruit at this point.

items.statement: FY25 total alcohol volumes expected at 21-21.5 crore litres
items.quote: For the present fiscal year, we expect our total alcohol volumes to rise quite substantially to approximately 21 - 21.5 crore litres.

items.statement: Power Transmission capex underway to raise gears capacity from ₹250 crore to over ₹500 crore, plus defence facility in Mysuru
items.quote: The business is currently executing a capex program, which enhances the capacity of our gears business from ₹ 250 crore to over ₹ 500 crore. This does not include our defen ce production. The investments are aimed towards a new bay and equipment in that new bay to manufacture gear boxes , both for power transmission and for some defence products. The expansions include establishing a large dedicat

items.statement: Water business order book ₹1,233 crore including ₹880 crore O&M contracts
items.quote: The outstanding order book on the 31st of March stood at ₹ 1,233 crore, which included ₹ 880 crore towards O&M contracts for a longer period of time.

items.statement: Power Transmission PBIT margin 36.7%, up 275 bps YoY
items.quote: The PBIT of the business grew faster than revenues at just over 40% - 40.1% to ₹ 107.1 crore with PBIT margins of 36.7%, up by almost 275 bps, compared on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Water PBIT margin 12.8%, up 600 bps YoY
items.quote: The PBIT margins stood at a healthy double-digit at 12.8% for the year, up by almost 600 bps Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Sugar domestic demand supported by higher realisations; export of 2 million tonnes requested by ISMA
items.quote: As a result, as I'm sure you all know, ISMA has written to the Government requesting a n export of 2 million metric tonnes, which we hope is under consideration

items.statement: Maize procurement prices down 10-15% vs last year due to 20% higher crop
items.quote: The maize crop this year is 20% higher. The prices have fallen quite dramatically, and the prices that we are seeing now for the first crop, what we're procuring for Bihar is substantially 10-12-15% lower than the prices that we were procuring earlier.

items.statement: Power Transmission export growth driven by global OEM relationships; majority of export order booking from existing customers
items.quote: So, without actually attributing any numbers, I think we have enough confident to say that over the next year, definitely two years, we will see substantial revenues especially order booking that will come from export markets. The majority of it from our existing customers.

items.statement: Final dividend ₹1.25/share recommended; interim ₹2.25 and special ₹2.25 already paid
items.quote: The Board has recommended a final dividend of ₹ 1.25 per equity share in addition to the interim dividend of ₹ 2.25 per equity share and a special dividend of a similar amount of ₹2.25 per equity share which was paid earlier during the year.

items.statement: Rani Nangal distillery commissioned at start of Q1 FY25, running at full capacity on grain
items.quote: I should also mention that the Rani Nangal distillery is now functioning at full capacity. It is commissioned at the very onset of this quarter and is running extremely well.

items.statement: Red rot disease reduced Co238 cane from 77% to below 50% area; target optimal in 2 years; uprooting and varietal substitution underway
items.quote: Two years ago, we had approximately for the entire group about 98% of our cane area was Co238. Last year, it was 77%. In the coming year, it will be just below 50%. And we expect that in two years' time, we'll be at absolutely optimal levels.

items.statement: Power Transmission aggressive HR programme domestically and internationally to service export customers
items.quote: And a lot of that has to do with new capacities that are coming our way, new hires, an aggressive HR programme domestically and internationally to be able to service our customers and partnering with our global OEMs in terms of supplies to their manufacturing locations around the world.

items.statement: Export prices robust despite record Brazil/Thailand production; 1-2 mt exports would not faze global market
items.quote: Export prices, while they have come down from all -time highs are still very, very robust, despite in fact, that is what I was talking about, when I gave the global industry scenario, that despite the record production in Br azil of sugar and a return to record productions in Thailand, which is very close to India, we are still seeing very robust raw and white sugar prices. If India does decide to

items.statement: Sugar inventory 58.94 lakh quintals valued at ₹35.3/kg driving higher debt

items.quote: So we are aiming for anywhere between INR160 crores to INR180 crores of PAT by FY'26.

items.quote: So we are expecting, obviously, to grow better than industry. So if the industry growth rate is 14%-15%, we expect to grow better than that.

items.quote: The aerospace vertical constituting 30% of consolidated revenue reflected robust growth of 27% over previous year, recording a revenue of INR285 crores as against INR225 crores in FY '23.

items.quote: Upon the retirement of debt in FY '25 we expect that these INR56 crores of finance cost and what is there on the P&L will reduce by at least 50%.

items.quote: Out of the net proceeds from the capital raise of INR203.47 crores out of the INR220 crores being the size of the QIP, INR158.45 crores is meant for repayment of the borrowing and balance INR45.02 crores is for general corporate purposes.

items.quote: We expect EBITDA margins to be about INR950 crores to INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Will continue dividend policy per DIPAM guidelines
items.quote: We will continue to pay dividend as per our policy and which is as per DIPAM guidelines only.

items.quote: Mr. Sourin, excess monsoon impacts us in a negative sense and lower monsoon also impact s in a negative sense in respect of our power stations, which are under operations. But moderate monsoon is always welcome. So in case excess monsoon comes, our construction projects gets

items.statement: FY25 consolidated net profit guidance of at least INR200 crores for PG Electroplast, 46% growth over FY24
items.quote: We are also guiding for consolidated net profit of at least INR200 crores in PG Electroplast, which is a growth of 46% over FY24 net profit of INR137 crores.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of INR370-380 crores, largely internally funded
items.quote: capex guidance for FY25 is in the range of INR370 to INR380 crores, and the company has planned to further expand room AC capacity by setting up a new integrated unit in Rajasthan.

items.statement: FY25 RAC revenue growth target of at least 35-40%
items.quote: But we are targeting at least 35% -40% growth in our RAC numbers for FY'25.

items.statement: FY25 washing machine and AC growth expected at 40-45% each
items.quote: We think that both AC and washing machine should grow, at about 40% to 45% this year.

items.statement: FY25 capex of INR370-380 crores, with INR170-180 crores for land and building (1 million sq ft) for future growth
items.quote: Out of the INR380 crores that I talked about, almost INR180 crores will be or INR170 crores will be going in the land and building.

items.statement: Expanding room AC capacity with new integrated unit in Rajasthan and SUPA facility expansion
items.quote: The company is also expanding their washing machine capacity from 1.2 million units to 2 million units with a new greenfield facility being planned in Greater Noida.

items.statement: Order book and visibility for product business remains robust, on track to accelerate growth significantly in FY25
items.quote: Order book and visibility for product business remains robust, and the company is on track to accelerate product business growth significantly in current financial year also.

items.statement: FY25 operating margins expected to have slight upward bias due to TV business exit (was 10%+ of revenue)

items.statement: FY24 raw material cost as % of revenue improved by 1.35% YoY due to lower commodity prices
items.quote: On a full year basis, it is a 1.35% improvement in the cost of raw material as a percentage of revenue versus the same percent last year.

items.statement: Raw material cost is pass-through; fixed conversion cost per unit means margins optically improve when commodity prices fall
items.quote: Actually in our business as I have been explaining, it is the fixed amount per unit which I get to make a product. I don't get a percentage. So raw material is a pass-through and optically the margins look better if the cost of raw material goes down.

items.statement: Pricing not compromised despite PLI benefits; prices same as or slightly better than competition
items.quote: Our pricing is almost same as the competition or slightly in some cases slightly better than competition and we are not compromising on the pricing because we have some cost adv antage or we have some PLI benefits as of now

items.statement: AC demand very strong; channel inventories at low levels; first-time buyers from tier 3/4 cities and villages driving secular growth
items.quote: We are seeing that channel inventories are at a very low level now. So we see this year going to remain very healthy for AC business.

items.statement: Industry facing capacity shortage in April-May; stock-outs likely at major brands due to unanticipated demand surge
items.quote: We are seeing industry overall being slightly short of the capacity right now on the monthly demand which we saw in month of April, May and June probably.

items.statement: PLI incentive of INR15 crores received in FY24; targeting INR30 crores in FY25, then INR36.5 cr, INR51 cr, INR60 cr over next 3 years
items.quote: The PLI is actually not a fixed run rate it is amount which has been decided depending upon the targets getting met. items.statement: State government incentives: INR4.7 crores net in FY24; targeting INR35-40 crores in FY25, then INR20-25 crores annually for 10-12 years
items.quote: In case of state government benefits first year is going to be little bump up maybe INR35, INR40 crores and then year after that every year about INR20 to INR25 crores.

items.quote: As we said initially Jaina first of all had a Google ODM license which only two other people have in India Dixon and one more company. So that comes into the JV because of the JV with Jaina.

items.statement: Acquired NGM for INR65 crores in FY24 for land and building availability at Supa for future growth
items.quote: During the year, the company has done significant capex in commissioning a new greenfield plant in B hiwadi, new building in Supa in the PGTL premise, and we have also acquired NGM for INR65 crores, thus assuring land and building availability for future growth in Supa

items.statement: Board approved 1:10 stock split (INR10 to INR1 face value) and final dividend of INR20 per split share (INR1 face value)

items.statement: ESOP expense of INR15.5 crores in FY24 covering ~200 employees; employee cost to grow in line with revenue
items.quote: We have given quite decent ESOPs, almost 200 people in our company are covered under ESOP and we have taken INR15.5 crores hit this year which is a part of our employee cost because of the ESOP.

items.quote: According to our calculation ROC E is about 21.6% on a last year basis and I have given the calculations in my presentation you can go through it this is one.

items.quote: will be updating you may be after this election and things are over. Because we are in talk with several clients but none of the clients are making any decision. items.quote: In fact, even in Q1 we will see some contribution from the TV business because what happened was that there was some inventory of the kits which was lying in the PG Electroplast. items.statement: AC: 80-85% branded, 15-17% private label; Washing machine: 65% branded, 35% private label; margins similar across both
items.quote: Yes almost 80% to 85% is going in the AC to the brands and about 15% to 17% is going to the to private levels. In the washing machine it is slightly on the higher side probably the private levels are close to about 35% and brands are about 65%.

items.quote: We are again aiming to double the AUM in current financial year.

items.quote: Disbursements were up 95% year-on-year to INR665 crores in FY24 versus INR341 crores in FY23.

items.quote: business increased very significantly, which grew from 5% of AUM as of March’23 to 24% as Page 2 0f 18 ‘Moneyboxx Finance Limited l\é MONEYBOXX May 21, 2024 of March’24. We will continue to increase the share of secured loans to over 40% by the end of financial year 25

items.quote: Opex has declined by almost half in last 3 years, from 24% to 20% to 15% and this year it stood at 12.7%. Excluding ESOP charge, opex stood at 12.4%. We still expect this over a medium term to come into single digit number, despite the expansion in branches

items.quote: The company has strong unit economics and interest rate improved by 200 basis points, to 15.9% this financial year compared to 13.9% in FY 23.

items.quote: We expect at least 100 basis point reduction in incremental cost of borrowing this year, driven by rating upgrade and increasing scale.

items.quote: Liquidity levels remain adequate at INR106 crores as on March end and company has another INR3S crores per month of partnership on-time funding available through co-lending partnerships and business correspondence

items.statement: Geographic diversification strategy to mitigate regional risks like erratic rains

Whilst, because of the fact that we are present in more than six, seven, cight states now, it helps us manage the book better

items.quote: the final dividend of 1,000%, which is INR 20 per share. You will all recall that we have just in February paid an interim dividend of INR 16 per share so with that, the overall dividend for the year is INR 36

items.quote: Base oil follows crude. As we have mentioned in earlier questions that it went up to above $90 recently and then now has come back to around $83- $84

items.quote: factory fill our 2x market growth has been 7% in the quarter and in the year, also, we are close to that 6.5

items.statement: Factory fill ~10% of volume, mostly commercial vehicles; CV production declined in last 2 quarters impacting overall volume
items.quote: roughly total 10% of our volume is coming from factory fill and this is largely from Commercial Vehicle segment

items.statement: Brand positioned #2-3 in most categories; focus on distribution and product quality over price competition

We expect that going forward in the medium term, the export segment will contribute 10% of the overall revenue, which is in line with our long-term target of 15% to 20% contribution.

items.statement: Expected asset turnover on incremental capex is ~3x.

items.quote: The sluggishness in consumer demand has been reflected in revenue degrowth during the first half of the year, followed by stability in Q 3 and in Q4, with sustained focus to healthy inventory in the distribution network, we could see resumption of growth trends.

items.statement: Management plans for gradual uptick in FY25, cautiously aggressive approach; optimistic on long-term demand but no specific growth target given
items.quote: FY'25, you know, I can see things may improve, but it is good if we plan that the uptick is gradual. I think later part of the year should be buoyant because I can see the growth in economy.

items.quote: We have embarked on this journey to modernize our distribution management system, aligning with our commitment to continuous improvement.

items.statement: Expect similar or slightly better EBITDA margin improvement of ~2% in FY25
items.quote: I am expecting similar type or slightly better than this in the next financial year. So, we are maintaining our guidance which we have given earlier.

items.statement: ARPOB growth expected at 5-6% in FY25 driven by specialty and payor mix
items.quote: I am expecting more like 5% to 6% ARPOB growth, mainly driven by the specialty and the payor mix improvement.

items.quote: So, you can safely assume the price increase of 2.5% and balance is towards case mix and other things. So, total ARPOB increase will be 5.5% to 6%.

items.quote: So, additional CAPEX will be somewhere around Rs. 1,200 crores to Rs. 1,300 crores, which include equipment also, everything put together.

items.quote: Our consolidated operating EBITDA increased 15.1% to Rs. 1,268 crores, which translates into a margin of 18.4% in Financial Year '2 4 versus 17.5% in Financial Year '2 3.

items.statement: Medium-term hospital EBITDA margin target of ~25% in 2-3 years
items.quote: And we expect that we will be around 25% margin in the next 2 to 3 years' time.

items.statement: Robotic surgeries and radiation therapy volumes grew >50% in FY24
items.quote: For instance, volume in key procedures such as transplant grew 11%, while in robotic surgeries and radiation therapy, volume growth was in excess of 50%.

items.statement: Cost optimization via supply chain, procurement, manpower productivity and formulary substitution

items.statement: Debt reduced by Rs. 76 crores to Rs. 264 crores; net debt/EBITDA 0.17x vs 0.30x
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, we have further reduced our debt by Rs. 76 crores to Rs. 264 crores, representing a healthy net debt-to-EBITDA of 0.17x as compared to 0.30% as on 31st March 2023.

items.statement: Working with PE investors on Agilus put option (Oct 2024 deadline); options include IPO revival or buyout via debt/equity
items.quote: So, we are working with the private equity investor s to come out with a solution for this particular thing. items.quote: We have reviewed the potential of all territories and confident to profitably scale Domino's network to 5,500 stores as we see a significant headroom to grow with immense potential in the territories that we operate in.

items.quote: Domino's Cheesy rewards membership base is now 23.1 mn strong and roughly contributing to ~50% of orders.

items.statement: Gained market share in pizza category; no competitor opened ~180 stores with 7.8% delivery LFL; focus on growing $50bn category not just $1bn pizza segment
items.quote: We track all competitors internally, and we have gained market share within the category. items.quote: As I said, 40% of our sales came through resident referrals in Dehradun. We have 2,600 repeat customers in AGEasy, right? So quite, quite high satisfaction scores. And , if you look at cross-sell in our care homes, there's a 38% cross-sell of services

items.statement: Consolidated revenue dip expected for few quarters due to expansion and no inventory to sell; temporary until Gurugram launch in Q2 FY25
items.quote: I had shared with you last time as well that for a few quarters you will see a dip in the consolidated revenue because as we expand and invest in to scale up, and we have no inventory to sell our residences, this will happen. But this is a temporary phenomenon. As we launch the residence work in the Gurgaon in Q2 FY25, this temporary phenomenon will get bridged.

items.statement: Board approved INR 50,000 crore market borrowing plan for FY25 to cover potential disbursements, committed liabilities and refinancing
items.quote: based on our internal assessment, we have taken this approval from Board for INR50,000 crores. We'll take care of any disbursement which may come up during the year, my committed liabilities and we are also exploring lot of refinancing opportunities.

items.statement: No EBR requirement from IRFC in FY24 and interim FY25 budget due to high budgetary support; final FY25 budget awaited
items.quote: In the financial year 2024, there was no requirement for extra budgetary resources to the railways due to the high budgetary support and, thus, there was no funding done by IRFC.

items.statement: AUM INR 4.64 lakh crore as of March 31, 2024; 98.94% exposure to Indian Railways
items.quote: Our assets under management as on the 31st March, '24 stands at INR4.64 lakh crores, and 98.94% of this AUM is for exposure to Indian Railways.

items.statement: Spreads stable at 40 bps for rolling stock and 35 bps for projects; no change expected for MoR lending
items.quote: Margin for rolling stock is 40 bps and it is 35 bps for projects. This margin is added to weighted average cost of funds raised during the year to work out lease tenders.

items.statement: New venture spreads will be based on project credit profile and industry standards, could be higher than regulated MoR spreads
items.quote: For the new venture, it is not linked to the -- our funding to MoR. Those spreads will be purely dependent upon the credit profile of the project and the numbers that is shown on the -- based on the due diligence.

items.statement: Railways capex INR 2.52 lakh crore in interim FY25 budget; 40,000 km new track planned over 6-8 years via economic corridors
items.quote: Gross budgetary support has been kept at INR 252,000 crores for capital expenditure for railways in the interim budget of the financial year 2024-'25.

items.statement: Lease agreements for FY17-18 projects now being signed post moratorium; pipeline to support earnings for next 2-3 years
items.quote: since we've been lending enormous sums of money over the past so many years to the Indian Railways, some of those moratorium periods are coming to an end and we are signing those lease agreements now.

items.statement: Actively exploring funding for rolling stock leasing to non-MoR entities, state JV railway infra, dedicated freight corridors, multi-modal logistics parks, renewable energy for rail network
items.quote: we are actively looking at funding such projects in the railway ecosystem apart from funding of the Indian Railways and exploring opportunities in collaboration with other infrastructure lenders.

items.statement: 98.94% AUM exposure to Indian Railways; seeking to diversify via forward/backward linkage projects
items.quote: 98.94% of this AUM is for exposure to Indian Railways.

items.statement: Interest capitalized on unsigned project lease agreements offsets AUM decline; capital recoveries from signed leases balance AUM

items.statement: Total borrowing INR 4.12 lakh crore as of March 31, 2024; mix: bonds 48.02%, rupee term loans 30.63%, ECB 16.71%, NSSF 4.25%
items.quote: Our total borrowing as on the 31st March, '24 stands at INR412,032.10 crores. And in order to keep the borrowing cost competitive, we raise funds from various sources like taxable bonds, from domestic market, rupee term loans, ECB, 54EC bonds.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR 0.70/share for FY24 plus interim INR 0.80/share; total INR 1.50/share
items.quote: Our board has recommended final dividend of INR0.70 per equity share for FY '24 which is subject to approval of our shareholders in AGM. This is in addition to interim dividend of INR0.80 per equity share.

items.statement: Team onboarded for new ventures but needs strengthening; internal credit committees set up; agencies onboarded for financial, technical, legal due diligence
items.quote: we have brought a team in place, but it does have to be strengthened. And certainly, we are in talks with certain companies so that we can take this forward.

items.statement: Charter permits funding entities with backward/forward railway linkages; may pursue charter expansion via new MoU with Ministry
items.quote: Yes. That would be one of the possibilities that we will be pursuing to expand our charter. But the point is that even -- that, as I said, we will be pursuing, but even without that, the forward and backward linkages with the railways itself throws up so much opportunity.

items.statement: Earnings resilient for next 2-3 years from existing pipeline; using period to build diversification before potential MoR lending slowdown
items.quote: as I said, for right now, our financials are very robust and will continue like this for the next two years. And this is the time and the opportunity for us to make sure that we diversify our businesses so that we can sustain it beyond that period as well.

items.statement: Expects to continue outpacing industry growth by at least 3x while maintaining profitability; no specific topline number given as it depends on industry demand
items.quote: The only guidance that we will give you is that whatever is the industry topline growth , we are fairly confident of continuing on our earlier trajectory of growing at least three times the industry topline growth.

items.statement: If industry growth returns to 7-9%, company targets 25-30% topline growth; if industry stays at 1-2%, expects 15-18% growth
items.quote: Now, if the industry topline growth comes back to the earlier levels, which has been the norm for the last 10 -15 years of industry registering a value growth of somewhere between 7% to 9%, if that happens, then we should be looking at the topline growth somewhere around 25%, maybe even 30%.

items.statement: Standalone Q4 FY24 gross margin 49.3%, highest in company history and industry; EBITDA margin 22.5% vs 22.0% YoY; PAT margin 14.5% vs 14.8% YoY due to higher depreciation
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter of 49.3% is not only the highest in the industry by a fairly wide margin, but also the highest in the history of our company.

items.statement: Full year FY24 standalone EBITDA margin 18.5% vs 16.9% FY23, in line with guidance; PAT margin 11.7% despite higher H2 depreciation
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the full year expanded by over 28% to Rs. 233 crores and our EBITDA margin for the full year clocked 18.5%, sharply up from 16.9% in FY23 and has been almost exactly in line with our earlier guidance.

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 22.0%, PAT margin 14.0%; full year EBITDA margin 18.2% vs 16.9% FY23
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has improved from 16.9% in FY23 to 18.2% in FY24.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 standalone value growth 12.5% vs industry <1%; consolidated revenue growth 18.3%; outperformed industry for 4th consecutive quarter
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, Our topline has grown by over 18% for the quarter against an industry average of less than 1% growth.

items.statement: Full year FY24 standalone growth 16.9% to Rs 1,255 cr; consolidated growth 21.7% to Rs 1,306 cr, far ahead of industry
items.quote: For th e full fiscal FY24, on a consol basis, Indigo Paints has achieved a revenue of Rs. 1,306 crores, which is a robust 21.7% growth over FY23 and it is far ahead of the industry growth rate

items.statement: Q4 FY24: >20% value and volume growth in putty and primer+distemper; emulsion volume mid-teens but value lagged due to price cuts; enamel and wood coatings muted
items.quote: For the quarter , Q4 of FY24, the Company witnessed over 20% value and volume growth in the putty segment and in the primer + distemper segment.

items.statement: Differentiated portfolio stable at ~30% of standalone revenue, growing at same pace as overall basket; waterproofing/construction chemicals now 5-6% of standalone topline within 6-7 months of launch
items.quote: So, it remains around the 30% mark on our overall revenue and as a percentage earlier, we used to see a steep climb happening year-on-year. I don't think we see that anymore.

items.statement: Waterproofing/construction chemicals contribution 5-6% of standalone topline; targets 8-10% in FY25 vs 8-9% for top 2 players
items.quote: In the last six months, they are contributing around 5%-6% of our topline, which is fairly significant. Now , we understand, and we don't have exact numbers for that, but we understand that the corresponding numbers for the two largest players in the paint industry is closer to 8% or 9% of their topline.

items.statement: Jodhpur water-based plant ~Rs 270 cr, solvent-based plant Rs 40-45 cr, putty expansion <Rs 15 cr; all to be funded by internal accruals
items.quote: The CAPEX cost for the new water based plant that is coming up at Jodhpur is roughly of the order of about Rs. 270 crores. The CAPEX cost for the new solvent base plant coming up at Jodhpur is somewhere in the region of about Rs. 40-Rs. 45 crores and the CAPEX cost of the expansion of the existing p utty facility at Jodhpur is less than Rs. 15 crores.

items.statement: Putty expansion completion by Nov-Dec 2024; solvent plant by Mar 2025; water-based plant targeting Mar 2025 but may slip 2 months due to labor availability
items.quote: We expect the putty expansion to be completed by November, December of this year, hopefully a little earlier. items.quote: The capacity expansion that we have done at Tamil Nadu is about 50,000 kiloliters per annum and that will keep us very comfortable for the next 4-5 years because that plant services most of southern India and small parts of central and east India.

items.statement: Active dealers >18,000, tinting machines ~10,000 as of Mar 2024; ~90% new dealers are existing paint dealers; tinting machine adoption drives 2-3x dealer productivity
items.quote: As on 31st March 2024, our count of active deal ers was over 18,000 and our tinting machin e population was almost 10,000.

items.quote: Having said that, particularly if you look at last fiscal, we had a huge focus on wholesale addition. So, this wholesale dealer addition earlier was not there as a focus area for our company, but last year it was definitely a focus and there we made significant gains in that area.

items.statement: No measurable impact from new entrants (Birla Opus, JSW, Astral) on topline, bottomline, tinting machine or dealer adoption; focus remains on competing with Asian Paints, Berger, Nerolac, Akzo
items.quote: We see absolutely no impact of their presence on our topline , bottomline, our tinting machine adoption or our dealer adoption , whatsoever.

items.statement: Apple Chemie subsidiary grew 50% in Q4 FY24 to ~Rs 51 cr full year; expects 50-60% growth in FY25; now supplying in 8-9 states beyond Maharashtra
items.quote: Our subsidiary, Apple Chemie has registered robust growth of 50% in Q4 of FY24 and we expect them to register strong growth in the upcoming quarters as well.

items.statement: Capex to be funded entirely by internal accruals; comfortable with treasury balance and cash flows
items.quote: As far as the means of financing is concerned at the moment, the intent is to finance this entire CAPEX by internal accruals. And we feel fairly comfortable with our treasury balance and with the profitability coming in, the cash flows coming in during the year that we should be able to manage it entirely by internal accruals.

items.statement: Low attrition, high variable pay and ESOPs for manpower retention; significant salesforce ramp-up in FY24
items.quote: We are able to retain our manpower with very low attrition rate. We are able to incentivize our manpower by high variable pay and ESOPs.

items.quote: But suppose the industry witnesses or continues to witness a slump in demand growth and the industry growth is 1%-2%, then I am afraid we will have to be satisfied with the topline growth of closer to 15%, 17%, 18%.

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY24 gross margin 37% vs 31% in Q3; EBITDA INR98 crores (+70% QoQ, +52% YoY); adjusted EBITDA INR88 crores (+53% QoQ, +36% YoY)

items.statement: Essentials BU targets 3-5x asset turn and 8-12% EBITDA margin

items.statement: China not importing material into India in essentials space; overcapacity in China may have plateaued prices; Laxmi holds share via cost positioning and technology edge; serving Chinese customers in specialties
items.quote: We certainly see China not bringing in "material" into India, especially into our essential space. Given that China's demand remains very muted post COVID, I think we are seeing that maybe the prices again this is our lens that prices may have plateaued out.

items.statement: Essentials BU new products share increased 2% QoQ on larger volume; Specialties BU improved mix driving robust top and bottom line growth

items.quote: Loan forex losses goes to OCI, other comprehensive income, which our Germany business has taken U.S. dollar loan from our U.S. business. So euro movement in last quarter has resulted in this kind of higher losses that you see in Europe business.

items.quote: Further, the loss before tax in FY'24 stood at INR 177 crores, against loss before tax of INR 324 crores in FY'23. The reduced loss is due to one-time positive impact of insurance and customer claims.

items.quote: Profit before tax for Q4'24 was INR 23 crores, against loss before tax for Q4 '23 of INR 128 crores. Further, the loss before tax in FY'24 stood at INR 177 crores, against loss before tax of INR 324 crores in FY'23.

items.statement: FGD ordering delayed; ~17 GW ordered in FY24, ~20 GW in FY23; 96 GW remains to be ordered over 4-5 years in staggered fashion
items.quote: Roughly, we see about 20 - 25 gigawatt will be ordered every year.. Ordering will take place, but in a staggered fashion.

items.quote: The breakeven revenue for the today's structure of the company is in the range of INR2,000 crores to INR2,500 crores, and we are far below that at this point in time, which is a challenge for the company.

items.quote: The net worth of the company has come down to almost INR57 crores as of March 2024 from INR226 crores in March 2023, and the company has been making losses for 3 consecutive years.

items.statement: FGD implementation deadline approaching; slower order flow over past 2 quarters; market expects further deadline extension; ordering dependent on regulatory decisions
items.quote: The data for FGD technology where we see the government deadline for implementing the FGD for thermal power plants is fast approaching. However, we see slower than anticipated flow of orders over the past 2 quarters.
