items.statement: New CEO appointed effective July 1st
items.quote: We recently announced the appointment of a new CEO, who will take over from 1st of July.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR0.75 per share recommended, total FY24 dividend INR1.25 per share
items.quote: Based on the results, the Board of Directors met today and recommended a dividend of INR0.75 per share, final dividend of INR0.75 per share versus or this was in addition to the interim dividend of INR0.50 per share, which was paid in October 31 -- on October 31, 2023.

items.statement: Actively evaluating inorganic acquisition targets for growth
items.quote: We are looking for suitable targets. We have been in a number of discussions, having concluded yet any one of them to a level where we can share the details.

items.statement: BFSI training grew 83% YoY, technology training grew 5% YoY in Q4 FY24
items.quote: In product mix terms are BFSI and other, and I alluded to that, that training grew 83% year-on-year and in technology, though we had the rebound coming from advanced technology sector as well -- advanced technology training as well as the Tier 2 GSIs and GCC's focus technology was also up 5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Early success in generative AI training programs and pedagogy
items.quote: We are also seeing early signs of success in training on generative AI and in using generative AI for training, both ways, training on generative and AI -- generative AI for training.

items.statement: 200+ corporate partnerships and 30+ OEM relationships
items.quote: We have 200-plus corporate partnerships. We have more than 30 OEM relationships and strong balance sheet to invest in innovation and growth.

items.statement: H1 FY24 revenue down 23% YoY, H2 FY24 up 4% YoY
items.quote: Another way to look at it is while H1 was down 23%, H2 was up 4% on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Dependence on Tier 1 GSI hiring recovery for FY25 guidance
items.quote: The reason I'm giving a range is that it is also dependent on the recovery of recruitment or hiring in Tier 1 GSIs.

items.statement: Value destruction in tech sector requires careful inorganic target selection
items.quote: There is a lot of destruction, I should say, value destruction, which has taken place in the tech sector, and therefore, one has to be careful that we don't make wrong choices.

items.statement: EBITDA to decline in Q1 and Q2 FY25 then improve sharply from Q3 FY25 as Jindal Supreme redeploys at higher rate
items.quote: EBITDA for the first quarter of FY25 will decline and then towards the third quarter will improve sharply.

items.statement: Jindal Supreme redeployment expected by October-November 2024 at much higher day rate
items.quote: As soon as refurbishment is completed, we expect to deploy the rig by October or November of 2024 on a much higher day rate.

items.statement: Order book stands at US$ 251 million as of 31 March 2024
items.quote: The order book as on 31st March 24 stands at US$ 251 million.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer acquisition at US$ 75 million approved, awaiting statutory approval; net cash outflow ~US$ 45 million after JV loan repayment
items.quote: The value at which the transaction will take place is 75 million that has also been communicated earlier very clearly in multiple announcements made to stock exchange or shareholder notices.

items.statement: Jindal Supreme under refurbishment for redeployment by October-November 2024
items.quote: One more rig Jindal Supreme, which was de-hired on 25th March, 2024 is currently under refurbishment.

items.statement: Jindal Explorer to be de-hired in May 2025 and move to new contract
items.quote: Jindal Explorer will be de-hired in May 2025 and then it will get onto a new contract.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA declined 11% QoQ due to one-time US$ 0.722 million write-off from ONGC settlement
items.quote: This was settled for US $ 0.982 million leading to a write-off of US$ 0.722 million which is equivalent to Rs. 6 crores approximately.

items.statement: Normalized Q4 FY24 EBITDA ~Rs 55 crore; normalized Q3 FY24 EBITDA ~Rs 63 crore
items.quote: So, Rs. 55 crores was a more normalized EBITDA for Quarter 4?

items.statement: Current day rates nearing US$ 100,000; last Jindal Supreme contract at US$ 84,000-88,000; expects rates to sustain or rise
items.quote: The current rate is around nearing US$ 100,000 a day. The last that we got for Supreme was around US$ 84,000-88,000.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer bareboat rate US$ 35,000/day in 2024, rising to US$ 40,000/day from Jan 2025
items.quote: This contract was started in March of 2019 and it will continue into 2025. Right now it is at US$ 35,000 per day for 2024 and then from 1st January 2025 it will incr ease to US$ 40,000 per day on bareboat basis

items.statement: ONGC currently operating ~34 rigs, up from low 20s; demand expected to increase further
items.quote: Right now ONGC is operating around 34 rigs.

items.statement: ONGC canceled HPHT tender due to rate disagreements; requirement to roll into next tender
items.quote: Apparently they had some negotiations with L1 party and they were not able to get the rates that they wanted. Plus, the L1 party had not quoted earlier rates. Looking into all those considerations, I guess ONGC canceled that contract.

items.statement: Gross borrowings increased due to rig refurbishments; net cash position Rs 51 crore; Rs 80 crore loan on Discovery-1 due 31 May 2024 to be paid from internal accruals
items.quote: The borrowings of the Company have increased on a gross level. However, at a net level, we are still net cash to the extent of Rs. 51 crores.

items.statement: No new debt for Jindal Pioneer acquisition; payment on staggered basis from internal accruals
items.quote: No we will not take any debt. We have only taken debt for refurbishment of our rigs which will get amortized as and when these rigs get deployed because we are getting good cash flows from all the rigs.

items.statement: Loans to JV companies and refurbishment amortization reflected in other financial assets (Rs 119 crore) and current loans (Rs 125 crore)
items.quote: The other financial assets that you are referring to are refurbishment expenses which are amortized gradually over the duration of the contract.

items.statement: Rig utilization: 5 rigs deployed in FY24; Jindal Supreme de-hired March 2024, 4 rigs operating in H1 FY25
items.quote: Since only 4 rigs will be operating in the first qu arter of FY25 and second quarter of FY25 earnings will be lower in these quarters as compared to the March quarter which will then pick up in the third quarter onwards

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer acquisition awaiting final statutory/regulatory approval; application submitted April 2024
items.quote: We have submitted an application in the third week of April, 24. We are following up on that application. Once approval is received, we can immediately buy it.

items.statement: Earnings fluctuation risk from rigs rolling off old low-rate contracts onto new higher-rate contracts
items.quote: Market is very good and the only reason why our earnings fluctuate primarily is because rigs are getting off hired from old contracts which were at much lower rates and are going on to new contracts which will be at much higher rates.

items.statement: Rig segment generates >90% of EBITDA; Mud Logging and Directional Drilling minor contributors
items.quote: Majority of EBITDA is generated from the rig segment. More than 90% is coming from the rig segment.

items.statement: ONGC sole customer for rigs; 30-year relationship; satisfied with services
items.quote: We have been supporting and serving ONGC for the past 30 years in their drilling programs. They are satisfied customers and we have always explored opportunities with them.

items.statement: International rig rates (US$ 120-140k) not directly comparable; ONGC-suitable rigs limited, supporting higher domestic rates
items.quote: The international markets went to US$ 140,000, US$ 120,000 per day. But it didn't really get the Indian market up to that rat e plus the Rigs that are avai lable even if Aramco softens this market, it is not appropriate for the ONGC segment

items.statement: Newbuild rig cost US$ 270-300 million with 2.5-3 year delivery timeline; not feasible vs acquisition
items.quote: Like what I said a few months ago, when we had found out it was about 2.5 years to 3 years, and the price was about US$ 270 to US$ 300 million depending on the specification on the rigs that you wanted.

items.statement: Promoter stake increased in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Also a point which was missed in my earlier discussion and also in the presentation is that promoter stake has also increased in the fourth quarter of FY24.

items.statement: JV impairment on Jindal Pioneer due to book value exceeding market value despite rate recovery
items.quote: The book value was much higher. Even after the market improvement, the book value of the rig was much higher because it was a new rig which was purchased right before the downturn in the oil and gas cycle.

items.statement: Rental arrangements for hired rigs are back-to-back with ONGC deployment days
items.quote: Rentals are back-to-back arrangements. The number of days that the Rig is deployed with ONGC will be the exact number of days that Jindal Drilling will pay rental to the rig owners.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 43.9 cr equity infusion via preferential allotment; Rs 28.9 cr received by end-March including 25% warrant exercise
items.quote: In the 4 th quarter the board of directors approved the infusion of Rs. 43.9 crores of equity by way of preferential allotment of equity shares and warrants. Of this Rs. 28.9 crores approximately was received at the end of March against the preferential allotment of equity shares and 25% of the warrants that were issued.

items.statement: Total net worth infusion over last two years exceeds Rs 72 cr to strengthen balance sheet and enable asset-light scaling
items.quote: With this infusion over the last two years the company's balance sheet will be strengthened by over 72 crores of net worth infusion.

items.statement: Target mid-teens revenue growth for next 2-3 years consecutively
items.quote: I would say I think a growth in the mid-teens is something that we should be looking to achieve over the next two to three years consecutively.

items.statement: Aim to reach close to double-digit EBITDA margins over next 2-3 years as scale and procurement benefits materialize
items.value: close to the double digit EBITDA margin figures
items.quote: I think we can easily look over the next 2 to 3 years reaching close to the double digit EBITDA margin figures, but it's going to take us a couple of years to get there

items.statement: Demand was flat in Q4; overall environment subdued due to credit crunch from new MSME Act impacting retail side
items.quote: The demand for our products were flat as reflected in our quarter-on-quarter revenue numbers. The overall business environment was quite subdued towards the end of the 4 th quarter for multiple reasons, in particular the credit crunch witnessed in March due to the new MSME Act that had a significant impact on the retail side of the business.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin 2% vs 7.2% YoY and 3.9% QoQ; FY24 EBITDA margin 4% vs 5.9% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the 4 th quarter stood at 2% as against 7.2% in Q4 FY23 and down from 3.9% in Q3 FY24. For the year ended the EBITDA stood at 4% as against 5.9% in the same period last year.

items.statement: COGS rose to 66.9% in Q4 from 66.1% previous quarters due to slow-moving inventory sold at lower realization
items.quote: Our COGS compared to the previous quarter saw an increase ending at 66.9% for the quarter as compared to 66.1% that was maintained over the previous quarters. This was largely due to sale of some slow-moving inventory both in raw materials as well as finished goods at a significantly lower realization that in turn hurt our profitability.

items.statement: Marketing spend increased to 6.4% of sales in Q4 from 3.6% in previous 9 months; FY24 average 4.3% vs 4.1% FY23
items.quote: Our marketing spend in Q4 stood at 6.4% of sales as compared to 3.6% of sales in the previous 9 months. As a result, our annual average marketing spend stood at 4.3% of sales.

items.statement: Duro brand grew 1% YoY; Tower brand grew over 40% YoY; Tower now 20% of revenue vs 80% Duro
items.quote: On the product segmentation, sale of Duro range of products saw a flat return this year with only 1% growth over previous year. And our foray to the mid-price markets through our secondary brand Tower saw strong growth of over 40% for the year.

items.statement: Launched Duro Advantage Lifetime Guarantee with 9X safety on select premium products in Q4; initial trade response extremely positive
items.quote: To boost a sale of our premium products after significant research we had launched Duro Advantage Lifetime Guarantee with 9X safety on select premium products. This was rolled out throughout all markets across Q4 and initial response has been extremely positive from the trade.

items.statement: Rajkot plant annual revenue capacity Rs 265-270 cr; currently at ~70% utilization (Rs 195 cr revenue)
items.quote: Our annual capacity in terms of revenue from Rajkot is approximately 265 to 270 crores. So, we are at about 195, so we are at about 70% utilization at this point.

items.statement: Debtor days 39 vs 35 YoY; inventory days 149 vs 134 YoY; creditor days decreased to 109 from 119; cash conversion cycle increased to 79 days from 49 days
items.quote: Our debtor days has stood at 39 days of sales as compared to 35 days during the previous year. Our inventory consumption has been up by 149 days as compared to 134 days in the previous year. Our creditor days has been decreased from 109 days of consumption from 119 days in the previous quarter. As a result the cash conversion cycle has been increased to 79 days in FY24 from 49 days in FY23.

items.statement: Interest cost 2.5% of sales in FY24 vs 2.3% in FY23
items.quote: Interest cost as a percentage of sales stood at 2.5% of sales as compared to 2.3% of sales.

items.statement: Branded plywood commands 18-25% premium over non-branded segment on like-to-like basis
items.quote: But typically like-to-like products across the industry...brands tend to enjoy anywhere in the range of 18 to 25% premium over the non-branded segment.

items.statement: New MSME Act requiring 45-day payments caused one-time credit crunch in Feb-Mar impacting retail procurement across industry
items.quote: Now, the retailers, you know, the industry is 75% unorganized and 25% belong to the organized player. So, the retailers therefore by that logic to 75 of their business from micro and small enterprises and they withheld payments to the larger organizations including us as well as I believe many of our competitors and therefore they slowed down their procurement to meet their statutory liability tow

items.statement: Strong in North; investing in South and West markets for growth; balancing investment with returns
items.quote: We are strong in the northern part of the country. And that will always remain an area of focus for us. But we are also seeing a lot of growth and development happening in the south and west for us as a brand. And there will be some invested elevation for us in terms of expenses in those markets.

items.statement: No plans for furniture manufacturing or value-added products beyond plywood in next 18-24 months; will consider after balance sheet strengthening and cash flow generation
items.quote: That’s not in the horizon for the next 18 to 24 months. - Mr. Dilip Sahu: - Great. - Mr. Akhilesh Chitlangia: - Once the balance sheet is strengthened, then the company is self-generating enough cash flow then we'll probably look at some kind of product diversification. But that's not on the horizon right now

items.statement: Plywood segment expected to grow robustly over next 5-6 years; substitutes like MDF growing from lower base
items.quote: I'm very, very confident that over the next three, four years, the plywood segment is going to grow quite robustly, although we are starting from a much larger base, the other products, such as MDF, is a relatively new product. So, the base is lower. So, you know, the percentage growth will always seem higher. But I think plywood is in a sweet spot for the next 5 to 6 years

items.statement: Targets 20% CAGR in AUM and 20% ROE on consolidated basis
items.quote: Well, what we have been talking about is a CAGR of 20% and ROE of 20%.

items.statement: Expects ROE of 20% to be maintained in current year despite marginal NIM decline
items.quote: We are hopeful of maintaining the same ROE during the current year also.

items.statement: Expects credit cost in microfinance to decline to 1.5% as collections improve
items.quote: once we i mprove the microfinance collection, this will come down where we were talking about in 1.5% is credit cost

items.statement: Sees robust growth in gold loan continuing in coming quarters
items.quote: we expect a robust growth in gold loan also in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Borrowing cost increased 16 bps in Q4; dollar bond issued at slightly higher cost for diversification
items.quote: The borrowing cost has gone up by 16 basis points in Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: Expects slight dip in net interest margin but to be offset by better growth
items.quote: There could be a slight dip in the net interest margin, but it will be overcome because of better growth.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM at INR42,070 crores, up 18.7% YoY and 4.2% QoQ
items.quote: Our consolidated AUM for Q4 FY '24 was INR42,070 crores, representing 4.2% sequential growth and 18.7% Y-o-Y growth.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM at INR21,500 crores, up 8.9% YoY and 3.6% QoQ
items.quote: Gold loan AUM stands at INR21,500 crores, an improvement of 8.9% over the year ago quarter and 3.6% sequentially.

items.statement: Asirvad Microfinance AUM at INR11,881 crores including INR890 crores gold loan, up 18% YoY
items.quote: AUM stands at INR11,881 crores, including the gold loan of INR890 crores, which is up by 3 percentage Q-on-Q and 18 percentage Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Vehicle finance AUM at INR4,111 crores, up 69.1% YoY and 14.3% QoQ
items.quote: In vehicle finance business, we have reported an AUM of INR4,111 crores, which is up by 14.3 percentage Q-on-Q and up by 69.1 percentage Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Home loan AUM at INR1,510 crores, up 37.8% YoY and 6.7% QoQ
items.quote: The home loan business had a total book of INR1,510 crores, which is up by 6.7 percentage Q-on-Q and up by 37.8 percentage Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Non-gold business share now 49% of total AUM, in line with diversification strategy
items.quote: The share of non-gold business now stands at 49% of the total assets under management.

items.statement: Consolidated GNPA at 1.93% vs 1.99% previous quarter; standalone asset quality below 2%
items.quote: GNPA is at 1.93 percentage versus 1.99 percentage during the previous quarter.

items.statement: Asirvad net NPA at 1.71% with CRAR 22.79%; collection efficiency 98%
items.quote: Net NPA stands at 1.71 percentage, with a CRAR of 22.79 percentage. In vehicle finance business, we have reported an AUM of INR4,111 crores, which is up by 14.3 percentage Q-on-Q and up by 69.1 percentage Y-o-Y. Our GNPA is at 2.9 percentage as on 31st March 2024. The home loan business had a total book of INR1,510 crores, which is up by 6.7 percentage Q-on-Q and up by 37.8 percentage Y-o-Y. It op

items.statement: Vehicle finance GNPA at 2.9%, collection efficiency 100% in certain regions, 77% via NACH
items.quote: The GNPA there is around 2.9% and we will be able to maintain that below 3% going f orward also. The collection efficiency is 100 percentage in certain regions. And for us, we have given a lot of emphasis for CRM. And around 77% of these are collected through the NACH

items.statement: MSME GNPA rose to 1.7% from 1.5%; digital personal loan GNPA ~12% but only 1% of standalone AUM
items.quote: Yes, it was 1.5%, increased to 1.7%. And if you see the digital personal loan in the overall ratio mix, it has come down to 9 percentage. Because of the higher delinquency, we have tightened the underwriting.

items.statement: MFI PAR elevated due to Punjab and Rajasthan; collection machinery strengthened, improvement seen week-on-week
items.quote: We have some problems in some states like Punjab, Rajasthan, etc. So, there we have reinforced collection machinery. And we hope the collections will improve going forward.

items.statement: Gold loan yield at 22%; average LTV at 58%, well below peers; online book 57% of gold loan portfolio
items.quote: it is going on gold loan at 22% yield, and that is the reason it will not impact the profitability.

items.statement: Higher gold prices have minimal impact on ticket size; customers bring less gold rather than borrow more
items.quote: when the gold price goes up, they bring lesser quantity of gold. They don't simply avail a bigger amount simply because of that.

items.statement: Fully compliant with INR20,000 cash disbursement limit from 8th May 2024; online gold loan now 63% and rising
items.quote: we are fully compliant about that from the 8th of this month and we are disbursing loans of INR20,000 and above that only into the bank account or through online gold loan mode.

items.statement: No level playing field loss as cash limit applies to all regulated entities; no structural customer loss expected
items.quote: this is applicable to all the regulated entities. So, we don't lose any level playing field because of that.

items.statement: Auction surplus reduced from INR48 crores to INR14 crores over 15 years; reducing ~INR2 crores per quarter; seeking RBI permission for branch expansion
items.quote: So, the Rs 48 crore was the accrual over the last 15 years. So we have employed many other measures including different agencies etc., for repayment and that is the end result. It has been brought down now to around INR14 crores from INR48 crores and we have informed RBI about that and we hope that we'll get permission to open more branches with this.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents INR3,181 crores; undrawn bank lines INR6,000 crores; CP exposure 4% standalone; leverage 2.9x
items.quote: With regard to liquidity, cash and cash equivalents stand at INR3,181 crores and undrawn bank lines of INR6,000 crores as on 31st March 2024. Our CP exposure is 4 percentage in the standalone entity.

items.statement: Issued dollar bonds to diversify funding mix and reduce bank borrowing dependence
items.quote: We are also pursuing a strategy of diversifying our funding mix by reducing dependence on bank borrowings and opted for dollar bonds with this objective.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR1 per share for the quarter
items.quote: The Board has declared an interim dividend of INR1 for this quarter.

items.statement: Improving dividend quarter-on-quarter; capital allocation favors secured lending with 10% to unsecured microfinance
items.quote: Going forward at the same time, as you said, we are giving back also by improving the dividend quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Employee rationalization in gold loan due to online shift; headcount growing in non-gold business as footprint expands
items.quote: Employee rationalization is also because of more online gold loan activity. So the employee count in gold loan segment has come down while in non-gold, we are slowly expanding our footprints.

items.statement: Consolidated ROA 4.9% (up 60 bps YoY); ROE 20%; standalone CRAR 30.6%; net worth INR11,548 crores
items.quote: ROE on a consolidated basis was 20% and ROA was 4.9 percentage. Our leverage is currently only 2.9x.

items.statement: Expects double-digit growth going forward
items.quote: Like even this year, ex-COVID products, we did see a double-digit growth. And coming forward, that's what we are expecting to see a double-digit growth.

items.statement: Plans ₹1,500-1,600 crore capex in FY25
items.quote: Yes, that's the correct understanding.

items.statement: Long-term supply agreement with MNC requires ₹650-700 crore investment, operational by January 2027
items.quote: We are in the process of entering into a long-term supply agreement with an MNC and planning for a capacity addition with an estimated investment between ₹650 crores to ₹700 crores, which will be funded from internal accruals. The proposed facility is expected to be operational by January of 2027.

items.statement: Unit III near Kakinada to commence production phase-wise during FY25
items.quote: Unit III facility near Kakinada is progress ing well with production activity expected to commence phase wise during financial year 2024-25

items.statement: Kakinada Phase I commercialization expected around Q2-Q3 FY25
items.quote: Kakinada would start operations during this year, probably around Q3 is what we are looking at currently, Q2-Q3.

items.statement: Two large CS projects added to portfolio are slowly commercializing
items.quote: We have 2 huge CS projects additionally added to our portfolio, which is slowly commercializing now, and you would see the benefit.

items.statement: Seeing substantial increase in CS inquiries from existing clients, new MNCs and niche companies
items.quote: It's a mix of everything. It's existing clients, new MNCs and also other niche product companies.

items.statement: Generic volumes consistently increasing despite pricing pressure
items.quote: the volume has been consistently increasing. And if we are looking at it from the growth pers pective, I think during this time when we are going through the price erosion, we can say that we haven't lost any business. Our volumes are consistently increasing, and we are confident that it would be the same in the next year

items.statement: Pricing pressure continues in generic segment across regulated and non-regulated markets
items.quote: there is pricing constr aints across the world, we are seeing both in the regulated and nonregulated markets. It's very hard to say when this will stabilize

items.statement: Backward integration helps protect gross margins in generic business
items.quote: I mean, I would say that is a fair assumption for now.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 product mix: Generics 49%, Custom Synthesis 51%
items.quote: Product mix for generics to Custom Synthesis is 49% to 51% for the quarter and 55% to 45% for the year.

items.statement: Exports 89% of quarterly revenue, 87% for full year; US and Europe ~70% of exports
items.quote: Exports for the quarter continues to be around 89% and for the year is about 87%. Exports to U.S. and Europe is about 70% for the year.

items.statement: Q4 high sales led to higher receivables impacting cash flow; expected to normalize
items.quote: If you are looking at our quarter-on-quarter sales, the Q4 sales were quite high compared to Q1, Q2 and Q3. And when you are looking at such as huge sales, the receivables also fall into the Q1 of this year. So I think that's what is the difference that is being first seen in cash flows.

items.statement: Cash on books ₹3,980 crore as of March 31, 2024
items.quote: As of 31st March, we have cash on book of ₹3,980 crores, receivables of ₹2,156 crores and inventories of ₹3,184 crores.

items.statement: Raw material prices declined and stabilized over the year; developing indigenous sources
items.quote: Over the year, the raw material prices have seen a decline and have stabilized. However, with evol ving challenges, we have remained extremely resilient in streamlining inventory management and diversifying the supply base. Building on the Make in India concept, we are actively developing indigenous sources for most of our key raw materials, wherever possible

items.statement: Red Sea crisis increased freight costs and transit times; implemented risk mitigation measures
items.quote: The ongoing Red Sea crisis has precipitated disruptions across global supply chains. The recent quarter witnessed profound impact of the crisis globally, which manifested in increased freight cost and transit time extensions with prolonged voyages attributed due to rerouting measures.

items.statement: Constant currency growth 21% in Q4, -2% for full year FY24
items.quote: Our constant currency growth for the quarter has been at 21%, while it is negative at 2% for the year.

items.statement: Nutraceutical business ₹188 crore in Q4, ₹724 crore for FY24
items.quote: Our Nutraceutical business amounted to ₹188 crores for the quarter and ₹724 crores for the year.

items.statement: Capitalized assets ₹201 crore in Q4, ₹402 crore for FY24; CWIP ₹778 crore
items.quote: We have capitalized assets of ₹201 crores during the quarter and ₹402 crores for the year. We have a capital work in progress of about ₹778 crores.

items.statement: Future generic products regulatory submissions completed globally; commercialization upon patent expiry
items.quote: Coming to our future generics, we have submitted all regulatory submissions in various countries across the world and these products will be commercialized once they go off patent.

items.statement: Seven post-patent expiry generic opportunities identified for FY25 onwards, 1-2 molecules in FY25
items.quote: We have about seven molecules that we have identified, okay, which from FY '25 onwards, for the next 5 years will come off patent, some, maybe -- I mean they depend on the molecules. By when if there is a para IV, whether the customers will fight. So, I don't know. Right now, we know from FY '25, we have 1 or 2 molecules coming off patent, and it will continue for the next 3, 4 years.

items.statement: Seeing opportunities from BIOSECURE Act but not a simple China exit; many Phase II/III fast-track projects
items.quote: we are seeing op portunities coming our way. But it is not something that says we're exiting China and they're coming to India. We are seeing a lot of Phase II, Phase III new molecules coming to us where we are working on, some of them are on fast track

items.statement: Works with 8 of top 15 global pharma companies for CS business
items.quote: Divi's works with 8 out of the top 15 companies in the world where we get several opportunities. And we work with most of the multinationals for the CS business.

items.statement: Contrast media is a key growth engine; working with all 4 innovators at various stages
items.quote: So first, I cannot commit that I'm working with an innovator or a particular innovator. All I can say is I'm working with all the 4 innovators. Okay? And we're at various stages with them.

items.statement: Kakinada Phase I capex ~₹1,500 crore, ~₹700 crore spent so far
items.quote: In the first phase, we have already spent about, you can say, approximately ₹ 700 crores.

items.statement: Pricing erosion duration uncertain; could be 6 months to 2 years based on 2009-10 precedent
items.quote: it is difficult fo r us to say till how long the pricing erosion will be there across the markets. Because we've seen, like I told in my previous statement, we have seen similar situations for year 2009-10, I think where we had price cost, market pricing pressures, where, again, the market stabilized over time. So we have to see how long this is? Is it 1 year, 2 years? Or is it 6 months? It's hard

items.statement: Built specialized R&D lab using flow chemistry, mechanochemistry, microwave technology for green chemistry and cost efficiency
items.quote: We have set up a complete innovative lab right now, where we are using flow chemistry, we are using mechanochemistry, okay? We are using different equipments -- microwave technology. items.quote: We see our order book over a 3 to 5 years to reach about 3x of our revenues. Revenues to grow in a 15% to 20% CAGR. EBITDA to be in the 13% to 15% range, again, the triggers being more O&M, more EP, going more and more International.

items.statement: Targets INR 16,000 crore order book by end of current fiscal year
items.quote: we are looking at about a INR 16,000 crore order book by the end of this year.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR 114 billion providing 3-year revenue visibility
items.quote: Our order book continues to remain strong at about INR 114 billion, which gives us a good 3 -year revenue visibility.

items.statement: EBITDA over 13% in FY24, up from 7-8% three years ago, driven by EP, international, industrial and O&M mix
items.quote: EBITDA, again, we were 7%-8%, and today, we are over 13% in EBITDA driven by more EP, more international, more industrial and gradually increasing our O&M

items.quote: Our O&M reached 15% average. We are in the 15% to 17% kind of range now, and our focus is to take it to 20% in the medium term.

items.statement: EP model avoids construction pass-through, improving margin quality and cash flow
items.quote: We want a top line, we can bring “C” into it, but we add no value. We subcontracted, or we partner with somebody and it's a pass-through in our books. When you have pass-through, we don't make the normal margins which we make in our technology projects.

items.statement: Strong pipeline with $1 billion bids submitted in Gulf region in last 4-5 months on mega projects >$100-200 million each

items.statement: India municipal tendering slowed pre-elections; expected to resume July-August

It will take time. Maybe July - August, it will start rolling again.

items.statement: Industrial clients (oil & gas, Reliance, PSUs) value advanced recycle/desal tech; municipal adopting two-pipe recycle systems
items.quote: There's not a single oil and gas, whether it's private like Reliance, Essars of the world, or whether it's PSUs, Indian Oil, HPCL, BPCL and all that, where they don't have recycle of their wastewater, okay?

items.statement: No longer compete with Veolia (asset-heavy) or Suez (acquired by Veolia, smaller); differentiated as tech EPC/O&M player
items.quote: We don't see Veolia as competitor anymore. And this must be clearly understood. We are a technology EPC and O&M contractor and Veolia is asset-heavy. You can go Google it, go to their net. They like owning assets. We hate owning assets.

items.statement: Stricter groundwater regulations driving industrial recycle/reuse demand (Chennai, Surat, Ghaziabad examples)
items.quote: Central Water Commission is disc onnecting these connections, finding people that you can't take. If they cannot take groundwater, what is the next water they want, recycled water. Nobody is going to close their factories because government is stopping their groundwater.

items.quote: We continued to generate cash th is year as well, a free cash flow of about INR 168 crore, and we closed with a net cash positive position of INR 236 crore.

items.statement: Net cash positive for 4th consecutive year at INR 236 crore; interest cost declining sequentially
items.quote: This is the fourth year where the company and the group has generated a net cash position, and we ended the year with INR 236 crore.

items.statement: ROCE improved to ~19% from 12.3% three years ago; targeting ~20%

items.quote: If you take our average age of our top mana gement and senior leadership team is 30 years plus. So we have been all living in water sector for many-many decades.

items.quote: O&M or service business is always at least 50% to 70% better margins than the EPC business. And EP business are always about 20% better margin than the EPC business because the C is passed through and EP business, 100% of the margin is accrued by us.

items.quote: Today, more than 95% - 97% of our EPC book is either multilaterally funded, sovereign funded, federal government funded or it is backed by a letter of credit. So there is no denial of payment.

items.quote: We'll not take any contracts from state government, okay? That's a learning. But there is a price to the learning. And we told you very clearly, transparently, we told you what we have written off, okay? So there's nothing to hide there.

items.quote: So going forward, I see desalination contributing virtually 40% to 50% of your top line. items.quote: Take the Chennai desal we are talking about, one of the largest projects, 50% of the EPC is O&M for 20 years.

items.statement: Headcount ~1,500; will add people for higher competency/skills but not proportionally to revenue growth; digitization and AI improving productivity
items.quote: We need a higher competency of the staff, higher skills of the staff to manage these international clients and the challenging environment, but not necessarily the numbers. Numbers will go up, but not to that order.

items.statement: Digitalization, SCADA connectivity, central monitoring, AI adoption to optimize plant operations and improve productivity
items.quote: Now if I have a central place where I'm able to connect to all t hese plants digitally, because all of them have SCADAs and all the kind of digital requisite infrastructure, which can enable me to connect through the Internet, so we are able to even take over the plant sitting in our office

items.statement: Provisions under Ind AS for payment delays, not write-offs; no plant ever rejected for performance specifications in 100-year history
items.quote: There can be some tweaking required to be done, commissioning required to be done, some adjustment, troubleshooting, it happens in any machinery. But there's no plant built by us which are rejected by the client and it's not meeting the performance. I want to make this very clear.

items.statement: Geopolitical risk mitigated via onshore/offshore model, dual-currency contracts (USD/EUR for offshore, local currency for onshore), multilateral funding/LCs

items.statement: Carbon credits expected to monetize in 2-3 years as countries meet treaty obligations; wastewater treatment is 100% circular economy

items.statement: One City One Operator model gaining traction; canvassing with governments, interest shown but tendering stage still work in progress

items.statement: Flat revenue guidance for FY25 with significant profitability improvement

items.statement: Finance cost expected to decrease by 100-200 basis points in FY25

items.statement: Plan to open 40-45 new EBOs in FY25 across India including Western and Southern regions
items.quote: For the coming year we are again committed to open 45 to 50 EBOs across India including Western South.

items.statement: Added 55 new EBOs in FY24, total EBO count reached 411
items.quote: The Company has added 55 new EBOs in financial year 24. The total number of EBOs now have reached 411.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin declined to 13.46% from historic 21% level
items.quote: EBITDA for this year stood at Rs.143 crore which declined by 34% year-on-year and EBITDA margins were reported at 13.46.

items.statement: Price increase of 7-8% implemented in FY25 to counter discount impact
items.quote: At the same time, we have increased the price around 7% to 8% in this financial year, to counter the effect of discount which happens in the discount season.

items.statement: Home furnishing EBITDA margin improved to around 20% in FY24
items.quote: Home furnishing margins have improved this year as compared to last financial year it has reached around 20% of EBITDA as per Silver Lining and as far as Monte Carlo is concerned.

items.statement: Winter season started very late in FY24 leading to higher discounts and returns
items.quote: So there was a disturbance, basically winter season it started very late. And secondly, the merchandise was more and thirdly when it started. So at that time, the time was very less, so we have to go for higher discounts.

items.statement: Summer season consumption not picking up, industry planning discounts from next week
items.quote: But yes, the summer season is also the consumption is not picking up. So as far as retail sales are concerned, it is almost flat. So all the companies in India are planning for discounts starting from next week.

items.statement: Prices raised 7-8% in FY25 across summer and winter collections
items.quote: Yes, we have raised our prices around 7% to 8% in this financial year in summers also. And also the same hike has been taken place in the winters.

items.statement: Volume growth in woolen (19L to 21.46L) and cotton (74L to 76.06L) categories in FY24
items.quote: In case of woolen it was from 19 lakh to 21,46,000. In the case of cotton category, it was 74 lakh to 76,06,000 so, volume growth was there but only because of higher discounts and revenues.

items.statement: Home furnishing revenue Rs 141 crore (4% decline), kids revenue Rs 92 crore in FY24
items.quote: Home furnishing contributed approximately 141 crore in last year's revenues and kids contributed around 92 crore in last years revenues. But the home furnishing has declined on an annual basis from 150 to 140? De-growth of around 4%.

items.statement: Online sales grew from Rs 91 crore to Rs 111 crore, contribution increased from 6-7% to 9% in FY24
items.quote: And as far as online sale is concerned, it has improved from 91 crore to 111 crore in this financial year and the contribution which was around 6% to 7% has gone to 9% of overall sales.

items.statement: Same store sales growth (SSSG) was zero for full year FY24, -3% in Q4
items.quote: The same store growth is zero. Even it was minus three in December quarter, but the full year in Jan, Feb, March the total SSSG is zero there is no growth and no de-growth.

items.statement: Higher inventory levels and increased interest rates drove finance cost increase in FY24
items.quote: Yes because there was higher inventory in the system as compared to last year and also the interest rates have gone up as compared to last two years. So that is also actually the interest cost have gone up because of these two reasons.

items.statement: Lease accounting (IndAS) added ~Rs 4 crore to finance cost in FY24 due to new showrooms
items.quote: Whenever the new showrooms are open, due to the lease accounting as per the IndAS all the rental part is capitalized, and depreciation and finance cost is incorporated. So, in this year you can see there is an increase in finance cost due to the lease is 4 crore approximately.

items.statement: Closing unprofitable stores: 4-5 EBOs, 30 SIS, 35-50 LFS sale points contributing ~Rs 20-25 crore revenue
items.quote: They are contributing around including SIS, including EBos, including LFS should be around 20 to 25 crore.

items.statement: Geographical mix: 88-89% from North/Central/East, 11-12% from West/South in FY24
items.quote: Geographical mix for the year basically almost 88% to 89% business come from the Northern, Central and East region and thus comes the Western and Southern region.

items.statement: MBO channel becoming risky as smaller MBOs shutting down due to high expenses and discount pressure
items.quote: Actually MBO business is becoming very risky as these smaller MBOs are basically shutting down now, because they have high expensive and when they buy outright, they are not able to meet their expenses, when the discounts are there from all the brands.

items.statement: Misplanning of inventory for FY24 winter season due to over-optimism from prior 33% growth
items.quote: But, this was one of the few year where the planning was a little wrong because of higher merchandise being planned, but this year we have taken corrective action.

items.statement: Installing app at gross stores for live sales data to prevent future return surprises
items.quote: But in SIS, MBO front, we could not get exact data, we only get up to 15 days. So that is how where we fail to plug that gap, but there again we have taken a action there and we are installing one app at our gross store also to get the live data from our customer representative.

items.statement: FY24 revenue Rs 1,062 crore (-5% YoY), EBITDA Rs 143 crore (-34% YoY), net profit Rs 61 crore
items.value: Revenue: 1062 crore, EBITDA: 143 crore, PAT: 61 crore
items.quote: For the financial year ending 2024, the Company reported revenue of Rs.1062 crore on a consolidated basis representing a de-growth of 5% year-on-year. EBITDA for this year stood at Rs.143 crore which declined by 34% year-on-year and EBITDA margins were reported at 13.46. Net profit for the year stood at Rs.61 crore.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue Rs 207 crore (-13% YoY), EBITDA loss Rs 10 crore, net loss Rs 19 crore
items.value: Revenue: 207 crore, EBITDA: -10 crore, PAT: -19 crore
items.quote: For the 4th Quarter under review, the Company reported revenue of Rs.207 crore representing a decline of 13% year-on-year. We had EBITDA loss for this quarter of Rs.10 crore while net loss stood at Rs.19 crore for this quarter.

items.statement: No strategic consulting planned; management attributes FY24 issues to season not supporting inventory plans
items.quote: There is no confusion as far as understanding of market is concerned. But yes, definitely when we were growing at a 30 CAGR definitely we want to grow 15 or 24 next year also. So you plan more inventory, but the season didn't supported you, it didn't turn out the way we wanted.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth target of 20% and EBITDA margin target of 20%
items.quote: Deepak Poddar: So, given that you have said this year, we are looking at 20% revenue growth rate, right? Vimal Kumar: Yes, 20% revenue growth. Deepak Poddar: And have you said anything on the margin front? How are we looking the margin this year? Vimal Kumar: Definitely, 20% of EBITDA, we will try to get it.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 expected to show 20% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Vimal Kumar: Definitely, things are very positive in the same direction which we are talking and in the same direction it is going on and we are hoping means we are confident that there will be 20% growth and we are about 20% EBITDA margin in the first quarter itself.

items.statement: IMD predicts 106% rainfall, expecting increased agrochemical demand and good farm results
items.quote: The Indian Meteorological Department predicts this year's rainfall at 106% of the long-term average. We anticipate increased demand for our agrochemical product. On the demand side, we anticipate the season to be good and alignment with the expected good farm results.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin declined to 12% from 18% due to shift to branded sales and higher OpEx
items.quote: For the year ended March 31st 2024, revenue from operations grew by 7% to Rs. 1,873 crores compared to Rs. 1,746 crores in FY23. This growth was mainly due to a significant growth in the branded sales compared to the previous corresponding period; however, our FY24 EBITDA was Rs. 225 crores, down by around 28% from Rs. 313 crores in FY23.

items.statement: B2C EBITDA margin expected at 23%, B2B at 16-17%, blended target 20%
items.quote: Vikas Jain: So, for B2C business, last year obviously then separate year because the season was not good. Otherwise more or less , according to us, the EBITDA margin if you see for B2C would be close to say 23 or so. And for B2B could be say around 16 -17 giving us an average of 20% EBITDA which is our projection.

items.statement: Ronfen sales Rs. 250 crore in FY24 (year 2), CTPR sales Rs. 145 crore in FY24
items.quote: Vimal Kumar: Ronfen is Rs. 250 crores. This is for FY24 which we are talking and for CTPR, our sales is around Rs. 145 crores with the CTPR sales.

items.statement: Branded sales mix increased from 30% in FY23 to 60% in FY24, targeting 70% in FY25
items.quote: Vikas Jain: So, when I said March 23, our breakup was close to 30%, 70%, 30% was branded and 70% was institutional. And presently it is close to, I can say, more than 50%, close to 60% branded and 40% institutional.

items.statement: Plan to launch 4 new patented products in FY25, total 6 patented products by FY25
items.quote: In FY23, we have launched one and this FY24, we have launched another one. In FY25, we will be launching 4 new patented products, so total will be 6 products till FY25.

items.statement: FY24 capex Rs. 50 crore incurred; Rs. 200 crore 2-year plan on hold, decision by end of July
items.quote: Vikas Jain: FY24, we have incurred close to Rs. 50 crores. From April till now, not much of CAPEX has happen, but this year decision will be taken in end of July or so.

items.statement: Acquired 99% stake in Kashmir Chemicals to enhance manufacturing capacity
items.quote: Further our recent acquisition of 99% stake in Kashmir Chemicals enhances our manufacturing capacities positioning us to meet this growing demand effectively and support our farmers in achieving a prosperous season.

items.statement: Sudarshan Farm Chemicals acquisition adds R&D center, technical backward integration, and dealer network
items.quote: The second part about it is that Sudarshan also had a very good R&D center and had a very capable team and portfolio of backward integration of technical. Sudarshan was not able to leverage or capitalize on this particular fact and the reason was that they were not able to invest or be able to develop a technical plant

items.statement: Price erosion of 6% in FY24 reduced gross margin from 28% to 24%
items.quote: Vikas Jain: So, for FY24 compared to 23, so there is a price erosion of close to minus 6% which is the reason you see our yearly gross margin has gone down from 28% to 24%.

items.statement: 3 MW solar at Gajraula plant projected to save 33% on energy cost
items.quote: Additionally, we have incurred sustainability through our recent tie-up for 3 MW solar energy at our Gajraula plant. This green initiative is proj ected to save us 33% on energy c ost reaffirming our place to clean energy and environment stewardship.

items.statement: Raw material prices at rock bottom from Sep-Mar purchases, benefit to flow through in Q1-Q2 FY25
items.quote: This inventory would be liquidated in next 6 months as we see this season will pan out. So, high cost inventory, most of it will get consumed during this season. So, our new purchases are happening at low prices because the pr ices are at rock bottom and in fact increasing a little bit in China

items.statement: Dealer network expanded to 10,000+ dealers (including Sudarshan), hired 120+ on-roll employees and 1,500 field assistants
items.quote: So, with respect to dealers, we have along with Sudarshan plus Best Agro, close to more than 10,000 dealer netwok across which we have presently and employees , we have hired more than 120 people last year, so and these are on-roll employees and also there are something called field assistants which are off-roll employees. These are close to 1,500 people which have to go and meet the farmers day i

items.statement: First Indian company to manufacture both active ingredient and formulation of pyroxasulfone; partnership with Syngenta for Movondo (Rs. 300 crore market)
items.quote: We have reached a significant milestone by becoming the first Indian company who manufactured both the active ingredient and the form ulation of pyroxasulfone. The achievement not only set us apart of in the industry but also enhances our control over quality and supply chain efficiency.

items.statement: International expansion focused on Far East, Africa, Europe; holding company opened in Mauritius, multiple subsidiaries planned
items.quote: We have been focusing on the Far East, parts of Africa and also in Europe. We have already opened our holding company in Mauritius and we look forward to opening multiple international subsidiaries in this year.

items.statement: Inventory Rs. 950 crore as of March 2024, to be liquidated in 6 months; receivables Rs. 460 crore, expected to reduce further by June-July
items.quote: Vikas Jain: Mr. Pratik, presently as of March, we had close to Rs. 950 crores of inventory. This inventory would be liquidated in next 6 months as we see this season will pan out.

items.statement: Factoring of receivables to start from mid-June to accelerate cash collection
items.quote: Vikas Jain: No, not major as of now, but this would be starting from say next month onwards, from mid June onwards.

items.statement: Bank loans fully utilized due to cash flow pressure from inventory, receivables and OpEx investments; credit rating under discussion
items.quote: Vikas Jain: So, Mr. Saumitra, with respect to ratings, what I want to say is that because obviously there are cash flow issues and as I said, we are a growing company. So, we had to make investments on our inventory, on our receivables, on our OpEx. So, that was the reason that we touched the peak of our cash flow and then our bank loan and everything we are at fully utilized level.

items.statement: Acquired 99% stake in Kashmir Chemicals and Sudarshan Farm Chemicals (Rs. 130 crore for ~Rs. 250 crore turnover)
items.quote: Vikas Jain: Sudarshan, till last March 23 it had close to Rs. 30 crores turnover, but March 24 we are going to end up with close to more than Rs. 200 crores of turnover, so it is around Rs. 250 crores. So, effectively we are paying just half of the turnover evaluation and also the cash flow for this is minimal because after assisting f or all these liabilities and all, we are just about paying clo

items.statement: India Crop Protection Chemicals market estimated at US$2.48B (2024) to US$3.13B (2029), CAGR 4.72%
items.quote: As per mode of intelligence, the India Crop Protection Chemicals market is estimated to reach US $2.48 billion by 2024 and US $3.13 billion by 2029 with indicating a CAGR of 4.72% from 2024 to 2029.

items.statement: Seasonal failure in Kharif and Rabi led to 46% YoY revenue decline in Q4 FY24 and EBITDA loss of Rs. 67 crore
items.quote: Just to reiterate, as Vimalji had already mentioned, revenue from operations for Q4 stood at Rs. 135 crores compared to Rs. 254 crore in Q4 of FY23. This represents year- on-year decline of 46% due to an unexpected seasonal failure in early quarters of FY24 as against the normal season conditions in the same period last year

items.statement: High inventory days (190+) and receivables cycle volatility due to seasonal nature; dependent on good monsoon for normalization
items.quote: Vikas Jain: Yes, as you rightly mentioned for this industry, the cycle is generally very difficult and volatile because it all depends upon the seasonal condition. But this part because we are a growing company, we can say that this is just about the second year where we are entering full-fledged into our dealer business model.

items.statement: FY24 order book at INR 6,049 crore, up 20% YoY
items.quote: The company closed the financial year with a highest ever outstanding order book of INR 6,049 crore, a YoY growth of 20%.

items.statement: FY24 order inflow at INR 3,498 crore, meeting guidance of over INR 3,000 crore
items.quote: During the yea r, the company received highest ever order inflow to the tune of INR 3,498 crore (excluding GST). We had expected an order inflow in excess of INR 3,000 crore and we have fairly achieved our order inflow guidance for this financial year

items.statement: FY25 order inflow guidance of nearly INR 3,500 crore
items.quote: For FY25, considering our bid book and the upcoming projects, I expect an order inflow of nearly INR 3,500 crore.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of around 15%
items.quote: As for revenue, I still believe that revenue growth will be around 15% from here.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance of 10% to 11%
items.quote: So, this year also, we would like to keep our margins within that range.

items.statement: FY24 revenue at INR 2,462 crore, up 28% YoY
items.quote: Overall, on the financial performance of the year, the company closed the financial year at a highest ever revenue of INR 2,462 crore, 28% YoY growth.

items.statement: FY24 capex of INR 150 crore, including INR 79 crore for precast facilities
items.quote: During FY 24, company has incurred capex of 150 crores including 2.88 crores of CWIP. Capex incurred for precast facilities amounts to 79 crores.

items.statement: Capex guidance of 3-4% of revenue excluding precast-related spend
items.quote: Normally, capex should not exceed 3-4%, but here, the capex is high since precast orders always require some capex due to the size of the orders and delivery timeline. This is the only reason why the capex has gone high, otherwise, capex still be taken as 3-4% of the revenue can, which is a standard practice and has been observed for the past six-seven years.

items.statement: Raised INR 244 crore via QIP in April 2024
items.quote: During April 2024, the Company successfully raised INR 244 crores by the way of qualified institutional placement and successfully placed wi th marquee domestic mutual funds and FIIs participating in the issue

items.statement: Repaid INR 188 crore debt from QIP proceeds; fund-based utilisation to reduce
items.quote: Yeah. So, basically out of this QIP money, we have already repaid INR188 crores of the debt, which was on a maximum utilisation as on 31st March. So, currently to that extent, that amount has reduced and going forward we will be using it as and when required for any future projects. So compared to FY24 definitely the utilisation of fund-based facilities will be on a lower side and in the same way

items.statement: Net working capital days at 35 as of March 31, 2024
items.quote: Working capital days are as follows: Debtor days are 50 Creditor days are 62 Inventory days are 47 Total net working capital days are 35

items.statement: Settled Surat Diamond Bourse dispute; SDB to pay INR 170 crore plus GST over certified value
items.quote: On 15th May 2024, an out-of-court settlement had been reached between the Company and SDB on the basis constructive dialogue, discussion and negotiations, effectively resolving all the disputes between the parties. Under the Settlement, SDB has agreed to pay a total amount of INR 170 crore over and above INR 1,790 crores already certified by them.

items.statement: Expect INR 100+ crore from SDB within 30 days, balance within FY25
items.quote: We are waiting for the final certificate probably next week only. So, that 50% you can expect in one month and 50% can be extended to one year.

items.statement: Bid pipeline at INR 5,746 crore including INR 2,000 crore Delhi project
items.quote: Shravan, my bid pipeline will be exactly INR5,746 crore. I will name each and every project because it is a big list. So I didn't mention it but you can hear now again.

items.statement: Precast capacity targeting INR 350-400 crore revenue in next 1-2 years
items.quote: I think within next 3 or 4 years, we should be in position to generate minimum year-on-year growth of about 25%-30% from what we are doing today and maximum we can generate a revenue of INR350 to INR400 crores maybe after 1 year or so.

items.statement: Precast margins expected to reach 14-15% in future
items.quote: In general, yes, we can think about 14%-15% margin in future because now the technology is being understood well by the market and more and more inquiries are coming from industrial side.

items.statement: Not engaging in aggressive bidding despite competition for large projects
items.quote: See, it is not like that somebody is quoting on aggressive side. So, we also start bidding on an aggressive side. Still we are going cautiously and we expect the order inflow about in the range of INR3,500 crores last year also.

items.statement: FY24 revenue CAGR of 30% over past 7 years
items.quote: The revenue of the company has grown at 30% CAGR over the past 7 years, EBIDTA at 22% and PAT at 17% CAGR growth.

items.statement: Arbitration for Bhiwandi in cross-examination; Pandharpur arbitration yet to start, may take 6 months
items.quote: Bhiwandi I think cross examination is going on. So, probably once the cross examination from their side is over, further it can take 2 or 3 months for the final conclusion on the arbitration side. Pandharpur is yet to start. Pandharpur cross examination is yet to start. So, probably we can say six months from here for Pandharpur.

items.statement: Government share of order book increased to ~70%; private investment slower
items.quote: It is majorly this percentage whether it is 50-50 or 60-40 or 30-70. We can't predict throughout our whole year. It is a process wherein private companies' investment is coming little bit less.

items.statement: Targeting net cash position by end of FY25 with SDB and UP collections
items.quote: That's right and that's what we are expecting provided we get all the money which we have just discussed about INR50-80 crores from UP projects and INR225 crores from Surat.

items.statement: Overhead costs increased to 5% of revenue from 3.5-4% previously, pressuring margins
items.quote: Because on the construction side, the cost which is required on the overheads, previously we were able to manage at 3.5%-4%. This year we have been doing at 5%. So, incremental cost of the staff and the overall labour cost has also impacted this year.

items.statement: Precast capex largely complete; future mould capex minimal at 15-20 moulds
items.quote: Last two years we have been able to invest majorly on the building side. We had expanded this into double size and that was proba bly on the infrastructure side. That order from L&T where we required a new mould. Otherwise, as far as building is concerned, we have sufficient moulds. Or on the building side, even if we have to expand, we have one-one line pending. So, that will be not more than 15-

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue at INR 649 crore, down 11% YoY
items.quote: Revenue from operations for the quarter is at INR 649 crore vs INR 727 crore, decreased by 11% YoY basis

items.statement: Q4 FY24 PAT margin at 2.3% vs 6.3% YoY
items.quote: Net profit for the quarter is at INR 15 cr vs INR 46 crore, reduced by 67% YoY basis. PAT Margin is at 2.3% vs 6.3%.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue Rs 162 cr vs Rs 212 cr in Q4 FY23 due to subdued US demand and lower global shrimp prices
items.quote: The net revenue for Q4 FY'24 came in at Rs.162 crores as against Rs.148 crores in Q3 of the same fiscal year, but lower than the revenue of Rs.212 crores in the Q4 of last fiscal, that is FY'23, mainly due to the subdued demand from our key market which is USA and overall lowered global shrimp prices.

items.statement: USA imposed preliminary countervailing duty of 4.36% on Indian frozen shrimp
items.quote: On top of that , the preliminary countervailing duties impo sed by the USA on Indian frozen shrimp at 4.36% also acted as an additional dampener.

items.statement: EU sales grew 31% YoY in FY24, EU share rose to 30% from 19%
items.quote: On the positive side, however, our shrimp sales to the market, such as the European Union continue to do well , sales to the EU posted a growth of 31% year -on-year in F Y'24. Consequently, the share of the EU in the overall sales mix increased to 30% in FY'24 from 19% last year.

items.statement: EU regulatory approvals for Ready-to-Eat products pending since 2019; expected progress after new government formation in June
items.quote: It's been five years since we have been waiting, because as I mentioned, it was around 2019 no approvals have been given and our capability of Ready-to-Eat was available since 2020 basically FY'21.

items.statement: US subsidiary setup progressing, pending Indian regulatory approvals; benefits expected from FY25
items.quote: The work on this front is progressing and actually pending certain regulatory approvals in India and which we are hoping to see the benefits coming in from FY'25 onwards.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced by Rs 60 cr from Rs 167 cr (Mar 2022) to Rs 107 cr (Mar 2024); debt-to-equity 0.22x
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, gross debt was reduced by Rs.60 crores from Rs.167 crores as of 31st March 2022 to Rs.107 crores as of 31st March 2024 , and the total debt -to-equity remains at a comfortable level of 0.22 times.

items.statement: Debtor days increased from 38 to 48 days due to Red Sea crisis; receivables from scripts/duty drawbacks expected in Q1 FY25 to reduce borrowings
items.quote: our major working capital is with regard to our debtors, which is our receivables and which was of course last year it was 38-days, but this year it has increased by 10-days, but that's mainly because our shipments with all the Red Sea crisis, which is there has been taking longer duration.

items.statement: Ecuador anti-dumping duty 10.58% and CVD 2.89% (preliminary); India CVD 4.36% and ADD 1.35%; level playing field emerging
items.quote: Ecuador has also been levied an anti -dumping, this is preliminary , anti-dumping duty of 10.58%. And, also along with Ecuador, again, Indonesia on a preliminary basis has been awarded an anti-dumping duty rate of 6.3%.

items.statement: Gross margins held due to EU market mix; RTE products fetch ~$0.50/kg higher margin
items.quote: With regard to the gross margins, of course, it's more on the market mix for sure , that EU business growing definitely during the quarter , has balanced out to maintain that even though we have had a huge drop with regard to our US sales in that quarter.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization dropped to 33% from 45%; RTE capacity added 5,000 MT but utilization low due to US demand drop
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier, with regard to overall capacity utilization, that also has dropped compared to last year; it is 33% currently, last year it was 45%, that is overall capacity utilization.

items.statement: RTE sales share fell to 16% in FY24 from 22% in FY23 due to US demand drop
items.quote: last year it was around 22% , but however this year because of the overall drop in demand it has dropped down to 16% in FY'24.

items.statement: Farmers reduced acreage and stocking densities due to decade-low farm gate prices; lease costs declining
items.quote: there definitely has been some conservative approach with the farmers especially towards the end of FY '24 and the beginning of FY '25, there's been some conservative approach because of very stable low farm gate pricing environment.

items.statement: Depreciation to reduce by Rs 1 cr per quarter (Rs 4 cr annually) after useful life reassessment
items.quote: Rs.1 crore can be reduced from next quarter onwards compared with the previous year.

items.statement: Some US customers switched to Ecuador due to shorter shipping time (1 week vs 5-8 weeks)
items.quote: they are at like a week sailing time from Ecuador to US ports, it's only a week, while today with regard to India, it takes anywhere between five to seven weeks, from almost five to eight weeks sometimes.

items.statement: Ecuador and Indonesia now face preliminary duties in US for first time; India at combined 5.71% vs Ecuador ~13.5%
items.quote: currently, even though on preliminary basis, we are at 5.71%, while Ecuador again that is also on preliminary side having an anti-dumping duty of 10.58%.

items.statement: No clear signals of US demand recovery; waiting for inflation/interest rate relief and lower gasoline prices
items.quote: we have not seen any such signals as of now or any indications as of now. There is a pressure for sure in the US market in general.

items.statement: RoDTEP and duty drawback schemes continuing; workings being prepared to potentially lower US CVD
items.quote: Currently, we have no information that it's going to be discontinued as such. However, with regard to the RoDTEP scheme and the duty drawback scheme , the Indian shrimp industry is awaiting for certain information also.

items.statement: Hatchery sales grew marginally from Rs 77M to Rs 90M; operations consolidated to main South Andhra hatcheries
items.quote: last year it was around Rs.77 million and this year it's been Rs.90 million, but it's nothing significantly increased.

items.statement: Exploring new markets in Scandinavia and Asia to offset US slowdown
items.quote: we are even looking at exploring the Scandinavian side of the European Union . Going to FY'25, we are exploring newer markets there too, along with a few other markets in Asia.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 15% for both consumables and equipment segments; EBITDA margin guidance 20-22% for consumables, 10-11% for equipment
items.value: 15% revenue growth; 20-22% consumables EBITDA margin; 10-11% equipment EBITDA margin
items.quote: Revenue, we expect the market guidance should be about 15% on a group, overall group level basis. EBITDA margins in the range of 20% to 22% for the consumable business segment, 10% to 11% for the equipment business segment.

items.statement: Consumables EBITDA margin sustainable range 20-22% on full year basis; Q4 seasonally stronger at ~30%
items.quote: On an overall basis, if you see on a full year basis, the consumable business segment gives a EBITDA margin of about 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Group order book INR 630 crore as of March 2024, up 30% (INR 150 crore) from start of FY24
items.quote: We also have a strong order book at a group level of INR 630 crores as of March 24 and vis-a-vis an order book of INR 480 crores at the beginning of the year i.e. an increase of INR 150 crores i.e. 30% during FY 23-'24.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization 60-65% in FY24, similar to FY23; company maintains 60-65% benchmark and adds capacity as needed
items.quote: the capacity utilization generally on an overall basis the capacity utilizations are about 65% for us. Srishti: And what was the same for FY23? Sharad Kumar Khaitan: It remains around the same level about 60%, 65% because we keep adding new capacities when need arises for us

items.statement: Supply chain challenges eased in Q4 FY24 but not eliminated; Red Sea crisis and West Asia tensions caused transportation delays leading to INR 30 crore higher finished goods inventory and ~INR 70 crore revenue deferral to Q1 FY25
items.quote: Supply chain challenges eased in Q4 of FY '24 but were not completely eliminated and resulted in transportation delays due to events ranging from the Red Sea crisis and the geopolitical tensions in West Asia. Such transportation delays resulted in higher finished goods inventory of approximately INR 30 crores in the consumables business segment, which, had that not been the case, would have result

items.statement: Copper and gold together constitute ~75% of consumables business; copper growth 2.2% in FY24 with headwinds in H1 2024 but strong outlook for 2025 from Russia and Congo projects
