items.quote: Another very noticeable and moment of pride was our win, our largest ever single order worth 1510 crores, which we won from NMDC Data Center Private Limited, which is also popularly called as Yotta.

items.statement: Gross margin declined from 5.7% to 5.35% due to product mix and sales cycles; outlook around 5%
items.quote: So, our gross margins have come down from 5.7 to 5.35%. It's a combination of product mix and the, you know, sales cycles and product mix so the range normally what we give and the margins are in that range only.

items.statement: Large data center orders have constrained margins but improve ROCE/ROE due to working capital structure
items.quote: In large projects, obviously margins are always constrained so I would only say at this stage that the margin for large projects will be normalized.

items.statement: No significant capex planned; only minor leasehold developments for volume growth
items.quote: Ours is not a capital expenditure side. Buying some few leasehold developments, which may, you know, happen because of the volumes increase or something like that otherwise we don't see any much of capital investment.

items.statement: Setting up first-ever embedded lab in Bangalore; launching LOEM Make in India and visual display verticals
items.quote: We are setting up our own laboratory for embedded business where we can live demo the products and solutions so this embedded lab, the first ever in India will be set up in Bangalore.

items.statement: Added 7 new brands (ViewSonic, Alcatel-Lucent, Numeric, Afox, JBL, Philips, American Megatrends) and TP-Link surveillance; total 60 brands
items.quote: Currently Rashi peripherals, we have 60 brands distribution portfolio, a basket of 60 brands, some of the new brands that we have added in the last one year noticeable are ViewSonic, Alcatel-Lucent, Numeric, Afox, JBL business expansion, Philips expansion and American Megatrends.

items.statement: Enterprise business grew ~70% YoY; embedded business grew ~92% YoY from small base
items.quote: Last year we had approximately 70% growth only in the enterprise business and in the coming year, we continue to maintain that momentum. On the embedded business which is our newer baby, we are just setting up the base and of course, we have a very small base right now but even in terms of size, we had almost 92% growth on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Expanding beyond 700 towns via roadshows in towns 51-100 to educate retailers and increase brand penetration
items.quote: We are organizing a seminar come training program in 51 to 100 th town of India. So, we are excluding the top 50 towns of India and we are going to have roadshows starting from 51 to 100 towns of India.

items.statement: Working capital days stable at 54-55 days; target 45-50 days; inventory days corrected 5% YoY in Q4
items.quote: Working capital days for our business, they have remained in the same range of 54 days around and we have been able to maintain ROCE of 13.39% as against the last year's ROCE of 14.21 %.

items.statement: Consciously working to reduce inventory days from 54-55 to 45-50 range
items.quote: Usually, our average inventory cycle ranges between 45 to 50 days. We were hoping that this comes down further, but it has not come down and we are consciously working towards how do we bring this down.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded from A to A+ with positive outlook by Crisil in March; debt reduced to ~Rs 600 cr post IPO proceeds utilization
items.quote: Our credit rating in the month of March from Crisil improved from A to A+ with a positive outlook. Based on our FY numbers, we hope that Crisil will further evaluate us to improve this further.

items.statement: IPO raised ~Rs 750 cr; Rs 50 cr remaining in IPO account utilized on April 1 for debt repayment
items.quote: With the IPO, with the public listing the capital that we raised for about 750 crores, 700 crores incremental capacity has been created. Most of this has gone into a working capital cycle purposes.

items.statement: Forex managed via 45-day supplier credit and 20-50% forward booking; inventory repriced at current exchange rates
items.quote: We have about 50-55 days of inventory, we get about 45 days of credit from all our suppliers on an open credit. So that means whatever we've imported at an exchange, we have a 45 days credit and window before they become due for payments.

items.statement: Data center competition limited to 5-6 players; large project wins uncertain
items.quote: There are some more projects under discussion but it is too early to comment when and how and who will get this because there is equal competition across on these large projects.

items.statement: Empowering 450 salespeople with SAP CRM for live data, visit tracking on smartphones
items.quote: This year we are going to empower all our 450 salespeople by CRM, which is also provided by SAP. So, all our sales people on their palm or on their smartphone will have all the data information, visit tracking live.

items.statement: Exceptional item: non-compete fee from subsidiary (0.5% of revenue) classified as non-recurring
items.quote: It is a non-compete agreement you know to give up on business and not to compete in future by one of subsidiary, it is insignificant subsidiary constituting only 0.5% of our total revenue.

items.statement: MRR potential from current CAPEX expected to reach INR 14-16 crore over next couple of months
items.quote: we believe that like the MRR potential with the current CAPEX that we have already done would be of the order of anywhere between like 14 to 16 crores from the current MRR number like we should be able to achieve over like next couple of months.

items.statement: Ideal FY25 CAPEX target of INR 800 crore or $100 million over next 12 months
items.quote: In an ideal world, like we would like to end another $100 billion or about Rs.800 crores over the next 12 months.

items.statement: FY25 CAPEX to be funded via bank financing, leasing partners, vendor financing and equity raise
items.quote: It's will have to be a combination of things including like financing from banks and leasing partners and vendor financing and some equity raise.

items.statement: FY24 CAPEX was INR 185 crore vs INR 35 crore in FY23
items.quote: there is a 185 crore CAPEX in FY 24 which was 35 crore last year.

items.statement: Demand for cloud GPU workloads growing exponentially; industry shifting from CPU to GPU-centric workloads
items.quote: The demand is only going to increase as the industry shifts to more cloud GPU centric workloads. That demand is only going to increase in the industry.

items.statement: Current CAPEX already deployed on cloud platform; sales cycle typically one to two quarters
items.quote: For the CAPEX done, is already deployed on our cloud platform, how quickly can we sell is like something that we do not make a statement on.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA INR 48 crore, up 45% YoY; Q4 FY24 EBITDA INR 15 crore, up 68% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA is 48 crore, representing a growth of 45% on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: FY24 revenue INR 95 crore, up 43% YoY; Q4 FY24 revenue INR 29 crore, up 67% YoY
items.quote: revenue from operations stood at INR 95 crore representing a growth of around 43% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Operated in red ocean for 15 years; differentiation via software, workload insight and product development
items.quote: for the past 15 years, as a business, as a company we have operated in what is called a Red Ocean. So, we have never shied away from competition, we continue to build up our portfolio of software, and services and solutions with a view to develop a better understanding of the workloads that our customers are bringing to us.

items.statement: GPU supply constraints easing; normal integration lead times expected going forward
items.quote: we don’t feel that in the future, that there is going to be that sort of shortage. And you will need like very, very special relationships to kind o f like move ahead of the queue

items.statement: Nearly 3,000 active customers across SMEs, startups, higher education, research and partner ecosystem
items.quote: currently we service nearly 3000 active customers.

items.statement: AI/ML platform Tir adding training, inference, deployment and data pipeline features; integrated with infrastructure services
items.quote: we have made very rapid progress on many new features and services. And we will continue to release those new features on our AI/ML platform called Tir within the workload environment for the AI/ML workloads, where we take care of the ability to do all four major things.

items.statement: Data center services (power, bandwidth, base) are major variable cost; expense proportion declines slowly with volume
items.quote: the services would be like in the same proportion as the revenue or a way that they will increase with the revenue in a certain incremental percentage fashion. Now again, it's the question of like, there is a broad number that is there and broadly that percentage will kind of like as the volume increases, like go down slowly.

items.statement: Right-of-use assets mainly for lease-to-own equipment; data center services rented not leased
items.quote: leasing relate to the equipment and this is all lease to own kind of equipment.

items.statement: Team size 140-150; organic hiring continues across technology, marketing and operations
items.quote: Broadly, we have claim to somewhere between 140 to 150 people in the team. So approximately about 150 and we continue to grow the team organically.

items.statement: Data center outage at older Noida facility due to vendor UPS issue; migrating customers to new Greater Noida facility over next couple of years
items.quote: our plan over next couple of years is to kind of slowly migrate without disruption all the customers in this facility, and obviously prioritize those custome rs who are kind of willing to put in the effort today to help them migrate over to our new facility

items.statement: Asset turn lower bound 0.55-0.6x; no upper bound in software-driven cloud model
items.quote: there is a lower bound for that which we can predict, which is like somewhere, anywhere between say 0.55 to 0.6. But that ’s the lower bound. But, o n the other hand, like there is no upper bound in a software driven

items.statement: Government AI announcements and support indicate exponential data center capacity growth for AI/ML over next five years
items.quote: one of course that the data center capacity required for artificial intelligence is going to kind of, exponentially grow over next five years or so. And that data center capacity is going to be applied majorly by AI/ML workload.

items.statement: Short-term GPU CAPEX all directed to Nvidia; open to evaluating alternatives like AMD if they offer specialized capabilities
items.quote: in the short term all our GPU investments that I see are definitely all going to Nvidia. Now, there is obviously no exclusivity as such in the sense that tomorrow if somebody is able to bring more capable check for any specialized used cases, we would definitely evaluate that independently.

items.statement: Equity raise process underway over next couple of quarters
items.quote: we are working on it, like over like next couple of quarters, I guess.

items.statement: FY24 net profit INR 22 crore, up 121% YoY; Q4 FY24 net profit INR 4 crore, up 39% YoY
items.quote: net profit of 22 crore, which witnessed a growth of around 121% on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Self-service public cloud platform continues to serve well; percentage of customers on self-service model growing
items.quote: the percentage of customers being served from our self-service, public cloud platform where we provide a lot of software support, which is very, very similar to what the hyper scalar cloud platforms do continues to serve us well.

items.statement: InfiniBand 3.2 Tbps deployed to handle unstructured data motion for AI/ML workloads at scale
items.quote: why do you need a 3.2 Tbps InfiniBand is to address the data in motion at these scales. Because these are the scales required for dealing with organizational data which is unstructured.

items.statement: Depreciation policy changed from WDV to straight-line from April 2023 per Companies Act
items.quote: The depreciation was changed from April '23, where we have changed from WDV to straight line method in line with the Companies Act.

items.statement: Internal organic revenue growth target of 25% for FY25, with inorganic growth on top
items.quote: As I said, internally, we have taken targets to grow by about 25%. It could be a couple of percentage points higher or lower, but that's what we take as internal targets.

items.statement: Long-term North Star target of ₹1,000 crore revenue in 6-9 years organically and inorganically
items.quote: But we have said we have spoken and agreed internally that that's the North Star at the moment that we are looking at.

items.statement: Expect margins to reach 19-20% range in 3-5 years as international services mix increases
items.quote: but absolutely, our expectation i s that if we're going to look at our margins in three to five years' ti me, they will be in the range that you are mentioning

items.quote: When we work in India, our margins on services are typically in the range of 22% to 25%. But when you are working with customers, let's say, in the United States, our margins are in the range of 50% to 55% on services.

items.statement: Net new customer acquisition in US improved, now competing with SAP/Oracle/Infor for greenfield deals
items.quote: We have had some really good (customer) acquisitions and as I said, this is where we are now competing there with the likes of maybe an SAP or Oracle or Infor.

items.statement: Increasing customer interest in IPA, copilots, and data engineering driven by Gen AI
items.quote: Increasingly, more number of customers have been showing interest in exploring the IPA, the co-pilots, and the data engineering.

items.statement: Repeat plus recurring revenue 88% for FY24, 79% for Q4 FY24

items.quote: We are now deciding to increase our investments on the sales and presales side in this region. Increasingly, more number of customers have been showing interest in exploring the IPA.

items.quote: We are currently in conversation with one data engineering company. What has not changed, the Board of Directors ... you're familiar with ... other than maybe some pictures changing on this slide.

items.statement: Headcount 360 (up from 350); attrition 7% in Q4, 16% for FY24 including performance exits
items.quote: The attrition rate during the quarter was 7%, and during the entire year, it stood at 16%.

items.quote: Our domestic services revenue was 35.2% for the year, and the U.S. was 45.8%, Africa, 9%, APAC, 6.6%, and Europe, 3.4%.

items.statement: Microsoft Dynamics 365 grew 23%, Azure 31%, Intelligent Cloud 21% in Microsoft Q3
items.quote: So the Intelligent Cloud business for Microsoft has grown by 21% as per the results of Q3 for them. The Azure Plus business grew by 31%, and the Dynamics 365 by 23%.

items.statement: IP-led solutions carry higher margins; all IP revenue retained after R&D investment
items.quote: Yeah, absolutely. I mean, whatever we get from the IP is all for us. And, of course, we have to keep investing in building these products and keeping solutions updated.

items.statement: Short-term loans/advances increased to ₹10 crore, primarily advances to subsidiaries
items.quote: Short-term loans, I need to get into the details. So it's basically, advances given to our subsidiaries.

items.statement: Cash balance ₹115 crore; primary use for acquisitions and international growth investments
items.quote: The top of our mind, of course is acquisitions. Inorganic growth, it's certainly going to be the biggest application of those funds.

items.statement: Key risk is rising talent costs; geographic diversification provides insulation from local turbulence
items.quote: So that's one part of it. The other part of it is that, well, if we are sloppy, if we don't do our job, then anyways, anything can happen.

items.statement: Expanding consulting and sales teams in US and India; adding campus and lateral hires
items.quote: We also need to increase the strength of our consulting and salespeople on the field; and that's an area that we are increasing our investments in.

items.statement: Three revenue components: consulting, product (Microsoft + IP), implementation/support services
items.quote: When we provide a solution to our customer, it has, I would say - broadly three components. There's an initial consulting piece involved in the overall engagement.

items.statement: No specific regulatory risks mentioned; geographic spread mitigates local turbulence
items.quote: But I would say the technology business has invariably done better even in adverse situations, as I was saying and just to repeat, how we saw the reaction of the world during pandemic.

items.statement: Certified Great Place to Work; 900+ implementations; Microsoft Inner Circle awards; multi-country operations
items.quote: We were, once again, certified as a Great Place to Work. We have done in excess of 900 implementations, ... close to a 1000 now, multiple times awarded with Microsoft's Inner Circle and other awards.

items.statement: First truck rollout expected end of August to mid-September 2025
items.quote: So that means, the first truck will be rolled out, we expect that to be sometime end of August, middle of September.

items.statement: Bangalore plant capacity of 7 vehicles simultaneously with 6-week turnaround targeting 30-40 trucks annually
items.quote: Seven at a time is what we are trying to do. So, we should be able to turn around something like 30 to 40 trucks per year, approximately.

items.statement: Received order for 4 runway rubber removal machines from Airports Authority of India to be integrated at Bangalore plant
items.quote: Today, you have received an order from the Airports Authority of India, for the four runway removal machines. So, will you be manufacturing those in the Bangalore plant or…? Unnikrishnan Nair: Yes. Manufacturing in the sense, we will be integrating it

items.statement: Margins slightly reduced due to forward investment in employee costs for new manufacturing plant
items.quote: And also, there is a slight reduction in the margins that is due to we are keeping the new manufacturing plant in view. We have appointed, we had to incur the employee cost.

items.statement: Borrowing cost reduced from INR74.47 lakhs to INR36.14 lakhs by closing high-interest term loans
items.quote: And then our borrowing cost has been reduced from INR74.47 lakhs to INR36.14 lakhs. The primary reason is that the term loans which are having more than 15% interest rates, which we have closed during the year

items.quote: Our cash flow from operations compared to the previous year, which was negative INR9.27 crores. But in the current financial year, we have increased by INR11 crores, which is now INR2.05 crores positive.

items.statement: Current ratio reduced from 3.28 to 2.53 due to good operating collections
items.quote: Our current ratio compared to previous year has reduced due to the good operating collections, the current ratio has come down from 3.28 to 2.53.

items.statement: Incurred INR4.42 crores on factory building under capital work in progress and INR20.46 lakhs on SAP implementation
items.quote: And we have incurred INR4.42 crores towards building our factory, which was during the financial year end, which was still under final completion, which is getting completed now.

items.statement: Added grass cutting and collection machines for airfields and firefighting chemical foam distribution to product portfolio
items.quote: And last very recently, we also entered into a new field, which is the grass cutting and collection from airport, airfield areas where the grass has to be grown to keep the dust under control. We also have now entered into distributing firefighting chemical form.

items.statement: Targeting cost reduction by avoiding European labour rates (EUR63/hour) through Indian assembly using experienced local engineers
items.quote: When it comes to manufacturing and assembly, a German engineer will charge you something like EUR63 per hour for assembly. items.statement: No single competitor across full product range; segment-wise competition from OshKosh, Iveco but no domestic player with fully ICAO-compliant crash fire tenders
items.quote: Therefore, when you talk about competition, we do not have a single competitor. We have competition segment -wise. And the advantage that we have is, see, let's say, one of our competitors is an American company called OshKosh.

items.quote: One example is Gurgaon. They have implemented our pump system all through the corporate office complexes in Gurgaon. So we need to meet that if we have to bring in FDI and process their equipment.

items.statement: ICAO compliance required for airport licensing; DGCA mandates maintenance records from OEM or accredited agency for airport category renewal
items.quote: ICAO is International Civil Aviation Organization, whose compliance are required for licensing your airport. So, this is one example. It more or less applies to runway rubber removal, runway friction tester.

items.statement: Post-sale service revenue mandated by DGCA regulatory requirements for airport fire truck maintenance and certification
items.quote: For example when you sell a fire truck to an airport the statutory agency DGCA tells the customer I need to see every now and then the maintenance record of the maintenance agency which has to be either the OEM or their accredited agency.

items.quote: I'm pleased to inform you that the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR2 or 200% per share of the face value of INR1. items.quote: You may recall that this time last year, we have set out the capex plan of about INR4,500 crores by FY '27, almost 50% of which comprised of these 2 cryogenic LPG terminals in Pipavav and Mangalore as well as the various liquid expansions in Haldia, Mangalore, JNPT, Kandla, and Kochi, which are proceeding on time and on budget. items.quote: Net debt-to-equity ratio improved as on 31 March 2024 is 0.30x, as compared to 0.34x in the previous year.

items.statement: Interest cost guidance of Rs 17-18 crores for FY25; depreciation Rs 21-22 crores standalone plus Rs 4-5 crores for new capex
items.quote: So, interest cost for the next financial year, we are expecting around 17 to 18 crore, and depreciation, we can assume around, for the current side, means for the standalone side, will be around 21 crore, 22 crores, and for the consolidated side, it will go up with the new CAPEX, say 4 to 5 crore more.

items.statement: Export contribution increased from 30% to 44% driven by Specialty Ingredients and Fragrance & Flavor divisions
items.quote: So, I think the two major contributors for the increase in the export contribution is the Specialty Ingredients Division as well as the Fragrance and Flavor Division.

items.statement: Product mix remains roughly one-third each across three divisions; camphor division EBITDA positive
items.quote: So, I think, Dhwanil, we will continue to be one -third, one -third, one -third, minor sub- aberrations happening in a few quarters, depending on one of the division having a little bit more or a little bit less, but we are pretty confident that in the few quarters from now, we should stay in the same configuration.

items.statement: Camphor and terpene chemicals face challenging competitive landscape with supply far outstripping demand
items.quote: Currently, our supply far outstrips the demand. This excess capacity has led to tremendous pressure on pricing for products like camphor powder and other terpene chemicals.

items.statement: Asset turnover for new Mahad plant ~1.2x; brownfield expansion ~1.5x on gross block
items.quote: on the existing capacity, because see it will, the answer will not be justifiable because we have the old plant also actually. Pradeep Rawat: Yeah, on the gross block. Girish Khandelwal: Yeah, so the new capacity in the last fi ve year which we did, we are getting asset turn of around 1.5

items.statement: Camphor overcapacity from India and China expected to persist; weak China demand may increase dumping
items.quote: I think just to add to what Dharmil just said, you also have a third element where there is a lot of camphor that's produced in China which also will have a tendency to kind of find its home in India. So, there are multiple capacity additions that have happened in India as well as globally.

items.statement: TMD order book at Rs 3,520 Crore as of March 31, 2024, down from Rs 5,500 Crore a year earlier
items.quote: The current order book is Rs 3520 Crore. The previous order book was Rs. 5500 Crore

items.statement: Active TMD order book is around Rs 2,300 Crore within the total order book
items.quote: The active order book within this is around Rs 2300 Crore.

items.statement: TMD order inflow for FY24 was closer to Rs 700 Crore, about 60% of prior year's inflow of ~Rs 1,300 Crore
items.quote: The order flow during the current year was closer to Rs 700 Crore

items.statement: TMD seeing prolonged downturn over 9 months; order discussions happening but off-take reduced; expect two quarters for capacity utilization clarity
items.quote: We are perhaps at a very low-capacity utilization, and it will take us perhaps two quarters to give us the clarity to say how are we going to go up in capacity utilization.

items.statement: Internal planning to sit tight for two quarters and conserve resources; no specific revenue or profit guidance given
items.quote: Our internal planning is that we have to be sitting tight for two quarters and save everything what we have got.

items.statement: Added 5 MW solar capacity in Q4 FY24, taking total renewable capacity to 53 MW serving ~90% of energy needs
items.quote: During the last quarter, we have put in another 5 MW of solar capacity, taking our total installed capacity to 53 MW of renewable power.

items.statement: Invested ~Rs 20 Crore in ATC division in FY24 for machines; MTD capex Rs 50-70 Crore annually over last 2-3 years
items.quote: We have invested earlier this year, around Rs 20 Crore. into ATC, in terms of machines alone.

items.statement: MTD capacity utilization at ~65% with 35% headroom; company adds capacity ahead of demand
items.quote: Our capacity utilisation is still in the range of 65%. So, we still have about 35% capacity available for utilisation in this particular division.

items.statement: TMD and foundry reduced working days in May 2024 to 5 days due to lower capacity utilization
items.quote: We have also announced a reduction in the number of working days in the month of May 2024 and currently, TMD is working 5 days because of lower capacity utilization

items.statement: MTD margins near single-digit due to underutilized capacity; expect return to double-digit margins as turnover rises
items.quote: The reason we have seen that our margins have come down closer to a single digit margin is that we have invested in capacities but not fully getting utilized

items.statement: MTD took 2-4% price revision in May 2024 across machine models, first in two years
items.quote: In the month of May 2024, we have taken a price revision for machines, which was on a hold for 2 years.

items.statement: MTD revenue mix steady at 75-80% traditional machines, 20-25% machining centres; new VMC models driving non-auto growth
items.quote: It is still hovering between 75:25, or 80:20, depending on whichever quarter we take

items.statement: MTD revenue split: 42% auto, 58% non-auto across 25 segments; defence/aerospace not significant
items.quote: We basically are almost 42% is auto segment, and the non-auto segment of around 58% is split across 25 different business segments.

items.statement: ATC export share >90% of Rs 160 Crore revenue; order book Rs 200+ Crore executable over 18 months
items.quote: Export contributed to more than 90% of this turnover, and within this, the metallic division contributes to about 80% of the turnover of this particular division.

items.statement: TMD domestic market share ~72% across machine segments; global share 12-15%
items.quote: We are upwards of, from the delivery perspective, if we see, we are upwards of 72%, in terms of overall market share.

items.statement: TMD spares revenue split: 70% domestic, 11-12% spares, 16-17% exports for full year; Q4 ~75% domestic, 12% export, 13% spares
items.quote: The breakup is around 70% domestic because of more projects getting shipped out around 11-12% of spares and around 16-17% of exports.

items.statement: Global economic challenges causing weak export demand for Middle East ops and TMD; expect weakness for couple of quarters
items.quote: The global economic challenges remain, and hence resulting in weak demand. This, we see as a business challenge for the exports market as well, for a couple of quarters

items.statement: TMD order book backed by ~10% security deposits reflected in balance sheet
items.quote: What we have reflected in the balance sheet, you would be able to add the two security deposits together. You would see that its almost 10%.

items.statement: LMW China subsidiary revenue fell 90% to Rs 28 Crore with Rs 13 Crore loss in FY24
items.quote: We have clocked a turnover of Rs 28 Crore for the year, compared to Rs 273 Crore for the previous year, registering almost 90% decline with almost Rs 13 Crore loss for the full year.

items.statement: India added slightly less than 2 million spindles in FY24
items.quote: The spindles added during the current year is little bit less than, in India, it is a little bit less than 2 million spindles.

items.statement: TMD full-year revenue Rs 3,575 Crore (-2% YoY); profit Rs 314 Crore (-8.9% YoY)
items.quote: For the full year, the turnover stands at Rs 3575 Crore as against Rs 3647 Crore for the previous year, resulting in a slight decline of 2%.

items.statement: MTD full-year revenue Rs 1,049 Crore (+7% YoY); Q4 Rs 293 Crore (+22% QoQ); profit Rs 74 Crore (+19% YoY)
items.quote: The revenue of the division stands at Rs 1049 Crore compared to Rs 985 Crore for the previous year, which is 7% higher

items.statement: Aerospace (ATC) revenue up 45% to Rs 160 Crore; profit Rs 14 Crore vs Rs 3 Crore prior year
items.quote: The revenue in this division is up by 45% from Rs 110 Crore to Rs 160 Crore. and ATC has clocked a profit of Rs 14 Crore as against Rs 3 Crore last year.

items.statement: Middle East ops revenue Rs 249 Crore with ~40% value addition; included in consolidated turnover
items.quote: achieved a turnover of Rs 249 Crore during the year FY 23-24, as against for the current year. The value addition there is around 40% and this is reflected in the consolidated turnover of the company

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected around ₹5,000 Cr (+/-5%)
items.quote: So, next year's turnover should be around ₹5,000 Cr, +-5%.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth expected around 2,000 metric tonnes from new Chhata and Kaapas units
items.quote: It is not 850 metric tonnes it would be around 2000 metric ton nes; putting together this Chhata unit and this Kaapas unit at Lodha

items.statement: Total capex of ₹725 Cr spent over two years on Denim, Mélange, Knitting and Kaapas projects
items.quote: Firstly, it is not ₹715 Cr, it is ₹725 Cr. It includes 30,000 spindles as in M elange yarn segment, one is around ₹155 Cr in Denim, and around ₹85 Cr in knitting. It makes around ₹410 Cr and again ₹315 Cr in case of Kaapas, Lodha so it is ₹725 Cr

items.statement: No major capex planned except for environmental improvements in ETPs and STPs
items.quote: We are not planning any big expenditure in risk management kind of thing except, we are addressing environmental issues by improvement in our ETPs and our STPs these kinds of risks are being addressed through the CAPEX otherwise no other CAPEX for debt management.

items.statement: Chhata acquisition adds 80,016 spindles, 720 rotors, 12 tonnes/day knitted fabric and processing
items.quote: The acquisition enlarges RSWM's footprint, cementing its standing in the spinning and fabric industry by incorporating substantial capacity: 80,016 spindles, 720 rotors, 12 tonnes per day of knitted fabric, and its processing.

items.statement: Knits plants collective capacity 780 tonnes/month at Chhata (350) and Mordi (430)
items.quote: Our Knits plants have a collective manufacturing capacity of 780 tonnes per month, which is spread at two locations, which is Chhata, district Mathura in UP with 350 tonnes and Mordi, Banswara with 430 tonnes.

items.statement: Kaapas premium cotton product commands ₹6-8/kg higher price vs competitors
items.quote: Our premium cotton product, Kaapas has achieved remarkable success, commanding a higher price point of ₹6 - ₹8 more per kg compared to our competitors.

items.statement: Lodha Kaapas project generating ₹6-8/kg plus profit with best quality and efficiency
items.quote: This plant is running well with the best quality, with best efficiency of production, with good profitability, with better value addition, compared to our peers, compared to other units within our company. It is abo ut ₹6/kg to ₹8/kg

items.statement: Positive flow of export enquiries for knits but low conversion to bulk due to price challenges
items.quote: There is a positive flow of enquiries for export sales. However, at the same time, the conversion rate to bulk is very low due to extreme challenges in terms of prices.

items.statement: Yarn prices declined ~10% YoY across categories; Mélange down 25% YoY
items.quote: Nowadays the prices from FY23 have become ₹164/kg from ₹189/kg in case of PV grey yarn. In the case of cotton grey yarn from ₹259/kg to ₹248/kg in cotton grey yarn. In the case of PV Dyed it was ₹244/kg in FY23 and FY24 it is ₹207/kg, so the price realization during this FY2023-24 was lower than by around 10%, in case of every type of yarn and in case M elange it is less by 25% from FY23 to FY24

items.statement: PTA and MEG prices expected to decline, positively impacting production costs
items.quote: Prices for PTA and MEG are expected to decline, which could positively impact production costs.

items.statement: BIS certification reduced polyester yarn imports from 106k tonnes (Sep'23) to 13k tonnes (Nov'23); imports expected to fall 40-50% to 240-260k tonnes in 2025
items.quote: Imports are expected to reduce by 40% to 50% from 455 k tonnes in 2024 to around 240k – 260k tonnes in 2025.

items.statement: Risk of increased dumping of cheap polyester fabric despite reduced yarn dumping
items.quote: However, there is a potential risk of an increase in the dumping of cheap polyester fabric.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of Ginni Filament's Spinning, Knitting & Processing undertaking at Chhata, Mathura
items.quote: In this quarter, we have completed the acquisition of the S pinning, Knitting and Processing undertaking of G inni Filament Limited, which will enhance the company’s production capacity

items.statement: Chhata plant running at full capacity but has quality issues due to 25-30 year old machinery; modernization investment under board evaluation
items.quote: Entire 80,016 spindles are being run at full capacity. But you know that since the machinery is 25-30 years old, the product of this has quality issues which will be addressed after some investment; which will come in due course, after our board approval.

items.statement: Unrealized mark-to-market gain of ₹138 Cr on Bhilwara Energy Limited equity investment (7.56% stake)
items.quote: The RSWM management is pleased to inform the investors about the value creation on its investment in equity shares of Bhilwara Energy Limited, through unrealized mark to market gain of ₹138 crore on fair valuation.

items.statement: Finished goods inventory reduced from ~12,000 MT to ~5,200 MT in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The stock levels were around 12,000 metric tonnes, which came to around 5,200 metric tonne in Q4 FY2023-24.

items.statement: No bad debts, major claims or held-up FCL; strong financial management
items.quote: Our financial health is robust with no instances of bad debts, major claims, or held-up FCL, reflects our strong financial management practices.

items.statement: Labour shortage and election-related absenteeism impacted production in April-May; resolved post Rajasthan elections
items.quote: Though we were running at full capacity except labour shortage and all, it resulted into lower production. Capacity utilization is full but when the workers will not come due to election or due to this drop, it remains difficult to run the plant fully. But after this election in Rajasthan, everything is addressed and now there is no issue at all.

items.statement: Risk Management Committee (Directors, CFO, Business Heads, CS, CIO) reviews risks twice yearly; Grant Thornton reviews compliance monthly
items.quote: The Company like RSWM is doing for risk management is that we have the Risk Management Committee which includes Directors, CFO and all Stakeholders like Business Head, Business Head - Yarn, Business Head - Denim, Business Head - Mélange, Business Head - Knitting and then Company Secretary and lastly Chief Information Officer. All kinds of risks are discussed and if any new risk is identified, it i

items.statement: Textile exports grew 7% YoY in first two months of 2024 after 7% decline in 2023
items.quote: Encouragingly, the positive trend has continued into the first two months of 2024 with exports growing by 7% YoY.

items.statement: H2 FY24 better than H1; Q4 seasonally strong; stable yarn prices expected in FY25 as polyester yarn dumping decreases
items.quote: Looking ahead to F Y25, we expect yarn prices to remain stable as the dumping of cheaper polyester yarn in India is likely to decrease

items.statement: Exports expected to reach $200 million in FY25
items.quote: We expect our exports to touch to $200 million.

items.statement: Capex planned at Rs 350-400 crore for FY25
items.quote: So, we would be spending between Rs. 350 crores to Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Wind energy revenue to double from Rs 250 crore to Rs 500 crore+ in 2-3 years
items.quote: From the current level of Rs. 250 crores, we should be reaching Rs. 500 crores plus in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: EV order book visibility peaks at $110-112 million in 2026, continuing to 2030
items.quote: So, the visibility at this point of time is that it's peaking in 2026, about $112 million, $110 million. And we expect that level of EV business, not only EV, like we have been saying, hybrid, PHV, ICE, EV, all coming under this export book to continue up to 2030.

items.statement: Order book pipeline stands at Rs 4,000 crore
items.quote: Yes. So, we have been talking about Rs. 4,000 crores of order book, the pipeline, and so that's where it is.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin at 17%, positive trajectory expected to continue
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter has come in at 17%. This is despite incurring some of one-time costs because of the impact of the flood, which is there in the quarterly numbers.

items.statement: Aspiration to return to 19-20% EBITDA margin band
items.quote: While getting back to 19.20 is definitely our aspiration.

items.statement: Domestic market strong across segments; CVs to benefit from government spending, tractors from monsoon, PV mid-single digit growth
items.quote: I think notwithstanding the elections, even the commercial vehicles have done well, with government spending happening in Q1 or later part of Q2. We expect that sector to perform very well. The monsoon, of course, always plays a crucial role in sale of tractors, as we all know. And I think with promise of higher than normal monsoon, I think tractors will reach the previous peak of 1 million units.

items.statement: Export demand recovery sustained; channel destocking over, customer forecasts positive
items.quote: Yes. These are demands, which are, which will be sustained recovery. And I think the customers are increasing our production. And the channel destocking which happened, it's behind us now. And I think we will grow and from what customer forecast, what we have got from our major customers, things are looking up.

items.statement: FY24 standalone capex Rs 343 crore; FY25 capex Rs 350-400 crore focused on fastener division for exports and hybrid/PH/EV at SEZ
items.quote: Now on the capital expenditure, we have incurred Rs. 343 crores for the year on standalone basis. We have invested across all our divisions for growth capital expenditure.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 65-70% across divisions; new projects across fastener, Autolec, MFD divisions
items.quote: So, the capacity utilization should be around 65% to 70%, yes, across I'm talking about. And quite a lot of new projects are coming up, which across all the divisions, whether it is a fastener division, we are getting new customers, we are getting new entries into the overseas market, direct exports to the OEMs.

items.statement: EV revenue currently 6-7%, targeting 10-12% near term, 10-15% eventually
items.quote: At current level, it would be close to about 6%, 7%. And then we are looking to take it up to maybe 10% to 12%. And eventually, we are trying to look at around 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Non-auto revenue 30% currently, aspiration to reach 50%
items.quote: See, with respect to the non-auto portion, while today we are at 30%, the aspiration is to go to 50%.

items.statement: BEV content per vehicle 25-30% lower than ICE; long-term mix seen as 50-60% ICE, 15% PHEV, 25-30% BEV
items.quote: So, purely an apples-to-apples, between a pure ICE to a pure BEV. So, let's say that the delta could be 25%. So, that would be maximum 25% to 30%.

items.statement: PV customers include all major OEMs; Tata Motors is number one; working with Hyundai and others on EV platforms
items.quote: The customers whom we are working with, I would say are predominantly with the EV spectrum. We are with the passenger cars and 3-wheelers. So, the passenger car, the customers to name is, of course, all the players. The number one player today is Tata Motors. So, we are well with them and then we are giving them all the requirements of the fasteners as far as the thing is concerned. And even with

items.statement: UK subsidiary (CPFL) turned around, expected to remain profitable despite UK truck market slowdown; China subsidiary strong despite real estate slowdown
items.quote: We expect the UK subsidiary to have another strong year. Notwithstanding the slowdown in the UK truck market, we expect our operations to be profitable this year in line with last year. And it has turned around completely and lots of operational improvements. The raw metal prices have been managed well and the freight costs have come down. And so there has been a strong operational performance in

items.statement: Raw metal prices stable in FY24; steel prices may rise due to Chinese import licensing restrictions; pass-through arrangements with all customers
items.quote: I think metal prices, especially the steel, have been largely stable last year. We expect that trend to continue. But having said that, the Chinese imports, there are certain licensing requirements now. So, the supply of Chinese steel is going to be limited. And for some market correction, there is a possibility of prices going up in steel.

items.statement: Pass-through arrangements with all customers for metal price changes
items.quote: Yes, sir. We have pass-through arrangements with all our customers.

items.statement: PLI application approved; product testing approval expected in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We have opted for PLI. We are one of the approved companies. Our products are yet to get an approval from the testing agency. And now things have slowed down a bit. We expect some traction in Q2.

items.statement: Atma Nirbhar and QCO orders driving import substitution in PV segment, accelerating local sourcing enquiries
items.quote: Actually, it's a good question. And what is going to be relevant is the extraordinary push from the government side in terms of Atma Nirbhar and the QCO orders, I hope you are familiar. So, it is kind of indirectly nudging and forcing the OEMs to localize whatever they are importing currently.

items.statement: Domestic revenue mix: PV 40%, M&HCV+LCV 25%, Tractors 8-10%
items.quote: With respect to the industry segment, we are at 40% of our domestic revenue with respect to passenger car segment. And between M&HCV and LCV, we should be looking at 25%, tractors in the range of 8% to 10%.

items.statement: PV volume growth budgeted at 8-10% for FY25 vs 7% last year; M&HCV at 12-13% with higher content per vehicle
items.quote: We are looking at around 8% to 10% kind of a growth. Last year, we had 7%. So, we are sure that it will reach maybe close to the double digit, but are 9% to 10%. I think this year should be good.

items.statement: Q4 volume growth 8-10% QoQ across segments except tractors which degrew; industry grew 3-4% QoQ
items.quote: Volume growth, I think barring tractors, all the other segments grew by around 8% to 10%, 7%. Only the tractor segment did not grow much. In fact, there was a degrowth in the tractor segment.

items.statement: Flood-related one-time cost of Rs 3.38 crore recognized in Q4 FY24
items.quote: It is there in our notes and accounts. I will give you the number, that is the net amount, it's Rs. 3.38 crores.

items.statement: FY25 capex guided between Rs. 500-700 crore
items.quote: So, even for FY25, our CAPEX would be between Rs. 500 to Rs. 700 crores.

items.statement: Mid-teen EBITDA margin target retained; no discounting for market share
items.quote: Our stated objective is to retain this mid-teen EBITDA margin. And that is why I think we're very clear of not really playing a discounting game and growing our market share on the basis of products and our extended network as well.

items.statement: Switch India e-bus order book at 1,500 units including 950 for Delhi and 320 for Bangalore
items.quote: We have 1,500 in hand, we have 950 to deliver in Delhi and another 320 to deliver in Bangalore and then few more.

items.statement: Switch UK Spain plant on track; first vehicles to be delivered in September
items.quote: The first vehicles actually by the way, will be delivered in coming September. I think it is a few numbers, but we want to ensure that we do make that small step in Spain.

items.statement: Current capacity sufficient for 2-3 years; evaluating footprint for expansion beyond that with flexible lines for ICE and EV
items.quote: For next 2-3 years, we see no problem as far as capacity is concerned, but hopefully we have to prepare ourselves for a period beyond that. So, we are looking at it, we will come out with more details and share with you.

items.statement: 6 new product launches planned in 2-3.5 ton SCV segment in FY25; LCV portfolio expansion to cover 70-80% of market
items.quote: We have planned for 6 new product launches in this segment in FY25, which should give us a further boost to our market share. Currently, we address about half of the LCV market in India. We are looking to expanding our LCV product portfolio to cover at least 70% to 80% of the market in the next few years.

items.statement: Export volumes grew despite subdued SAARC and Africa markets; strategy of local presence and focused product development working
items.quote: Despite subdued market conditions in SAARC and in some parts of Africa, Ashok Leyland registered growth in export volume s, this reflects that our strategy of local market presence, focused product development for IO markets and our strong distribution relationships in key markets is working well for us

items.statement: Net debt close to zero at end of FY24 after Rs. 1,500 crore investment in Optare Switch
items.quote: Our net debt at the end of FY24 is close to Zero. This is after Rs. 1,500 crore investment in Optare Switch and owned during the year.

items.statement: KM Balaji appointed CFO effective 1 June 2024; Gopal Mahadevan moves to Director, Strategic Finance and M&A
items.quote: we announced the appointment of Mr. KM Balaji as Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Gopal Mahadevan, currently CF O and Whole-Time Director will continue to be associated with Ashok Leyland as Director, Strategic Finance and M&A. Mr. Balaji, currently Deputy CFO, will take over the role of Chief Financial Officer with effect from 1st June 2024

items.statement: Hinduja Leyland Finance reverse merger back on track; expected to complete in a couple of quarters; exploring third-party investment in Hinduja Housing Finance
items.quote: The reverse merger process is back on track. It had some procedural issues more than anything else. So, otherwise what was envisaged as the original merger strategy continues. So, we expect that this may take a couple of more quarters.

items.statement: OBD-II norms caused pre-buy in Q4 FY23 creating high base; replacement demand from aging BS-IV fleet (avg age 10 years) to drive growth
items.quote: And that was because of OBD-II norms that had forced some prebuy. So, we have to just keep in perspective that if we exclude that period of high base number because of which the industry degrew, industry has been growing before that by 8%-9%.

items.statement: Dedicated Freight Corridor impact not expected in short run; TCO model not working yet, fundamental issues to be resolved over few years
items.quote: The whole TCO of this new model for potential new model around DFC is not working out yet. So, there are some like fundamental issues in the model which have to be sorted out and I really think it will take a long time. It will take a few years at least before it starts taking some shape.

items.statement: Switch India turned EBITDA positive in Q4 FY24; expected to remain EBITDA positive in FY25; no major investment needed in H1 FY25
items.quote: Switch in quarter four has been EBITDA positive. Yes, so this is the first quarter where they have turned around into being a p rofitable company. And even in FY 25, we are, as I said, we are still kind of refining the plans. But we hope that S witch would remain EBITDA positive, Switch India would remain EBITDA positive

items.statement: Market share gains to come from product superiority and expanding reach, not discounting; confident of increasing share in trucks and buses
items.quote: We are clear that we are not going to discount our products to win market share. We are confident that our market share wins will come on the back of our products superiority and our expanding reach.

items.statement: Strong interest in eLCV from e-commerce and logistics multinationals for green last-mile; order book building since March launch
items.quote: There is a lot of interest from e-commerce and logistic companies, especially many multinationals who are looking for the last mile to be green as well. So, I would say that it is early days, but a lot of strong interest.

items.statement: Capex expected to continue at INR 300-600 crore per year
items.quote: on an average, we've had a capex of between INR 400 crores to INR 600 crores -- INR300 crores to INR 600 crores, if I can be broade r year -on-year. And this is a trend that we will continue

items.statement: Growth in FY25 expected similar to FY24 with Q1 slow due to elections
items.quote: The growth of FY '23-'24 is something that we are looking forward to also in the upcoming year. The first quarter could be a little slow because of the election effects.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement expected to continue
items.quote: Overall, we see continued improvement in our margins and performance as we move forward.

items.statement: EGT localization line SOP April 2025 at Bosch plant
items.quote: We expect SOP, the start of production in April '25 because you have to understand that these are quite complex lines. And -- but it's on the way. It's decided. It's ordered SOP April '25.

items.statement: Capex estimated at INR 400-600 crore for localization goals over next 3-5 years
items.quote: We've estimated that our capex requirements will be in the region of INR400 crores to INR600 crores.

items.statement: CV injector assembly line in Nashik ramped up; third-party supplier localization ongoing
items.quote: We have a very good ramp-up of the line of the assembly interesting. Meanwhile, we had last year or in this financial -- in the last financial year, we had a ramp-up of the component business.

items.statement: Building Technologies secured pivotal projects across metros, airports, government, energy, consumer, education, health sectors
items.quote: The division secured pivotal projects across transportation, including metros and airports, government, energy and consumer sectors, which remain significant contributors to business growth.

items.statement: Building Technologies divestiture expected to close by Q1-Q2 2025
items.quote: We expect this to go through by Q1, Q2 of 2025.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 13.2% in Q4 FY24 from 12.9% in Q4 FY23
items.quote: EBITDA as a percentage of total revenue improved from 12.9% in Jan to March '23 to 13.2% in Jan to March '24.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin improved to 12.5% from 12.1% in FY23
items.quote: EBITDA as a percentage of total revenue improved from 12.1% to 12.5%.

items.statement: Other expenses reduced to 14.7% in March 2024 from 16.8% in March 2023 due to cost measures and divestment
items.quote: We were in April, March 2024 on a 14.7%, comparable in '23, 16.8%. S o besides the lower spending and, of course, some more costs variable due to the growth, we also see that our cost measures are well fit in the base now

items.statement: Localization ongoing for common rail and exhaust gas treatment; supplier development for complex parts underway
items.quote: In the common rail, we are working on it. We are comin g up in the localization rates. So therefore, of course, you see this in the gross margin and in addition, besides the finished goods, it's also a component. We are working on the supplier development, even for very complex parts

items.statement: Two-wheeler division achieved 19.2% sales growth; cordless tools reached 11% of power tools sales
