items.quote: If you see today, our work in hand, we may have 50 jobs in hand. And out of that, about eight contribute to 80% of our revenue.

items.statement: Moving to bigger marine jobs to reduce competition; established overseas track record and client relationships as differentiators
items.quote: We have realized that a few segments like small marine jobs is no more a profitable segment. So one thing that we have gone to bigger marine jobs or bigger jobs.

items.statement: Working capital cycle sustainable at current levels; payments received on time per contract terms
items.quote: In fact, most of our projects, we are getting payments on time. As soon as we bill, as per the contract terms, we are getting our payments. So I mean, we don't expect any significant change in the working capital cycle going forward.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity ratio under 0.2x as of FY24
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to be extremely healthy and the net debt-to-equity ratio is under 0.2x.

items.statement: Underground Metro opportunity around INR 15,000-16,000 crores this year; 3-4 bids submitted
items.quote: If you see, underground Metro is probably around INR2,000 crores plus, and they are kind of few are in the pipeline. So, I think around INR15,000, INR16,000 crores job opportunities are there in this year.

items.statement: Some recent large orders still in initial margin declaration phase; margin to add to bottom line from Q2/Q3 FY25
items.quote: But there are a few jobs which we have secured towards the end of the last year, are still in initial limit of the margin declaration. So we have taken the revenue. So margin is yet to be declared, which we'll definitely add to the bottom line second or third quarter onwards.

items.statement: Did not participate in Maharashtra coastal road/tunnel tenders due to high capex for TBMs and qualification issues
items.quote: We have not participated because we found that it requires a lot of investment, particularly tunnel job, where the tunnel boring machine surge is quite big, and requires a lot of investment. And if the stage that we have today, we have to contain our capex within a limit. That is the main reason. And in some cases, to all these, there is a qualification issue as well.

items.statement: Employee cost increase will be marginal vs revenue growth; headcount to rise but not proportionately
items.quote: The delta increase in the employee cost will be less compared to the increase in revenue. So in that way, proportional if you see only marginal increase or even flat in terms of percentage.

items.statement: JV projects (Calcutta Metro, Bombay Metro) at finishing stage; no substantial cash impact expected
items.quote: JV jobs are almost now on the finishing stage because if you see Calcutta Metro is completed, I think it's completed, leaving few work. Bombay Metro is almost completed. And there is no other JVs that we are doing. So all at the fag end. And there'll be a little bit of margin and cash will remain there.

items.statement: Overseas bidding conflict with parent company resolved; mutual understanding on project allocation
items.quote: If you have noticed that 2 years to 3 years back we never have been to overseas, and then we have discussed with our parent. It is not that they have interest. It is they wanted to see our ability to do what we want. And that we have demonstrated that, yes, we can do and we can do well.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow upper limit around INR 9,000 crores; not conservative but realistic maximum
items.quote: So probably this, I'm not conservative. I think whatever number I have said, that is the upper limit, around INR9,000 crores.

items.statement: Management projects ~10% topline growth in FY25 to ~Rs 4,800 crore, with potential to reach Rs 5,000 crore if CV and car industries grow.
items.quote: More or less we are saying that we will go by 10% this year on the topline. So, that would come out to a number of Rs. 4,800 crores, around that number.

items.statement: Volume target of 20 million wheels in FY25 vs 19 million in FY24.
items.quote: On numbers, we are looking at 20 million wheels this year versus 19 million last year.

items.statement: Domestic CV industry expected flat to tepid growth in FY25 due to election year and monsoons.
items.quote: we all know that this is an election year and so there is, we have seen a slight slowdown in the CV industry so far and this is going to be followed by monsoons. last year we did the highest CV volume. This year our forecast is ranging from a flat year to somewhat tepid growth

items.statement: Domestic aluminum wheel business expected to grow ~10% in FY25 driven by new project nominations.
items.quote: On the domestic aluminum wheel side, we expect about a 10% growth. This is based on our past performance, past projects that we have been nominated for.

items.statement: Two-wheeler EV wheel business targeted to grow ~16% in FY25.
items.quote: And there we are leaders now for wheels and they are in much better value addition on these wheels and this business should grow about 16%.

items.statement: Passenger car steel wheel business projected to grow 10.6% in FY25 after regaining Maruti projects.
items.quote: So, but this year I am glad to tell you that we are projecting a 10.6% growth in the steel wheel for passenger cars.

items.statement: Tractor business expected to grow ~12% in FY25 from new LTAs and market share gains.
items.quote: So, here I can say with prominence that our tractor share of business is going to go up this year and this means about 12% growth in revenue in terms of volume and obviously value also will follow suit.

items.statement: Export business expected to grow ~10% in FY25 with new OTR and alloy wheel traction in Europe and America.
items.quote: We expect this to grow by another 10% this year and in the export business we're adding new product lines like off-road vehicle wheels.

items.statement: Aluminum knuckles production to start in September FY25, targeting Rs 35 crore revenue in FY25, doubling thereafter and 4x later.
items.quote: We should start our revenue growth from September onwards. Revenue is coming in from knuckles perhaps a little bit earlier and this year we should be doing close to about if I am not mistaken, about Rs. 35 crores in revenue and then going forward, we expect this revenue to go more than double and then after that, this revenue to go more than 4x.

items.statement: Alloy wheel capacity raised to ~5 million wheels; current FY25 target 3.3 million; expects to cross 4 million in FY26.
items.quote: We have raised our capacity to close to 5 million wheels in alloy and we are banking on a big growth in exports and also a big growth in the domestic market.

items.statement: New alloy wheel factory planned in Punjab near Maruti plant for FY26-FY27 based on nomination progress.
items.quote: So, FY26, FY27, yes, but we would definitely need to come closer to Maruti. So, I am just giving you a heads up and all to the investor community that we may be coming up with a new factory in Punjab, very close to Maruti.

items.statement: FY25 capex estimated at ~Rs 225 crore, to be funded entirely from internal accruals.
items.quote: In terms of overall CAPEX, which was there on the table, I think for next year was in the range of Rs. 225 odd crores which can be funded entirely from the accruals, and nothing needs to be borrowed from the outside market.

items.statement: AMW acquisition equipment being relocated to Jamshedpur for CV capacity addition of ~400,000 wheels, operational by June FY25.
items.quote: We are adding a new CV capacity of almost 400,000 wheels that is coming from equipment that was lying in AMW. We're not letting the equipment idle. We're just moving that equipment to other parts of our locations where they're already producing in mass.

items.statement: EBITDA per wheel expected to improve above FY24's Rs 253 due to favorable mix (alloy, export, tractor) and passenger car steel wheel price correction.
items.quote: 253 was the number last year, so definitely you will see a much better number than 253.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA per wheel ~Rs 255; full year FY24 ~Rs 253.
items.quote: Rs. 255 is fourth quarter, Rs. 253 was the full year.

items.statement: Passenger car steel wheel price correction agreed with major OEMs, effective from April 1 FY25, to improve margins on 70-80% of volumes.
items.quote: We have been able to come close to understanding with a couple of OEMs to correct the prices that were depressed for the last two decades. So, that's the historic thing I had mentioned this in the last conference call also with other people also, that has actually happened now.

items.statement: Export prices cut 5-6% in FY24 due to competition from Vietnam/Thailand; freight advantage now favors India.
items.quote: We had to drop our prices close to 5% to 6% in terms of our export prices. So, that sort of kicker did sort of dampen our export margins.

items.statement: Export revenue target Rs 700-720 crore in FY25; Red Sea crisis impact mitigated as customers adjusted inventories.
items.quote: I think we are targeting around Rs. 700 crores to Rs. 720 crores in terms of total numbers that we are anticipating in this financial year.

items.statement: March 2024 debt Rs 1,048 crore (LT Rs 487 cr, ST Rs 561 cr) is peak; scheduled repayments ~Rs 105 cr/year for 3 years; FY25 capex funded from accruals.
items.quote: The existing capex was almost Rs. 380 crores which we had already shared with the market, which will be incurring this year covering multiple facets the alloy wheel expansion, then knuckles and the renewal energy that we are working with and then the couple of flow forming equipment that we did decide, the general CAPEX that we do.

items.statement: Debt expected to taper down from March 2024 peak via repayments and prepayments from accruals.
items.quote: So, as we guided last time that the debt that you are seeing as on March 24 is the peak debt in our books and subsequently it should taper down.

items.statement: Alloy wheel order book visibility extends to 2027; Maruti nomination breakthrough with 7 model refreshes over next year.
items.quote: I have an order book in front of me that is extending up till 2027. I see the numbers. I see the possibility of expanding my market beyond India and that's what I am focused on.

items.statement: Maruti alloy wheel nomination secured; designing underway, Japan testing in 4-5 months; 7 model refreshes over next year; revenue potential Rs 45-50 crore from first RFQ.
items.quote: The designing concept is already underway right now, the Japan testing will be underway over next 4 to 5 months. The feature which we are expecting right now is that the refresh of each model will now come to us, right now we got only one model, but over the next one year, close to 7 refreshers are coming.

items.statement: Aluminum knuckles developed jointly with Mahindra; second OEM signed; no exclusivity but high IP barrier.
items.quote: It has been a joint collaboration with the OEM. The OEM has supported us and we have done the work and we have a very tight relationship with Mahindra, for example, and there's a lot of trust, lot of transparency and a lot of value that we bring to each other.

items.statement: Vietnam/Thailand competitors (Chinese-owned) face EU anti-circumvention probes; India has freight advantage (half the cost).
items.quote: There is constantly some kind of investigation going on against those companies supply to America and also to Europe. So, going forward we feel that we will really not suffice because the European Union is moving against anti-circumvention.

items.statement: Domestic alloy wheel penetration at 37%, expected to reach 50% over 3-4 years; Maruti currently 29-30%, targeting 40% in 4 years.
items.quote: We had interactions with many OEMs, where they are all projecting that this 37% will not immediately go to 50%, but they see this 50% happening over next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Employee cost grew 60-65% vs 25% revenue growth over 2 years; management targeting to contain future growth to 10-12% and optimize.
items.quote: I think we are trying to reduce that 10% to 12% kind of a number. We're trying to optimize that number. I feel this 10% to 12% kind of a growth number will definitely be contained.

items.statement: AMW acquisition liabilities governed by NCLT-approved resolution plan; exceptional item from write-back of differential liabilities.
items.quote: On the exceptional item that you are looking at in the consolidated it is predominantly the write back of the liabilities, which are there in the books of AMW. So, there were some official creditors and other liabilities, which are there in the books. Now ourliabilities to pay will be governed by a resolution plan, which got approved by the NCLT

items.statement: CV industry outlook uncertain; no visibility from OEMs; growth dependent on market share gains in tractor, passenger car, exports, two-wheelers.
items.quote: I can answer that very easily, nobody knows. Not even the OEM knows, not even the buyers, nobody in the industry knows what will happen to the CV industry.

items.statement: Effective tax rate reduced to 25.17% from 34.94% after shifting to new tax regime.
items.quote: We have shifted to a new tax regime where the effective tax rate has come down to 25.17% hitherto it was 34.94%.

items.statement: Targets INR 1,000 crores revenue from India over next 5 years
items.quote: We remain optimistic on building our India presence with 2 brands, both Himeya and Atmosphere, and we continue to want to achieve revenues of approximately INR1,000 crores from India over the next 5 years.

items.statement: Aims to reach full capacity utilization in 18-24 months
items.quote: We would like to head in that direction and be running at full capacity over the next 18 months or so, 18 months, 2 years kind of time frame, if not earlier.

items.statement: Targets net debt to EBITDA below 3.5x and DSCR 1.8x-2.2x
items.quote: So we would like to bring our net debt to EBITDA levels to below 3.5x, which is where we used to be. And so we would like to head there. And we would like to make sure that our DSCRs are in the region of 1.8x to 2.2x.

items.statement: Plans to raise equity sometime this fiscal to strengthen balance sheet
items.quote: So keeping all of these things in line, we would like to strengthen and raise equity sometime this fiscal, that's what we're running for.

items.statement: Current capacity can generate approximately INR 4,000 crores revenue including Himeya brand
items.quote: Approximately INR4,000 crores, just over INR4,000 crores, is our estimate.

items.statement: Spinning plant at 100% utilization, Sheeting and Terry plants at 67% each in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The capacity utilization during the quarter remained stable across our 3 plants. As you've seen, the utilization in our spinning plant came in at 100%, and the Sheeting and Terry plants were at 67% each.

items.statement: No major capex planned beyond annual maintenance and organic requirements
items.quote: We don't have any plans for any additional capex of any consequence other than our annual maintenance and organic capex requirements and something we've shared very openly and clearly with stakeholders.

items.statement: Demand environment stable with slight negative bias in major markets; growth to come from market share gains
items.quote: So the absolute demand remains stable. I would say, there is an overhang of caution in major markets. So I'm using the word stable with a slight negative bias, if you will, at least in major markets.

items.statement: EBITDA margin stable in 18%-22% band driven by product mix, brand mix, cost controls, technology and efficiencies
items.quote: It's typically where we are in stable state. So the India growth will not -- we don't see it diluting our EBITDA profile. It will not dilute our EBITDA profile, is what we estimate.

items.statement: Lost INR 200 crores revenue from exiting non-core product categories
items.quote: We've also pulled out of some categories of products, which I've shared with stakeholders earlier, we lost INR200 crores on that front because we don't see that as core going forward.

items.statement: Lost revenue from Bed Bath & Beyond due to their wind-up; consciously stopped trading certain non-core products
items.quote: So one of our clients, Bed Bath & Beyond, we have lost market share with them because of the condition and then finally have to wind up. So specifically speaking, we had lost revenue on that front.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt at INR 2,634 crores end March 2024 vs INR 2,626 crores end December 2023
items.quote: On the consolidated net debt, we've ranged down our co nsolidated net debt to INR2,634 crores, at the end of March '24 versus INR2,626 crores at the end of December '23

items.statement: Working to deleverage through ordinary course and equity raise; focus on growth, deleveraging, strengthening equity
items.quote: Yes, focusing on growth, focusing on deleveraging, and focusing on strengthening equity. These are the 3 things I would like to focus on, and that's what we've shared with stakeholders.

items.statement: Working to improve working capital cycle time but not specifying reduction targets
items.quote: Well, see, that's something I wouldn't want to specifically spell out. But I would say that we are working to be better our current cycle time.

items.statement: Growth driven by broader product mix, larger client mix, more markets served; manufacturing platforms offer flexibility and unique product base
items.quote: Our ability to not just offer world-class manufacturing platforms -- sustainable manufacturing platforms, but also to give our global plans a product mix and base that would be, let's just say, unique.

items.statement: Peak revenue was INR 3,200+ crores in FY22; aims to return to that level and grow beyond
items.quote: Our peak revenues were about INR 3,200 plus crores in FY '22, and then we lost some steam post some of the macro issues that the market faced. And so we want to head back in that direction and then onwards from there.

items.statement: Geopolitical overhang from Middle East crisis and Russia-Ukraine situation plus macroeconomic headwinds in major markets
items.quote: Of course, there is an angle of the global overhang that one sees because of the crisis in th e Middle East and the Russia -Ukraine situation, coupled with other macroeconomic headwinds that some of the major markets see

items.statement: Raw material prices remained range-bound and stable during quarter contributing to YoY operating performance improvement
items.quote: Raw material prices remained range bound and largely stable during the quarter and have contributed to Y-o-Y improvements on the operating performance.

items.statement: Won TEXPROCIL silver trophies for second highest exports in Cotton Madeups Terry Towels and Bed Linen Sheeting categories
items.quote: We won the silver trophies from the Cotton Textile Export Promotion Council, TEXPROCIL, for the second highest exports of Cotton Madeups in the Terry Towels category, and Cotton Madeups of the Bed Linen and Sheeting category as well.

items.statement: Certified Great Workplace by Great Place to Work Institute
items.quote: And we have also been certified Great Workplace by the prestigious Great Place to Work Institute, a global leader in workplace culture.

items.statement: Consolidated FY25 revenue guidance of INR 1,500-1,600 crore and blended EBITDA margin of 16%
items.quote: we are looking for a sales turnover of over INR1500 to INR1600 crores on consolidated basis and margins should be now to 16% on blended basis

items.statement: Full capacity consolidated revenue target of INR 1,700-1,800 crore when all plants fully operational
items.quote: From our subsidiaries and it can be on a console basis we are looking for a sales of about INR1,700 crores to INR1,800 crores when all the plants will be fully operational

items.statement: FY25 capex plan of INR 70-80 crore including solar installation and maintenance, expansion plans to be finalized soon
items.quote: roughly, as of now, we are having the capex plan about INR70 to INR80 crores, but for capacity expenses we will come out with the plans very soon

items.statement: Warangal unit capex spent INR 600 crore against envisaged INR 650 crore, third rPET line pending
items.quote: we have spent over about INR600 crores on our Warangal unit and almost all the plants have been operating, except this rPET granule line, which is expected to be operational by end of next month

items.statement: Standalone Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 11.72%, down 101 bps QoQ due to lower finished product prices
items.quote: We earned EBITDA of INR. 27.79 crores during Q4 FY24, dropped to 11.72% by 101 basis points over Q3 FY24 EBITDA margins of 12.73%

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 15.40%, up 137 bps QoQ with subsidiaries contributing INR 19.27 crore EBITDA
items.quote: EBITDA margins at 15.40% have improved by 137 basis points. In absolute terms, we achieved revenue of INR 305.53 crores and earned EBITDA of INR47.06 crores

items.statement: Warangal unit achieved over 22% operating profit in Q4 FY24 on improved utilization and new lines
items.quote: We achieved a very good set of numbers from our Warangal plant where we achieved operating profits of more than 22% during the quarter

items.statement: Subsidiary EBITDA per kg ~INR 30 (22% margin) sustainable, expected to improve with regulations from FY26
items.quote: the numbers are quite achievable and in future also. So, we are working and initially the regulation is to be started from FY26, from April 25. So, we are, in fact, looking for the improvement in margins going ahead

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting from 65% textile to 50% packaging / 50% textile in next 1-2 years driven by rPET capacity
items.quote: going forward, as we are moving ahead on the putting of more and more rPET general capacities, the major turnover, will come from the major sale will come from the packaging industry. So, going forward, say, in the next one or two years, we are seeing almost 50% contribution in sales will be from the packaging sector, 50% from the textile and technical textile

items.statement: Warangal sales mix includes year-long and multi-year contracts under discussion plus spot sales
items.quote: We have a few customers whom we have locked for year-long contracts and the multi-year contracts also already under discussion. And there are some sales that we are currently doing on spot basis

items.statement: FSSAI/EFSA food-grade approval for HDPE/PP recycling still pending, slowing non-PET expansion
items.quote: the regulation for approval from FSSAI for food safety of HDPE, PP is still pending. The FSSAI and EFSA both are not very much clear. It is still the EFSA, European Food Safety Council has also not decided the particular process

items.statement: Working capital cycle ~91-92 days, targeting reduction to 80 days with textile demand recovery
items.quote: the current working capital cycle is around 91-92 days which we are looking for to bring back to 80 days on average basis

items.statement: Average cost of borrowings 8.5% post debt reduction
items.quote: The cost of funds is about 8.5%.

items.statement: Warrants allotted January 2024, 18-month exercise period till September 2025, no conversion planned in FY25
items.quote: The warrant currency is for 18 months and we have allotted the warrants in January itself. So, the 18-month period is up to September 25. So, based on the requirement of the funds, we will convert the warrants in trenches also we can, but as of now there is no plan to convert in this financial year

items.statement: Rooftop solar installation at Warangal (~INR 30-32 crore) to save marginal power costs
items.quote: We are also installing a rooftop solar power plant at our Warangal unit to further our vision towards sustainable operations and to save marginal power costs on the other hand

items.statement: Industry rPET capacity expected 200,000-250,000 tons by FY25 end; competitors include JB Ecotech, VLS, Indorama
items.quote: as of today, the current expected capacity for the rPET industry by FY '25 end would be around 200,000 to 250,000 tons, which is currently under installation

items.statement: rPET market requirement 300,000-350,000 tons from April 2025 (30% of 1.2M tons), doubling to ~1M tons by 2028-30
items.quote: presently there is about 1.2 million tons of PET chips consumption, virgin chips. So, by regulation, from April'25 onwards 30% will have to be recycled and the rPET granules have to be mixed with the virgin. So, there is a requirement of 300,000 to 350,000 tons

items.statement: Warangal capacity: 42,000 tons rPET granules, 12,600 tons RPSF, plus filament yarn and PP staple fiber
items.quote: 42,000 ton is the rPet capacity and 12,600 ton is for the RPSF capacity. And rest is the filament yarn and polypropylene staple fiber

items.statement: Applied DNA traceability technology ready for launch, awaiting brand demand for consumer-facing recycled content verification
items.quote: we have done the trials and now we are ready to launch this. But yes somebody has to -- it has to come from the brands, from the market that they need this traceability to give, I should say a confidence to the consumer

items.statement: Manjushree 1% stake in South subsidiary not yet operative, shareholding agreement pending execution
items.quote: Though we have made the terms with them, but it has not been operative as of now. So, the shareholding agreement has not been executed so far maybe we may do it in the next quarter or so

items.statement: Lifetime merchant base reached 1.4 million, up from 240,000 in FY20, with 400,000 monthly transacting merchants
items.quote: We started in FY'20 at about 240,000 merchants. We closed FY'24 at close to 1.4 million merchants.

items.statement: Customer gross transaction value (GTV) grew 7% YoY to Rs 1.08 lakh crore in FY24, second consecutive year above Rs 1 lakh crore
items.quote: It's been a relatively flat year because of headwinds in the AePS business. So only a 7% growth , 107,000 crores compared to 100,000 crores in the previous year .

items.statement: Gross transaction value CAGR of 49% since FY20
items.quote: this number has grown at a CAGR of about 49% since FY'20.

items.statement: Service fee gross margin grew 10% YoY to Rs 169 crore in FY24 from Rs 154 crore in FY23
items.quote: Service fees, the main number that we track,which has grown from Rs. 154 crores the previous year to Rs. 169 crores in the last financial year .

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA of Rs 14.2 crore and PAT of Rs 12.1 crore in FY24
items.value: EBITDA Rs 14.2 crore, PAT Rs 12.1 crore
items.quote: We have achieved an EBITDA of Rs. 14.2 crores for the financial year and a PAT level of Rs. 12.1 crores at consolidated level .

items.statement: AePS industry Off-Us GTV declined 6% YoY to Rs 3.14 lakh crore in FY24 due to 2FA implementation and issuer bank limits
items.quote: In FY'23, if you look at the industry, it did about the Off-Us part of the industry, FY'23 was about Rs. 3,33,000 crores and in FY'24 that's dropped 6% to Rs. 3,14,000 crores.

items.statement: Spice Money AePS market share increased to 17.34% for FY24 from 17.15% in FY23, ending Q4 at 17.53%
items.quote: Despite the industry declining 6%, if you look at Spice Money GTV, we have declined 5%. So, we are gaining market share in the AePS industry. So, from 17.15%, we moved overall for the financial year for 17.34%, but we ended Q4 last year at 17.53% market share.

items.statement: Cash Management Services (CMS) GTV grew 54% YoY to Rs 27,682 crore in FY24, with 7,300 large CMS merchants contributing 90% of volume
items.quote: So, we are close to Rs. 27,000 crores in FY'24. This is the gross transaction value of the collections made from the branches compared to Rs. 18,000 crores in the past year .

items.statement: Bharat Bill Payment System (BBPS) GTV grew 90% YoY to Rs 4,190 crore in FY24, EMI loan repayments up 2.4x to Rs 3,160 crore
items.quote: year-on-year overall while we have grown 90% in customer GTV Rs. 4,190 crores compared to Rs. 2,210 cr ores which is about 1.9x growth. Within this EMI , loan repayments have grown 2.4x year-on-year, Rs. 3,160 crores from Rs. 1,325 crores.

items.statement: Cash & Cash-out share of gross margin fell from 77% to 68%, Collections rose from 8% to 14%, Subscription packs now 6%, Banking 2%
items.quote: if you look at our core business of Cash and Cash out, it's declined from a GM contribution point of view from 77% to 68%. And we have seen new product lines, especially if you look at collections, our contribution of collections to gross margin has grown from 8% to 14%.

items.statement: Lifetime savings accounts opened crossed 3.5 lakh, with 16,000 Adhikaris each opening 5+ accounts; BBPS repeat customer ratio near 50%
items.quote: We have opened close to 3.5 lakh accounts lifetime to-date as well as working with third-party lenders to lend to our merchants on our platform nearly about close to 100,000 loans that have been lent to-date

items.statement: Board approved entry into lending business via strategic NBFC acquisition to create credit products for merchants and small businesses
items.quote: we have also passed a resolution and made the necessary announcements where we are looking to enter the lending business through a strategic NBFC acquisition within the company.

items.statement: No short-term lending targets committed; building credit business over 10-20 years brick-by-brick with focus on product innovation, physical proximity, and risk management
items.quote: I will not commit to any short-term numbers here. This is a business over the next 10 to 15 to 20 years that we want to build, and we will build it like brick-by-brick, block-by-block.

items.statement: AePS headwinds from 2FA mandate and issuer bank transaction limits aimed at fraud control; company committed to reducing fraud-to-sales ratio
items.quote: This has led to a lot of restrictions in terms of two factor authentication, different limits set in by the issuer banks, which has caused an impact on the transaction numbers.

items.statement: Changed device capitalization policy in FY24; previously capitalized devices and provided right-to-use, now expensed, contributing to gross margin
items.quote: This is basically a change in capitalization policy because till FY'23, we were capitalizing the devices and providing a right -to-use to the Ad hikaris. This is something that we changed as a policy in FY '24

items.statement: Network covers 6,000+ blocks and nearly 2.5 lakh villages; focus on consolidating North, East, Central corridors for next 2 years, then expanding South and West
items.quote: Over the last five years, we have managed to achieve a significant pin code presence, mainly in Tier 3, Tier 4, Tier 5, Tier 6 India with over 6,000 blocks and nearly 2.5 Lakh villages covered

items.statement: Credit supply from third-party lenders has been erratic despite consistent demand; own NBFC planned to ensure consistent product manufacturing
items.quote: even though demand has remained consistent, supply has been erratic. And because of that, we are looking to also have our own NBFC so that we can ensure that we can cater to consistent demand.

items.statement: Third-party loans disbursed to merchants and customers neared 100,000 lifetime; key learnings include demand for customized products with friendly repayment mechanisms
items.quote: working with third-party lenders to lend to our merchants on our platform nearly about close to 100,000 loans that have been lent to-date

items.statement: Subscription packs introduced to ringfence high-transacting merchants and grow revenue market share during AePS industry consolidation
items.quote: what we mean by subscription packs is the merchants who are using our platform to do transactions, they are subscribing to these rental packs wher e they're paying us for the month

items.statement: AePS industry consolidating; Spice Money gaining share (17.53% in Q4) by focusing on merchant onboarding, training, fraud controls, and subscription model
items.quote: we are seeing consolidation in the space and the opportunity for a player like Spice Money to grow market share.

items.statement: PPI wallet license now UPI interoperable for 2 years; targeting inoperative bank accounts in rural India to drive UPI adoption via wallet
items.quote: we want to strategically use our PPI wallet license, which is now for the last two years, become UPI interoperable. It was not earlier .

items.statement: Figital model leverages physically enabled merchant network with digital platform for sourcing, KYC, and collections in lending business
items.quote: we have this digitally enabled merchant network on the ground, we are uniquely placed to build a physical plus digital model as we think about the le nding business.

items.statement: Exited all non-fintech businesses (Digital Technology Services) classified as discontinued operations; focusing purely on Spice Money fintech going forward

items.statement: Net cash flow US$12mn in Q4 FY24 before Pen-G and new market investments; net cash US$18mn end March 2024

items.quote: It is around 60-40; 60% value-added.

items.quote: EPR, already we registered for Andhra Pradesh unit, and the Tamil Nadu portal was not functioning for so many months. We are closely following it up with the government agency. Now only, it started working. Already, we applied for Tamil Nadu also.

items.statement: Green lead (hydrometallurgy) project at feasibility stage; commercial viability at scale being analysed
items.quote: So we have right now put it in the feasibility stage and we are analyzing the commercial viability on a large scale basis. Because, again, the new technology it is, like I said, the hydrometallurgy, expansion of it will eventually take some time.

items.statement: Unorganised sector 60-70% in lead, expected to decrease to 40% over coming years benefiting organised players
items.quote: So, if today, I see the unorganized market roughly to be 60% to 70%, so that number will probably increase -- decrease in the coming years, to say, for example, 40% would be unorganized, 60% would be

items.statement: Plastics division supplying to 10-11 OEM customers at 440-500 tonnes per month
items.quote: So right now, we have about, I think, 11 -- 10 to 11 customers, who we are supplying to. We are doing roughly about 400 to 500 -- between 440 tonnes to 500 tonnes a month, to be precise.

items.statement: Order book of 3.3 GW as of May 2024, split one-third EPC and two-thirds non-EPC, meant for FY25 and FY26 delivery
items.quote: This includes order book of 2.9-gigawatts as on 31st March '24, plus 402 megawatts of order announced in May. This is a well-diversi fied and healthy order

items.statement: Management does not provide delivery guidance; expects India wind installations of 4.5-5 GW in FY25, 7-8 GW in FY26, 9-10 GW in FY27; Suzlon market share historically 25-30%
items.quote: Ketan obviously, we cannot provide any guidance and we have followed that practice earlier and we continue to follow that as said J.P. sir earlier, we believe that in FY '25 installations on the ground will be around 5-gigawatts.

items.statement: WTG contribution margin 19.5% in FY24; fixed expenses ~INR 600 cr; FY25 margin expected in 15-20% range due to commodity cost pressure and S144 transition
items.quote: The contribution margin, Sumit, for FY '24 in the WTG division is about 19.5% whereas the fixed expenses, as we've been saying earlier, is close to about INR600 crores.

items.statement: O&M margin to remain around 40% vicinity for next 1-2 years; no significant improvement expected due to 3-year free O&M period on new installations
items.quote: So again, we maintained always t hat O&M margin will continue ar ound this vicinity, -- of course, a few basis points here and there. But I don't think improvement in O&M margins should be expected

items.statement: No new capex guidance given; manufacturing capacity not a constraint; working capital tie-up with REC Limited announced in December 2023
items.quote: Supply is not a constraint, especially now with our working capital and orders were available.

items.statement: 3 MW turbine (S144) order book share 83%; ramped up smoothly with >100 MW supplied and commissioned; no 5 MW turbine
items.quote: So the current order book is significantly for 3-megawatts. And as you look over in the investor presentation, 3-megawatt order book is 83% share.

items.statement: India wind installations 3.3 GW in FY24 (highest post FY17); FY25 expected 4.5-5 GW; strong pipeline of 27 GW bids awarded/announced; C&I share 58% of order book
items.quote: Wind installations for India for FY'24 broke the ceilings to registe r 3.3-gigawatt installation, the highest post FY'17

items.statement: Net cash position INR 1,148 cr as of March 2024; REC working capital tie-up in Dec 2023 with one-time INR 11 cr processing fee; LCs and BGs issued to customers/vendors increased interest cost
items.quote: We are pleased to report our balance s heet as of March '24 demonstrates a very strong posi tion of strength with a consolid ated net worth of INR3,920 crores, whereas the net cash position of the company as of March '24 stands at INR1,148

items.statement: Entire debt repaid; consolidated net worth INR 3,920 cr; net cash INR 1,148 cr as of March 2024; interest cost lower due to debt repayment
items.quote: All of this is a result of several initia tives that have been taken the company over the last -- in the last financial year, which incl ude margin improvements, cost optimization and lower interest costs as a result of repayment of the entire debt

items.statement: Government working on land and ROW issues; MNRE agreed in principle to reserve grid capacity in wind zones; exploring hybrid use of solar substations for wind
items.quote: the Ministry agreed in principle to see that we can cre ate a capacity, a grid capacity in exclusively the wind zones and given reserved for the wind

items.statement: C&I market share 58% of order book; targeting PSU bids (NTPC etc.) after net worth improvement; development contract model to secure land in advance
items.quote: Our orders would not be a concern. As a country, how much we're going to do each of the year becau se market share for me is a little misleading

items.statement: No significant competition pressure expected in next 2 years as market grows to 9-10 GW; Suzlon cheaper than European OEMs; turnkey EPC capability unique
items.quote: I don't think so when the pie is increasing to 9 to 10 gigawatt s. Obviously, I don't think we are even dreaming that we can deliver 9 to 10 gigawatts in FY'27

items.statement: India wind installation capacity addition: FY24 3.3 GW, FY25E 4.5-5 GW, FY26E 7-8 GW, FY27E 9-10 GW; Suzlon market share 27% in FY24
items.quote: Expectation this year is that the -- there are figures being talked today in the beginning of the year anywhere between 5 gigawatts and 7 gigawatts.

items.statement: Key external risks: grid connectivity delays (3-6 months), land acquisition challenges, solar booking CTU capacity before wind data available
items.quote: Challenges with transmission capacity -- not capacity, but coming on time would always remain a s t h e i s s u e.

items.statement: Multi-brand OMS acquisition started cautiously with 220 MW operating; will stabilize before significant expansion; not commenting on Siemens Gamesa specifically
items.quote: Today, we have about 220 megawatts we are operating today. Mos t part of it is we acquired during this year. But we want to take, look at them, stabilize before we actually expand

items.statement: Offshore wind not a near-term needle-mover (5-6 years to execute); green hydrogen demand to pick up in 2-3 years, will require wind for round-the-clock supply
items.quote: Offshore would happen at some point of time, but I don't think it's going to be a significant needle-mover immediately, because any offshore project, even today, to start, it won't be -- not for the next 5 years to 6 years.

items.statement: Expects India GDP growth at 6.5% for FY2025, with H1 below 6.5% and H2 at 7.2%
items.quote: Overall, ICRA expects the GDP growth to land at 6.5% in this financial year.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR100 per share including special dividend of INR60 per share for FY2024
items.quote: I am pleased to advise that the board has recommended, subject to shareholder's approval a dividend of INR100 per share, which includes a special dividend of INR60 a share.

items.statement: Pragati Development Consulting Services received SEBI approval as Category 1 ESG Rating Provider
items.quote: Pragati Development Consulting Services Limited to the subsidiary of ICRA Limited has received SEBI's approval for registration as Category 1 ESG Rating Provider.

items.statement: Acquired 60% of D2K Technologies in November 2023 to transform ICRA Analytics into diversified product company
items.quote: We are also excited about the prospects of our acquisition of D2K Technologies, a company that we acquired 60% of in November 2023, which aims to transform ICRA Analytics into a diversified product company.

items.statement: Rating accuracy metric ADP improved to 94% in FY2024 from 93.3% in FY2023
items.quote: The ADP print was 94% for the just concluded fiscal. We saw 93.3% in the previous year and against a long period average of 76%.

items.statement: Default instances dipped to 5 in FY2024 from 22 in FY2023 and 42 in FY2022
items.quote: The number of instances of defaults dipped to 5 in FY '24 compared to '22 in FY '23 and 42 in FY '22.

items.statement: Large rating change rate reduced to 0.7% in FY2024 from 1.4% in FY2023
items.quote: The severity of rating actions as measured by the large rating change rate also reduced to 0.7% in FY '24 from 1.4% in FY '23 and 2.3% in FY '22.

items.statement: Bank credit outstanding and bond issuances grew 16.3% and 17.2% respectively in FY2024
items.quote: Both the bank credit outstanding as well as bond issuances grew significantly at 16.3% and 17.2% respectively in FY '24 year -on-year as the overall cost of borrowing in the global market remained elevated and large corporates preferred to borrow domestically.

items.statement: Securitization volumes grew ~25% in FY2024 excluding large HFC exit impact
items.quote: Securitization volumes in the market are estimated to have grown at about 25% which is after ex cluding the impact of a large HFC that exited.

items.statement: Bank credit growth may face headwinds in FY2025 due to higher risk weights and elevated credit-to-deposit ratios
items.quote: Bank credit growth may face some headwinds with higher risk weights for certain high growth consumption segments as well as their elevated credit to deposit ratio for which the regulator has expressed some concern.

items.statement: Bond issuances likely to benefit from competitive domestic funding costs and possible RBI rate cut in FY2025
items.quote: Bond issuances are likely to benefit from competitive funding cost domestically which may additionally be supported by a possible rate cut by RBI sometimes later in FY '25.

items.statement: Higher risk weights on NBFC lending may shift funding to bond markets and securitization
items.quote: Hence, these entities are likely to shift to bond markets for their funding needs. So, what is likely to happen is the larger entities and the ones with better ratings would find it easier to tap the bond markets whereas the smaller entities would need to look at securitization more than what they have done in the past.

items.statement: Management focused on margin improvement through cost rationalization, technology efficiencies, repricing and rationalizing offerings
items.quote: We will continue to use multiple levers to deliver on this, either in terms of cost rationalization or bringing in efficiencies through technology interface or repricing some of our offerings, rationalizing some of our offerings, etc.

items.statement: Technology investments to continue for next few years; bulk of people cost corrections done 1-2 years ago
items.quote: Where we will continue to see spends over the next two to three years essentially will be in the technology area. This is an area where we have to naturally invest in infrastructure as well as enhancing the quality or efficiency of our applications to improve user experience both internally and with respect to our external users.

items.statement: Knowledge services growth slowed due to automation-driven project reduction; FTE billing stable
items.quote: Yes, it would be fair to say that we were hit more on the project side rather than on the FTE side.

items.statement: D2K acquisition strengthens risk management with credit monitoring, regulatory reporting, data management tools
items.quote: We see a strong demand from D2K on three verticals. First is on credit monitoring, second is on regulatory reporting and third is on data management.

items.statement: ESG rating business launched under Pragati subsidiary; teams and structure in place, engaging with market
items.quote: Well, we have been ready with this for some time now, because if you recall, the original consultation paper, I think was issued by SEBI a good probably about 18 months ago. And one was expecting the final framework, regulatory framework to land soon . So, we've had enough time to prepare ourselves well for it.

items.statement: Knowledge services heavily dependent on Moody's; diversifying to other global and domestic clients
items.quote: the knowledge servi ces business is heavily Moody's dependent. The acquisition that we made towards the end of last year in the non-ratings space, acquisition of D2K technologies, that again is consistent with our strategy of growing the non-ratings business

items.statement: Added marquee clients in securitization, BFSA, renewable energy, roads and EV sectors in FY2024
items.quote: On the corporate sector front, renewable energy, roads and EV sectors saw addition of marquee clients.

items.statement: Compete with captives for Moody's projects; automation both threat and opportunity for knowledge services
items.quote: The captives are a part of the set of entities which we compete with in order to get the business. So that's something which is ongoing.

items.statement: SEBI increased risk weights on bank lending to NBFCs/HFCs in late FY2024, moderating credit growth
items.quote: Credits to NBFCs and personal loan segmentsstill leads the rest in terms of incremental bank credit, though it moderated over the previous year as RBI increased the risk weight on bank lending to these segments in the later part of FY '24 as well as due to the merger of a large housing finance company with the bank in FY '24.

items.statement: ESG rating pricing will be market-driven, not regulated by SEBI
items.quote: So, see, it is not regulated the pricing is not regulated neither on credit rating nor on ESG ratings. There is a regulatory framework which SEBI has put in place under which many entities including ours has got a license. So, pricing is -- will be market driven. So, we will see how it evolves.

items.statement: Employee count ~1,500; ~400-450 in ratings, balance in non-ratings
items.quote: We would be at 1500. 400 ~, 450 would be Rating, and the balance would be non-rating side.

items.statement: No specific fund raise mentioned; capital allocation reviewed constantly, balancing expansion and payouts
items.quote: From a payout perspective, we increased the dividend last year. This year also, we have upped the dividend, and we also did an acquisition as well . When we look at allocation, we try to strike a fair balance between what we want for expansion and what we want as a payout.

items.statement: Watchful on FY2025 H1 economic momentum due to election-related capex slowdown, monsoon, weak merchandise exports, commodity price deflation dissipation
items.quote: ICRA is, however, watchful about the momentum of economic activity in the first half of this financial year, that is FY2025, stemming from potential slowdown in government capex during the general elections and the monsoon period, weakness in merchandise export growth and dissipation of the benefit of deflation in global commodity prices.

name: Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd

items.statement: FY25 capex target of Rs 17,000 crore, aiming for 6% of gross block

items.statement: FY25 capitalization target doubled to Rs 15,000-16,000 crore
items.quote: Capitalization was Rs. 7,618 crore, this year we will try to double it. We have many projects in pipeline and we are working day and night to achieve our capitalization; double of what we achieved last year. Maybe around 15,000-16,000 crores.

items.quote: EBITDA margin will be almost equivalent to the RTM. items.statement: Dividend payout not expected to reduce despite higher capex
items.quote: Not really. Like if we see the profit this year, it is Rs. 15,475 crore. And what I was taking that CapEx, it will be about Rs. 17,000 to 20,000 crore. items.statement: Work in hand of Rs 86,000 crore, over 80% for renewable energy evacuation

items.quote: In project execution, we had target of about Rs. 8,800 crore last year in FY24 but with the support of our partners we were able to achieve Rs. 12,500 crore CapEx in FY24, which is over 4% of our Gross Block, which is about Rs. 2,75,000 crore.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin ~87% for FY24

items.statement: TBCB projects target IRR of 10-12%
items.quote: For TBCB projects, when we bid for any project, we are very particular about IRR and we maintain that by ensuring our timely completion, cost overrun and financial cost is not there and we try to maintain about 10-12%. So we ensure that.

items.statement: FY24 dividend Rs 10,463 crore (68% of PAT), highest dividend payer

items.statement: Inter-regional capacity 99,580 MW (83% of total), system availability 99.85%
items.quote: Interregional capacity about 99,580 Megawatt, which is almost 83% of interregional capacity. This indicates that more than 100,000 Megawatts can be transmitted from one corner of the country to another corner of the country.

items.statement: Commissioned 5 TBCB projects in FY24: 19,720 MVA, 6 substations, 4,036 ckm
items.quote: As I told, we have executed the 5 TBCB companies which involved 19,720 MVA capacity, 6 numbers of substations and 4,036 circuit kilometers of transmission line.

items.quote: MoU we have signed with RVPNL, Rajasthan for formation of 74:26 JV company for intrastate transmission projects initially for about 10,000 crores transmission system and maybe later on many more will be there.

items.quote: Similarly, we are also in discussion with Andhra Pradesh Transmission company APTRANSCO for formation of JV company similar to Rajasthan and also with Assam and U.P. So, intrastate transmission system also is likely to be developed by POWERGRID through joint venture or through Intrastate TBCB companies.

items.statement: 7-8 year outlook: Rs 2,07,000 crore potential (transmission Rs 1,90,500 crore + other businesses)
items.quote: We see POWERGRID, how it looks like in another 7-8 years. We have mainly outlook in transmission business. Inter-state, we see it is on conservative side. items.quote: As per the Goldman Sach's report, that say that up to 2050, for energy transition, $1.68 trillion are to be spent only in transmission system. So $1.68 trillion, that means maybe around 135 to 140 lakh crore are to be spent by 2050 for energy transition and for transmission system.

items.statement: Smart metering: 69 lakh meters awarded, 30,000 installed, facing teething software issues
items.quote: Yeah, we have already awarded about 69 lakhs meter for Gujarat, Madhya Gujarat and Uttar Gujarat. And about 30,000 meters have been installed. Because this metering system is prepaid... earlier days it was postpaid basis, now it is on prepaid basis. So, there will be some teething problems. So, we are facing some teething problems which are being taken care, especially in software.

items.statement: Telecom revenue grew from Rs 729 crore to Rs 822 crore, 121 new customers, Rs 870 crore multi-year orders
items.quote: The telecom performance also has improved from Rs. 729 crore to 822 crore in FY23-24. 121 new customers have been added. Rs. 870 crore multiple year orders have been received.

items.statement: Green Energy Corridor for Ladakh (Pang to Kaithal HVDC) approved by Cabinet in FY24
items.quote: The cabinet approved Green Energy Corridor, especially for Ladakh, Pang to Kaithal HVDC and at Pang and Kaithal VSC stations and associated AC transmission line at Pang and Leh. This was approved in FY23-24.

items.statement: Intrastate JV projects to be regulated by SERCs, not CERC
items.quote: It will be on regulated, but it will be on state level regulation. It will not be through CERC, it will be through SERC.

items.statement: Committed to 50% renewable auxiliary consumption by 2025, net water positive by 2030, zero waste to landfill by 2030, net zero by 2047
items.quote: Towards sustainability aspirations, we are committed to reduce our electricity consumption from fossil fuel by 2025, that is more than 50% power will be through renewable for our auxillary consumption and other requirements. We are committed for net water positive organization by 2030, then zero waste to landfill status by 2030, net zero by 2047.

items.statement: Director (Personnel) Dr. Yatindra Dwivedi received ATD BEST Award 2024 in US (third time)
items.quote: Our Director (personnel) Dr. Yatindra Dwivedi, has gone to U.S. for receiving one of the very prestigious ATD BEST Award 2024 which we have received for the third time. It is a matter of pride for all of us.

items.statement: Achieved ISO 55001 Asset Management System Certification and ISO 37001 Anti-Bribery Management System Certification
items.quote: It is a matter of pride for POWERGRID that our operations have been certified for ISO 55001 for Asset Management System Certification. Only limited companies worldwide have been certified for ISO 55001 in recent past.

items.statement: Targets cumulative presales of ~INR 13,500 crore over FY25-FY27 backed by ~INR 25,000 crore portfolio
items.quote: For FY25, FY26, and FY27 we are targ eting a cumulative sales of ~INR 13,500 crore. This is backed by a sizab le projects portfolio of ~INR 25,000 crore

items.statement: Targets FY25 presales of INR 3,500 crore with launches of ~9 msf and INR 8,000 crore topline potential
items.quote: For FY25, we have a strong visibility of launching ~9 msf with a topline potential of about INR 8,000 crore.

items.statement: Expects FY25 EBITDA margins in early teens and FY26 margins towards late teens or around 20%
items.quote: FY'25, our EBITDA margins will be early teens. And FY'26, we are expecting our EBITDA margins towards late teens or even around 20.

items.statement: Targets FY25 revenue recognition of ~INR 2,000 crore and FY26 of ~INR 3,000 crore
items.quote: This is with the revenue recognition projections of around INR 2,000 crores in the ongoing financial year and around INR 3,000 crores in FY'26.

items.statement: Aims to acquire projects with topline potential of INR 8,000 crore in FY25 across Pune, Mumbai, Bengaluru
items.quote: In the current fiscal, we aim to acquire projects with the top-line potential of INR 8,000 crore across our key operating geographies of Pune, Mumbai and Bengaluru.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 3.7% due to low-margin legacy projects, higher overheads, and one-time charges
items.quote: FY24 EBITDA was recorded at INR 51.1 crore in FY24. During the year we reported a loss of INR 69.4 crore this is post minority interest.

items.statement: Embedded EBITDA margins on FY23 sales ~18-19%, improved to 26% for FY24 sales
items.quote: So if we do that calculation for FY'23, that number is close to 18%, 19%. And for FY'24, these numbers have improved from 18% / 19% to 26%.

items.statement: Life Republic FY24 gross margin ~29% at INR 5,100 avg realization; other projects 11-18% gross margin
items.quote: So LR GP was around 25%. So barring LR, for all other projects, the gross profits were in the range of 11% to 17%, 18%.

items.statement: Launched 2 projects in April-May 2024; plans INR 3,500 crore launches in Q1-Q2 FY25, Mumbai in H2
items.quote: in Q1 and Q2, we are talking about l aunches to the tune of around INR 3,500 crores, and we are confident of launching this kind of inventory

items.statement: Life Republic FSI increased from 0.5 to 1.7; new 24K high-rise project to consume >3 lakh sq ft/acre vs 1.8-2 lakh currently
items.quote: Now consistently, we are consuming around 1.8 to 2 lakh square feet per acre. And with this new development, we are going to consume more than 3 lakh square feet per acre.

items.statement: Life Republic realization improved from INR 5,400 (Dec 2022) to INR 6,000 avg; Phase 2 launched at INR 6,500; row house at INR 7,400-8,500
items.quote: Just 1 year back, December '22, we launched 1 sector at township at INR 5,400 as a launch price, but effectively, we have improved price in that same sector to INR 6,000.

items.statement: FY24 presales INR 2,822 crore (highest ever), volumes up 20% YoY to 3.92 msf, realization up 6%
items.quote: With sales value of INR 2,822 crore, we have achieved highest ever presales and have closed the year in line with our stated guidance. Sales volumes saw a significant uptick of 20% YoY reaching 3.92 msf compared to 3.27 msf in FY23. Realization improved by 6%.

items.statement: Net debt turned negative to -INR 25 crore (net cash) from INR 112 crore; net debt/equity -0.03
items.quote: Our net debt as on 31st March 2024 stands at INR -25 crore compared to INR 112 crore as on 31 st March 2023. Our net debt to equity stands at -0.03 as on March 31, 2024

items.statement: Finance cost run rate ~INR 100 crore/year for FY25-27 (Marubeni, other partners); goodwill impairment concluded in FY24
items.quote: Finance cost, Marubeni will be there. Other financial partners' cost will be there, which is why we anticipate INR 100 crores run rate for the next 3 years, that's FY'25, '26 and '27.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 4 per equity share (face value INR 10)
items.quote: We are happy to inform that the Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of INR 4/- per equity share of face value of INR 10/- each.

items.statement: 24K luxury segment at all-time high: sold INR 900 crore in FY24 vs INR 2,000 crore in last 10 years
items.quote: In last 10 years, we have sold an inventory close to INR 2,000 crores, and in this ongoing financial year itself, we have sold an inventory of around INR 900 crores.

items.statement: Non-Pune markets to contribute 25-30% of presales by end of FY25; Pune northwest market share 12-13%, rest of Pune <1%
items.quote: Pursuing our objective of diversification, we are confident that towards the end of the year, non-Pune markets will contribute 25-30% to pre-sales.

items.statement: Environment clearance received for most FY25 launch projects; RERA approvals pending for Wagholi, NIBM, Life Republic R5 sector
items.quote: We have received environment clearance for most of the projects. So considering that, we are confident about these launches.

items.statement: Acknowledges BD execution risk: landowner negotiations take multiple quarters; treading judiciously on BD front
items.quote: Agree, fair point, and which is why we are treading judiciously on this BD front.

items.statement: Enabling resolution for INR 1,000 crore debt/equity raise; no immediate plans, valuation sensitivity acknowledged
items.quote: So Viraj, this is just an enabling resolution. And, since last few years, we are taking this enabling resolution in order to save time if we find the right opportunity.

items.statement: Acquired 5% stake in Life Republic Township from minority stakeholders, taking ownership to 100%
items.quote: Additionally, during the year we acquired 5% stake in Life Republic Township from minority stakeholders, taking our ownership in the township from 95% to 100%.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY25 is INR5,600-5,700 crores, implying 15-16% growth
items.quote: As we told you before, like we are looking for a growth of around 15% to 16%. So we are looking for a number of INR5,600 to INR5,700 for FY '25.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 15-16% within 6-8 quarters from current 14-15% range
items.quote: And we should be surely able to maintain this margin, which is at the margins at which we have backed these orders. And of course, with the operational efficiency, we will be trying to -- we are working that within coming 6 to 8 quarters, we will try to take this EBITDA margin from 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY25 is INR6,000-8,000 crores including L1 projects, targeting order book of INR20,000-22,000 crores by end FY25
items.quote: And we intend to take our order book in this financial year of FY '25 close to around INR6,000 crores to INR8,000 crores, fresh order book and maintaining an order book of around INR20,000 to INR22,000 crores by end of FY '25.

items.statement: Debt guidance for FY25 is INR600-650 crores, to be funded through internal cash accruals

items.quote: The capex plan for this year is similar to be average of last year, plus we'll be adding a new facility. For that, we made an announcement that we'll be doing INR50 crores on that facility in Pune. INR50 crores.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 500 bps YoY to 26.1% in Q4 FY24 due to higher value-added sales and FOC catalyst strategy
items.quote: We have improved our gross profit margin consistently, which now stands at 26.1% from 20.9% in the corresponding quarter of last year. This margin expansion of more than 500 bps can be attributed to higher value-added sales.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 235 bps YoY to 14.1% in Q4 FY24 and 243 bps to 12.9% for FY24
items.quote: Notably, the EBITDA margin for the full year has expanded by 243 basis points, progressing from 10.4% in FY '23 to 12.9% in FY '24.

items.statement: FOC catalyst strategy on RDE products drove gross profit growth of 24% vs industry 5-10%; brick share reduced significantly
items.quote: our new products which have come in, in RDE have all been FOC, right? That's why one of the reasons why gross profit is up and it has outperformed the industry. So I think for the year, it's roughly up 24%, 25% versus industry growth of 5% to 10% if you take a blended rate

items.statement: TREM V tractor emission norms from April 2026 to be major growth driver; currently 5% of sales from off-highway
items.quote: When TREM V kicks in then we will be having additional revenues coming in from the industry. And that is going to be slightly large in size. It will definitely be a solid tailwind and we are looking forward to good business on the tractor industry.

items.statement: Nominated for 50%+ of tractor industry for TREM V; 3-player market in advanced emissions
items.quote: Mostly nomination 50% plus of the industry has already happened. And when the nomination happens, it's based on the go ahead to invest and to fully develop and to start on training the manufacturing lines, testing and so on, right?

items.statement: Added one new customer and nominated for EV+ICE platform in lightweighting vertical
items.quote: We have added one additional cust omer, plus we've been nominated for a good-sized platform, which is EV plus ICE for an existing customer. And that has given us a lot of confidence in this segment

items.statement: TREM V notified by government; OEMs investing and nominating suppliers; implementation expected April 2026
items.quote: It's notified by the government. It's a formal notification and almost all OEMs have nominated and started development also, right? So maybe there's just one or two OEMs left. So they are investing money into it.

items.statement: Buyback of INR228 crore plus final dividend of INR9.92/share (496% of face value); total distribution ~INR257 crore for FY24
items.quote: In line with our commitment to rewarding our shareholders, the company has declared a buyback of INR228 crores approx. inclusive of taxes. Furthermore, the Board has proposed a final dividend of INR9.92 per equity share equating to 496% of the face value of INR2 per share.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with surplus funds of ~INR900 crore including bonds and mutual funds
items.quote: The company continues to be debt free with surplus fund of approximately INR900 crores, including investment in bonds and mutual funds.

items.statement: Actively exploring M&A in powertrain agnostic segments with high moats and ROCE; conservative and selective approach
items.quote: We are actively exploring. However, we are conservative and selective because we want to only enter into segments which have high modes, have high ROCE and not just acquire for the need of acquiring.

items.statement: Gross profit growth of 24% YoY in FY24 vs industry 5-10% indicates strong value-added sales outperformance
items.quote: If you look at our gross profit increase, that has been far ahead of industry growth. And hence, the underlying growth in value-added sales is robust.

items.statement: LCV/PV demand environment business as usual; no particular positive or negative signals
items.quote: I mean we are not seeing anything in particular from the demand side. I think it's business as usual so far. And we don't see any kind of difference. So I would say nothing to comment upon, positive or the other way.

items.statement: Other expenses increased due to higher value-added sales (labour hire, freight, consumables, power, fuel); trend to continue
items.quote: So it has gone up because of the higher value-added sales in terms of labour hire charges, freight outward charges, consumables, power, and fuel etc. And as Aashim just said that it is going to continue like that.

items.statement: Low-cost advantage vs global peers in tractor emissions; 3-player market in advanced emissions
items.quote: Yes. So that's an advantage for us, right, being the low-cost player any of this, as the other two, three competitors are global companies. So, that is one of our strengths, and that's why we're not to play out on the tractor industry as well.

items.statement: Export timing uncertain due to global off-highway slowdown in US/Europe; pipeline good but difficult to time
items.quote: Also, as Puru sir mentioned that globally, the off-highway segment is in a slowdown, which has more to do with the U.S. and Europe market. So to time is difficult. However, the pipeline is good.

items.statement: Lightweighting vertical (suspension, control arms) growing; addressable market larger than emissions; selective profitable sub-segments focus
items.quote: This sector is or this segment is very big when it comes from an addressable market perspective. However, we want to be cautious and only address the sub-segments, which are profitable and have an overall good ROCE picture.

items.statement: No specific revenue or margin guidance; gross profit absolute preferred metric; steady-state EBITDA margin not guided
items.quote: So it's very hard to guide on one number but you can look at gross profit as the base for any year and that would be helpful to look at growth versus industry. And it would never be exact on a sequential quarterly basis and so on.

items.statement: No specific export revenue guidance; addressable market multi-fold of India opportunity; building team and pipeline
items.quote: The numbers that we are seeing in terms of how these larger companies are buying, especially on the segments that we are working on, on our product and its adjacencies has positively surprised us also. So the addressable market when we look is multi-fold of the India opportunity.

items.statement: Eberspaecher JV contribution small at 2-3% of consolidated profit; focused on CV/HCV, cyclical, hard to predict
items.quote: As a percentage of our overall consolidated profit, it's still roughly 2% to 3% only. It's not a lot. And we do expect this business to do better as we go forward but very hard to predict because this is focused on the commercial vehicle and heavy commercial vehicle industry.

items.statement: 3-4 litre engine segment in development phase; product ready but commercialization timing uncertain; potential 30-40% market share
items.quote: We are in the development phase only of that. We are ready. This is a market that is harder to penetrate in terms of timing though we are optimistic that we'll be able to penetrate it. And once we penetrate it, we straightaway get about 30%, 40% market share of it.

items.statement: Construction equipment volumes ~20% of tractor industry; high-value adjacencies; global OEMs buying from China currently
items.quote: It would be roughly, I would guess, about 20% of the tractor industry or slightly under 20%. But this is a guesstimate because I don't have the numbers in front of me. However, this is a very attractive segment as this has a lot of adjacencies for our part.

items.statement: CEV V and TREM V notified; Euro 7/BS-VII timing depends on global developments; content increase linked to legislation
items.quote: Within the Indian market, the legislation that's on the Horizon are CEV-V, TREM V and then Euro 7. CEV V and TREM V are much closer and notified. And Euro 7 or BS-VII will depend on how it plays out globally.

items.statement: Building bigger export team over FY25; senior management accessibility being improved
items.quote: We have built a team. We are building a team -- a bigger team now, which we'll be building over the course of this year.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 had a mixed bag of content with some successes and underperformance; FY24 showed industry resilience with diverse releases across languages and genres.
items.quote: Overall, the fourth quarter had a mixed bag of content, closing the year with a blend of successes and underperformance.

items.statement: Management does not provide specific revenue projections for FY25 but offers directional views on business model margins.
items.quote: You may have noticed that we don't provide projections or estimates for future years. This is a strategic decision we've made.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin improved by 796 bps to 16.5% from 8.5% in FY23.
items.quote: The EBITDA Margin improved by 796 bps from 8.5% in FY23 to 16.5% in FY24.

items.statement: Advertisement screen network expanded to 3,859 screens in FY24 from 3,348 in FY23, with Prime Screens up 419 and Popular Screens up 92.
items.quote: The Advertisement screen network was at 3,859 screens as compared to 3,348 screens in FY23 and 3,792 scr eens in FY20 with a notable boost in both Prime Screens by 419 and Popular Screens by 92 screens as compared to FY23

items.statement: CapEx was consciously controlled in FY24 to observe industry performance; future CapEx expected to increase with exhibition industry growth.
items.quote: Additionally, last year, we consciously controlled our capital expenditures (CapEx) to observe industry performance.

items.statement: Working capital stabilized over past 5-6 quarters post-COVID; incremental requirements not significantly increasing, aiding cash flow.
items.quote: Over the past 5-6 quarters, as our business has stabilized post-COVID, we've reached a point where incremental working capital requirements have not significantly increased.

items.statement: Company remains net cash positive as of March 31, 2024, with consolidated funds balance of Rs. 1,098 million.
items.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the company continues to be net cash positive after considering outstanding debt.

items.statement: Multiplex screens now constitute ~55% of network (2,117 screens) vs single screens 1,742; Prime screens 85% multiplex.
items.quote: Consequently, the proportion of multiplex screens now around 55%.

items.statement: Government ad revenue grew 85% YoY in FY24 to ~INR 41 crores (incl. Caravan); driven by state governments and PSUs (INR 28 crores), central government contribution minimal.
items.quote: Our total government ad revenue increased from INR 17 crores in FY23 to nearly INR 41 crores (including caravan). Of this INR 24 crores increase, INR 12 crores came from state governments and PSUs, and about INR 8 crores from Caravan.

items.statement: Government ad spending restricted during election code of conduct; political parties use network for campaigns; clarity on central government spending expected post-June.
items.quote: As for the current quarter, government spending is restricted due to the code of conduct during the election period.

items.statement: NOVA Cinemaz project has 16 screens across 8 properties in pipeline; first two properties near Meerut expected to open in Q1 FY25 (one awaiting license, second 95% complete).

items.quote: Annually, this is close to 2,000 movies, up from around 1,800 pre-COVID.

items.statement: Incremental advertisement revenue yields 65-70% operating margin; incremental CDC revenue fetches nearly 90% margin.
items.quote: Incremental advertisement revenue typically yields a 65 -70% operating margin, while incremental CDC revenue fetches nearly a 90% margin.

items.statement: Central government ad spend remains significantly reduced (INR 3.6 crores vs peak INR 100 crores); recovery uncertain and dependent on post-election policy.
items.quote: For context, our best year saw INR 100 crores in revenue from the central government, compared to just INR 3.6 crores this year.

items.statement: Caravan ad revenue hit highest since FY19 after CBC empanelment; growth expected from both government and corporate advertising.
items.quote: Caravan's advertisement revenue sustained the momentum and marked the highest advertising revenue since FY19.

items.statement: Expects 15% revenue growth in FY25 with margins similar to FY24; targets Rs 1,000 crore revenue by FY28
items.quote: So, we expect 15% minimum growth for next year and let us see that we achieve this target of 1000 crore by FY28.

items.statement: Expects 15% growth in FY25; margins not expected to change much; 1,000 crore target remains
items.quote: Yes, for this year we are expecting 15% growth and margins we don't expect to change much. We are working towards it, but we don't expect as of right now, for a change in margins. And yes the 1000 crore goal is also set.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 13.72% for FY24; expects similar margins in FY25, possible 50 bps improvement by FY28
items.quote: Margins would be in the range only. So, margins would be in that range only, whatever we are doing little bit variation, but not much expected.

items.quote: The total CAPEX outlay for FY24 was INR 26 crore, and the company plans to invest an additional INR 60 crores in FY25 funded through internal accruals.

items.quote: The company achieved a branded sales percentage of 41% during FY24 up from 36% in FY23. This was because of rising demand of branded range of PPE in India, Middle East and Southeast Asia. Before also in accordance to the lackluster growth in Europe and some supply chain issues that we face for private label markets.

items.quote: So the percentage split, we are looking at a similar percentage split as what we had this time. So, I don't see much difference in the percentage split for 25 and 26.

items.quote: Yes, definitely that is happening. So the labor regulations are getting stricter. items.quote: So, for three segments like we manufacture leather, and leather gloves and safety shoes for that we use leather, then we use PU for shoe sole, we use nitrile compound for synthetic glove PU also for synthetic gloves, then garments this fabric both cotton and poly cotton and synthetic. items.quote: It is in the range of for export business, it is networking capital days are almost 90 to 100 days, and in case of domestic market it is around 30 days max.

items.quote: So, operating cash flow is on the lower side, because of increase of working capital requirements. items.quote: So, in terms of your first question for M&A, so we are always on the lookout for interesting offers that there are, we would definitely like to strengthen ourselves in those product categories, where we are not present or in those geographies where we are not present and if something like that comes up, which complements our current offering, we will be definitely interested to look into it.

items.statement: ~50-60% of Indian market unorganized; organized market growing as demand shifts from unorganized to organized due to quality awareness, MNCs, larger corporations seeking certified products
items.quote: Yes, we do almost, we say almost 50% to 60% of the Indian market is unorganized. So, you can understand the size of the unorganized market and till the point proper certifications in place in India and there is proper policing of the standards and certification, this market will continue to grow. So, that's the competition that we are in.

items.quote: And most of our products are in 90%, or maybe more 95%. We are manufacturing on our own. items.quote: So between $4 million and $5 million was the capital investment in the unit, we are expecting to have full production from June.

items.quote: We will build capacity, expect to be EUR3 million to EUR4 million. That's the sort of expectation on the investment. It won't be large. We are evaluating and we will revert back once there is any finality on that.

items.statement: European operations at 85% utilization, can grow 10% in FY25 without additional capacity
items.quote: We are about, I would say, 85% capacity utilization in the European context. Therefore, for FY '25, we have no challenge for growth. We should be able to grow 10% thereabouts without any additional capacity constraint.

items.statement: Gross margin sustainable at 44-45%, no further improvement expected long-term
items.quote: I think the margin at current 44%, 45% gross margin will be sustainable. We will look at maintaining that kind of margin. There is no further expectation of improvement of margins in this scenario on a longer-term basis.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 16% sustainable, operating leverage to improve margins after Vashivali restoration
items.quote: Yes. On the net margin basis, these are good products, so they are high-volume throughput products. So, we have low operating cost per kilo but the gross margin at a per kilo level will be lower. The net margins are the same as a normal business.

items.statement: Global Ingredients business turned profitable through backward integration and cost reduction, now market leader with >50% global share
items.quote: Our strategic response included Q4 & FY24 Concall Transcript implementing a comprehensive backward integration project in India and focusing on improvements of productivity and cost reduction, which has significantly transformed this segment this quarter. items.statement: Raw material prices stable with slight upward movement since February-March lows

items.quote: We are already doing a business of more than $10 million in the Southeast Asia region, in ASEAN. and having this facility within ASEAN makes it duty free and easy for accessing the ASEAN market. We built this as one of our next growth pillars.
