items.quote: We see an 8% to 10% growth rate on a sustainable regular CAGR basis and additional geographies, additional customers or new customers where we don't have an existing business will ramp up the growth rate to 12% and above in terms of a CAGR growth.

items.statement: Strengthened talent pool with high-quality senior personnel from industry for next leg of growth

items.quote: So, the tax rate, what you see now, there is an increase because of our deferred tax reversal, which is a one-off. On a normalized basis, our tax rate will be 29% to 30%.

items.quote: See, the capex that we have guided was about INR 1000 crores. We slightly underspent on that. So, that's probably the INR 850-crore number you're looking at

items.quote: We are also very experienced now within all dimensions of it, whether it is an acquisition in Israel or Spain or Latin America, US, etc. We have covered significant ground and experience to understand the various challenges and dynamics. So we will be carefully calibrating. If the right opportunity emerges, we'll guide you towards that.

items.statement: Organic revenue growth ~18.5% YoY in Q4 FY2024 on consolidated basis after global impact adjustments.
items.quote: Now, when we look at the organic growth of our company in this Q4 at an overall consolidated level, and not just at developed markets or emerging markets level, we achieved organic growth of about 18.5% y-o-y in this quarter.

items.statement: Premium inventory and touchpoints strategy; inventory & data cost 61% of revenue in Q4, flat YoY but improved sequentially despite premium calibration.
items.quote: our Inventory and Data Cost stood at 61.0% of revenue from operations in this quarter, which was almost in line with Q4 previous year, while it witnessed margin improvement sequentially despite our ongoing platform calibrations on to prem ium inventories, touchpoints and deeper ecosystem -level

items.statement: Pricing power expected to improve as premium value demonstrated; gestation period for higher CPCU rates via innovation, competition, and proof of ROI.
items.quote: Pricing is always a sensitive topic and to command a higher price, you have to first demonstrate higher value, right? So the way it works is that as you go more premium, we'll be able to show to the advertisers that when they're working with us, they're getting higher value. Consequently, we should command better pricing.

items.statement: Filed 15 new GenAI patent claims; received 1 US patent grant; total IP portfolio 36 patents (9 granted); 2 new grants in early FY2025 (1 US, 1 India).
items.quote: We have further expanded our technological prowess harnessing next -gen technologies in a responsible manner, particularly in AI by filing 15 new Gen AI patent claims, as well as received 1 US patent grant that was previously filed, to unlock competitive advantage and to augment our market position. Additionally, we have started FY2025 with significant momentum, having recently secured one patent

items.statement: Strong 20-25 CXO/VP level leaders (many 10-18 years tenure); acquired talent retained via stock options aligned to 5x growth expectation; no management bandwidth issue.
items.quote: I would say there's at least a good 20 to 25 people who are CXO VP level people in this company of only 600 people. So we don't have a management bandwidth issue at the moment.

items.statement: Real money gaming in India not fully recovered; taxes raised consumer costs, lowered incentives; solution is premium user targeting via iOS, CTV, CPCU, GenAI.
items.quote: I wouldn't say real money gaming has bounced back fully . It's yet to be back to its past glory, and there is definitely some impact. But Affle has gone beyond that. We are not interested in just talking real money gaming because Affle is way more than

items.statement: Seasonality remains: Q3 typically peak, Q4 lower; Q4 FY2024 was normalized base, not one-off; model Q4 FY2025 slightly below Q3 FY2025.
items.quote: I would expect that trend to continue. But at the same time, this Q4 is not a one -off in the sense that this is the new base. This is the new base where we are a t, and on this base we will be able to continue to build

items.statement: Tax rate increased in Q4 FY2024 and expected to gradually inch upwards.
items.quote: Our Profit After Tax for the quarter stood at Rs. 875 million, an increase of 40.2% y-o-y and 13.9% q-o-q, despite an increase in the effective tax rate this quarter and our tax rate is expected to gradually inch upwards.

items.statement: Targets ~19% revenue CAGR (last 5-year pace) for FY25; volume growth at FY24 run-rate (~21%); aims to reach 10-11% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We believe that we have been growing at the same steady state at what we have been doing last 5 years. If you see the CAGR for the last 5 years, we have been at about 19% but this year has been at the exceptional different year.

items.statement: First target is to reach 10-11% EBITDA margin in FY25; believes this is the year to perform
items.quote: We have been successful increasing our gross margins and the rest will automatically follow we believe. And with the growth that we aspire, I think the first target is to first get to that between 10% to 11% and we believe this is the year to perform.

items.statement: Current demand environment not great; not in summer products like fans/coolers; growth driven by new channels and products
items.quote: On the current times , I can tell you that on the demand , particularly we are not in the summer products like fans or coolers but overall, the business is going through not great demand times.

items.statement: Added 117 stores in FY24 (target was 7-8/month); ended with 171 stores in 50 cities across 8 states; pipeline full for 25-30 stores/quarter
items.quote: It gives me immense satisfaction to shar e that the Company has added 117 stores in FY24 , far exceeding our initial target of adding 7/8 stores per month. We concluded the year with a strong network of 171 stores in 50 cities across 8 states.

items.statement: Capex cycle ending; FY25 budget Rs 50 cr (includes concluding capex); ongoing maintenance capex ~Rs 25 cr; FY25 capex well below depreciation
items.value: Rs 50 cr budget; Rs 25 cr maintenance
items.quote: For this year, we have a budget of Rs. 50 crores. That includes the concluding CAPEX and a normal ongoing CAPEX will be about Rs. 25 crores.

items.statement: Manufacturing localisation at 91-92% of revenue; Himachal facility now 100% inner-lid pressure cookers; no new capex planned
items.quote: We are currently between 91 % and 92%, the total contribution from our revenue is coming from the manufactured products within the factories of Stovekraft.

items.statement: Aluminium input cost degrowth passed to consumers; value growth muted but volume strong; no input-cost disruption this year unlike last year
items.quote: There has been a huge I can say input cost degrowth which as a policy of the Company we pass on the benefits to the consumer. So, in value terms we are not seeing growth but volume of course we are growing.

items.statement: Q4 growth led by appliances (+33%), cookware (+33%), induction cooktops (+63%); launched Pigeon Healthy ifry, cast iron cookware, kettles, dough makers, bottles, hobs
items.quote: The biggest growth for us has come in from appliances which is 33% . O n the non-stick cookware, the growth has been 33% again or the cookware category, it's not exactly nonstick. Overall, the cookware category has grown by 33% for us and in the quarter our induction cooktop we have grown by 63%.

items.statement: Q4 growth from corporate sales & own retail; general trade flat; e-com +9% FY24; exports +26% FY24; FY24 revenue mix: GT 540 cr, e-com 440 cr, MT 165 cr, exports 160 cr, corporate 77 cr, retail 42 cr
items.quote: Channel wise also I can give you, for the quarter our general trade has been flattish but e-com is the bigger growth have come in our corporate sales and our own retail. These two channels have given higher growth, both our corporate sales and our retail.

items.statement: ECL provision raised to Rs 4.7 cr (from 1.5-1.6 cr) for legacy reconciliation items; one-time cleanup; receivables now more comfortable
items.quote: So, there were some reconciliation items that were pending from the previous year for which we have provided in our ECL. They are continuing for a long time and in the process of cleaning up our receivables, we have brought it in the ECL.

items.statement: Targets near debt-free by end FY25; lease liability includes manufacturing (foundry) not just retail; Ind-AS 116 lease interest ~Rs 6-7 cr, depreciation ~Rs 9-10 cr
items.quote: This year h opefully before the end of the year we should be very close or aspirationally we should be debt free.

items.statement: Board recommended first maiden dividend of Rs 2.5 per share
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that our board has recommended our first maiden dividend of Rs. 2.5 per share.

items.statement: CTO and CHRO recently left; management broadening; some initiatives fructify, others not; win-win needed for professionals
items.quote: We have a dynamic situation. We are embarking on several initiatives. Some of the initiatives of course, we are broad basing our management team and some things fructify based on our plans and some not necessarily.

items.statement: Channel conflict possible but managed; general trade grows in cities with COCO stores; franchise pipeline strong (30-35 signed, 15-18 handed over)
items.quote: We would want to be available to our consumer wherever they would want to by our products. We will explore all possibilities on expanding our channels , particularly domestically and then of course internationally.

items.statement: Operates in value segment; leader in categories; pressure cooker value -2% but volume +18%; growing in all categories
items.quote: We are operating in a different segment. We are addressing the largest consumer base in this country, the value consumer. And in the category that we operate we are leaders.

items.statement: Aluminium cost degrowth passed to consumers; no input cost disruption this year; gross margin protected
items.quote: This year we have not experienced that and we believe that there is a lot of learning that has happened and we will be cautious enough to protect our margins at the gross margin level.

items.statement: Sold modular kitchen manufacturing facility to vendor; SKAVA merged with LED and defocused; Black & Decker not highlighted
items.quote: We have let go ne our manufacturing facility. We have sold it to a vendor who takes care of the manufacturing part . The need base we buy and then they sell it to only through our retail outlets.

items.statement: Retail model shifting: 171 COCO stores capped; future stores COFO (franchisee-operated, funded by franchisee deposits); 25-30 stores/quarter run-rate
items.quote: We will retain 100. At any point of time, the number of Company owned, Company operated stores will not exceed 171. The newer and increasing number of these stores will be through the franchise route.

items.statement: Target EBITDA of at least INR 300 crores in FY27
items.quote: In 2024, we have taken significant steps to lay a foundation for accelerated growth in coming years, with the target of achieving an EBITDA of at least INR 300 crores in FY27.

items.statement: Expect faster growth in revenue and EBITDA in FY25
items.quote: We are optimistic about FY25 anticipating faster growth in both revenue and EBITDA and the impact of many of our initiatives should be visible from onwards.

items.statement: Raised INR 950 crores equity capital in FY24, net cash balance ~INR 1,450 crores
items.quote: This year, we have arisen successfully between the parent entity and our subsidiaries INR 950 crores of equity capital marking our largest fundraise to date and resulting in a net cash balance of approximately INR 1,450 crores.

items.statement: At least 4-5 ongoing diligences, expect to close a couple by Q2 FY25
items.quote: At this point of time, we at least have 4-5 ongoing diligences with various companies and we hope to get at least a couple of them across the finished line by Q2 of FY25.

items.statement: Focus on core gaming IP acquisitions, AI playbook for margin expansion and growth
items.quote: one key focus is core gaming IP s, very similar to what we did with WildWorks and Animal Jam, which is playing out pretty well for us and we think we can double down over there

items.statement: Active conversations with large RMG players, no definitive timeline
items.quote: On the R MG side , we are not waiting for any regulatory clarity, like you have right away mentioned, GST is already quite clear going forward and we are active plea in conversations with a couple of large players in that space to do something

items.statement: Predominantly all-cash deals going forward, may use equity for founder incentives
items.quote: So, I think there will be predominantly all cash deals at this point of time. We want to reduce the amount of equity we issue unless it is really needed.

items.statement: Acquired remaining stake in World Cricket Championship, new game launching shortly
items.quote: We have also in recent times scaled up our marketing and starting to see good traction. We see some global expansion opportunities. We see platform expansion opportunities on consoles, PCs and other platforms outside of mobile. And we are also launching a brand new game now in this quarter very shortly.

items.statement: Core gaming businesses should generate 25-30% margins, confident of uplifting margins over next 1-2 years
items.quote: We believe that core gaming businesses should generate 25%-30% kind of margins and there is enough room for us to increase our margins. So, I think there is a lot of focus on that and over the next year or two years, we are very confident of uplifting the margins.

items.statement: Sportskeeda margins expected to continue strong performance in FY25
items.quote: We do expect actually that it will continue for a while longer still. The market in the US is much larger than what we currently tap, even in terms of number of sports.

items.statement: Esports expected to come back strongly in FY25, bullish on Playground IP and international expansion
items.quote: But that said, we personally expect FY25 to come back very strongly on Esports and are very bullish. We have seen also some good signs, for example, our playground IP is really taking strong footing.

items.statement: Ad Tech business expected to return to growth from Q2 FY25
items.quote: We are backing that Q2 onwards of this year. We should be able to achieve our growth status on the Ad Tech. I think again we have done a lot of groundwork there and FY2 5 should bounce back on go to growth both in terms of revenue and EBITDA

items.statement: Kiddopia exploring IP licensing to drive organic traffic and breakthrough UA plateau
items.quote: What we are very bullish about right now is that by bringing in popular IP of known characters, because these IP's and characters are very popular with kids, we should be able to drive a lot more organic traffic, which kind of provides us scale and provides us with a much better blended cost per trial.

items.statement: Animal Jam new game in alpha in 3-4 months, beta by end of FY25
items.quote: When we say new game, we mean something different, which is an entirely new game bein g developed by the team and that is something that we expect to take into alpha in about 3-4 months and beta by the end of the year

items.statement: Publishing platform primary focus on India market, targeting global games underexplored in India
items.quote: The primary focus for the publishing team is actually the India market. So, we have essentially two kinds of studios that we work with or intend to work with on the publishing side, one are the smaller indie studios where maybe small indie developers locally from India, who may also target the US market.

items.statement: AI task force created to build playbook for studio optimization and player engagement
items.quote: We have AI task force internally that is focusing on many innovative ways of using AI, testing it out on a couple of our studios with intent to create a playbook that can be replicated across everything else we do.

items.statement: NODWIN FY24 revenue INR 427 crores, Q4 revenue INR 99.1 crores (down 9% YoY)
items.quote: During FY24, NODWIN raised INR 190 crores from strategic investors and made several acquisitions including Comic Con India, Publish.Me, Ninja, Freaks4U, which is an investment branded and the IP related to Playground.

items.statement: Sportskeeda FY24 revenue INR 196 crores (up 60% YoY), Q4 revenue INR 49 crores (up 71% YoY)
items.quote: Sportskeeda reported a robust year-on-year revenue growth of 60% to INR 196 crores in FY24 and 71% year-on-year growth in Q 4 FY24 to INR 49 crores

items.statement: Ad Tech FY24 revenue INR 104 crores (down from INR 153 crores), gross margin improved to 27%
items.quote: Ad Tech FY24 was a reset for data works as we shifted focus from lower-margin clients to higher-margin clients and product business . This strategy pivot resul ted in the revenue drop from IN R 153 crores in FY23, INR 104 crores in FY24. Gross margins improved from 19% in FY23 to 27% in FY24

items.statement: Kiddopia Q4 revenue declined ~12% to INR 60.9 crores, EBITDA increased to INR 11.7 crores, ARPU up ~1% QoQ
items.quote: Kiddopia, the FY24 revenue was stable, while EBITDA grew by 57% year-on-year. Q4 revenue declined by around 12% to INR 60.9 crores, while EBITDA increased to Rs. 11.7 crores.

items.statement: Animal Jam FY24 revenue INR 95 crores, EBITDA ~INR 19 crores; Q4 revenue up 7% to INR 24 crores
items.quote: Moving to Animal Jam: FY24 revenue was INR 95 crores with EBITDA of around Rs. 19 crores. Q4 revenue increased by around 7% to INR 24 crores with EBITDA going to INR 2.9 crores.

items.statement: NODWIN market share ~80%, Playground Season 3 had 24 million viewers, revenue at least 50% higher than Season 2
items.quote: NODWIN currently has 80% market share and I think that is a tough one to breakthrough given the kind of partnerships and investors NODWIN today has.

items.statement: GST regime since Oct 2023 impacted RMG industry profitability, exploring consolidation post regulatory clarity
items.quote: The new GST regime since October 23 has impacted the entire real money gaming industry profitability. Our focus has been on improving operating efficiencies through new product launches and cost optimization. We are exploring consolidation in the R&D space following regulatory clarity.

items.statement: NODWIN not worried about competition (e.g., BGIS by Tesseract), competition helps expand market
items.quote: I think competition is always good to be there. It keeps us on our toes. We think NODWIN is way ahead of the game at this point of time in terms of market share, brand awareness and partnership that is advanced.

items.statement: Founders retain significant stake and autonomy post-acquisition, liquidity events at higher valuations
items.quote: First of all, whenever you acquire the business founders take one significant stake in the business. Second, we never considered them as an employee of the business, right? They are founders running the business and in fact largely have autonomous way of running the business.

items.statement: Media rights slowdown due to OTT funding crunch and TV/large media company issues
items.quote: The OT T players, given the start up funding crunch have struggled to raise capital and therefore have kind of slowed down media spends and also everything that is going on with the TV channels and the large media companies that kind of slowed down that process

items.statement: Industry expected to see double-digit revenue growth in FY25
items.quote: Anticipating a robust performance, the consumer durable and electronic industry is poised for a double-digit revenue surge in F Y'25

items.statement: Plan to open 30-plus stores in FY25 with 10 in Q1
items.quote: So we would be doing around 30-plus stores in this financial year, out of which we have already opened six in the first quarter itself and then another five are getting ready which are due opening in the next 30 to 40 days.

items.statement: Store count reached 160 at end of March 2024 (147 MBOs, 13 EBOs)
items.quote: Our store count at the end of March '24 stands at 160 stores, 147 of which are MBO s and 13 are EBOs

items.statement: EBITDA margin 7.1% in Q4 FY24 and 7.2% for FY24; expect similar margins in FY25
items.quote: I think we would look at a similar number also going forward.

items.statement: Robust surge in consumer demand for premium appliances in FY24
items.quote: In FY'24, the segment has observed a robust surge in consumer demand for premium appliances.

items.statement: FY24 revenue mix: 45% large appliances, 42% mobile, 13% small appliances/IT/others
items.quote: For FY'24, around 45% of our revenue came from large appliances, 42% from mobile and 13% from small appliances, IT and others.

items.statement: Working capital days at 74 as of March 2024 due to summer inventory stocking
items.quote: The working capital days as on 31st March '24 stood at 74 days, which was mainly due to stocking of inventory to meet the demand during the upcoming and ongoing summer season.

items.statement: Gross and net debt-to-equity at 0.5x, net debt-to-EBITDA at 1.4x; cost of borrowings reduced 7% YoY
items.quote: Both the gross debt-to-equity and net debt-to-equity stood at 0.5X, and the net debt-to-EBITDA stood at 1.4x.

items.statement: Blended gross margin ~15%; mobile/IT 7-8%, large appliances 17-18%
items.quote: So for blended number, it would be what you see on a balance sheet around 15% and the lowest I would tell you would be around 7% to 8% for IT, mobile as a category and the larger appliances would be upwards of say 17%, 18%.

items.statement: 65% of sales via credit/financing, 35% via UPI/cash; similar across metro and Tier-2/3
items.quote: So the total blended would be around 65%: 35%, 65% being through credit card, payment financing or the financing activities on the floor versus 35% through UPI, direct payments and cash payments.

items.statement: Cannibalize own stores strategically in high-performing locations (100 crore+ stores)
items.quote: So whenever we try to do it is there for all the stores which are 100 crore plus for us for example.

items.statement: New store capex ~Rs 2,500/sq ft; 10,000 sq ft store needs ~Rs 2.5 cr capex + Rs 2.5 cr inventory
items.quote: Around 2.5 crores of inventory and 2.5 crores of CAPEX, around 5 crores is what we look at as our store cost initially when we set up a new store of a 10,000 square feet area.

items.statement: North cluster breakeven 20-24 months vs 12-14 months in South; target 35 cr/store for 5-6% pre-Ind AS EBITDA
items.quote: North cluster will give us that number upward of 35 crores average per store net of GST.

items.statement: Cooling products ~15% of blended annual revenue
items.quote: Overall blended to be around 15%.

items.statement: Cannot control rising costs from credit card penetration, NBFC costs, rental, manpower, advertising
items.quote: So these are all costs that we actually can't control because they are directly linked to the mode of payments and all.

items.statement: Revamped small appliances category with brand tie-ups for stock return to avoid dead inventory
items.quote: we had to take a strong step where we had to revamp that whole category again and start off from scratch, create a model where we have tied up with brands where they take the stocks back after every quarter whatever stocks are left with us s o that we don't have the loss of inventory at the end of the year or a dead stock with us

items.statement: Mobile share may rise 1-2% from current 42% as Andhra penetration improves
items.quote: I would look at that going up by one or two more per cent in the coming time, but it will not drastically change from here on going forward.

items.statement: 14 stores in pipeline for Delhi NCR over next 8-12 months; three warehouses currently
items.quote: We already have like 14 stores in pipeline today in Delhi NCR region for the next 12 months, right? So we opened six on the 30th of March in Q4 FY'24 and then we got another 14 stores in the pipeline which we will open in the next 8 to 12 months.

items.statement: Tier-2/3 store throughput: Year 1 Rs 25-30 cr, Year 2 Rs 35 cr, Year 3+ Rs 40 cr stabilized
items.quote: But if I look at a store in a Tier-two or a Tier-three town, I would start looking at 25, 30 crores in year one, then 35 crores in year two , then stabilize it by 40 c rores in year three onwards

items.statement: Kitchen appliances (wet grinders, mixers, rice cookers) seeing steep degrowth due to ready-to-make shift
items.quote: In the kitchen appliance category, we see a steep degrowth is because of the utilization of the product, because now everything is like ready-to-make idli maker so people are now actually picking up ready-to-make rather than cooking or making that dough at home.

items.statement: Expanding built-in category (chimneys, microwaves, ovens) in 7-8 stores; higher ASPs than traditional
items.quote: right now, we're focusing on built-in category as well. Hop chimneys along with microwaves, built-in appliances, and built- in ovens. That is the category that we're expanding because the ASPs are quite high there compared to the traditional microwave, hop and chimneys

items.statement: Top 5 brands contribute ~60% of revenue; work with limited brands in huge volumes for bargaining power
items.quote: About 98% of our revenues come from the retail segment, and the top five brands contributed around 60% to our revenues.

items.statement: Andhra market underpenetrated: EMIL 38-39 stores vs competitors 60+ stores; see huge mobile/AC/large appliance growth opportunity
items.quote: Our store count is less than half in terms of bigger partners like Reliance, also, Sono Vision has 60 plus stores, we are still operating with 38, 39 stores in that region. So we still see that there is a huge opportunity for us to go especially with the underpenetrated mobile phone as a categor y there

items.statement: Future store additions funded through internal accruals and remaining IPO proceeds
items.quote: Given the healthy cash flows from operations in F Y'24, we are optimistic on the future cash flows from operations being effective working capital management and hence almost all future store additions will be well funded through internal accruals and remaining IPO proceeds

items.statement: Plan 50:50 expansion mix between North and South; will expand in AP/Telangana organically and enter Odisha, Punjab, Western UP
items.quote: Right now, it will be more of 50:50 mix up North and down South, because there are a lot of markets that we don't even have a store here. AP, Telangana expansion will go on and then with that what happens is that organically every year, whichever city you've already entered in the past, you would see a new market developing in the same city.

items.statement: North cluster margins to remain similar until stores mature in couple of years; heavy marketing spend currently
items.quote: Margins will all remain the same more or less, because we'll be adding up of new stores as well for this coming year as well. So expansion in Delhi or that region is going to be heavier than other regions.

items.statement: North cluster like-for-like SSG ~25-30% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: So the SSG growth in the North region is like 25%, 30%? Karan Bajaj: Yes

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at 8-10%
items.quote: And therefore you know it will be 8% to 10% topline growth for FY25.

items.statement: FY26 expected to return to 15-20% CAGR trajectory
items.quote: I feel, I mean the conclusion that, it's not a feeling it's a conclusion of our analysis that we will pretty much, get back on the track, of 15% CAGR.

items.statement: Export order annualized value INR 75-80 crores with 8 part numbers across US, Mexico, Portugal
items.quote: But as of now, on an annualized basis, if I look at the RFQ volumes, the value of that order is about INR75 crores to INR80 crores, depending on the volume that you consider.

items.statement: New business wins with lifecycle revenue of INR 900+ crores, including INR 390-400 crores export
items.quote: The orders we have won have a lifecycle revenue of INR 900 plus crores. Of this, we have export business with marquee Tier 1 North American. So not just one BorgWarner, but their peers as well.

items.statement: IPO capex of INR 170 crores, INR 45 crores deployed to date, INR 78 crores spent in FY24
items.quote: Out of the IPO process of capex of INR170 crores, till date we have deployed INR45 crores and capex spent for FY '24 was INR78 crores.

items.statement: Target to maintain EBITDA above 20% and minimum ROIC of 18%
items.quote: The commitment of the company is to sort of maintain EBITDAs above the 20% range and ROIC all our quotations everything is done to achieve minimum ROIC of 18%.

items.statement: Headwinds from 4 major OEMs (Mahindra, Tata EV, MG Motors, Mahindra Defense) to continue in H1 FY25
items.quote: The headwinds that caused this dent in the last two quarters of FY24 we expect that to continue for the first two quarters of FY25.

items.statement: EV transmission revenue grew 160x YoY in Q4 FY24, now 10% of FY24 revenue
items.quote: EV business now contributes around 10% of our business.

items.statement: Shirwal plant commissioned in record time with high-speed dynamometer for EV testing
items.quote: First and foremost, we commissioned our plant at Shirwal near Pune in record time, along with the development of the design and the commissioning of a world -class manufacturing facility and infrastructure in this plant.

items.statement: Export revenue recognition to start Q1 FY25 from US warehouse shipments
items.quote: We have, we are filling up our warehouses in the U.S. and revenue recognition will start in the first quarter of FY25.

items.statement: Strategic alliance with Toyota Group parts distributor for Japan and Southeast Asia opportunities
items.quote: The visit was hosted by the parts distribution company of the Toyota Group, with whom we have a long -term strategic alliance. And working with them, we are looking at opportunities both in India and Southeast Asia with Japanese OEMs.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR 2.60 per equity share (face value INR 5) recommended for FY24
items.quote: The Board of Directors at its meeting has recommended final dividend of INR2.60 per equity share of face value of INR5 each for FY'23-'24.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 225 crores as of FY24, intend to maintain net cash status
items.quote: As you all know, we are a net cash company and we will try to maintain it going ahead. Our current net cash position for FY '24 is INR225 crores.

items.statement: EV transmission quality at zero PPM on NVH, first pass yield 98-100%
items.quote: We have been zero PPM (Parts Per Million) and we have the data to prove that.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues impacted China and Russia business; China market access currently muted
items.quote: The geopolitics hit our China business, Russia business, initially. Of course, the whole China factor is now helping us in the United States, but it's taking a little bit of time.

items.statement: Export business brings decidedly better margins than domestic; aftermarket opportunities in US
items.quote: Now when it comes to actually delivering a proprietary product the margins are of course the best, but even otherwise at the component level compared to the domestic business there is no doubt that overseas business brings decidedly a better margin.

items.statement: Working with Japanese OEMs and Tier 1s through Toyota alliance; pursuing North American front-end presence
items.quote: We continue to talk globally to transmission Tier 1's. So not just in the United States, but also the leading Tier 1's in Europe and I might add in Japan.

items.statement: Capex timing synchronized with product development; EV equipment lead times extended from Japan, Europe
items.quote: We are timing the development of a lot of our new products and the injection okay, this is a bit of a dicey thing because we don't want to prematurely over invest we want to make sure that, that investment is synchronized.

items.statement: COO Dipak Vani outlines 4 operational KPIs: on-time delivery, customer/internal PPM, revenue per employee, cost reduction
items.quote: So the first and foremost KPI what we monitor for our internally as well as for customer is on -time delivery, then the customer PPM and internal PPM, then for productivity we track progress in terms of revenue per employee and for the fourth one what we track on monthly basis is cost reduction.

items.statement: Mahindra E-Jeeto launch pending PLI issues resolution with Government of India
items.quote: We are waiting for some PLI issues, to get sorted out with the government of India and once that happens this program will go into launch.

items.statement: Global pickup truck program with large OEM fully tooled up; markets in Asia and Africa
items.quote: We are looking at a global pickup truck with one of our largest OEMs. It has a carryover product configuration from an existing application. So, the basic chassis is more or less the same.

items.statement: Three-wheeler EV transmission development with incumbents and startups; ATV/UTV export potential
items.quote: We are working with one of them on this the numbers are pretty significant, I mean, they go at some point in the life cycle, they cross the 100,000 mark.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 21%, PAT margin 16%; Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 20%, PAT margin 14%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 21%. Profit after tax for FY '24 was INR40 crores as compared to INR51 crores in FY '23, degrowth of 22% on year-on-year basis with PAT margins at 16%.

items.statement: Suboptimal capacity utilization at plants due to OEM production cuts impacted FY24 EBITDA
items.quote: Fall was due to high overhead expenses on commissioning of Shriwal plant and suboptimal capacity utilization at other plants.

items.statement: ROCE 9.3%, ROIC 11% in FY24; expected to improve with operating leverage
items.quote: Return on capital employed for FY'24 is at 9.3%. Return on invested capital for FY'24 is at 11%. Both the above metrics is expected to improve as operating leverage will start playing out.

items.statement: Transfer case business degrew 36% in Q4 FY24 and 20% in FY24 due to OEM production slowdown
items.quote: The transfer cases business has seen degrowth of 36%, this largely due to slow pickup of our units for major OEMs.

items.statement: Management targets 18-20% top-line growth and 15-20% bottom-line growth for FY25
items.quote: we will want to continue to grow at about 18 % to 20% in terms of top line. And in the same way with our mix of gold versus diamonds stud ratio and the other products, we will also want to ensure that our bottom line also grows approximately between 15 % to 20%.

items.statement: Management aims to improve EBITDA margin towards 8% from current 7.2-7.3%
items.quote: our EBITDA margin is at 7.3% that we have seen, and we will work on increasing it towards 8%, that's what we are saying, that is going to be our endeavor.

items.statement: Management targets 100-130 bps annual stud ratio increase and 20-30 bps gross margin and EBITDA improvement
items.quote: we will continue to work on our stud ratio strategy, increasing our stud ratio by 100 to 130 basis points every year, which will mitigate the price pressure which will come on the gold business and we will look at around 20 to 30 basis point improvement in the gross margin and EBITDA.

items.statement: Average capex per store is Rs 2.5 crore (Rs 6,000-7,000 per sq ft); most stores leased not owned
items.quote: on an average around Rs. 2.5 crore is our CAPEX per store, there are stores w here we have incurred Rs. 1.6 crore also, there are stores which have got Rs. 1.6 crore and Rs. 1.2 crore and Rs. 2.5 crore, there are multiple ranges, but average is around Rs. 6,000 per store, per square feet

items.statement: Plan to add 15-20 stores in FY25 (8-10 COCO, 8-10 franchise); 70-80% in East and North
items.quote: we are looking at about 8 to 10 Company owned, Company operated stores and 8 to 10 franchisees these are the thought process with which we are working for the new financial year. so about adding between 15 to 20 odd stores in the coming year.

items.statement: FY24 revenue grew 28.5% to Rs 5,240 crore; retail grew 25%; PAT grew 14.2% to Rs 181 crore
items.value: Rs 5,240 crore revenue, Rs 181 crore PAT
items.quote: revenue from operations overall has grown by 28.5% Out of that, if we look at the retail business growth, we have grown by about 25% If we see the PAT growth that we have seen, it has grown by 14.2% at a figure of Rs. 181 crore vis-à-vis Rs. 158 crore in the previous financial year and our top line also has been Rs. 5,240 crore approximately compared to Rs. 4,077 crore in the previous financial ye

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 7.2% (Q4 7.7% vs 8.2% prior year); gross margin 15.3%; pressure from competitive intensity and discounting
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA margin, it was 7.7% is the Q4 FY24, which has come down from the previous financial year of 8.2%. But our effort overall in the EBITDA margin level and on the annual basis has been 7.2%.

items.statement: Gold price rose from ~Rs 57,000 to ~Rs 67,000 in FY24; consumers shifting to lighter diamond/platinum jewellery; wedding jewellery demand inelastic
items.quote: the way it has worked out in the previous financial year, which has moved from ~Rs. 57,000 in the beginning of the year to about Rs. 67,000 by the end of the year, while the jump has been more in the month of March, but till January and February it was in the range of Rs. 60,000 to Rs. 62,000.

items.statement: 5.88 lakh transacting customers in FY24; ~2.88 lakh new (45-50%); repeat buyers 55%; loyalty customers 55%+ by value
items.quote: the number of customers that has transacted with us, it's been about 5,88,000 customers, out of which we have seen that approximately the new customer base that has been a part of our journey has been around 2,88,000 and the remaining of the customers that have been there are our old customers that have come back.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle 165-169 days; inventory days stable at ~151 days (2.41x turns) despite 15% gold price rise and new stores
items.quote: Cash conversion cycle that has been in the range bound to 165 to 169. The press release which we have issued highlighted some other important parameters, particularly we must look at the finance cost from the Ind AS angle. So, the finance cost which is visible in the financials, it includes a lease rental impact of Rs. 28 crore. So, effectively as we said the finance cost or blended interest rate

items.statement: Debt/equity improved 1.24x to 1.10x; net debt/equity 0.80x to 0.71x; total borrowing Rs 1,497 crore (61% gold metal loans at 3.2-3.8%, rest CC/WCDL at ~9.5%); blended rate ~6%
items.quote: Our debt equity ratio has slightly improved from 1.24x to 1.10x is based on the free cash flow for the current year and the IPO funds which came in and which has been used for the working capital. The TOL / TNW, which is the important parameter for credit rating that has also improved from 1.7x to 1.44x, the net debt to equity which is a very important parameter to understand what is the net debt,

items.statement: Target gold metal loan share 75% of borrowing (currently 61%) to lower finance cost
items.quote: See we are looking at around 75% is optimum, I don't have the exact breakup of the competitor or the industry peers, last year it was around 55% and has improved to 61% as of March 24, we propose to take it to around 75%.

items.statement: Exports grew from Rs 70 crore to Rs 187-188 crore in FY24 (~4-5% of revenue); export gross margins 6-7% diluting blended margin
items.quote: export last year was Rs. 70 crore to be precise and this year we have done exports around Rs. 187 crore to Rs. 188 crore. So, as you are aware export business gross margins are usually lower, let's say 6% to 7% range. So the gross margin is marginally diluted.

items.statement: Competitive intensity increasing with more discounts/offers from peers; margin pressure expected to continue 4-5 years until consolidation; organized share growing
items.quote: the competitive scenario is increasing, we have our fellow jewelers who are also working towards , trying to acquire new customers. And in that competitive scenario, there are more offers and discounts and aggressive campaigns that are happening and that is what is leading to this whole, downward pressure on the margins.

items.statement: Hallmarking policies driving shift from unorganized to organized; old gold exchange rose from 25% to 32% of business
items.quote: our old gold exchange with our customers has grown substantially, two years back it was about 25% of the overall business,, but today we see 32% of the overall business is happening through the exchange of old gold. Now, that is a kind of a signal that yes, one is the hallmarking policies that are being taken by the government is working in the right direction

items.statement: Same-store sales growth (SSSG) 18% for FY24 (own stores 26%, franchise 22%); North SSSG 19%; Q1 FY25 SSSG 12% (like-to-like)
items.quote: retail growth of 35% overall, which includes own store of let say 26%, franchise 22% North growth is 22%, which includes SSSG of 19% which means that the North business is clearly growing.

items.statement: Average selling price (ASP) Rs 41,000 (up from Rs 36,000); average ticket value (ATV) Rs 63,000 (up from Rs 56-57,000); gold ASP Rs 54,800, diamond ASP Rs 42,000
items.quote: the ASP (average sale price) is around Rs. 41,000 for the full year improving from Rs 36,000 range for last 3 years. Similarly The ATVs (average ticket value) was in Rs 63000 range improving from Rs 56,00 to Rs 57,000 for last 3 years.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 growth driven by strong wedding season (Jan-Feb); post mid-March slowdown; Akshaya Tritiya value growth ~15% but volume flat; rural demand optimistic post monsoon
items.quote: For Q4 the wedding season, we had a large number of weddings up to 7th of March. So, if we look at January and February month, we had a very strong performance and demand from the consumer end, post middle of March, the numbers started moving a little downward.

items.statement: Gold price volatility, global uncertainty, war, heat wave, elections impacting near-term sentiment; competitive intensity to persist 4-5 years
items.quote: It is also impacted by the global uncertainty , the war, the gold price volatility, all of that put together maybe the conservative estimate is 15%. And the positive , optimistic estimate will be about 20%. This is how we are looking at the picture.

items.statement: Launched SENNES sub-brand (lab-grown diamonds, leather) with 3 pilot stores in Kolkata; products displayed in Kolkata, Chandigarh, Delhi
items.quote: last year we also took the initiative of launching a new brand or rather a sub brand called SENNES, which was focusing on lab - grown diamonds and leather accessories ; and we have started our pilot project by opening three Sennes stores in Kolkata

items.statement: Dubai store inaugurated on Akshaya Tritiya; global expansion long-term (5-6 years) after East/North and West/South focus
items.quote: the store in Dubai we did the puja and the auspicious beginning on the Day of Akshaya Tritiya, store in Dubai is under I wouldn't say the initiatives, the plan, the consumer connect, all those things are under process and right now there is nothing substantial to talk about

items.statement: Launched Marygold savings scheme (6-9 month tenure, fixed/flexible options) to help consumers manage gold price volatility
items.quote: we have launched the Marygold scheme, in which a consumer can keep accumulating their money, save it with us over a period of six months or nine months and then they can buy it at the end of the tenure and there is a flexible option and a fixed option.

name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd

items.statement: Management confident of sustaining 29% revenue growth and 35% EBITDA growth for years ahead
items.quote: We feel quite confident in sustaining this growth for the years to come. We have occupancy ramp up yet remaining. We have ARPOB that is growing on even quarter-on-quarter. So, we are quite confident of maintaining the growth margins that we have shown in the last few years in the years ahead to come also.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion CAPEX estimated at Rs 60-65 lakh per bed for 450 beds across Noida Extension and Greater Noida
items.quote: So, the CAPEX that we have taken for the expansion of our existing Brownfields because it is not a Greenfield expansion, it is Brownfield. So, we feel 60 lakhs to 65 lakhs per bed CAPEX is required in terms of our both Noida Extension and Greater Noida Hospital coming up.

items.statement: Acquisition CAPEX estimated at Rs 60-70 lakh per bed for future hospital purchases
items.quote: As far as the CAPEX per bed is concerned, see if you look at it recently, we acquired the hospital in Faridabad, and it is when we expanded and we add medical equipments to it. So, we are paying roughly around Rs. 150 crores for a bed capacity of close to 200 beds, so coming to the CAPEX for bed of 60 lakhs to 70 lakhs roughly.

items.statement: Acquired Asian Fidelis Hospital in Faridabad for Rs 1,160 million; operationalized May 12, 2024; targeting one acquisition per year through FY26
items.quote: This strategic move with the purchase consideration of INR 1,160 million underscores our commitment to growth through inorganic mode and is in line with the commitment to acquiring one hospital each year through Financial '24 to '26.

items.statement: Noida Hospital at 89% occupancy with no space to add beds; Greater Noida at 67% occupancy adding 200 beds; Noida Extension at 44% occupancy targeting full occupancy next year; Jhansi at 34% occupancy in Q4
items.quote: Noida Hospital stands out with an impressive occupancy rate of 89%. Furthermore, our Greater Noida facility has seen an increase in occupancy to 67% now. We anticipate this facility to achieve optimum utilization in this fiscal. Our Noida Extension has been growing rapidly with current utilization reaching 44% versus 31% in the previous year and this facility will be reaching occupancy level by th

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 113 bps to 26.8% in FY24; management expects margins sustainable at current levels for next 3-4 years despite new hospital ramp-up
items.quote: EBITDA margins, we are quite good in terms of EBITDA margins are concerned and we expect the margins to be sustainable because even though new hospitals are coming up, but there is still lot of occupancy growth that is going to happen in our existing hospitals of Greater Noida and Noida Extension. So, overall, EBITDA margins are quite sustainable even in the next 3-4 years that we have currently.

items.statement: Negotiated 7-8% rate increase with insurers for Noida Hospital; annual cash rate revisions of 6-8%; insurance rates negotiated every 1-2 years with GIPSA
items.quote: Totality, I think it is difficult to say because it is 135 odd procedures are being discussed and got the rate. But I think anything between, it will have impact of 7%-8% kind of impact will come and because that there is an annual revision of the rates as well, every hospital does it.

items.statement: Oncology now ~10% of Noida Extension revenue; robotic surgeries (115 completed), organ transplants driving case mix shift to super specialties; super specialty share rising, internal medicine share falling
items.quote: With oncology now contributing nearly 10% to our revenue stream in Noida Extension Hospital, I anticipate significant growth in the current Fiscal Year, the establishment of cancer radiation line. With addition to this, robotic surgeries, and expansion of organ transplant procedures, I am confident of a case mix shift towards more specialty treatments.

items.statement: International patient volume growing; 150 kidney transplants in last 1.5 years with 90% international patients; targeting double-digit revenue contribution from international patients
items.quote: International patient volume has been increasing given the fact that we have done around 150 kidney transplants and in last year and a half and 90% of those kidney transplants are international patients. We are now also targeting international liver transplant and international bone marrow transplant.

items.statement: Receivables increased to Rs 227 crore due to higher government scheme share (~40% of revenue) and election-related payment delays; management expects significant reduction in coming quarters
items.quote: As we proceed further with the new financial year coming up with quarter 1, quarter 2, these debtors have significantly come down as always does with these three government schemes plus with the additional of cash and insurance revenue increasing. We are quite confident in the coming quarters, the revenue that is being generated in terms of the cash flow would be at an optimized and at a good leve

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs 1,556 million; took Rs 800 million debt to assume Asian Fidelis liabilities; expect to remain net debt free despite acquisition funding
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to be strong with a net cap position of Rs. 1,556 million. We remain dedicated to deploy these funds strategically to drive further growth and value creation.

items.statement: Income Tax department froze Rs 70 crore in October 2023; money remains in company accounts but cannot be used; expect resolution within FY25
items.quote: Yes. So, we had already informed the Stock Exchange in October 2023, we had the people coming from income tax. So, they found that because we were through with the IPO money and a lot of cash we had been having which was basically for the specified purposes. So, the zeal of things, they had kept this money. Now this money is with us. They have not taken it away. It is still with us.

items.statement: ARPOB for FY24 at Rs 28,571, up 8% YoY; Noida Extension highest at Rs 33,994; Q4 consolidated ARPOB Rs 29,266 up 6% YoY; targeting Rs 40,000 at Noida Extension
items.quote: Our average revenue per operating bed, ARPOB for the quarter, was 29, 266, up by 6% year-over-year. The improvement was driven by a consistent shift towards higher complexity procedures observed across various specialties with gastroenterology, pulmonology, orthopedics and oncology emerging as key drivers of growth.

items.statement: Payer mix: government schemes ~40% (ESI, ECHS, CGHS), cash ~30-33%, private insurance ~30-33%; government rates 25-30% below cash rates but oncology rates closer to cash
items.quote: So, the payer mix, as we mentioned that the government category is very close to 40% now in terms of the total topline and the remaining is then equally divided between cash and TPA segment. So, somewhere around let us say 30%-33% for both cash segment as well as the private insurance segment.

items.statement: Supreme Court PIL on rate standardization; industry bodies made representations; Court observed uniform rates across super specialties not practically possible; management not worried
items.quote: So, this is already, the body of the private health segment, AHPI and Net Health has already made the representations and I think recently if you have heard that the Supreme Court had the observation about the PIL filed by Ophthalmic Society of India, then said that it is not practically possible to have same rate for across the super specialties and across this thing.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guided at Rs. 600-650 crore with 20% volume growth
items.quote: So we may see around Rs. 600-650 crore of sales.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of Rs. 900-1,000 crore with EBITDA around 10%
items.quote: According to the figures from the last 3 years, we expect to reach Rs. 900 to Rs. 1,000 crores in revenue, with an EBITDA of around 10% in the next 3 years.

items.statement: FY25 capex of Rs. 45-50 crore funded from internal accruals
items.quote: Around Rs. 45 crore capex that I have been saying. We will incur Rs. 45 to 50 crore capex this year as well.

items.statement: Wada Maharashtra Phase 1 capex Rs. 40-45 crore to complete by Q4 FY25
items.quote: Phase 1 capex, including the purchase of land and civil work, is estimated to be around Rs. 40-45 crores and is expected to be completed by quarter 4, 2025.

items.statement: Metal Drum capacity increased to 50,000 units/month, targeting 70,000 by Sep 2024 and 90,000 with further automation
items.quote: We have increased our Metal Drum capacity from 30,000 to 50,000 units per month using automation at our Unit 6, Gujrat plant. And as highlighted in our earlier communications, we have already purchased land adjacent to our existing Unit 6. In the near term, we are targeting to reach 70,000 units per month capacity by September 2024, with potential to reach 90,000 units by furthermore automation.

items.statement: IBC Line 1 at 50% utilization, Line 2 to be ordered at 70-75% utilization
items.quote: At Unit 7, we have already commissioned Line 1 for IBC in July '23, which is currently operating at 50% capacity. We plan to order Line 2 IBC very soon, as soon as we cross 70-75% of the capacity.

items.statement: Wada Maharashtra unit civil work completion by Sep 2024, operations expected Dec 2024
items.quote: Construction is ongoing and they are expecting to complete by September and I have considered that it will be completed by December and we expect that during the year we may get some incremental revenue from there.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 9.1%, impacted by raw material price lag; expect 10-11% in FY25
items.quote: We are expecting it to be between 10% to 11%.

items.statement: 20% volume growth expected in FY25 across all three verticals
items.quote: We believe that we will achieve 20% volume growth this year as well.

items.statement: Chemical sector recovery driving HDPE and IBC demand growth
items.quote: This year we see an opportunity in the chemical sector also, and the HDPE sector also. This year the entire industry is hoping to be good, because chemical sector is also recovering at the same time the HDPE demand is coming from them so as the demand will grow the prices will start increasing.

items.statement: Polymer prices fell from Rs. 105 to Rs. 95 per kg in FY24, now at 10-year low and bottomed out
items.quote: From Rs. 105 it has come to Rs. 95.

items.statement: Raw material price changes reflected in selling price with monthly announcements; 45-day inventory causes lag
items.quote: As per the pricing norm in the industry, typically raw material price changes are reflected in the selling price as monthly prices are announced. However, we maintain an inventory of 45 days and we see a lag in co st reduction when raw material prices are falling

items.statement: FY24 volume mix: IBC 33%, Metal Drum 10%, HDPE Drum 47%; FY25 expected: IBC 36-37%, Metal Drum 11%, HDPE ~43%
items.quote: About 33% volume is from IBC right now and 10% is in Metal Drum. And 47% is coming from my HDPE Drum. So, there will be growth across all three. 10% will be 11% going ahead for MS Drum. IBC will be 36-37% and balance would be Polymer Drum this year in 25.

items.statement: Net cash balance sheet maintained; capex funded from internal accruals to keep net debt zero
items.quote: Balance sheet strength remains healthy as we have a net cash balance sheet. We expect to continue maintaining a healthy balance sheet and capex is expected to be funded from internal accruals and cash balance, to maintain net debt zero balance.

items.statement: IBC gross profit Rs. 1,000-1,200 per drum at 50% utilization
items.quote: We are getting Rs.1,000 – 1,200, sir.

items.statement: Raw material prices fell for 12 straight months first time in 10-12 years; inventory loss ~Rs. 5 crore for FY24
items.quote: I assume that my inventory loss on my stock would have been around Rs. 5 crores for the whole year.

items.statement: Other income increased due to forex gain ~Rs. 3 crore and trading income from raw material sales
items.quote: We book forex and have an extra income of approximately Rs. 3 crore. Additionally, the other income you see is the trading income, from the sale of raw materials.

items.statement: Target SSSG of 2-3% positive for FY25 with EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: So going ahead, our target is to retrieve the SSSGs at least to a positive of 2% to 3% along with the implementation plan that we already initiated.

items.statement: Plan to add 90,000 sq ft retail area in FY25, majority in Tamil Nadu under Varamahalakshmi format
items.quote: As per the plan, we aim to open additional store capacity of close to 90,000 square feet in this financial year. Majority of it would be coming in the Tamil Nadu area and with our brand Varamahalakshmi Silks.

items.statement: Additional store area expected to generate INR300-350 crores incremental turnover in FY25
items.quote: So additional store area , in the normal course itself, should give at least another INR300 crores to INR350 crores of turnover.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 gross margin at 40.97% vs 39.77% last year; EBITDA margin ~17% in Q4
items.quote: Our gross margin stood at 40.97 compared to last year of 39.77. Our PAT for the quarter stood at 28.73 compared to last year's of 20.24, which has grown by about 41.95 percentage.

items.statement: Store-level margins: Varamahalakshmi 33-34%, Mandir similar, KLM 24-25%, Kalamandir at company average
items.quote: Store level margins for Varamahalakshmi should be in the range of about 33% to 34%. While KLM, it would be in the range of about 24% to 25%.

items.statement: Revenue per store FY24: Varamahalakshmi ~INR45-46k/sqft, Mandir ~INR44k/sqft, KLM INR14k/sqft
items.quote: is co ntinuing to be approximately 45,000 to 46,000 at a company level. Tamil Nadu would be slightly higher and the is Mandir continues to be almost on the same range about 44,000 per square feet. KML has shown a slight improvement, 20,000 per square feet there. And KLM currently is at INR14,000 rupees per

items.statement: Saree industry growing at 8% CAGR; Tamil Nadu equals Andhra+Telangana combined in consumption
items.quote: If you take that as a metric, a few of the highlights that I would like to highlight at this point of time is in the overall saree consumption, the SSSG, I mean, the CAGR growth is around 8% CAGR growth that saree as an industry sees.

items.statement: Sarees 69.5% of revenue (pure silk >25%, mixed silk 35-40%, Banarasi, fancy); non-saree 30% (lehenga, kurta, men's/kids occasion wear)
items.quote: So though SSKL has about 69.5% sarees and another 30% coming from other categories, if you just focus on sarees alone it's growing at an 8% CAGR.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow in FY24 due to INR170 cr creditor reduction to gain cash discounts; benefits expected in 2-3 years
items.quote: you would have seen that in the cash flow statement, the reduction in creditors has been to the extent of about INR170 crores, of which a part of it was used from GCP and the entire year's generations were deployed for this.

items.statement: Inventory write-offs ~1% annually per bank surveillance audits; will report as separate line item from FY25
items.quote: Broadly, we have realized that this amount is in the range of about plus or minus 1% on an annual basis. We are planning that from this year onwards, we would declare it as a separate line item.

items.statement: Active customer base 6.5 million; 53-54% repeat purchase rate in trailing 12 months
items.quote: We have an active customer base as of today around 6.5 million and are growing strong as we expand. Our contribution coming from the loyal customer base also continued this season. We still continue to hold our loyal customer base of about 53% of our repeat purchases.

items.statement: FY25 store additions: ~25,000 sq ft by June, ~50,000 sq ft by H1 end, balance in H2; all Varamahalakshmi format
items.quote: We would be putting up another 25,000 sft in June in VML format itself. And by half year end, we should be completing the expansion of approximately plus or minus 50,000 square feet and the balance in the second half.

items.statement: 95%+ full-price sales company-wide; Varamahalakshmi 100% full-price, no discounting
items.quote: More than 95% of our entire sale is full price sale. We do not believe in end of season sale or discounting in a timely manner or a seasonality basis.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 SSG +3%; full year FY24 SSG -6%; wedding dates marginally lower in Q4 but March saw recovery
items.quote: SSGs in the last quarter were recorded at 3%. So, we hope to maintain this year the recovery process and the target is to maintain at least the 3% levels t hat we have already seen

items.statement: Total retail area 647,300 sq ft end FY24 vs ~603,000 sq ft end FY23; 60 stores (VML 26, KLM 19, Kalamandir 11, Mandir 4)
items.quote: For the full year, we have added close to 43,900 square feet that puts us at a total at 6,47,300 square feet worth of retail area presence as of now.

items.statement: No immediate Kalamandir store openings in FY25; focus on Tamil Nadu Varamahalakshmi expansion; Kalamandir may follow cluster maturation
items.quote: at this point of time, we do not have any solidified plans for Kalamandir to execute immediately. Probably after first two quarters of Varamalakshmi implementat ion, if there is a possibility, we will try and see if we can expand into Kalamandir for next

items.statement: Q4 FY24 sales grew 10% QoQ after accident impact in Q3
items.quote: we were able to grow our business in Q4 compared to Q3 FY '24 by 10%.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin improved 1.8% to 32.2% driven by lower raw material prices
items.quote: EBITDA for the full year is 32.2% an improvement of 1.8% compared to FY23. This is predominantly driven by reduction in raw material price

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA dropped ~3.9% due to WIP and finished goods change of INR27 crores
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA Q4 it dropped approximately by 3.9%. This is primarily because of change in WIP and finished goods.

items.statement: Spent ~INR200 crores in FY24; guiding INR200 crores per annum for next two years
items.quote: We have spent close to INR200 crores in this financial year, the asset which is capitalized plus the capital work in progress, and we should be spending at least INR200 crores per annum for the next two years at least on the capex plan for our units, for our existing units.

items.statement: Unit 2 Ambernath block ready for validation in Q1 FY25; Unit 3 Mahad delayed one quarter to Q1 FY26 for validation batches
items.quote: As indicated in our previous call, this block will be ready for validation in the quarter 1 of FY '25. With regard to Unit 3 Mahad, we foresee a delay of a quarter. The plant will now be ready for validation batches in quarter 1 of FY '26.

items.statement: Unit 4 Greenfield site at Borivali expected on stream in H2 FY27
items.quote: We expect this unit to be on stream in the second half of FY27.

items.statement: Order book confirmed for next 18 months in pharma intermediates segment
items.quote: Confirming our order book for the next 18 months.

items.statement: Contrast media volumes impacted by customer destocking and longer maintenance; variability should ease after Q2
items.quote: degrowth in contrast media is certain actions by the customers in terms of destocking and their plan to take a longer maintenance which is actually disturbing the overall shipment. So today you see a variability on quarter-to-quarter dispatch which in our opinion should get eased out after Q2

items.statement: Key raw material prices declined marginally in FY24; trend expected to sustain supporting gross margins
items.quote: Almost all of our key raw materials, we could see a marginal decline in the prices, and we believe this particular trend should sustain and which should actually help us in sustaining our gross margin.

items.statement: Receivables reduced due to customer mix shift from contrast media to pharma intermediates with different credit terms
items.quote: There is a reduction in receivable. This is due to the customer mix. We talked about contrast media sale declining due to customer offtake and pharmaceutical intermediate sale is going up because of this. There is a different credit term between contrast media customers versus pharmaceutical intermediate customers and because of this customer mix credit term, the working capital has actually come

items.statement: Pharma intermediates (CRAM) grew 156% YoY to 14% of business; started commercial production for innovator customer in FY24
items.quote: The second vertical, pharma intermediates, the CRAM segment, about 14% of our business which grew about 156% year-on-year. We started commercial production of pharmaceutical intermediate for our mnovator customer in FY '24.

items.statement: ROCE at 26%, EBITDA at 32%, fixed asset turnover north of 5x
items.quote: We believe to have strong abilities in capital management with the key ratios of ROCE at 26%, EBITDA at 32% and fixed asset turnover north of 5x.

items.statement: Fixed asset turnover expected upwards of 3x on new capex vs current 4x on depreciated block
items.quote: I would actually put it in the range of upwards of three.

items.statement: Business concentrated with three major contrast media players plus new innovator in PI segment; no change in customer mix otherwise
items.quote: Our business is concentrated with three major players in contrast media. And in addition to that list is the new imnovator in the PI segment. Apart from that, technically, there is no change in the customer mix.

items.statement: Contrast media industry consolidated with four key players holding >75% global share for 10+ years; Indian and Chinese players in remaining 20%
items.quote: Yes, so I think the industry is fairly consolidated. And in four key players have about more than 75% of global market share. And for the past 10 years or more.

items.statement: Cardiovascular intermediate received US label expansion approval in May 2024; European approval expected
items.quote: The label updation and the label expansion were already approved in the US this year, this calendar year. I think it happened in the month of May. After that we expect something similar label expansion in the European market as well.

items.statement: Contrast media sales on DAP terms; revenue recognized only when material reaches customer site causing quarterly cut-off effects
items.quote: See, in our case, the supplies to the key customer in contrast media is on a DAP term, which is Delivery at Place. Technically, unless the material reaches the site, we cannot actually recognize that sale.

items.statement: Mahad incident loss of INR97 million classified as extraordinary expense; insurance claim reversal expected
items.quote: We had actually classified INR 97 million on account of the Mahad incident as extraordinary expense. This is a conservative approach wherein we have actually taken the entire loss of plant and machinery is taken as an extraordinary item. As and when we receive the claim from the insurance company this would be reversed and will be shown as a credit to the P&L.

items.statement: Employee cost to increase significantly in FY25 with senior and execution level hiring plus R&D expansion
items.quote: If you see our numbers, FY'25, the employee cost is significantly higher. But then our sales are also increasing. Even in FY'25, we would be adding some people, both at the senior management level and at the execution level. We will be also increasing our R&D further.

items.statement: Solar plant live in Q3 FY24; 60-70% power requirement to be met from renewable energy
items.quote: With our solar plant going on stream in the previous financial year almost 60% to 70% of our power requirement should be met from renewable energy sources.

items.statement: New sweetener product at pilot stage; unlikely to be major revenue contributor in FY25, potential launch in FY26
items.quote: The other sweetener that we spoke about is currently at the pilot stage. We are trying to optimize a few things, but you will hear from us if there's any positive update. But the results so far are fairly encouraging.

items.statement: Capex outlay increased to ~INR600 crores over three years from ~INR500 crores due to larger Unit 4 plan for risk mitigation and customer needs
items.quote: We are keeping a slightly larger outlay for unit four. That is we will be replicating quite a few capacities. One as a risk mitigation and also like taking care of the higher needs of the customer. So, the plan for unit four could be slightly larger than what we envisaged last year.

items.statement: Full capacity inflection point expected in FY26-27 as capacities kick in phases
items.quote: Yes, I think the capacities would be kicking in different phases in this financial year as well in the next year, but full extent would be seen in '26, '27.

items.statement: Contrast media supply normalization to largest customer estimated by Q2 FY25
items.quote: In our estimate, it will be Q2.

items.statement: APD prices saw marginal reduction during year; backward integration underway for strategic independence and cost control
items.quote: There is actually a reduction in the APD prices, marginal reduction during the year and Shivan can take on the new contract. So, I think with this backward integration play, I think we would be able to further improve the profitability of this major product.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 15%-17% with potential to reach 20% if glassware ramps up well
items.quote: Looking forward to FY25, we anticipate a growth of around 15%-17%, fueled by all segments and the new plant.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance of 24%-26%
items.quote: We expect EBITDA margins to remain steady at 24%-26%, as our focus remains on surpassing industry growth and enhancing our position in the consumer market.

items.statement: Capex for vacuum bottle manufacturing estimated at INR30-35 crores
items.quote: It's a little labour-oriented too. Because if we take five to 10 lines also, it is, the capex is around INR30 crores. INR30 crores to INR35 crores.

items.statement: Annual capex budget of INR60-70 crores for FY25
items.quote: Yes, our result is definitely. That's the maximum what we are thinking.

items.statement: Glassware furnace will take 1.5 years to reach full capacity of INR250 crores sales
items.quote: It will take one and a half years for us to achieve the capacity of the furnace.

items.statement: Opalware capacity utilization increased to 80-82% in FY24 from 60-65% in FY23
items.quote: This year it will utilize around 80% to 82%.

items.statement: Glassware and Opalware division internal sales target of INR460-475 crores for FY25
items.quote: I think our internal target was around 460 to 475.

items.statement: Writing instruments EBITDA margin improved to 29.3% in FY24 from 25.8% in FY23
items.quote: The EBITDA margins stationary is at around 29.3%, which earlier was 25.8%.

items.statement: Consumer ware gross margin 55.9% in Q4 FY24 vs 58.7% in Q3 FY24; molded furniture gross margin 37.7% in Q4 vs 42.8% in Q3
items.quote: Consumer ware was 58.7% and molded furniture was 42.8%. So, molded furniture has gone a little down the reason being because of the little raw material which has gone up.

items.statement: Raw material prices still 3-4% below peak levels; gas prices for Opalware dropped from INR120 to INR55
items.quote: Even as I said the gas prices in Opalware has come down from INR120 in starting of last year '24 to around INR55 now.

items.statement: Demand picked up in March and early April but muted due to elections; rural demand improving, urban demand not at peak
items.quote: Demand has picked up very well in March and April early, but I think so because of the ongoing elections. A little muted for some time.

items.statement: Premiumization strategy in consumer ware with new back-to-school and lunch carrier ranges carrying 7-8% higher margins
items.quote: We have launched special categories for back-to-school children and water bottles, lunch carriers, where the margins are approximately on the normal model than what we have, margin is around 7% to 8% more.

items.statement: General trade contribution declined from 81% to 77%; export contribution increased from 8% to 10% of total sales
items.quote: If you see a channel shift also, from last year 81% which was general trade has come down to 77%.

items.statement: Receivables increased due to 10-15 days extra credit to general trade and INR18-20 crores government tenders with 5-6 month payment terms
items.quote: The general trade last whole year was not very, very good. So, we had given a little 10 to 15 days extra credit line to most of the customers to push in more to the retail.

items.statement: Expect receivables to normalize by September 2024
items.quote: I think so by September this year, we should be in line with what we were in FY22 to 23.

items.statement: QIP planned for next month; proceeds for debt repayment, glassware capex, and acquisition opportunities
items.quote: Yes, we are working almost next month.

items.statement: Wim Plast merger on the cards and expected very soon
items.quote: Yes, it is on the cards and it will be very soon. Very, very soon.

items.statement: Evaluating acquisition opportunities in consumer segment; ticket size medium to small
items.quote: We are thinking there are some opportunities where we can acquire a couple of companies. That's why we think it's not very big, like it would be in a medium note or small note of purchase.

items.statement: BIS certification for vacuum bottles extended to June 4; local manufacturing BIS deadline September; Cello already certified for insulated bottles
items.quote: So, BIS is now extended till 4th June and I think so it will get further extended on the import. Even on local, you have to take the BIS by September.

items.statement: Expect consolidation in writing instruments market; smaller players may struggle to survive over next 2-3 years
items.quote: And consolidation will definitely happen in the Indian market. The smaller players and all will be a little difficult for them to survive over the next two, three years.

items.statement: Writing instruments export contribution 40-42% of segment revenue in FY24 vs ~45% in FY23
items.quote: Export would be 40% to 42%.

items.statement: Writing instruments domestic market growth expected at 12-15% for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Writing instruments will grow at for next two, three years around 12% to 15%.

items.statement: Vacuum flask imports constitute 80% of total imports and ~12% of consolidated sales; plan to manufacture 20-30% of SKUs locally over 2-3 years
items.quote: It should be around 12% on the consolidated level.

items.statement: Potential interim disruption from BIS implementation on vacuum bottles; long-term advantage expected
items.quote: Disruption will happen, definitely. There is an opportunity also in this and for some time even our company could get affected.

items.statement: Writing instruments distributor count increased by ~350 in FY24; retail outlets expanded from 55,000 to 65,000
items.quote: So on a yearly basis, if you see, I think instrument, the number of distributors have gone up by around 350.

items.statement: EV charger market expected to grow 40%-60% CAGR from INR1,400 crores in FY24 to INR9,000 crores in FY28
items.quote: Based on these developments and various industry reports including CRISIL, we expect the four-wheeler market to grow between 40%-50% CAGR till 2028 which also means that all underlying charging hardware market which is the area we operate in whether it's for fleet charging, bus charging or residential charging or public charging will also grow between 40%-60% CAGR in terms of absolute numbers that

items.statement: Open orders at start of FY25 stood at INR360 crores vs INR290 crores at start of FY24
items.quote: We started with about INR360 crores of open orders with us, confirmed open orders with us. This is much higher than the previous financial year, where on 1st of April '23, we had INR290 crores of orders.

items.statement: Total orders booked in FY24 were INR1,106 crores vs INR952 crores in FY23
items.quote: We overall had INR1,106 crores of orders booked in the financial year '24 as compared to INR952 crores in financial year '23.

items.statement: Gross margin improved by 2% in FY24 due to cost optimisation
items.quote: In terms of the overall performance for the year, the gross margin has increased by 2%, which is a healthy sign because of optimising on cost that we are trying to hold on.

items.statement: DSO improved from 166 days to 81 days in FY24
items.quote: The account receivable on working capital has also shown improvement where we have improved from 166 days down now to 81 days in DSO.

items.statement: Hyderabad integrated manufacturing facility capex of INR170 crores funded from IPO proceeds
items.quote: The overall investment being made in this facility is about INR170 crores which approximately INR170 crores which is one of the main object losses for which the IPO funds were raised.

items.statement: Hyderabad facility civil work completion by end of CY2024, trial production by April 2025
items.quote: The construction is in full swing and we expect to complete civil work by end of this calendar year, install plant and machinery in first quarter of next calendar year, which is 2025 and start trial production by April of 2025.

items.statement: Critical power demand driven by 5G deployments, lead-acid to lithium conversion, BSNL 4G upgrade, border village connectivity, and panchayat broadband projects
items.quote: continuing solarization of telecom sites where feasible, conversion of retiring battery assets from lead acid to lithium ion because of better cost of ownership and large projects funded by Government of India namely which is upgrading the network to 4G at BSNL, putting communication network in uncovered border villages, connecting more than 1 lakh panchayats by high speed broadband.

items.statement: EV charger revenue grew 11% YoY with presence across home, fleet, CPO, and bus charging segments
items.quote: Our other business unit EV charger grew at 11% from INR219 crores to INR243 crores and supported deployments across all vertical markets including home chargers, network rollout by leading charge point operators, captive fleet charging and heavy duty vehicle charging for buses and trucks.

items.statement: Export efforts ongoing in Southeast Asia and Europe with pilots and certifications underway; products to be exported from India
items.quote: Efforts to diversify geographical revenue are ongoing in Southeast Asia and Europe particularly.

items.statement: Export from India to Europe and Southeast Asia; no overseas manufacturing planned
items.quote: No, we will be exporting from India.
