items.statement: Data centre lithium battery market estimated at INR3,000-4,000 crores but addressable market for lithium-ion still early
items.quote: Theoretically, the batteries in data centre is a fairly large market. To my best of knowledge from industry reports is in INR3,000 crores to INR4,000 crores, but that is not probably the addressable market for lithium-ion battery players.

items.statement: Government of India expected to release new EV policy framework with enhanced focus on charging infrastructure
items.quote: It is expected that Government of India will be releasing new EV policy framework with enhanced focus on charging.

items.statement: Company shifted to new tax regime at 25% effective rate from FY24
items.quote: So we have already shifted to the new tax regime this year and also the percentage of tax mix effectively will come about 25% which is the new tax regime going forward.

items.statement: OEM partnerships are non-exclusive; company is single source for some OEMs with short to long-term agreements
items.quote: The partnerships are not exclusive in nature. OEMs, as you are aware, they have a strategic sourcing policy, not just for EV chargers. This is a general answer for a variety of components they source. And we do enjoy being single source at some of these OEMs, but the partnership is not exclusive.

items.statement: Competition acknowledged in fast-growing EV charging market; strategy focuses on own R&D, IP, integrated manufacturing, and new product launches like Spin Air and Gen 1.5 Harmony 400kW DC charger
items.quote: Like any fast-growing big industry, there is always competition. We acknowledge competition but we are really focused on how we can provide the best value to the customer and what we have to do internally for that and that is based on what we heard from the customers based on where we thought improvements have to take place.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR400 crores received; INR296 crores remaining in FD to be spent per object clause
items.quote: The IPO receipts that we had of INR400 crores is as per schedule, which has already been reported. And we have about INR296 crores still in FD, which is still to be spent as per the object clause.

items.statement: Critical power business benefited from lead-acid to lithium-ion battery conversion by tower companies and telcos
items.quote: Our critical power business registered 59% growth year-on-year from INR489 crores to INR776 crores and benefited from ongoing 5G deployments by Telcos, replacement of battery assets in field from lead acid to lithium ion by leading tower companies, additional exports and securing large projects for upgrading telecom networks, particularly in underserved regions.

items.statement: Company has own R&D center, IP, and Pan-India service network as key strengths
items.quote: We have our own R&D center, own IP which allows us to control the design, the cost, the manufacturability of the product and lastly, Pan-India Service Network.

items.statement: Telecom capex moderation risk offset by solarization, battery conversion, exports, and government projects
items.quote: However, our business is determined by not -- just this one factor, there are other things such as solarization. People are, at these lean times, people look at efficiency. So solarization of telecom sites is a factor which is playing on as articulated in our presentation. Conversion of lead acid to lithium ion, which was spoken about two, three times today, that's a factor which is growing our bu

items.statement: Targets 25-30% annual revenue growth for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Yes, as I said we are going to continue our growth by 25 % to 30% year after year.

items.statement: Expects to maintain current EBITDA margin zone with endeavor to improve
items.quote: Nikhil, we will continue to maintain the same zone. The endeavor is to better it definitely and next year w e are making all our strategies , our plan to increase our service

items.statement: Sees multi-year growth driven by Make in India, infrastructure, healthcare, education, waste management
items.quote: So multiple services, Narendra that we are going to lead and there are multiple avenues where we are going to acquire business. So as per the F&S study also while we went and filed our R HP we had the largest service book ing offering.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 6.4%, up 149 bps YoY due to contract mix change
items.quote: Our EBITDA excluding the other income for the quarter stands at Rs. 18.8 Cr while EBITDA margin is 6.4% higher by 149 bps. A change in the mix of contract s undertaken this quarter helped to improve the mar gin.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 6.7%, down 35 bps YoY due to higher raw material costs on two projects
items.quote: Our EBITDA excluding other income for the year stands at Rs. 68.7 Cr, while EBITDA margin is 6.7%, a marginal decline of 35 bps. Higher raw material expenses incurred for two project s had a bearing on the margin.

items.statement: Achieved 100% contract renewal rate in FY24 across government and corporate clients
items.quote: Even this year, we have achieved 100% renewal. We have in the corporate side almost 17% of our customers in who give us 80% of our revenue, they are all with us since last 15 years, 18 years like HDFC Bank, Phoenix Mills, Mumbai Airport, Hinduja Hospital, DMart and they have renewed even this year.

items.statement: Government contract renewal rate 65-70% due to incumbency advantage
items.quote: Almost 65% to 70% because we have already been there. We already worked there. We already know the entire set of activities. We have studied the entire thing. So the chance is that we will bid it again in a rebate is very superior.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of Rs 175 crore fresh issue allocated to debt repayment, working capital, capex for new machinery, general corporate purposes
items.quote: Out of 175 also, we had the objects which were very clear, some small repayment of borrowings, funding towards working capital requirement , CAPEX and towards new machinery and general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Expanding training infrastructure nationally via ITI partnerships; signed agreement with ITI at Tukkuguda, replicating model across geographies
items.quote: We are going to replicate this model wherein we get students to train also , we make them employable, we give them choice to work with us or anywhere else. And at the same time, with the colleges, schools and all those things which have grounds and classrooms, we also have their tie up wherein we train their students and we get their facilities to use as a training facility so that solves this tra

items.statement: Investing in technology and robotics to curtail costs and improve operational efficiency
items.quote: We are making strategic initiative s to improve operational efficiency such as investments in technology, robotics to curtail cost.

items.statement: Revenue split 70% government, 30% corporate; corporate clients include HDFC Bank, Phoenix Mills, Mumbai Airport, Hinduja Hospital, DMart with 15-18 year relationships
items.quote: Our revenue split is also very good with 70 and 30 , 70 with government and 30 with corporate. Even this year, we have achieved 100% renewal. We have in the corporate side almost 17% of our customers in who give us 80% of our revenue, they are all with us since last 15 years, 18 years like HDFC Bank, Phoenix Mills, Mumbai Airport, Hinduja Hospital, DMart

items.statement: Organized compliance-focused model creates moat; unorganized players not a threat as clients prioritize compliance and governance
items.quote: But even in corporate if you see our business acquisition is with our prospects or clients for whom paramount importance is compliance, whether it is all sort of compliance , they would like to deal with companies which are fully compliant and also if you are considering the overall governance in our country which has become very stringent, the corporate and the kind of sector that we are doing bu

items.statement: Receivable days 70-75 for both government and corporate; expects improvement over time with stringent credit control
items.quote: Again, receivable days , generally also if you have both government and corporate they are about 70 to 75 days.

items.statement: IPO raised Rs 300 crore (Rs 125 crore OFS, Rs 175 crore fresh issue) subscribed 13x; listed on BSE and NSE
items.quote: Krystal, through this listing, we raised Rs. 300 crores, about 125 was OFS and 175 was our fresh issue.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of Rs 1.50 per share (15% of face value Rs 10) for FY24
items.quote: The board has recommended dividend of Rs. 1.50 paisa per equity share that is 15% of the face value of Rs. 10 each for the financial year 24, subject to shareholder's ap proval.

items.statement: Attrition reduced from ~30% at IPO to 17% currently vs industry ~60%; two army veterans head training and recruitment
items.quote: Our attrition percentage is the best in the industry, the industry percentage is about 60. When we went to market, we were about 30.36 and as of last week it is 17%.

items.quote: And it is supposed to grow by more than 12% to 13% from FY23 to FY28. So security services, the market is also huge and it is a growing market.

items.statement: Key execution risk is timely recruitment, training and deployment of people; mitigated via training academy expansion and army veteran leadership
items.quote: The only risk to which would prevent getting into and taking all these opportunities, your timely recruitment of people and timely training of people and deployment because all our services are offered through people, man , machine and material.

items.statement: Government tenders require bank guarantees of 2-5% of tender value; stringent pre-qualification criteria (CRISIL rating, turnover, experience) create entry barriers
items.quote: It depends between the tender to tender , anywhere between 2% and 5% of the tender value.

items.statement: Staffing revenue grew organically from MP Electricity Board adding more units under existing contract
items.quote: We had acquired a good staffing business of our MP Electricity Board and over the period of time they added more units which they wanted staffing and payroll. So under that contract only our business grew organically and that quantum is the reflection in the kind of numbers of our staffing payroll increase.

items.statement: Geographic diversification underway: expanding government business in Delhi, MP, Gujarat, North India to reduce Maharashtra/Tamil Nadu concentration
items.quote: Now, we are also very actively moving in the northern state. So Delhi, we will see good progress coming in on the northern side in the Delhi government. Also MP, we will make progress. In Gujarat government, in Gujarat, we are very hopeful that we will expand our government businesses in Gujarat.

items.statement: Higher raw material expenses on two projects pressured FY24 EBITDA margin by 35 bps
items.quote: Higher raw material expenses incurred for two project s had a bearing on the margin.

items.statement: Tax rate fluctuates due to Section 80JJAA benefits; benefit expected to continue
items.quote: The tax rate what you are referring is due to our 80 JJAA benefits. So that is the reason why you see our tax components are fluctuating year-on-year.

items.statement: Management expects MRR potential of INR 14-16 crore from current CAPEX over next couple of months
items.quote: we believe that like the MRR potential with the current CAPEX that we have already done would be of the order of anywhere between like 14 to 16 crores from the current MRR number like we should be able to achieve over like next couple of months.

items.statement: Management targets INR 800 crore CAPEX over next 12 months in ideal scenario
items.quote: In an ideal world, like we would like to end another $100 million or about Rs.800 crores over the next 12 months.

items.statement: CAPEX funding to combine bank financing, leasing, vendor financing and equity raise
items.quote: It's will have to be a combination of things including like financing from banks and leasing partners and vendor financing and some equity raise.

items.statement: Demand for cloud GPU workloads expected to increase as industry shifts to GPU-centric computing
items.quote: The demand is only going to increase as the industry shifts to more cloud GPU centric workloads. That demand is only going to increase in the industry.

items.statement: Differentiation through software capabilities and workload understanding creates long-term value
items.quote: that insight into the workload, that ability to understand the need for the workloads and implementing those in the software. That product differentiation is what creates long-term value for our customers.

items.statement: Customer base includes SMEs, higher education, research, startups and partner ecosystem; no migration imperative observed
items.quote: The nature of our customers like primarily is the four different buckets today. So one is of course, like we have the SME segment, which continues to be our main the bulk of our customers, then we have the higher education and research category, then we are back with a bang with working with a lot of startups today.

items.statement: Revenue primarily from India; focus on EMEA and US markets for international expansion
items.quote: currently, like our focus continues to be in India, although we would obviously not refuse any customers coming from outside as well. So from a focus outside your perspective, like majorly we are focused on the EMEA market and the US market.

items.statement: Team size approximately 140-150; organic hiring continues across technology, marketing and operations
items.quote: Broadly, we have claim to somewhere between 140 to 150 people in the team. So approximately about 150 and we continue to grow the team organically.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA INR 48 crore with 45% YoY growth; Q4 FY24 EBITDA INR 15 crore with 68% YoY growth
items.quote: EBITDA is 48 crore, representing a growth of 45% on year-on-year basis

items.statement: FY24 revenue INR 95 crore with 43% YoY growth; Q4 FY24 revenue INR 29 crore with 67% YoY growth
items.quote: revenue from operations stood at INR 95 crore representing a growth of around 43% year-on-year basis

items.statement: GPU supply constraints easing; normal integration lead times expected going forward
items.quote: There is always going to be some queue. But it's not going to be the longest queue that we have seen in the past of that type okay, like we are looking at 52 weeks, 56 weeks, 60 weeks and so on. That is not going to be the future.

items.statement: InfiniBand 3.2 Tbps deployed to handle unstructured data at scale for AI/ML workloads
items.quote: the overall idea is that , what is difference between the old world o f the CPU and the storage and the new world of CPU plus GPU plus very high speed panel file system kind of storage and so on

items.statement: Management sees no risk of GPU investment obsolescence; GPU compute shift is irrevocable
items.quote: I don't see there is any risk, the process of going to the GPU is irrevocable. The kind of exponential computing offered by GPU is kind of like really changes the era in which we are operating.

items.statement: Services purchased (data center, power, bandwidth, software licenses) scale with revenue; percentage decreases incrementally with volume
items.quote: So the services would be like in the same proportion as the revenue or a way that they will increase with the revenue in a certain incremental percentage fashion.

items.statement: Right-of-use assets relate to lease-to-own equipment; data center services rented not leased under IndAS 116
items.quote: leasing relate to the equipment and this is all lease to own kind of equipment.

items.statement: Government AI announcements indicate exponential data center capacity growth over next five years
items.quote: one of course that the data center capacity required for artificial intelligence is going to kind of, exponentially grow over next five years or so.

items.statement: Expecting 30% revenue increase in FY25 with PAT margin of 6-6.5%
items.quote: Considering the overall growth in the spice market and our future plans we are expecting a 30% increase in our revenue in FY '25. This strategy is focusing on increasing our brand and PAT margin would be in range of 6% to 6.5% in FY '25.

items.statement: Acquired Vita Green Products for INR7.75 crore including plant, machinery and brand
items.quote: I'm very happy to announce that to cater above both sectors, we recently signed a terms sheet with Vita Green Products Private Limited, which are located at Rajkot, Gujarat.

items.statement: Vita Green peak revenue was INR30 crore in 2021, FY23 revenue INR20 crore, profit INR65 lakh
items.quote: The top peak of the company was in 2021 and that was around INR30 crores. And this company was 100% acquisition base and we have acquired it at INR7.75 crores, including the plant and machinery and brand.

items.statement: 50% of acquisition consideration paid; balance to be paid after fixed assets removed from Vita Green
items.quote: We have paid almost 50% to the company and as I mentioned earlier that we have acquired the plant and machinery and the brand itself, while some fixed assets like land, building are in the name of Vitagreen.

items.statement: No additional capex needed for Vita Green manufacturing capacity; can utilize 70-80% in FY25
items.quote: Yeah, in FY '25, we can utilize more than 70 -80% of Vitagreen. Because Vitagreen has production line of only blended and instant mix. While ground spices are acquired by some vendors, which we are currently providing by Madhusudan Masala. So, I don't think any more capex to be utilized in manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: Blended spices EBITDA margin expected to improve significantly in FY25; current blended margins below 20% vs established players at 20-25%
items.quote: Yeah, it is a fair. So, because after adding the blended spices and instant mix, our EBITDA margin must be improved.

items.statement: Powder/blended spices margins almost double whole spices margins
items.quote: Second question of the margins in whole spices and powder spices is margins were almost double for the powder spices.

items.statement: Spice industry valued at INR1 lakh crore in FY24 growing at 10% CAGR; only 35% branded share
items.quote: The spiciest industry is valued at INR1 lakh crore in FY '24 and is growing at a CAGR of 10%. And the noticeable thing in this industry is that only 35% market share is hold by branded companies.

items.statement: Branded sales share increased to 56% from 47% driving margin expansion
items.quote: The PAT margin was increased because our market share of branded sales in total revenue was increased to 56% from 47%.

items.statement: Vita Green adds 228 SKUs (mostly small INR5/10 packets) taking combined portfolio to 500+ SKUs
items.quote: They have 228 SKUs in their product portfolio and we at Madhusudan Masala have 272 SKUs. So our SKUs portfolio will be more than 500 after this acquisition.

items.statement: Vita Green distribution network covers Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Telangana, Punjab, Jammu & Kashmir; 19 million small SKUs sold annually
items.quote: The main strong factor of this company is that their super scopes and distributed network are widely spreaded in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Telangana, Punjab, and Jammu, Kashmir.

items.statement: Targeting HoReCa segment for whole spices with consistent quality supply

items.statement: 70% of raw material procured in season to ensure consistent quality year-round
items.quote: So, we procure our required procurement was 70% procurement was done in respected season only.

items.statement: Current debt level sufficient for INR160-250 crore turnover; will increase if turnover grows beyond
items.quote: No, no. For this type of INR160 crores to INR250 crores is enough. But in the near future, if turnover is going to be increased indefinitely, that will also increase.

items.statement: Installed capacity 2400 metric tons; chili powder at 62% utilization; turmeric/coriander have sufficient capacity
items.quote: No, as of now, I don't think we have to increase our capacity, production capacity, because we have almost 2400 metric ton capacity installed in our unit. And turmeric coriander has more than sufficient capacity we have.

items.statement: Only papad, soya chunks and asafoetida procured from vendors; all other products manufactured in-house

items.statement: Products listed on Amazon and JioMart; own e-commerce website generating good numbers; margins similar to offline after returns
